ceqa-65c7f1b6dc6f9400d3.name: 568380_Group_Aera_UIC
ceqa-65c7f1b6dc6f9400d3.description: The primary work objective is to sidetrack two (2) existing well(s). This work is designed to support continuation of oil and gas resource development in the area. The wells are not being sidetracked (i) for abandonment purposes only or (ii) in connection with an enforcement order to mitigate or prevent environmental damage or surface expression. Sidetracking is the process of drilling a new wellbore from an existing wellbore. This is typically done when the original wellbore encounters a problem, when accessing remaining hydrocarbons within portions of the same reservoir, or when obstructions in the wellbore need to be bypassed. This process allows drilling a new section in an existing wellbore in the same rock formation restoring the well’s original functionality. The potential disturbance footprint would encompass an existing 20,000 square foot (100 ft x 200 ft) well pad per well. The entirety of this work would be located in an area of existing disturbance and no change in the surface topography (such as drainage patterns) would result. There will be no expansion of the existing well pads, roads, staging areas, or pipelines. No new grading would occur in any undisturbed areas. No new road construction or expansions would be required for the proposed project. Routine maintenance activities at the site would include removal of weeds and other ruderal vegetation for fire control and road maintenance. The work will commence after CalGEM permit approval. The time of year the work would occur is dependent on the date of final CalGEM permit approval. For a single well, it is expected to take approximately 17 operational days to complete all construction phases. Construction activities would generally include the following phases with estimated duration: 1. Plugging a portion of existing wellbore – 2 days • Zonal plugging of wellbore to be sidetracked from in accordance with CalGEM plugging requirements. 2. Site preparation – 7 days • Site location work on existing well pads to create safe work site for personnel and environment 3. Sidetrack drilling (construction) of the well – 3 days • Sidetracking operations in accordance with CalGEM regulations 4. Well completion – 2 days • Subsurface completion of well in accordance with CalGEM regulations 5. Final site surface construction – 3 days • Re-installation of various aboveground piping and equipment to connect well sites to the existing infrastructure Each phase requires different combinations of temporary equipment. At the end of each construction phase, the temporary equipment would be removed from the well site. All work during the project phases, except for the drilling phase, will occur during the days Monday through Friday, and approximate hours from 6 am to 5 pm. The drilling rig will operate 24 hours per day. The construction activity will not include installation of new pipelines or infrastructure. No new ground disturbance would occur. The proposed construction activities would use existing electrical lines. The proposed construction activities would involve a combination of re-use, repair, or reinstallation of various above-ground piping to connect subject well sites to the existing infrastructure. The proposed sidetracks are of existing cyclic steam wells which are completed in the Lombardi Sands (Pool: Lombardi, Pool Code: 10). The Lombardi Sands in the San Ardo Oil Field is a known hydrocarbon zone. The proposed sidetracks will remain in the same pool as the original wellbore. The pool designation will not change. The proposed sidetracks will NOT change the current designation of the existing wells. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving two (2) permit(s) for Aera Energy LLC to perform sidetrack work on the wells listed below, in the San Ardo Oil Field. API # Well Name 0405322271 Orradre 1613-12 0405322264 Orradre 1438-12

ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.name: Pajaro/Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.projectTitle: Pajaro/Sunny Mesa Springfield Area Regional Consolidation Project
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.agency: Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Service District
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.agencyName: Pajaro Sunny Mesa Community Service District
ceqa-ac572207d157d187be.description: The Proposed Project is a two (2)-phased project consisting of the consolidation of the Pajaro Water System (“PWS”), Sunny Mesa Water System (“SMWS”), and Springfield Water System (“SWS”), as well as the various water connections in the North of Moss Landing (“NOML”) area into a single water system to be owned and operated by the District. The First Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded by the State Water Resources Control Board (“SWRCB”) Expedited Drinking Water Grant and would consist of annexation of parcels into the District’s service area, land acquisition and easements, an Iron and Manganese Treatment System at the existing District office, consolidation pipelines (Transmission Mains) connecting the PWS to the SMWS and the SMWS to the SWS, Transmission Pump Station to convey water from PWS to SMWS, rehabilitation of the PWS’ existing 600,000 gallon welded steel water storage tank, electrical upgrades to the Sunny Mesa tank site, conversion of SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 to standby-only use, radio meter upgrades, and installation of a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (“SCADA”) system. The First Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded through the State Water Resources Control Board (“SWRCB”) Expedited Drinking Water Grant Program. The Second Phase of the Proposed Project is anticipated to be funded by the California Safe Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (“CA SRF”) funds from the SWRCB and would consist of the installation of the Springfield Expansion Distribution Main and the Bluff/Jensen Distribution Main, construction of the Bluff/Jensen tank and pump station, and installation of lateral service connections located on private property. The First Phase of the Proposed Project has been designed so that it could operate as a standalone water system in the event that the Second Phase of the Proposed Project is not funded or otherwise delayed. Once operational, the Proposed Project is anticipated to serve approximately 967 total connections. The Proposed Project includes approximately 46,000 linear feet (“LF”) of potable watermains between both phases, and a total of 235,000 LF of total pipeline when including service laterals and appurtenances. The pipeline infrastructure would include pipelines of six (6), eight (8), and 10-inch diameters. The Proposed Project would primarily be supplied water from three (3) sources, comprised of Pajaro Wells No. 1 and No. 2 and Springfield Well No. 2. Additionally, SMWS Wells No. 1 and No. 2 would be retained as standby sources of water for the Proposed Project, for an overall total of five (5) water sources. In addition, the Proposed Project includes additional infrastructure improvements at the existing PWS Water Storage Tank and Sunny Mesa Tank Site to facilitate O&M of the new water system.

ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.name: 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy and 2050 Regional Transportation Plans for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey Counties
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.projectTitle: 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy and 2050 Regional Transportation Plans for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey Counties
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.agency: Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.agencyName: Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments
ceqa-192c1a0b3f58f53691.description: As the metropolitan planning organization for the tri-county region of Monterey, San Benito, and Santa Cruz counties, the Association of Monterey Bay Area Governments (AMBAG) is charged with developing a 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy (MTP/SCS). The 2050 MTP/SCS is both a long-range transportation plan and Sustainable Communities Strategy for Monterey, San Benito, and Santa Cruz counties. The Council of San Benito County Governments, the Santa Cruz County Regional Transportation Commission, and the Transportation Agency for Monterey County are the state-designated Regional Transportation Planning Agencies for San Benito, Santa Cruz, and Monterey counties, respectively. Each prepares a county-level long-range Regional Transportation Plan, which is evaluated in the EIR. The 2050 MTP/SCS is used to guide the development of the Regional and Federal Transportation Improvement Programs, as well as other transportation programming documents and plans. The MTP outlines the region's goals and policies for meeting current and future mobility needs, providing a foundation for transportation decisions by local, regional, and state officials that are ultimately aimed at achieving a coordinated and balanced transportation system. The 2050 MTP/SCS sets forth actions, programs, and projects to address these needs consistent with adopted policies and goals. The 2050 MTP/SCS also documents the financial resources needed to implement the plan. Additionally, pursuant to SB 375, AMBAG (as the regional MPO) must prepare an SCS that demonstrates how the region will meet its greenhouse gas reduction target (6% reduction by 2035) through integrated land use, housing, and transportation planning.

ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.name: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.projectTitle: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-932089dc15ff99e40f.description: The proposed PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement project involves the replacement and upgrade of existing natural gas distribution infrastructure within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area in unincorporated Monterey County, California. The project area includes Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APNs) 031-101-031, 031-101-032, 031-171-033, and 031-181-056, and encompasses multiple residential streets within the East Campus Housing Area. The project is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Company’s (PG&E) statewide initiative to replace aging Aldyl “A” plastic gas pipelines manufactured prior to 1973, which have a documented history of cracking and failure. The replacement program was initiated in response to safety concerns following a pipeline failure incident in Cupertino, California, in 2011. The proposed project consists of replacing approximately 27,543 linear feet of existing gas distribution main and 390 service connections with new polyethylene plastic pipelines. Work would occur primarily within existing paved roadway corridors and disturbed areas using a combination of horizontal directional drilling (HDD) and open trenching construction methods to minimize surface disturbance. Construction activities would occur in multiple phases within the existing utility easements and rights-of-way. The purpose of the project is to reduce threats to the integrity of the natural gas distribution system, improve public safety, and enhance system reliability within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area. The project would also ensure continued safe and efficient delivery of natural gas to residents and campus facilities and reduce the need for future emergency repairs and maintenance.

Electric vehicle owners would benefit from this project as well as the City residents, indirectly, as electric vehicles help reduce air pollution.

ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.name: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.projectTitle: PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement Project
ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.agency: California State University Board of Trustees
ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.agencyName: California State University Board of Trustees
ceqa-01c583e121726b6996.description: The proposed PG&E East Campus Gas Line Replacement project involves the replacement and upgrade of existing natural gas distribution infrastructure within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area in unincorporated Monterey County, California. The project area includes Assessor’s Parcel Numbers (APNs) 031-101-031, 031-101-032, 031-171-033, and 031-181-056, and encompasses multiple residential streets within the East Campus Housing Area. The project is part of Pacific Gas and Electric Company’s (PG&E) statewide initiative to replace aging Aldyl “A” plastic gas pipelines manufactured prior to 1973, which have a documented history of cracking and failure. The replacement program was initiated in response to safety concerns following a pipeline failure incident in Cupertino, California, in 2011. The proposed project consists of replacing approximately 27,543 linear feet of existing gas distribution main and 390 service connections with new polyethylene plastic pipelines. Work would occur primarily within existing paved roadway corridors and disturbed areas using a combination of horizontal directional drilling (HDD) and open trenching construction methods to minimize surface disturbance. Construction activities would occur in multiple phases within the existing utility easements and rights-of-way. Please refer to Attachment A, CEQA Supporting Documentation, for additional project description information, available for review upon request at CSUMB’s Campus Planning and Development offices. The purpose of the project is to reduce threats to the integrity of the natural gas distribution system, improve public safety, and enhance system reliability within the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area. The project would also ensure continued safe and efficient delivery of natural gas to residents and campus facilities and reduce the need for future emergency repairs and maintenance. The beneficiaries of the project include Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) and residents of the CSUMB East Campus Housing Area on the California State University, Monterey Bay main campus. The project would provide long-term safety and reliability improvements to the local natural gas distribution system, consistent with PG&E’s ongoing efforts to modernize critical utility infrastructure across California. CSU discretionary action related to this project is limited to the issuance of a Right to Access permit and a Temporary Work Authorization permit to PG&E to allow it to carry out the proposed improvements on the CSUMB campus.

ceqa-989342df1b909a2220.name: Moss Landing Tide Gate Repair
ceqa-989342df1b909a2220.description: The purpose of the permanent repair project proposed by the Monterey County Water Resources Agency is to restore the Moss Landing Tide Gate facility to its original operational condition. This facility provides protection from flooding due to tidal influence and prevents seawater from Moss Landing Harbor form entering the Moro Cojo Slough. The Moro Cojo Slough is normally brackish body of water habitat that protects critical habitats where federally listed species can occur.

ceqa-3a9c32c10dfe2f071f.description: The project involves development of the 18.7-acre site with a 61,219 sq. ft. BMW auto dealership and 95 for-sale residential units and other related improvements. ceqa-df920fd10f2a50a11d.description: The Proposed Revised Modified Revised Project ("Project") is similar to the originally approved Project, approved by the District on June 27, 2019. The Project proposes an average annual production of five million gallons per day of potable water from slant wells drilled at Doheny State Beach, in addition to associated raw water conveyance lines and various related improvements to Doheny State Beach campground, and a desalination facility on existing District property located approximately ¼-mile inland, adjacent to San Juan Creek. The Project also includes an Energy Center with various renewable energy facilities, and minor improvements to Paseo Costa Sur (access road). The State Lands Commission action is an amendment of a 20-year General Lease – Public Agency Use through October 2046.

ceqa-bf2ee3d000987e9662.name: First & Mountain View Project
ceqa-bf2ee3d000987e9662.description: The proposed project involves demolition of an existing 11,300-square foot single-story commercial/industrial building and associated improvements to construct 61 for-sale townhome units (including three live/work units) on an approximately 3.3-acre site within the City associated with Assessor Parcel Numbers (APNs) 188-021-11, 188-021-12, and 188-021-10. The residential community would consist of nine separate three-story townhouse buildings with units ranging from 1,318 square feet to 2,154 square feet in size. The project overall would provide 10,024 square feet of common open space and 135 total parking spaces, two-garages per unit and 13 guest stalls. The project is requesting a General Plan Amendment (GPA) to change the land use designations from General Commercial (GC) and Low-Medium Density Residential (LMR-11) to Urban Neighborhood-Low (UN-20) and an Amendment Application (AA) to change the zoning designations from General Commercial (C2) and Light Industrial (M1) to a Specific Development (SD) zoning designation. Additionally, the project requests a Vesting Tentative Tract Map (VTTM) to consolidate the three existing parcels into one development site and subdivide the property into 61 condominium townhome units, and a Density Bonus Agreement to permit development incentives/concessions and waivers associated with the proposed residential community.

ceqa-5823f00bb3ff7a55bb.description: The Gypsum Canyon Veterans Cemetery is a multi-phased, multi-year project that would construct a veterans cemetery on an approximately 80-acre parcel in Gypsum Canyon, including acquisition and easements; rough and fine grading; utility trenching and installation; paving of drive aisles, main entry and access roads, and cortege lanes; landscape planting and irrigation; interim storm drainage inlets; a storm water treatment basin and underground detention facilities; storm drains; potable, fire and irrigation water lines, and electrical/communications utilities within the access road and cemetery; sanitary sewer system and storage tank; development of approximately 40,759 crypts, 472 over-sized crypts, 49,395 in-ground cremains plots, and 67,040 columbaria niches (the precise number of each will be determined as each phase develops); administration and public restroom buildings; a maintenance building and paved maintenance yard with above-ground fuel storage for equipment; a ceremonial (main) entrance/avenue of the flags and cortege assembly area; a committal service shelter; a carillon tower, flag/assembly area, memorial walk and memorial wall; and signage and flower water stations.

ceqa-5cc95d4f2f9c2e9f8b.description: The South Coast Water District proposes to rehabilitate approximately 5,033 linear feet of existing 6- and 8-inch vitrified clay pipe (VCP) gravity sewer mains at 18 locations within the Cities of Laguna Beach, Dana Point, and San Clemente. Work would include cleaning, inspection, and cured-in-place pipe lining installed through existing manholes, as well as 12 point repairs at 6 locations in Dana Point requiring localized excavation within the paved street right-of-way. All work would occur within existing street rights-of-way, and all disturbed surfaces would be restored. The Project would not add new connections or expand system capacity. The purpose of the Project is to extend the service life of aging sewer infrastructure and reduce the risk of leaks and sewage spills.

ceqa-ee3d9af801a3870795.name: Crystal Cove Coastal Access Preservation Project
ceqa-ee3d9af801a3870795.projectTitle: Crystal Cove Coastal Access Preservation Project
ceqa-ee3d9af801a3870795.description: This is an emergency project on State Route 1 adjacent to Crystal Cove State Park. Currently the slope and roadway are being compromised due to erosion caused by increasing wave energy and storm surges relating to Super El Nino storm events. The project will provide temporary slope and roadway stabilization measures along with temporary energy dispersing devices to prevent further erosion of the slope and possible failure of the roadway. This project falls under the Governor’s State of Emergency Proclamation dated September 21, 2026.

ceqa-d26ec6d6988a148e36.name: IBC Multi-use Trail Barranca Segment Project
ceqa-d26ec6d6988a148e36.projectTitle: IBC Multi-use Trail Barranca Segment Project
ceqa-d26ec6d6988a148e36.description: The proposed trail would total approximately 0.36 miles of an off-street paved Class I shared-use path. The proposed trail would include a two-foot wide paved shoulder nearest to the Barranca Channel, an eight-foot wide paved path for pedestrians and cyclists, and an additional three-foot wide paved shoulder opposite the Barranca Channel. The proposed trail would include a pedestrian bridge over Jamboree Road for pedestrian and bicyclist safety. The pedestrian overcrossing for the proposed trail would be comprised of retaining walls, a concrete slab bridge supported by CIDH pile foundation, and a prefabricated truss bridge with chain link fence.

ceqa-a25b3a0d195bdae039.name: San Juan Creek Channel (L01) Repair Project
ceqa-a25b3a0d195bdae039.projectTitle: San Juan Creek Channel (L01) Repair Project
ceqa-a25b3a0d195bdae039.description: The proposed project includes replacement of damaged concrete channel lining within the San Juan Creek Channel (L01) (Project) between 300 to 800 feet upstream of Stonehill Road within the City of Dana Point. The proposed Project scope of work includes the removal and replacement of the existing damaged unreinforced concrete slope lining and installation of sheet piles. The sheet piles will be installed vertically into the invert of the channel, and voids behind damaged channel lining will also be backfilled. The proposed Project is an emergency repair project for the purposes of public health and safety and will be completed in Winter 2026/2027.

ceqa-d4a605add9a036ae48.name: Installation Of EV Charging Infrastructure at OC Waste & Recycling Active Landfills (OC Waste & Recycling Log #741)
ceqa-d4a605add9a036ae48.projectTitle: Installation Of EV Charging Infrastructure at OC Waste & Recycling Active Landfills (OC Waste & Recycling Log #741)
ceqa-d4a605add9a036ae48.description: OC Waste & Recycling (OCWR) proposes the approval of the County of Orange's participation in the Southern California Edison's Charge Ready Transport (CRT) Program to reduce the county's cost for fleet electrification that is needed to comply with California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) mandates. The CRT Program provides incentives to public agencies by either allowing SCE to design and construct ready-made electrical infrastructure on participant property or providing rebates of up to 80 percent for customer-constructed make-ready infrastructure . Participating in the CRT Program requires the execution of program agreements with Southern California Edison (SCE) and for certain sites, allowing temporary construction and/or permanent utility easements to allow SCE to install and operate electrical infrastructure . If approved, the proposed project will include the installation of EV (electrical vehicles) charging infrastructure at the County's three (3) active landfills. All work is within the existing OCWR Landfill property.

ceqa-97bed8c4c01273251e.description: The proposed project involves the demolition of a 41,519 square foot office building to construct a 58-unit, three-story, for-sale attached townhome community on approximately 4.4 acres. The development features three- and four-bedroom floor plans with enclosed garages, along with 24 guest parking spaces distributed throughout the site. ceqa-8cd4fdc86eef40be47.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Diazyme Laboratories, Inc., Brea, California
ceqa-8cd4fdc86eef40be47.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Diazyme Laboratories, Inc., Brea, California
ceqa-8cd4fdc86eef40be47.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-8cd4fdc86eef40be47.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to Diazyme Laboratories, Inc. (EPA ID# CAL000503509) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with a chemical solution. Specifically, two (2) 15-gallon and four (4) 125-gram containers of Picric Acid must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. This chemical is currently being stored at Diazyme Laboratories, Inc. located at 510 W. Central Avenue, Suite D, Brea, California 92821. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued to chemically stabilize the hazardous waste prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site. The treatment of these hazardous wastes involves the addition of a solution to the containers in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemical. Treatment will take place within a designated exclusion zone. Only technicians from Clean Harbors will be allowed in the exclusion zone. Movement, preparation, and treatment of the containers will be in accordance with established standards. Within 10 business days of the expiration of this permit, Diazyme Laboratories, Inc. will submit a final report, signed in accordance with Title 22, CCR Sec. 66270.11(d). The report shall include certification that the treatment area has been cleared of all residual hazardous waste generated from this emergency treatment and all generated waste has been properly managed. The Emergency Permit is effective beginning October 19, 2026 and shall expire on December 18, 2026

ceqa-75e7c64198ac92cae5.projectTitle: Zoning Map Amend. (Zone Change) P-ZC2026-0003 & Development Code Amend. P-DCA2026-0005. As well as amend. to Title 6 and 12 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
ceqa-75e7c64198ac92cae5.description: 1.)Zoning Map Amendment (Zone Change) P-ZC2026-0003 & Development Code Amendment P-DCA2026-0005 – City-initiated petitions for consideration of an amendment to Title 9 (Development Code) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code, to allow new permitted uses, new conditionally permitted uses, parking standard refinements, and streamline the entitlement process. The Code amendment is intended to create a more efficient and business-friendly regulatory framework while maintaining appropriate land-use compatibility, community character, and quality development standards. A Development Code Zoning Map Amendment (Zone Change) is proposed to create an Indoor Entertainment overlay zone to provide additional flexibility for appropriate indoor entertainment uses. Indoor entertainment uses are to be permitted in the overlay zone, which is proposed to include the Mission Viejo Freeway Center, Mission Viejo Village Center, and Kaleidoscope. The proposed amendments also include updates to the City’s floodplain management regulations (Chapter 9.100) to better align with current Federal and State regulations. 2.)Amendments to Title 6 – Health and Sanitation (Chapters 6.10 and 6.65) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code include to better align the City’s regulations with current Federal and State requirements. 3.)Amendments to Title 12 – Traffic (Chapter 12.08) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code to strengthen the Orange County Sheriff’s Department’s (OCSD) ability to enforce parking permit requirements throughout the City.

ceqa-175b448bc119348bf5.name: Class 1* Permit Modification for Southern California Edison; San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station
ceqa-175b448bc119348bf5.projectTitle: Class 1* Permit Modification for Southern California Edison; San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station
ceqa-175b448bc119348bf5.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-175b448bc119348bf5.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) approves of the Class 1* Permit Modification (Permit Modification) regarding an extension to the closure schedule for a partial closure of the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) facility located at 5000 Old Pacific Coast Highway, San Clemente, CA 92672. Although closure activities have begun, there were additional demolition and disposal activities necessary for the closure and the extension request is to complete the ongoing closure activities of the South Yard Facility (Sections A&B) hazardous waste storage units at SONGS. The date for final closure of the units has been extended to March 31, 2027. The remaining activities for closure of these units include sampling in accordance with the approved sampling plan, laboratory analysis of the samples, and submittal of the final closure report. Background: SONGS is a nuclear power generating facility undergoing decommissioning located on the coast of Southern California in San Diego County. SONGS began operation in 1968 and is operated and primarily owned by Southern California Edison. The facility operated three pressurized water nuclear reactors (Unit 1, 2, and 3) and several smaller standby diesel generating units which all ceased operation by 2013. The decommissioning and decontamination of the facility will result in the generation of hazardous waste, some of which will be contaminated with radio nuclides, referred to as mixed waste or combined waste. The mixed waste and combined waste include, but are not limited to, used oil, chemical solvents, lead solids, and asbestos which are to be stored in sealed containers and shipped offsite within one year from the date they are placed in a permitted storage unit. SONGS was first authorized by DTSC in 1989 to operate a hazardous waste storage facility under a grant of interim status. The first Hazardous Waste Facility Permit (Permit) issued to SONGS became effective on January 31, 2005, and was permitted for ten years. A Permit Renewal became effective on May 23, 2016, that allowed the facility to continue to store hazardous waste while it undergoes decommissioning. SONGS notified DTSC that closure of the LSAW and HSAW storage areas would begin in July of 2023. SONGS requested an extension to the 180-day timeframe allowed to complete closure in December of 2023. Project Activities: The year of final closure of the HazMat Pads A&B storage units has been extended to March 31, 2027. There are no proposed changes to the closure activities other than to extend the closure schedule for decommissioning the hazardous materials storage units at SONGS. The Permit Modification does not include any other changes to closure requirements, operational changes, or significant ground disturbing activities at the facility.

ceqa-adc0cd666982d586ac.name: Western Realco Enterprise Way Industrial Project
ceqa-adc0cd666982d586ac.projectTitle: Western Realco Enterprise Way Industrial Project
ceqa-adc0cd666982d586ac.description: The proposed project is comprised of two sites. Site 1 is located at 26110, 26140, and 26160 Enterprise Way, is approximately 8.41 acres comprised of three parcels (Assessor’s Parcel Numbers [APNs] 610-401-10, -11, and -13). Site 1 involves the demolition of three existing two-story office buildings totaling approximately 150,000 sq. ft. In its place, two new 35-foot tall, tilt-up concrete industrial buildings totaling 156,800 sq. ft. would be constructed and operated. Site 1 includes a truck loading area, 291 parking spaces, and new landscaping. Building 1 would include a maximum of ten usable dock doors and Building 2 would include a maximum of eight usable dock doors. Although the tenant(s) has not been determined yet, Site 1 includes a mix of office, manufacturing, and warehouse space. Building 1 would include 52,702 sq. ft. of manufacturing space, 40,098 sq. ft. of warehouse space, and 10,000 sq. ft. of office space. Building 2 would include 25,500 sq. ft. of manufacturing space, 20,500 sq. ft. of warehouse space, and 8,000 sq. ft. of office space. Site 2, located at 26250 Enterprise Way, is approximately 4.77 acres and is comprised of one parcel (APN 610-401-21). Site 2 involves the demolition of the existing 76,978 sq. ft., two-story office building. In its place, a new 35-foot-tall, 77,000 sq. ft. tilt-up concrete industrial building would be constructed and operated. Site 2 includes 767 linear feet of retaining walls up to 8-feet tall along the northerly and westerly property lines, a truck loading area, seven usable dock doors, 107 parking spaces, and new landscaping. Although the tenant has not been determined yet, Site 2 includes a mix of office and warehouse space. Approximately 8,000 sq. ft. would serve as office space and 69,000 sq. ft. would serve as warehouse space. Additionally, the project includes off-site improvements at five intersections within the City to enhance public safety and address concerns related to large truck turning movements: Bake Parkway/Commercentre Drive, Bake Parkway/Dimension Drive, Dimension Drive/Commercentre Drive/Enterprise Way, Lake Forest Drive/Dimension Drive, and Lake Forest Drive/Rancho Parkway.

ceqa-1bb7e7404ae9253d59.name: West Coyote Hills and Robert E. Ward Nature Preserve Remedial Action Plan
ceqa-1bb7e7404ae9253d59.projectTitle: West Coyote Hills Specific Plan/Robert E. Ward Nature Preserve
ceqa-1bb7e7404ae9253d59.description: The Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) has approved the Remedial Action Plan (RAP) for the West Coyote Hills and Robert E. Ward Nature Preserve (Site) to address surface and subsurface soil impacted with constituents of potential concern (COPCs) associated with historical oil field operations. The RAP, along with a Remedial Action Workplan submitted to the United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA), will require excavation of approximately 11,410 bank cubic yards (BCY) of soil contaminated with total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs), including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), metals, and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs). The Site is located in the northwestern area of the City of Fullerton (City). The current footprint of the former WCH oil field is an approximately 483-acre property separated by a public road, Gilbert Street, into an approximately 352-acre Western Property and an approximately 131-acre Eastern Property. The Eastern Property excludes portions of the former WCH oil field that were sold to the City in 2021 (Parcels 1 and 3; approximately 24 acres) or previously donated to the City in 1983 (the Robert E. Ward Nature Preserve; approximately 72 acres). Figure 1 (included with this Notice of Determination for reference) depicts the Western Property and Eastern Property areas which will be remediated under the RAP. The RAP is associated with the long-term use of the Site as open space. Upon completion of site remediation activities, the Site will be conserved in perpetuity as protected open space under a land use covenant. The site remediation activities set forth in the RAP consist of soil excavation with off-site disposal. The total anticipated volume of excavated soil is approximately 11,410?bank cubic yards (BCY): 4,451 BCY of non-PCB impacted soil (overseen by DTSC) and 6,959 BCY of PCB-impacted soil (overseen by USEPA). Excavation of PCBs and other soil impacts are planned to be performed concurrently. The excavated soil would be transported via covered and lined end-dump trucks to appropriate landfill facilities (depending on whether excavated soil is hazardous or non-hazardous). The excavations would be backfilled with imported clean fill to approximately original grade and restored with an appropriate seed mix consisting of native plant species. Institutional controls (ICs), in the form of land use covenants (deed restrictions), would be established to restrict future property use to open space purposes and to limit actions that could interfere with this land use. Implementation of the RAP is estimated to take approximately 8 working months to complete between January 2028 and late 2029, which takes into account pausing work from February 15 through August 30 to avoid disrupting the coastal California gnatcatcher (Polioptila californica) nesting season.
ceqa-1bb7e7404ae9253d59.crossStreets: N. Gilbert St and Rosencrans Ave

ceqa-66832c9057f6e68c3e.description: The Santa Margarita Water District (SMWD) proposes to remove and replace less than 1,000 feet of existing water and sewer pipelines as part of the utility realignment. The project consists of the relocation of an existing water pipelines to accommodate the Caltrans SR-74 Ortega Highway Widening Project. Project activities would include utility trenching, grading, and construction of retaining walls. Work would be conducted within a new temporary construction easement, and the pipelines would be relocated to a new SMWD utility easement. The purpose of the project is to implement the utility realignment of SMWD’s water and sewer pipelines while maintaining the integrity, reliability, and safe operation to accommodate the Caltrans SR-74 Ortega Highway Widening Project. Beneficiaries include SWMD and its customers, who rely on continued safe and reliable water service. The project involves no expansion of use of the relocated pipeline.

ceqa-05b8211aed08cd5579.name: Costco Wholesale Facility and Fueling Station Project
ceqa-05b8211aed08cd5579.projectTitle: Costco Wholesale Facility and Fueling Station Project
ceqa-05b8211aed08cd5579.description: The proposed project entails development of a 159,889-SF Costco wholesale facility and fueling station, with associated site improvements, on the project site. Construction of the proposed project would require demolition of the three existing industrial buildings and parking areas, retention of 38 existing ornamental trees, removal of 214 ornamental trees, and associated on-site and offsite improvements, including the removal and relocation of driveways on Ranger Street and Birch Street and the removal of an existing driveway along Kraemer Boulevard. The Costco wholesale facility would be constructed on the northeastern portion of the project site and include typical Costco departments: sales floor, bakery, meat, cooler/freezer facilities, pharmacy, optical center, hearing aid center, food service, tire center, food court, and associated back-of-house functions. Loading docks would be on the southeast corner of the warehouse. Outdoor equipment would include two trash compactors and emergency generators. Costco wholesale facility retail center hours are anticipated to be Monday through Friday from 9:00 am to 8:30 pm, Saturday from 8:30 am to 6:00 pm, and Sunday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. A Costco fueling facility would be constructed on the western portion of the project site. The fueling facility would be housed under a prefabricated canopy, with 20 fuel islands and 40 fueling pumps that would be accessed via oneway queuing lanes. Three underground storage tanks (two 40,000-gallon gasoline tanks and one 1,500-gallon additive tank) and associated monitoring and safety equipment would be installed. The fueling facility hours are anticipated to be 5:00 am to 10:00 pm Monday through Friday, 6:00 am to 8:00 pm on Saturday, and 6:00 am to 7:30 pm on Sunday. A total of 943 parking stalls would be provided onsite. Ingress/egress to the site would be provided on East Birch Street, South Kraemer Boulevard, and Ranger Street, and truck access would be primarily from Ranger Street.

ceqa-c7d3aeffa59c62dd0d.agencyName: Fullerton Joint Union High School District
ceqa-c7d3aeffa59c62dd0d.description: The proposed project would install 18 new field lights at the existing baseball and softball fields. No other development or installation of educational-related structures would occur as part of the proposed project. ¦ Eight field lights would be located along the perimeter of the varsity baseball field. One light would have an approximate height of 60 feet, four lights would have an approximate height of 70 feet, and three lights would have an approximate height of 80 feet. ¦ Six field lights would be located along the perimeter of the junior varsity baseball field. One light would have an approximate height of 70 feet, and five lights would have an approximate height of 80 feet. ¦ Four field lights would be located along the perimeter of the varsity softball field. One light would have an approximate height of 60 feet, two lights would have an approximate height of 70 feet, and one light would have an approximate height of 80 feet. With the addition of field lights, the proposed project would add 11 evening practices between 3:30 PM and 8:00 PM for baseball and softball. No other changes to operations are proposed: the proposed project would not result in any changes to the number of participants, time of year (season), or number of spectators for games at BPHS. The proposed project would not increase enrollment capacity or student enrollment at BPHS. Major spectator events such as varsity football games would continue to occur at Buena Park High School, Fullerton Union High School, and La Habra High School. Construction of the proposed project would occur in a single phase, anticipated to begin in March 2027 (no confirmed end date as of this notice). All construction activities would comply with the City of Buena Park's noise standards in Section 8.28 of the Municipal Code, which prohibits construction-generated noise between 8:00 PM and 7:00 AM Monday through Saturday, and at any time on Sundays, anticipated to begin in March 2027. The discretionary actions and approvals required for project implementation are 1) project approval by the District, 2) the adoption of the MND, and 3) the adoption of the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program.

ceqa-1ac2c4245a8501d6c1.projectTitle: The City of Santa Ana Walnut Pump Station PFAS Treatment Project
ceqa-1ac2c4245a8501d6c1.description: The City of Santa Ana Walnut Pump Station PFAS Treatment Project consists of removing PFAS contaminants from wells 16, 29, 33 and 41 at a new centralized PFAS treatment plant located in the Walnut Pump Station. The key project components include ion exchange vessels, booster pumps, cartridge filters, an expanded sodium hypochlorite disinfection system, a new water conveyance pipeline, flow meters, valves, drains, electrical and instrumentation control equipment. Eight ion exchange vessel systems in a lead-lag configuration (for a total of sixteen vessels) will be installed as part of the new centralized PFAS treatment plant. This Project also includes a new water conveyance pipeline to connect wells 16 and 41 to a new centralized PFAS treatment plant utilizing ion exchange in the Walnut Pump Station.

ceqa-599ed715539590da1b.description: The purpose of this Agreement is to fund development of actionable intelligence (AI)-based advanced multi-horizon net-load forecasting models that explicitly predict Behind-the-Meter (BtM) distributed energy resource behavior of solar photovoltaic (PV), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicles (EVs) with focus in improving short-term forecasting accuracy under high-variability events, which will help grid operators to efficiently improve California's grid resilience and flexibility and deliver significant cost savings for ratepayers through enhanced load shifting and demand response.

ceqa-e418e9c172e4d5aa54.name: Neighborhoods Where We All Belong Zoning Updates and Housing Element Implementation
ceqa-e418e9c172e4d5aa54.projectTitle: Neighborhoods Where We All Belong Zoning Updates and Housing Element Implementation
ceqa-e418e9c172e4d5aa54.description: The proposed Project is a comprehensive effort to address housing needs, comply with State Housing Law, and address the City Council goal to “diversify, stabilize and increase housing to reflect community needs.” The City proposes to implement the Project in accordance with approved Measure K ballot measure, which facilitates the development of housing in commercial and industrial areas. Properties identified in Measure K include sites that are included in the City’s 2021-2029 Housing Element Update as well as non-Housing Element sites. The City’s Housing Element identifies specific programs to encourage the development of housing for residents at various income levels and housing sizes. Implementation of these programs would update zoning regulations to increase development opportunities, simplify the process of building housing, and accommodate the City’s mandated fair share of Orange County’s housing needs (also known as the Regional Housing Needs Allocation [RHNA]) as well as a necessary buffer of additional development capacity. The proposed Project implements portions of the Housing Element as required by State Housing Law. Implementation of Housing Element programs include rezoning of Housing Element sites and Measure K sites, along with modifications to the City’s zoning regulations across existing urban plans, overlays, and specific plans with the intent to clarify, consolidate, and streamline regulations where possible. As such, the Project would amend the City’s existing Mixed-Use Overlay District (MUOD), as codified in Chapter V (Development Standards) of Title 13 (Planning, Zoning, and Development) of the CMMC. The amended MUOD would be applied to all Measure K sites, including Housing Element and non-Housing Element sites. Application and utilization of the amended MUOD assumes that residential only or mixed-use (residential and commercial) would be developed on Housing Element sites. The Project analyzes the capacity of the Housing Element sites, which as identified in the Housing Element is comprised of 17,042 units (the Regional Housing Needs Assessment of 11,760 units and Housing Element-required buffer capacity) as well as additional capacity for Measure K non-Housing Element sites. At full buildout in 2056, the proposed Project studies an increased capacity for the development of approximately 21,522 dwelling units and approximately 17,306,003 square feet of commercial uses. Given that the Planning Area contains existing non-residential land uses (i.e., commercial and industrial), including approximately 11,619,124 square feet of existing commercial uses and approximately 5,223,256 square feet of existing industrial uses, the net new non-residential buildout for all Measure K sites is anticipated to be approximately 10,630,361 square feet within the Planning Area by 2056.

ceqa-7c0cffadd8d37cb38e.name: Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 and Commercial Cannabis Permit CCP-2026-0001.
ceqa-7c0cffadd8d37cb38e.projectTitle: Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 and Commercial Cannabis Permit CCP-2026-0001.
ceqa-7c0cffadd8d37cb38e.description: On August 5, 2026, the Laguna Woods Senior Planner approved Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 and Commercial Cannabis Permit CCP-2026-0001, both of which relate to the proposed establishment of a cannabis storefront retailer at the Project Location. Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 also applies to eligible successors at the project location, while Commercial Cannabis Permit CCP-2026-0001 is nontransferable. The property owner is JTP Laguna Woods LLC. In approving Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 and Commercial Cannabis Permit CCP-2026-0001, the City Manager made the following findings: 1. General Plan. The use or project proposed is consistent with the General Plan. The project is within the Commercial land use designation of the General Plan. The project is consistent with the Commercial land use designation of the General Plan, which is intended to "[cover] a broad range of non-residential, non-industrial uses. Typical commercial uses include retail stores, restaurants, administrative offices, retail services such as dry cleaners and barbershops, automobile sales and services, and may include institutional uses such as hospitals and churches." The establishment of a cannabis storefront retailer would aid in achieving Goal 1 in the General Plan Land Use Element, which is to "promote land uses that accommodate the diverse needs of City of Laguna Woods residents," as well as Policy I.B in the General Plan Land Use Element, which is to "actively participate with property owners and their representatives to expand the range of retail goods and services." In this case, over a period of several years, a number of City of Laguna Woods residents have expressed interest in the establishment of cannabis storefront retailers in Laguna Woods, including in 2020 with the passage of Measure V, which asked voters: "Should the City of Laguna Woods allow the establishment and operation of marijuana dispensaries offering the retail sale of medical and non-medical marijuana in commercial zoning districts within the City of Laguna Woods city limits?" 6,651 ballots were cast for "Yes." 6,426 ballots were cast for "No." The project would not change the existing floor area ratio for the existing building located at the Project Location, which was constructed prior to the City of Laguna Woods' incorporation. 2. Zoning Code. The use, activity or improvement(s) proposed is consistent with the provisions of the Zoning Code. The Project Location is within the Community Commercial (CC) zoning district. The establishment of cannabis storefront retailers within the Community Commercial (CC) zoning district is explicitly permitted in the Laguna Woods Municipal Code. Condition of Approval #3 for Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 requires compliance with the Laguna Woods Municipal Code, which includes the Laguna Woods Zoning Code. 3. CEQA. The approval of the permit application is in compliance with the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act. Based on the information received from the Project Applicant and staff's assessment of the same, the project has been determined to be categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations. Additional information is contained in the "Reasons Why Project is Exempt" portion of this Notice of Exemption and incorporated herein by this reference. 4. Compatibility. The location, size, design and operating characteristics of the proposed use will not create conditions or situations that may be incompatible with other permitted uses in the vicinity. The project involves occupancy of an existing building for commercial use and certain interior and exterior alterations to accommodate the specific commercial use. The Project Location has housed commercial uses since prior to the City of Laguna Woods' incorporation with no significant change in other permitted uses in the vicinity, which generally include private residences and a mortuary. The only abutting private property from which direct access is not obstructed by walls is occupied by a mortuary, which is also a commercial use. Conditions of approval for Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 are included to ensure that appropriate measures are taken to avoid conditions or situations that may be incompatible with other permitted uses in the vicinity. For example, Condition of Approval #3 requires the project – including all alterations – to "comply with all then-current requirements of the Laguna Woods Municipal Code and the California Building Standards Code, as well as federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations..." Laguna Woods Municipal Code Section 13.26.025 contains regulations regarding the operation of cannabis storefront retailers, which are also likely to promote compatible uses with other permitted uses in the vicinity. 5. General welfare. The approval of the permit application will not result in conditions or circumstances contrary to the public health and safety and the general welfare. The project is subject to conditions of approval for Site Development Permit SDP-2026-0001 that will regulate the use in manners consistent with the Laguna Woods Municipal Code. Several of the conditions of approval relate to public health, safety, and general welfare including, but not limited to, reservation of the City of Laguna Woods' rights to require additional security or safety measures, if warranted. Such conditions would assist in protecting the public from potential risk or danger. The conditions of approval also explicitly require the project to comply with all then-current requirements of the Laguna Woods Municipal Code and the California Building Standards Code, as well as federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations. Laguna Woods Municipal Code Section 13.26.025 contains regulations regarding the operation of cannabis storefront retailers, including minimum security measures. Laguna Woods Municipal Code Section 13.26.025(f)(21) makes clear that cannabis storefront retailers are responsible for providing adequate security, reading in part: "In addition to complying with this section, cannabis storefront retailers shall develop, implement, and actively monitor security measures sufficient to protect the health, safety, and welfare of officials, officers, agents, employees, volunteers, associates, customers, visitors, passersby, and all other persons who may enter, cross over, or otherwise interact with parcel(s) on which they are located, whether invited or not, at all times and on all days, regardless of the cannabis storefront retailer's hours of operation or any other factor." 6. Public facilities. The approval of the permit application is in compliance with all City-required public facilities regulations. The project has been evaluated against all City of Laguna Woods regulations through the site development permit process and commercial cannabis permit process. Following such evaluation, the project is deemed to be in compliance, subject to the conditions of approval. The project would not require the addition or modification of any public facilities, nor heightened levels of service for any public services operating from public facilities.

ceqa-2033f23c3a93a1ce89.description: Full Title: 2026 East End Horse Stable Project, Addendum to the Previously Adopted Final Initial Study (IS) and Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) for the Proposed Drainage Improvements and Restoration Activities at the Rancho Mission Viejo Riding Park at San Juan Capistrano Premier Equisport Events, LLC (Premier) operates the City-owned Riding Park property at the Rancho Mission Viejo Riding Park, San Juan Capistrano, pursuant to a Ground Lease approved by the City Council in July 2025. Premier is responsible for operating and maintaining the property's existing water quality infrastructure, known as the Concentrated Animal Feeding Operation (CAFO) Water Quality Improvements. Premier proposes the 2026 East End Horse Stable Project, which includes: (1) eight standard-size row-stall horse barns similar to, or the same as, the existing horse barns on-site, which would be approximately 9 feet in height and would include 10-foot by 12-foot stalls arranged side-by-side in two rows, accommodating up to approximately 315 stalls total; and (2) berms and a dedicated stormwater capture and infiltration basin intended to isolate and manage stormwater generated by the new horse stables. The proposed system would operate independently from the existing CAFO water quality infrastructure. The proposed project was evaluated under CEQA through an Addendum to the previously adopted 2020 Mitigated Negative Declaration. The Addendum concludes that the project would not result in new significant environmental impacts or substantially increase the severity of impacts previously identified. The existing Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program remains applicable, and no additional mitigation measures are required. Premier has also received the necessary authorization from the San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Board under the applicable Industrial General Permit framework. On August 18, 2026 the City Council of the City of San Juan Capistrano, after considering the Addendum and the IS/MND, adopted the Addendum, found the 2026 East End Horse Stable Project “functionally equivalent” to the previous Drainage Improvements and Restoration Activities, and approved the Revised Project.

ceqa-18682c1d06775f444f.name: Area 5 Flood Control Basin Memorandum of Understanding
ceqa-18682c1d06775f444f.projectTitle: Area 5 Flood Control Basin Memorandum of Understanding
ceqa-18682c1d06775f444f.description: On August 12, 2026, the Laguna Woods City Council approved a memorandum of understanding with the Golden Rain Foundation of Laguna Woods to allow the City to operate, maintain, and construct certain improvements at the Area 5 Flood Control Basin, which could potentially include Statewide Trash Provisions-related capital improvements, although no specific capital improvements were proposed or approved as part of the approval of the memorandum of understanding. The memorandum of understanding is related to the City’s ongoing efforts to develop a Statewide Trash Provisions compliance approach that: 1. Does not require private property owners to construct, operate, or maintain their own capital improvements, or pay new fees or charges for the City to do so; and 2. Leverages existing storm drain infrastructure for compliance, thereby avoiding or reducing the need for disruptive activities such as the excavation of portions of El Toro Road or Moulton Parkway to construct underground treatment devices. The memorandum of understanding will assist staff in finalizing a Statewide Trash Provisions compliance approach and developing potential, future capital improvement projects for City Council consideration. The memorandum of understanding is envisioned to be long-term, initially running through June 30, 2060, with the potential for mutually agreed upon extensions thereafter. During the term of the memorandum of understanding, the Golden Rain Foundation will remain the owner of the Area 5 Flood Control Basin and the City will be responsible for operation and maintenance thereof. The City’s obligations will include, but not be limited to, landscaping, irrigation, and ensuring compliance with both agreements for drainage encumbrance affecting the Area 5 Flood Control Basin. Landscaping and irrigation responsibilities will include the vegetated fence that runs parallel to the eastbound El Toro Road sidewalk.

ceqa-e380743096df7340eb.name: Electric Vehicle Charging Fees
ceqa-e380743096df7340eb.description: On August 19, 2026, the Laguna Woods City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-33 titled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LAGUNA WOODS, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING INCREASED ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING FEES FOR USE OF CITY-OWNED ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS LOCATED AT LAGUNA WOODS CITY HALL, 24264 EL TORO ROAD, LAGUNA WOODS, CA 92637; AND DETERMINING AND CERTIFYING THAT THE RESOLUTION IS EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT The City adopted a new electric vehicle charging fee schedule which will increase and modify the existing fees that the City charges to recover no more than the reasonable costs associated with providing electric vehicle charging to persons who choose to charge motor vehicles at City-owned electric vehicle charging stations located at Laguna Woods City Hall. The new fee schedule will take effect on August 20, 2026.

ceqa-d94a84eb191fb8efda.name: Falcon Academy of Science and Technology Multipurpose Building and Classroom Buildings Project
ceqa-d94a84eb191fb8efda.projectTitle: Falcon Academy of Science and Technology Multipurpose Building and Classroom Buildings Project
ceqa-d94a84eb191fb8efda.description: The proposed project would demolish the existing kitchen and restroom building east of Building C and replace it with a new 9,623-square-foot Multipurpose (MP) Building with a kitchen, along with an approximately 2,000-square-foot lunch canopy either west or south of the new MP Building. Additionally, five existing modular classroom buildings in the southern portion of the campus would be demolished and replaced in kind on existing asphalt with five new modular classroom buildings, each approximately 960 square feet and including a restroom. Site work would include new asphalt paving around the MP Building and a new 31-stall parking lot to the north to address existing parking shortages. The proposed project would also add new landscaping, softscaping, trees, and light poles. Construction is anticipated to take place from approximately June 2027 through July 2028.

ceqa-1849fe9583213baf80.name: Santa Ana Bus Base Hydrogen Fueling Replacement and Capacity Expansion Project
ceqa-1849fe9583213baf80.projectTitle: Santa Ana Bus Base Hydrogen Fueling Replacement and Capacity Expansion Project
ceqa-1849fe9583213baf80.description: The Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) will modernize the existing hydrogen fueling system at the Santa Ana Bus Base to support the agency’s growing fleet of zero-emission hydrogen fuel-cell electric buses. The project supports OCTA’s long-term transition to a 100% zero-emission bus fleet by 2040.

ceqa-1bc06f4980c55e9f02.name: Portola Reservoir Spillway Maintenance
ceqa-1bc06f4980c55e9f02.description: Nature of Project: Santa Margarita Water District (SMWD) will perform routine maintenance of the Portola Reservoir Spillway, consisting of vegetation and sediment removal along approximately 200 linear feet of the existing concrete V-ditch. Work will be limited to the district’s existing easement and to areas necessary to maintain proper spillway function. The spillway will remain operational throughout the maintenance activities. No new construction, expansion, or modification of the existing spillway facilities is proposed. All removed vegetation, sediment, and debris will be hauled offsite and disposed of at an appropriate facility. Purpose of Project: The purpose of the project is to maintain the Portola Reservoir spillway in a safe and functional condition by removing accumulated vegetation and sediment that could obstruct or reduce the conveyance capacity of the spillway. The work is part of SMWD’s regular reservoir maintenance program and is performed in accordance with maintenance requirements associated with the California Division of Safety of Dams (DSOD).Beneficiaries of Project: The project will benefit SMWD customers and the surrounding community by maintaining the safe and reliable operation of the Portola Reservoir and its spillway facilities. Routine maintenance helps preserve the drainage and overflow capacity of the spillway.

ceqa-c662f112aff5edb828.name: Building, Planning, Encroachment, and Grading Permit Fees
ceqa-c662f112aff5edb828.projectTitle: Building, Planning, Encroachment, and Grading Permit Fees
ceqa-c662f112aff5edb828.description: On August 19, 2026, the Laguna Woods City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-32 titled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LAGUNA WOODS, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING NEW AND INCREASED OR MODIFIED BUILDING AND PLANNING SERVICES FEES, AND ENCROACHMENT AND GRADING PERMIT FEES; AND DETERMINING AND CERTIFYING THAT THE RESOLUTION IS NOT SUBJECT TO THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT PURSUANT TO TITLE 14 OF THE CALIFORNIA CODE OF REGULATIONS The City adopted new building and planning services fee schedules, which will increase and modify the existing fees that the City charges to recover no more than the reasonable costs of providing building and planning review, permitting, inspection, and related activities and services. Building and planning services fees are charged to both public and private parties, as applicable, including, but not limited to, individuals, businesses, and homeowners’ associations, for a variety of purposes, projects, alterations, and improvements. The City adopted a new encroachment permit fee schedule, which will increase and modify the existing fees that the City charges to recover no more than the reasonable costs of providing review, permitting, and inspection of encroachments on public property/right-of-way, and related activities and services. Encroachment permit fees are charged to both public and private parties, as applicable, including, but not limited to, individuals, businesses, and homeowners’ associations when work or activities are to occur on public property/right-of-way. The City adopted a new grading permit fee schedule, which will increase and modify the existing fees that the City charges to recover no more than the reasonable costs of providing grading review, permitting, inspection, and related activities and services. Grading permit fees are charged to both public and private parties, as applicable, including, but not limited to, individuals, businesses, and homeowners’ associations for a variety of purposes, projects, and work (e.g., earthwork, excavation). The new fee schedules will take effect on October 19, 2026.

ceqa-876fcf8280b50343e1.name: Presidio at Pacific Park Residential Development Project

ceqa-876fcf8280b50343e1.description: The proposed project involves the demolition of a 41,519 square foot office building to construct a 58-unit, three-story, for-sale attached townhome community on approximately 4.4 acres. The development features three- and four-bedroom floor plans with enclosed garages, along with 24 guest parking spaces distributed throughout the site. The project will incorporate landscaped areas surrounding all buildings and along public streets, as well as amenities such as a dog play area, a community garden, a recreation/yoga lawn, and a barbeque area integrated across the site.

ceqa-5f5c18f6cda6743bc7.description: The proposed project approvals would facilitate the future redevelopment of the 92-acre project site, including the demolition and removal of existing oil and gas production infrastructure consistent with phaseout plans and the future construction of up to 800 residential units, up to 350 hotel rooms or other permitted visitor-serving uses, and various open space and park areas. Future buildout of the site would include new vehicular access points and internal circulation roadways, informational signage, utility and infrastructure connections, and multi-use paths. Under the proposed Palm/Goldenwest Specific Plan Amendment, the project site would be divided into three planning areas: Planning Area 1 (16 acres of Commercial Visitor uses), Planning Area 2 (53.2 acres of Medium Density Residential uses, which would be subdivided into Planning Areas 2A [30.8 acres] and 2B [22.4 acres]), and Planning Area 3 (22.8 acres of open space/park uses, which would be subdivided into Planning Area 3A [19.7 acres] and 3B [3.1 acres]). Project-specific design details for future residential and commercial development facilitated by approval of the proposed project are unknown at this time. Each future discretionary project facilitated by the proposed project would be subject to a project-specific CEQA review at the time it is proposed for consideration by the City. In order to streamline the process of future CEQA review, the proposed project conservatively analyzes a “worst-case” scenario of development, or the maximum allowable scale of future development allowed under applicable development standards as set forth in the Draft Amended Palm/Goldenwest Specific Plan.

ceqa-f6b29c1c8949cac74c.name: Auto Mall Digital Billboard
ceqa-f6b29c1c8949cac74c.projectTitle: Santa Ana Off- Premises Commercial Advertising Signs Ordinance Update Project
ceqa-f6b29c1c8949cac74c.description: Conditional Use Permit No. 2025-25 The project includes the reconstruction of an existing freeway-oriented, on-premise digital sign into a digital billboard with off-premise commercial advertising at 1505 S. Auto Mall Drive. The request also includes allowing the digital billboard to continue to exceed the maximum permitted height of 60 feet. The scope of work includes removing the existing digital screen and installing a two-sided, V-shape billboard with two 840-square-foot screens on either side. Additionally, the existing "Exit on Edinger" text will be removed. The adoption of Ordinance No. NS-3023 was accompanied by the adoption of the 2022 Santa Ana Off-Premises Commercial Advertising Signs Ordinance Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) (SCH No. 2022030204), as well as the adoption of a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP). The MND evaluated the potential environmental impacts associated with the implementation of digital billboard signage within designated allowable areas, referred to as "Potential Billboard Areas," where new digital display billboards are permitted. Due to the linear nature of the freeway corridors, the City was divided into six Potential Billboard Areas for purposes of environmental analysis. These areas are generally located along freeway frontages within 300 feet of the edge of pavement and are limited to non-residentially zoned properties, including areas governed by specific plans and specific development zoning districts. The ordinance further restricts billboard placement by prohibiting digital billboards within 500 feet of residentially zoned properties and within Caltrans right-of-way or designated landscaped freeway corridors. The subject site is located within Potential Billboard Area 4, one of the designated allowable areas evaluated in the MND. Accordingly, the MND analyzed the environmental setting, potential impacts, and applicable mitigation measures associated with digital billboard development in locations such as the subject site, and the MMRP was adopted to ensure implementation of those mitigation measures. In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and Section 15162 of the CEQA Guidelines, the Project is within the scope of the 2022 Santa Ana Off-Premises Commercial Advertising Signs Ordinance Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) (SCH No. 2022030204). The previously adopted MND adequately describes the Project's environmental setting, impacts, and mitigation measures. This is to advise that the City of Santa Ana (Lead Agency) has approved the above-described project on July 27, 2026, and made the following determination regarding the above-described project: 1. The project will not have a significant effect on the environment. 2. The Project is covered by a previously prepared Negative Declaration (SCH No. 2022030204) pursuant to the provisions of CEQA. 3. Mitigation measures were made a condition of the approval on the previous Negative Declaration (SCH No. 2022030204) and reaffirmed for this Project. 4. A mitigation reporting or monitoring plan was adopted for the previous Negative Declaration (SCH No. 2022030204) and is applicable to this Project. 5. A Statement of Overriding Considerations was not adopted for this Project. 6. Findings were not made pursuant to the provisions of CEQA. This is to certify that the final EIR with comments and responses and record of project approval, or the Negative Declaration, is available to the General Public at https://ceqanet.lci.ca.gov/2022030204

ceqa-72e4a574b009580a49.description: Site Plan Review (SPR) No. 2026-1-SPR, Density Bonus Agreement (DBA) No. 2026-1-WDV, Appeal (APPL) No. 2026-1-WDV The applicant and property owner propose to demolish office buildings and surface parking to construct a 7-story residential building with 274 dwelling units, including 14 affordable units (5%) for extremely low-income households. ceqa-1df2d8c16135175d37.name: Trabuco Ranger District Silverado Fuel Break Maintenance
ceqa-1df2d8c16135175d37.projectTitle: Trabuco Ranger District Silverado Fuel Break Maintenance
ceqa-1df2d8c16135175d37.description: The project goals are to reduce wildfire risk to life, property, and natural resources while enhancing forest health and biodiversity. Project activities include manual and mechanical fuel reduction activities and fuelbreak maintenance. These efforts are designed to restore the fuelbreaks effectiveness, complimenting maintenance recently done on the Riverside County portion of the fuelbreak. The project will treat 262 acres of an existing fuelbreaks footprint. CAL FIRE has provided funding toward the implementation of this project via Grant #8GG23601.

ceqa-0bd1e111c5b31f67d6.name: Deer Creek Preserve - SALT Anaheim
ceqa-0bd1e111c5b31f67d6.description: The Project Site is approximately 76.01 acres, located generally along E. Santa Ana Canyon Road, between Festival Drive and Eucalyptus Drive in Anaheim, California. The Project consists of a residential development of up to 359 units comprising of up to 299 single-family detached units and up to 60 units of Affordable Senior Citizen Housing Development (consisting of 59 deed-restricted lower-income senior units and one manager’s unit), along with related roadway, utility, and other improvements to serve the proposed residential uses. The affordable multifamily component would be restricted to qualifying senior households pursuant to applicable state law and implemented through the final affordability covenant, management, lease, and occupancy-control structure. Of the total units, up to 16.4% (59 units) are designated for lower-income households. The Project may include a potential (optional) recreation amenity center for the single-family residences on a lot that is up to 45,492 sq. ft. If the recreation amenity center is not built, passive open space shall take its place on the lot; in addition, the Project would incorporate passive amenity open spaces, gated entries, a guardhouse, monument signs, a water quality basin, and retaining walls. For a conservative, worst-case scenario analysis under CEQA, the Project’s analysis includes construction of the potential recreation amenity center. The Project application seeks approval of a Tentative Tract Map, Conditional Use Permit, and Specimen Tree Removal Permit. The Project Application was submitted as a Builder’s Remedy Housing Development Project pursuant to Government Code Section 65589.5 and the Housing Accountability Act. Per Government Code Section 65589.5(f)(6)(D)(i), the Project is not required to apply for, or receive approval of, a general plan amendment, specific plan amendment, rezoning, or other legislative approval. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Project remains subject to full environmental review under CEQA, including the identification and mitigation of all significant environmental effects.

ceqa-cf298f903c7df88348.description: A Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to allow a tutoring center, within a 1,200 square foot vacant tenant suite comprised of two tutoring rooms, a learning lab, work room, and restroom. The proposed tutoring facility would offer tutoring sessions in one- or two-hour blocks by appointment only. The Applicant has designed the facility to accommodate up to 12 students. The proposed hours of operation would be Monday through Friday, from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with the business closed on weekends. All tutoring activities would occur inside the tenant suite.

ceqa-15629e1b5e93dd135f.name: Interstate 5/El Toro Road Interchange Project
ceqa-15629e1b5e93dd135f.description: The project proposes to modify and improve the existing interchange between post miles (PMs) 17.8 and 19.7 within the cities of Lake Forest, Laguna Woods, and Laguna Hills in Orange County, California. The Project limits on Interstate 5 extend from approximately 0.2 mile south of the Los Alisos Boulevard overcrossing (PM 17.8) to approximately 0.2 mile south of the Lake Forest Drive overcrossing (PM 19.7), a distance of approximately 1.9 miles. Two Build Alternatives (Build Alternative 1: Southbound I-5 Hook Ramps, including design option 1a, Build Alternative 3: TSM and TDM) and the No-Build Alternative are being considered. The purpose of the proposed project is to improve traffic flow and traffic signal optimization, to improve traffic mobility at and through adjacent local street intersections, to reduce freeway ramp queuing, and apply technology to help manage traffic demand.

ceqa-dd532bfa08c91ffbb3.name: Fairview Developmental Center Specific Plan
ceqa-dd532bfa08c91ffbb3.description: The proposed project is a specific plan that would guide the development of a mixed-income, mixed-use community on a 95-acre portion of the former Fairview Developmental Center site, pursuant to the requirements of State Government Code Section 14670.31 and the City's Regional Housing Needs Allocation obligation for the site. The residential development would include a minimum of 2,300 dwelling units, 200 of which are required to be permanent supportive housing, with the potential for up to 4,000 units. 15 acres of the site would be developed by the State Department of Developmental Services for individuals with developmental disabilities. The commercial development will include up to 35,000 square feet of space, including but not limited to, retail, restaurants, coffee shops, fitness studios, and childcare facilities. At least 14 acres of publicly accessible open space will be provided as neighborhood parks, plazas, walking and biking trails, recreation centers, and picnic areas. The project would also result in off-site improvements, including the construction of a secondary access roadway through the adjacent golf course, requiring the reconfiguration of a minimum of six holes at the course, and a multi-use trail connecting the project site to Tanager Drive.

ceqa-7993c5337471f061b7.description: The proposed Caltrans District Directors Order (DDO) will remove and replace 47 non-bicycle grates at 20 locations on State Route 74 (SR-74) within unincorporated areas in Orange County. This work is needed to immediately restore functional use of the state facility. Work will be completed during the day to facilitate faster repairs on the highway. No saw cutting or new asphalt will be required. Removal and installation of grates would be administered by a small truck mounted boom. Disturbed soil area is anticipated to be less than 1.0 acre. The project has state funding. All work will occur in State right of way. No new right of way will occur. The public benefits.
