ceqa-7081417a66592aa0b1.name: Alexander Street Resurfacing Project
ceqa-7081417a66592aa0b1.description: The County of Riverside Transportation Department is proposing to resurface approximately 1.2 miles of Alexander Street from Cajalco Road to Markham Street. Alexander Street is classified as a secondary highway in the County of Riverside’s General Plan. Alexander Street is a two-lane road and currently ranges from 26-28 feet wide with asphalt concrete (AC) dike along various segments of the roadway. The proposed project will include removing the existing pavement, stabilizing the subgrade and placing Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA) concrete. A few segments of this project will be reconstructed to solve flooding issues within these areas. The proposed project will also include: • Resurfacing of roadway • Construct PCC dip section • Add AC/Conc driveway as needed • Adjusting all surface utilities to grade • Drainage improvements at selected areas • Re-Application of pavement striping • Removing and installing various signs and signposts as needed. • Reconstruct/construct AC/Conc driveway as needed • Reconstruction of existing mailboxes per USPS standards • Placement of safety edge and shoulder backing • Signal/Traffic light modification at Cajalco Road/Alexander Street intersection. No additional right-of-way or temporary construction easements (TCE) will be required to construct the proposed improvements. The project improvements will be within the existing footprint of the roadway and will raise the roadway profile. Work Order# D00064C Task Code #Z1530

ceqa-1fd237a6417651fc79.name: SBD/RIV WTI CCTV Replacement TMS/RWIS Stations Component Replacement, Census Secondary Work
ceqa-1fd237a6417651fc79.projectTitle: SBD/RIV WTI CCTV Replacement TMS/RWIS Stations Component Replacement, Census Secondary Work
ceqa-1fd237a6417651fc79.description: Caltrans proposes to replace cameras and station components of Traffic Management Systems (TMS) in poor condition at various locations; there are 7 locations in San Bernardino County and 3 locations in Riverside County. The purpose of this project is to enhance roadway safety and improve overall traffic operation. New cameras would connect to existing electrical connections and be located overhead, and other replacements would occur at cabinets located off the shoulders. There would be Driving/Parking off pavement, although no ground disturbance would occur. There would also be no need for equipment staging areas, and no utility relocations or connections to new infrastructure are anticipated. All work would be performed within Caltrans R/W. This project is funded by State funding.

ceqa-d2de06d9303142c8dd.description: Conditional Use Permit No. 190012 (CUP190012) is a proposal to construct a 125,781 square foot self-storage facility on a 6.98 gross acre lot. ceqa-a47661295d6ceca78b.name: Summer Villas Special Planning Area Project
ceqa-a47661295d6ceca78b.projectTitle: Summer Villas Special Planning Area Project
ceqa-a47661295d6ceca78b.description: The proposed project would require City approval of a General Plan/Rural Area Community Plan Amendment and a Rezone to allow for the creation of the 115.9-acre Summer Villas Special Planning Area (SPA). The Summer Villas SPA project contains three distinct sub-zones: 1) Active Adult Neighborhood (71.3 acres), 2) Laguna Creek Open Space (20.3 acres), and 3) Waterman Recreational Open Space (19.4 acres). It should be noted that the remaining five acres of the site would be dedicated to the Waterman Road and Sheldon Road right-of-way (ROW). In addition, subsequent potential development of the 115.9-acre site would include a maximum of 499 age-restricted single-family homes, as well as various associated improvements, such as a private community recreation center/clubhouse, private park space, trails and open space areas, landscaping, and a number of on- and off-site roadway and utility improvements.

ceqa-96e8980a3235805390.name: Jackson Bulk Substation Project
ceqa-96e8980a3235805390.description: The Project includes the construction of an approximately 18-acre bulk substation within a 44 acre parcel. The proposed substation would convert high voltage from 230,000-volt (230kV) transmission lines to 69,000-volt (69kV) through transformers for local distribution into residential and commercial customers along the Jackson Highway corridor. Key features of the new substation include installation of new electrical equipment, a control building, driveway access, site fencing, lighting, stormwater drainage, and utilities. SMUD will also grade the remaining 26 acres for drainage improvements and maintain temporary soil storage south of the substation footprint. The substation will retain a 200-foot setback from Jackson Road and Excelsior Road. The Project also includes construction of new or modified overhead power lines that would link the substation to the existing electrical grid. Planned overhead line improvements involve constructing approximately 0.7 miles of new 69kV overhead lines and converting approximately 5.35 miles of existing 12,000-volt (12kV) pole and overhead lines to single-circuit 69kV overhead lines with a 12kV underbuild.

ceqa-070dc2df24dcf19f61.projectTitle: Threemile Slough Pipeline Crossings Remediation and Decommissioning Project
ceqa-070dc2df24dcf19f61.description: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) is proposing the Threemile Slough Pipeline Crossings Remediation and Decommissioning Project (Project), which consists of four primary components: project area preparation and equipment mobilization, remediation of the active L-131Y and L-131Z pipelines within Threemile Slough, removal of the terrestrial and submarine portions of the previously abandoned L-131 East and West pipelines, and post-construction restoration of the Project area and demobilization activities. Long-term operations of the active L-131Y and L-131Z pipelines would not differ from existing conditions.

ceqa-89958434be6c463752.name: SMUD Transmission Line Steel Pole Recoating Project
ceqa-89958434be6c463752.projectTitle: SMUD Transmission Line Steel Pole Recoating Project
ceqa-89958434be6c463752.description: SMUD is proposing to recoat eight painted steel poles with nominal operational transmission line voltage of 115 kilovolt (kV) phase to phase. The heights of the poles are between 90 and 114 feet. The poles were originally installed in 2000 and are being recoated for maintenance and corrosion prevention and may require existing paint to be removed. The proposed project is not subject to Article 19, Section 15330 for "minor actions to prevent, minimize, stabilize, mitigate, or eliminate the release or threat of release of hazardous materials or substance," because the proposed action is not undertaken to address the potential release of paints containing hazard materials (metals), but rather to perform a traditional form of maintenance and prevent further corrosion of the existing poles. The effects of the paint removal and pole repainting on the environment have been evaluated indicating the project will comply with air quality and worker exposure regulations and will have no significant adverse effects on any other resources. One transmission pole requires all existing coating of this pole to be fully removed. The entire pole shaft and the cross arms bracket mounting area will be enclosed with scaffolding, wrapped, and all existing coating will be removed by sandblasting. For the initial refinishing of this pole, it will be necessary to remove all paint layers down to exposed steel to eliminate rust and ensure appropriate adhesion and life of the paint re-coating. All removed material will be captured with high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filter-equipped vacuum attachments. The material will be tested and if found to be hazardous, disposed of in a Class I controlled landfill. The remaining poles will be recoated with brushes and/or rollers. All coating and overcoat applications shall be done according to the paint manufacturer's recommendations. All work performed for the recoating will be done with the transmission lines de-energized. The pole locations are located directly adjacent to the RT Gold Line East Sacramento corridor. The trains will remain in operation with the use of flaggers who will work cooperatively with the pole maintenance crews. Maintenance will occur between the hours of 6 am and 6 pm Monday through Friday. The eight poles are owned by SMUD and six are located within the Sac RT right of way between Redding Avenue and 59th Street, Sacramento, CA. The eight poles will be recoated over approximately 4 weeks between mid-October and mid-November 2026. The painting contractors will comply with all environmental regulatory requirements by capturing dust generated during paint removal with HEPA-filtered vacuum attachments and employing Best Management Practices (BMPs) to control releases of paint particulates into the surrounding environment. These measures consist of laying a plastic tarp at the base of each tower to collect paint scrapings and collecting and labeling the worker clothing sent to the laundry. All contaminated wastes will be collected, sealed, and transferred to an appropriate Treatment Storage and/or Disposal Facility (TSDF). The plastic sheeting will be placed around the base of the poles at a distance of 20 feet out from the base of the poles. Additional sheeting will be used where there is the possibility of material entering storm drains or being transmitted onto adjacent properties.

ceqa-f1065c592866c6e82c.name: Dead Horse Cut Stream Gage Installation - CalSIP
ceqa-f1065c592866c6e82c.projectTitle: McCormack-Williamson Tract, Dead Horse Cut Stream Gage Installation Project
ceqa-f1065c592866c6e82c.description: As part of the California Stream Gage Improvement Program, the California Department of Water Resources has executed a contract with Reclamation District 2110 to install a stream gage on the east bank of Dead Horse Cut near the confluence with Snodgrass Slough. The stream gage equipment would be housed in a cabinet with solar panels and an antenna mounted to two 2" galvanized steel pipes anchored in the ground with concrete footings. The cabinet would be installed outside the channel along a private levee road (Dead Horse Island Road). A steel pipe conduit would be secured above ground and extend from the cabinet down the levee bank (rock slope) into the channel to a sonde transmitter and bubbler. The project would involve minor trenching and backfilling outside the channel in a previously disturbed area. No tree removal anticipated.

ceqa-003b892b91f8520978.description: The project consists of a Conditional Use Permit to allow an indoor recreational facility in the MP zoning district, located at 3999 N. Freeway Blvd., within the Natomas community.

ceqa-ed0f42e27ed3cfc49a.projectTitle: SAC 51 - PM 0.0/4.8 - 0.10' Cold Plane and RHMA-O
ceqa-ed0f42e27ed3cfc49a.description: The California Department of Transportation proposes a maintenance project to repair pavement along State Route 51 in Sacramento County from Post Mile 0 to 4.76.

ceqa-e808a93458e97bbfde.description: This project consists of a request for Site Plan and Design Review to add two additional models to Village 5 and remove model 2538 previously approved under DR24- I 54 for 229 single-unit dwellings within the Single-Unit Dwelling Zone (R-1-PUD) in the Delta Shores Planned Unit Development and Design Review Area. On June l 0, 2025, the City of Sacramento Community Development Department approved the Delta Shores East Village 3, 4, & 5 Project (DR24-154) for Site Plan and Design Review to construct 229 single-unit dwellings on individual lots of varying sizes consistent with FPM23-001 l, -00 l 9 & -0020, originally approved under P06-097. The proposed dwellings meet height. setback. and lot coverage requirements for the R-1 zone and Delta Shores PUD. On January 13, 2009, the Sacramento City Council certified an Environmental Impact Report and adopted the Findings of Fact and a Mitigation Monitoring Program for the Delta Shores (P06- l 97) project.

The 2,704-acre Project will construct and operate an approximately 200-megawatt alternating current photovoltaic solar energy generating facility and include an on-site substation, inverters, fencing, roads, and a supervisory control and data acquisition system (SCADA).

ceqa-2c3ceabcbe8cad3bc7.name: Trash Full Capture Projects (W14230102/W14230104)
ceqa-2c3ceabcbe8cad3bc7.description: The City of Sacramento is proposing to construct three full trash capture systems as part of the Trash Full Capture Project (project) within the greater Sacramento area to comply with the Central Valley Regional Water Board's (Water Board) requirements to prevent the discharge of trash greater than 5 mm into receiving waters through the implementation of certified Full Capture Systems. The three project sites were selected based on engineering, hydraulic. and trash capture feasibility analyses. They intend to provide full trash capture within the designated watersheds: Site 144 at the Interstate 80 (1-80) North Ditch approximately 170 feet east of the intersection of Phillipi Way and Rio Linda Boulevard. Site 151 located approximately 150 feet west of Exposition Parkway south of Slobe Avenue. and Site 157 at the 1-80 South Ditch approximately 700 feet east of Western Avenue The site improvements consist of the installation of a Water Board certified, manufacturer-prefabricated trash capture system at existing concrete lined stormwater channels.

ceqa-92b0b614b08cc68066.name: Freeport Regional Water Project - Golden Mussels
ceqa-92b0b614b08cc68066.projectTitle: Freeport Regional Water Project - Golden Mussels
ceqa-92b0b614b08cc68066.description: Sacramento County Water Agency (SCWA) proposes the authorization of copper compounds and other chemicals necessary at the intake of the Freeport Regional Water Project (FRWP) to treat and control golden mussels (Limnoperna fortunie), a newly identified threat to SCWA FRWP facilities following discovery within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta in 2024. Dense colonization (biofouling) of golden mussels can lead to blocked municipal and industrial water intakes and can result in diminished water quality. SCWA further proposes to amend the 2006 Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Agreement to include language that allows the use and storage of sodium hypochlorite and chemicals needed to combat golden mussels or other invasive species at the intake facilities.

ceqa-b234d8e1f0947fd349.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit Ordinance Repeal

ceqa-0436da961556577323.description: The 47-acre Project consists of constructing an auction sales lot. Grading the Project site will permanently impact approximately 3.82 acres of seasonal wetlands.

ceqa-8959d8951b863cae1c.projectTitle: Morrision Creek and Beach Lake Levee Resiliency Project

ceqa-20617c6a5fed590112.name: Hazel Strauch Elementary School Permanent Universal TK Building Project
ceqa-20617c6a5fed590112.projectTitle: Hazel Strauch Elementary School Permanent Universal TK Building Project
ceqa-20617c6a5fed590112.description: The proposed project will be developed on the southern boundary of the Hazel Strauch Elementary School campus. The area is currently occupied by 10 trees that will be removed. The proposed project would not require demolition of any existing buildings or structures. The proposed project would include the construction of a new transitional kindergarten (TK) building that will contain two new TK classrooms, restrooms, and a support room. The proposed project will accommodate an additional 40 students, representing a 9 percent increase in total campus capacity. Additionally, the proposed project would include surrounding hardscape and utility improvements, implementation of a new 20-foot fire access lane, and a new 80-foot roundabout adjacent to the new classroom building. Additionally, the proposed project will include surrounding hardscape and utility improvements. Construction of the proposed project will occur in one phase, beginning in winter 2027, and will be completed in fall 2027. Less than one acre of the project site would be disturbed during project construction.

ceqa-71b553ebf92d0ab56f.name: Garden Valley Elementary School Permanent Universal TK Building Project
ceqa-71b553ebf92d0ab56f.projectTitle: Garden Valley Elementary School Permanent Universal TK Building Project
ceqa-71b553ebf92d0ab56f.description: The proposed project will be developed on the southeastern corner of the Garden Valley Elementary School campus, along Larchwood Drive. The area is currently occupied by 24 trees that will be removed. The proposed project will not require demolition of any existing buildings or structures. The proposed project will include the construction of a new 4,331-square-foot transitional kindergarten (TK) building that will contain two new TK classrooms, a TK support room, three TK restrooms, one staff restroom, a storage room, and an electrical room. The proposed project will accommodate an additional 40 students, representing a 10 percent increase in total campus capacity. Additionally, the proposed project will include surrounding hardscape and improvements surrounding the new classroom building. New utility connections will serve the classroom building. A new playground will be constructed just north of the proposed classroom building, replacing an existing one. Construction of the proposed project will occur in one phase, beginning in winter 2027 and will be completed in fall 2027. Less than one acre of the project site would be disturbed during project construction.

ceqa-f6e64995aa5e57d2bf.projectTitle: Foothill Oaks Elementary School Permanent Universal TK Building Project
ceqa-f6e64995aa5e57d2bf.description: The proposed project will be developed on the northeastern corner of the Foothill Oaks Elementary School campus, along Lancelot Drive. The area is currently occupied by three existing trees, fencing, and playground equipment that will be removed. The proposed project will not require demolition of any existing buildings. The proposed project will include the construction of a new classroom building that will contain one new TK classroom, one TK restroom, and a utility room. The proposed project will accommodate an additional 24 students, representing a 5 percent increase in total campus capacity. Additionally, the proposed project will include surrounding hardscape and improvements surrounding the new classroom building. New utility connections will serve the classroom building. A new playground will be constructed just north of the proposed classroom building, replacing an existing one. Construction of the proposed project will occur in one phase, beginning in winter 2027 and will be completed in fall 2027. Less than one acre of the project site would be disturbed during project construction.

ceqa-83c5741058208cf176.name: 2025 ACM Reference Manual Update September 2026
ceqa-83c5741058208cf176.description: Public Resources Code, section 25402.1(e) directs the California Energy Commission (CEC) to certify an energy conservation manual for use by designers, builders, and contractors of residential and nonresidential buildings no later than 180 days after approval of the updates to Part 6 and Part 1 of Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations (Energy Code). To implement the requirement of section 25402.1(e), CEC staff developed an energy conservation manual that is comprised of several documents, including alternative calculation method reference manuals, compliance manuals, a data registry requirements manual, and other compliance documents, all of which contain information to assist designers, builders, and contractors in meeting the 2025 Energy Code, including forms, charts, and other data. The CEC developed updated content for the Alternative Calculation Method Reference Manual (ACM Reference Manual), which document the modeling methods used in the 2025 compliance software used to demonstrates performance compliance with the 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards. The CEC certified the ACM Reference Manual at the September 9, 2026, CEC Business Meeting.

ceqa-f9bbfbe1a2cb83c9f8.name: PLNP2024-00105 435 W. Delano Street Parcel Map
ceqa-f9bbfbe1a2cb83c9f8.projectTitle: PLNP2024-00105 435 W. Delano Street Parcel Map
ceqa-f9bbfbe1a2cb83c9f8.description: The proposed project consists of the division of a 5-acre (gross) lot into two residential parcels, consistent with the AR-2 (Agricultural-Residential) zoning designation. Parcel 1 will be approximately 2.8 acres (net) in size, while Parcel 2 will comprise approximately 2.0 acres (net). Both parcels are intended for residential use and will be served by individual private water wells and septic systems. Access to Parcel 2 will be provided via a proposed 20-foot-wide ingress/egress easement extending from Delano Street through Parcel 1. A fire department turnaround is proposed on Parcel 2 in accordance with Sacramento Metropolitan (SacMetro) Fire District standards. Additionally, a 10-foot-wide Public Utility Easement (PUE) is proposed along the project frontage to accommodate utility connections. Parcel 2 includes an approximately 1 .4-acre designated buildable area to support the development of a residential homestead and associated infrastructure. Each parcel will also include one shipping container for private storage. Existing accessory structures, such as sheds, will be either relocated or removed , and several trees are proposed for removal to facilitate the new parcel configuration. The proposed project consists of the following entitlements: 1. A Parcel Map to divide one 5-acre lot, zoned AR-2, into two new parcels, located at 435 W. Delano Street in the Rio Linda/Elverta community. 2. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).
ceqa-f9bbfbe1a2cb83c9f8.crossStreets: West Elverta Boulevard and Rio Linda Boulevard

ceqa-43924c6c48049151ee.projectTitle: CBH Warehouse and CUP Modification (Z20-102) & WeDrop (P19-065)
ceqa-43924c6c48049151ee.description: A request for 1) a Site Plan and Design Review to construct an 8,800 square-foot warehouse facility and site improvements and 2) a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) Minor Modification to allow volatile cannabis manufacturing within the existing building located on an approximately 1 .4-acre parcel within the Light Industrial (M-1-EA-3) zone and Executive Airport Overlay. ceqa-9ed7a66edb08da0787.name: Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing (P25-015)
ceqa-9ed7a66edb08da0787.description: The Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing Project includes the rezoning of the project site from EC-50-PUD to C-2, subdivision of the project site into seven parcels (totaling approximately 10.18 gross acres or 8.66 net acres), and the development of two new retail buildings and one new office building within the Development Area. The proposed buildings would be located on the western and southern portions of the Development Area, respectively, and would include associated parking lots and other associated site improvements. The approximately 7.32-acre Remaining Area would not include any development at this time. The two proposed retail buildings would each be approximately 6,300 gross square feet (sf) and the office building would be approximately 9,000 gross sf. The two retail buildings would be located southwest of the intersection of Truxel Road and Del Paso Road, and the office building would be located south of the existing office buildings at the existing business center. The proposed project would also provide additional parking, new trash can locations, new landscaping, and pedestrian circulation to connect the proposed buildings to the existing buildings. Site access would be provided through the existing internal roadways of the Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing business park, which includes an existing driveway off Del Paso Road to the north. The proposed project entitlements of a Rezone, an amendment to the Natomas Crossing Area 1 PUD, Tentative Subdivision Map, Site Plan and Design Review, and a Tree Permit were approved by City Council on September 15, 2026.

ceqa-f837f443443e49fbed.name: California Winter Rice Habitat Incentive Program
ceqa-f837f443443e49fbed.projectTitle: California Winter Rice Habitat Incentive Program
ceqa-f837f443443e49fbed.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Habitat Conservation Planning
ceqa-f837f443443e49fbed.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife (Headquarters), Habitat Conservation Planning Branch - Sacramento
ceqa-f837f443443e49fbed.description: The California Winter Rice Habitat Incentive Program (Project) incentivizes rice growers to flood harvested fields in the winter to benefit migrating and wintering waterbird. In partnership with the California Rice Commission, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife will oversee the administration of funds and implementation of the Project. Winter-flooding of harvest rice fields in the Central Valley provides approximately 75% of the energetic needs of dabbling ducks and a significant portion of the energetic needs of migrating shorebirds. Not only do these practices provide waterbird habitat, but they are also beneficial for landowners and improve California’s climate resiliency by recharging groundwater, allowing flexibility during drought scenarios, reducing flood risk, decomposing rice straw, and improving recreation benefits for rural communities.

ceqa-0a553040350aa82ecf.name: I Street Bridge Replacement (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2023-061-02 (ITP))
ceqa-0a553040350aa82ecf.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2023-061-02, pursuant to section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, the City of Sacramento. The project involves the construction of a new bridge over the Sacramento River between the cities of Sacramento and West Sacramento to replace the vehicle crossing that is currently provided by the existing I Street Bridge located just south. The new bridge will cross the Sacramento River between the Sacramento Railyards at Railyards Boulevard and the West Sacramento Washington planned developments at C Street and provide a new bicycle, pedestrian, and automobile crossing. The structure will be a movable bridge (vertical lift) that satisfies the vertical clearance and river navigation requirements.

ceqa-e234ae36f862250496.name: Rancho Cordova 2050 General Plan
ceqa-e234ae36f862250496.description: The project would update the existing 2006 General Plan to reflect the City’s past accomplishments, adopted plans and initiatives, and new priorities. The project would modify goals, policies, and implementation programs and update the General Plan land use diagram.

ceqa-fd6b8e449155a64d43.name: Clover Apartments Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-070-02 (ITP))
ceqa-fd6b8e449155a64d43.description: The Project includes the development of 11.31 acres of undeveloped land into a 348-unit affordable housing project composing of eleven residential buildings, bicycle and vehicle parking spaces, a large community clubhouse, pool, barbeques, two and outdoor community and recreational areas. A six-foot iron bar fence will be installed along the eastern property line, a six-foot masonry wall will be constructed along the western property line, and six-foot-tall fences and tall shrubs will be planted along the northern and southern sides of Ellwood Avenue and the eastern and western sides of Wainscott Way. The Project will result in impacts to 11.31 acres of western burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia) habitat; the Project will permanently remove 11.31 acres of western burrowing owl nesting and foraging habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of western burrowing owl, which is/are designated as a candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-7f412a8aa9a0ae4b03.name: I-5 Grade Raise Project
ceqa-7f412a8aa9a0ae4b03.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes the I-5 Grade Raise Project. The project is located on Interstate 5 (I-5) in Sacramento County, between Post Miles 0.21 and 4.63. The total length of the project is 4.42 miles. Within the limits of the proposed project, I-5 is a four-lane highway. This project was programmed for Pavement Rehabilitation. The purpose of this project is to restore and improve the existing pavement condition and extend the life of transportation infrastructure. The project aims to preserve and sustain the I-5 corridor and its structures, while enhancing safety, reliability, rideability, and existing drainage systems.

ceqa-00cda65deaf59a52bb.name: Surgery & Emergency Services Pavilion (SESP) Chem Line Lab Remodel and Equipment Replacement
ceqa-00cda65deaf59a52bb.projectTitle: Surgery & Emergency Services Pavilion (SESP) Chem Line Lab Remodel and Equipment Replacement
ceqa-00cda65deaf59a52bb.description: UC Davis Health proposes to renovate an existing lab space in the Main Hospital Surgery and Emergency Services Pavilion (SESP). The project will replace aging lab equipment with new equipment, including analyzers, lab benches, and workstations. The project will also upgrade the deionized water connections, IT cabling and systems to support the room, electrical system improvements; HVAC repairs, and modifications to the restroom to meet ADA restroom requirements. The project is a renovation of exiting space at the hospital that will result in negligible or no expansion of existing use.

ceqa-afd6333efeb8b929c7.name: PLER2025-00142 Aquifer Storage and Recovery Project Vineyard Surface Water Treatment Plant
ceqa-afd6333efeb8b929c7.projectTitle: PLER2025-00142 Aquifer Storage and Recovery Project Vineyard Surface Water Treatment Plant
ceqa-afd6333efeb8b929c7.description: Sacramento County Water Agency (SCWA) proposes to convert an inactive supply well (PW-1) at the Vineyard Surface Water Treatment Plant into an Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) well and construct associated conveyance pipelines. The work includes installing a permanent 100-horsepower pump, electrical controls, and 12-inch piping and valves connecting to the existing potable water system. SCWA also plans four future ASR wells, associated pipelines, and the conversion of three active Excelsior supply wells to ASR. ASR implementation would involve removing the existing pump, performing pre- and post-rehabilitation downhole video surveys, cleaning the well screen and filter pack to remove scaling, biomatter, and sediment, and reinstalling the pump with an ASR valve. The existing above-ground pipeline would be reconfigured to include a backflushing loop.
ceqa-afd6333efeb8b929c7.crossStreets: Florin Road, Knox Road, Excelsior Road

ceqa-226696754d780586fb.description: The proposed project includes modernization of the existing Earl Warren Elementary School (see Figure 1). All construction activities will occur within the existing disturbed areas of the campus. The proposed project would include the following: - Removal of 14 existing modular structures; - Construction of a new14,124-square-foot building for TK and Kindergarten classrooms and a new administration office wing; - Interior classroom modernization improvements; - Construction of new pick-up and drop-offs areas along 73rd Street; - Construction of new staff parking lot at the northeast corner of the campus; - Existing parking lot and pick-up/drop-off area along Lowell Street would be reconfigured for bus drop-off and fire access, and the parking lot would remain in place but would be re-striped; - New landscaping and concrete installed throughout the school site; and - Replacement of the play area with a newly designed play area and separate TK and Kindergarten play area. The proposed project would serve the existing student enrollment and would not result in an increase in student or program capacity, nor would the project result in an increase of employees at the project site. In addition, all construction activities would take place on campus.

ceqa-b50ac057ff455a7478.name: Rio Americano High School Stadium Improvements Project

ceqa-b50ac057ff455a7478.description: The proposed project consists of improvements to the existing Rio Americano facilities, including installation of new high-mast light standards, removal of existing bleachers and installation of new and expanded bleacher seating, an upgraded public address system, and a new press box. New light standards would also be installed along the existing paved fire lane between the stadium and the main campus parking lot to provide pedestrian safety. The high-mast light standards would be installed to light the field, and would replace the current field lighting provided by portable diesel- powered lights. The project proposes four light standards, two on each side of the field (north and south), and each 80 feet tall. Six new 15-foot-tall light poles would be installed between the south end of the existing main parking lot and the field, along the paved fire lane, for pedestrian safety. New bleacher seating on the north and south sides of the stadium would accommodate up to approximately 2,575 people. A new press box would also be installed atop and central to the bleacher seating on the south (home side) of the stadium. Two existing Sacramento Metropolitan Utility District (SMUD) wood light poles within the campus fire lane (used for pedestrian ingress and egress) would be removed.

ceqa-5bd360ee9d13bbf006.name: PLNP2023-00206 Design Review Administration Update
ceqa-5bd360ee9d13bbf006.description: The project consists of a Zoning Ordinance Amendment (ZOB) to amend Chapter 6 of the Sacramento County Zoning Code (Zoning Code) and Chapter 1 or the Countywide Design Guidelines. The proposed amendments generally fall under the four topics found below: • Simplify Zoning Code Section 6.3 and the Countywide Design Guidelines have been reorganized and simplified to provide clarity while navigating the administrative requirements of the Design Review Program. • Exceptions The list of exceptions in Zoning Code Section 6.3 is proposed to be expanded to narrow the scope of projects that would require Design Review. • Levels of Review The levels of Design Review have been amended to ensure consistency between discretionary and non-discretionary projects. • Approving Authority Roles The proposed amendment further defines and restructures the role of the Design Review Administrator (ORA) and the Design Review Advisory Committee (DRAC). The proposed amendments generally fall under the three categories found below: 1) Minor Clarifications - Proposed changes to the Zoning Code and Countywide Design Guidelines that result in short text amendments that are of minor consequence. These changes fix typographical errors, codify accepted staff practice, codify minor Planning Director's interpretations, and generally do not represent changes from existing practices. 2) Major Clarifications - Proposed changes to the Zoning Code and the Countywide Design Guidelines that result in text amendments that are longer or affect more frequently used procedures than those specified in "1 ". These changes solidify interpretations of standards but are still generally not major changes from existing practices. These changes do not result in intensification of land use compared to uses already permitted by right within respective affected zoning districts. 3) Minor Policy Updates - Proposed changes to the Zoning Code that result in policy changes to procedures that are of relatively minor consequence. This involves minor changes to sections of the Zoning Code that are used somewhat frequently or major changes, up to complete elimination, of outdated or obsolete sections of the Code. This also includes the codification of informal historical policies that are generally noncontroversial.

ceqa-ecb7aa762c91eb620f.description: Approval of Permit No. 15045-1, under California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Article 3, Section 6, for work within an adopted plan of flood control: To relocate an existing sewer line. The project will remove approximately 270 feet of an existing 6-inch sewer pipe that runs parallel to the levee, approximately 20 feet from the landside levee toe, and approximately 100 feet of an existing 3-inch sewer pipe that runs perpendicular to the levee at 1577 Garden Highway, authorized under Board Permit No. 15045. The new sewer line will consist of a 4-inch-diameter American Water Works Association (AWWA) C200 steel pipe. The new pipe will run westward, parallel to the levee along the waterside shoulder, for approximately 220 feet before crossing the levee for approximately 106 feet and connecting to an existing manhole located on the landside, outside of the levee section. The pipe invert will be above the 200-year Water Surface Elevation (36.37 feet, NAVD88) and will have 4 feet of cover beneath the levee crown. On the waterside, the pipe will extend an additional approximately 17 feet at an angle to the levee alignment before connecting to the existing 3-inch force main. The project also includes a new 4-inch gate valve, a new 1-inch air release valve, a 4-inch by 3-inch reducer, and three (3) WYE fittings with cleanouts. This permit, including its conditions, supersedes Permit No. 15045 GM that was issued to Laraine C. Patching of Virgin Sturgeon to install a 6-inch diameter sewer along the landside of the levee and through the left bank of the levee of the Sacramento River

ceqa-56ca1e50c49036daa7.name: Carli Expansion Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-56ca1e50c49036daa7.description: In 2020, the County Board of Supervisors approved a request for Triangle Rock Products, LLC (Applicant) to amend their existing Use Permit to expand mining operations at their Sacramento Aggregates Facility by an additional 161 acres. The expansion proposal was known as Carli Expansion (Carli Expansion, County Control Number PLNP2017-00243). As set forth in the conditions of approval for the Sacramento Aggregate Facility, mining activities will cease on February 5, 2033, and reclamation shall be completed by February 5, 2035, with monitoring continuing until February 5, 2040. The Carli Expansion proposal did not change the rate of processing or rate of production of the permitted Sacramento Aggregates Facility and is expected to have the same closeout date as the previously approved use permits. Of the 161-acre Carli Expansion area, there was an approximate 11-acre area that was to be excluded from mining activities due to the presence of wetland features. The applicant is now requesting to amend the Carli Expansion Use Permit and Reclamation Plan to include mining activities and operations on the previously avoided 11-acre site (a portion of APN 067-0120-073). The proposed Carli Expansion Amendment (i.e., proposed project), to now include the 11-acre parcel, would not change the operations of the mine, the daily amounts for mined materials, nor change the expected dates for closeout and reclamation. Requested entitlements include the following: 1. An Amendment to a Use Permit (PLNP2017-00243) to allow expansion of surface mining onto an additional 11 acres, within the previously approved expansion area. 2. An Amendment to the Reclamation Plan to include the expanded mining area. The end use of open space and dry grazing of the Reclamation Plan will remain unchanged. 3. A Development Agreement Amendment between the Applicant and the County of Sacramento. CONTROL NUMBER: PLNP2025-00130

ceqa-9f4e9d96758dde9cfa.name: Emergency Exit Pathway Installation
ceqa-9f4e9d96758dde9cfa.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-9f4e9d96758dde9cfa.description: The goal of this project is to upgrade an existing emergency fire exit egress at the California State Railroad Museum to an ADA compliant emergency fire exit egress to comply with fire and accessibility code. Project will: • Remove twelve (12) existing 2-ft x 2-ft concrete pads; • Excavate soil up to 6-in. deep; • Install approx. 90-ft of 4-in. x 6-in. redwood lumber pinned down with 2-ft long 5/8-in. rebar; and • Install decomposed granite over a compacted Class A road base.

ceqa-5c08525c0542fb91d2.name: Elk Grove Subaru Amendment (PLNG26-028)
ceqa-5c08525c0542fb91d2.description: The Elk Grove Subaru Amendment Project (the “Project”) consists of a Major Design Review Amendment for a new ±56,159 square-foot automobile dealership with associated site improvements including landscaping, parking, and lighting located within the Elk Grove Auto Mall. The Project shall comply with the City’s Climate Compass for new non-residential development, including measures related to renewable energy (BE-3), active transportation (TR-1), construction emissions (TR-3), and electric vehicle supply equipment (TR-2).

ceqa-c3d940c4eea4b60150.name: Issuance of General Lease – Public Agency Use
ceqa-c3d940c4eea4b60150.projectTitle: Issuance of General Lease – Public Agency Use
ceqa-c3d940c4eea4b60150.description: Authorize issuance of a General Lease – Public Agency Use, beginning August 25, 2026, for a term of 20 years, for the use of an existing concrete deck over a wood-framed and pile-supported dock, building, boat dock, and gangway.

ceqa-076ba772bb386d3754.name: Elkhorn Booster Pump Station and Pipeline (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-66489-R2)
ceqa-076ba772bb386d3754.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-66489-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Natomas Mutual Water Company. The project is limited to the conversion of approximately 2.56 miles of open irrigation canals and laterals in the Elkhorn service area to buried pipelines and the construction of a booster pump station.

ceqa-38e27295a2acbb7a99.name: Issuance of General Lease – Recreational Use – Lease 7694
ceqa-38e27295a2acbb7a99.projectTitle: Issuance of General Lease – Recreational Use – Lease 7694
ceqa-38e27295a2acbb7a99.description: Authorize issuance of a General Lease – Recreational Use beginning April 1, 2026, for a term of 10 years, for the use of an existing boat dock and appurtenant facilities.

ceqa-1fdef5fcbeb69a0baa.name: Warren Park Restroom Replacement (L19913200)
ceqa-1fdef5fcbeb69a0baa.description: The project consists of demolishing an existing restroom and installing a new prefabricated single-stall, all-gender restroom facility at Earl Warren Park. The project also involves new water, sewer, and electrical connections, associated concrete flatwork and walkway improvements, turf and irrigation adjustments, installation of new landscaping and trees, and installation of updated park rules signage.

ceqa-6c6e1e96d8824d0fff.name: Burberry Park Restroom (L19109600)
ceqa-6c6e1e96d8824d0fff.description: The project would install a prefabricated two-stall restroom facility at Burberry Community Park. The project work also includes improvements to water lines and utilities connections, walkways, the soccer field turf, irrigation system, and installation of updated park rules signage.

ceqa-9ae03c95d69436edc4.name: UCDH Skyline Signage Replacement
ceqa-9ae03c95d69436edc4.description: UC Davis Health proposes to replace the existing skyline signage on Davis Tower at the Main Hospital at the Sacramento Campus. The project will remove the existing illuminated letters on the west side of the Davis Tower that read “UC Davis Children’s Hospital” and replace them with new signage that read “UC Davis Health”. The new sign letters will be approximately seven feet tall and halo illuminated with LED lights that are 7100 K temperature. The LED lights will be installed with a dimmer and timer option. The project will also remove the existing skyline signage on the north side of the Davis that reads “UC Medical Center”. This sign will not be replaced at this time.

ceqa-8f914e7be450b1ab11.name: SAC 104 Replace Corrugated Metal Pipe (EA 03-3N000)
ceqa-8f914e7be450b1ab11.description: California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes removing the failed corrugated metal pipe (CMP) culvert and replace with new reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) culvert, install headwall and flared end section, soil excavation, backfill, traffic control, and incidental work on State Route 104 in Sacramento County.

ceqa-c0b58994bee1d9b739.name: Light Rail Station LED Lighting Upgrades
ceqa-c0b58994bee1d9b739.projectTitle: Light Rail Station LED Lighting Upgrades
ceqa-c0b58994bee1d9b739.description: The project includes replacing deteriorated light fixtures, installing new fixtures to provide additional illumination, upgrading electrical writing (if needed), and transitioning sites to energy-efficient LED lighting. Benefits include reduction of lighting systems’ energy demand, and the safety and security of passengers.
ceqa-c0b58994bee1d9b739.crossStreets: Light Rail Stations and Park-and-Ride Lots

ceqa-60fe62518429a4a716.name: Office of Information Services New Leased Space Sacramento
ceqa-60fe62518429a4a716.projectTitle: Office of Information Services New Leased Space Sacramento
ceqa-60fe62518429a4a716.description: The Department of Industrial Relations, Office of Information Services (OIS) needs new office space in Sacramento, CA to accommodate an increase in staff. OIS expects to house 236 employees and needs parking for two state-owned vehicles. OIS is currently located at 2180 Harvard Street, Suite 160, in Sacramento, but there is no space for their team to renew their current lease.

ceqa-25680b35463aa2fe26.name: Georgiana Slough Erosion Control and Habitat Enhancement Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SAC-50748-R3)
ceqa-25680b35463aa2fe26.projectTitle: GEORGIANA SLOUGH EROSION CONTROL AND HABITAT ENHANCEMENT PROJECT
ceqa-25680b35463aa2fe26.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (EPIMS-SAC-50748-R3), pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, the project Applicant, Brannan-Andrus Levee Maintenance District (BALMD). The project is a multi-benefit levee erosion control/habitat enhancement project limited to one site at Georgiana Slough between levee stations 291+00 and 305+00. The work consists of mobilization, site preparation, levee slope and wetland bench construction, installation and maintenance of plants, and site demobilization.

ceqa-cc2ad43c35c2a019ad.name: Richards Boulevard Drainage Improvements Project
ceqa-cc2ad43c35c2a019ad.description: The project would improve transportation and reduce flooding in the Basin 111 around Richards Boulevard between Sequoia Pacific Boulevard and North 5th Street. The project would include the installation of 700 linear feet of 54-inch Drainage pipe on Richards Boulevard, between Sequoia Pacific Boulevard and North 5th Street. The project would require that PG&E relocate 400 linear feet of gas main two feet over from its existing location within the existing right-of-way to accommodate the new drainage pipe. The scope would include excavation, installation of 36-inch pipe, dual 42-pipes, manholes, junction structures, backfill, and roadway surfacing.

ceqa-d765a437284a56d545.name: Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing (P25-015)
ceqa-d765a437284a56d545.description: The Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing Project includes the rezoning of the project site from EC-50-PUD to C-2, subdivision of the project site into seven parcels (totaling approximately 10.18 gross acres or 8.66 net acres), and the development of two new retail buildings and one new office building within the Development Area. The proposed buildings would be located on the western and southern portions of the Development Area, respectively, and would include associated parking lots and other associated site improvements. The approximately 7.32-acre Remaining Area would not include any development at this time. The two proposed retail buildings would each be approximately 6,300 gross square feet (sf) and the office building would be approximately 9,000 gross sf. The two retail buildings would be located southwest of the intersection of Truxel Road and Del Paso Road, and the office building would be located south of the existing office buildings at the existing business center. The proposed project would also provide additional parking, new trash can locations, new landscaping, and pedestrian circulation to connect the proposed buildings to the existing buildings. Site access would be provided through the existing internal roadways of the Centerpointe at Natomas Crossing business park, which includes an existing driveway off Del Paso Road to the north. The proposed project would require City approval of a Rezone, an amendment to the Natomas Crossing Area 1 PUD, Tentative Subdivision Map, Site Plan and Design Review, and a Tree Permit.

ceqa-b12230daf6e45e98ad.name: Pocket Substation Rebuild Project
ceqa-b12230daf6e45e98ad.description: SMUD proposes to construct and operate a new 230 kV substation that would replace the existing Pocket Substation. The proposed substation would convert or “step down” voltage from 230kV transmission lines to 69 kV subtransmission voltage through transformers and supporting equipment to safely reduce transmission voltages for local distribution. The new substation would be located immediately north of the existing Pocket Substation across Gardendale Road on a vacant parcel that is owned by SMUD. In addition, five new transmission poles would be installed, and four existing transmission poles would be repainted or replaced. Finally, the project would include installation and reconstruction of electrical lines to tie the proposed substation into the existing grid.
ceqa-b12230daf6e45e98ad.developmentType: Other (Transmission Poles and Powerlines), Power:Other Power Type (Substation)(Megawatts 230)

ceqa-2df3bc80ea15589e73.name: Raising Cane’s Restaurant
ceqa-2df3bc80ea15589e73.description: The proposed project consists of a 3,301-square-foot Raising Cane’s restaurant building and associated paving, drive-thru, outdoor eating area, parking lot, landscaping, lighting, waste enclosure, and site improvements on an undeveloped 1.34-acre pad within the Broadstone Pointe Shopping Center.

ceqa-5a51504cef360b5d56.name: FLB Entertainment Center Expansion
ceqa-5a51504cef360b5d56.description: The proposed project consists of a remodel and addition to the existing FLB Entertainment Center building. The project includes an upgraded building façade, a new outdoor entertainment area, patio and table seating, a new outdoor children's recreation area, a new restaurant kitchen and indoor dining room, two new party rooms, a new amusement arcade, an expanded parking lot, and new landscaping. The applicant also proposes live entertainment as an incidental use.

ceqa-7f1035634a85cd96fe.name: United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) Transit Storage Project (P26-002)
ceqa-7f1035634a85cd96fe.description: This project requests a Conditional Use Permit to establish a Transit Vehicle-service. repair, storage and Site Plan and Design Review for the development of 72 bus/van parking stalls, and associated site improvements on a 5.44-acre parcel in the Office Building (OB) zone. The development of the 72 parking stalls would be located at the southern 1.3-acre portion of the existing parcel. Site improvements consist of the addition of 72 paved parking stalls. paved drive aisles, additional lighting, additional drainage capacity. landscaping improvements, and the installation of a 6.000 gallon above-ground fueling tank.

ceqa-39729524ab5c34f8bb.name: J and P LLC (Project)
ceqa-39729524ab5c34f8bb.description: The project is located at 1700 Kathleen Avenue, Sacramento California on APN 265-0401-015-0000. This project was issued a Conditional Use Permit (Z17-106) to operate a cannabis cultivation facility within an existing 6,000 square feet commercial building on a 0.41 acre parcel in the Light Industrial (M-1) zone. The building was previously used for cannabis cultivation, and this project will not expand on the previous use. Water is provided by the City of Sacramento Department of Utilities and electricity is provided by SMUD.

ceqa-240d2d641c913e6ffa.name: Johnson Cosumnes Floodplain Restoration (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-59964-R2)
ceqa-240d2d641c913e6ffa.projectTitle: Johnson Cosumnes Mitigation Bank Floodplain Restoration Project
ceqa-240d2d641c913e6ffa.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-240d2d641c913e6ffa.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-240d2d641c913e6ffa.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-59964-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Westervelt Ecological Services, LLC. The project will preserve and restore approximately 204 acres of wetland, riparian, and riverine, notching stream banks to restore hydrologic connectivity with the Cosumnes River and Laguna Creek. The project will grade and contour existing agricultural fields to connect approximately 4,400 linear feet of pilot channels and swales to restore and promote topographic complexity associated with floodplain wetland and riparian habitats. The project will plant native wetland and riparian plant species to encourage native plant recruitment.

ceqa-ff088a77a5845fe738.name: Laguna Springs-Sirroco 12kV Extension (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-64615-R2)
ceqa-ff088a77a5845fe738.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-ff088a77a5845fe738.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-ff088a77a5845fe738.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-64615 -R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Sacramento Municipal Utility District. The project is limited to the installation of an approximately new 350-foot 12kV utility cable within conduit below Elk Grove/Laguna Creek by horizontal directional drilling. Impacts to bed, bank, channel, and riparian habitats are not anticipated.

ceqa-0a2fd7a3a32c5b380b.name: NORTH WATT AVENUE SPECIFIC PLAN
ceqa-0a2fd7a3a32c5b380b.description: The North Watt Avenue Specific Plan (Specific Plan) encompasses approximately 705 acres along a 4-mile segment of Watt Avenue, north of Interstate-80 (I-80) to Antelope Road/U Street, within unincorporated Sacramento County. The Specific Plan proposes three zoning districts, each with its own established allowable land uses and development and design standards. The zoning districts would allow a mix of residential and commercial retail and service uses, industrial uses and compatible uses focused south of the Union Pacific Railroad main line, and parks and open space areas. The Specific Plan also identifies the water, sewer, drainage, and stormwater infrastructure investments required to support infill development within the corridor and transportation improvements needed to ensure multi-modal access for residents, employees, and visitors.
ceqa-0a2fd7a3a32c5b380b.crossStreets: Watt Avenue and James Way/A Street 95660

ceqa-8d11cb77809275411e.name: Fox Park Well Hexavalent Chromium Treatment-Water Supply Permit Amendment (Project)
ceqa-8d11cb77809275411e.projectTitle: Fox Park Well Hexavalent Chromium Treatment-Water Supply Permit Amendment (Project)
ceqa-8d11cb77809275411e.description: The Applicant proposes installation and operation of a skid mounted strong base ion exchange treatment system for removal of hexavalent chromium from the drinking water at the Fox Park Court Well. The proposed treatment will be used in conjunction with the existing well and chlorination system.
ceqa-8d11cb77809275411e.crossStreets: 8623 Fox Park Ct. and Redwater Dr.

ceqa-912f4ff08d8c4fcfe0.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-912f4ff08d8c4fcfe0.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova

The project is limited to the installation of an approximately new 350-foot 12kV utility cable within conduit below Elk Grove/Laguna Creek by horizontal directional drilling. Impacts to bed, bank, channel, and riparian habitats are not anticipated.

ceqa-af739061885371cf35.name: Arcadian State Route 160 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-0283)
ceqa-af739061885371cf35.projectTitle: Arcadian State Route 160 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-0283)
ceqa-af739061885371cf35.description: Arcadian, in coordination with the California Department of Technology and the California Department of Transportation, proposes to install underground broadband infrastructure consisting of conduit, fiber optic cable, vaults, and markers on SR 160 between PM 1.3 and PM 10.753 in Sacramento County.

ceqa-740c8e98bf6494a293.name: Arcadian Interstate 5 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-2290
ceqa-740c8e98bf6494a293.projectTitle: Arcadian Interstate 5 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-2290
ceqa-740c8e98bf6494a293.description: Arcadian, in coordination with the California Department of Technology and the California Department of Transportation, proposes to install broadband infrastructure, consisting of conduit and fiber optic cable on structures on I-5 between PM 1.031 and PM 1.238, PM 4.642 and PM 4.694, PM 8.1 and PM 8.126, PM 12.80 and PM 13.10, and PM 0.052 in Sacramento County. This project is associated with the linear broadband installation approved in Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-0290.

ceqa-245c0a3c7dd5e25ba7.name: Chabad Community Center (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-65120-R2)
ceqa-245c0a3c7dd5e25ba7.projectTitle: Chabad Community Center (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-65120-R2)
ceqa-245c0a3c7dd5e25ba7.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-245c0a3c7dd5e25ba7.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-245c0a3c7dd5e25ba7.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-65120-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Chabad Jewish Community Center. The project is limited to the construction of a new 23,485-square-foot community center, an associated parking lot, and a fence on a 2.17-acre site. Construction of the community center (4,607 square feet) and the associated parking lot (3,619 square feet) involves the removal of the existing residence, removal of 6 riparian trees, and grading and paving outside of the bank of Willow Creek. The riparian trees range from dead to fair health, and their removal may involve excavation of the roots or leaving the stump.

ceqa-fdae924b611e4bdb5f.name: Ordinance No. 1375 - An Ordinance of the City of Folsom Re-Adopting Ordinance 1353 To Amend Chapter 17.52 of the Folsom Municipal Code for the Historic District
ceqa-fdae924b611e4bdb5f.projectTitle: Ordinance No. 1375 - An Ordinance of the City of Folsom Re-Adopting Ordinance 1353 To Amend Chapter 17.52 of the Folsom Municipal Code for the Historic District
ceqa-fdae924b611e4bdb5f.description: Re-adopting updates to the Folsom Municipal Code Chapter 17 (Historic District) relating to development standards and level of review for Design Review, Sign Permits, Demolitions, and accessory buildings.
ceqa-fdae924b611e4bdb5f.crossStreets: Bidwell St. Stafford St., River Way, Leidesdorff St., American River

ceqa-9e6ff340fdd5320589.agency: California Military Department - Office of the Adjutant General
ceqa-9e6ff340fdd5320589.agencyName: California Military Department - Office of the Adjutant General

ceqa-6073a34b4c42d0fc73.name: Johnny Cash Art Experience
ceqa-6073a34b4c42d0fc73.description: The Johnny Cash Trail Art Experience is in the northern portion of the City of Folsom in northeastern Sacramento County. The installation of eight art sites is proposed, and art sites one through four are located along East Natoma Street between Randall Drive and Folsom Lake Crossing. Art sites five through eight are located behind the Folsom Zoo and Dan Russell Rodeo Arena, along Leidesdorff Street, and terminate at Greenback Lane. The southern half of the project area is located in un-sectioned lands of the Rancho "Rio de los Americanos" land grant and the northern half of the project area is located in Section 30, Township 10 North, Range 8 East (Mount Diablo Base and Meridian, United States Geological Survey 7.5 minute "Folsom Quadrangle").
ceqa-6073a34b4c42d0fc73.crossStreets: Folsom Lake Crossing; East Natoma Street; Leidesdorff

ceqa-ac9710e3bd6ecc2c32.name: Vineyard South Mine Expansion (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-64369-R2)
ceqa-ac9710e3bd6ecc2c32.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-64369-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Granite Construction Company. The project is limited to the surface mining of a 38.65-acre parcel (Phase 2B) of the Vineyard South Mine. Approximately two-thirds of the parcel (25.77 acres) will be mined with the remainder left undisturbed or reserved for alternative uses. After mining is completed, the parcel will continue to be open space (suitable for dryland grazing) and/or non-prime agriculture. No in-water work will be required for the project; construction activity will occur while the existing drainages are dry. There will be no work on the Elder Creek channel, and no riparian trees will be removed.

ceqa-e3cb4ad6086a235ddf.name: Laguna Creek Inter-Regional Trail Crossing at State Route 99 (WTL016) Project
ceqa-e3cb4ad6086a235ddf.projectTitle: Laguna Creek Inter-Regional Trail Crossing at State Route 99 Project (WTL016)
ceqa-e3cb4ad6086a235ddf.description: The Project will construct the final segment of the City of Elk Grove’s Laguna Creek Inter-Regional Trail (LCIRT). The final segment of the trail will include a pedestrian overcrossing spanning West Stockton Boulevard, State Route 99, and East Stockton Boulevard; a multi-use trail east of the pedestrian overcrossing; and a pedestrian bridge spanning Whitehouse Creek.

ceqa-0761f710a73bf5783f.name: HM-4 TMS Detection Technology Replacement, EA 03-4G200
ceqa-0761f710a73bf5783f.projectTitle: HM-4 TMS Detection Technology Replacement, EA 03-4G200
ceqa-0761f710a73bf5783f.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes a HM-4 rehabilitation project along various state routes in Sacramento and Placer counties to rehabilitate, replace, or relocate existing ramp-metering and Traffic Management System (TMS) elements at multiple locations. The work includes conduit trenching, cleaning, and replacement of existing electrical conductors, installation of new Cast-in-Drilled-Hole (CIDH) pile foundations and poles equipped with Microwave Radar Systems (MRS), Flashing Beacons, and/or Microwave Vehicle Detection Systems (MVDS), installation of new guardrail at light pole locations where needed, and replacement of existing electrical detection loops.

ceqa-b0a5a4acb96e5a7a6e.name: Morrision Creek and Beach Lake Levee Resiliency Project
ceqa-b0a5a4acb96e5a7a6e.projectTitle: Morrision Creek and Beach Lake Levee Resiliency Project
ceqa-b0a5a4acb96e5a7a6e.description: The project would raise approximately 17,550 linear feet (LF) of the existing levees, by regrading the existing levee crowns and performing minor landside slope fills; removing and replacing approximately 1,279 LF of existing floodwalls, and constructing an additional 437 LF of new floodwall; landside slope flattening, repair of an existing Union Pacific Railroad stoplog structure, construction of a new levee turnaround, and nature-based solutions enhancing the ecological function and long-term resilience of the levee system.
ceqa-b0a5a4acb96e5a7a6e.crossStreets: Beach Lake Levee Road and Cosumes River Boulevard

ceqa-78aa277ecef448b16a.name: The Academy EG (PLNG26-020)
ceqa-78aa277ecef448b16a.description: The Academy EG Project (the “Project”) consists of a Minor Conditional Use Permit (MUP) to utilize an existing 18,000 square-foot tenant space in the Light Industrial (LI) zoning district as a Specialized Education and Training/Studio that will offer kickboxing, wrestling, and jiu-jitsu training.

ceqa-24bd677bc90401f685.name: Greenback Lane Improvement Project-Phase 1 (Chestnut Ave to Folsom City Limit)
ceqa-24bd677bc90401f685.projectTitle: Greenback Lane Improvement Project-Phase 1 (Chestnut Ave to Folsom City Limit)
ceqa-24bd677bc90401f685.description: The project proposes the addition of bike lanes, separated sidewalks and a landscaped median along Greenback Lane. One (1) new conventional traffic signal would be installed at the intersection of Greenback Lane and Chestnut Avenue. In addition, two (2) existing traffic signals would be relocated to accommodate the wider intersection. In addition, utilities would be relocated underground within the road right-of-way (ROW) or public utility public facility easement (PUPFE). A joint trench would be constructed under the proposed sidewalk or proposed landscape strips. Boxes/vaults would be in sidewalk, landscape strips, or behind sidewalk as necessary, within acquired PUPFE/PUE easements.

ceqa-acc272af4815864750.name: Johnson Cosumnes Williamson Act Amendment Quitclaim Deed (BRB)
ceqa-acc272af4815864750.projectTitle: Johnson Cosumnes Williamson Act Amendment Quitclaim Deed (BRB)
ceqa-acc272af4815864750.description: The project consists of a quitclaim deed to correct an incorrect legal description recorded as Exhibit A to an Open Space Easement Agreement pursuant to the Williamson Act, for a floodplain-riparian mitigation bank, consisting of approximately 214 acres along the Cosumnes River and Laguna Creek.

ceqa-6a00d4c1194c4c2f18.name: Coyote Gulch Erosion Control Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-17340-R2) Extension
ceqa-6a00d4c1194c4c2f18.projectTitle: Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area General Plan
ceqa-6a00d4c1194c4c2f18.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-6a00d4c1194c4c2f18.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has extended Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-17340-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, California Department of Parks and Recreation. This extension will allow for the continued stream rehabilitation of the Coyote Gulch channel as a part of an 18.5-acre erosion control restoration at the Prairie City SVRA. During project activities, the stream channel will be reestablished to its former configuration, a vegetated bioswale will be established, designated culvert crossings will be constructed, and the stream channel will be fenced to protect the restored channel from unrestricted vehicular use.

ceqa-4eda08d74fa6ff88e4.name: Aspen VIII & IX Expansion Conveyor Bridge (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-63545-R2)
ceqa-4eda08d74fa6ff88e4.projectTitle: ASPEN VIII & IX MINING USE PERMIT AMENDMENT PROJECT
ceqa-4eda08d74fa6ff88e4.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-63545-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Teichert Materials. The project is limited to the construction of a crossing at Elder Creek to allow for the extension of an existing electric conveyor belt system over the channel to transport aggregate materials from the Aspen IX expansion area to connect to an existing conveyor in the Aspen IX area, from which the material would be transported to Teichert’s Perkins processing facility. ceqa-5b2376bab4dde83ccd.name: Notice of Preparation The Reserve Specific Plan Draft Environmental Impact Report
ceqa-5b2376bab4dde83ccd.projectTitle: Notice of Preparation The Reserve Specific Plan Draft Environmental Impact Report
ceqa-5b2376bab4dde83ccd.description: A conceptual land use plan for the Specific Plan Area is shown in Exhibit 2. Lotz Parkway extends into the Plan Area from Kammerer Road to a large, landscaped roundabout, providing a distinct entry to the community. In addition, subject to future planning and design led by the Cosumnes Community Services District, approximately 100 acres shown on Exhibit 2 as an area outlined and labeled “Regional Park”, may be designed to include a regional sports facility, a portion for community serving parkland, and approximately 30 acres of commercial uses supportive of community and regional serving recreational facilities. The Specific Plan Area is located within an area where the Cosumnes Community Services District would provide fire protection, emergency medical, and parks and recreation services. The Land Use Plan proposes higher-density residential and mixed-use development along the northern portion of the Specific Plan Area, consistent with the Livable Employment Area Community Plan’s vision for the Kammerer Road corridor. Non-residential uses are focused in the eastern portion of the Specific Plan Area. Lower-density residential uses are proposed for the center and southern portions of the proposed Specific Plan Area, with the lowest residential densities along the southern boundary as the land use transitions back to agricultural-residential. The proposed Land Use Plan is organized so development transitions from Mixed Use, Commercial, and Light Industrial/Flex uses to Medium Density Residential to Low Density Residential. The Land Use Plan incorporates a comprehensive bicycle and pedestrian network, which provides multi-use paths that connect the various residential neighborhoods, parks, school, and regional park. The Specific Plan proposes to allow the development of a mix of commercial, office, and light industrial uses within the “Commercial” and “Light Industrial/Flex” land use districts proposed in the eastern edge of the Specific Plan Area adjacent to SR 99. The Specific Plan will ultimately identify land use designations for the plan area and the corresponding City Zoning Districts, which will specify allowable land uses and development standards for development within the Specific Plan Area. The City’s Limited Commercial (LC) and General Commercial (GC) Zoning Districts allow a broad range of retail, commercial services, lodging (in GC), banking and other professional services, offices, medical services, commercial recreation, eating and drinking establishments, live-work facilities, and other commercial uses, as well as public uses and social service and housing support uses. The City’s Light Industrial/Flex (LI/FX) Zoning District allows a broad range of non-residential uses, such as offices, storage, warehouses, wholesaling, retail, automobile and vehicle services, small-scale manufacturing, recycling facilities, public and quasi-public uses, wineries, tasting facilities, and other uses. The City’s General Plan, along with the Livable Employment Area Community Plan and Livable Employment Area Special Planning Area adopted in 2025, establish transect-based land use designations, to be implemented through transect-based zoning. Consistent with this direction, the Specific Plan proposes transect-based zoning in the northern and northwestern portions of the Specific Plan Area along Kammerer Road, including Neighborhood Center Medium (T4) and Neighborhood Center Low (T3). The T4 and T3 (“T” for “transect”) zoning designations allow for a mix of uses, densities, and development intensities to provide housing, employment, and commercial opportunities, as well as two parks of approximately three acres each. Farther south from Kammerer Road and transitioning to the southern boundary of the Specific Plan Area, traditional Medium Density Residential (MDR) and Low Density Residential (LDR) are proposed, along with several parks (14 acres), an elementary school (10 acres), and two detention basins (44.1 acres); an existing detention basin (4.6 acres) in the eastern portion of the Specific Plan Area would be connected via an existing open space channel (3.9 acres) to the proposed detention basin in the southeastern portion of the Specific Plan Area.
ceqa-5b2376bab4dde83ccd.crossStreets: Southwest of Kammerer Road West Stockton Blvd and State Route 99

ceqa-2f0084314115db565f.description: Caltrans proposes a safety improvement project to reduce cross-over collisions along this segment of State Route (SR) 160 from Post Mile (PM) 2.73 to 6.98 in Sacramento County. The project aims to provide errant drivers with additional space to take corrective action before entering the opposing travel lane. A segment between PM 0.09 to PM 5.23 of SR 160 was identified in the 2021 Cross-over Collisions Monitoring Report, which was based on collisions between January 2017 and December 2021 caused by vehicles that crossed into the opposing travel lane. Based on the same collision period from that report, a segment was identified and analyzed from PM L2.73 to L6.98. A total of 6 fatal and 8 serious injury collisions occurred in that segment.

ceqa-7430c0eeaece3b8994.description: Sacramento County Department of Transportation (SacDOT) is proposing to widen the intersection of Bradshaw Road and Gerber Road in the Florin Vineyard Community in unincorporated Sacramento County. The intersection will be widened from the existing four by four lanes to modified four by six lanes (project). The additional lanes will taper off approximately 900 feet north, east, and south of the intersection, and approximately 1,500 feet west of the intersection. Additionally, the implementation of the project will require removal of native oak and non-native trees. Utility poles, electrical, sewer, water, and communication facilities are located along the project alignment and may require adjustment or relocation. Utility relocation coordination will be an on-going effort as the project progresses and conflicts are identified and resolved with utility companies. Construction of the project will require permanent right of way acquisition for public roadway public utility easements (PRPUE) and public utilities public facilities easements (PUPFE) from 17 parcels along Bradshaw Road and Gerber Road. Full acquisition will be required for three parcels, totaling approximately 78,811 square feet, located along Bradshaw Road. Existing structures will be demolished in the areas where full acquisitions are required. Total right of way to be acquired for PRPUE is approximately 51,232 square feet, and for PUPFE is approximately 14,090 square feet. In addition to the permanent acquisitions identified above, temporary construction easements (TCE) will be required from 14 parcels along Bradshaw Road and Gerber Road, totaling approximately 12,174 square feet. However, these easements will be temporary in nature and only be required during construction of the project. All necessary easements will be finalized during final design of the project and will be captured on final design plans. CONTROL NUMBER: PLER2023-00030

ceqa-b8488a1ead823b53ad.name: Sloughhouse RCD CalSIP Stream Gages Installation (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-65117-R2)
ceqa-b8488a1ead823b53ad.projectTitle: Sloughhouse RCD Stream Gage Installation Project
ceqa-b8488a1ead823b53ad.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-b8488a1ead823b53ad.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-b8488a1ead823b53ad.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-65117 -R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Lindsey Carter/Sloughhouse Resource Conservation District. The project is limited to the installation of seven stream gages. Each station will include the following components: • Stage sensor: A pressure transducer in a stilling well or a radar/sonic sensor mounted on a bridge or pole. • Stilling well or pipe: Protects the pressure transducer, provides stable water levels and can be anchored to a bank, abutment or pile. • Staff gage: A graduated staff mounted near the sensor for manual stage readings and calibration. • Data logger and telemetry: Housed in a weatherproof enclosure above flood levels, the logger records, stores, and sends site data to the California Data Exchange Center (CDEC). • Power supply: Solar panel with battery to power sensors, logger, and transmitter. • Secured housing and fencing: Deters vandalism and protects equipment from livestock or debris. Upon completion of data collection activities or the end of the monitoring program, each stream gage will be removed to the maximum extent practicable. The disturbed area will be restored to pre-construction elevations and contours. Disturbed soils will be stabilized as necessary to prevent erosion and sediment discharge. No permanent in-channel structures, footings, or foundations will remain.
