ceqa-6c6ccc443ae68dc57b.name: Water+ Treatment Plants Resiliency and Improvements Project Addendum
ceqa-6c6ccc443ae68dc57b.projectTitle: Water+ Treatment Plants Resiliency and Improvements Project
ceqa-6c6ccc443ae68dc57b.description: The project consists of significant improvements at both of the City's drinking water treatment plants: Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant (SRWTP), located north of downtown, and E. A. Fairbairn Water Treatment Plant (FWTP), located east of Sacramento State University. These improvements replace critical treatment infrastructure past its useful life, improve resiliency to address environmental and regulatory changes impacting drinking water, and increase the drinking water treatment capacity at the Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant in order to ensure sufficient water supply to support projected water use increases through 2050. The initial phase would improve treatment reliability by replacing facilities at the end of their effective lives. This phase of work would also provide treatment resiliency through the addition of ozone treatment to both the E. A. Fairbairn Water Treatment Plant (FWTP) and the Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant (SRWTP). In parallel with the initial reliability and resiliency improvements at both water treatment plants, the SRWTP raw-water supply and treatment capacity would be increased from 160 million gallons per day (MGD) to 235 MGD. Timing of the components of this phase will depend on available funding and project timing. Additional phases would be staged to meet the increasing City potable water demand through 2050 for an ultimate capacity of3 IO MGD at the SRWTP. No expansion of treatment capacity at the FWTP would be implemented due to limitations placed on withdrawal amounts from the American River. Specifically, implementation of the proposed project would involve the following components: • Replacement of aging infrastructure at both FWTP and SRWTP; • Integration of ozone into the treatment process at both FWTP and SRWTP; • Conversion from chlorine gas to sodium hypochlorite as the primary chemical for disinfection of the water at both FWTP and SR WTP; • Construction and operation of a secondary intake in the Sacramento River and pipelines for transferring water to SR WTP; • Expansion of existing treatment processes at SR WTP to accommodate the additional capacity (including the grit basins, flocculation and sedimentation basins, filtration, and finished water storage); • Installation of pipe Iines between the existing Sacramento River Intake and the replacement intake and SRWTP; and • Improvement of the water transmission and distribution system in the vicinity of SRWTP to address critical hydraulic constrictions. Since certification of the EIR and project approval, the City proposes changes to the approved project that include an expansion of the existing eastern boundary of the SRWTP property to incorporate an adjacent City-owned parcel (Assessor Parcel Number 00 l-0061-026-0000), approximately two acres in size. The proposed changes also include the relocation, construction and operation of the new gravity thickeners infrastructure at this new area. The new gravity thickeners would be moved to the new area to provide additional space between this infrastructure and to improve access. The new area would include hardscape to accommodate the gravity thickeners and support maintenance activities. In addition, new vegetated areas or swales would be established along the perimeter of the new area to provide stormwater management. No new treatment infrastructure is proposed to be constructed and operated at the SRWTP. All other components of the approved project remain unchanged.

ceqa-8cb9c52b8632cd2c96.name: APPROVAL OF AN ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR RELOCATABLE PUBLIC SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN THE 2025 ENERGY CODE
ceqa-8cb9c52b8632cd2c96.projectTitle: APPROVAL OF AN ALTERNATIVE PROCEDURE FOR RELOCATABLE PUBLIC SCHOOL BUILDINGS IN THE 2025 ENERGY CODE
ceqa-8cb9c52b8632cd2c96.description: The California Energy Commission (CEC) adopts and regularly updates regulations for new construction, additions, and alterations to residential and nonresidential buildings, which are contained in California Code of Regulations, Parts 1 and 6 (the California Energy Code). These regulations go through an extensive public process and are adopted at a CEC business meeting before going into effect. Part 1 of the Energy Code includes administrative regulations for implementation. In certain circumstances, interested parties or the CEC may identify alternative procedures that meet the minimum requirements of the Energy Code, but that require additional regulatory action to ensure compliance and consistency with the Energy Code. In these situations, section 10-109(h) of the 2025 Energy Code states that “In addition to the procedures and protocols identified in Sections 10-109(c), 10-116 and the Reference Appendices, the Commission may authorize alternative procedures that demonstrate compliance with Part 6.” The 2025 Energy Code defines a relocatable public school building as “a relocatable building as defined by Title 24, Part 1, Section 4-314, which is subject to Title 24, Part 1, Chapter 4, Group 1”. On November 12, 2025, the Division of the State Architect (DSA) in accordance with California Education Code Sections 17310 and 81142 published Procedure PR 18-02 that introduced an alternative procedure for demonstrating compliance with the 2025 Energy Code for relocatable public school buildings. The approach allows relocatable public school building designs analyzed using the performance compliance approach to be evaluated for the four cardinal azimuths and introduced the climate zone group method as an acceptable alternate method of compliance. In keeping with the CEC mission to maintain accurate and technically feasible compliance procedures, CEC staff proposed an additional alternative procedure to the Nonresidential Appendix NA4 “Compliance Procedures for Relocatable Public School Buildings” specification of the 2025 Energy Code to align with the alternative compliance approach allowed by DSA, using representative climate zones to demonstrate compliance for specified climate zone groups, and rotating the relocatable public school building through the cardinal azimuths of 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees to demonstrate compliance. On May 4, 2026, the CEC provided a copy of the proposed alternative procedure to interested parties, and accepted comments through June 11, 2026. No comments were received. CEC staff analyzed the proposed alternative procedure for demonstrating compliance and determined that it is technically feasible and effective at reducing the building energy budget to save at least as much energy as currently approved 2025 Energy Code compliance approaches. CEC staff and the Executive Director recommended the CEC approve the additional alternative procedure to the Nonresidential Appendix NA4 “Compliance Procedures for Relocatable Public School Buildings” specification of the 2025 Energy Code, consistent with Section 10-109(h). CEC staff and the Executive Director further recommended incorporating this alternative procedure in the California Building Energy Code Compliance software (CBECC), which is a CEC-approved software for demonstrating performance compliance with the nonresidential provisions of the 2025 Energy Code. The alternative procedure for relocatable public school buildings was approved at the CEC’s July 8, 2026 Business Meeting.

ceqa-8e104b3490043121db.name: Major Amendment to California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2023-054- 00 (ITP)
ceqa-8e104b3490043121db.projectTitle: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-8e104b3490043121db.description: The discretionary approval by CDFW is the issuance of the ITP amendment identified above. The ongoing operations of the State Water Project (SWP) in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and Suisun Marsh as approved by the lead agency is expected to result in incidental take and impacts to habitat of Longfin Smelt (Spirinchus thaleichthys), Delta Smelt (Hypomesus transpacificus), Winter-run Chinook Salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), Spring-run Chinook Salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), and White Sturgeon (Acipenser transmontanus). Longfin Smelt and Spring-run Chinook Salmon are designated as threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act. Delta Smelt and Winter-run Chinook Salmon are designated as endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act. White Sturgeon is designated as a candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act. This Amendment to the ITP changes Condition of Approval 9.1.3 (Delta Smelt Summer-Fall Habitat Action), Condition of Approval 9.1.4 (Delta Smelt Supplementation Program), Condition of Approval 9.1.4.1 (Delta Smelt Supplementation Program CDFW Staff), and Condition of Approval 10.1 (Security Amount). Changes made to these Conditions of Approval allow Permittee to implement an alternative Summer-Fall Habitat Action in 2026 and require Permittee to enhance the Delta Smelt Supplementation Program through funding for staffing and equipment to support efforts to develop and implement pond rearing strategies on Bouldin Island in the Delta and protect the refugial Delta Smelt population at Livingston Stone National Fish Hatchery. The ITP referenced above as issued and amended by CDFW authorizes incidental take of Longfin Smelt, Delta Smelt, Winter-run Chinook Salmon, Spring-run Chinook Salmon, and White Sturgeon that may occur as a result of ongoing operations of the SWP facilities, as is more specifically described in the ITP.

ceqa-fbb32adb63ee442e79.name: Delta Conveyance Project
ceqa-fbb32adb63ee442e79.description: On December 21, 2023, DWR certified the environmental impact report (“EIR”) for, and approved, the Delta Conveyance Project (State Clearinghouse No. 2020010227). After certification of the Final EIR, DWR continued project planning, engineering, permitting, and environmental compliance activities and evaluated project refinements and additional information relating to the Project. Pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21166 and CEQA Guidelines sections 15162 and 15164, DWR prepared a First Addendum to the Final EIR evaluating project refinements and additional information developed after certification of the Final EIR. On February 13, 2025, DWR approved the First Addendum and determined that none of the conditions described in CEQA Guidelines section 15162 requiring preparation of a subsequent or supplemental EIR had occurred and that no subsequent or supplemental EIR was required. DWR subsequently prepared a Second Addendum to the Final EIR evaluating additional project refinements and information developed through continuing engineering, design, permitting, and environmental review activities. On August 29, 2025 DWR approved the Second Addendum to the Final EIR and determined that none of the conditions described in CEQA Guidelines section 15162 requiring preparation of a subsequent or supplemental EIR had occurred and that no subsequent or supplemental EIR was required DCA is a responsible agency, and as such, on June 18, 2026, it made CEQA Findings of Fact pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15091 and 15096 for the Delta Conveyance Project, and approved Resolution No. 26-06 which adopted findings as a responsible agency concerning the First Addendum and Second Addendum to the Final EIR. DCA also found that the Second Addendum to the Final EIR would cause no substantial change to the implementation activities and environmental impacts addressed in the Final EIR, the First and Second Addenda thereto have been addressed, and no new or additional mitigation measures or alternatives are required.

ceqa-ad58e1296db4d60789.projectTitle: Arcadian Interstate 80 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-1515)

ceqa-32c09815d89d2cba89.description: The project is a roadway maintenance project and proposes to rehabilitate the pavement of Florin Perkins Road and FPIP roadways to a state of good repairs that include needed curb ramp upgrades, traffic signal and median improvements. The anticipated pavement rehabilitation method will include base repairs, grind, overlay and microsurfacing. At the northeast corner of the Florin Perkins Road and Belvedere Avenue intersection, a new curb ramp will be constructed. There is an existing bus stop approximately 160' north of that FP/Belvedere intersection, for which coordination with Regional Transit will occur for installation of curb, gutter and sidewalk to the bus stop and a bus stop pad if existing right-of-way and site features allow.

ceqa-18a36ca1f4c81a3df7.name: Permit No. 19704 – Elverta Road Bridge Replacement Project
ceqa-18a36ca1f4c81a3df7.description: Approval of Permit No. 19704, under California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Article 3, Section 6, for work within an adopted plan of flood control: To remove the existing two-lane bridge, construct a new six-lane reinforced concrete bridge supported on nine (9) new bents, and reconstruct the bridge approaches to conform to the new wider bridge. The project also includes the construction of ten (10) new 2-foot diameter cross-culvert pipes west of the bridge to facilitate the passage of drainage beneath Elverta Road and prevent backwater on the west side of the project. The existing double arch corrugated metal pipe (CMP) culvert east of 28th Street will also be replaced with an 8-foot by 5-foot double-cell reinforced concrete box culvert.

ceqa-08d0dca07bfac3615a.name: Permit No. 19901 – Alamar Dry Boat Dock Storage Project
ceqa-08d0dca07bfac3615a.projectTitle: Permit No. 19901 – Alamar Dry Boat Dock Storage Project
ceqa-08d0dca07bfac3615a.description: To construct an approximately 120-foot wide by 100-foot-long dry boat storage metal building with concrete access stairs and a retaining wall with riprap along the west foundation on top of previously permitted waterside berm fill material located along the left (east) bank levee of the Sacramento River. To construct new paved parking stalls and a 4-inch diameter PVC drainage line with catch basins. New landscaping and hardscaping are proposed along the waterside shoulder fenceline. To remove existing features including a wood fence, chain link fence, foundation, storage sheds, storage box, and trees. To authorize the following existing encroachments on the parcel: metal fencing and slide gate along the levee waterside shoulder, cattle gate, and storage box concrete pad.

ceqa-6aebab89bc3c58e1a0.description: Continuation of routine maintenance. Levee system protects property and inhabitants within District.

ceqa-49affe312f92a1a639.name: Permit No. 19916 – Nadal Cross Levee Fence Project
ceqa-49affe312f92a1a639.projectTitle: Permit No. 19916 – Nadal Cross Levee Fence Project
ceqa-49affe312f92a1a639.description: The proposed project consists of installing a metal chain link cross-levee fence (CLF) up and over the levee and recessed stairs with railing on the landside of the levee. The fence will have 6-foot-high by 8-foot-wide sections on both slopes. The waterside slope will be approximately 50 feet in length with 7 removable sections and the landside slope will be approximately 30 feet in length consisting of 5 sections that are not removable. There will also be a 14-foot-wide double-leaf gate across the levee crown for vehicle access, 33 concrete steps on the landside slope, each 36-inches wide, with an adjacent 6-inch-wide concrete curb, all flush with the levee slope, a metal handrail on the landside levee slope and a 36-inch by 42-inch concrete landing at the top and bottom of the stairs. The maximum excavation depth for the stairs on the slope will be 12 inches. The posts for the CLF will be embedded 18 inches below the crown and slope.

ceqa-e1a0a4e54cd512df06.name: Operation of Florin County Water District PFAS Treatment Water Supply Permit Amendment
ceqa-e1a0a4e54cd512df06.projectTitle: Operation of Florin County Water District PFAS Treatment Water Supply Permit Amendment
ceqa-e1a0a4e54cd512df06.description: The Applicant proposes the operation of two ion exchange filter vessels to remove per and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from their drinking water supply. The filters were installed within an existing well facility to be used in conjunction with the well.

ceqa-a936cceda27e159065.name: Permit No. 19806 -Silva and RVIA Cross Levee Fence Project
ceqa-a936cceda27e159065.projectTitle: Permit No. 19806 -Silva and RVIA Cross Levee Fence Project
ceqa-a936cceda27e159065.description: To install a metal, chain link, cross levee fence and multiple access gates across the left bank levee of the Sacramento River. The waterside fence will be 50 linear feet of 6-ft high and 8-ft wide, removable sections and posts of chain link fence along the levee slope with footings at a maximum depth of 16-inches. The section across the crown will have a 16-ft wide, 7-ft tall, double-leaf gate for vehicle access with footings a maximum of 18-inches deep. Approximately 46 linear feet to be installed on the landside levee slope with a new 14-ft wide maintenance access gate and a new 45-inch wide access gate.

ceqa-ec6ad7d09bdc62974b.description: The project applicant proposes to install a 420 square foot private floating dock, with a 120 square foot cover, within the Georgiana Slough and a 76-foot-long gangway from the dock to the top of the levee, within a 60-acre parcel within the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta in unincorporated Sacramento County. Construction includes pile driving within the slough to install four 8-inch piles to anchor the dock and pile driving on the bank of the levee, above the ordinary highwater mark, to install two 4-inch by 4-inch piles to support the gangway. A Use Permit and Design Review are requested for the project.

ceqa-c67577ee1da3312e26.name: Chabolla Skate Park Enhancements Project
ceqa-c67577ee1da3312e26.description: The proposed Chabolla Skate Park Enhancements Project (project) would include the demolition of the existing Chabolla Skate Park facilities and concrete pad, and the construction of a new skate park, landscaping, and other park amenities. The proposed skate park improvements would include construction of a new central bowl and various ramps, banks, box jumps, ledges, curbs, and pipes. An eight-foot by 20-foot black cantilevered shade structure, picnic table, drinking fountain, and trash/recycle receptacles would be installed near the northern park entrance. Modular seating, trash/recycle receptacles, and a short-term bicycle rack would be installed near the eastern park entrance. The proposed improvements would be constructed primarily within the existing Chabolla Skate Park footprint.

ceqa-0793ddf46b619195b9.name: 10132 Sheldon Road Rezone & Map (PLNG20-050)
ceqa-0793ddf46b619195b9.description: The 10132 Sheldon Road Rezone & Map Project (the “Project”) consists of a Rezone to amend the designation of ±4.97 gross acres from the AR-5 (Agricultural Residential – Minimum 5-Acre Lot) designation to the AR-2 (Agricultural Residential – Minimum 2-Acre Lot) and a Tentative Parcel Map (TPM) to subdivide one existing parcel into two new parcels, each consisting of a lot area of at least 2.0 gross acres. Each parcel will have access off Sheldon Road through an existing proposed 40-foot-wide private road and utility easement. Any future home construction will be required to comply with the City’s Climate Action Plan (CAP) measures for new single-unit residential construction.

ceqa-96a9a608f9b9e07c2b.name: Assessing New Electricity Rate Structures to Support LDES systems that operate for 8 or 12 hours
ceqa-96a9a608f9b9e07c2b.projectTitle: Assessing New Electricity Rate Structures to Support LDES systems that operate for 8 or 12 hours
ceqa-96a9a608f9b9e07c2b.description: Aspen will assist the California Energy Commission in identifying, validating, and stress-testing revenue pathways and financing structures that can support the deployment of long-duration energy storage (LDES) technologies that provide approximately 8 to 12 hours and longer durations of service to the California grid. This information is critical to allow these LDES systems to received future payments for the services they provide that exceed the current standard of four hours. This knowledge will allow the CEC to work with the CPUC and CAISO to update the energy storage revenue options the State offers for all emerging LDES technologies so these technologies can be integrated into the California Electric Grid of the future.

ceqa-3df88c0d5e233d322d.name: Renewables Portfolio Standard 2021-2024 Verification Results Reports for 25 Local Publicly Owned Electric Utilities for Compliance Period 4
ceqa-3df88c0d5e233d322d.projectTitle: Renewables Portfolio Standard 2021-2024 Verification Results Reports for 25 Local Publicly Owned Electric Utilities for Compliance Period 4
ceqa-3df88c0d5e233d322d.description: Public Resources Code section 399.25(b) requires the California Energy Commission (CEC) to prepare Renewables Portfolio Standard Verification Results Reports finding whether the procurement claim amounts listed are consistent with Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) certification and procurement requirements specified in the Renewables Portfolio Standard Eligibility Guidebook, Tenth Edition (RPS Guidebook) and the Enforcement Procedures for the Renewables Portfolio Standard for Local Publicly Owned Electric Utilities (RPS POU Regulations) and are eligible for the RPS program as indicated. These results reports are issued for each POU and adopted by the CEC at a regularly scheduled business meeting. CEC staff have prepared Compliance Period 4 (2021-2024) verification results reports for 25 POUs, titled the California Energy Commission Staff Draft Report Renewables Portfolio Standard Verification Results, which include the verification findings for each of these 25 POUs. The CEC adopted the 25 verification results reports at the May 13, 2026, CEC business meeting.

ceqa-4c489b5dfd1e768ce6.name: Renewables Portfolio Standard 2021-2024 Retail Sellers Procurement Verification Staff Report for Compliance Period 4
ceqa-4c489b5dfd1e768ce6.projectTitle: Renewables Portfolio Standard 2021-2024 Retail Sellers Procurement Verification Staff Report for Compliance Period 4
ceqa-4c489b5dfd1e768ce6.description: As part of the verification process, Public Resources Code section 399.25(b) requires the CEC to prepare the Verification Report finding that the procurement claim amounts listed are consistent with RPS certification and procurement requirements specified in the Renewables Portfolio Standard Eligibility Guidebook (RPS Eligibility Guidebook) and the Enforcement Procedures for the Renewables Portfolio Standard for Local Publicly Owned Electric Utilities (RPS POU Regulations) and are eligible for the RPS program as indicated. This Verification Report is issued for all retail sellers and adopted by the CEC at a regularly scheduled business meeting. The CEC then transmits the Verification Report to the CPUC, so the CPUC may determine a retail seller’s compliance with California’s RPS. CEC staff prepared the Compliance Period 4 (2021-2024) Verification Report, titled the California Energy Commission Renewables Portfolio Standard 2021-2024 Retail Sellers Procurement Verification Staff Report, which includes the verification findings for all of the retail sellers. The CEC adopted the Verification Report at the June 22, 2026, CEC business meeting.

ceqa-73286c334258ba0693.name: American River Common Features, 2016 Flood Risk Management Project (American River Erosion Contract 3B North and 3B South)
ceqa-73286c334258ba0693.projectTitle: American River Common Features, 2016 Flood Risk Management Project, Sacramento, California
ceqa-73286c334258ba0693.description: The Flood Risk Management Project consists of design refinements to the authorized 2016 ARCF Project, including engineering design modifications, footprint expansions, and compensatory habitat mitigation approaches. The design refinements include actions within eight major project components: Magpie Creek Project; American River Erosion Contracts 3B North, 3B South, 4A, and 4B; Sacramento River Erosion Contract 3; American River Mitigation Site; Sacramento River Mitigation Site, and installation of a Piezometer Network. The purpose of the Flood Risk Management Project is to address slope stability and erosion concerns along the levees of the American and Sacramento Rivers to reduce the overall flood risk. The State Lands Commission action is approval of a 49-year General Lease – Public Agency Use through June 22, 2075 for American River Erosion Contract 3B North and 3B South.

ceqa-baed146bf7e1cfbe41.name: 2024 Cathodic Protection Project
ceqa-baed146bf7e1cfbe41.description: The Project purpose is to project is to install corrosion protection system near 21 towers. Soil disturbance to install the corrosion protection below ground will temporarily impact wetlands.

ceqa-0cbeb857ffb488d5b5.name: Bridge Preventative Maintenance on Various Bridges in the City of Rancho Cordova
ceqa-0cbeb857ffb488d5b5.projectTitle: Bridge Preventative Maintenance on Various Bridges in the City of Rancho Cordova
ceqa-0cbeb857ffb488d5b5.description: The proposed project would make necessary improvements to extend the existing life of the bridge deck. The specific scope of the project consists of removing the existing asphalt from the bridge deck and replacing it with polyester concrete overlay, mill and fill 25 feet from approach, res-tripe bridge deck and approaches.

ceqa-1574379a7169f0ff8d.name: Sloughhouse RCD Stream Gage Installation Project
ceqa-1574379a7169f0ff8d.projectTitle: Sloughhouse RCD Stream Gage Installation Project
ceqa-1574379a7169f0ff8d.description: Sloughhouse Resource Conservation District (SRCD) has received funding from CalSIP to reactivate or install new surface water gaging stations at seven (7) locations throughout Amador and Sacramento Counties. The Project is designed to provide a net benefit to the watershed by enhancing the precision of real-time surface water data. This data is critical for informed instream flow management and the long-term protection of sensitive aquatic and riparian resources. While construction may result in minor, localized, and temporary impacts, these effects will be minimized through avoidance and minimization measures. Ultimately, the improved data stream will facilitate adaptive management strategies that balance agricultural needs with the biological requirements of local fish and wildlife populations.

ceqa-0cedf51663b3b609eb.name: Pocket Road Sewer Replacement at East Shore Project (X14120309)
ceqa-0cedf51663b3b609eb.projectTitle: Pocket Road Sewer Replacement at East Shore Project (X14120309)
ceqa-0cedf51663b3b609eb.description: The project would improve safety along a section of a roadway at the intersection of Pocket Road and East Shore Drive and maintain reliability of DOU's wastewater infrastructure. A roadway depression was discovered at the intersection of Pocket Road and East Shore Road. City crews performed a video review of the sewer main and found that Manhole 707UU12 is currently dealing with a failure in which the base has settled, causing groundwater to infiltrate into the manhole. Additionally, the adjacent sewer piping is settling and will be repaired. The project will remove and replace the existing manhole and approximately 50 linear feet of 21-inch sewer pipe. This project will also include dewatering, excavation, backfill, and surface restoration.

ceqa-956b2c582881800296.name: Quick Quack Car Wash
ceqa-956b2c582881800296.description: The project includes construction and operation of a drive-thru car wash facility on two vacant parcels totaling approximately 1.50 acres located at 6701 and 6711 Folsom-Auburn Road. The project is proposed to consist of a drive-thru queue for up to 18 vehicles, a 3,588-square-foot, 29-foot-tall car wash building, vacuum stalls, and site improvements.

ceqa-ca4fbbfb5fd29f5940.name: California Beaver Coexistence Training and Support Program (Project)
ceqa-ca4fbbfb5fd29f5940.projectTitle: California Beaver Coexistence Training and Support Program (Project)
ceqa-ca4fbbfb5fd29f5940.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Watershed Restoration Grants
ceqa-ca4fbbfb5fd29f5940.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Watershed Restoration Grants Branch
ceqa-ca4fbbfb5fd29f5940.description: On September 18, 2024, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) executed a $2,000,000 grant with Nature Based Solutions: Wetlands and Mountain Meadows funding to the Occidental Arts and Ecology Center to launch a program facilitating widespread beaver coexistence strategies. Initial grant activities related to planning have recently been completed. These activities included setting up a Help Desk website, training professionals in nonlethal deterrence strategies, setting up data collection and analysis strategies, and conducting outreach. The Grantee will assist landowners with implementation of beaver damage-deterrent installations that result in the alleviation of beaver depredation and reduction in beaver take by providing non-lethal deterrence strategies and support for beaver coexistence installations. Now CDFW is authorizing the next phase of the grant agreement: implementation of the following physical activities on a programmatic basis as “low-impact” activities to be funded under the grant (Project): • Non-invasive activities to prevent and minimize flooding caused by beaver damming, such as pond levelers, fenced notches, and beaver deceiver flow pipes; • Strategies to prevent blocked culverts and water conveyance structures, using methods such as culvert protection (exclusion) fencing, beaver back savers (a retrofit to an existing weir allowing water to flow through the structure using a perforated pipe capped with a metal grate), or diversion fencing installations (fencing upstream of a culvert which diverts beavers damming efforts away from the culvert); • Tree protection strategies, including use of regular or electric fencing around individual or groups of trees, and painting trees with sand paint; and • Replacement and maintenance activities related to all installed devices.

ceqa-6c9af17f5b5083e1f5.name: Kaiser Permanente Folsom Comprehensive Care Center Project
ceqa-6c9af17f5b5083e1f5.description: The project proposes a 27,104-sf expansion of the existing Kaiser Ambulatory Surgery Center, a new 183,417-sf medical office building, 1,109 parking spaces, landscaping, and solar canopies over a portion of the parking lot. The project would construct three driveways, two off Broadstone Parkway and one off Iron Point Road. This project is an Addendum to the Final Program Environmental Impact Report for the Broadstone II Master Plan certified on October 27, 1992 (State Clearinghouse No. 1989092523).

ceqa-2abbb07ec76e83c7e3.description: The Applicant proposes to change the status of the Hemlock Well from standby to inactive. Deactivation is accomplished by excavating to the connection point and physically disconnecting the well from the distribution system.
ceqa-2abbb07ec76e83c7e3.crossStreets: 5640 Hemlock Street between Rambler Way and Cherokee Way

ceqa-cde3a9266e63471087.name: Threemile Slough Pipeline Crossings Remediation and Decommissioning Project
ceqa-cde3a9266e63471087.projectTitle: Threemile Slough Pipeline Crossings Remediation and Decommissioning Project
ceqa-cde3a9266e63471087.description: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) is proposing the Threemile Slough Pipeline Crossings Remediation and Decommissioning Project (Project), which consists of four primary components: project area preparation and equipment mobilization, remediation of the active L-131Y and L-131Z pipelines within Threemile Slough, removal of the terrestrial and submarine portions of the previously abandoned L-131 East and West pipelines, and post-construction restoration of the Project area and demobilization activities. Each Project component includes a defined series of steps summarized in the Mitigated Negative Declaration. Long-term operations of the active L-131Y and L-131Z pipelines would not differ from existing conditions.

ceqa-f06cca0a2127aa30ab.name: St. Lukes Detention Basin (W14150704)
ceqa-f06cca0a2127aa30ab.description: This project will construct a new stormwater detention basin on an undeveloped parcel adjacent to St. Luke's Lutheran Church. The Stormwater detention basin will 15'e unlined and approximately 13 feet deep with 3: 1 side slopes, a concrete access ramp, and a concrete low-flow swale. The top of the basin will be setback at least five feet from adjacent property fences. Excess stormwater will be diverted into and out of the basin through a new 36-ince conveyance pipe connected to a new 7-foot by 10-foot vault in Center Parkway. The vault will include an adjustable weir that diverts storm water into the basin system when water levels in the existing system reach a critical height. A one-way flap gate will be included to allow storm water to flow back into the existing system once a storm has passed. Site improvements will include six-foot-tall perimeter fencing around the basin, a wrought iron fence at the property entrance with a rolling gate and asphalt driveway, and a gravel access road from the entrance to the perimeter basin fencing and second gate.

ceqa-5e21ea71da33d40bd4.name: PLNP2018-00284 Upper Westside Specific Plan
ceqa-5e21ea71da33d40bd4.description: The Specific Plan encompasses a 1,524 acre Development Area and a 542± acre Ag Buffer Area that is located west of the Development Area, providing a transition to the Garden Highway. Within the Development Area , the project proposes an urban , commercial mixed-use town center district near the intersection of El Centro Road and West El Camino Avenue surrounded by neighborhoods. The Development Area includes 9,356± dwelling units and 3,096,245± square feet of commercial uses, with three K-8 school sites, one high school site, and several parks. Other amenities include trail networks, a greenbelt and urban farm corridor, and a canal system that will all encourage pedestrian and bicycle use by providing connections between neighborhoods. In addition to the adoption of the Specific Plan, the Project requires amendments to the Sacramento County UPA and USB boundaries. The Project also requires amendments to the General Plan to include the proposed policy amendments and land uses, streets and bikeways on the General Plan 's Land Use Diagram, Transportation Plan, and Active Transportation Plan. The Project will also require adoption of a Water Supply Master Plan amendment, and a Water Supply Assessment pursuant to California Water Code.

ceqa-793d45cfca2d4de8f9.name: Crowing Fowl County Code And Zoning Code Amendments (ZOB) PLNP2024-00226
ceqa-793d45cfca2d4de8f9.projectTitle: Crowing Fowl County Code And Zoning Code Amendments (ZOB) PLNP2024-00226
ceqa-793d45cfca2d4de8f9.description: The project consists of two separate legislative actions: the addition of new sections to Title 8 of the Sacramento County Code establishing standards for the care, housing, and regulation of roosters; and a County-initiated Zoning Code Amendment to amend Chapters 3, 5, and 7 of the Sacramento County Zoning Code related to the keeping of roosters in residential and noncommercial settings. The Zoning Code Amendment would establish numerical limits on roosters by zoning district and parcel size, and clarify general and development standards applicable to rooster keeping. The amendment would also introduce additional development standards in residential zoning districts to address nuisance concerns, consistent with existing County noise regulations, and strengthen enforcement provisions by clarifying complaint-based enforcement procedures and compliance timelines following written notification from the County. The Zoning Code Amendment would remove the Minor Use Permit requirement for agricultural education programs and establish a no-cost registration process within Chapter 3 of the Zoning Code, allowing legitimate breeders, exhibitors, and hobbyists to exceed the standard rooster limits without requiring a use permit or public hearing. The County Code Amendment would add definitions related to roosters and enclosure, and establish standards for the keeping of roosters, including provisions related to animal care, sanitation, enclosure requirements, and prohibition of tethering. The amendment also includes enforcement provisions and penalties to address violations and deter illegal or inhumane practices. The proposed County Code and Zoning Code amendments do not modify regulations applicable to egg-laying hens, does not apply to commercial poultry operations, and do not authorize new development or expansion of existing uses.

ceqa-a55c613c6fb576da51.name: City of Elk Grove Climate Compass (SP0013)

ceqa-a55c613c6fb576da51.description: The proposed Climate Compass is a comprehensive update to the City of Elk Grove's current Climate Action Plan (CAP), adopted in 2019. The proposed Plan establishes a roadmap for the City to achieve its greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reduction targets and includes actions and strategies to adapt to anticipated climate-related impacts. In addition, the Plan aligns local efforts with Assembly Bill (AB) 1279 (2021-22 Legislative Session), which requires California to achieve net-zero GHG emissions and an 85 percent reduction in anthropogenic GHG emissions by 2045.

ceqa-1e773e6233be104b59.name: Kiefer Landfill Gas Utilization Project
ceqa-1e773e6233be104b59.description: Kiefer Landfill Generating III, LLC is proposing to construct a renewable natural gas (RNG) plant with a capacity of 8,000 standard cubic feet per minute (scfm) at Kiefer Landfill and a pipeline connecting the plant to existing Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E) natural gas pipelines in Sacramento County. The RNG plant would process landfill gas to meet air quality standards and produce pipeline-quality natural gas (i.e., primarily methane) by removing moisture and impurities. The proposed project would also construct a new pipeline to transfer the pipeline-quality RNG from the plant to existing PG&E pipeline infrastructure, with two route options under evaluation. Pipeline Routes would be located within the public rights-of-way and/or private easements and run northwest from Kiefer Landfill along Kiefer Boulevard either to the intersection of Kiefer Boulevard/Rancho Cordova Parkway or to the intersection of Kiefer Boulevard/Sunrise Boulevard, then north along Sunrise Boulevard where it would terminate in the vicinity of the intersection of Sunrise Boulevard/Douglas Road. Either a compressor station would be constructed near the intersection of Douglas Road and Sunrise Boulevard to connect existing Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E) distribution and transmission pipelines or a metering and regulating (M&R) station may be constructed in the vicinity of the PG&E interconnect on Douglas Boulevard depending on the pipeline route (APN 067-0030-079-0000 or 067-2370-018-0000).

ceqa-83caf52ed35b219ba9.name: 8040 16th Street AT&T Wireless Communication Facility
ceqa-83caf52ed35b219ba9.description: The project is a request for the following entitlements from Sacramento County: 1. A Use Permit to allow a new 55-foot faux water tank wireless communication facility and associated equipment in the Agricultural Residential (AR-5) Zone. 2. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standard: • Separation – Public Right of Way (Section 3.6.7.A, Table 3.6.2): New towers and equipment enclosures located on Group 1 parcels shall be separated from the public right of way by 31 feet if a public utility public facility easement (PUPFE) is required. The tower and equipment enclosure are proposed to be setback 21 feet from the public right of way. 3. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). The project consists of a Use Permit to construct a new 55-foot-tall faux water tank wireless communication facility on the southwest portion of the subject property (adjacent to 16th Street). The new WCF will be located within a 40-foot by 31-foot (1,240 square feet) ground lease area, enclosed by a 6-foot-tall chain link fence with brown or neutral tone colored privacy slats with a 12-foot-wide access gate. A 5-foot wide landscape easement will be installed around the outer perimeter of the lease area. The facility will consist of six (6) panel antennas and six (6) air antennas, which will be mounted at a height of 51 feet. In addition, a total of 12 remote radio units (RRU’s) will be mounted at a height of 50 feet. The antennas will be mounted on a monopole structure encased within the faux water tank. The lease area consists of equipment cabinets and a diesel backup generator. Access to the WCF is proposed via a compacted gravel 20-foot wide access drive with hammerhead turnaround for fire access. Electrical and fiber lines will extend from the ground equipment in the lease area along the access drive and north along west property line approximately 180 feet to the existing utility pole. The property is located within the Elverta Specific Plan with a future land use designation of Residential (RD-10). The wireless communication facility is consistent with the policies of the Elverta Specific Plan and the proposed location at the southwest corner will accommodate future development. In addition, the WCF is located outside of the ultimate right-of-way of 16th Street. Control Number: PLNP2025-00173

ceqa-b1514f1c229dd9dbfd.name: Micro-Community Projects
ceqa-b1514f1c229dd9dbfd.description: The proposed projects are a part of the City's efforts to address homelessness within Sacramento. Each proposed project would include the development of a "micro-community" for unhoused seniors (aged 55 years and older) that would include 120-sf prefabricated units as well as various associated on-site amenities, such as shared bathrooms, gathering space, and dog-run areas, as discussed in further detail below. Pets would be limited to two small or one medium dog or cat per resident and would be required to be registered, vaccinated, and spayed/neutered. Such services would be provided free to residents. Project Site 1 The proposed project would include the development of a "micro-community" for seniors with a total of 40, 120-sf prefabricated units. The project would also include six shared bathrooms which would each include an Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)-compliant shower, lavatory, and toilet; one shared two-stall bathroom; and two shared laundry facilities. An outdoor dining area with a sink, two electric cooking devices, and seating would be provided. A 2,700-sf dog run would be included on the southeastern portion of the site. A portion of Project Site 1 is located within a FEMA floodplain. Thus, development of Project Site 1 would include elevating the micro-community unit pads above the base flood elevation using ground screws to reduce risk of flooding. The ground screws would be installed along the perimeter of the proposed units and would raise the units approximately three feet above ground level. The existing utility shed, utility pole, and trees would remain as is. Project Site 2 The proposed project would include the development of a "micro-community" for seniors with a total of 28, 120-sf prefabricated units. The proposed project would also include three shared bathrooms which would each include an ADA-compliant shower, lavatory, and toilet; two shared two-stall bathrooms; and two shared laundry facilities. An outdoor dining area with a sink, two electric cooking devices, and seating would be provided. A dog run would be included on the southwestern portion of the site. Pets would be limited to two small or one medium dog or cat per resident and would be required to be registered, vaccinated, and spayed/neutered. Such services would be provided free to residents. Project Site 3 The proposed project would include the development of a "micro-community" for seniors with a total of 40, 120-sf prefabricated units. The proposed project would also include four shared bathrooms which would each include an ADA-compliant shower, lavatory, and toilet; one shared two-stall bathroom; and two shared laundry facilities. An outdoor dining area with a sink, two electric cooking devices, and seating would be provided. A 2,800-sf dog run would be included on the northwestern portion of the site. An optional kennel located south of the dog run would be provided as well. Development of all three project locations would also include associated parking and access, landscaping, and utility improvements. Dogs would be required to be leashed at all times. Animal waste would be collected and disposed of in sealed containers daily by residents and on-site staff.

ceqa-bfe1510582c5aa0d0d.name: Long-term Operation of the State Water Project
ceqa-bfe1510582c5aa0d0d.projectTitle: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-bfe1510582c5aa0d0d.description: DWR is proposing to modify actions to improve SWP operational flexibility while maintaining similar or equal level of protection proportional to SWP impacts, particularly given recent and best available scientific findings, the status of the historical and supplemented Delta Smelt population. Additionally, recent modifications of joint actions for Fall X2 for the CVP and SWP (U.S. Bureau of Reclamation 2025) occurred. DWR proposes to modify COA 9.1.3 Delta Smelt Summer-Fall Action in exchange for additional alternative actions in COA 9.1.3 and COA 9.1.4 that are expected to provide equal or better benefits to the species. This approach is consistent with the initial 2008 FWS application of Fall X2 as adaptive management to determine whether a benefit could manifest that would help Delta Smelt survival. The anticipated benefits provided through the Fall X2 requirement have not, after several years, manifested in a meaningful benefit, so other approaches to generating a benefit should be attempted. The proposed major amendment, together with ongoing monitoring and data collection consistent with the adaptive management approach, is more likely to achieve the intended benefit of food supply during a time when Delta Smelt may be present, as explained further below. The proposed major amendment is also consistent with the limited term amendment to the ITP for the 2025 water year (2081-2023-054-00-A1). Proposed Modifications and Alternative Actions COA 9.1.3 Proposed modification of COA 9.1.3 includes a permanent removal of the September and October Fall X2 requirement (80 km) as described in the 2024 LTO ITP, instead operating to SWRCB D-1641 for September and October, consistent with the limited term amendment (CDFW 2025a). DWR proposes an alternative action to mitigate SWP impacts by flooding approximately 315 acres of wetlands during the summer and fall of Wet and Above Normal water years to provide food subsidies in Suisun Marsh where juvenile Delta Smelt have been abundant historically. Changes to the food action region may be proposed by DWR, in coordination with CDFW, if monitoring data of Delta Smelt suggest a food action may have benefits outside the Suisun Marsh region. This alternative action is estimated to provide a biomass of zooplankton equal to the SWP’s proportional share of the biomass of Delta Smelt’s main diet taxon, Pseudodiaptomus forbesi, transported during a Fall X2 action. COA 9.1.4 Proposed modification of COA 9.1.4 includes an additional condition “9.1.4.2 Delta Smelt Survival Evaluation and Enhancement Plan” with the goal to improve Delta Smelt survival and abundance, and the production of hatchery smelt for applied science activities. Activities may include development of key research questions and implementation of hypothesis-driven studies to inform process improvements to the Delta Smelt Supplementation Program. These activities are complementary to, but distinct from, Supplementation Program releases. Project Location The project location for the Proposed Project is the same as described in the 2023 ITPA (ICF 2023:3-1–3-2) and 2024 LTO ITP (California Department of Fish and Wildlife 2024:2).

The Rancho Seco Switchyard would be modified to accept the new interconnection.

The approximately 10-acre park also contains picnic areas, children 's play equipment, a swimming pool, an outdoor archery range, and soccer fields. ceqa-55f6fadd27f774b2a3.description: Basin G43 is currently identified in the Florin-Vineyard Drainage Master Plan (FVDMP) to be located just south of Gerber Creek, about 0.3 miles west of Bradshaw Road, across four parcels encompassing approximately 8 acres. There are three residences within the Basin G43 area. The Sacramento County Department of Water Resources (DWR), in conjunction with County Real Estate, is pursuing acquisition of the required land for Basin G43. However, due to the existing residences, DWR is proposing to move the basin further south from the original planned location to avoid compulsory acquisition of the three existing homes. As such, the modified project is the acquisition of a portion of parcel APN: 121-0050-021-0000 for future construction of Basin G43. Parcel APN: 121-0050-021-0000 is a "frying pan" shaped parcel, totaling 12.9 acres. The purchase acquisition would be only for the southern portion of the parcel where the basin will be located and does not include the "handle" of the "frying pan". CONTROL NUMBER: PLER2023-0006

ceqa-abd5aec013f4717d0f.name: Vineyard South Mine Expansion
ceqa-abd5aec013f4717d0f.description: The proposed project consists of the following requests: 1. A Use Permit Amendment (PLNP2016-00130) to allow surface mining on four additional parcels totaling86 acres and three additional years of mining. 2. A Rezone to add the Surface Mining Combining Zone to 86 acres of IR zone (Interim Agricultural Reserve) on four parcels (APNs 064-0080-009, 064-0080-061, 066-0040-003, and 066-0040-004. 3. A Community Plan Amendment to add language to the Florin-Vineyard Community Plan that would allow for surface mining activity on two parcels (APNs 064-0080-009 and 064-0080-061 ), a use that is compatible with the zoning on these parcels prior to adoption of the Florin-Vineyard Community Plan, for the duration of the related Use Permit. 4. A Reclamation Plan Amendment to include new mining area into Reclamation Plan that include end use of open space (suitable for dryland grazing) and/or non-prime agriculture. 5. A Development Agreement Amendment between the Applicant and the County of Sacramento. Granite Construction Company (Granite) will expand mining operations onto four additional parcels to the south of the existing Vineyard South Mine. Granite would mine approximately 60 of the 86 acres on the four expansion parcels. Average depth of overburden (thickness) is estimated at 20 to 35 feet. Average depth of sand and gravel is estimated at 20 to 40 feet. The anticipated maximum depth of mining is 75 feet below ground surface (bgs), which corresponds to elevation negative 16-18 feet above mean sea level (amsl). Based on current mine design, the project expansion parcels contain an anticipated 3.5 million cubic yards of overburden and anticipated 3.1 million tons of sand and gravel. Granite proposes no change to approved annual production rates. Granite is currently permitted to produce up to 2,000,000 tons per year. No aggregate processing plants are proposed in the Project area. Consistent with the current approvals, limited in-pit dry screening may occur occasionally to support conveyor transport (e.g., if large cobbles are encountered). The project proposes to reconfigure the Phase 28 mining area analyzed in the EIR and add a third phase (Phase 3). Other physical improvements include the installation of fencing around Phase 28 and Phase 3 areas for public safety and site security. The project will also extend the existing earthen berms to separate the mining pits from the 100-year floodplain along the south side of Phases 28 and 3. No other drainage course alterations, diversions, or work in active waterways is anticipated. Landscape screening will be installed along the frontage of Florin Road, consistent with the approved planting pallet. CONTROL NUMBER: PLNP2024-00037

ceqa-fd0827bf25eb01da0b.name: Citrus Heights Creek Erosion and Bridge Scour Protection Project
ceqa-fd0827bf25eb01da0b.projectTitle: Citrus Heights Creek Erosion and Bridge Scour Protection Project
ceqa-fd0827bf25eb01da0b.description: The Citrus Heights Creek Erosion and Bridge Scour Protection Project (project) would include the installation of scour and erosion protection measures, including creek channel and slope stabilization, underneath the Indian River Drive Bridge (Indian River Bridge), Matheny Way Bridge (Matheny Bridge), Arcade-Cripple Creek Trail Bridge (Sundance Bridge), and Patton Avenue Bridge (Patton Bridge). The project would also include the removal of an abandoned Consolidated Communications, Inc. (CCI) and Comcast joint trench with exposed conduits in the creek bed of the Indian River Bridge project impact area and would include the relocation of existing and exposed Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E) inactive and active gas lines in the Matheny Bridge project impact area. The project work would occur where natural erosion is impacting existing public infrastructure and inhibiting City of Citrus Heights maintenance activities. The project is proposed to extend the service life of the bridges, maintain public safety, protect critical infrastructure, and reduce long-term maintenance needs.

ceqa-41c6b556607287b939.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-62993 -R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Robert Rawdanowicz. The project is limited to the construction of a concrete crossing over Cripple Creek. Six inches of soil along the creek banks and creek bed will be excavated where the concrete will be placed. Steel rebars will be installed into the excavated areas before concrete is poured. The south bank will have an approximately 25-foot by 10-foot concrete ramp, the north bank will have an approximately 22-foot by 10-foot ramp, and the creek bed will have an approximately 20-foot by 5-foot concrete path tied in with an abandoned sewer pipe.

ceqa-f2fedd5deabd4c5159.name: Galt Ranch Commercial Development
ceqa-f2fedd5deabd4c5159.description: The proposed project would include the subdivision of the 45.65-acre project site into 20 parcels, and the subsequent development of restaurant, retail, medical office/clinic space, hotel, and retail automotive parts and service uses. A 9.11-acre portion of the project site is currently designated for high-density residential uses, which (based on the existing zoning) could include the future development of up to 240 residential units. However, the development of that 9.11-acre area is not proposed as part of this project, and the remainder parcel is only included within the project site for parcelization purposes in order to exclude the acreage from the project’s development area. The proposed project would include a total of 189,070 square feet (sf) of commercial uses, comprised of five quick-serve restaurants ranging in size between 2,400 sf and 3,887 sf; a 6,000-sf restaurant; seven retail buildings ranging between 6,900 sf and 30,000 sf; two medical office buildings 10,000 sf and 20,000 sf in size; a hotel with approximately 80 rooms; one car wash; and one gas station with a convenience store. A total of 1,175 parking spaces would be provided throughout the site. Vehicle site access would be provided by a new connection to Simmerhorn Road at the northern end of the site, which would lead to the new internal road, Galt Ranch Road, which will connect to Simmerhorn Road and Crystal Way. The project was approved by the Galt City Council on May 19, 2026 (the February 12, 2026 Planning Commission approval was appealed - SCH#2026020567).

ceqa-6004629921b3f7beba.name: Alhambra Redevelopment Project (P24-007)
ceqa-6004629921b3f7beba.description: The project consists of a redevelopment of the existing uses at 320 and 324 through 350 Alhambra Boulevard; 3004 and 3012 C Street; and 301, 311, 315, and 317 30th Street, Sacramento, CA. The project proposes to develop a six-story, mixed-use building on a 2.26-acre site located within the General Commercial (C-2-SPD) zone and the Alhambra Corridor Special Planning District (SPD). The proposed building consists of 2,400 square feet of ground-floor commercial, 332 multi-unit dwellings, and a six-level parking garage comprised of an underground/basement level and five above-ground levels containing 322 total parking stalls. To accommodate the site redevelopment, the project requests the demolition of on-site structures, removal and non-standard pruning of trees, and the abandonment of Chinatown Alley.

ceqa-4fb73c384cef6a110d.name: Rancho Murieta Equestrian Center Culvert Replacement Project
ceqa-4fb73c384cef6a110d.projectTitle: Rancho Murieta Equestrian Center Culvert Replacement Project
ceqa-4fb73c384cef6a110d.description: The culverts beneath the Rancho Murieta Equestrian Center access road, part of the local stormwater system, began failing during the 2024-25 rainy season and were identified in late 2025 as a public safety risk due to pipe deterioration, separation, and roadway damage. Engineering review indicates that a significant storm event could cause complete culvert failure, posing a danger to the public and cutting off primary access to key facilities south of the channel. The proposed project will replace the failing culverts to mitigate flood hazards, maintain and reinforce the access road, and ensure reliable emergency vehicle access.

Associated site improvements would include roadway widening along West Elkhorn Boulevard and Marysville Boulevard with new curb, gutter, and a bifurcated sidewalk within a proposed 20-foot public utilities and public facilities easement (PUPFE). A Conditional Use Permit, Special Development Permit, and Design Review entitlements would also be required for the proposed gas station and car wash. Control Number: PLNP2022-00166

A cross-access easement agreement would be recorded between the applicant and the seller on the development area parcel to memorialize traffic circulation and ingress/egress rights. ceqa-0359c8ba0ed4bc9a93.description: The City proposes to construct a 0.5-mile addition to the planned 16-mile Creek Corridor Trail in Citrus Heights. The Project will extend east from the existing Stock Ranch Trail behind the Costco/Walmart shopping center to Sylvan Road. The purpose of this Project is to construct one of the several planned segments by replacing dirt and narrow concrete paths with an Americans with Disabilities Act-compliant Class I multi-use trail. This trail extension is needed to enhance pedestrian and bicycle connectivity, provide a safe recreational facility, and improve access through the Arcade Creek greenbelt. Proposed facilities include a paved trail, a new prefabricated bridge across the unnamed creek tributary, solar lighting, bank protection along a segment of Arcade Creek, and an at-grade signalized pedestrian crossing at Sylvan Road.

ceqa-bd0baade7529ed975e.name: Jackson Bulk Substation Project
ceqa-bd0baade7529ed975e.description: SMUD is proposing to construct and operate the new Jackson Bulk Substation project. The Project includes the construction of an approximately 18-acre bulk substation. The proposed substation would convert high voltage from 230,000-volt (230kV) transmission lines to 69,000-volt (69kV) through transformers for local distribution into residential and commercial customers along the Jackson Highway corridor. Key features of the new substation include installation of new electrical equipment, a control building, driveway access, site fencing, lighting, stormwater drainage, and utilities. SMUD will also grade the remaining 26 acres for drainage improvements and maintain temporary soil storage south of the substation footprint. The substation will retain a 200-foot setback from Jackson Road and Excelsior Road. In addition, the Project also includes construction of new or modified overhead power lines that would link the substation to the existing electrical grid. Planned overhead line improvements involve constructing approximately 0.7 miles of new 69kV overhead lines and converting approximately 5.35 miles of existing 12,000-volt (12kV) pole and overhead lines to single-circuit 69kV overhead lines with a 12kV underbuild. This work will require replacing the existing poles with taller, stronger poles (see Figure 2-2). Project construction is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2030, with commissioning and energization scheduled for December 2032. The anticipated construction duration for the Project is approximately 36 months.

ceqa-31567c70d27e85e218.name: The Residences at Murieta Hills and The Retreat at Rancho Murieta (Stonehouse Substation Project)
ceqa-31567c70d27e85e218.projectTitle: The Residences West, Residences East and the Retreat at Rancho Murieta
ceqa-31567c70d27e85e218.description: SMUD proposes the construction and installation of a two-transformer electric distribution substation, known as the Stonehouse Substation project. This substation is necessary to meet the electrical demand of the Project. The proposed substation would be located immediately west of Stonehouse Road, just outside but adjacent to the Project’s previously evaluated western boundary. The facility is designed to serve the 12,000-volt (12kV) demand for the Project. Components include two 20-megavolt ampere (MVA) transformers, up to six capacitor banks, four feeder tie switches, two switchgears, two switch poles and other associated substation equipment. Construction would involve excavation and grading activities to install substation infrastructure, including up to six new power poles, resulting in a total disturbance area of approximately 1.33 acres. The substation would be enclosed by a ten-foot-tall concrete block wall with access gates compatible with its surroundings. Within the substation, 69,000-volt (69kV) electricity would be stepped down to 12 kV for distribution to the surrounding areas, where local transformers would further reduce the voltage to household service levels. New underground 12 kV distribution lines would connect to the substation circuits through utility conduits and would be accessed via pad-mounted switchgear and subsurface pull boxes to distribute power throughout the Residences West subdivision. No new overhead distribution lines outside of the substation site or existing SMUD utility easement are proposed. Maintenance of the distribution lines would follow SMUD’s standard practices. Initial site preparation, including access development, rough grading, and drainage improvements, would be completed by the developer or SMUD as part of the overall Project development. Following site preparation, SMUD would construct the substation infrastructure, which includes minor grading, construction of a new driveway, concrete block walls, conduit grounding, and foundations for substation equipment. This phase would also involve the installation and energization of equipment, cleanup, and backfilling of trenches for conduit installation. Excavated soil would be reused onsite where feasible. Site Access and Substation Perimeter Wall SMUD will utilize existing driveways whenever possible and may add temporary construction access during staging and construction. To maintain site security and public safety, the perimeter of the new substation would be enclosed by a ten-foot-tall concrete block wall with access gates compatible with its surroundings. All staging area(s) would be contained on site during construction. Areas that are not paved or that house equipment or structures would be covered in crushed gravel. Construction Schedule Project construction is anticipated to begin in fall 2028 with commissioning and energization expected to occur in May 2029. SMUD anticipates the overall construction duration to be approximately 10 months. Installation of underground distribution lines would ideally occur concurrently with construction of the subtransmission (69kv) lines.

ceqa-bf55ed6b460bf8da08.name: San Francisco Bay and Delta Sand Mining Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2013-047-03 (ITP))
ceqa-bf55ed6b460bf8da08.projectTitle: San Francisco Bay and Delta Sand Mining Project
ceqa-bf55ed6b460bf8da08.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP amendment (No. 2081-2013-047-03), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to Martin Marietta Marine Operations, LLC. This proposed project involves continue commercial hydraulic sand mining operations in the central San Francisco Bay, Middle Ground Island shoal, and Suisun Channel. This operation provides local marine aggregate for use in highway maintenance and construction, new residential complexes, and commercial and public buildings within the greater San Francisco Bay Area. Project activities include hydraulic sand mining and sand offloading. This ITP minor amendment extends the ITP expiration date from April 30, 2026 to October 31, 2026. The Project will result in impacts to Central Valley spring-run Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), Sacramento River winter-run Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), Delta smelt (Hypomesus transpacificus), and longfin smelt (Spirinchus thaleichthys) habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of Central Valley spring-run Chinook salmon and longfin smelt which are designated as a threatened species and Sacramento River winter-run Chinook salmon and Delta smelt which are designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act. The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-584ee43bf417e89f6e.name: Water + Treatment Plants Resiliency and Improvements Project
ceqa-584ee43bf417e89f6e.projectTitle: Water+ Treatment Plants Resiliency and Improvements Project
ceqa-584ee43bf417e89f6e.description: The project consists of significant improvements at both of the City's drinking water treatment plants: Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant (SRWTP), located north of downtown, and E. A. Fairbairn Water Treatment Plant (FWTP), located east of Sacramento State University. These improvements replace critical treatment infrastructure past its useful life, improve resiliency to address environmental and regulatory changes impacting drinking water, and increase the drinking water treatment capacity at the Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant in order to ensure sufficient water supply to support projected water use increases through 2050. The initial phase would improve treatment reliability by replacing facilities at the end of their effective lives. This phase of work would also provide treatment resiliency through the addition of ozone treatment to both the E. A. Fairbairn Water Treatment P1ant (FWTP) and the Sacramento River Water Treatment Plant (SRWTP). In parallel with the initial reliability and resiliency improvements at both water treatment plants, the SRWTP raw-water supply and treatment capacity would be increased from 160 million gallons per day (MGD) to 235 MOD. Timing of the components of this phase will depend on available funding and project timing. Additional phases would be staged to meet the increasing City potable water demand through 2050 for an ultimate capacity of310 MGD at the SRWTP. No expansion of treatment capacity at the FWTP would be implemented due to limitations placed on withdrawal amounts from the American River. Specifically, implementation of the proposed project would involve the following components: Replacement of aging infrastructure at both FWTP and SRWTP; Integration of ozone into the treatment process at both FWTP and SRWTP; Conversion from chlorine gas to sodium hypochlorite as the primary chemical for disinfection of the water at both FWTP and SRWTP; Construction and operation of a secondary intake in the Sacramento River and pipelines for transferring water to SRWTP; Expansion of existing treatment processes at SR WTP to accommodate the additional capacity (including the grit basins, flocculation and sedimentation basins, filtration, and finished water storage); Installation of pipelines between the existing Sacramento River Intake and the replacement intake and SRWTP; and Improvement of the water transmission and distribution system in the vicinity of SRWTP to address critical hydraulic constrictions.

ceqa-76580510f2c54fd9c1.name: Liberty Ranch Elementary School Project
ceqa-76580510f2c54fd9c1.description: The proposed Liberty Ranch Elementary School Project (proposed project) involves the construction and operation of a new Kindergarten (K) through 6th grade public elementary school campus on an approximately 8.9-acre parcel (APN 148-1240-024-0000) east of Marengo Road and south of Twin Cities Road within the Liberty Ranch subdivision in the northeastern portion of the City of Galt, Sacramento County, California (project site). The project site is designated Public/Quasi-Public (PQ) in the City’s General Plan and identified as a future school site on the Liberty Ranch Tentative Subdivision Map. The proposed project would accommodate up to 600 students and approximately 60 staff members, including teachers, administrators, and support personnel. The proposed project would include seven one-story buildings totaling approximately 50,475 square feet, consisting of an administration and library building, a kindergarten classroom building (with four classrooms), a multipurpose building with an associated kitchen, and four classroom buildings serving grades 1 through 6 (with six classrooms each). Each building would be designed and constructed in accordance with the California Building Code (CBC) requirements and the Division of the State Architect (DSA) standards for structural safety, fire/life safety, and accessibility. The proposed project layout groups classrooms by grade level, with direct access to outdoor play areas, hard courts, and a playfield on the southern portion of the project site. A lunch canopy would be provided towards the middle of the project site and a dedicated kinder playground would be on the west side of the campus, adjacent to the kinder classroom building. Site improvements would include approximately 104,000 square feet (2.4 acres) of landscaping with drought-tolerant plantings, 237,500 square feet (5.45 acres) of hardscape improvements such as walkways, plazas, and play areas, and a surface parking lot providing 50 spaces, including ADA-accessible and electric-vehicle stalls, and a pick-up/drop-off curb. The proposed project would incorporate efficient, modern building design in accordance with the California Building Code (CBC) and Division of the State Architect (DSA) standards for seismic safety, energy efficiency, and accessibility. Primary access to the project site would be provided from Walnut Avenue via a drop-off and pick-up loop connected to the on-site parking lot. Pedestrian and bicycle access would be provided from Walnut Avenue and Liberty Ranch Road, which are planned two-lane local collectors with sidewalks and bicycle-friendly features. The school site would be delivered rough-graded with water, sewer, storm drain, and dry utilities extended to the site boundary by the Specific Plan developer. Construction of the proposed project would occur in a single phase over an estimated five- to seven-year period, including site preparation, grading, installation of underground utilities, building construction, paving, landscaping, and final finishing. Upon completion, the proposed project would operate on a traditional August to June academic calendar, with typical hours from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and would serve as a key public facility supporting the growing residential neighborhoods within the Liberty Ranch and Eastview Specific Plan Area.

ceqa-3405589406ec26235b.description: The Project consists of long-term (30 years) operations and maintenance of the Permittee’s electrical and natural gas facilities and infrastructure within its service area, as well as minor new construction activities and habitat conservation and enhancement activities. ceqa-d130df20d0434aa80d.agency: State Water Resources Control Board, Divison of Financial Assistance
ceqa-d130df20d0434aa80d.description: The State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) is a Responsible Agency for the Project. The State Water Board is funding the Project referred to internally as Tier 2 – Secondary Urgency Projects. Between March 20 and March 26, 2026, the Division of Financial Assistance received Cleanup and Abatement Account (CAA) funding applications from five Regional Water Quality Control Boards (Regional Boards) and the State Water Board’s Division of Water Quality (DWQ). The requested funding is proposed to be put towards the State Water Board’s Statewide Chemistry Contract (26-XXX-270, Chemistry Contract), San Jose State University Research Foundation (24-059-270, SJSURF Contract), and University of California, Davis (24-057-270, UC Davis Contract), all of which are managed by the State Water Board’s Office of Information Management and Analysis. The Project includes water quality sampling, monitoring, and analysis from sites across the State. While proposed sampling locations range from cleanup sites to specific waterbodies, to broader regionwide monitoring, the use of the requested funding across the various Regional Boards and DWQ have the same goal to monitor and gather data so that further site characterization is possible, to proactively prevent potentially negative impacts to waters of the State (either surface or groundwater).
