This project funds the procurement and installation of Juniper network equipment — including wireless access points, switches, and supporting hardware — integrated concurrent with construction to avoid costly retrofitting and operational disruption. Primary beneficiaries are CCC Headquarters staff who rely on network connectivity for administrative functions, program coordination, and statewide communications.

ceqa-b42458b0c797b7059e.name: Donnawood Way Water Main Project (C25-103)
ceqa-b42458b0c797b7059e.description: Replacement and reconstruction of existing water main serving the east-central portion of the Citrus Heights Water District's service area. Existing main is old and approaching its end of life and needs to be replaced to continue to provide reliable water service.

ceqa-ce432135b2829af44a.name: Star Motor
ceqa-ce432135b2829af44a.description: Site Plan and Design Review to remodel the existing single-unit dwelling and include an office for auto sales on site on a 0.4-acre parcel in the Light Industrial (M-1) Zone within the Citywide Design Review District.

ceqa-8e0d2257779c5ed369.name: Major Amendment to California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2024-018- 00 (ITP)
ceqa-8e0d2257779c5ed369.description: The discretionary approval by CDFW is the issuance of the ITP amendment identified above.The construction and operations of the Delta Conveyance Project in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and a portion of Alameda County as approved by the lead agency is expected to result in incidental take and impacts to habitat of Delta smelt (Hypomesus transpacificus), Longfin smelt (Spirinchus thaleichthys), Winterrun Chinook salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), Spring-run Chinook salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), White sturgeon (Acipenser transmontanus), California tiger salamander (Ambystoma californiense), Giant garter snake (Thamnophis gigas), Swainson’s hawk (Buteo swainsoni), Tricolored blackbird (Agelaius tricolor), Crotch bumble bee (Bombus crotchii), and Mason’s lilaeopsis (Lilaeopsis masonii). Crotch bumble bee and White sturgeon are designated as candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act. Longfin Smelt, Spring-run Chinook Salmon, California tiger salamander, Giant garter snake, Swainson’s hawk, and Tricolored blackbird are designated as threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act. Delta Smelt and Winter-run Chinook Salmon are designated as endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act. The California Fish and Game Commission designated Western burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia hypugaea) as a candidate species under CESA on October 25, 2024. This amendment to the ITP 1) adds Western burrowing owl as a Covered Species subject to the take authorization provided by the ITP, 2) excludes small diameter (less than 8-inch diameter) land-based soil borings and land-based soil borings with water quality testing using auger and/or mud rotary drill and soil and rock sampling, and land-based cone penetration tests (CPTs) using a truck-mounted rig equipped with a one-to-two-inch diameter cone, conducted prior to and inclusive of December 31, 2029 from coverage under the ITP, 3) amends the Project Description to reflect Project refinements resulting in engineering modifications to select project facilities, and 4) corrects a prior typographical oversight in the Tricolored blackbird compensatory mitigation nesting acres . The amendment makes the following changes to the existing ITP: (1) inserted an Amended ITP Background section, (2) revises the Effective Date and Expiration Date of the ITP section, (3) updates select sections of the Project Description to reflect Project refinements, (4) adds installation of small diameter land-based soil boring and land-based CPTs conducted before and inclusive of December 31, 2029 to the list of Components Not Included as Covered Activities, (5) adds Western burrowing owl as a Covered Species, (6) revises the impacts of the Taking on Covered Species to include Western burrowing owl, (7) revises Conditions of Approval 6.1, 6.2, 10.4, 10.8, 10.17, 11.3, 11.5, 11.11, 11.20, 11.38, and 12.4 to include Western Burrowing owl, (8) amends take Minimization measures to include Western Burrowing Owl measures including 11.109, 11.10, 11.111, 11.111.1, 11.111.2, 11.112, 11.113, 11.114, 11.114.1, 11.115, 11.116, 11.116.1, 11.117, 11.117.1, 11.117.2, 11.117.3, 11.117.4, 11.117.5, 11.118, and 11.119, (9) amends Condition of Approval numerals to accommodate Western burrowing owl conditions, (10) revises Table 12-1 to include Permanent and Temporary project Construction Impacts and Associated Compensatory Mitigation Acres for Western Burrowing Owl, (11) amends Compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act section to add findings for the addition of Western burrowing owl as a Covered Species through the amendment, (12) increases compensatory mitigation for Tricolored blackbird nesting habitat, and (13) amends attachments 2, 4, 5, 6 to include Western Burrowing owl as well as adds attachment 7 Amendments. The ITP referenced above as issued and amended by CDFW authorizes incidental take of Delta smelt, Longfin smelt, Winter-run Chinook salmon, Springrun Chinook salmon, White sturgeon, California tiger salamander, Giant garter snake, Swainson’s hawk, Tricolored blackbird, Crotch bumble bee, Mason’s lilaeopsis and Western burrowing owl that may occur as a result of preconstruction activities, construction, maintenance, and operational activities of the Delta Conveyance Project, as is more specifically described in the ITP.

ceqa-69c40c82483c10fd77.name: Collinsville 500/230 Kilovolt Substation Project
ceqa-69c40c82483c10fd77.description: The Project involves constructing the new Collinsville Substation, two 500 kV interconnection lines connecting Collinsville Substation to PG&E's existing Vaca Dixon-Tesla line, and a 230 kV transmission line connecting Collinsville Substation to PG&E's existing Pittsburg Substation, as well as constructing other ancillary infrastructure and modifying PG&E's existing facilities associated with interconnection
ceqa-69c40c82483c10fd77.crossStreets: Stratton Ln & Collinsville Rd (proposed substation site approx. 1 mile east)
ceqa-69c40c82483c10fd77.developmentType: Power:Electric Transmission Lines (Substation, Transmission, and Distribution Infrastructure)(Megawatts 1)

ceqa-92a7fc71be6adde7d3.name: Sheffield Subdivision (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-63769-R2)
ceqa-92a7fc71be6adde7d3.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-63769-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Sheffield 65 LLC. The project is limited to the development of a new multi-use trail along the northern and eastern property boundaries and along the new Lyonia Drive connection. The trail is part of a larger project that includes the demolition of the existing on-site single-family residence and removal of the associated septic system, removal of 21 on-site trees, and subdivision of the site into 65 single-family residential lots.

ceqa-dd78717259c314b2b6.name: 8700 Antelope North Road Tentative Parcel Map
ceqa-dd78717259c314b2b6.projectTitle: 8700 Antelope North Road Tentative Parcel Map
ceqa-dd78717259c314b2b6.description: The project is a request for a parcel map to divide a single 38-acre parcel into five parcels. The western portion of the property is currently developed and used for truck storage and parking (approximately 21 acres), and will be divided into Parcels 1, 2, 3, and 5. The eastern portion of the lot is undeveloped (approximately 17 acres) and will be Parcel 4. Parcel 4 is to be developed and used for truck storage and parking. Implementation of the project will require grading and installation of improvements on Parcel 4. Mass grading will be required for new paved roads - including a driveway across a drainage feature, new gravel truck parking areas, on-site detention basin and outfall structures, and an off-site detention basin to the north of the property, located in Placer County. Improvements will consist of the extension of utilities onto the subject property.
ceqa-dd78717259c314b2b6.crossStreets: Antelope North Road and Ridgepoint Drive

ceqa-fe5dce2155b89b82be.name: McCormack-Williamson Tract 2026 Levee Erosion Repair Project Sites 1 -14
ceqa-fe5dce2155b89b82be.projectTitle: McCormack-Williamson Tract 2026 Levee Erosion Repair Project Sites 1–14
ceqa-fe5dce2155b89b82be.description: Reclamation District No. 2110 is planning to repair 14 outboard levee erosion sites around the McCormack-Williamson Tract on Dead Horse Cut, Snodgrass Slough, and Lost Slough to address existing erosion and protect existing infrastructure.

ceqa-eda49d5425e35df47e.name: Vista Nueva Career & Technology High School Outdoor Learning Shade Structure & Path of Travel Improvements Project
ceqa-eda49d5425e35df47e.projectTitle: Vista Nueva Career & Technology High School Outdoor Learning Shade Structure & Path of Travel Improvements Project
ceqa-eda49d5425e35df47e.description: Installation of one 26x44 metal shade structure & associated site work, fabrication & delivery by owner/manufacturer, off-loading & assembly/installation by site contractor. Accessible upgrades, new toilet partitions (BLDG C), relocate toilet accessories (BDG A), adjust drinking fountain for a complete & operable project. Replacement of Paving & four ramps associated with portable classrooms (BLDG G, H, &I).

ceqa-8064a3b9ff1ad86da9.name: Hillsdale Elementary School Fencing & Ramp Replacement Project
ceqa-8064a3b9ff1ad86da9.projectTitle: Hillsdale Elementary School Fencing & Ramp Replacement Project
ceqa-8064a3b9ff1ad86da9.description: The replacement project includes the installation of nine aluminum ramps, three aluminum stairs, site improvements iincluding but not limited to flatwork, drainage, handrails, chain link perimeter fencing and gates for a complete and operational project. The project is replacing existing fencing, ramps, and stairs on a previously developed campus, and will not expand or increase existing capacity.

ceqa-3e17e91070ed383e9f.name: Javanifard and Zarghami Project
ceqa-3e17e91070ed383e9f.projectTitle: Folsom South of U.S. Highway 50 Specific Plan
ceqa-3e17e91070ed383e9f.description: The Project consists of developing a residential community and associated infrastructure including roads, utilities, landscaping, stormwater facilities, passive recreation open space, and conservation areas within the approximately 30-acre parcel. Construction of the Project will require mass grading using heavy equipment which will result in temporary and permanent impacts to waters of the state.

ceqa-adf6412c371802f86e.name: 1110 Front Street Deck Fix project
ceqa-adf6412c371802f86e.description: The existing outdoor deck overlooking the Sacramento River was deemed unsafe and in need of replacement. Project includes the removing and replacement of the existing decking with wood timber and structural steel.

ceqa-381d8d4b9900d9a6b7.name: Sale of conserved water to Sacramento Suburban Water District
ceqa-381d8d4b9900d9a6b7.projectTitle: Sale of conserved water to Sacramento Suburban Water District
ceqa-381d8d4b9900d9a6b7.description: San Juan Water District (San Juan) will sell up to 6,000 AF of water to Sacramento Suburban Water District (SSWD), which San Juan has previously conserved through various conservation efforts, including primarily the improved water use efficiency of its customers. The project does not involve the construction of any new facilities or the modification or expansion of capacity of existing facilities. San Juan will benefit from the project as a result of being better able to utilize the surface water supplies it has available to it for public benefit, as well as receiving revenue that will improve its wholesale enterprise’s financial position. SSWD will benefit from the receipt of surface water to improve the conjunctive management and health of its north groundwater basin.

ceqa-c8e9ffe8ab331f7839.name: 9th Street Separated Bikeway (T15245200)
ceqa-c8e9ffe8ab331f7839.description: The purpose of the 9th Street Bikeway Project is to improve bicycle connectivity along 9th Street and within the Central City. The 9th Street Bikeway is a key component of the Central City Mobility Project, which is designed to improve transportation options, reduce traffic congestion, and enhance mobility for pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists. The project will reallocate the available right-of-way to install an enhanced biking facility on 9th Street starting at Q Street and terminating at Broadway. The number of vehicle lanes will remain unchanged; however, the two class 2 bike lanes will be replaced by a parking-protected bike lane. All improvements are anticipated to be contained within the available right-of-way.

ceqa-a0e1de090cf6df9eec.name: WHITE ROCK NORTH MINE
ceqa-a0e1de090cf6df9eec.description: The White Rock North Mine project (project) proposes a 20-year mining operation to extract aggregate materials from old dredger mine tailings and reclaim the area to allow for future uses. The mining operation would also include the construction of an off-site conveyor to transport aggregate material to the nearby Teichert Grantline Plant. The proposed project is located on a 2,136-acre portion of the Aerojet Rocketdyne, Inc. (Aerojet) property in Sacramento County. The Project will require the following Sacramento County entitlements: • A SPA Implementation Permit to allow surface mining and reclamation on 2,125± acres for a period of 20 years, with an additional 3 years to complete reclamation. The Applicant requests the ability to mine and transport up to 3 million tons per year, with an average anticipated production of 1.25 million tons per year. Pursuant to Section 1A of the SPA Implementation Agreement, the SPA Implementation Permit will incorporate the mining plan, serve as the vehicle for imposing conditions, be subject to CEQA review, and be reviewed by the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors. • A Reclamation Plan to return the land to its current undeveloped condition, which is readily adaptable to future uses allowed under the Aerojet SPA. • A Work Authorization Permit prior to commencement of any surface mining activities. • A Use Permit for a 1± acre off-site conveyor connection and undercrossing at White Rock Road to transport mined materials to the existing, separately permitted off-site Teichert Grantline processing plant. Any permitting for the portion of the conveyor connection south of White Rock Road would be separately addressed by Teichert, if needed. • A Development Agreement between the Applicant and the County of Sacramento. • An Encroachment Permit and Improvement Plans as needed to allow installation of a conveyor undercrossing and driveway improvements along White Rock Road.

ceqa-9b4217d35322768bdb.name: 840 Watt Avenue Cargo Container
ceqa-9b4217d35322768bdb.description: The project consists of a Minor Use Permit to allow an existing cargo container on a 0.59-acre property zoned Residential 3 (RD-3). The existing cargo container is located at 840 Watt Avenue and is placed within the side yard of the property.

ceqa-305102e3aed210a72d.name: 6649 Rio Linda Blvd Cargo Container
ceqa-305102e3aed210a72d.description: The project consists of a Minor Use Permit to allow an existing cargo container on a 0.31-acre property zoned Residential 5 (RD-5). The existing cargo container is located at 6649 Rio Linda Boulevard and is placed within the side yard of the property.

ceqa-3a237d2030a91127d5.name: SMUD Reliable, Equitable, and Accessible Charging for Multi-family Housing (REACH 2) Phase 2 Project
ceqa-3a237d2030a91127d5.projectTitle: SMUD Reliable, Equitable, and Accessible Charging for Multi-family Housing (REACH 2) Phase 2 Project
ceqa-3a237d2030a91127d5.description: SMUD proposes to construct and operate 400 level 2 Electrical Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations at up to 50 multifamily housing sites located in SMUD's Service Area. This project will provide access for residents in approximately 3500 housing units. Construction of the electric vehicle charging infrastructure at these 6 locations will consist of digging, trenching, and other construction activities for installation of Level 2 chargers, potential replacement, or installation of 208 to 480 voltage alternating current down power transformers, and installation of power cabinets and switch gear to support the EV charging equipment. The installation of the EVSE chargers and transformers may require installation of conduit and underground cables to connect to existing infrastructure. All electrical conduits will be installed via trenching or underground directional boring. The construction crews will follow established best management practices for soil management during all ground disturbing activities. Where necessary the parking lots will be repaired once all work has been completed. All work completed on traffic paths of travel will utilize traffic management plans. The project is scheduled to begin March 2026 and be completed by December 2026.

ceqa-eb3e2c8a81c13a8cff.name: Acquisition of 6650 Asher Lane, Sacramento, CA 95828
ceqa-eb3e2c8a81c13a8cff.projectTitle: Acquisition of 6650 Asher Lane, Sacramento, CA 95828
ceqa-eb3e2c8a81c13a8cff.description: SMUD intends to purchase the property at 6650 Asher Lane, Sacramento, CA 95828 to proactively support expected future growth in the Elder Creek, Fruitridge, and Florin neighborhoods. In order for SMUD to reliably support long term growth in this area as increased electrification of existing customers continues, along with new customers coming into this area, SMUD is forecasting the need for another distribution substation in this general area. Although there are no immediate plans to construct a new substation, acquiring the property at this time will enable SMUD to respond promptly to future load growth as needed. There is no design, project footprint, capacity, or construction schedule that exists. Future use of the site is speculative; therefore, CEQA review for any project that would occur will be performed at the appropriate time.
ceqa-eb3e2c8a81c13a8cff.crossStreets: Asher Lane and Elder Creek Road

ceqa-ca626bca7c59df88e5.name: Hurley 1 Unit Replacement Project
ceqa-ca626bca7c59df88e5.description: The Hurley Unit 1 Replacement Project (Project) consists of replacing an aging 224-megavolt-ampere (MVA) transformer, tertiary structures, and buswork. The existing equipment associated with Unit 1 will be removed, including the surrounding grounding grid which is approximately 18-inches deep. A new 224-MVA transformer will be placed in the same location on a new concrete pad foundation. Additional related infrastructure, such as 12kV tertiary structures, bus support structures, and the drilled piers needed to support them, will also be placed within the same general area. The Project will also include modification and/or replacement of support infrastructure (i.e. switch pole, tap pole, pull box, conduit, grounding, etc.) to service the new transformer. Surface excavation will be required, reaching depths of up to 6 feet for the transformer foundation and up to 14 feet for the drilled piers supporting the tertiary and bus structures. The new substation structures will be similar in height to the existing ones. The overall footprint of the existing substation will remain the same. Construction is expected to begin in October 2027 and be completed by March 2028.

ceqa-67f649577d14b9d16e.name: Economic Development and Participation Agreement - Sunrise Tomorrow- Sunrise Sports Center
ceqa-67f649577d14b9d16e.projectTitle: Economic Development and Participation Agreement - Sunrise Tomorrow- Sunrise Sports Center
ceqa-67f649577d14b9d16e.description: The Economic Development and Participation Agreement (EDPA) is intended to facilitate development of the Sunrise Sports Center Project. The EDPA will clearly establish the roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations between the City and its private partners. This project pertains solely to the financial agreement; any subsequent development will be subject to the appropriate entitlement processes and review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

ceqa-c54aa39733d223914f.name: Cove Park Shade Canopy
ceqa-c54aa39733d223914f.description: The project involves installation of a 45' x 43' x 22' shade canopy to cover the existing playground structure at Cove Park. The project also includes removal and replacement of the playground access ramp.

ceqa-22973a46d4b717b1a1.name: Arcadian United States Highway 50 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-0293)
ceqa-22973a46d4b717b1a1.projectTitle: Arcadian United States Highway 50 Middle-Mile Broadband Network Project (Encroachment Permit 03-25-6-BB-0293)
ceqa-22973a46d4b717b1a1.description: Arcadian, in coordination with the California Department of Technology and the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), proposes to install underground broadband infrastructure consisting of conduit, fiber optic cable, vaults, and markers on United States Highway 50 (US 50) between post mile (PM) 2.3 and PM 23.136 in Sacramento County and between PM 0.0 and PM 0.9 in El Dorado County

ceqa-2b8c20eb3f3e41632a.name: H Street Cycle Track
ceqa-2b8c20eb3f3e41632a.description: This Project will improve the existing one-way eastbound Class II facility and the one-block Class III section between 7th and 8th Streets and provide safe cycle crossing of the light rail tracks. The project proposes to install a two-way separated bikeway on the south side of H Street between 5th and 10th Streets. Travel lanes may be reduced from two to one on some blocks to accommodate the bikeway. Other potential improvements include traffic signal modifications and accessibility improvements. The project also proposes to install a Class IV buffered bikeway on the east side of 10th Street between H Street and I Street. The improvements proposed for this project would be implemented within the City's existing right-of-way.

ceqa-c49b609872c96ee5ae.name: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) Warehouse
ceqa-c49b609872c96ee5ae.projectTitle: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) Warehouse
ceqa-c49b609872c96ee5ae.description: CDPH proposes to renew warehouse lease located at 837 N. Market Boulevard in Sacramento, CA. Total space is 14,260 s/f comprised of 729 s/f of office space and 13,531 s/f of warehouse space.

ceqa-56665468333379b63e.name: Water Distribution Infrastructure
ceqa-56665468333379b63e.description: This project will replace and enhance existing water mains and pipleines that will improve the ability for the district to move water within boundaries and outside fo the service area. These facilities will provide the opportunity for the district to utilize existing and recently constructed groundwater wells. The Regional Water Authority is the lead under CEQA and is receiving funding through the State of California which it will then reimburse to Fair Oaks Water District.

ceqa-07428d4b6b6525a7be.name: Brannan Island Marina Restoration Project – Geotech Investigation
ceqa-07428d4b6b6525a7be.projectTitle: Brannan Island State Recreation Area – Facilities Improvements
ceqa-07428d4b6b6525a7be.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-07428d4b6b6525a7be.description: Conduct geotechnical investigations at Brannan Island State Recreation Area marina to evaluate subsurface conditions at the site and provide geotechnical engineering design parameters and recommendations for the work proposed for the marina reconstruction project. Work will drill use a truck-mounted drill, equipped with mud rotary auger to drill four (4) exploratory borings within the existing marina, on land a minimum of 30 feet away from the toe of any levees around the marina perimeter. Each boring will be 4-inches-diameter and up to 51.5 feet-deep, with representative soil samples recorded for future analysis.

ceqa-19a89a2f78ba5cea1b.name: BLA-1025-0031 Sunridge Village 4 Boundary Line Adjustment
ceqa-19a89a2f78ba5cea1b.projectTitle: BLA-1025-0031 Sunridge Village 4 Boundary Line Adjustment
ceqa-19a89a2f78ba5cea1b.description: Boundary line adjustments among 2 parcels in the City of Rancho Cordova zoned Residential (RD 5 and RD 10). The proposed adjustments are being made solely for the purpose of correcting, confirming, or relocating property lines.

ceqa-966a17d75e3859a676.name: American River Parkway Natural Resource Management Plan
ceqa-966a17d75e3859a676.projectTitle: American River Parkway Natural Resources Management Plan
ceqa-966a17d75e3859a676.description: Project involves the restoration of 30 acres of degraded land to native grassland and forb habitat. Non-native invasive grasses and forbs will be treated using integrated pest management strategies including mowing, grazing, light disking, and chemical treatments. Native seed mixes will be installed by drill-seeding or broadcasting, and mulch may be used to protect seeds and help retain moisture. WCB Project Tracker ID: 2025020.

ceqa-f82a29953f2bc6cfce.name: Upgrade and modernize the Klamath Training Room - Cal EPA Building
ceqa-f82a29953f2bc6cfce.projectTitle: Upgrade and modernize the Klamath Training Room - Cal EPA Building
ceqa-f82a29953f2bc6cfce.description: The proposed project will upgrade and modernize the Klamath Training Room for the State Water Resources Control Board office located in Sacramento, CA. The project will involve upgrading existing analog equipment to digital equipment. The room footprint will remain the same. All electrical work will be within existing raceways. Walls will not be moved or otherwise impacted.

ceqa-0745131755059d871a.name: Prescribed Burn
ceqa-0745131755059d871a.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-0745131755059d871a.description: This project will conduct a prescribed burn in the approximately 180-acre Vernal Pool Management Areas within Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area. Vegetation is primarily medusa-head grass and the associated buildup of flammable thatch. This project will reduce Medusa-head seed viability and plant cover which is beneficial to the health of the vernal pool landscapes. Work will use water tenders, Type 3 fire engines, Type 6 fire engines, hand tools, mowers and/or string trimmers, drip torches, and dozers.

ceqa-bec53b20fcbd003fec.name: 4107 and 4047 Smallwood Ln Lot Line Adjustment
ceqa-bec53b20fcbd003fec.projectTitle: 4107 and 4047 Smallwood Ln Lot Line Adjustment
ceqa-bec53b20fcbd003fec.description: The project consists of a lot line adjustment between the subject parcels, addressed at 4107 Smallwood Lane and 4047 Smallwood Lane, located North of Capitola Avenue on a private road, in the Fair Oaks community of unincorporated Sacramento County. The project proposes to shift the common lot line between APNs -006 and -035

ceqa-3b138b763bbf0100ad.name: HP Hood Energy Efficiency and Wastewater Treatment Project
ceqa-3b138b763bbf0100ad.projectTitle: HP Hood Energy Efficiency and Wastewater Treatment Project
ceqa-3b138b763bbf0100ad.description: This project will implement wastewater treatment upgrades and steam system efficiency measures at the Recipient's facility. The wastewater treatment technology will include a screw press, flowmeter, feed pump, polymer feeder, and equalization tank. The efficiency upgrades will include insulation and condensate pumps and headers. This project will improve energy efficiency and reduce the facility’s energy usage, water consumption, and greenhouse gas emissions. The project is consistent with the California Energy Commission's mission of leading the state to a 100 percent clean energy future.

ceqa-e3982cc37a59eb41b7.name: Leland Stanford Mansion Fourth Floor Window Rehabilitation
ceqa-e3982cc37a59eb41b7.projectTitle: Leland Stanford Mansion Fourth Floor Window Rehabilitation
ceqa-e3982cc37a59eb41b7.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-e3982cc37a59eb41b7.description: This project will rehabilitate the windows on the fourth floor of the Leland Stanford Mansion in Leland Stanford Mansion State Historic Park to help protect and preserve this historic building. The windows were restored circa 2003 but the materials used during the restoration have caused original materials and joints to deteriorate.

ceqa-6c5e7cc571a16b1533.name: SMUD POWER - Preventing Outages with Enhanced Reliability
ceqa-6c5e7cc571a16b1533.projectTitle: SMUD POWER - Preventing Outages with Enhanced Reliability
ceqa-6c5e7cc571a16b1533.description: The project will deploy grid infrastructure upgrades to replace 230 network protectors and an estimated 210,000-280,000 circuit feed of underground cable in the SMUD service territory. The Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition ready (SCADA-ready) systems in the new network protectors to allow for remote monitoring and operation, which supports efficient energy management and quick responses to potential issues. The underground cable replacement will retire 1960s cables containing lead, which pose an environmental risk as they age. Additionally, the replacement will also retire pre-1981 direct buried unjacketed cables that frequently fail and disrupt service.

ceqa-d41431f03ad6e2a0bf.name: Carillion Water Treatment Plant Deep Well Project
ceqa-d41431f03ad6e2a0bf.projectTitle: Carillion Water Treatment Plant Deep Well Project
ceqa-d41431f03ad6e2a0bf.description: The City of Galt Public Works Department plans to replace Well 16 within the Carillion Water Treatment Plant (WTP) and target a new aquifer. The existing well would be destroyed. The Carillion WTP has two wells, River Oaks Well and Well 16, both of which undergo a chlorine and chemical treatment process for arsenic, iron, and manganese removal in raw water. Upgrades to the water treatment system would occur. These upgrades would include construction of a production well, booster pump station, and storage tank. A permanent test well will also be placed for future well replacement needs. The Project area is a flat 1.4-acre parcel with a water treatment system located at the western end and an open grassy area extending across the eastern portion of the parcel. Landscape trees are present, some of which would be removed for the construction of a new driveway connecting to the street. Trenching through landscaped areas will be completed for new drainage and piping to Di Maggio Boulevard. Modifying and/or moving existing irrigation is also planned. Surface grading would be done to improve drainage to storm drain inlets. At the grassy unimproved eastern portion of the site there would be installation of a new 1.5 MG tank, gravel at the location of a second future 1.5 MG tank, a concrete vault, underground piping and conduits, a booster pump station extending below ground, and pavement at all unpaved areas up to the existing treatment system slab.
ceqa-d41431f03ad6e2a0bf.crossStreets: Carillion Boulevard and D Maggio Way

ceqa-24b4b7f52a9e1ebcbd.name: Sacramento Railyards Digital Sign Program - Digital Billboards at Locations 1 and 2 (DR26-005)- Prior Project Railyards Specific Plan Update Project (P15-040)
ceqa-24b4b7f52a9e1ebcbd.projectTitle: Railyards Specific Plan Update, KP Medical Center, MLS Stadium, & Stormwater Outfall Subsequent EIR
ceqa-24b4b7f52a9e1ebcbd.description: The Sacramento Railyards Digital Sign Program includes the construction and operation of up to five digital billboards within the Sacramento Railyards Specific Plan (RSP) Area (or Railyards Special Planning District). The proposed project consists of the two freeway-oriented digital billboards along Interstate 5 (I-5) in the western RSP Area (Locations 1 and 2). The proposed digital billboard faces will be light-emitting diode (LED)-through-hole design, with an LED pixel pitch of nineteen millimeters.

ceqa-49eba347ae2d0360f2.name: Former Dorris Lumber & Moulding Company Revised Interim Removal Action Workplan
ceqa-49eba347ae2d0360f2.projectTitle: Supplemental to 2035 General Plan MEIR to Address Changes to Roadways Improvements in North Natomas
ceqa-49eba347ae2d0360f2.description: The Project consists of the implementation of the Former Dorris Lumber & Moulding Company Revised Interim Removal Action Workplan (RAW) to address soil impacted with chlordane, lead, and dioxins/furans identified in subsurface soils that exceed residential screening levels. The RAW is associated with a proposed redevelopment of the Site for which the City of Sacramento is the CEQA lead agency. The site remediation activities consist of Soil Excavation and Offsite Disposal: Excavation of approximately 2,525 cubic yards of soil above residential screening levels from various locations across the Site. The approximate total area of soil disturbance activities is less than 1 acre and will range from 18 inches below ground surface (bgs) to six feet bgs. The soil excavation, stockpiling, and confirmation sampling will take approximately five weeks and the off site disposal will take approximately three weeks requiring approximately 158 truck trips.

ceqa-df89a1198a2f4b48b6.projectTitle: Supplemental to 2035 General Plan MEIR to Address Changes to Roadways Improvements in North Natomas

ceqa-157d382c49e43c1393.name: SMUD Thornton Avenue Former Electrical Substation Remedial Action Plan
ceqa-157d382c49e43c1393.projectTitle: SMUD Thornton Avenue Former Electrical Substation Remedial Action Plan
ceqa-157d382c49e43c1393.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-157d382c49e43c1393.description: The proposed Remedial Action Plan for the remediation of contaminants of concern in soil at the SMUD Thornton Avenue former electrical substation. The remedial action would consist of excavating soil on the Site and eastern adjacent property containing arsenic and lead. The cleanup would also reduce the potential for leaching to groundwater. The excavated areas would be backfilled with clean soil. All excavated soil would be removed from the Site and transported to an appropriate, permitted off-Site facility for disposal. Asphalt pavements and concrete curbing on the eastern adjacent property would be restored after backfilling the excavation with clean soil.

ceqa-1a3b78d7db73f48a11.name: The Fruits of Our Labors, Inc. (Z25-043)
ceqa-1a3b78d7db73f48a11.projectTitle: The Fruits of Our Labors, Inc. (Z25-043)
ceqa-1a3b78d7db73f48a11.description: A request for a Conditional Use Permit minor modification to change the previously approved floor area for cannabis land uses within an existing building, as follows: 1. Decrease cannabis cultivation from 19,222 to 18,641 square feet; 2. Increase cannabis distribution from 2,590 to 3,493 square feet; 3. Increase cannabis manufacturing from 410 to 932 square feet; and 4. Increase cannabis dispensary delivery-only from 800 to 1,406 square feet. No exterior changes are proposed to the existing building or site improvements. The project site is a 1.23-acre developed parcel within the Heavy Industrial Zone (M-2S). On February 13, 2018, the Zoning Administrator approved with conditions a CUP for Cannabis Production (cultivation), within the existing warehouse building, and two proposed interior additions (Z17-199). The project involved the division of the building into two equal tenant spaces (front and rear), plus the addition of 2nd floor mezzanines in each separate tenant space, for a total approved cannabis cultivation area of 23,022 square feet in the entire building. The project also included SPDR for minor exterior changes to the building (entry-exit doors and roll-up door changes). On February 28, 2019, the Zoning Administrator approved with conditions a CUP for an 800-square- foot Delivery-Only Cannabis Dispensary, and a CUP Modification of the prior approved Cannabis Production use, to reduce the previously approved cannabis cultivation area by 800 square feet from 23,022 to 22,222 square feet (Z18-077). The proposed Delivery-Only Cannabis Dispensary was to be a separate tenant space carved out of the rear tenant space, at the northwest corner of the building. On February 03, 2020, the Zoning Administrator approved with conditions a CUP modification of the prior approved Cannabis Production use for a new tenant space for cannabis manufacturing and cannabis distribution, that will thereby reallocate the previously approved square footage of the specific areas devoted to cannabis cultivation, distribution, and manufacturing (Z19-128).

ceqa-9f02827ff91be56ee4.name: Permit No. 19893 – Railroad Bridge 140.11 Segment Replacement Project
ceqa-9f02827ff91be56ee4.projectTitle: Permit No. 19893 – Railroad Bridge 140.11 Segment Replacement Project
ceqa-9f02827ff91be56ee4.description: To remove an existing 73-span, 1,094 feet-long, timber stringer glulam-open deck (TSGOD) UPRR bridge section (Bridge MP 140.11) that crosses the American River overflow area and replace it with a 42-span, 1,258 feet long prestressed concrete box (PCB) bridge.

ceqa-54c443d6879f2fac84.name: NOTICE OF PREPARATION OF A SUPPLEMENTAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT FOR THE RIVER DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN
ceqa-54c443d6879f2fac84.projectTitle: NOTICE OF PREPARATION OF A SUPPLEMENTAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT FOR THE RIVER DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN
ceqa-54c443d6879f2fac84.description: The City of Sacramento (City) is the Lead Agency responsible for preparation of a Supplemental Environmental Impact Report (SEIR) for the proposed River District Specific Plan Update (Plan). The SEIR to be prepared by the City will evaluate potential significant environmental effects of the proposed Plan and other actions associated with the proposed Plan. Since adoption of the original 2011 River District Specific Plan, new information, changed circumstances, and proposed updates to the Plan warrant additional environmental review pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Written comments regarding the issues that should be covered in the SEIR, including potential alternatives to the proposed Project and the scope of the analysis, are invited. The SEIR for the proposed Plan is being prepared in compliance with CEQA. Under CEQA, the City, as lead agency, must issue a Notice of Preparation (NOP) to inform trustee agencies, the public, and responsible agencies of its decision to prepare an SEIR. The purpose of the NOP is to provide information describing the Plan and its potential environmental effects and to solicit input on the scope and content of the SEIR. Agencies should comment on environmental issues related to their statutory responsibilities. The SEIR will provide an evaluation of potential environmental impacts that may result from implementation of the proposed project. The proposed Plan project description, location, and environmental issue areas that may be affected by development of the proposed project are described below. The SEIR will evaluate potentially significant environmental impacts of the proposed project, on both a direct and cumulative basis, identify mitigation measures that may be feasible to lessen or avoid such impacts, and identify reasonable alternatives to the proposed project.
ceqa-54c443d6879f2fac84.developmentType: Other (Area includes a mix of land uses.)

ceqa-c37b8890936c062fc8.name: Long Term Warren Act Contract
ceqa-c37b8890936c062fc8.description: The project is a 25-year Long Term Warren Act Contract between San Juan Water District and the Bureau of Reclamation to allow conveyance of up to 25,000 acre feet per year of non CVP water from Placer County Water Agency through federal facilities including Folsom Reservoir and Folsom Dam, using existing facilities and consistent with historic water conveyance.

ceqa-8ee83748766eeedfb7.name: Warren Act Contract One-Year Extension
ceqa-8ee83748766eeedfb7.description: The project is a 1-year extension to an existing Warren Act Contract between San Juan Water District and the Bureau of Reclamation to allow conveyance of up to 25,000 acre feet per year of non CVP water from Placer County Water Agency through federal facilities including Folsom Reservoir and Folsom Dam, using existing facilities and consistent with historic water conveyance.

ceqa-0d35d3444f1f346ecf.name: Capitol Mall Office Buildings Demolition Project
ceqa-0d35d3444f1f346ecf.projectTitle: Capitol Mall Office Buildings Demolition Project
ceqa-0d35d3444f1f346ecf.description: The project would involve the demolition of three state-owned office buildings that have a combined gross floor area of approximately 729,700 square feet to remove underutilized office space and allow for the future development of another use within these parcels. Upon completion of the demolition, the site will be ready for construction of a future use. DGS has been in discussions with California State University, Sacramento (hereinafter referred to as Sacramento State or University) for the potential reuse of the site. The intent of the proposed project is to demolish the subject properties regardless of whether a transfer to Sacramento State occurs. Because the University has not yet developed specific plans for the project site, there is insufficient detail to analyze future uses at a project level of detail (see CEQA Guidelines Section 15161) in the EIR. Accordingly, as identified above, the EIR will evaluate the site’s future development at a programmatic level consistent with CEQA Guidelines Section 15168. Once a future land recipient is confirmed and a more detailed development scenario is identified, the University or other appropriate lead agency will prepare a separate CEQA analysis for the development scenario.

ceqa-5530b9b52497033e88.name: St. Thomas Estates
ceqa-5530b9b52497033e88.description: The St. Thomas Estates Project (project) consist of rezoning 2.04 acres of a 5.49- acre parcel to establish consistent zoning and the creation of a 27-unit single-family residential subdivision located between Florin Road and Gerber Road, on Gardner Avenue, within unincorporated Sacramento County. The following entitlements are being requested for the project: 1. A Rezone of an existing 5.49-acre split zoned parcel to change 2.04 acres of Agricultural Residential 5 (AR-5) to Residential 5 (RD-5) to create consistent zoning across the project site. 2. A Tentative Subdivision Map to create 27-unit single-family residential lots. 3. A Major Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). The project is considered infill development, referring to the construction or redevelopment of vacant and / or underutilized parcels in existing urban areas (Sacramento County, 2024a). Infill sites are generally small (several acres or less), with eliminated or reduced habitat, scattered through urbanized areas, and are located near existing infrastructure, transportation and services. The project site is currently vacant and surrounded to the north, east, and south by the Gardner Parke Subdivision Project (2004-0218, PLNP2016-00077), which is currently under construction and existing single-family dwellings to the west of Gardner Avenue. The project would be served by existing infrastructure (water, sewer, electricity, and roadways) in the area. As previously described, the project site is a split zoned 5.49-acre parcel, 2.04 acres zoned AR- 5 and 3.45 acres zoned RD-5 located along the east side of Gardner Avenue within the Florin- Vineyard Gap area. The parcels created as a result of the project would range in size from 5,53,6 square feet to 9,652 square feet. Vehicular access to the project site would be provided via Gardner Avenue, Fawnbar Way, and Edgeland Way. Fawnbar Way and Edgeland Way are currently under construction as part of the Gardner Park Subdivision and end at the edge of the project site property line. These roadways would be extended through the project site to provide access and connect to Oneta Way and Irondequoit Way (east-west roads within the Garnder Parke Subdivision). Access to Parcels 1 through 5 of the project would be via Gardner Avenue. The remaining parcels would be accessed via Fawnbar Way and / or Edgeland Way (Plate AD-3). Frontage improvements along Gardner Avenue include two lanes of travel, a bike lane, a seven-foot landscape corridor, and a six-foot separated sidewalk. These improvements are consistent with the requirements of a 42-foot Parkway I, as required in tho Florin-Vineyard Gap Community Plan (FVGCP).

ceqa-e27ee9974c6927a387.name: Bar None Auctions
ceqa-e27ee9974c6927a387.description: The project includes the development of three (3) parcels, totaling approximately 47 acres, for the purpose of using the land to store and auction surplus heavy equipment, commercial trucks, agricultural equipment, and industrial support items. The project also includes a request for a Use Permit, Special Development Permit, and Design Review to establish an online auction business facility that would include: a 21,510 square-foot two-story office and reception building, a 12,800 square-foot workshop, and outdoor storage yard for trucks and heavy equipment.

ceqa-5276a7d0e17905e487.name: 7948 Sunset Avenue Subdivision Map
ceqa-5276a7d0e17905e487.description: The applicant is proposing to divide a single legal parcel totaling approximately 1.77 acres into seven parcels and a remainder, resulting in the following parcel sizes: Lot 1 = 6,546 square feet, Lot 2 = 8,038 square feet, Lot 3 = 5,337 square feet, Lot 4 = 5,620 square feet, Lot 5 = 5,653 square feet, Lot 6 = 5,558 square feet, Lot 7 = 5,462 square feet, and a Remainder Lot = 16,768 square feet. The existing structures on Lots 1 through 7 will be removed as part of the project. The existing primary home will be maintained on the Remainder Lot. The removal of on-site trees is anticipated to allow for development. The Remainder Lot will maintain access from Sunset Avenue through an existing driveway. The seven lots will be accessible from a new connector road proposed to tie into the existing Shrewsbury Avenue and Glenbar Way on the east side of the project site.

ceqa-e89ce5e1b5318b5aba.name: Housing Element Amendment 1 and Zoning Code Amendment (Program A2)
ceqa-e89ce5e1b5318b5aba.projectTitle: Housing Element Amendment 1 and Zoning Code Amendment (Program A2)
ceqa-e89ce5e1b5318b5aba.description: The proposed project consists of: 1. Housing Element Amendment 1, a mid-cycle amendment to the 2021-2029 Housing Element required to achieve full compliance with State Housing Element Law. Amendment 1 incorporates parcel-specific site analysis, updated Appendix C land inventory, and updated fair-housing analysis reflecting outcomes of the Countywide Rezone Program (Program A 1 ). Amendment 1 makes no land-use changes, authorizes no development, and does not modify zoning, densities, or development standards. 2. Zoning Code Amendment (Program A2) to incorporate the State definition of "use by right" for qualifying lower-income housing developments pursuant to Government Code §65583.2(i). The amendment is administrative and does not alter development capacity, zoning boundaries, allowable intensities, or authorize any construction. The proposed project does not authorize physical development and does not include any rezoning or modification to land use designations. All physical environmental impacts associated with Program A 1 rezones were previously analyzed in the certified Subsequent Environmental Impact Report for PLNP2020- 00042 (SCH Number: 2023060304). The following entitlements are required for the proposed project: 1. A General Plan Amendment to amend the 2021-2029 Housing Element post adoption of the Countywide Rezone Program (Housing Action Plan Program A 1) approved through the Sacramento County Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA) rezone project (PLNP2020-00042). 2. A Zoning Ordinance Amendment to Chapter 1 section 1.7.3.A of the Zoning Code to integrate the state definition of Use by Right as defined in California Government Code Section 65583.2(i) (Housing Action Plan Program A2).

ceqa-b7b2afdb2dbe27a0e5.name: Lease Agreement No. 1930 District Attorney's Office
ceqa-b7b2afdb2dbe27a0e5.projectTitle: Lease Agreement No. 1930 District Attorney's Office
ceqa-b7b2afdb2dbe27a0e5.description: The District Attorney is moving to 980 9th Street. The leased space will consist of approximately 121,074 square feet of office space, plus an additional 2,164 square feet of storage space, for a combined total of 123,238 square feet. Improvements will include office and cubicle workspaces, conference rooms, breakrooms, new LED lighting and flooring throughout, and access control and alarm systems. The lease term is for a total of 15 years.

ceqa-34ef62981e30fb7d89.name: Trilogy Medwaste West (PLNG25-020)
ceqa-34ef62981e30fb7d89.projectTitle: City of Elk Grove Climate Compass Project
ceqa-34ef62981e30fb7d89.description: The Trilogy MedWaste Project (“Project”) consists of a request for a Text Amendment to Elk Grove Municipal Code (EGMC) Title 23, Zoning, to amend the following: 1. Add the “Medical Waste Transfer Facility” use to Chapter 23.27 (Allowed Uses and Required Entitlements); 2. Add an associated description to EGMC Section 23.26.050; 3. Allow a “Medical Waste Transfer Facility” use upon approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) in the Heavy Industrial (HI) zoning district; 4. Add minimum parking requirements for “Medical Waste Transfer Facility” to EGMC Table 23.58-2; and 5. Add definition of “Medical Waste” to EGMC Section 23.100.020 (General definitions). The Project also includes a Conditional Use Permit to allow the operation of a new medical waste transfer facility in an existing tenant space in an industrial building on the Project site. No exterior improvements are proposed as part of the Project.

ceqa-c495cbebc48859c6a6.name: Richfield Way Bike Trail Irrigation and Tree Planting
ceqa-c495cbebc48859c6a6.projectTitle: Richfield Way Bike Trail Irrigation and Tree Planting
ceqa-c495cbebc48859c6a6.description: The project consists of installing, a bubbler irrigation system with a backflow preventer with an enclosure on a concrete pad, an irrigation controller, and native tree planting along the existing bike and detention basin along an existing bike trail on Richfield Way.

ceqa-6b2cc4c73ebe2cae40.name: Prime Data Centers
ceqa-6b2cc4c73ebe2cae40.projectTitle: McClellan Air Force Base Draft Final Reuse Plan and Draft Implementation Plan
ceqa-6b2cc4c73ebe2cae40.description: The project consists of the following entitlement requests: 1. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standards: Minimum Front Yard Setback (Section 5.6.2.A, Table 5.14): 56 feet. As proposed, the front yard setback is 31 feet. 2. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). The project applicant is requesting the above entitlements to allow for a proposed data center expansion with incidental administrative offices on approximately 7.74 acres. The site is developed with a one-story 68,450± square foot building, known as Prime Data Center, an operational electric substation, and associated parking lot, fencing, and landscaping. The request includes the construction of a new two-story data center (110,269± square feet), a two-story administration building (11,276± square feet), and a one-story generator building (8,378± square feet).Thirty (30) parking spaces will be added for on-site employees along with new landscaping for parking lot and public street frontages. New landscaping will also be provided along the perimeters of each newly constructed building. CONTROL NUMBER: PLNP2024-00238

ceqa-993687f274c93dddbb.name: Adoption of Resolution of Florin County Water District Following Consideration of Timely Submitted Written Objections and District Responses
ceqa-993687f274c93dddbb.projectTitle: Adoption of Resolution of Florin County Water District Following Consideration of Timely Submitted Written Objections and District Responses
ceqa-993687f274c93dddbb.description: The Florin County Water District Board heard and considered submitted written objections and District responses to those objections. After doing so, the Board adopted a resolution finding the objections and responses did not warrant reduction, modification, delay, or clarification of the proposed rates, and to proceed with the scheduled Proposition 218 Protest Hearing on February 11, 2026. The project benefited members of the public and the District by complying with AB 2257 as part of the Proposition 218 process.

ceqa-1a281619f00680b026.name: Adoption of Resolution of Florin County Water District Determining that the Proposed Water Rates Comply with California's Proposition 218.
ceqa-1a281619f00680b026.projectTitle: Adoption of Resolution of Florin County Water District Determining that the Proposed Water Rates Comply with California's Proposition 218.
ceqa-1a281619f00680b026.description: The Florin County Water District Board held the required public hearing under Proposition 218 for consideration of proposed water rates. There was a presentation of the proposed rates, an opportunity for public comment, and a counting of all protests submitted in public view. There was no majority protest, so the Board considered and adopted the proposed rates. This will benefit the public by ensuring the District can continue to provide water to its customers, as well as benefit the District by ensuring it has sufficient funding to provide water to its customers and meet state requirements.

ceqa-7b35d8469332d21651.name: St. Vincent de Paul Watt Avenue Parcel Map
ceqa-7b35d8469332d21651.projectTitle: St. Vincent de Paul Watt Avenue Parcel Map
ceqa-7b35d8469332d21651.description: The project consists of the following entitlements: 1. A Tentative Parcel Map to subdivide an existing 1.87-acre parcel into two new parcels within the Light Commercial zoning district. 2. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). The proposed parcel map will split the existing commercial site into two new commercial parcels, in which each parcel will retain one existing commercial building, along with existing paved parking lot and on-site landscaping. No new development is proposed with this request.

ceqa-06fea10903a16f4c63.name: 7101 Winding Way Parcel Map
ceqa-06fea10903a16f4c63.description: The proposed project is a request for the following entitlements: 1. A Tentative Parcel Map to divide an existing 0.94-acre parcel into four new parcels in the Residential 5 (RD-5) zoning district. 2. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standards: a. Public Street Frontage (Section 5.4.2.B, Table 5.7.A [8]): Up to two lots may be served by a private drive without meeting the public street frontage requirement. As proposed, four lots will be served by a private drive. 3. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). The proposed entitlements will result in four new residential lots, with one of the parcels retaining the existing single-family residence, while the remaining three parcels will be ready to be developed for new single-family residences.

ceqa-5ad5015e90b80c3129.name: Eswaran Tentative Parcel Map
ceqa-5ad5015e90b80c3129.description: The project consists of the division of an existing 1.08-acre parcel into two resultant lots to be served by an existing private drive. The site contains an existing single-family dwelling which will remain on resultant Parcel B. Resultant Parcel A will be developed with a single-family dwelling in the future. The project consists of the following entitlements: 1. A Tentative Parcel Map to divide a 1.08-acre parcel into two parcels in the Residential Density 2 (RD- 2) zoning district. 2. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standard: • Public Street Frontage (Section 5.4.2.B, Table 5.7.A): Up to two lots may be served by a private drive without meeting the public street frontage requirement. As proposed, the existing private drive will serve five lots. 3. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).

ceqa-39156471b87f5e50ce.projectTitle: Folsom South of U.S. Highway 50 Specific Plan
ceqa-39156471b87f5e50ce.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed an Extension to Master Streambed Alteration Agreement Notification Number 1600-2012-0198-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Folsom South Area Group. This Extension extends the Master Streambed Alteration Agreement expiration from February 11, 2026 to February 11, 2031. All other conditions in the original Master Streambed Alteration Agreement remain in effect.

ceqa-4d6d5a8515adc6d2cd.name: EA 03-1J630_SR 99 PM 6.07 & 7.06 Willow Slough Bridge Replacement (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-49817-R2) Amendment
ceqa-4d6d5a8515adc6d2cd.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed an amendment to the Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-49817-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, California Department of Transportation, as represented by Katlin Ly-Lee. The amendment increases project impacts by permanently removing an additional 0.02 acres of riparian habitat. A valley oak tree measured 12-inch diameter at breast height will be removed. Compensatory mitigation will be increased from 0.52 acres to 0.60 acres of created or restored riparian habitat. Project applicant will also be updated.

ceqa-af85a920199cd80ee6.name: Sutter Health Park Perimeter Fence Replacement
ceqa-af85a920199cd80ee6.projectTitle: Sutter Health Park Perimeter Fence Replacement
ceqa-af85a920199cd80ee6.description: Replacement of an existing perimeter fence and easement dedication of street frontage for City monument signage and public art.

ceqa-b919170e44ff38fdca.name: Panhandle Villages 6 & 7 (Lower East Village) Project (DR25-146) in the Panhandle PUD (P16-013)
ceqa-b919170e44ff38fdca.projectTitle: Panhandle Annexation and Planned Unit Development
ceqa-b919170e44ff38fdca.description: The project consists of construction of 214 single-unit dwellings on individual lots of varying sizes consistent with FPM-0027, originally approved under Z22-054. These parcels are in the Single-Unit Density or Duplex Dwelling Zone (R-1A-PUD) and General Plan Designation of Suburban Neighborhood Low Density (SNLD-V in the Panhandle PUD). The proposed dwellings meet height, setback, and lot coverage requirements for the R-1A zone and Panhandle PUD. The designs will utilize stucco siding, horizontal lap siding, and decorative finishes. As designed, the project meets all applicable development standards for the R-1A zone and the architectural Panhandle PUD design guidelines. Furthermore, the project is deemed consistent with the citywide design standards in relation to massing and scale.
ceqa-b919170e44ff38fdca.crossStreets: north of Del Paso Road and west of Sorento Road

ceqa-f736afe3cc66945d1f.name: CARB 5th Floor Occupancy Conversion - Cal EPA Building
ceqa-f736afe3cc66945d1f.projectTitle: CARB 5th Floor Occupancy Conversion - Cal EPA Building
ceqa-f736afe3cc66945d1f.description: The proposed project consists of converting an existing storage room and conference room to open office space. This conversion will prepare the space for new modular systems furniture (MSF) workstations and provide electrical connections for the MSF. The project will also provide new room identification signage, new door hardware and card readers at the entry doors. The project complies with ADA requirements by providing entry/exit wall signs in braille and compliant door hardware.

ceqa-17934fcb80c0cb1ab2.name: Robla Park Restroom (L19913700)
ceqa-17934fcb80c0cb1ab2.description: The Project Involves construction of a new prefabricated two-stall, all gender restroom building, as well as utility connections, concrete flatwork, and walkways, turf and irrigation modifications, landscaping, and signage at Robla Park.

ceqa-32a91f79e3de246567.name: Tanzanite Park Lighting Improvements (L19148400)
ceqa-32a91f79e3de246567.description: The project involves park lighting improvements to the parking lot lighting, pathway lighting, futsal court lighting and electrical panel at Tanzanite Park. The improvements will consist of branch circuiting from the existing electrical service to an existing sport lighting service and establishing an electrical connection to new lighting control cabinet, and the installation of new pathway and parking lot lighting.

ceqa-40553bb19d82539dee.name: Blackbird Park Restroom (L19109400)
ceqa-40553bb19d82539dee.description: The project involves construction of a new prefabricated two-stall, 204 S.F. restroom building, as well as utility connections and concrete flatwork at Blackbird Park.

ceqa-14a3cdbd4816712341.name: Zacharias Ranch Mitigation Bank (Notification of Lake or Streambed Alteration, (No. EPIMS-SAC-55001-R3)
ceqa-14a3cdbd4816712341.projectTitle: Zacharias Ranch Mitigation Bank (Notification of Lake or Streambed Alteration, (No. EPIMS-SAC-55001-R3)
ceqa-14a3cdbd4816712341.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Bay Delta Region 3
ceqa-14a3cdbd4816712341.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 3 - Bay Delta, Fairfield
ceqa-14a3cdbd4816712341.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-SAC-55001-R3, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Westervelt Ecological Services as represented by Chris McColl. The levee breaches and channel connections will create tidal connections between Snodgrass Slough, Railroad Cut, and the adjacent 580-acre restoration area.

ceqa-780a8c0074f469167a.name: Victor's House Addition

ceqa-eb4a870dfc94fc3b9e.description: The Bartholomew Winery Amendment Project (the “Project”) consists of a request for a Text Amendment to the Elk Grove Municipal Code (EGMC) Title 23, Zoning to allow “Outdoor Event Center” use upon approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) within the Agricultural-Residential zoning districts (AR-10, AR-5, AR-2, and AR-1) when on parcels that are a minimum 10-gross-acres in size and that have direct primary public access from one or more Major Arterials (as defined in the General Plan), and where the Outdoor Event Center use is ancillary to an approved winery or agricultural tourism use on the site. The Outdoor Event Center use would be prohibited on Agricultural-Residential parcels in the Rural Area Community Plan. In conjunction with the Text Amendment to the EGMC, the Project included a new Conditional Use Permit to allow an “Outdoor Event Center” use with up to 18 events per year with amplified music and an Amendment to the previously-approved Bartholomew Vineyard Conditional Use Permit (CUP) (PLNG19-008) to expand the hours of on-site wine tasting and to allow additional winery events up to 48 events per year with amplified music, at the Project site of 9696 Elk Grove Boulevard/9654 Bradshaw Road.

ceqa-14459c015bb78cb4bd.name: Brannan Island State Recreation Area – Facilities Improvements
ceqa-14459c015bb78cb4bd.projectTitle: Brannan Island State Recreation Area – Facilities Improvements
ceqa-14459c015bb78cb4bd.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-14459c015bb78cb4bd.description: The purpose of this project is to repair and/or upgrade items at the restroom facilities at Brannan Island State Recreation Area to ensure ADA compliance and full functionality for public use. Updating these facilities will also create an overall more enjoyable and inclusive experience for visitors. The work will occur in eight (8) of the park’s restrooms at the following locations: Windy Cove; Willow North; Willow South; Cottonwood North; Cottonwood South; Sacramento Group Camp; Swim Beach Day Use; and Boat Launch. Additionally, a free-standing water fountain at the Bait Shop will be replaced as well. Items to be upgraded for health and safety compliance include: doors, drinking fountains, faucets, mirrors, restroom waste bins, signs, sinks, showers, toilets, water bottle fillers, and water heater tanks and all necessary accessory parts. Work will also include removal and disposal of all non-compliant or broken fixtures, patching walls where necessary with either matching tile or stainless-steel blanks and replacing or repairing any cracked or broken tile as necessary.

ceqa-8e597bd8969a1dcf4c.name: Galt Ranch Commercial Project
ceqa-8e597bd8969a1dcf4c.description: The project includes the subdivision of the 45.65-acre project site into 21 parcels and the subsequent development of restaurant, retail, medical office/clinic space, hotel, and retail automotive parts and service uses. A 9.11-acre portion of the project site comprised of Parcels 21 and 22 is currently designated for high-density residential uses, which (based on the existing zoning) could include the future development of up to 240 residential units. However, the development of Parcels 21 and 22 is not proposed as part of this project, and the parcels are only included within the project site for parcelization and rough grading purposes. The proposed project would include a total of 189,070 square feet (sf) of commercial uses, comprised of five quick-serve restaurants ranging in size between 2,400 sf and 3,887 sf; a 6,000-sf restaurant; seven retail buildings ranging between 6,900 sf and 30,000 sf; two medical office buildings 10,000 sf and 20,000 sf in size; a hotel with approximately 80 rooms; one car wash; and one gas station with a convenience store. A total of 1,175 parking spaces would be provided throughout the site. Vehicle site access would be provided by a new connection to Simmerhorn Road at the northern end of the site, which would lead to the new internal road, Galt Ranch Road, which will connect to Simmerhorn Road and Crystal Way.

ceqa-e93a64923631716ab9.name: Citrus Heights Gateway Activation Project
ceqa-e93a64923631716ab9.description: The Project proposes improvements on a 0.45-mile section of Old Auburn Road from the Sacramento County line south to Roberts Creek Court and on Wachtel Way from Old Auburn Road south approximately 0.61 miles to the Woodside Oaks Park segment of the Arcade-Cripple Creek Trail. The proposed improvements include intersection enhancements such as roundabouts, as well as the installation of pedestrian and bicycle facilities such as multi-use pathways, Class IV bikeways, crosswalks, sidewalks, and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)-compliant curb ramps. The Project includes amending the Bikeway Master Plan, Pedestrian Master Plan, and the General Plan Bikeway Map to incorporate these new bicycle and pedestrian segments. These improvements are needed to address traffic congestion along Old Auburn Road as well as current deficiencies in pedestrian and bicycle access along Old Auburn Road and Wachtel Way.

ceqa-6cc9851bc562b66d33.description: Full Title: Sacramento Republic FC Stadium - Optional Expansion (Z25-095) within the Railyards - Prior Project Railyards Specific Plan Update Project (PlS040) and Sacramento Republic FC Stadium (Z25-042) On September 8, 2025, the Sacramento Republic FC Stadium - Z25-042 project (Stadium Project) was approved. The entitlements include: 1) Approval of an Addendum to the Certified SEIR; 2) Minor Modification to the terms and conditions of a Conditional Use Permit for a previously approved sports complex; and 3) Site Plan and Design Review for the development of a 12,000-seat stadium with a main VIP building, grandstands, ancillary support buildings, associated plaza areas, lighting, and offsite transportation and utility infrastructure improvements as an initial phase. The Sacramento Republic FC Stadium Project could be expanded to approximately 20,000 or more seats, up to a maximum of 25,000 seats. The NOD for the Stadium Project was filed on September 8, 2025, and the statute of limitations to challenge the project approval expired on October 8, 2025. The current action includes approval of a modification to the terms and conditions of the Conditional Use Permit for the optional expansion of the sports complex previously evaluated in the certified SEIR and addendum which documented that the modification of the CUP does require further environmental review pursuant to CEQA guidelines section 15162. The current action constitutes a minor modification of the Stadium Project and does not constitute a re-approval of the Stadium Project.

ceqa-cb2bb794db56623ec6.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes the I-5 Grade Raise Project. ceqa-060b8e8ba23e74daa7.description: Caltrans proposes a project to improve highway traffic monitoring and reduce traffic congestion by replacing 22 Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) locations in various counties. The project will leverage various sensor technologies to continuously monitor traffic flow and manage traffic safety at various post miles on State Route (SR) 99, 65, 267 and Interstate (I) 5 and I-80. This project is needed as a list of 22 chronic CCTV locations that have been identified. These 22 locations are outdated and need replacement, allowing efficient use of traffic monitoring and relieving traffic congestion. The project involves only electrical work and requires no soil disturbance

The Outdoor Event Center use would be prohibited on Agricultural-Residential parcels in the Rural Area Community Plan. In conjunction with the Text Amendment to the EGMC, the Project included a new Conditional Use Permit to allow an “Outdoor Event Center” use with up to 18 events per year with amplified music and an Amendment to the previously-approved Bartholomew Vineyard Conditional Use Permit (CUP) (PLNG19-008) to expand the hours of on-site wine tasting and to allow additional winery events up to 48 events per year with amplified music, at the Project site of 9696 Elk Grove Boulevard/9654 Bradshaw Road.

ceqa-cd3c3e9206c41174f3.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-61121-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Taylor Morrison. ceqa-7e2204bf4bca40e71e.name: McCormack-Williamson Tract 2026 Levee Erosion Repair Project Sites 1–14
ceqa-7e2204bf4bca40e71e.projectTitle: McCormack-Williamson Tract 2026 Levee Erosion Repair Project Sites 1–14
ceqa-7e2204bf4bca40e71e.description: The proposed project would repair 14 outboard (waterside) erosion sites on McCormack-Williamson Tract (MWT), a North Delta island. The repairs are proposed to address existing erosion, protect existing infrastructure, maintain MWT access, reduce the risk of uncontrolled breaches, and protect investments that the Department of Water Resources and Reclamation District 2110have made on MWT. The erosion repair sites are along the outboard perimeter of MWT at Dead Horse Cut, Snodgrass Slough, Lost Slough, and the East Levee, ranging from 50 to 250 feet in length. These erosion repair sites would be repaired to address bank loss, toe scour, and erosion. The repairs would entail flattening the waterside levee slope, placing imported riprap to re-establish the bank slope and channel, and constructing a toe berm. To address vegetation effects from erosion repairs and result in no net loss of sensitive or protected habitat, in-water planting benches would be constructed onsite as part of the proposed project. The repairs would entail placing material within the original configuration of the levees before erosion and following the current standard of practice for rural levee erosion repairs.

ceqa-deeb81ed2bfd1e1e7d.name: Aspen IV Time Extension
ceqa-deeb81ed2bfd1e1e7d.description: The project consists of a Use Permit Amendment to extend the expiration of the Use Permit to allow the continued operation of Aspen IV. The project consists solely of a time extension for Use Permit No. 04-UPB-0230 and Reclamation Plan No. 04-REB-0229 to allow the continued operation of an existing pre-wash facility, associated settling ponds, and grading activities, as well as to extend the deadline for implementation of the approved Reclamation Plan. No new construction, modification, or expansion of facilities or site activities is proposed.

ceqa-6a8192b662f4a23e7f.name: City of Galt Routine Maintenance Agreement Project
ceqa-6a8192b662f4a23e7f.projectTitle: City of Galt Routine Maintenance Agreement Project
ceqa-6a8192b662f4a23e7f.description: The City of Galt proposes to enter into a 12-year Streambed Alteration Agreement with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife for routine maintenance activities within improved and unimproved stream channels and drainage facilities and associated habitat areas throughout the City to streamline the permitting process for small-scale routine maintenance activities. The City anticipates completing approximately 20 to 30 maintenance projects a year over the 12-year life of the RMA. Maintenance would primarily involve hand tools for vegetation control and sediment removal efforts but may occasionally involve small pieces of equipment like mini-excavators or backhoes. In addition, the City is planning to implement a larger scale initial clearing effort along a segment of Deadman Gulch to improve flood conveyance capacity.
ceqa-6a8192b662f4a23e7f.crossStreets: City-wide within Creeks and Drainage Cooridors
