ceqa-ac1d3a7246a642a947.description: The project consists of a Minor Use Permit to allow a proposed vocational school to operate within the North Watt Special Planning Area (SPA). The existing office building is located on a 1.29-acre parcel at the corner of Roseville Road and Myrtle Avenue.

ceqa-3f093de0f8f6df6f9c.name: Alta Arden Expressway Phase I
ceqa-3f093de0f8f6df6f9c.description: Sacramento County Department of Transportation (SacDOT) is proposing to improve the pedestrian and bike facilities along Alta Arden Expressway in the Arden-Arcade community in unincorporated Sacramento County. Improvements will include installing sidewalk where it is missing, installing buffered bike lanes, installing new streetlamps, restriping roadways, modifying traffic signals, rehabilitating pavement, and resurfacing (project). The project will be implemented along approximately 0.9 miles on Alta Arden Expressway, approximately 390 feet west of Howe Avenue to Fulton Avenue Additionally, gas, electric, water, sewer, and telecommunication facilities within the project area may require adjustments or relocations to facilitate pedestrian and bicycle improvements.
ceqa-3f093de0f8f6df6f9c.crossStreets: Alta Arden Expressway from Howe Avenue to Fulton Avenue

ceqa-0be5a6e76a2f2f312b.name: Raising Canes at Gateway Park (P24-027)
ceqa-0be5a6e76a2f2f312b.description: The project is located on a 1.77-acre project site and would include the development of 3,329 square foot (sf) drive-through Raising Cane's restaurant. The proposal includes dual-lane drive-through lanes with decorative screening, a 1,554 square foot outdoor covered patio, and 29 parking stalls within the Shopping Center (SC-PUD) zone and Coral Business Park Planned Unit Development. Entitlements include: Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to authorize a drive-through restaurant use on 1.77-acre project site in the SCPUD Zone and Site Plan and Design Review for construction of a 3,329 square foot restaurant building with double drive-through lanes and necessary site improvements.

ceqa-8f283a3f99463fd95d.name: The Enclave at Airport Road (P25-010)
ceqa-8f283a3f99463fd95d.description: The proposed project would include the development of a 32-unit two-story single-family subdivision and associated internal "Private Alley" roadways. Each of the 32 units would consist of three bedrooms, 2.5 bathrooms, and a two-car garage, and would range from1,932-square feet (sf) to 2,088-sf. Primary site access would be provided by three new driveways along Tanzanite Avenue on the project site's southern frontage. The proposed project would include the demolition of the existing farmstead and small agricultural buildings currently located on the project site. Additional detail regarding the proposed project's parking, access, and circulation; landscaping and design; and utility infrastructure is provided below. The proposed project would require City approval of a Development Agreement, Rezone, Amendment to the Natomas Crossing Planned Unit Development (PUD), Tentative Map, and Site Plan and Design Review.

ceqa-f301a1dfba9908dc49.name: Century Palms Estates
ceqa-f301a1dfba9908dc49.description: The proposed project consists of a residential subdivision and construction of single-family residences and associated improvements. The project will be implemented on three parcels southwest of the intersection at M Street and Rio Linda Boulevard in the Gateway Area of the Downtown Rio Linda Special Planning Area (DRLSPA) in the Rio Linda and Elverta community of unincorporated Sacramento County. The applicant is proposing to develop single-family residences ranging from approximately 1,567 square feet to 1,631 square feet on three parcels subdivided into 120 single-family residential lots and four parcels for bioretention basins and landscape (project). The resulting residential density is 8.84 dwelling units per acre (du/ac). Each parcel will be approximately 2,800 square feet. Two new paths of ingress and egress will allow accessibility from existing M Street and Rio Linda Boulevard in addition to new internal roads. Frontage improvements and streetscape will be installed along M Street and Rio Linda Boulevard as well. New sewer infrastructure will be required as part of the project. Sewer and water services will be provided by the Sacramento Area Sewer District and the Rio Linda Elverta Community Water District.
ceqa-f301a1dfba9908dc49.crossStreets: Rio Linda Boulevard and M Street

ceqa-14ab30f87c2576e893.name: Permit No. 19714--Saddique SID Private Boat Dock Installation Project
ceqa-14ab30f87c2576e893.projectTitle: Saddique's Private Boat Dock Installation Project
ceqa-14ab30f87c2576e893.description: To install a single-berth, pile guided, steel frame boat dock consisting of two finger floats.Each finger float is 4-feet-wide by 40-feet-long. The project also includes 1) the construction of a steel frame gangway landing dock 12-feet-wide by 20-feet-long, 2) the construction of a 4-feet-wide by 73-feet-long aluminum gangway, 3) driving four 14-inch-diameter 68-feet-long steel piles, 4) the construction of a 5 feet by 6 feet concrete abutment, 5) installation of rip rap, 6) installation of one light pole connected to existing underground electric box with 2-feet-long maximum conduit, and 7) a temporary 40-feet-long by 8-feet-wide by 8-feet-tall storage container anchored to ground,

ceqa-a7d9fca42745071c2d.name: Marina Sediment Sampling
ceqa-a7d9fca42745071c2d.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-a7d9fca42745071c2d.description: Collect sediment samples within the Brannan Island Marina to characterize their physical and chemical properties, ensuring they meet standards for disposal, and identifying potential contaminants (metals, PCBs, etc.) to prevent environmental harm, using devices like Ponar or Ekman dredges, push cores, and augers, with locations planned across the dredge footprint and specific zones analyzed for contaminants. The intent is to create a Sampling and Analysis Plan (SAP) that dictates sample locations, depths, and testing protocols

ceqa-4c7b7dcd63ae20e28b.name: Baytrans Inc. Trucking Service (DR25-109)
ceqa-4c7b7dcd63ae20e28b.description: Baytrans, Inc. (Baytrans) Trucking Service Facility supports Baytrans trucking operations services, which includes a 19,600 square foot (sf) light industrial pre-engineered metal building (housing an office, service bays, a break room and warehouse storage and shop), 79 trucking parking spaces, 46 passenger vehicle parking spaces and security fencing and gates around the perimeter on 4.7 acres. Passenger vehicle parking is separated from truck parking and service bays by a security fence and controlled gate. There would be up to 12 employees. The site improvements also include stormwater bio-retention basins, utility connections with City of Sacramento water and sewer service and a Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD) electricity power box. The site currently has a single-family home, which will be removed as part of the proposed project, and is graveled for overnight truck parking. There are no other site improvements under existing conditions. The trucking facility would receive, service and store cargo trucks.

ceqa-a55f9497168e8626b5.name: Sylte Boat Dock (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-56149-R2)
ceqa-a55f9497168e8626b5.projectTitle: Sylte Boat Dock (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-56149-R2)
ceqa-a55f9497168e8626b5.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, North Central Region 2
ceqa-a55f9497168e8626b5.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-a55f9497168e8626b5.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-56149-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Roberta Sylte. The project is limited to the installation of a new u-shaped boat dock and associated gangway. The dock structure will be steel framed with encased foam and composite decking. The dock will be supported by three (3) 12-inch diameter pilings that will be installed using a vibratory hammer. The gangway will be held in place by two (2) 4-inch diameter galvanized steel pipes at the landing on the riverbank. A concrete pad will be installed on the riverbank for the gangway landing. Riparian vegetation in the footprint of the concrete pad will be removed to facilitate the installation. No mature trees (diameter at breast height of 4-inches or greater) will be removed.

ceqa-471b2a4cac238f6ee6.name: SAC 160 Sinkhole (EA 03-2N460)
ceqa-471b2a4cac238f6ee6.description: California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes mobilization, remove failed corrugated metal pipe (CMP) culvert and replace with new reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) culvert, excavation, backfill, water diversion, shoring, hot mix asphalt (HMA) paving, striping, traffic control, and incidental work on State Route 160 in Sacramento County.
ceqa-471b2a4cac238f6ee6.crossStreets: State Route 160 and Sherman Island Cross Road

ceqa-acc9488316654edf79.name: Routine Maintenance for the Calendar Year 2026
ceqa-acc9488316654edf79.projectTitle: Routine Maintenance for the Calendar Year 2026
ceqa-acc9488316654edf79.description: The program of routine maintenance includes, but is not limited to, all mowing, vegetation pruning, fallen or hazardous tree removal, road grading, minor earthwork repairs and the placement of rock revetment on Sacramento area flood control levees, as well as any other similar activities that are needed to meet standards established by applicable law.. The north and south levees of the American River, Arcade Creek, Robla Creek, and Dry Creek and the east levees of Steelhead Creek and the Sacramento River are part of the federal Sacramento River Flood Control Project and have been turned over to the American River Flood Control District for operation and maintenance. These levees protect residents. property, infrastructure, government facilities, and habitat in the Sacramento metropolitan area. In addition, the District undertakes the operation and maintenance of other levees in the Sacramento metropolitan area under contract with the Sacramento Area Flood Control Agency or other public agencies in the region

ceqa-670807d9dc690cf61d.name: California Artisanal Medicine
ceqa-670807d9dc690cf61d.description: The proposed project will operate a distribution license out of an existing facility located at 2424 Del Monte Street, West Sacramento, CA 95691(APN 67-150-035). The two buildings total 85,262 sq ft, with 695 sq ft designated for distribution, on 5.77 acres. The neighborhood is zoned for Industrial Warehouse and Storage. The parcel is flat, hosts multiple ornamental vegetation and provides a parking lot. The building was constructed in 1976, painted white and has a flat roof. The property will host both licensed cultivation and distribution businesses. The property is located on the corner of Del Monte Street and Terminal Street and south of HWY 50.
ceqa-670807d9dc690cf61d.crossStreets: Terminal Street and Del Monte Street

ceqa-c362059a3d5f74642e.name: Sacramento Railyards Digital Sign Program - Master Lease - Prior Project Railyards Specific Plan Update Project (P15-040)
ceqa-c362059a3d5f74642e.projectTitle: Railyards Specific Plan Update, KP Medical Center, MLS Stadium, & Stormwater Outfall Subsequent EIR
ceqa-c362059a3d5f74642e.description: The Sacramento Railyards Digital Sign Program and Master Lease Agreement project (Project) implements the elements of the Project where the SEIR described a sign program be developed. The Current Project will authorize the construction and operation of up to five digital billboards within the Sacramento Railyards Specific Plan (RSP) Area (or Railyards Special Planning District). The proposed digital billboards would include two freeway-oriented digital billboards along Interstate 5 (1-5) in the western RSP Area (Locations I and 2), two gateway billboards between the 5th and 6th Streets rail crossings (Location 3) and at the north and south entries into the RSP Area at the 7th Street/B Street intersection (Location 4), and movement of the previously analyzed digital sign from the south side of the Central Shops Plaza to outside the Central Shops Historic District at the entry point of the Plaza at the proposed Stanford Street and Stevens Street driveway intersection (Location 5). The proposed digital billboard faces will be light-emitting diode (LED)-through-hole design, with an LED pixel pitch of nineteen millimeters. The Master Lease between the City of Sacramento and Downtown Railyard Venture, LLC allows for up to five digital billboards, includes a term of 34 years, and includes early termination clause if the project does not build out consistent with the definitive documents.
ceqa-c362059a3d5f74642e.crossStreets: North B Street, 7th St, H St, 5th and 7th streets, I St

ceqa-06cef13c299e9a662f.name: Sheldon Meadows Map and Rezone (PLNG23-003) First Reading
ceqa-06cef13c299e9a662f.projectTitle: City of Elk Grove Climate Compass Project
ceqa-06cef13c299e9a662f.description: The Sheldon Meadows Map and Rezone Project (the “Project”) consists of a Rezone from Agricultural Residential-5 (AR-5) to Agricultural Residential-2 (AR-2), and a Tentative Subdivision Map and Subdivision Design Review to subdivide a ±14.50-acre parcel into 7 lots. The Project also includes a Determination of Consistency with the General Plan for the Abandonment of a SMUD Easement. Any future home construction will be required to comply with the City’s Climate Action Plan (CAP) measures for new single-family construction.

ceqa-3b51e0e27580f63954.name: Holy Cross New Church and Hall Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-3b51e0e27580f63954.projectTitle: Holy Cross New Church and Hall Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-3b51e0e27580f63954.description: The project consists of a Use Permit Amendment (93-UPB-0753) and Design Review to increase the seating capacity from 150 to 253 persons and to modify the previously approved phasing plan at an existing church in the Interim Agricultural Reserve/Surface Mining (IR/SM) zoning district. Construction associated with the proposed project consists of a new 18,000 square-foot, two-story church . The church structure will consist of a 9,100 square-foot social hall on the first floor and an 8,900 square-foot worship space on the second floor, which will be completed in two separate phases. In addition, a new 575 square-foot property maintenance storage structure and a 900 square-foot play structure are proposed. The project also includes demolition of three structures on the subject property. Those three structures include a 1,340 square foot caretaker residence, a 485 square foot food closet (two-car detached garage) and a 950 square-foot single family residence that is currently being used for refreshments and education. The existing 2,200 square-foot chapel and 3,900 square-foot shade structure will remain on the project site.

ceqa-fea27e1106ab2bc666.name: 53rd Street Residential Improvements
ceqa-fea27e1106ab2bc666.description: Site Plan and Design Review to construct an addition to an existing residential dwelling and a detached accessory structure (garage) on a 0.21-acre lot in the Single-Unit Dwelling Zone (R-1) within the Citywide Design Review Area.

ceqa-bc1956db432efba650.name: Ordinance No. 1359 (Inclusionary Housing)
ceqa-bc1956db432efba650.description: An Ordinance of the City of Folsom amending certain sections of Chapter 17.104 (Inclusionary Housing) of the Folsom Municipal Code to update the methodology for calculating in-lieu fees applicable to residential development, and to incorporate non-substantive cleanup revisions for clarity and consistency.

ceqa-a98dfb3c047b6ed968.name: Sky Port Restaurant & Bar Outdoor Seating (PLNG25-031)
ceqa-a98dfb3c047b6ed968.projectTitle: Sky Port Restaurant & Bar Outdoor Seating (PLNG25-031)
ceqa-a98dfb3c047b6ed968.description: The Sky Port Restaurant & Bar Outdoor Seating Project (the “Project”) consists of an Outdoor Activity Design Review to allow for permanent outdoor seating and a Minor Conditional Use Permit to allow outdoor amplified music in the outdoor seating area. No expansion of the building is proposed.

ceqa-1f977fce581dbba53f.name: Cattlemens Steakhouse Repaint (PLNG25-038)
ceqa-1f977fce581dbba53f.description: The Project consists of a Minor Design Review for façade improvements to an existing restaurant building at 9105 W. Stockton Boulevard. The proposed modifications include new exterior paint treatments to the building elevations. No expansion of the building is proposed with this application

ceqa-0009697d2f621521a6.name: Seasons at Strawberry Lane MHP (PLNG25-024)
ceqa-0009697d2f621521a6.description: The application involves the master home plan design review of 5 new single-family residential home plans for the Strawberry Lane (formerly known as Sage Glen) Subdivision.

ceqa-b5aed4c4b4a1741307.name: POWER LINE ROAD PHASE 2 (PLR2/ER-1)
ceqa-b5aed4c4b4a1741307.description: The project consists of planned widening Power Line Road from a two-lane local road to a two-lane arterial with a center turn lane. Widening will occur from the intersection of Power Line Road at Allbaugh Drive to West W Elverta Road and 2,100 linear feet (0.4 miles) along West W Elverta Road. The project will include a potable water line and storm drain improvements to accommodate the road widening . A total of twenty utility poles will be relocated by Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD) along Power Line Road and W Elverta Road. Seven poles located east of the Power Line Road/ W Elverta Road intersection will be relocated south approximately 30 feet from the existing pole locations. Thirteen poles located south of the Power Line Road/W Elverta Road will be relocated approximately 75 feet from the E3xisting pole locations. The total length of the project is approximately 4,900 linear feet.

ceqa-0cad09a06acea6b019.name: Aspen VIII & IX Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-0cad09a06acea6b019.projectTitle: ASPEN VIII & IX MINING USE PERMIT AMENDMENT PROJECT
ceqa-0cad09a06acea6b019.description: The project is an amendment to an existing use permit and reclamation plan for the Aspen VIII and IX Project (PLNP2014-00201) to expand mining of aggregate material (sand and gravel) to two distinct expansion areas, that total 245.6 acres of unmined areas. The Aspen VIII Expansion area would encompass 63.26 acres located adjacent to the northwest corner of Aspen VIII. The Aspen IX Expansion area would encompass 182.38 acres south of the existing Aspen IX mining area. As a part of the expansion, Teichert is proposing to extend its existing electric conveyor belt system over Elder Creek to transport aggregate materials from Aspen IX Expansion area back to the Perkins processing facility. The expansion of mining to areas adjacent to Aspen VIII and IX would include amendments to the existing Mining Use Permit, Reclamation Plan, and Development Agreements for Aspen VIII and IX. The project would also include amendmHnts to several conditions of approval on the Use Permit that are necessary to incorporate the expanded mine areas.

ceqa-7e2fb66fb22146cec7.name: IU-Mien Buddhist Temple
ceqa-7e2fb66fb22146cec7.description: The project applicant proposes to construct a 4,816 square foot Buddhist temple, 1,381 square foot service building , recreational lawn/ garden, and associated parking and landscaping within a 9.6- acre parcel in the Vineyard Community (community) of unincorporated Sacramento County. Improvements include the construction of curb, gutter, and sidewalk along the subject parcel's frontage, extension of the existing on -site driveway to connect to the eastern portion of the parcel, and construction of an 88-stall parking lot. A Use Permit and Design Review are requested for the project.

ceqa-1c371fe24ab021e83f.name: Bach Court Fence
ceqa-1c371fe24ab021e83f.description: The proposed project consists of a Minor Use Permit to replace an existing 6.5 ft residential side-street yard fence with a seven-foot fence and two foot retaining wall, totaling nine feet in height on a property in the Residential Density 7 (RD-7) Zoning District.

ceqa-885b72f2840e70d1df.name: AC Overlay Project 2026 Phase C
ceqa-885b72f2840e70d1df.description: Roadways within the stated limits will receive a conventional or rubberized asphalt concrete overlay or a slurry seal. Bridge deck maintenance work includes a one-inch polyester concrete overlay. Associated work includes constructing ADA compliant curb ramps, repairing damaged pavement areas, conform grinding, adjusting manholes, and striping the roadway. All elements of the project will be within the developed roadway, and no new impervious surface area will be installed.

ceqa-5665b52042b496a75c.name: AC Overlay Project 2026 Phase A (Contract No. 4685)
ceqa-5665b52042b496a75c.projectTitle: AC Overlay Project 2026 Phase A (Contract No. 4685)
ceqa-5665b52042b496a75c.description: Roadways within the stated limits will receive a conventional or rubberized asphalt concrete overlay or a slurry seal. Associated work includes constructing ADA compliant curb ramps , repairing damaged pavement areas, conform grinding, adjusting manholes, and striping the roadway. All elements of the project will be within the developed roadway, and no new impervious surface area will be installed.

ceqa-bd2a14ab5d4f5e99ba.name: AC Overlay 2026 Phase B (Contract No. 4686)
ceqa-bd2a14ab5d4f5e99ba.description: Sacramento County Department of Transportation (SacDOT) will resurface roadways within the stated limits using conventional asphalt concrete, rubberized asphalt concrete, or slurry seal over the existing pavement. Associated work includes construction of ADA compliant curb ramps, repairing damaged pavement areas, conform grinding, adjusting manholes, base repair, and striping of the roadway. All elements of the project will be within the developed roadway, and no new impervious surface area will be installed.
ceqa-bd2a14ab5d4f5e99ba.parcels: N/A - project is located within public roadways.

ceqa-495dcf66785ad3436f.name: Curb, Gutter, and Sidewalk Replacement Project 2025
ceqa-495dcf66785ad3436f.projectTitle: Curb, Gutter, and Sidewalk Replacement Project 2025
ceqa-495dcf66785ad3436f.description: Sacramento County Department of Transportation (SacDOT) will replace the existing damaged curb, gutter and sidewalk within the stated limits. Construction of the project includes removal and replacement of 2,870 lineal feet of curb and gutter as well as 6,610 feet of sidewalk. Additional work includes pavement restoration per county standards and reconstruction of the asphalt concrete next to the curb and gutter. The depth of work is approximately one (1) foot deep for removal of the existing curb and gutter, and ten inches deep for removal of existing sidewalk. All elements of the project will be within the existing right-of-way, and no new impervious surface will be installed.
ceqa-495dcf66785ad3436f.parcels: N/A - project is located within public roadways

ceqa-ba7257ec5c20e0c4ad.name: Sacramento County Department of Waste Management and Recycling (WMR)- Jackson Road Surplus Sale
ceqa-ba7257ec5c20e0c4ad.projectTitle: Sacramento County Department of Waste Management and Recycling (WMR)- Jackson Road Surplus Sale
ceqa-ba7257ec5c20e0c4ad.description: The project consists of the sale of a 7.52± acre surplus property. Sacramento County Department of Waste Management and Recycling (WMR) is selling the subject parcel along Jackson Road to the Wilton Rancheria. The project is limited to the sale of the property and does not involve physical improvements nor physical impacts.

ceqa-2c088c4067751c552d.name: OED - Metro Air Parkway Old Elkhorn Boulevard Conveyance
ceqa-2c088c4067751c552d.projectTitle: OED - Metro Air Parkway Old Elkhorn Boulevard Conveyance
ceqa-2c088c4067751c552d.description: Sacramento County will convey exempt surplus property located along the old Elkhorn Boulevard alignment to the adjacent property owners while retaining right of way.

ceqa-ab8a6fcdbb1b0afde4.name: 6702 Filbert Avenue Subdivision Map
ceqa-ab8a6fcdbb1b0afde4.description: The project consists of the following entitlements from the County of Sacramento: 1. A Community Plan Amendment of approximately 10-acres from the existing Agricultural Residential 2 (AR-2) land use designation to the proposed Agricultural Residential 1 (AR-1) land use designation. 2. A Rezone of approximately 10-acres from the existing Agricultural Residential 2 (AR-2) zoning district to the proposed Agricultural Residential 1 (AR-1) zoning district. 3. A Tentative Subdivision Map to subdivide a 10-acre parcel into ten residential lots in the Agricultural Residential 1 (AR-1) zoning district. 4. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standards: • Public Street Frontage (5.3.1.A. Table 5.4 footnote 2): Up to four lots may be served by a private drive without meeting the public street frontage requirement. As proposed, the 10-lot subdivision would be served by a private street. 5. An Exception pursuant to Section 22.24.630 of the Sacramento County Code to deviate from public water and sewer requirements stating that the water purveyor not be a homeowners association, mutual water company, or corporation. As proposed, the project would be served by a water corporation. 6. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines). Implementation of the project will involve the removal of vegetation and trees; grading and excavation to allow construction of building foundations, utilities, roadways, drainage facilities, curb & gutter, streetlights (Class B & Class D public street improvements), and landscaping. The proposed project will be served by two new roadways including a new private road from Filbert Avenue and the extension of Crown Street from the east.

ceqa-a48887f0fd308cceee.name: Stacy Ave Parcel Map
ceqa-a48887f0fd308cceee.description: The project consists of the following entitlements: 1. A Tentative Parcel Map to divide two parcels totaling 2.28-acres, into four lots with one remainder, and is to be accessed by a new private drive in the RD-5 zone of the South Sacramento community. 2. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standards: • Private Drive (Section 5.4.2, Table 5.7.A): Up to two lots may be served by a private drive without meeting the public street frontage requirement. As proposed, four new lots with one remainder parcel shall be accessed by a new private drive. 3. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).

ceqa-3e7a0dadd457899110.name: Plant Lab Window Sealant Replacement
ceqa-3e7a0dadd457899110.description: The proposed project consists of replacement of existing window sealants and gaskets of the employee breakroom and library at the 3294 Meadowview California Department of Food and Agriculture building. The project is necessary to prevent further water intrusion and damage to an existing facility.

ceqa-ee6630272881eddbe1.name: Sunrise Bridge Crew Facility Roof Repairs (03-1N540)
ceqa-ee6630272881eddbe1.projectTitle: Sunrise Bridge Crew Facility Roof Repairs (03-1N540)
ceqa-ee6630272881eddbe1.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) initiated a Director’s Order to repair damaged sections of the roof at the Sunrise Bridge Crew Maintenance Station. The facility is in Sacramento County on SR 51 near PM 1.7. The scope of work includes mobilization, removal and replacement of roof, replacement of damaged insulation, replacement of rusted purlins, siding replacement, painting, and incidental work. The purpose of this project is to improve the structural safety and operational efficiency of the Sunrise Bridge Crew Maintenance Station.

ceqa-7b59481667479ddaba.name: North Watt Avenue Specific Plan
ceqa-7b59481667479ddaba.description: The North Watt Avenue Specific Plan (Specific Plan) encompasses approximately 705 acres along a 4-mile segment of Watt Avenue, north of Interstate-80 (I-80) to Antelope Road/U Street, within unincorporated Sacramento County. The Specific Plan proposes three zoning districts, each with its own established allowable land uses and development and design standards. The zoning districts would allow a mix of residential and commercial retail and service uses, industrial uses and compatible uses focused south of the Union Pacific Railroad main line, and parks and open space areas. The Specific Plan will identify the water, sewer, drainage, and stormwater infrastructure investments required to support infill development within the corridor and transportation improvements needed to ensure multi-modal access for residents, employees, and visitors.
ceqa-7b59481667479ddaba.crossStreets: Watt Avenue and James Way/A Street
ceqa-7b59481667479ddaba.action: General Plan Amendment, Rezone, Specific Plan
ceqa-7b59481667479ddaba.developmentType: Residential (Units 7260, Acres 0.001), Commercial (Sq. Ft. 1, Acres 1, Employees 1), Industrial (Sq. Ft. 1, Acres 225, Employees 1), Recreational (Parks and open space areas), Other (Public infrastructure improvements to support new infill develop)

ceqa-d68a551a32d1f4087c.name: State Route 51 Bridge Deck Replacement Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-21522-R2) Amendment 2
ceqa-d68a551a32d1f4087c.projectTitle: SAC-51 American River Bridge Deck Replacement
ceqa-d68a551a32d1f4087c.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Amendment 2 to Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-21522-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, California Department of Transportation. Amendment 2 includes increasing the footprint of the staging and access area within the riparian habitat on the northern side of the American River by an additional one acre. The amendment includes changes in the Project Description, Project Impacts, and Compensatory Measures to reflect the additional permanent and temporary impacts and compensatory mitigation. Project Contact Information is also updated in the amendment.

ceqa-dadedd35e0cce04800.name: Motorcross Practice Track Expansion
ceqa-dadedd35e0cce04800.projectTitle: Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area Proposed Road and Trail Management Plan
ceqa-dadedd35e0cce04800.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-dadedd35e0cce04800.description: The California Department of Parks and Recreation (DPR) proposes to expand the existing motorcross practice track at Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area (SVRA) under the process outlined in the Prairie City SVRA Road and Trail Management Plan (RTMP) approved in 2024. Project-level review has been completed, and staff has determined that the project is covered under the Prairie City SVRA RTMP initial study and Negative Declaration, with the adoption of specific Standard Project Requirements and Mitigation Measures from the RTMP (CEQA Guidelines 15168) and implementation of the project description.

ceqa-79361b5f82159e8a70.name: Flow Control Facilities Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-79361b5f82159e8a70.description: The project is generally described as water distribution system repairs, rehabilitation, replacement, and new infrastructure to improve City of Folsom water system deficiencies. The project consists of rehabilitating and relocating water distribution system pressure reducing stations above ground at four locations, abandoning two existing pressure reducing stations, and installation of one new pressure reducing station at various locations throughout the city.

ceqa-36af60c439ffc8e7a5.name: Water Treatment Plant Caustic Soda Storage and Feed System Project

ceqa-d0461b20609b873078.name: Cable Replacement S281201 FDR Project (Old Auburn Road)
ceqa-d0461b20609b873078.projectTitle: Cable Replacement S281201 FDR Project (Old Auburn Road)
ceqa-d0461b20609b873078.description: SMUD is proposing to install approximately 500 feet of 12kV utility cable within conduit below a tributary of Cripple Creek (stream). The project would employ the use of Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD), a method intended to reduce environmental impacts through the avoidance of surface disturbance in sensitive habitats. The launch and receiving bore pits for the HDD under the stream will be located within upland habitats that are categorized as residential or urban land use. The pits, located within the sidewalk along the north side of Old Auburn Road, are each more than 100’ from the water’s edge, and would each measure no more than 25 square feet in area. All HDD activities will occur at a minimum depth of approximately 60 inches below the ground surface level and at least 10 feet below the bed, bank, and channel of the stream. Project equipment and staging will be restricted to urban, upland habitats and will not encroach upon the banks of the stream. The HDD activity is anticipated to be completed by May 2026, after the California Department of Fish and Wildlife Streambed Alteration Agreement is obtained. The HDD activity is anticipated to take no longer than five days.
ceqa-d0461b20609b873078.crossStreets: Fair Oaks Boulevard and Old Auburn Road

ceqa-f9fa1a01081c61c677.description: SMUD is proposing to install approximately 350 feet of new 12kV utility cable within conduit below Elk Grove Creek / Laguna Creek (Laguna Creek). The project would employ the use of Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD), a method intended to reduce environmental impacts through the avoidance of surface disturbance in sensitive habitats. The sending and receiving bore pits for the HDD bore under Laguna Creek will be located within upland habitats that are categorized urban land use. The southwestern pit is more than 200 feet from the water’s edge, and the northeastern pit is more than 40 feet from the water’s edge. A total of four conduits - two 6-inch and two 4-inch - will be pulled through the bore path under Laguna Creek, completing the installation. All HDD activities will occur at a minimum depth of approximately 60 inches below the ground surface level and at least 10 feet below the bed, bank, and channel of the creek. Project equipment and staging will be restricted to urban, upland habitats and will not encroach upon the banks of Laguna Creek. The Laguna Creek HDD activity is anticipated to be completed by June 2026, after the California Department of Fish and Wildlife Streambed Alteration Agreement is obtained. The work is anticipated to take no longer than five days.

ceqa-93f3f582a2c91ab61f.name: Rio Americano High School Stadium Improvements Project
ceqa-93f3f582a2c91ab61f.projectTitle: Rio Americano High School Stadium Improvements Project
ceqa-93f3f582a2c91ab61f.description: San Juan Unified is proposing to improve the existing Raider Stadium within the existing Rio Americano High School Campus, by adding high mast light standards, additional bleacher seating, an upgraded public address (PA) system, and a new press box. New light standards would also be installed along the existing paved fire lane between the stadium and the main campus parking lot, to provide for pedestrian safety. Four permanent high mast LED light poles (approximately 80 feet tall) would be installed at the existing Raider Stadium. In addition, six new approximately 16-foot-tall light poles would be installed between the south end of the existing main parking lot (which is accessed at the campus entrance from American River Drive at Saverien Drive) and the stadium entrance, along the existing paved fire lane, which would serve as the proposed pedestrian travel route; this lighting would provide nighttime visibility for pedestrian safety. The existing bleacher seating would be replaced with new bleacher seating on the north (visitor side) of the stadium and new bleacher seating on the south (home side) of the stadium accommodating a total capacity of approximately 2,500 people. A new press box would also be installed as part of the bleacher seating on the south (home side) of the stadium. The proposed project also includes removing the existing metal storage sheds on the northwest side of the stadium, and a small storage shed on the south side of the stadium. Two existing Sacramento Metropolitan Utility District (SMUD) wood light poles within the campus fire lane (which would be used for pedestrian ingress and egress) would also be removed after the installation of new lighting. Finally, the existing PA system would be upgraded.

ceqa-bb4d0c6aa7580bb123.name: Leidesdorff-Coloma Substation Project
ceqa-bb4d0c6aa7580bb123.description: SMUD proposes upgrading the existing Leidesdorff-Coloma Substation, which will primarily involve replacing aging equipment to enhance the reliability and efficiency of the substation. To complete the substation upgrade, the substation will be deenergized and all the existing equipment will be removed including the grounding grid which is buried approximately 18-inches deep. The only exception is the subtransmission tower, located in the eastern portion of the substation, which will remain and to which only minor upgrades are required. Prior to replacing the substation equipment, the substation will be graded and leveled by importing soil and gravel to raise the northern half of the substation approximately 5 feet. The driveways within the substation will be replaced, and new substation equipment will be installed including the transformers, switch gear, spill and stormwater containment, and the underground grounding grid. The heights of the new substation structures will be comparable in height to the existing structures in the existing substation. The footprint of the approximately 1-acre substation will not increase; although, the configuration of the fencing will slightly change to accommodate the design. The new substation fence around the perimeter of the substation will consist of 10-foot chain link fence topped by barbed wire with larger entrances for both gates along Leidesdorff Street. An additional component of the project consists of trimming or removing vegetation within a 27-foot strip of SMUD-owned property located adjacent to the substation’s western boundary and installing a new non-conductive fence along the western property line. If the vegetation is removed rather trimmed, the area will be graveled and used as a secondary maintenance access route to the substation and SMUD’s property located north of the substation. Construction is anticipated to start in the fall of 2026, and the substation will be reenergized in spring 2027.

ceqa-abe6bda9e5f04fefec.name: Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) Eligibility Guidebook, Tenth Edition
ceqa-abe6bda9e5f04fefec.projectTitle: Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) Eligibility Guidebook, Tenth Edition
ceqa-abe6bda9e5f04fefec.description: The Renewables Portfolio Standard Eligibility Guidebook (RPS Guidebook or guidebook) describes the eligibility requirements and process for certifying eligible renewable energy resources for California’s Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) and describes the process used to verify compliance with the RPS. California’s RPS has a target of obtaining 60 percent of the state’s electricity from eligible renewable energy resources by 2030. The Renewables Portfolio Standard Eligibility Guidebook, Tenth Edition includes amendments clarifying various existing requirements. These clarifications do not result in any changes to how the RPS program is currently administered. Additional amendments establish new eligibility criteria and reporting requirements pursuant to existing authority, as well as address changes in the law. While the amendments to the guidebook result in changes to certification requirements for electrical generation facilities as eligible renewable energy resources—including expanding RPS eligibility to include linear generators—the amendments do not require development of new generation facilities in the state, nor result in changes to existing facilities. Further, even if the amendments incentivize the development of new generation facilities, they would only encourage the development of renewable energy facilities that would benefit the environment by improving air quality and decreasing reliance on fossil fuels. Therefore, no significant adverse environmental impacts have been identified as resulting from this action. For these reasons, adoption of the amendments to the CEC’s regulations is not subject to CEQA under the Common-Sense exemption of CCR, Title 14, section 15061(b)(3).

ceqa-0fe7cb1636c4a38711.name: SB 1215 Covered Battery-Embedded Products Emergency Regulations
ceqa-0fe7cb1636c4a38711.projectTitle: SB 1215 Covered Battery-Embedded Products Emergency Regulations
ceqa-0fe7cb1636c4a38711.agency: California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
ceqa-0fe7cb1636c4a38711.agencyName: Resources Recycling and Recovery, Department of (CalRecycle)
ceqa-0fe7cb1636c4a38711.description: The Electronic Waste Recycling Act of 2003 (“the Act”) (Public Resources Code (PRC), Section 42460, et seq.) established a program to finance the end-of-life management of certain electronic devices (i.e., video display devices). In 2022, Senate Bill (SB) 1215 amended the Act to add battery-embedded products to the types of covered electronic devices eligible for payment in California’s Covered Electronic Waste (CEW) Recycling Program (Program). The Program is funded by a covered battery-embedded waste recycling fee paid by consumers at the point of retail sale for new or refurbished covered battery-embedded products. Pursuant to PRC Section 42478(b)(2), CalRecycle shall begin accepting payment claims for battery-embedded CEW collected on or after January 1, 2026. CalRecycle is proposing emergency regulations in response to SB 1215 that would clarify the statutory definition of “covered battery-embedded product,” and establish requirements for battery-embedded covered electronic waste (CEW) recycling payment claims, including specifying an approved cancellation method for dismantling battery-embedded CEW. The proposed regulations would also update procedures within the CEW Recycling Program, including net cost reporting requirements and establish reinstatement procedures, reconsideration procedures, and payment claim review procedures. In addition, the proposed regulations would describe reporting and notification requirements for manufacturers of covered battery-embedded products, among other conforming editorial and clarifying changes for the state to successfully implement California’s CEW Recycling Program (Program). Finally, the proposed regulations repeal existing regulations allowing manufacturers of video display devices to register and submit manufacturer payment claims if they choose to take back covered electronic devices from consumers for purposes of recycling those devices at a processing facility as no manufacturer has done this in the Program’s history.

The ongoing operations of the State Water Project (SWP) in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and Suisun Marsh as approved by the lead agency is expected to result in incidental take and impacts to habitat of Longfin Smelt (Spirinchus thaleichthys), Delta Smelt (Hypomesus transpacificus), Winter-run Chinook Salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), Spring-run Chinook Salmon ESU (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha), and White Sturgeon (Acipenser transmontanus). Longfin Smelt and Spring-run Chinook Salmon are designated as threatened species under the California Endangered Species Act. Delta Smelt and Winter-run Chinook Salmon are designated as endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act. White Sturgeon is designated as a candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act.

ceqa-01790ee51790633574.description: The Stone Beetland 69kV Project (Project) consists of upgrading existing lower voltage lines to 69kV and constructing new 69kV lines along the perimeter of the Stone Beetland development project. Approximately 0.55 mile of existing 12kV overhead line located along the northern boundary of the development project will be upgraded with taller, stronger poles and 69kV circuit. Along the western boundary of the development project, approximately 950 feet of new overhead 69kV line will be installed which will include approximately 3 new wood or metal poles. The Project will tie into existing 69kV lines on Cosumnes River Boulevard and is needed to enhance the reliability of the electric system across the region, improve the operational flexibility of the electric system and accommodate future load growth. ceqa-be414c3c236bad0e33.name: Downtown Riverfront Streetcar Project
ceqa-be414c3c236bad0e33.description: The Sacramento Downtown Riverfront Streetcar Project (‘DRSP’ or the ‘Project’) will be a 1.8-mile service between West Sacramento and downtown Sacramento. The Project route would travel within public roadways from its western terminus at Sutter Health Park, cross the Tower Bridge that spans the Sacramento River, turn south at 3rd Street and Capitol Mall to N Street, where the alignment would turn east to 7th and 8th Streets and connect to SacRT’s existing light rail tracks on these streets. The Streetcar would use the light rail tracks on 7th Street to travel south from the eastern terminus, across the street from the historical Southern Pacific Railroad Depot) to head toward Sutter Health Park; the streetcars would use the light rail tracks on 8th Street to travel north from Sutter Health Park toward the eastern terminus. At 7th and 8th Streets, the Project would continue along SacRT’s existing light rail tracks on H Street to the route’s eastern terminus near the historical Southern Pacific Railroad Depot where passengers could connect to Amtrak passenger trains and short- and long-haul bus routes. Three new stations would be constructed: West Sacramento/Bridge District Station at Sutter Health Park; 2nd & Capitol Station serving Old Sacramento; and N Street, serving high-intensity office and residential uses in Downtown Sacramento.

ceqa-4ef645384ce2280ddd.name: UPPER WESTSIDE SPECIFIC PLAN
ceqa-4ef645384ce2280ddd.description: The Project is a Specific Plan that encompass approximately 2,066 acres in the unincorporated Natomas community of Sacramento County, approximately 3.5 miles from downtown Sacramento. The Project area is bounded by Interstate 80 to the south, the West Drainage Canal to the east, Fisherman’s Lake Slough to the north, and Garden Highway to the west. The Project is located outside of the County’s Urban Policy Area (UPA) and Urban Services Boundary (USB), but is bounded on three sides by the City of Sacramento, bordering the communities of North and South Natomas. The Project area is mostly agricultural, but has existing agricultural residential homes inside the northeastern and southwestern boundaries, and commercial uses located near the intersection of El Centro Road and West El Camino Avenue. Existing General Plan Land Use designations include Agricultural Cropland, Agricultural Residential, Commercial and Office, and Recreation. A number of individuals own property within the Project area. The Specific Plan encompasses 2,066-acres and contains two geographic issues including a Development area totaling 1,524- acres planned for development with urban uses and a 542-acre Agriculture Buffer (Ag Buffer) along the western edge of the plan area where land uses will remain agricultural, which provides a physical separation between the Development area’s urban uses and existing residential uses along Garden Highway. The project envisions a community with a 1,532± acre Development Area and a 534± acre Ag Buffer Area that is located west of the Development Area, providing a transition to the Garden Highway. Within the Development Area, the applicant has proposed an urban, commercial mixed-use town center district near the intersection of El Centro Road and West El Camino Avenue surrounded by neighborhoods. The Development Area includes 9,356± dwelling units and 3,096,245± square feet of commercial uses, with three K-8 school sites, one high school site, and several parks. Other amenities include trail networks, a greenbelt and urban farm corridor, and a canal system that will all encourage pedestrian and bicycle use by providing connections between neighborhoods.

ceqa-1d22e9db8711fb177c.name: Sheffield Subdivision Project
ceqa-1d22e9db8711fb177c.description: The project site is currently flat and undeveloped with the exception of one vacant single-family residence and consists of annual grassland and scattered trees throughout. The project site is located within the Northeast Area Specific Plan (NEASP) and designated Maximum Density Single-Family Residential (R-1-C, SP). The 2030 General Plan designates the project site as Low-Density Residential, and the site is zoned Low-Density Single-Family Residential (R1A). The proposed project would include the demolition of the existing on-site single-family residence, removal of the associated septic system, abandonment of the associated well, removal of 21 on-site trees, and subdivision of the site into 65 single-family residential lots. Subsequent to demolition and subdivision, the project would include the future development of 65 single-family residential units, an internal circulation network, continuation of South Deadman’s Gulch Trail, frontage improvements along East Stockton Boulevard, and off-site roadway improvements. The proposed project would require approval of a General Plan Amendment to change the General Plan land use designation from Low-Density Residential to Medium Density Residential; a NEASP Map Amendment; a NEASP Text Amendment; a Rezone to change the site’s zoning designation from R1A to Medium Density Residential-Planned Development (R2-PD); and a Tentative Subdivision Map. Design Review would be a separate entitlement required for future development of the project site under a separate, future application. It should be noted that the project site is not included on any of the lists of sites enumerated under Section 65962.5 of the Government Code including, but not limited to, lists of hazardous waste facilities, land designated as hazardous waste property, and hazardous waste disposal sites.

ceqa-2ecc37b36db1bea7db.description: This project involves the fire alarm system modernization at the Secretary of State (SOS) Building, located at 1500 11th Street, Sacramento, California. The SOS Building consists of a six-story, 531,040-square-foot state office building. The complex includes three interconnected quadrants with an open central area. The existing fire alarm system was installed in 1992 to meet the EST3 fire alarm standard and is currently lacking certain operational and replacement parts. The project will replace and upgrade the fire alarm system to EST4 standards to be fully compliant with current codes and regulations. The main fire alarm control unit will be replaced, all fourteen (14) existing fire alarm remote control panels will be upgraded, and all fire alarm terminal cabinets will be upgraded.

ceqa-48a6137f9aa18dbf05.name: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-48a6137f9aa18dbf05.projectTitle: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-48a6137f9aa18dbf05.description: DWR is proposing an alternative decision-making approach to the collaborative approach described in the FEIR in section 2.3.3.2, Start of OMR Management, subsections of 2.3.3. Real-Time Adjustments, including Adult Delta Smelt Entrainment Protection Action and Larval and Juvenile Delta Smelt Protection Action, and section 2.3.22 Governance, subsection 2.3.22.4, Delta (2024 Incidental Take Permit for the Long-Term Operations of the California State Water Project Conditions of Approval [COAs] 8.5.1 and 8.6.1, which in turn would affect three of the Delta Smelt Actions [COAs 8.3.1, 8.3.2, 8.4.1]). The proposed modifications include the following: • The First Flush Action, Adult Delta Smelt Entrainment Protection Action (Turbidity Bridge) and Larval and Juvenile Longfin Smelt Protection Action will be added to the list of SWP management actions that are subject to assessment. o Assessments will propose operational adjustments within boundaries no more negative than -5,000 cfs OMR. o Assessments will include an evaluation of impacts to covered species by proposed operations, informed by available quantitative tools and real-time data, which may include entrainment and routing, modeling, distribution, and other real-time data, as appropriate. • Allow real-time assessment for Delta Smelt winter and spring entrainment protection actions. o DWR will provide an assessment framework that considers covered species impacts. o DWR will develop a science plan to improve understanding of Delta Smelt and salmonid movement and migration behaviors during the OMR low period that will inform the real-time assessment framework of OMR low management for Delta Smelt and Salmon and develop new operational conditions by 2029. No changes to SWP facilities or other operations are proposed.

Site improvements include a new driveway, a new parking area, a new trash enclosure, new patio seating, new pedestrian connectivity, and new landscape areas in the Shopping Center (SC) zoning district. The Habit Burger proposes to operate between 10:30 am and 10:00 pm daily for dining in, take­out, and drive through orders, and with extended hours from 10:00 pm to 11 :00 pm Fridays and Saturdays for drive through orders. The project includes the following entitlements: 1. A Use Permit to allow a drive-through restaurant with amplified sound within 300 feet of residential zoning in the Fair Oaks Blvd Central Special Planning Area (SPA)/Shopping Center (SC) zoning district. 2. A Special Development Permit to allow the proposed project to deviate from the following development standards: Landscape Standard (Section 3.9.3.V.1.f): When a drive-through lane is adjacent to a public right­of-way, a minimum of 25 feet of landscaping shall be provided between the drive-through lane and right-of-way as measured from the back of sidewalk. As proposed, the project would have 22.5 feet of landscaping between drive-through lane and right of way. 3. A Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).

ceqa-17c7735f0183fb9dff.name: ITS Norwood Project (T15255000)
ceqa-17c7735f0183fb9dff.description: This project proposes installing Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) and Accessible Pedestrian Signal (APS) upgrades along portions of Norwood Avenue, including traffic signal cabinets and controllers, traffic signal interconnects, advanced loop detections, pedestrian push buttons and countdown pedestrian heads within the City of Sacramento.

ceqa-e4a1568f1daba1699a.description: The proposed Wellington Crossing Project consists of a Tentative Subdivision Map for Condominium, Subdivision Design Review, and Major Design Review for 188 unit attached townhomes and a new ±4500 square foot clubhouse with onsite amenities. The Project proposal includes a three-story multi-family residential development with onsite amenities, landscape areas, and associated improvements on a vacant parcel. The new townhomes will comply with the City’s Climate Action Plan (“CAP”) measures.

ceqa-46ac1b02e2d7457f71.name: Permit No. 20026 –ARCF Project/NLIP, Phase 4b Landside Improvements Project, Natomas Basin Project/Overhead Communications Utilities
ceqa-46ac1b02e2d7457f71.projectTitle: Common Features/Natomas PACR/Natomas Levee Improvement Program, Phase 4b Project
ceqa-46ac1b02e2d7457f71.description: Approval of Permit No. 20026, under California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Article 3, Section 6, for work within an adopted plan of flood control: To install a total of nine (9) utility poles and overhead communication lines along and across the Garden Highway levee. Eight (8) poles will be installed on the waterside slope of the levee, and one pole will be located approximately 70 feet from the existing landside levee toe. The overhead communication lines will cross from the landside to the waterside at Orchard Lane and will continue along the poles on the waterside. All poles will be wood, ranging in height from 35 to 40 feet, and set to a depth of 6 feet below the existing grade. The communication lines on the waterside will also be attached to three (3) existing Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD) utility poles authorized under Board Permit Nos. 19637 and 19735, issued on April 20, 2022, and July 10, 2023, respectively. This utility work is associated with Natomas Basin Civil Works Project, Reach A.

ceqa-707a47bae9e96ece3b.name: Twitchell Island Eco-Cultural Burn Pilot Project
ceqa-707a47bae9e96ece3b.projectTitle: Twitchell Island Eco-Cultural Burn Pilot Project
ceqa-707a47bae9e96ece3b.description: In collaboration with the Department of Water Resources (DWR), a team of researchers propose to conduct a single 10-acre wetland cultural burn and carbon sequestration research project on Twitchell Island in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta on a weather-permitting day in January-March 2026. This goal is to reintroduce fire to remove excessive dead biomass to enhance ecosystem function and wetland carbon sequestration on DWR’s subsidence reversal wetlands to determine the feasibility and potential to reintroduce ecocultural burning to appropriately manage DWR's Delta wetlands. The burn will be orchestrated by Dr. Don Hankins with CSU Chico, a pyrogeographer and Miwok (Plains Miwok) cultural practitioner and carbon measurements by Dr. Kyle Delwiche and other researchers from the Biometeorology lab at UC Berkeley and Dr. Patty Oikawa from CSU East Bay. The burn will be done on a day where winds are between 2-8 mph and air quality conditions allow. Contingency lines will be created in advance to ensure the controlled burn is contained and the River Delta Fire Academy is invited to be on site as a training opportunity.

ceqa-9ebe7576803909001b.name: PLANEJANE L.L.C.
ceqa-9ebe7576803909001b.description: The Department of Cannabis Control, pursuant to authority granted under Business and Procession Code Division 10, Chapter 2, Section 26012, approved a Cannabis Distribution License submitted on 8/26/2025, by PLANEJANE L.L.C. The proposed project will operate a distribution license out of an existing facility located at 8842 Elder Creek RD, UNIT B, Sacramento, CA 95828 (APN 064-0020-047-0007). The applicant will store cannabis products for distribution on a 1.92-acre parcel. The project will not expand the existing structure and no modifications are needed to this site.

ceqa-c267c5bc22e71320c3.projectTitle: Common Features/Natomas PACR/Natomas Levee Improvement Program, Phase 4b Project

ceqa-6980fd317c79ea09de.name: Consumnes River and Deer Creek Stream Gage Installation - CalSIP
ceqa-6980fd317c79ea09de.projectTitle: Cosumnes River and Deer Creek Stream Gaging
ceqa-6980fd317c79ea09de.description: As part of the California Stream Gage Improvement Program, the California Department of Water Resources has executed a contract with the Omochumne-Hartnell Water District to install a stream gage on Deer Creek downstream of the Old Vine Drive bridge crossing and repair and upgrade two existing stream gages on the Consumnes River located at the Rooney and Mahon flashboard dam sites. The proposed stream gage installation and upgrades will monitor water levels and streamflow to inform groundwater management and improve the understanding of conditions when groundwater recharge can be performed.

ceqa-a08d01a25162e30015.name: Delta Meadows Parking Lot Improvements
ceqa-a08d01a25162e30015.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-a08d01a25162e30015.description: The purpose of this project is to install an accessible parking pad, accessible portable toilet, outdoor bulletin board, and create two (2) picnic areas in and near the existing gravel parking lot at Delta Meadows Park Property to make the property more accessible and provide recreational and related facilities to park visitors. Work will: Use weed whippers, hedgers, and mowers to remove vegetation from work areas; Level four (4) areas where concrete or decomposed granite will be poured; Pour a 17-ft x 18-ft x 4-in. deep concrete pad to create one fully striped (1) 9-ft x 18-ft ADA parking space with a 5-ft access aisle; Pour a 6-ft x 11-ft x 4-in. deep concrete pad to support one (1) ADA compliant portable restroom; In the proposed picnic areas, install 6-in. of decomposed granite (DG) to create one (1) 50-ft x 45-ft picnic area and one (1) 25-ft x 25-ft picnic area; Construct a 36-in. wide by 30-ft long ADA compliant path from the ADA parking pad to the picnic areas; Dig one (1) 48-in. deep hole to install an outdoor bulletin board and one (1) 12-in. deep hole to install an accessible parking sign; and Pour concrete to set the bulletin board and the parking sign posts in concrete.

ceqa-faed17b037fffcc545.name: Brannan Island SRA ADEP Enhancement and Wallflower Introduction
ceqa-faed17b037fffcc545.projectTitle: Brannan Island SRA ADEP Enhancement and Wallflower Introduction
ceqa-faed17b037fffcc545.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-faed17b037fffcc545.description: The purpose of this project is to remove and control non-native plant species at Brannan Island State Recreation Area while enhancing the existing population of Antioch Dunes evening primrose (ADEP) and introducing a new population of Contra Costa wallflower (CCW), both federally endangered plants. The creation of multiple spatially distinct populations will preserve the long-term biological diversity of both species. On an annual basis, State Parks staff will: Use hand tools and chainsaws to remove all non-native vegetation and selectively thin native vegetation within 5 feet of either ADEP or CCW for a maximum plot of 1.7 acres; Treat cut stump woody vegetation and foliar application of herbicide up to three times to observe regrowth; Use a string trimmer or walk-behind mower in spring and summer to create a disturbance regime; After mowing use hand tools to scrape a maximum of 2 inches of soil; and Dispose of removed vegetation by either chipping onsite, as directed by Environmental Scientist, or haul offsite to a local green-waste facility for disposal.

ceqa-eec92532ff3fd5f45b.name: Preferred Pump & Equipment DR24-216
ceqa-eec92532ff3fd5f45b.description: Preferred Pump & Equipment, LP (Applicant) proposes Site Plan & Design Review Application No. DR24-216 pertaining to one (1) parcel (APN 215-0250-015-0000) that totals approximately 7.2 acres located on northeast corner of Dry Creek Road and Claire Avenue in Sacramento, CA. Site Plan & Design Review Application No. DR24-216 proposes the development of the subject property with an approximately 40,500 square foot (sf.) building consisting of a 9,500-sf. two-story office and 36,748 sf. warehouse along with 35 parking spaces and on and off-site improvements including drive aisles, curb, gutter, sidewalk, lighting, a trash enclosure, and landscaping. The facility will serve as the new location of Preferred Pump & Equipment’s operation. The SPDR would also allow for the development of a storm drainage basin located on the northwest corner of the subject property. The storm drainage basin will be owned and maintained by the developer.
ceqa-eec92532ff3fd5f45b.crossStreets: Dry Creek Road and Claire Avenue

ceqa-99d55613caef36e7da.name: Minor Text Amendments to the 2040 General Plan
ceqa-99d55613caef36e7da.projectTitle: Sacramento 2040 General Plan and Climate Action & Adaptation Plan
ceqa-99d55613caef36e7da.description: The project includes amending the 2040 General Plan by making minor text changes to fix typographical errors and to make clarifications to Employment Mixed-Use (EMU) designation in the Land Use and Placemaking Element. General Plan Designation descriptions indicate that they allow for a range of activities, and each designation includes a companion list of types of allowable uses. The current description of the EMU designation already states that "this designation provides for a range of light industrial and high technology uses." The modified text will further clarify that the types of allowable uses include light industrial uses that do not generate substantial noise or noxious odors.
ceqa-99d55613caef36e7da.crossStreets: The project area is the City of Sacramento and adjacent areas.

ceqa-d1a5dde0a5ee033b8d.name: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-d1a5dde0a5ee033b8d.projectTitle: Long-Term Operation of the State Water Project in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, Suisun Marsh, and Suisun Bay
ceqa-d1a5dde0a5ee033b8d.description: DWR is proposing an alternative decision-making approach to the collaborative approach described in the FEIR in section 2.3.3.2, Start of OMR Management, subsections of 2.3.3. Real-Time Adjustments, including Adult Delta Smelt Entrainment Protection Action and Larval and Juvenile Delta Smelt Protection Action, and section 2.3.22 Governance, subsection 2.3.22.4, Delta (2024 Incidental Take Permit for the Long-Term Operations of the California State Water Project Conditions of Approval [COAs] 8.5.1 and 8.6.1, which in turn would affect three of the Delta Smelt Actions [COAs 8.3.1, 8.3.2, 8.4.1]). The proposed modifications include the following: • The First Flush Action, Adult Delta Smelt Entrainment Protection Action (Turbidity Bridge) and Larval and Juvenile Longfin Smelt Protection Action will be added to the list of SWP management actions that are subject to assessment. o Assessments will propose operational adjustments within boundaries no more negative than -5,000 cfs OMR. o Assessments will include an evaluation of impacts to covered species by proposed operations, informed by available quantitative tools and real-time data, which may include entrainment and routing, modeling, distribution, and other real-time data, as appropriate. • Allow real-time assessment for Delta Smelt winter and spring entrainment protection actions. o DWR will provide an assessment framework that considers covered species impacts. o DWR will develop a science plan to improve understanding of Delta Smelt and salmonid movement and migration behaviors during the OMR flow period that will inform the real-time assessment framework of OMR flow management for Delta Smelt and Salmon and develop new operational conditions by 2029. No changes to SWP facilities or other operations are proposed.

ceqa-e4e2426bdcb9d2605f.name: 5207 Madison Ave WCF (UPZ-SPZ-DRS).
ceqa-e4e2426bdcb9d2605f.description: The proposed project consists of a Use Permit to allow for the construction of a new 80-foot monopine wireless communication facility (WCF) in the Light Commercial (LC) zoning district. The project also includes a Special Development Permit to deviate from both the height - maximum requirement and separation - interior property boundaries requirements. Lastly, the project also includes a Design Review to determine substantial compliance with the Sacramento County Countywide Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).

ceqa-3213fed1bbb49479b7.name: Facilities Modernization and Expansion Project
ceqa-3213fed1bbb49479b7.description: The Citrus Heights Water District proposes to modernize its existing corporation yard at 6230 Sylvan Road and relocate some existing staff to its newly acquired office building at 7803B Madison Avenue. The project would address existing facility deficiencies and projected office/maintenance needs through 2045. The project would include interior renovations of office buildings, demolition of an existing maintenance shop, construction of a new maintenance shop, and site improvements.
ceqa-3213fed1bbb49479b7.crossStreets: Sylvan Road and Greenback Lane; Madison Ave and Sunrise Ave

ceqa-4b1f92a95a2176f989.name: Levee Damage Repair (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-61958-R2)
ceqa-4b1f92a95a2176f989.projectTitle: Levee Damage Repair (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-61958-R2)

ceqa-4b1f92a95a2176f989.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 2 - Northern Central, Rancho Cordova
ceqa-4b1f92a95a2176f989.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-61958-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, The Nature Conservancy.
