ceqa-fa7c0bd5d4c1963cc7.name: Meister Way Improvement project
ceqa-fa7c0bd5d4c1963cc7.description: The project would widen Meister Way to a two-lane arterial road from Bear Paw Drive to Lone Tree Road. This project would also include curb and gutter improvements, curb ramps, and three new traffic signals at the intersections of Meister Way and Metro Air Parkway, Badiee Drive, and Lone Tree Road (to be constructed). Existing utilities would be adjusted to project grade level and extended to new traffic lights. No right-of­way acquisition is proposed for this project. There would be dedications by the adjacent property owners for County road right of way. The total length of the project is approximately 3,500 linear feet.

ceqa-3dbf5e570a31a333d9.name: Waterman Road at CCTC Railroad Crossing
ceqa-3dbf5e570a31a333d9.description: Sacramento County Department of Transportation (SacDOT) is proposing to connect Waterman Road between Thimbleberry Drive and Ribera Street in the North Vineyard Station Specific Plan area in unincorporated Sacramento County. Waterman Road will be connected by a new at-grade crossing over the Central California Traction Company (CCTC) railroad crossing. Additionally, curb, gutter, sidewalk, raised landscape medians, and Class 2 bike lanes will be installed along the project alignment. The project is anticipated to take approximately seven months to be constructed, and construction activities will be restricted to between 7:00am and 7:00pm on weekdays. Nighttime construction is not anticipated and will only be performed upon approval from the County. Construction activities are anticipated to include excavation, grading, and paving. Standard construction equipment will be utilized and includes generators, compressors, backhoes, loaders, and a variety of trucks. Water facilities including water valves and drainage manholes are located along the project alignment and may require adjustment. Utility coordination will be an ongoing effort as the project progresses and conflicts are identified and resolved with the utility company. Construction of the project will require permanent right of way acquisition for public roadway public utility easements (PRPUE) and public utilities public facilities easements (PUPFE) from two parcels along Waterman Road. Approximately 2,648 square feet will be required from Assessor's Parcel Number (APN) 066-0210-045 for PUPFE and approximately 7,200 square feet will be required for PRPUE. Approximately 1,658 square feet will be required from APN 065-0052-003 for PRPUE. This may be altered during final design; however, no full property acquisitions would be required. Additionally, no demolition of existing structures within the acquisition areas would be required.

ceqa-704b29ba5b13c287a6.name: The Ranch – Rancho Cordova Parkway Widening (Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. SAC-59569-R2)
ceqa-704b29ba5b13c287a6.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number SAC-59569-R2, pursuant to section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, K. Hovnanian at Jaeger Ranch, LLC. The project is limited to a 4.9-acre roadway improvement project of Rancho Cordova Parkway that includes a culvert extension. This project is related to the Ranch Project (Agreement No. 1600-2020-0096-R2) but instead of installing a new reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) box culvert under Rancho Cordova Parkway, the existing culvert will be upgraded and extended concurrent with the widening of Rancho Cordova Parkway.

ceqa-0cc22a468b09695c92.name: SMUD Station J Project (P25-014)
ceqa-0cc22a468b09695c92.projectTitle: Station J Bulk Transmission Substation Project
ceqa-0cc22a468b09695c92.description: The project includes entitlements for a new substation, new transmission lines, and new transmission poles within the River District, to bring increased electrical capacity to the surrounding area. The project consists of demolition of existing on-site structures and construction of a new substation with up to six 115/21 Kilovolt (kV) transformers, including up to 9 miles of overhead and underground 115 kV and 21 kV connections into the substation from nearby existing SMUD facilities and infrastructure. The following entitlements were approved: a) a Transmission Facilities Permit for a substation and transmission lines; and b) Site Plan and Design Review for a substation and associated transmission lines and transmission poles, with a deviation to height standards for transmission poles.
ceqa-0cc22a468b09695c92.crossStreets: North B Street and North 14th Street, City of Sacramento

ceqa-1513cddb8b64743a24.name: Change of Ownership and Decommissioning Two Wells
ceqa-1513cddb8b64743a24.projectTitle: Change of Ownership and Decommissioning Two Wells
ceqa-1513cddb8b64743a24.description: The Applicant proposes to operate the former Del Paso Manor County Water District (DPMCWD) as the Sacramento Suburban Water District Del Paso Manor Service Area and will change Wells 03 and 08 from standby to inactive.
ceqa-1513cddb8b64743a24.crossStreets: North of Rockwood Drive and bounded by Marconi, Watt and Eastern Avenues

ceqa-b1b544b432d03b075a.name: Hilton Garden Inn Repaint (PLNG25-028)
ceqa-b1b544b432d03b075a.description: The Project consists of a Minor Design Review for façade improvements to an existing Hilton Garden Inn Hotel at 9241 Laguna Springs Drive. The proposed modifications include new exterior paint to the building elevations and trash enclosure. No expansion of the building or site modifications are proposed with this application.

ceqa-1517ed33aeeaf76bdb.name: American River Salmonid Rearing Habitat Planning
ceqa-1517ed33aeeaf76bdb.projectTitle: American River Salmonid Rearing Habitat Planning
ceqa-1517ed33aeeaf76bdb.description: Project includes restoration planning activities on the lower American River within the American River Parkway to identify and prioritize sites that are feasible for creating or enhancing juvenile salmonid rearing habitat. Ten sites will be prioritized and advanced from conceptual designs up to 65% to complete environmental review and identify a programmatic permitting pathway. WCB Project Tracker ID: 2025089.

ceqa-4528cc9e7c45639f4b.name: Bar None Auction
ceqa-4528cc9e7c45639f4b.description: The project includes the development of three (3) parcels, totaling approximately 47 acres, for the purpose of using the land to store and auction surplus heavy equipment, commercial trucks, agricultural equipment, and industrial support items. The project also includes a request for a Use Permit, Special Development Permit, and Design Review to establish an online auction business facility that would include: a 21,510 square-foot two-story office and reception building, a 12,800 square-foot workshop, and outdoor storage yard for trucks and heavy equipment.
ceqa-4528cc9e7c45639f4b.crossStreets: Bradshaw Road and Elder Creek Road
ceqa-4528cc9e7c45639f4b.action: General Plan Amendment, Rezone, Use Permit

ceqa-dfa8e60c597453d298.name: 2025 MTP/SCS EIR
ceqa-dfa8e60c597453d298.projectTitle: 2025 Metropolitan Transportation Plan/ Sustainable Communities Strategy (MTP/SCS) EIR
ceqa-dfa8e60c597453d298.description: The MTP/SCS is an integrated land use and transportation strategy for the SACOG region, updated every 4 years to ensure eligibility for federal and state transportation funding. The MTP is a long-term (20+ year) plan that guides multimodal transportation investments, while the SCS, required under SB 375, aligns transportation, housing, and land use planning to meet CARB per-capita GHG reduction targets.

ceqa-21b2d1a69178bd8ba4.name: High Grade Venture LCA25-0000391
ceqa-21b2d1a69178bd8ba4.description: The Department of Cannabis Control, pursuant to authority granted under Business and Professions Code, Section 26012, approved a Nursery commercial cannabis license submitted on 09/05/2025, by High Grade Ventures.

ceqa-1ce8e29f315022fc58.name: Sac Pain Elimination/ Massage by Ginger Certificate of Nonconforming Use (NCS)
ceqa-1ce8e29f315022fc58.projectTitle: Sac Pain Elimination/ Massage by Ginger Certificate of Nonconforming Use (NCS)
ceqa-1ce8e29f315022fc58.description: The project consists of a Certificate of Nonconforming Use to allow for continued operations of a massage establishment with multiple providers in the BP zone. The massage establishment was established in 2022 at this location and this project will allow for the continuation of the existing use. It does not involve expansion or a change in the existing use.

ceqa-30b6f9a9b09b9c12f3.name: 4005 Manzanita Avenue Lot Line Adjustment
ceqa-30b6f9a9b09b9c12f3.description: The project consists of a lot line adjustment between the subject parcels, addressed at 4001 and 4005 Manzanita Avenue and the properties located at 7423 and 7433 Fair Oaks Boulevard, located on the western side of the intersection of Fair Oaks Boulevard and Manzanita Avenue, in the Carmichael community of unincorporated Sacramento County.

ceqa-a7a820ce926773cb1e.name: Power Inn Apartments
ceqa-a7a820ce926773cb1e.description: The proposed Power Inn Apartments Project consists of a Major Design Review for a 72 unit, deed-restricted affordable housing development and one (1) manager's unit on 1.44-acres. The project will consist of one, five-story building as well as indoor and outdoor amenities including a community room, fitness center, and an inner courtyard. In addition, associated site improvements including parking, lighting, and landscaping will be installed/constructed. The Project was submitted under SB35, a state law which provides for streamlined, ministerial review and approval of qualifying housing development projects.

ceqa-ee4d2fe6e1138d5053.name: Anne Rudin Preserve Williamson Act Contract (APB)
ceqa-ee4d2fe6e1138d5053.projectTitle: Anne Rudin Preserve Williamson Act Contract (APB)
ceqa-ee4d2fe6e1138d5053.description: The project consists of a request to amend an existing Agricultural Preserve for Williamson Act contract 2004-AP-005 to a total of 109. 71 acres, by merging 56.38 acres in the AG-40 zone (Cummings Preserve) with an additional 53.33 acres in the AG-40 zone (Anne Rudin Preserve), in the Natomas community.

ceqa-0bef39499cca92f9ed.name: Holy Cross New Church and Hall Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-0bef39499cca92f9ed.projectTitle: Holy Cross New Church and Hall Use Permit Amendment
ceqa-0bef39499cca92f9ed.description: The project consists of a Use Permit Amendment (93-UPB-0753) and Design Review to increase the seating capacity from 150 to 253 persons and to modify the previously approved phasing plan at an existing church in the Interim Agricultural Reserve/Surface Mining (IR/SM) zoning district. Construction associated with the proposed project consists of a new 18,000 square-foot, two-story church. The church structure will consist of a 9,100 square-foot social hall on the first floor and an 8,900 square-foot worship space on the second floor, which will be completed in two separate phases. In addition, a new 575 square-foot property maintenance storage structure and a 900 square-foot play structure are proposed. The project also includes demolition of three structures on the subject property. Those three structures include a 1,340 square foot caretaker residence, a 485 square foot food closet (two-car detached garage) and a 950 square-foot single family residence that is currently being used for refreshments and education. The existing 2,200 square-foot chapel and 3,900 square-foot shade structure will remain on the project site.

ceqa-5d03391556b20dbc7d.name: Legado Specific Plan Project
ceqa-5d03391556b20dbc7d.description: The Legado Specific Plan Project (proposed project) would establish a framework and strategy for development of a large-scale, mixed-use, mixed-density master planned community in the City of Rancho Cordova. The Specific Plan document will include proposed land use designations, policies to guide the development, and plans for infrastructure and public services. The proposed land uses include a mix of residential densities, commercial/employment uses, two elementary school sites, an underlying secondary high school/middle school site, parks and open space, a lake recreation area, and a system of trails. The Specific Plan would include over 234 acres of wetland preserve areas and over 140 acres of Laguna Creek corridor and open space. The proposed project would require approval of Annexation into the Sacramento Area Sewer District (SacSewer) service area, General Plan Amendment, Specific Plan, Rezone, Large and Small Lot Tentative Maps, and a Development Agreement.
ceqa-5d03391556b20dbc7d.crossStreets: Jackson Road (Highway 16), Grant Line Road, Sunrise Boulevard, Kiefer Boulevard, etc.

ceqa-5d03391556b20dbc7d.developmentType: Residential (Units 5245, Acres 678.6), Commercial (Sq. Ft. 1215324, Acres 27.9, Employees 1), Educational (Public/Quasi-Public: 24.8 acres), Recreational (Park: 110.8 acres), Other (Open Space/Preserve/Natural: 440.9 acres), Transportation:Other (Major Streets: 59.3 acres)

ceqa-9c1aa3d2ee7ef48a3d.name: Coyote Creek Agrivoltaic Ranch Project
ceqa-9c1aa3d2ee7ef48a3d.description: CONTROL NUMBER: PLNP2021-00191 The project is a request for a use permit to construct, operate, and ultimately decommission an approximately 200-megawatt (MW) alternating current (AC) photovoltaic (PV) solar energy generating facility and associated 4-hour/100 MW AC battery energy storage system (BESS) on parcels that total approximately 2,700 acres in the Cosumnes community of unincorporated Sacramento County. The project is generally located south of U.S. Route 50 , northwest of Rancho Murieta, southeast of the Prairie City State Vehicle Recreation Area (PCSVRA), and south of White Rock Road in the Cosumnes community. Specifically, it is located on what is known as the "Barton Ranch" adjacent to 3830 Scott Road. A dedicated transmission line called a generation tie (gen-tie) line would extend approximately 1.3 miles west to provide an interconnection to the Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD) 230 kilovolt (kV) powerline which runs through PCSVRA. The applicant is proposing to construct, operate, and at the end of the project's life, decommission a solar generation and energy storage facility . The development area (approximately 1,412 acres of the 2,700 acres) will include an on-site substation, inverters, fencing , roads , and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system.

ceqa-625fbb723f0ec4b6b0.name: AT&T at Tetotom Park WCF
ceqa-625fbb723f0ec4b6b0.description: The proposed project will be completed in two phases. The first phase consists of executing a lease agreement between Sunrise Recreation and Park District and AT&T for a Wireless Telecommunications Facility (WCF) permit at Tetotom Park at 5127 Heartland Drive in the Antelope community of unincorporated Sacramento County. The second phase of the proposed project can only occur if the proposed lease agreement is executed (approved). Execution of the lease would allow for AT&T to construct and operate a new WCF. Therefore, Phase 2 consists of a request for a Use Permit by the Sacramento County Planning Commission to construct a new 50-foot-tall WCF within a lease area of about 556 square feet, located on the east side of the tennis courts at Tetotom Park. The WCF is designed to match existing cell towers, located on the west and east side of the tennis courts. The proposed WCF will accommodate six (6) panel antennas, nine (9) RRUs (remote radio units), three (3) air antennas, 30KW backup generator, and associated electrical equipment. The WCF will be unmanned and will require occasional maintenance; site access will be via a shared (with Verizon) 10’ wide utility easement which would connect to the park’s existing interior roadway. Pruning of nearby trees will be required for the construction of the WCF. The applicant will coordinate work with a qualified arborist. In addition, AT&T proposes to replace an existing light pole, located directly outside of the WCF lease area, with a new 50-foot-tall light pole.
ceqa-625fbb723f0ec4b6b0.crossStreets: Don Julio Boulevard and Heartland Drive

ceqa-95aab7bcf5909b4182.name: Touch Therapy NCS
ceqa-95aab7bcf5909b4182.description: The existing massage establishment is seeking a Certificate of Nonconforming Use to continue operations after updates to the Zoning Code prohibited multiple provider massage establishments in the Business Professional Office (BP) zoning district.

ceqa-01bfc1081e837dbafb.name: Issue Right of Entry Permit to Aerojet for New Monitoring Locations
ceqa-01bfc1081e837dbafb.projectTitle: Issue Right of Entry Permit to Aerojet for New Monitoring Locations
ceqa-01bfc1081e837dbafb.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-01bfc1081e837dbafb.description: Issue a Right of Entry (ROE) Permit to Aerojet Rocketdyne to Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area for the purpose of installing new monitoring wells within the park. All work conducted in association with the ROE permit will comply with all State and Federal environmental laws, including but not limited to the Endangered Species Act, California Environmental Quality Act, Section 5024 of the Public Resources Code, and all conditions identified in the Right of Entry Permit;

ceqa-96d81b893ef6766962.name: CAT POWER Hub The California Advanced Technology Portable Off-road Job Site Energy Resource Hub
ceqa-96d81b893ef6766962.projectTitle: MORRISON CREEK MINING REACH UPSTREAM (NORTH) OF JACKSON HWY
ceqa-96d81b893ef6766962.description: Project will develop and demonstrate an off-road, off-grid operations hub in Sacramento for mobile, machine charging, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to support electric machines and equipment operating at two job sites. The project will install a minimum of 56 EV charging ports (Level 2, DC fast chargers, and mobile chargers), 12 acres of solar photovoltaic, and eight megawatt hours of BESS to support zero-emission construction vehicles across both job sites. This agreement is in coordination with a California Air Resources Board grant for zero-emission vehicles.

ceqa-08b3692aac1cdf24fa.name: Permit No. 20021- Snake Marsh Restoration Project
ceqa-08b3692aac1cdf24fa.description: The project proposes to restore approximately 343 acres of perennial freshwater marsh habitat as part of the Snake Marsh Wetland Restoration Project through the construction of two earthen berms and installation of two 18-inch High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) pipelines to convey irrigation water from an existing irrigation well to the marsh. The two pipelines, approximately 300 and 4,900 feet long, will be installed within 3.5-foot-deep trenches along existing access roads. The two berms will be approximately 1,750-foot and 750-foot long, 7-foot high, with 12-foot-wide crowns, 5:1 side slopes, and will include the installation of water control structures. The project also includes planting 35 native oak trees.

ceqa-93d47c6c9b829c5bd0.name: Minor Alteration No. WA2025113 – Septic Chamber Repair Project
ceqa-93d47c6c9b829c5bd0.projectTitle: Minor Alteration No. WA2025113 – Septic Chamber Repair Project
ceqa-93d47c6c9b829c5bd0.description: To repair an existing septic system by excavating a 3.5-foot-deep trench to expose the existing pipe, removing the existing pipe, installing two Prinsco Inc. Pro4 wastewater chambers, backfilling the trench per Title 23 standards, and restoring the ground cover to pre-project conditions. The septic system is currently permitted by Board Permit No. 3777.

ceqa-c81bdf93d417144e34.name: Tyler Island Road Bridge over Georgiana Slough Technical Analysis (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SAC-58445-R3)
ceqa-c81bdf93d417144e34.projectTitle: Tyler Island Road Bridge over Georgiana Slough Technical Analysis (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SAC-58445-R3)
ceqa-c81bdf93d417144e34.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Bay Delta Region 3
ceqa-c81bdf93d417144e34.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 3 - Bay Delta, Fairfield
ceqa-c81bdf93d417144e34.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-CCA-58445-R3, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to Sacramento County Department of Transportation. The project is limited to a geotechnical investigation of the Tyler Island Bridge Road Bridge to inform repair decisions and design. Bridge inspection reports have noted scour at the swing span piers; therefore, Sacramento County Department of Transportation will conduct geotechnical investigations to assess the subsurface conditions at the pier locations of the existing bridge. The investigation will include drilling three bore holes and conducting a cone penetration test near Piers 2 and 3, with a maximum depth of 120 feet below ground surface. All geotechnical investigations will be conducted from a barge or small watercraft that will be launched from an existing ramp and driven to the project area. No vegetation will be removed, and water diversion will not be conducted.

ceqa-a1c6b1c6b9800d18e1.name: Minor Alteration No. WA2025084 – Syphon Irrigation Pipe in the Georgiana Slough Project
ceqa-a1c6b1c6b9800d18e1.projectTitle: Minor Alteration No. WA2025084 – Syphon Irrigation Pipe in the Georgiana Slough Project
ceqa-a1c6b1c6b9800d18e1.description: To repair an existing 10-inch siphon irrigation pipe and pump assembly by lowering the platform on which the pump stands, digging down to expose the existing 10-inch pipe, cutting the pipe and installing a 10-inch by 8-inch reducer, installing an 8-inch pipe that connects the reducer to the pump, installing a new positive closure device on the waterside pump connection, and restoring the levee to pre-project conditions per Title 23 standards. The pipe and pump assembly are currently permitted by Board Permit No. 11177.

ceqa-9d4d1fb38bd8525a6e.name: Russell at Truxel Residential (P22-042)
ceqa-9d4d1fb38bd8525a6e.description: The project request consists of Tentative Subdivision Map, Tentative Map Design Deviations, Site Plan and Design Review, and State Density Bonus Law approval to allow for the construction of up to 219 residential units, including up to 100 single-family detached for sale market-rate units and 119 multifamily below market rate rental units (including one manager's unit), and associated infrastructure and amenities on an approximately 17 .39-acre project site. The proposed project may record multiple final maps to create separate legal parcels for the market rate housing component, affordable housing component, and a stormwater detention basin. Creation of separate legal parcels would enable separate phasing of construction and financing for each component, as needed.

ceqa-e0823424c6951ead15.name: Luxelocker Sacramento
ceqa-e0823424c6951ead15.description: Site Plan and Design Review to construct three storage buildings with associated amenities and site improvements on a 3.08-acre parcel in the Light Industrial Zone (M-1) within the Citywide Design Review Area.

ceqa-0e99fe5b8b25824358.name: Rio Del Oro Land Use Transfer-Phase 5
ceqa-0e99fe5b8b25824358.projectTitle: Rio Del Oro Land Use Transfer-Phase 5
ceqa-0e99fe5b8b25824358.description: The project consists of a minor amendment to the Rio Del Oro Specific Plan (RDOSP). The revision would reduce Industrial Park (MP) land from 166.7 acres to 149.2 acres, increase Business Park (BP) land from 44.7 to 62.3 acres, and would move MP and BP parcels to better accommodate future projects along Gold Dredge Way.
ceqa-0e99fe5b8b25824358.crossStreets: Gold Dredge Way and Rancho Cordova Parkway

ceqa-c13c4298ada805e159.name: Delta Shores West (Part 2) Project (DR25-094)
ceqa-c13c4298ada805e159.description: This project consists of a request for Site Plan and Design Review to construct 27 single unit dwellings on individual lots (lots 112-114 inclusive, 123-136 inclusive, and 148-157 inclusive of the Delta Shores West Subdivision Map, P06-197) in the Single-Unit Dwelling Zone (R-1-PUD) within the Delta Shores PUD Design Review Area
ceqa-c13c4298ada805e159.crossStreets: The site sits within the Delta Shores Master Plan area.

ceqa-85224c75995a3dd7c0.name: Permit No. 19976: Natomas PACR/NLIP / Landside Improvement Phase 4b: Street Light Utility Poles Replacement
ceqa-85224c75995a3dd7c0.projectTitle: Common Features/Natomas PACR/Natomas Levee Improvement Program, Phase 4b Project
ceqa-85224c75995a3dd7c0.description: Approval of Permit No. 19976, under California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Article 3, Section 6, for work within an adopted plan of flood control: To remove and replace 15 existing steel streetlight poles (Caltrans Type 15; 8-in diameter, 34-ft length, 5-ft embedment depth) along the landside edge of levee crown on Garden Highway (5-ft from edge of pavement) from Gateway Oaks Drive to Truxel Road as part of the USACE Reach I Contract 2 Project. Replacement poles will be auger drilled and existing streetlights to be removed off site by the Contractor.

ceqa-3336e95d9aa3e86f89.name: Minor Alteration No. WA2025123 – Watt Avenue Levee Access /Waterline Repair Project
ceqa-3336e95d9aa3e86f89.description: The proposed work includes excavation of the levee embankment near the damaged pipe, removal of the existing galvanized metal pipe, excavation and compaction of the levee to address voids caused by the leak and sinkhole, installation of a new ductile iron pipe with compatible Romac connections, and restoration of the aggregate base and paved levee crest. No in-water work will be performed. Existing air-release and shutoff valves located on the landside of the levee will remain unaltered. This existing 2-inch waterline supplies municipal water to American River Parkway facilities and are components of the Sacramento River Flood Control Project (SRFCP). It is permitted under Board Permit 9125-B.

ceqa-4abe9852c60c62f01a.name: Holistic Massage by Susan Certificate of Nonconforming Use
ceqa-4abe9852c60c62f01a.projectTitle: Holistic Massage by Susan Certificate of Nonconforming Use
ceqa-4abe9852c60c62f01a.description: The project consists of a Certificate of Nonconforming Use to allow for continued operations of a sole practitioner massage establishment that is over 400 square feet in floor area. The business was established in 2019 at this location and this project will allow for the continuation of the existing use. The project does not involve expansion or change in the existing use.

ceqa-ad12552650e945154f.name: 5300 N LLC Cannabis Cultivation License
ceqa-ad12552650e945154f.description: The Department of Cannabis Control, pursuant to authority granted under Business and Procession Code Division 10, Chapter 2, Section 26012, approved Cannabis License submitted on 02/06/2025, by Bryant Lee applied for a Nursery license.

ceqa-19cf57e764313acf22.name: Maverik Fueling Station and Convenience Store (PLNG24-031/APLA25-001)
ceqa-19cf57e764313acf22.projectTitle: Maverik Fueling Station and Convenience Store (PLNG24-031/APLA25-001)
ceqa-19cf57e764313acf22.description: The Maverik Fueling Station and Convenience Store Project (PLNG24-031) consists of a Conditional Use Permit to allow a fueling station use on the Project site and Minor Design Review for the proposed fueling station and convenience store. The proposed development includes a ±5,951 square foot convenience store, two fuel canopies with a total of 25 pumps and associated site improvements (i.e. landscaping, parking, and lighting). The Project shall comply with the City’s Climate Action Plan (CAP) for non-residential development.

ceqa-c190837af505e0a452.name: Folsom Plan Area Specific Plan (FPASP) – Folsom Heights (Streambed Alteration Agreement Notification No. 1600-2012-0198-0013-R2) Extension
ceqa-c190837af505e0a452.projectTitle: Folsom South of U.S. Highway 50 Specific Plan
ceqa-c190837af505e0a452.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has extended Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification Number 1600-2012-0198-0013-R2, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the project Applicant, Folsom South Area Group. This Extension extends the Sub-Notification expiration from November 12, 2025 to November 12, 2030. All other conditions in the original Sub-Notification remain in effect.

ceqa-ce177ef7d6c718829a.name: Georgiana Slough Erosion Control and Habitat Enhancement Project
ceqa-ce177ef7d6c718829a.projectTitle: GEORGIANA SLOUGH EROSION CONTROL AND HABITAT ENHANCEMENT PROJECT
ceqa-ce177ef7d6c718829a.description: The Brannan-Andrus Levee Maintenance District (BALMD) is proposing the Georgiana Slough Erosion Control and Habitat Enhancement Project to resolve upper slope erosion problems and a major lower slope undercutting issue along the right bank levee of Georgiana Slough, on Lower Andrus Island. The Proposed Project would involve construction of proven erosion control methods involving placement of quarry stone rip rap (or rock slope protection) at the toe of the levee, which doubles as a foundational base for a habitat bench that will be constructed along the entire length. The State Lands Commission action is issuance of a 20-year General Lease – Public Agency Use through November 6, 2045

ceqa-a86bbc379e84c96b2b.name: Oveja Ranch Solar Project
ceqa-a86bbc379e84c96b2b.description: A Sacramento County Board of Supervisors review for three Williamson Act Contract Amendments (69-AP-023.2, 69-AP-023.6 and 69-AP-023.5) to allow Commercial Solar Facilities and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) as compatible uses within the three Williamson Act Contracts. Approval of the amendments will allow for the establishment of a SMUD renewable energy generation facility across three agricultural properties in the Agricultural - 160 Acres (AG-160) and Flood Combining (F) zoning districts. The proposed SMUD renewable energy generation facility (SMUD Facility) will include construction of PV solar panels, a BESS, a substation, and new upgraded distribution lines to interconnect the project to SMUD's existing distribution system. SMUD, as Leady Agency, prepared an Environmental Impact Report; SMUD approved the SMUD Facility project and certified the Final Environmental Impact Report on 9/18/2025.

ceqa-818d4cf5d281358c0c.name: CALMADE: California Manufacturing for Activated Dry Electrode
ceqa-818d4cf5d281358c0c.projectTitle: CALMADE: California Manufacturing for Activated Dry Electrode
ceqa-818d4cf5d281358c0c.description: LiCAP Technologies, Inc. proposes to retrofit a vacant facility to accommodate the installation of a 500 MWh Activated Dry Electrode® (ADE) manufacturing line. This commercial-scale manufacturing operations focused on LiCAP’s proprietary ADE process, a solvent-free method of producing lithium-ion battery electrodes. This project will increase domestic battery supply chain security and clean energy jobs.

ceqa-57d65a5543fbf0e834.name: Caltrans Sac HQ Translab Directors Order (03-3G280)
ceqa-57d65a5543fbf0e834.projectTitle: Caltrans Sac HQ Translab Directors Order (03-3G280)
ceqa-57d65a5543fbf0e834.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) initiated a District Director’s Order to repair the non-functioning Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) components at the Caltrans Translab facility located at 5900 Folsom Boulevard in Sacramento adjacent to US 50 near PM R2.13 in Sacramento County. The purpose of this project is to improve the operation of the HVAC system at the Caltrans Translab facility.

ceqa-82dec5ae65a37ef925.name: Orangevale Parks Wildfire Reduction and Habitat Restoration
ceqa-82dec5ae65a37ef925.projectTitle: Orangevale Parks Wildfire Reduction and Habitat Restoration
ceqa-82dec5ae65a37ef925.description: The project consists of the removal of ladder fuels including fallen trees, dead wood, and brush from four (4) park sites and natural areas to reduce wildfire hazards. The removal will include chipping dead wood and leaving woodchips in place or recycling for mulch. The project will also limb up trees along trails and fire access roads, string trim to reduce fire-fuel, create or maintain firebreaks by mowing, and maintain or replace native plants and trees. The total project size is approximately 23.6 acres with a breakdown as follows. Orangevale Community Park (12.5± acres), Sundance Nature Area (1.1± acres), Rollingwood Nature Area (5.1± acres), and the Shackelton Woods portion of Orangevale Community Center Park (4.9± acres).

ceqa-23211dbd5e8343c144.name: 5001 Date Avenue Second Story ADU (SPM)
ceqa-23211dbd5e8343c144.description: The project consists of a Minor Special Development Permit to allow for the construction of a 748-square foot Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) constructed above a new 544-square foot detached storage area. The project proposes to deviate from the maximum number of stories allowed for an ADU, as well as the required 10-foot rear setback for detached ADUs 20 feet in height. ceqa-7ce164e708f5ad2a6e.projectTitle: Minor Alteration No. WA2025065 – Oxbow Marina Sanitation Facility Infrastructure Repair Project
ceqa-7ce164e708f5ad2a6e.description: To perform emergency repair to the sewer line in Oxbow Marina. The sanitation facility infrastructure including the forced sewer main was permitted under Board Permit No. 4398 which was issued in 1973. Potholing of the levee was conducted to locate and determine the extent of damage to the sewer main. Condition assessment of the pipe was performed to evaluate whether a repair or full-in-kind replacement was necessary. The investigation revealed that the existing forced sewer main had been compromised by an unknown source. Emergency repairs were executed based on the assessment findings. The compromised coupler was replaced in-kind by welding a new coupler at the identified location. Excavation backfill was completed using controlled low-strength material through the levee crown, or native material along the slope and toe of the levee, depending on the final position of the repair. Site restoration was performed to return the area to pre-existing conditions, including roadway repaving and the replacement of any features disturbed during the investigation and repair work.

ceqa-4a3f1ce3d03c6502bd.description: The proposed project includes the construction of a new 54,892-square-foot, single-story police station with associated landscaping, surface parking, and utility improvements, as well as a new 1,173 square foot, single-story plaza building, a 1,832 stage, and 3.3-acre civic park on a 9.18-acre site located at the northwest corner of Seneca Road and Civic Drive in the City of Victorville. Additionally, the proposed project would require a Specific Plan Amendment (SPA) to the Civic Center Specific Plan to conditionally allow for government uses in the Specific Plan’s Civic Mixed Land Use Category. The proposed project is intended to address the City of Victorville's growing public safety needs in response to increasing demand for police services. The existing police station, located at 14200 Amargosa Road, was constructed in 2001 and occupies 15,828 square feet. At the time of construction, the station served a population of 67,854 residents with a staff of 57 sworn officers. However, the City's population has since grown to approximately 140,721, and the number of sworn officers has increased to 103, resulting in space constraints within the existing facility.

Intersections with Palomar, Avalon, Camarilla, Del Monte, Hermosa, Indio, and La Contenta Avenues would be repaved to provide smooth transitions.The proposed project would pave and realign Indio Avenue within a 70-foot right-of-way. North of Sunnyslope Drive, pavement would be extended to SR-62 (approximately 0.5 mile), and at the southern end, Indio Avenue would be realigned about 150 feet west to match the alignment south of Yucca Trail. ceqa-3f16e8a44ea4664a25.projectTitle: Silverwood Treatment Plant Golden Mussels Mitigation
ceqa-3f16e8a44ea4664a25.description: Golden mussels have been found in Crestline Lake Arrowhead Water Agency's (CLAWA) raw water line, which supplies the CLAWA Silverwood Treatment Plant. Golden mussels pose a growing statewide threat to California's water supplies and infrastructure. They spread quickly, attach to pipes and equipment, and can disrupt water delivery, making prompt treatment essential. To eliminate the infestation, CLAWA proposes to install a small containment tank and a dosing pump next to the existing pumps at the Department of Water Resources' Silverwood tower outflow location to meet current standards of public health and safety. The equipment will deliver low doses of a treatment solution to the raw water line to remove the golden mussels to meet current standards of public health and safety.

ceqa-ec11f1c4b08f7f9fb0.description: Caltrans District 8 proposes to conduct vegetation management activities within State right-way areas to reduce wildfire ignition risk, establish and maintain roadside fuel breaks, and ensure safe and reliable access for the traveling public and emergency responders. ceqa-fdc38fc6afdd4e043f.name: SB-62 CAPM
ceqa-fdc38fc6afdd4e043f.description: Description of Nature, Purpose, and Beneficiaries of Project: The project is from post mile 94.0 to post mile 106.0 on Route 62 in San Bernardino County. No Federal Land Transfer needed. Scope of Work: Pavement rehab will be performed with a depth of 0.25’ PDR and 0.15’ overlay with RHMA-G. There will be concrete cutoff walls at Post Mile (PM) 95.7, PM 101.8 and cut off wall at PM 101.4. Shoulder backing will be performed on the entire project limits on both sides of the roadway as provided on the cross-sections. Purpose: The purpose of this project is to cost-effectively preserve and extend the service life of the existing pavement, improve its ride quality, and prevent washout. Need: Under heavy and continuous traffic over long periods, the existing pavement has shown signs of deteriorations within the project limits. The 2019 Automated Pavement Condition Survey (APCS) indicated that poor rutting conditions, minor distresses, and unacceptable ride quality, if left uncorrected, will trigger a more costly major roadway rehabilitation. Given the local geography and weather conditions, the roadway segment also has been undermined and washed out after past flood events. To avoid the reoccurrence of imminent roadway failure, preventative measures need to be installed.

ceqa-ba870911286854dde5.projectTitle: SBCFCD Zone 6 Emergency Activities - Tropical Storm Rachel and El Nino 2026-2027
ceqa-ba870911286854dde5.description: Between October 10-12, 2026, the unincorporated communities of Yucca Valley and Twenty-Nine Palms, San Bernardino County, received between 1.5-2" of rain from Tropical Storm Rachel, which resulted in increased storm flows causing severe channel erosion and sediment deposition within 29 Palms Channel, Hospital Channel, and Church Channel. Additionally, on September 21, 2026, the Governor Proclaimed a State of Emergency, statewide, for the anticipated 2026-2027 El Nino. This project may include future emergency activities throughout SBCFCD's Zone 6 throughout the 2026-2027 fall and winter seasons, as El Nino continues to develop and create new storms. Emergency activities may include, but not be limited to, the removal of accumulated sediment and debris; repair of eroded or washed out side-slopes, levees, and access roads; and, repair of appurtenant flood control structures to protect private and public infrastructure, private property, and public safety.

ceqa-d79a6ff27d55181d3b.name: UT1063 - Well No. 53
ceqa-d79a6ff27d55181d3b.description: The Ontario Municipal Utilities Company (OMUC) is proposing the installation and operation of a new groundwater production well in the 1,212-foot pressure zone to increase the reliability of its water supply system. The proposed project consists of drilling, construction, operation, and maintenance of a new groundwater well identified as Well No. 53 (hereinafter referred to as the “Project”). Well No. 53 is proposed to be drilled to a depth of approximately 1,000 feet below ground surface (bgs). The well will be equipped with a 600 horsepower (hp) electric motor and designed to produce a maximum of 3,500 gallons per minute (gpm). The well will include a standby backup diesel generator. The wellhead will be constructed inside an approximately 2,000 square feet (SF) split-face concrete masonry unit well building. The maximum height of the well building will be 20 ft. The well building will include an office, an electrical room to house the electronics to operate the well, and a room housing the 0.8% chlorine generation system, which will store salt in a brine tank. Once produced, the chlorine will be introduced into the pumped groundwater prior to the water entering OMUC’s potable water system. The chlorine generation system is enclosed in a fiberglass tank that will include 110 percent secondary containment. Other Project Site improvements include an asphalt driveway for access from Doubleday Avenue and asphalt around the well building. A pipeline will be constructed from the well head to the City’s existing water pipeline and in Doubleday Avenue. For security purposes, the Well No. 53 site will be enclosed with either a metal fence or a solid wall. Access to the site will be via a locked gate from Doubleday Avenue.

ceqa-c43147590cd0467eeb.name: Bernell Hydraulics Property Removal Action Workplan
ceqa-c43147590cd0467eeb.projectTitle: Bernell Hydraulics Property Removal Action Workplan
ceqa-c43147590cd0467eeb.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-c43147590cd0467eeb.description: The project consists of implementing the Bernell Hydraulics Removal Action Workplan (RAW) to address elevated levels of total petroleum hydrocarbons - diesel range organics (TPH-DRO), lead, mercury, and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in soil at 8810 Etiwanda Avenue (Project Site) in the City of Rancho Cucamonga. The remediation consists of soil excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 138 cubic yards (cy) of contaminated soil and the recordation of a Land Use Covenant (LUC) restricting future use to commercial and industrial purposes. Background: The Project Site is approximately 0.75 acres and consists of a single parcel identified by the County of San Bernardino as Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN): 0229-131-07-0000. Based on a review of historical documentation, the Project Site was initially developed as a California Department of Transportation maintenance yard by 1938. It operated as a metal recycling facility between 1970 and 1980, and later as a hydraulic systems fabrication, maintenance, and repair from the 1980s through August 2023. Currently, the Project Site is an unimproved, vacant parcel; all former buildings, ancillary structures, and concrete surfaces were demolished and removed early in October 2024. The Project Site is bordered by trucking facilities to the north and west, vacant lands to the south, and Etiwanda Avenue to the east. Bernell Hydraulics entered into a Voluntary Cleanup Agreement [Docket No. HSA-FY21/22-076, dated January 2022] with DTSC to oversee the investigation and remediation of hazardous substances at the Project Site. Previous Investigations: In October 2021, a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) was completed for the Project Site, identifying recognized environmental conditions (RECs) associated with historical site operations, heavy oil staining, and the potential for vapor encroachment. To further evaluate these impacts, a Supplemental Site Investigation (SSI) was conducted in 2025. The SSI identified elevated concentrations of TPH-DRO, lead, mercury, and PCBs in shallow soil. These concentrations exceed DTSC screening levels, necessitating the proposed removal action. Project Activities: The RAW proposes excavating and disposing off-site of approximately 138 cubic yards of contaminated soil from three designated grid-squares: E-1 (20 cy impacted by TPH-DRO), D-2 (117 cy impacted by lead and mercury), and C-3 (1 cy impacted by PCBs-Arolclor 1254). Excavation will reach a maximum depth of 5.5 feet below ground surface (bgs). The excavated soil will be managed through a combination of direct loading into transport trucks and secure on-site staging. Staged soil will be covered with plastic sheeting during non-work hours to prevent wind dispersion and stormwater runoff. Off-site disposal of the excavated soil at licensed facilities (such as Soil Safe in Adelanto, CA; La Paz County Landfill, AZ; CWM in Kettleman Hills, CA; and US Ecology in Nevada) is estimated to require approximately 9 truck trips. Following the removal of contaminated soil, confirmation sampling will be conducted to verify that cleanup goals are achieved. Field activities are scheduled to be completed within 15 days. Soil excavation activities will be permitted through the South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD). To comply with dust-suppression and stormwater-management requirements, all transport trucks and earth-moving equipment will undergo tire and exterior washing before leaving the Project Site to prevent the tracking of soil onto neighboring streets. Additionally, air quality will be monitored throughout the operation to verify that dust and contaminant vapors do not exceed levels of concern. These measures include conducting perimeter monitoring to confirm emissions do not migrate beyond the Site boundaries and applying foams or other vapor-control materials to suppress any present contaminant vapors. Although not anticipated, in the event biological, cultural or historical resources are discovered in the course of project activities, work will be suspended while a qualified biologist, cultural or historical specialist makes an assessment of the area and arrangements are made to protect or preserve any resources that are discovered. If human remains are discovered, no further disturbance will occur in the location where the remains are found, and the County Coroner will be notified pursuant to the Health and Safety Code, Chapter 2, Section 7050.5.

ceqa-e1fb918fab5c44219e.name: Fontana 210 Roadside Rehabilitation; EA: 08-1T730/PN: 0826000108
ceqa-e1fb918fab5c44219e.description: The landscape rehabilitation will occur in the city of Fontana in the westbound direction of State Route 210 in San Bernardino County between postmiles (PM) 12.9-15.0. Work will include removal of invasive plant species, degraded/dead trees, installation of new trees and groundcover plantings, implementation of erosion control measures, and upgrades to the irrigation systems. Irrigation improvements will consist of replacing multiple irrigation controllers, remote control valves, electrical wiring, and irrigation pipe (12" to 24") with standard trenching. Equipment staging areas, driving/parking off-pavement, and ramp closures will also be needed. All work will be performed within Caltrans right-of-way (ROW). Purpose: The purpose of this project is to maintain our Classified Landscaped Freeway status by re-establishing planting and improving Roadside Safety for Maintenance Workers by relocating irrigation systems to safe and accessible locations. Need: The need of this project is to address gaps of landscape that can lead to the de-classification of the Classified Landscaped Freeway status. Maintenance worker safety is a current issue due to the location of existing valves near the roadway. Additionally, invasive plant species have taken over the landscape slopes and require additional maintenance and worker exposure.

ceqa-2d8df388f25fc5dc25.name: Glen Helen Parkway Grade Separation Pavement Repair
ceqa-2d8df388f25fc5dc25.projectTitle: Glen Helen Parkway Grade Separation Pavement Repair
ceqa-2d8df388f25fc5dc25.description: The San Bernardino County Department of Public Works proposes to repair approximately 550 feet of existing pavement along Glen Helen Parkway, approximately 125 feet southwest of the Union Pacific Railroad crossing in the Devore area. The project consists of removal and replacement of the existing roadway pavement section. Associated improvements include modification of two drainage inlets and construction of curb and gutter. The work area has a maximum width of approximately 36 feet and a maximum excavation depth of approximately 3.45 feet. Construction equipment may include a bulldozer, wheel loader, excavator, rollers, asphalt paver, concrete breaker, jumping-jack rammer, and backhoe loader. Construction is anticipated to take approximately 30 working days and is expected to begin in spring 2027. The project will not increase roadway capacity, affect a streambed or storm drain, require nighttime construction lighting, require a traffic detour, remove vegetation or trees, affect existing buildings, or require utility relocation. Construction access will be from Glen Helen Parkway, and all work is proposed within the existing County right-of-way. The subject roadway segment was constructed as part of the Glen Helen Parkway Grade Separation Project, W.O. H14057. The original Grade Separation Project received a statutory exemption under Section 15282(g) of the State CEQA Guidelines for railroad grade separation projects. The Notice of Exemption was signed on March 11, 2010 and filed with the San Bernardino County Clerk of the Board on March 15, 2010. The existing roadway has since been damaged and requires repair.
ceqa-2d8df388f25fc5dc25.crossStreets: Glen Helen Parkway and Union Pacific Railroad crossing

ceqa-020f533c029483e531.name: Lucerne Valley Channel Emergency Activities - El Nino 2026-2027
ceqa-020f533c029483e531.projectTitle: Lucerne Valley Channel Emergency Activities - El Nino 2026-2027
ceqa-020f533c029483e531.description: This project is being undertaken in anticipation of an exceptionally strong El Nino event forecast for the 2026-2027 fall and winter seasons and the current, degraded, state of the SCBFCD's Lucerne Valley Channel. Without emergency repairs to the channel, any rain event, but especially a large rain event, may result in significant structural integrity degradation, ultimately posing a clear and imminent threat to public and private property, infrastructure, and life. Emergency activities may include, but not be limited to, the removal of accumulated sediment and debris; repair of eroded or washed out side-slopes, levees, and access roads; and repair of appurtenant flood control structures to protect private and public property and infrastructure, and public safety. Activities may occur as necessary before, during, or following a storm event based on site conditions.
ceqa-020f533c029483e531.crossStreets: Foothill Road and Rabbit Springs Road

ceqa-b62ce175811d780754.projectTitle: Adelanto Gateway Logistics Center - Location Development Plan (LDP) No. 25-02
ceqa-b62ce175811d780754.description: The Project would develop seven industrial warehouse and distribution buildings totaling approximately 8.26 million square feet on approximately 451 acres, under Land Development Permit (LDP) 25-02 and Tentative Parcel Map No. 20837. Buildings would range from approximately 151,000 to 1.5 million square feet and include warehouse and ancillary office space. Up to 20 percent of total floor area may be used for cold storage. Site improvements include landscaping, parking, stormwater retention and infiltration, water and sewer infrastructure, roadway and intersection improvements, and dry utilities. Construction is expected from October 2027 through December 2030. The buildings are designed to be all-electric and served by Southern California Edison. If SCE cannot serve a building when it is ready for occupancy, the Applicant may install natural gas generation at up to three buildings (22.5 megawatts combined) until SCE service begins, subject to a Conditional Use Permit and MDAQMD permits. This SEIR updates the 2009 EIR (SCH No. 2008071129) for the site.

ceqa-fe23d629b0a4ccf741.name: Bloomington Business Park Specific Plan Project
ceqa-fe23d629b0a4ccf741.description: The Specific Plan Area is 213 acres and is divided into two planning areas: Planning Area A and Planning Area B. Planning Area A is approximately 141.4 acres. Planning Area B includes approximately 71.6 acres and a proposed buildout year of 2040. The Specific Plan allows development within Planning Area A to have a floor area ratio (FAR) of 0.5 and a FAR of 0.05 within Planning Area B. The maximum development potential is 3,235,836 square feet (SF). Adoption of the proposed Specific Plan requires a Policy Plan Amendment and Zoning Map Amendment. The land use designation of the Specific Plan Area would change from Very Low Density Residential (VLDR) and Low Density Residential (LDR) to Special Development (SD) and the zoning would change from Single Residential with 1-Acre Minimum Lot and Additional Agriculture Overlay (RS-1-AA) and Single Residential with 20,000 SF lot minimums (RS-20M) to Specific Plan (SP). The proposed Project includes three separate components and associated permits and approvals (“entitlements”), as well as a Community Benefits Agreement: 1) Bloomington Business Park Specific Plan (“Specific Plan”), which is a land-use guiding document for the development of industrial and business park uses and the necessary on- and off-site infrastructure to serve these uses. 2) Opening Year Development within the Specific Plan’s Planning Area A (“Opening Year Development of Planning Area A”), including associated Vesting Tentative Parcel Maps and Conditional Use Permits; and 3) Rezoning a residential site (“Upzone Site”) to a higher density in compliance with the Housing Crisis Act of 2019 (Senate Bill 330) to offset the redesignation of the Specific Plan Area from residential to a non-residential use.
ceqa-fe23d629b0a4ccf741.crossStreets: Santa Ana Ave, Maple Ave, Jurupa Ave, Alder Ave

ceqa-842a5de5a10136bf60.name: Lighting Resources, LLC., Approval of Closure Plan Modification
ceqa-842a5de5a10136bf60.projectTitle: Lighting Resources, LLC., Approval of Closure Plan Modification
ceqa-842a5de5a10136bf60.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-842a5de5a10136bf60.description: The Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) approves the Closure Plan Modification for modifications to the Standardized Hazardous Waste Facility Permit Closure Plan. Lighting Resources elected to no longer operate as a destination facility for spent fluorescent linear lamps. The modification of the Closure Plan is to effectively close the Facility’s Standardized Permit and allow Lighting Resources to continue operating as a large quantity handler for Universal Waste (i.e., spent lamps, non-PCB containing lighting ballasts, batteries, air bags, mercury devices, non-empty aerosol cans, photo voltaic (solar panels) and electronic waste). Hazardous waste will continue to be transferred on hazardous waste manifest within the 10-day regulations based on the Lighting Resources CA Hazardous Waste Transporter Permit #3379. Background: DTSC issued the first Series A Standardized Hazardous Waste Facility Permit to the Facility in 1996 and renewed the authorization by issuing a renewal permit in 2007. The permit was renewed again in 2022. The permitted storage and treatment activities involve the management of offsite generated hazardous waste [spent fluorescent lamps, High Intensity Discharge (HID) lamps, other spent mercury-containing lamps, mercury-containing instruments (e.g. manometers), and intact Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCB)-containing lighting ballasts]. Project Activities: The following Units will be closed: Unit ID #1: Universal Waste Lamp Storage Area #1, Unit ID #2:Universal Waste Storage Area #2, Unit ID #3: Hazardous Waste Storage Area #1, Unit ID #4: Hazardous Waste Storage Area #2, Unit ID #5: Treatment Area #1 (Lamp Machine), Unit ID #6: Treatment Area #2 (HID Glove Box), Unit ID #7: Storage Unit, Unit ID #8: Hazardous Waste Storage Area, Unit ID #9: Balcan Lamp Machine. In accordance with the Standardized Permit, the Closure Plan addresses the closure of current Waste Storage and Management Units. Additionally, Units #7 through #9 are previously approved proposed units that have not been built and will be administratively closed.

Emergency activities may include, but not be limited to, the removal of accumulated sediment and debris; repair of eroded or washed out side slopes, levees, and access roads; and repair of appurtenant flood control structures to protect private and public infrastructure, private property, and public safety.

ceqa-cb75b96acc26017710.name: CLAWA Lake Silverwood Water Treatment Plant Conduit Installation and Pavement Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-cb75b96acc26017710.projectTitle: CLAWA Lake Silverwood Water Treatment Plant Conduit Installation and Pavement Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-cb75b96acc26017710.description: The Project involves rehabilitating (i.e., removing and replacing) approximately 200,000 square-feet (sf) of existing asphalt-paved access roadways, parking areas, and paved areas surrounding tanks and equipment at CLAWA’s active Silverwood Lake WTP. The existing pavement is in poor condition and exhibits alligator cracking, oxidation, deteriorated asphalt binder, and previous utility-trench repairs. Depending on pavement and subgrade conditions, the work may include grinding and asphalt overlay, full-depth pavement reconstruction, localized pavement repairs, utility-trench pavement repairs, and subgrade stabilization. Pavement elevations would remain close to existing conditions. Construction staging will stay within the limits of the WTP on pavement. Construction will be completed in phases to maintain access for facility operations, maintenance and emergency vehicles, deliveries, and equipment servicing. The Project also includes installing two 4-inch-diameter PVC conduits extending approximately 315 linear feet to provide a sleeve for chemical injection tubing between two existing subsurface vaults. The alignment of the conduits is located where there is existing asphalt pavement slated for rehabilitation. Open trenching will be used for installation. Construction staging will stay on pavement within the limits of the WTP. Both elements of the Project would not change the existing capacity of the treatment facility. Beneficiaries of the Project will be the WTP staff and CLAWA employees.

ceqa-7b2077234b9e91e53c.name: Santa Ana River Woollystar and Slender-Horned Spineflower Management in the Woolly Star Preserve Area (Project)
ceqa-7b2077234b9e91e53c.projectTitle: Santa Ana River Woollystar and Slender-Horned Spineflower Management in the Woolly Star Preserve Area (Project)
ceqa-7b2077234b9e91e53c.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Habitat Conservation Planning
ceqa-7b2077234b9e91e53c.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife (Headquarters), Habitat Conservation Planning Branch - Sacramento
ceqa-7b2077234b9e91e53c.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a California Endangered Species Act scientific, educational, or management permit pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 2081, subdivision (a) to San Bernardino County Flood Control District (Permit No. 2081(a)-26-006-RP) for a project to collect Santa Ana River Woollystar (SARWS) and Slender-Horned Spineflower (SHSF) seed, conduct seed viability and seedbank germination trials, and implement weed management within the WSPA. Together these actions will satisfy objectives of the Multi Species Habitat Management Plan for the WSPA, inform species distribution and viability assessments, and support the development of a seed repository for future management needs. A portion of the collected seed will be used to conduct germination trials to test seed viability. Remaining seed will be placed into long-term conservation storage to be used for future management needs that may include seed bulking, population enhancement, and restoration activities in the WSPA. Soil samples from the top 2-centimeters of soil will be collected from each of the 13 SHSF patches that were historically occupied but are presently unoccupied. Germination trials to determine whether a dormant viable seed bank remains will be conducted at CalBG. Approximately 1-quart of soil will also be collected from each patch for soil analysis of texture, nutrient levels, organic matter, pH, salinity, electrical conductivity, and cation exchange capacity. Weed management will be restricted to areas approved by the WSPA steering committee. A combination of herbicide application and physical control will be implemented based on the phenology of the target species. All physically controlled plant material will be removed from the treatment areas. During site monitoring visits, qualified biologists will remove non-native vegetation by hand in and around the two SHSF occupied patches. A 2-meter protection buffer will be delineated around each SHSF patch and non-native grasses will be treated from the buffer extending to 10 meters.

ceqa-cfe48ac9adb46a7c79.name: Barstow Sanitary Landfill Phase 1C Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-039-06 (ITP))
ceqa-cfe48ac9adb46a7c79.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP (No. 2081-2025-0139-06), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to San Bernardino County Public Works Department. The Project involves the expansion of the Barstow Sanitary Landfill and will develop 127-acres of undisturbed open space for the construction of Phase 1C of the Barstow Sanitary Landfill. Project activities will include vegetation removal and grading of the entire Project Area, excavation of the expansion area, construction of access roads, water lines, erosion control, and the construction of a containment system and exclusionary fencing. The Project will result in impacts to 127 acres of Agassiz’s desert tortoise (Gopherus agassizii) and western burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia hypugaea) habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of Agassiz’s desert tortoise (Gopherus agassizii), which is designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA) and incidental take of western burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia hypugaea), which is designated as a candidate species for potential listing under CESA. The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-e27cf8508eaeebd8f4.name: Public Works Corporate Yard
ceqa-e27cf8508eaeebd8f4.description: The Project consists of a General Plan Amendment and Zone Change to accommodate the construction and operation of a new Public Works Corporate Yard at 2200 East Philadelphia Street. This new corporate yard would replace the existing facility located at South Bon View Avenue. The Project consists of 10 buildings and 13 non-building structures, and would consolidate City administrative services, public works, information technology, and Ontario Municipal Utilities Company operations on a single municipal campus. The Project would include administrative offices, a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition facility with the ability to serve as an alternate emergency operations center, warehouse and storage facilities (including storage for the City's Community Life and Culture division), fleet maintenance and industrial water operations facilities, hazardous waste handling facilities, vehicle wash facilities, a municipal waste transfer station, and a multi-level parking structure. Site improvements would also include vehicle and equipment storage, parking, fueling stations, and electrical infrastructure. Circulation improvements, utility infrastructure, landscaping, and backup power generation would also be built. The Project would require a General Plan Amendment and Zone Change to change the existing land use designation and zoning district from Open Space – Parkland (OS-R) and Open Space – Recreation (OS-R) to Public Facility and Civic (CIV), respectively. Additionally, to achieve the goals and objectives of the City of Ontario Community Climate Action Plan, greenhouse gas emissions reduction features would be incorporated into the Project, including alternative fueling, water recycling and conservation practices, waste diversion, solar energy generation, and active transportation features. On- and off-site improvements would include roadway, utility, drainage, bridge construction, telecommunications, and traffic signal improvements.

ceqa-c58c4cdf8c6424ec6d.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife (Headquarters), Habitat Conservation Planning Branch - Sacramento
ceqa-c58c4cdf8c6424ec6d.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a western Joshua tree hazard management permit to Guadalupe Flores Garcia (Permit No. 1927-HMP-2026-279) pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1927.4 for a project to remove two dead and detached western Joshua trees and four dead and detached western Joshua tree crowns, and to trim and remove four dead and attached western Joshua tree trunks. Western Joshua tree hazard management permits are issued to property owners for the purpose of removing or trimming a dead western Joshua tree or trimming a living western Joshua tree, provided that the dead western Joshua tree or any limb to be removed meet one of the following conditions: (A) has fallen over and is within 30 feet of a structure; (B) is leaning against an existing structure; or (C) creates an imminent threat to public health or safety.

ceqa-34390623c9df6fc462.name: Ossum Wash Repair Project
ceqa-34390623c9df6fc462.description: Victor Valley Wastewater Reclamation Authority (VVWRA) owns two existing gravity trunk sewer pipelines (36-in Reinforced Concrete Pipe [RCP] and 42-in Vitrified Clay Pipe [VCP]) that cross Ossum Wash. These large diameter sewer pipelines transport around 1-MG of the City of Victorville’s daily sewage. After recent heavy rain events, the existing grade above these pipelines has eroded substantially. VVWRA is concerned that future rain events might expose the two pipelines, making them susceptible to a pipe break and sewage spill from bedload or debris travelling down the wash during a rain event. The two existing pipelines are estimated to have approximately 4 feet of cover remaining above them. VVWRA is proposing to construct emergency improvements to the wash to mitigate the risk of pipe exposure and damage. To address the critical erosion issues within the wash described above, VVWRA hired Dudek to design emergency improvements to protect the sewer lines. The proposed improvements include the following: • Installing grouted riprap on the channel side slope along the easterly side of the existing grouted riprap channel. • Installing an extension of the grouted riprap channel from the downstream end of the existing grouted riprap to the northerly extent of the VVWRA pipeline easement. • Installing loose riprap lined channel downstream of the proposed grouted riprap.

The trimming and removal of the living western Joshua tree specifically authorized under this Permit shall not disturb the root ball. Western Joshua tree hazard management permits are issued to property owners for the purpose of removing or trimming a dead western Joshua tree or trimming a living western Joshua tree, provided that the dead western Joshua tree or any limb to be removed meet one of the following conditions: (A) has fallen over and is within 30 feet of a structure; (B) is leaning against an existing structure; or (C) creates an imminent threat to public health or safety.

Of this total, 1,050,222 ± square feet would consist of warehouse distribution space and 26,652± square feet would consist of office space. Office areas would be located at the four corners of the building. The building is proposed for general warehousing and will not include cold storage facilities. ceqa-52fcefb2a13a14a0c6.agency: State Water Resources Control Board, Division of Drinking Water
ceqa-52fcefb2a13a14a0c6.description: The Project consists of water treatment system improvements to Well 34 and Well 19. The project includes excavation, addition of ~10,586 square feet of concrete pads, the installation of four GAC vessels to treat for 1,2,3-TCP followed by two IX structures to treat for nitrate, 6 aboveground storage tanks (2 brine tanks and 4 waste tanks), the reconfiguration of the well discharge piping, additional site lighting, and the backfilling of soil to restore the ground level at the existing Well 34 site. Each of the two parallel trains would treat 1,000 gallons per minute (gpm). Concrete pad space was included to allow a third train of GAC and IX to be installed to treat Well 19. This would result in the concentrations of 1,2,3-TCP and nitrate at levels within the respective MCL. Approximately 0.87 acres of the 1.38-acre Project Site would be disturbed over the course of construction. There will be no expansion of permitted use to produce water from Well 34 and Well 19.
