ceqa-cffc562aac6a746acf.name: Swarthout Canyon Road Emergency CMP Replacement
ceqa-cffc562aac6a746acf.projectTitle: Swarthout Canyon Road Emergency CMP Replacement
ceqa-cffc562aac6a746acf.description: The atmospheric river that occurred between December 23-26, 2025, and the heavy rainfall that occurred between December 31-January 5, 2026, resulted in significant flooding on Swarthout Canyon Road resulting in a clear and imminent threat to public infrastructure and residents. Project includes, but is not limited to, removing approximately 50 feet of cement along the roadway that is covering a clogged 4 foot squash corrugated metal pipe, which typically conveys flows from Cajon Creek upstream of Swarthout Canyon Road to downstream of the road but is clogged with debris from the high-flow rain events, replacing it with a new corrugated metal pipe, and pouring new cement to repair what was removed.

ceqa-7ccc346b460ce535d8.description: The proposed project would involve the development of the 8.52-acre site with a new multiple-family residential development that would consist of 99-townhouse units with recreational amenities including a club house, pool area, game courts, and walkways. The proposed 99 unit townhome complex would include 20, 3 story buildings consisting of the following: 5 six-plex buildings with 6 units each, 13 five-plex buildings with 5 units each, 1 four-plex building with 4 units each, and 1 recreational building. Each of the 99 townhouse units would include an enclosed two or three-car garage. The 20 buildings would have a total floor area of 248,414 square feet. Each unit would have 1,138 square feet of common open space and between 175 to 354 square feet of private open space. The total site area is 8.52 acres or 371,131 square feet. Vehicular access to the project site would be provided by a new gated driveway connection with the north side of Silica Drive and a gated secondary connection with the west side of First Avenue. A total of 254 vehicle parking spaces and 38 bicycle parking stalls would be provided. Landscaping would total 112,714 square feet.

ceqa-b3fc475f8ae57f3177.name: Yard 11 - Flood Impacted Roadways Emergency Repairs
ceqa-b3fc475f8ae57f3177.projectTitle: Yard 11 - Flood Impacted Roadways Emergency Repairs
ceqa-b3fc475f8ae57f3177.description: Heavy rainfall can result in significant increased runoff and sediment/debris flows which have historically eroded, washed out, and inundated roadways, public infrastructure, residences, other real property, and entire communities within the Mojave Desert and Southern California mountain communities, posing an imminent threat to life and property. Project includes but is not limited to structural/appurtenant structure repairs, and excavation/removal of accumulated sediment, debris, and rocks from impacted roadways and adjacent tributaries in, including but limited to, the unincorporated communities of Wrightwood, Phelan, Oak Hills, and Pinion Hills, and the City of Hesperia. Any excess material may be used to repair road washouts and erosions, divert flows away from the road and into the ordinary flow path, and/ or may be disposed of off-site.
ceqa-b3fc475f8ae57f3177.crossStreets: Phelan Road, Summit Valley Road, Lone Pine Canyon Road, Oasis Road, Bear Valley Road, Etc.

ceqa-d48f50c2b65efe8b1d.description: The San Bernardino County Department of Public Works (DPW) is proposing a sewer expansion project consisting of the installation of a new sewer main and new sewer manholes allowing for present and future land development improvements to connect and convert from septic to sewer. Equipment planned for use on this project will include but is not limited to excavator, paving machine, and asphalt roller. No traffic detours, nighttime construction, or utility relocation are planned at this time. Construction duration is anticipated for approximately five (5) months. San Bernardino County Development Code 83.01.80(g)(3): exempts noise from temporary construction, maintenance, repair, or demolition activities between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., except Sundays and Federal holidays.

ceqa-96e10c35a3a3503d71.description: The project proposes to apply Polymer Modified Asphaltic Emulsion (PMAE) chip seal coat with flush coat on the entire width of the asphalt concrete (AC) pavement on Route 62 from PM 94.0 to PM 106.0 in San Bernardino County. In addition, the project will include 0.4' of AC replacement on defective areas along Route 62. All the work will be done within the existing pavement and Caltrans Right of Way only. There will be Driving/Parking off pavement. No ground disturbance will occur and connections to new infrastructure are not anticipated. There will also be no need for equipment staging areas. Utility relocations are to be determined. This project is funded by State-only funding.

ceqa-a11caaae3ae029e0e1.description: Project consists of minor alternations to the 6th floor training room, including replacement of existing demising wall between the training and conference room, new corridor doors, and new audio/visual credenza.

ceqa-ec0046eb816f043a20.name: SBD 395 – Perform Preventative Maintenance with Pavement Seal
ceqa-ec0046eb816f043a20.projectTitle: SBD 395 – Perform Preventative Maintenance with Pavement Seal
ceqa-ec0046eb816f043a20.description: The project purpose is to preserve the existing pavement, prevent future deterioration, prolong the service life, and delay the need for rehabilitation by applying a rubberized chip seal coat with flush coat over the entire width of the asphalt concrete pavement on Route 395 from Post Mile (PM) 44.0 to PM 73.5 in San Bernardino County. In addition, the project would include asphalt concrete replacement in defective areas along Route 395. The project would also include construction area signage, bike lane signage, crosswalk striping, pavement delineation, and replacement of two (2) existing loop detectors at the traffic monitoring stations at PM 45.587 and PM 47.294.

ceqa-b794dd5574546bc3aa.name: Cemex Project Phase 1 (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-037-06 (ITP))
ceqa-b794dd5574546bc3aa.projectTitle: Upper Santa Ana River Wash Land Management and Habitat Conservation Plan
ceqa-b794dd5574546bc3aa.agency: San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District
ceqa-b794dd5574546bc3aa.agencyName: San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District
ceqa-b794dd5574546bc3aa.description: This proposed project involves extraction, processing, separation, stockpiling and selling of sand, gravel, rocks, and other construction aggregate materials in a new 51.8-acre footprint as well as an existing 121-acre mining area. The Project will result in impacts to 51.8 acres of San Bernardino kangaroo rat (Dipodomys merriami parvus), Slender-horned spineflower (Dodecahema leptoceras), and Santa Ana River woollystar (Eriastrum densifolium ssp. sanctorum) habitat with no temporary impacts; the Project will permanently remove 51.8 acres of San Bernardino kangaroo rat, Slender-horned spineflower, and Santa Ana River woollystar habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of San Bernardino kangaroo rat, Slenderhorned spineflower, and Santa Ana River woollystar, which are designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act. The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-cf88d03c9cf35e4855.name: Soda Mountain Solar Project
ceqa-cf88d03c9cf35e4855.description: Soda Mountain Solar, LLC (applicant), proposes to construct, operate, and maintain a utility-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) electrical generating and storage facility and associated infrastructure (operations and maintenance buildings, stormwater infrastructure, and related infrastructure improvements) to generate and deliver renewable electricity to the statewide electricity transmission grid. The project would generate up to 300 megawatts (MW) of renewable energy and include up to 300 MW/1,200 MW-hours (MWh) of battery storage. The batteries would be lithium ion or similar. The project would include a switchyard and substation. The power produced by the project would be conveyed to the regional electrical grid through an interconnection with the existing Mead-Adelanto 500-kilovolt (kV) transmission line operated by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP). The approximately 200 foot wide, 1-mile long 500 kV gen-tie line would run from the project substation, just southeast of I-15, to the switchyard and then to the point of interconnection with the existing LADWP Mead-Adelanto transmission line. A small segment of the gen-tie line, approximately 450 feet, would cross I-15.

ceqa-b90654152e14ce9a4a.projectTitle: Kelso-Cima and South Kelbaker Road Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-b90654152e14ce9a4a.description: Road improvements include restriping pavement, adding mumble strips, widening shoulders, paving with asphalt concrete, realigning road segments at three locations, and adding exclusion fencing for desert tortoises. ceqa-95f34f6cf0ebc8cec1.name: Taxilane G Reconstruction
ceqa-95f34f6cf0ebc8cec1.description: The Proposed Project would involve the full-depth reconstruction of Taxilane G and the pavement area west of Gate 36, along with pavement rehabilitation near the intersection with Taxiway N. Activities would include demolition and removal of degraded pavement, installation of new asphalt concrete layers suitable for aircraft movement, and replacement of pavement markings. All construction would occur within previously disturbed areas of the existing taxilane alignment. Environmental and safety best management practices would be implemented to minimize impacts to airport operations and ensure compliance with applicable regulations.

ceqa-bfb320d35023d13f6a.name: CenterPark Specific Plan
ceqa-bfb320d35023d13f6a.description: The Project consists of a Specific Plan to allow for a residential and mixed-used retail/office development on 29 parcels covering approximately 257.34 acres in the City. The development would include up to 250,919 square feet of commercial retail/office uses, up to 4,293 residential units across medium density and mixed-use residential uses, 67.26 acres of open space parkland/non-recreation uses, and associated on-site and off-site infrastructure improvements. The Project site is comprised of two "Ownership Areas" (representing different ownership conditions) with 22 planning areas. The "Ownership Area 1” is owned by the applicant of the CenterPark Specific Plan. The “Ownership Area 2” is comprised of parcels owned by others and are included as part of the Specific Plan. Ownership Area 1 of the Project includes Planning Areas 5 and 7 through 18, which would allow for the development of up to up to 3,095 residential dwelling units, 210,544 square feet of mixed-use retail and office uses, and 55.98 acres of parkland use. Ownership Area 2 of the Project includes Planning Areas 1 through 4, 6, and 19 through 22, which would allow for the development of up to 1,198 residential dwelling units, 40,376 square feet of mixed-use retail and office uses, and 11.28 acres of parkland use.

ceqa-68e29d1ad85d0f70db.name: Protected Left-Turn Signal at SR-18 and Knickerbocker Rd.
ceqa-68e29d1ad85d0f70db.projectTitle: Protected Left-Turn Signal at SR-18 and Knickerbocker Rd.
ceqa-68e29d1ad85d0f70db.description: Caltrans proposes to modify the existing traffic signals at the intersection of State Route 18 (SR-18) and Knickerbocker Road in the City of Big Bear, in San Bernardino County at Postmile (PM) 49.2. The project would provide a dedicated and protected left turn phase along the eastbound and westbound directions of SR-18 by replacing existing signal poles and foundations. Most of the existing conduits and pull boxes would be utilized to reduce the amount of trenching. All new poles would be placed at the same locations. "No U-turn" signs would be installed on the signal mast arms. A Transportation Management Plan (TMP) would be developed to minimize traffic impacts during construction. All work would be done within the State right of way.

ceqa-a97a5b9a5cca4b6e00.name: 6th Cycle Housing Element Program 33 Upzone
ceqa-a97a5b9a5cca4b6e00.description: In accordance with the City’s certified 6th Cycle Housing Element Program 33 (Strategically Enhance Access to Areas of Opportunity), the City is proposing to upzone approximately five (5) acres of moderate to high resource areas on the easterly portion of the City of Highland to a maximum residential density of thirty (30) dwelling units per acre (du/ac) (with a density range of 20 du/ac to 30 du/ac). As stated in the City’s 6th Cycle Housing Element, “while the City has identified an adequate supply of land to fully accommodate the City’s 6th Cycle Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA), the City will provide an additional buffer of sites to mitigate land use patterns of access to resources and opportunities, and patterns of segregation and integration.” The Project site encompasses approximately 89 acres on the easterly portion of the City of Highland and is currently designated as Agricultural Equestrian AG/EQ under the current General Plan Land Use. The proposed GPA 025-001/ZC 025-001 would redesignate the site to Planned Development (PD) with a range of densities including approximately 5 acres of the site upzoned with high density of 20-30 du/ac, approximately 61 acres of the site with 6-12 du/ac and remaining 23 acres of the project site as open space (assumed to not be developable as it is the steep-sloped foothills of the San Bernardino Mountains). This would result in an overall 2.66% increase in density compared to what was analyzed in the General Plan Environmental Impacts Report (EIR). The current General Plan Land Use Designation and Zoning District for the subject location is AG/EQ (with a maximum density of 2 du/ac). On April 1, 2025, the City of Highland Planning Commission conducted a public workshop to receive public comments on a preferred location to upzone in accordance with the City’s Housing Element Program 33, and the subject location was determined to be the preferred option. The existing General Plan Land Use designation and Zoning Classification will be changed to PD with a footnote stipulating that at least five (5) acres of the area be incorporated into a future master plan for housing at a density range of 20 du/ac to 30 du/ac. The proposed designation of PD will provide for superior development by allowing a greater degree of design and land use flexibility within the framework of a site-specific development plan (Highland Municipal Code (HMC) Section 16.12.010 (A)(1)). The PD designation will allow for the clustering of units and building types, and the formula of specific development standards and design criteria which respond to the particular features or conditions effecting a site (HMC Section 16.12.010(A)(2)). The proposed PD designation also encourages the merging of areas or parcels in a single overall land use plan and site design which might otherwise be developed separately (HMC Section 16.12.010(A)(3)(c)).

ceqa-cb5c6ac05b429a23cb.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed and issued Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBR-42438-R6, pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, to the project Applicant, The Metropolitan Water District of Southern California. The Project proposes to rehabilitate the slide gate valve and replace the discharge valve within the Copper Basin Dam valve house; install new conduit and electrical components within the valve house; install three new concrete pads and electrical components 250 feet southwest of the Copper Basin Dam; install and anchor-in-place approximately 250 feet of above-ground electrical conduit from the new concrete pads to Copper Basin Dam; replace the ladder on the dam face; install a new catwalk and stairs immediately downstream of and adjacent to the valve house; remove and reconstruct two existing concrete weirs approximately 125 feet downstream of Copper Basin Dam; and install electrical conduit and instrumentation from the two weirs along the catwalk to the valve house. The proposed project would disturb a total of approximately 20.7 acres and would include approximately 0.23 acres of the Granite Hills HS campus. The proposed project would install a new track and field with artificial turf, four stadium lights, two football field goal posts, a scoreboard, permanent bleachers to the west and east of the track and field, a concessions building, a teams building, a trash enclosure, a PA system, four parking lots, a flood control basin, walkways, ornamental landscaping, and fencing with gates. Project construction would occur in two phases. The first phase of the proposed project would have a tentative start date of spring 2026 and would conclude in spring 2027. Phase two would start in the fall of 2027 and would conclude in the spring of 2028.

ceqa-8501065792ab0beb3c.name: East Ames-Reche Recharge Facility Project
ceqa-8501065792ab0beb3c.description: The Project consists of the development of two (2) new recharge basins (north and south) on 10 acres surrounded by 12-ft tall berms. Improvements include: an access road surrounding the perimeter of each basin; 6-foot perimeter fencing with barbed wire; a new tee connection within the Winters Road right-of-way; approximately 500 linear feet of 12-inch nonpotable water pipeline from Winters Road to the eastern perimeter of each basin; two (2) headwalls located along the eastern perimeter of each basin connecting to the new nonpotable water pipeline; outlet with energy dissipator; and a nested or multi-completion monitoring well located within the proposed site to monitor infiltration rates, groundwater levels, and water quality. The proposed improvements will allow MWA to increase its groundwater recharge capacity of annual State Water Project Table A allocations. The development of the recharge basins will result in a maximum flow rate of 5 cubic feet per second (cfs) with an anticipated annual recharge capacity of 1,500 AFY.

ceqa-5a397487d3cf1ee422.name: Interstate 40 Minor Pavement Rehabilitation Project
ceqa-5a397487d3cf1ee422.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes to install 0.15-ft thick Rubberized Hot Mix Asphalt (RHMA-G) overlay on the I-40 mainline and shoulders; construct 0.4-ft thick localized digouts (10% of total Asphalt Concrete[AC]); replace AC dikes; upgrade existing metal beam guardrail to Midwest Guardrail System (MGS); replace rock slope protection under two bridges at Gas Line Wash due to inadequate rock type and size; replace traffic sign panels with type XI retro-reflective sheeting to meet federal requirements, and replace four culverts in poor or fair condition under Drainage Restoration program in order to protect the embankment and roadway from potential failure. The pavement grinding would include the removal of thermoplastic traffic stripes. Lane closure would be required to minimize traffic impact during construction and to ensure the safety of the traveling public and construction workers. Construction is expected in the night time and 8 hours a night. The new MGS at the bridge locations will be connected to a new concrete barrier transition at the beginning and the end of each bridge railing. The concrete barrier transition will be attached through drilling and bonding into the existing bridge railing. Asbestos testing may be required for the existing bridge railing. No other bridge work is planned. Below is the list of all bridges that require concrete barrier transition: Gas Line Wash-Bridge No. 54-0715 R/L, Twin Hills Wash-Bridge No. 54-0716 R/L, Crest Wash-Bridge No. 54-0717 R/L, W Newberry Road Undercrossing-Bridge No. 54-0708 R/L, Newberry Road Overcrossing-Bridge No. 54-0709, Fort Cady Overcrossing-Bridge No 54-0710. All work is expected to be performed within the existing Caltrans right of way.

ceqa-ca19e30b8dbadf6633.name: Mountain Rim Fire Safe Council Regional Fire Safe Project – Wrightwood, Mt. Baldy, and Lytle Creek
ceqa-ca19e30b8dbadf6633.projectTitle: Mountain Rim Fire Safe Council Regional Fire Safe Project – Wrightwood, Mt. Baldy, and Lytle Creek
ceqa-ca19e30b8dbadf6633.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-ca19e30b8dbadf6633.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-ca19e30b8dbadf6633.description: The intent of this project is to assist residents of the Wrightwood, Lytle Creek, and Mt. Baldy communities in creating defensible space and removing fire hazards in compliance with defensible space/hazard abatement regulations. The proposed project would include the removal of vegetation, hazardous trees, debris, and other materials within 100 ft. of structures. Removal of vegetation will occur manually; cut material will be left in place, piled for firewood, chipped and spread back on site, and/or hauled away. Ground vegetation to be removed will primarily consist of shrubs, leaves, pine needles, weeds, and downed branches. Trees may be pruned to allow for the passage of emergency response vehicles and as necessary to maintain defensible space standards (e.g., recommended distance from chimneys/stovepipes or other trees). Dead, dying, diseased, and hazardous live trees will be removed. All trees will be felled in the least ground-disturbing manner feasible. Project implementation is expected to begin immediately. The number of parcels completed within the project area will be determined based on funding availability. Work may be done during nesting bird season if nesting surveys are performed prior to commencement of operations, as described below. Equipment necessary for project implementation includes chainsaws, hand tools (shovels, Mcleods, pulaskis, etc.), and chippers. Heavy equipment (i.e., chipper) and vehicles will use existing improved and/or disturbed areas such as roads, driveways, and pullouts. If tree logs need to be removed from the project site, then the logs will be cut into carry-able size lengths and removed by hand to minimize ground disturbance. Maintenance will occur as necessary to maintain the standards listed above and may occur as frequently as an annual basis. Maintenance needs will be determined in coordination with CAL FIRE.

ceqa-dfa11f2a7a6f9aecdc.description: The San Bernardino County Department of Public Works (DPW) proposes the full-depth reconstruction and widening of approximately 1.25 miles of San Bernardino Avenue, extending from Cherry Avenue east to Fontana Avenue in the City of Fontana. The roadway will be reconstructed to an 80-foot curb separation, with a maximum excavation depth of 1.35 feet for the road surface and approximately 4 feet for drainage structures. Improvements include pulverizing asphalt and cold planing, installing ADA-compliant concrete ramps and driveway approaches, placing asphalt concrete driveways and asphalt dike, and constructing concrete curb, gutter, sidewalks, spandrels, and cross gutters at multiple locations. The project also includes relocation of fencing and block walls, as well as traffic signal relocations at Cherry Avenue, Redwood Avenue, Live Oak Avenue. Hemlock Avenue. and Fontana Avenue. Drainage facilities will be reconstructed east of Cherry Avenue, east of Live Oak Avenue, and west of Fontana Avenue. Additional work consists of constructing three concrete bus stop pads, removing approximately 35 mature trees and stumps, and demolishing three residential structures and one storage building to accommodate easement acquisitions.

The Development Agreement is to address community benefit responsibilities of the applicant.

ceqa-57113f71d50971c59a.name: Arrowbear Boat Storage
ceqa-57113f71d50971c59a.description: The Applicant is requesting approval of a Minor Use Permit to develop approximately 3.93 acres of a 5.88-acre parcel into a Personal Property Storage facility that will provide indoor boat storage. The Project Site is located in Arrowbear Lake, an unincorporated area of San Bernardino County (see Figure 1 – Regional Location). The parcel is described as Assessor’s Parcel No. 0328-165-16 and has a split Countywide Plan zoning of Multiple Residential (RM) (1.95 acres) and General Commercial-Sign Control overlay (CG-SCp) (3.93 acres). The Applicant intends to develop the designated CG-SCp portion of the property; the remainder of the property will remain undeveloped. One of the three existing structures near the entrance and adjacent to Highway 18 (SR-18) is vacant with a second structure being used for storage. An existing shed on the property is also used for storage. Access to the Project Site would continue to be provided by the existing gravel entrance directly off SR-18 that would be graded and paved with concrete. The Applicant also owns an adjacent property (APN 0328-165-07) that is shown on the Site Plan, but will not be developed. This parcel has a Countywide Plan zoning of Single Residential (RS). The Project is proposed as a Personal Property Storage facility that would include the construction of one 10,974-square-foot (SF) building to be used for storage, and the use of a 1,757-SF existing building to be used as an office (see Figure 2 – Site Plan). Two of the three existing buildings would be demolished (see Figure 2 – Site Plan). All new structures would be prefab/modular, constructed off-site, and installed on footings. The scope of the construction work would consist of demolition, site clearing, site preparation, various utility improvements, and installation of the modular structures with on-site parking and open space. The Proposed Project will operate 12 months of the year by appointment only and require a maximum of 3 employees. Proposed hours of business = Summer-10am-2pm (by appointment only); Winter (Nov-April) by appointment only. Anticipated truck trips to deliver and/or pick-up is two per year for 80%. Client would like to move 252 boats and trailer in and out each way every season. The Proposed Project would include a total of 7 parking spaces (including one handicap accessible space) for the Project Site. Parking will be placed along a concrete sidewalk. Wastewater would be treated by Arrowbear Park County Water District. Potable water would also be provided by Arrowbear Park County Water District. There is an existing on-site well that will remain for irrigation only. The Proposed Project would rely on Southern California Edison (SCE) electric facilities to meet energy demands.

ceqa-96871c54e0591740a3.description: Caltrans proposes to relocate and replace the existing main electrical switchboard and relocate the existing backup generator within the existing fence, and add three overhead lights for the Caltrans Vidal Junction Maintenance Station. ceqa-858ca42221fce18dcf.description: The proposed project would involve the construction of 12 condominium units within the 1.0-acre site. Of the total number of units, 10 units would consist of two-levels and 2 units would be single-level units. The residential units would be located in two new buildings that would be located on the north and south sides of a new internal drive aisle. Each building would contain 6 units. This drive aisle would provide vehicular access to the north side of Lime Street and the parking spaces and garages within the project site. The two-level units would have a total living area of 1,911 square feet while the one level units would have a total living area of 1,846 square feet. All of the units would have 3-bedrooms. A 2,400 square foot tot-lot and open space area would be located in the site’s south-central portion of the site near the entry. A covered pavilion, consisting of 320 square feet would be located next to the tot lot. Landscaping would be located in the front yard, side yards, and rear yard areas and would total 4,492 square feet or 10.3%. A total of 27 parking spaces would be provided including 24 parking spaces in the enclosed garages and 5 guest parking spaces (including 1 ADA space). Water and connections would be provided by new connections with water connections to lines located in Lime Street and sewer connections would be made by a new sewer main from C Avenue.

ceqa-92afb2d382457c8575.description: The applicant proposes the development of 1,765,000+/- square feet (SF) of industrial warehouse and distribution space on an 87.72-acre site located on the north side of Yermo Road, approximately 0.5 miles east of the Ghost Town Road/ Daggett Yermo I-15 interchange in San Bernardino County, California. The Project site plan proposes two industrial buildings totaling 1,764,560 SF, 866 car parking stalls, trailer parking stalls, 683,180 SF of landscaping, and five (5) stormwater retention basins totaling 276,839 SF. Building 1 is 1,152,480 SF and Building 2 is 612,080 SF. Both Buildings have a maximum height of 50 feet to top of parapet. Building 1 has a total of 176 truck loading docks and Building 2 has a total of 98 truck loading docks located on the north and south sides of the buildings. The site will be accessed from three (3) driveways along Yermo Road, each providing both ingress and egress. Buildings and on-site parking will be accessed via internal drive aisles.

ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.name: Camp De Benneville Pines Fuel Reduction Project
ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.projectTitle: Camp De Benneville Pines Fuel Reduction Project
ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.description: The project is located at Camp Benneville de Pines (Camp) in the San Bernardino National Forest (BDF). The project site includes 13 structures and a 100-foot radius surrounding these camp facilities totaling approximately 12.76. acres, and a 0.33-acre equipment and materials staging area, for a combined total of 13.09 acres. The project proposes to assist the Camp in compliance with local and state defensible space/hazard abatement regulations, as required by their lease with the BDF. Project activities will include the removal of vegetation within 100 ft. of structures for the purposes of maintaining defensible space, and the removal of dead, dying, or diseased trees. Removal of vegetation will occur manually; cut material will be left in place, piled for firewood, chipped and distributed back on site, and/or hauled away. Spread chip material will not exceed 2 inches in depth; additional chip material will be staged in piles in existing disturbed areas for future use. Dead, dying, and diseased trees <11” DBH may be removed for defensible space purposes; retained trees will be limbed to the extent feasible to meet defensible space standards (i.e., required clearance from chimneys and other trees) and to allow for the passage of emergency vehicles. The project also includes the removal of large (>12” DBH) dead, dying, or diseased trees, identified in coordination with the BDF. All trees will be felled in the least ground-disturbing manner feasible. Project implementation requires both small (chainsaws, hand tools, etc.) and large (chippers, lift or crane for the removal of the large trees, etc.) equipment. Heavy equipment (i.e., chipper, lift) and vehicles will use existing improved and/or disturbed areas such as roads, driveways, and pullouts. Cut material will be removed to these areas by hand to further minimize ground disturbance. Maintenance will occur as necessary to maintain the standards listed above and may occur as frequently as an annual basis. Maintenance needs will be determined in coordination with CAL FIRE.
ceqa-1d75a4ab589c760ca4.crossStreets: Highway 38 and Jenk Lake Road West

ceqa-f56758e12bf4ec2e1a.description: The Project site is comprised of two (2) parcels, Accessor Parcel Numbers (APNs) 05917104 and 05916208. The Project site is within the incorporated Town of Yucca Valley General Plan with the development code of Mixed Use and is currently designated with the zoning of Mixed-Use Commercial (C-MU). The County of San Bernardino Facilities and Project Management Department proposes to develop the new Fire Station #41 at 7238 Joshua Lane by constructing a new 13,230 square-foot station and new associated facilities (Project). The new fire station will house 5 personnel, 1 engine, and 1 paramedic truck. The total footprint of the building is 12,993 square feet. The new fire station will be part of the District’s Division 4, which will serve the unincorporated area adjacent to the Town of Yucca Valley, and the contract cities of Joshua Tree and 29 Palms. Improvements to the site would include new security fencing, a hose house, hose rack, generator, fuel tank, trash enclosure, new access road, landscaping, and hardscaping. Parking will consist of seventeen (17) parking spaces. Ingress and egress to the Project site will be via Twentynine Palms Outer Highway and Joshua Lane through two driveways: the southern driveway will be the primary entrance and exit for the emergency vehicles, while the northern driveway will serve as the public entrance and exit.

ceqa-f7afaadcef9e07e76c.name: Damage repair resulted from an Atmospheric River Strom.(EA 1R640)
ceqa-f7afaadcef9e07e76c.projectTitle: Damage repair resulted from an Atmospheric River Strom.(EA 1R640)
ceqa-f7afaadcef9e07e76c.description: This Director’s Order request proposes emergency repairs resulting from an Atmospheric River storm that brought heavy precipitation, causing flooding and debris flows within the Line Fire burn scar along sections of State Route 330 (SR-330). Drainage basins were filled up with large amounts of sediment, which overwhelmed drainage systems, over topped basins, and covered the roadway with debris. The debris flows that over topped the roadway damaged debris barriers, guardrails, cable railings, roadway signs, and also eroded and undermined parts of the roadway embankments, making the roadway unsafe for travel. Currently, SR-330 is closed to the public in both directions between Highland Avenue (PM R29.6) to Live Oak Drive (PM 41.8).
ceqa-f7afaadcef9e07e76c.crossStreets: PM 29.6 to 43.9 near the town of Running Springs within San Bernardino County. SR-330

ceqa-3ac76f3c732cb2de46.description: The Project involves constructing an 83,369-square-foot, two-story addition to the Desert Valley Hospital (hospital). The first floor will connect to the hospital via a widened corridor, and the second floor will connect via a new bridge. The existing ground-level helipad will be removed and replaced with a rooftop helipad on the new structure. A service yard on the northeastern portion of the Project site will include a pump house, cooling tower, chiller room, and electrical rooms. Adjacent to the service yard, a bulk oxygen storage yard will be built, along with two underground emergency water storage tanks. Project activities include grading of the entire Project location, building construction, trench digging, pile driving, road and parking lot construction, and landscaping. The Project will result in incidental take of 3 western Joshua tree (Yucca brevifolia), which is protected under the WJTCA and the California Endangered Species Act. The WJTCA ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of western Joshua tree that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-b1dfc0eb76fbe01fe3.name: Weed Management and Eradication Project
ceqa-b1dfc0eb76fbe01fe3.description: The MDRCD has received a three year grant to carry out weed management and eradication within its service area boundaries. Participating agencies include the Bureau of Land Management; National Park Service; Department of Defense; County Department of Agriculture; U. S. Forest Service; University of California Riverside Extension; Amargosa Conservancy; Mojave Desert Land Trust; and California Department of Fish and Wildlife. The MDRCD administers the grant and the listed parties will carry out their specific approved weed eradication and treatment projects. The protection and rehabilitation work will be performed during the best season to conduct eradication and management of sits hosting the weeds. Bird nesting season will be avoided in riparian areas and other sensitive bird nesting areas. The goal is to eradicate the most noxious weed populations with the limited funding available. The eradication and management activities will consist of mechanical and hand work that will remove or eliminate the weeds in a given area. Additionally, it will include the use of herbicides. Potential herbicides to be used include: glyphosate, clopyralid, indaziflam, aminopyralid, imazapyr, triclopyr, isoxaben, dithiopyr, glufosinate, and/or fluazifop.

ceqa-d4d08fe1c700e1c6f3.description: The Project involves the following legislative actions: (1) Amendment No. 8 to East Valley Corridor Specific Plan Concept Plan No. 1, which would add a new development plan application procedure under Section IV, Part A (Discretionary Actions); and (2) Planned Development No. 6, which would establish a multi-phased development plan for the expansion of the existing onsite medical facility. Each phase of the development will require subsequent development permit from the City of Redlands Planning Commission, pursuant to East Valley Corridor Specific Plan section EV1.0405(c) and Redlands Municipal Code chapter 18.12. The proposed development comprises a seven-story general hospital, two multi-story medical office buildings, a central utility plant, a seven-story parking structure and associated site improvements including driveways, utility connections, and landscaping. Although development would occur over four phases, the Draft PEIR analyzes the anticipated impacts resulting from buildout consisting of an approximately 580,000 square-foot, 321-bed hospital and 248,000 square feet of medical office floor area.

ceqa-b81b69ab68d12faad9.name: City of Barstow General Plan and Barstow International Gateway Project Draft Environmental Impact Report
ceqa-b81b69ab68d12faad9.projectTitle: City of Barstow General Plan and Barstow International Gateway Project Draft Environmental Impact Report
ceqa-b81b69ab68d12faad9.description: The proposed Project includes: 1) a comprehensive update to the City of Barstow General Plan to bring it current with State laws and plan for the City’s overall long-term development and 2) the BIG facility and Specific Plan. The proposed General Plan updates all of the City’s General Plan Elements except for the Housing Element, which was updated in 2024. During the 25-year planning horizon of the proposed General Plan, the Plan Area could potentially result in a growth of 6,326 households, 6,608 dwelling units, 18,531 residents, 15,341,198 square feet of non-residential uses, and 10,819 jobs by 2048. BNSF Railway Company (BNSF) proposes the new approximately 5,000 acre BIG facility and its Specific Plan to be located partly in incorporated Barstow and partly in an existing unincorporated portion of the County, which the proposed General Plan proposes for concurrent annexation to the City. The BIG Specific Plan proposes a rail yard consisting of an intermodal facility, a “block swap” yard and ancillary rail area, as well as a transload warehouse center and a private utility (i.e., solar farm), and an approximately 680-acre area at the northern boundary of the Specific Plan area that would remain ungraded, a portion of which is proposed to be placed under a conservation easement. Additionally, to serve the proposed rail yard and transload warehouse center, BNSF proposes off-site rail improvements (i.e., lead track extensions) and off-site non-rail improvements (i.e., stormwater drainage, utilities, and circulation/roadways).

ceqa-26a62d66bc041dce77.name: San Bernardino County Behavioral Health Comprehensive Treatment Campus
ceqa-26a62d66bc041dce77.projectTitle: San Bernardino County Behavioral Health Comprehensive Treatment Campus
ceqa-26a62d66bc041dce77.description: The Project Site is comprised of one (1) parcel, Accessor Parcel Numbers (APN) 3105-191-11. The total acreage for the site Is 29.47 acres located In the City of Victorville a parcel owned by San Bernardino County. The Project Site is located at 13333 Palmdale Road in the City of Victorville southeast of the Intersection of Palmdale Road and Cobalt Road. The Proponent of the Project and Lead Agency Is San Bernardino County. The Project Site Is within the City of Victorville General Plan with the development code of Low Density Residential and is currently designated with the zoning of Single Family Residential (R-1). The proposed Project Is the improvement and expansion of the St John of God Health care Services center into the San Bernardino County Behavioral Health Comprehensive Treatment Campus. The County intends to develop this site with new treatment facilities and transitional housing for individuals in recovery under the Behavioral Health Continuum Infrastructure Program (BHCIP) and Community Care Expansion (CCE) program. The Project includes one 36-bed Adult Residential Treatment Facility; one 24-bed Adult Withdrawal Management building; one Outpatient building (contains three group rooms, offices, nurses station, examination room, commercial kitchen and reception); two Adolescent Residential and Psychiatric Residential Treatment Facilities (contains 32 beds, restroom facilities, staff offices, group rooms, therapy rooms, psychiatrist office, exam room, medicine room, nurse station, dining room, living/game room, conference rooms, and family visiting room); and one Wellness Center containing a full-size basketball court, commercial kitchen, group room, arts and crafts room, multipurpose room and offices. Additionally, the CCE facilities will provide 52 beds in one Recovery Residences Building. This Project would develop the Project Site with an additional 144 additional beds. Additionally, new gates and perimeter fencing will be installed, along with a new access road off Cobalt Road. Landscaping will also be added throughout the campus. Parking will consist of the reconfiguration of the existing lot with 33 stalls and adding an additional 228 new stalls. Ingress and egress point on Palmdale Road will be discontinued.

ceqa-a2cfffaa88f80571e5.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a California Endangered Species Act and Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act scientific, educational, or management permit pursuant to Fish and Game Code sections 2081, subdivision (a), and 1927.2, subdivision (h) (Permit No. 2081(a)-25-017-RP) for a project to investigate practical approaches to post-fire restoration of western Joshua trees in the Mojave Desert, a species limited by low germination and high seedling mortality. A pilot experiment will be implemented on MDLT property to compare differences in germination between two habitats (burned vs. unburned) with two different microclimates (open vs. underneath shrubs). The experiment will build on research indicating the importance of microclimates on the recruitment of this species. A thermal time germination model that was developed from growth chamber data will be used to help determine the best field sowing windows, matching soil conditions to the temperatures needed for germination. The pilot will test whether model-informed sowing combined with microsite selection and water addition can substantially improve germination and early survival in post-fire habitats. Up to 60 plots measuring 50 centimeters by 50 centimeters will be divided evenly between burned and unburned habitats. Forty western Joshua tree seeds will be sowed in each plot. Plots will be assigned to one of three treatments within each habitat (burned vs. unburned): (1) under shrub canopy; (2) open microsites; or (3) open microsites with water addition. A total of 40 plots will be caged to deter herbivory. Sensors will be deployed at a depth of <5 centimeters in a total of six plots to investigate whether microclimates differ in temperature and soil moisture. Plots receiving the water addition treatment will be irrigated with a backpack sprayer up to once a week for up to a 6-month period to simulate natural precipitation events during the early germination window. Soil volumetric water content, available soil moisture, soil temperature, precipitation, and ambient air temperature data will be collected. Plots will be monitored once a week for germination and survivorship. Data collected from the experiment will be used to validate the hydrothermal germination model to predict optimal germination conditions in burned and unburned habitats.

ceqa-d74e906abe8936f50b.name: El Camino Project
ceqa-d74e906abe8936f50b.description: A private company, Lone Oak – Rancho LLC, is proposing to expand an existing beverage distribution facility. Existing buildings currently occupy the southern and northern portions of the site (approx. 17.9 acres) while the central portion (a former vineyard) occupies 12.2 acres of the site. The southern portion is developed with a beverage distribution facility and two office buildings. The northern portion of the site contains an existing 62,210-square foot warehouse on approximately 3 acres. The Project applicant is proposing to demolish up to 237,895 square feet of existing buildings and construct up to 1,054,541 square feet of new manufacturing, light industrial, and office uses on the Project site across two phases of construction. Building heights will range from 34 to 131 feet and the Project will have a solar energy/battery storage system and a cogeneration system to help reduce energy consumption. Also included is a 4-story parking structure totaling 335,475 square feet and a new water well. The proposed Project includes two different development options. Phase 1, which includes the retention of one of the existing office buildings and the construction of a new Production Center (PC), Distribution Center (DC), an Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS) and the parking structure, plus Phase 2A results in 783,741 net square feet of building area of non-residential uses (Industrial and Office), not including the new parking structure which does not generate vehicular trips or house employees. In contrast, Phase 1 plus Phase 2B results in 761,616 square feet of building area, or 22,125 less square feet than Phase 1 plus Phase 2A. The difference between the two options is that Phase 2A would reuse the existing 62,210 square-foot warehouse building while Phase 2B would demolish the existing warehouse building and construct a new 40,085 square foot light industrial building. Phase 1 also includes the construction of infrastructure, site improvements, and Project vehicle access.

ceqa-a0db692a516118779d.description: The Project includes the development of 85.73 acres of undeveloped land into a residential development. The Project includes the construction of 159 single-family homes on 32.29 acres, a community recreation center on 0.94 acres, private interior streets on 14.46 acres, debris basins on 1.02 acres, utility infrastructures, and other associated improvements. The Project also includes a 15.15-acre fuel modification zone, including a wet zone, dry zone and special maintenance area, around the residential development. Additional elements of the Project include 10.79-acres of graded and landscaped slopes, 1.89-acre oil tank relocation site, 8.08-acres of open space, 0.26-acre easement access, and 0.85-acre of off-site improvements adjacent to the Project boundary that will be impacted to accommodate road improvements and cleanup from past oil productionrelated contamination. Of the 130.66-acre site, 44.93 acres will not be developed or impacted by Covered Activities and have been proposed to be on-site mitigation, subject to review and approval by CDFW. The Project will result in permanent impacts to 26.82 acres of coastal sage scrub habitat and 58.91 acres of disturbed habitat dominated by invasive species including black mustard (Brassica nigra) for Crotch’s bumble bee (Bombus crotchii). The project is expected to result in incidental take of Crotch’s bumble bee, which is/are designated as a candidate species under the California Endangered Species Act.

ceqa-1a426c8c2ebf868500.name: Yaeger Well Replacement Project
ceqa-1a426c8c2ebf868500.description: GSWC is planning to construct and operate replacement potable water supply well, Yeager Well 4, at its Yeager-Vale Plant. Yeager Well 2 will be decommissioned once Well 4 has been established. An adjacent GSWC-owned parcel to the south (APN: 058326107) has been identified by GSWC as the proposed location for the replacement well. The parcel is approximately 130 feet (east to west) by 100 feet (north to south). The addition of the parcel to the south would expand the total area of the Yeager-Vale Plant to approximately 0.77-acre. The Proposed Project would be part of GSWC’s Morongo Del Sur System, which delivers groundwater pumped from the Morongo Valley portion of the Morongo Basin located east and west of the Twenty-Nine Palms Highway between Morongo Valley and Yucca Valley. GSWC is proposing to decommission Yeager-2 once Yeager Well 4 has been established. Yeager-2 is approximately 300 feet deep, and the new Yeager-4 well would reach approximately the same depth. The facility would not require a crew or staff; therefore, no bathroom facilities would be built. The southern parcel, Parcel B, of the Project Site is undeveloped land, with mesquite dominated vegetation and cottonwood tree (Populus sp.) towards the eastern side, and overhead power lines parallel to the northern property line between the southern parcel and the Yeager-Vale Plant. The overhead power lines proceed north along the eastern perimeter of the Yeager-Vale Plant. As part of the construction, the vegetation and the large cottonwood tree will need to be removed and the ground leveled and prepared (i.e., temporary gravel bed) for heavy equipment prior to construction activities. The cottonwood tree measures 25 feet tall and has a 14.6-inch diameter at breast height (DBH). The Project ingress/egress would be on the western property boundary from Vale Drive (see Figure 3). The Yeager-Vale Plant has several permanent structures that would be protected in place: the Yeager-Vale Plant treatment building, generator, motor control center, and chemical building. The existing onsite discharge pond located on Parcel A would also remain in place. To manage excess water volumes generated during the well development phase that exceeds the capacity of the existing discharge pond, a temporary above-ground high-capacity discharge pipeline would be installed. The line will extend east along Mojave Drive and then continue north along East Drive before terminating south of the East Drive and Covington Drive intersection, with the line discharging into an upland area (see Figure 3). The pipeline would span approximately 500 linear feet and be completely contained within the developed roadway and shoulder of Mojave Drive and East Drive. This alignment has been selected to avoid encroachment on wetland habitat within the Big Morongo Canyon Preserve. GSWC maintains regulatory coverage for this discharge under the State Water Board National Permit Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit for Drinking Water System Discharges (Order No. WQ 2014-0194-DWQ, WDID No. 4DW0623), administered by the State Water Board Division of Water Quality. In June 2015, GSWC received a Notice of Applicability (NOA) for the Statewide Drinking Water System Discharge Permit, identification number 4DW0623, which asserts coverage under Order No. WQ 2014-0194-DWQ. Under this NOA, GSWC is authorized to discharge water from GSWC’s Morongo Del Sur Drinking Water system into the Big Morongo Creek (located within the Big Morongo Canyon Preserve). To ensure NPDES permit compliance, two temporary settling tanks would be deployed on Parcel B to remove suspended solids, reduce turbidity, and decrease flow velocity prior to discharge. These tanks operate based on gravitational sedimentation principles and serve as a best management practice for the discharge. The temporary discharge pipeline and settling infrastructure would be fully decommissioned and removed upon completion of construction activities. The highest pumping rate at Yeager-2 was 415 gallons-per-minute (gpm) when measured in 1990, and the pumping rate has declined nearly 50 percent in recent years. Yeager-4 is anticipated to have a capacity of 300-400 gpm. Pumping rates would be determined during drilling and are impacted by several factors including well interference at the well field, the nearby domestic wells across the street, and water quality. To meet the local noise ordinances, 24-foot-high sound walls would be required during well drilling. It is expected that the Project Site would need to be partially enclosed with sound walls strategically placed to minimize impacts to sensitive receptors to the west and south sides of the Project Site. Project construction, consisting of grading, well drilling, and equipping, would begin in August 2025 and take approximately five to six months to complete. Drilling would occur for approximately 150 days. Some components of the well drilling would require 24-hour operations. The Proposed Project is located on approximately 20 acres of parcel APN: 0457-041-02, which is an approximately 77-acre parcel. It also includes approximately one acre of the adjacent parcel to the west, APN: 0457-041-03, which totals approximately 159 acres. Additionally, the approximately 77-acre parcel APN: 0457-041-04 is incorporated into the project site. The three parcels totaling approximately 312 acres (APNs: 0457-041-02, -03, and -04) are planned to be merged as part of the project. The project site located in El Mirage, unincorporated San Bernardino County, California approximately ten miles west of the City of Adelanto (see Figure 1-Regional Location). The airfield is designated Rural Living (RL) and General Industrial (GI) according to the San Bernardino County Countywide Plan/Policy Plan 2020 (Policy Plan), with zoning designations of Rural Living (RL) and Institutional (IN). ceqa-5cc2507379ba5fc338.description: The proposed work under Encroachment Permit No. 11-26-N-MC-0409 is a component of the Red Beach Operations Access Points Project (P-159) on Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton. This work will be performed under Interstate 5, in San Diego County, at Post Mile R61.46 adjacent to the Las Flores Creek, in the United States Marine Corps (USMC) Camp Pendleton. The transit and maneuver corridors are avenues or roads that facilitate the transit of troops and tactical vehicles between Red Beach and inland training areas at USMC Camp Pendleton. At Red Beach, a corridor measuring 15 feet high and 50 feet wide is required to allow tactical vehicles and equipment to access inland training sites.

ceqa-38b5394a54cb88336a.name: West Elevator Improvements by San Diego Unified Port District at B Street Cruise Ship Terminal
ceqa-38b5394a54cb88336a.projectTitle: West Elevator Improvements by San Diego Unified Port District at B Street Cruise Ship Terminal
ceqa-38b5394a54cb88336a.description: The proposed project would involve the removal and replacement of an existing 2-stop, hydraulic passenger elevator and modernization of an adjacent machine room within the B Street Cruise Ship Terminal (CST) by San Diego Unified Port District in the city of San Diego, California. The existing passenger elevator on the north end of the CST has been decommissioned due to corrosion from storm water infiltration to the elevator pit, and the project proposes the removal of the existing elevator, repairs as outlined below, and in-kind replacement of the elevator. Work to specifically complete the proposed project would include a complete replacement of the elevator cab frame and platform, guides, buffers, safeties, hoistway entrance frames and doors, elevator pit structural components below the pier deck, and other necessary and associated elevator equipment. Work would also include electrical upgrades related to elevator equipment to provide a code-compliant hoistway, elevator car, and machine room, and to further modernization efforts at the CST. Construction specifics would involve removal of the corroded steel frame and replacing the existing frame with a new concrete cast elevator pit. A work platform consisting of supports attached to the piles would be installed to the underside of the deck prior to construction of the elevator pit. This work platform would support the stainless-steel enclosure and cast placement during demolition and construction of the new pit. Temporary shoring would be provided at the underside of the elevator pit to fully support the hoistway and allow for removal of the pit framing. The contractor would remove the existing wall panels and sheet rock to allow for demolition and removal of the existing steel pit framing and associated equipment, and construction of the new concrete pit. After placement of the new concrete cast, new corrugated wall panel and sheet rock would be installed to replace the removed material. All surfaces affected by demolition and replacement work would be patched, textured, and painted to match the adjacent surfaces. The existing stainless-steel enclosure would be protected in-place as well as the existing piles, pile caps, and concrete deck. A water pump would be installed at the bottom of the replaced elevator pit to resolve existing flooding issues and prevent future stormwater impacts to the structure. Equipment required for the proposed project would include a hoist crane for the removal and replacement of the elevator pit and cab as well as a forklift and hand tools. The contractor would comply with all loading capacity requirements of the deck. Contractor lay down areas would be located directly adjacent to the elevator and machine room and would not impact any CST operations or public access. Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to occur in approximately Fall 2026 and would take approximately 12 months to complete. No in-water work would be conducted as part of the proposed project. The contractor would be required to provide a Best Management Practices (BMP) plan prior to the commencement of work. BMPs for the proposed project would include, but are not limited to deployment of construction netting, tarp, or a catchment system below the construction zone to ensure that no discharge of debris or material occurs. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-2d112040e4917f29c5.description: The Encino Ranch Habitat Restoration and Enhancement Project entails enhancing the resilience of the Ranch's 30.5 acre riparian forest community through fuel reduction (e.g., removal of 50 to 60 dead or diseased coast live oaks (Quercus agrifolia) infested with gold spotted oak borer (GSOB), ladder fuel removal, pruning, etc.) restoration / enhancement of 12.3 acres of native grassland through prescribed fire and subsequent revegetation with native grass species, removal of 6.1 acres of invasive species including Armenian blackberry (Rubus armenicanus) and Russian olive (Olea europa), reforestation of 2.05 acres of Engelmann oak woodland, 0.25 acre of groundwater enhancement via process based restoration (PBR) practices, installation of 200 pollinator-friendly native plants, and fence repairs to protect sensitive habitats from potential livestock browsing / herbivory. No herbicide use or work within designated waters of the United States (WOTUS) will be required as part of the Project.
ceqa-2d112040e4917f29c5.crossStreets: Black Canyon Road and Hallyeyaaw Lane

ceqa-5da0239f7b0298de40.name: Power Electronics and Control for 2nd-Life Lithium EV Battery Pack Integration
ceqa-5da0239f7b0298de40.projectTitle: Power Electronics and Control for 2nd-Life Lithium EV Battery Pack Integration
ceqa-5da0239f7b0298de40.description: Amendment to grant agreement to change the recipient’s facility site (also the project facility site) and add a demonstration site to the project. This project will design, construct and demonstrate an innovative integrated power electronics / energy storage system to serve the grid-tied energy storage market. The system will be rated for 120kW (power) and 500kWh (energy) and use repurposed EV packs (2nd-life battery). The recipient will conduct a one-year technology demonstration that will directly benefit either a disadvantaged community (DAC) or a low-income community. The Energy Commission made CEQA findings pertaining to this project, including finding it was categorically exempt under 14 CCR 15301, when the project was originally adopted by the Commission at the Business Meeting held on May 12, 2021. The change in project facility site and the addition of a demonstration site does not change the applicability of the exemption under 14 CCR 15301.

ceqa-2ae1c360a80db3e342.name: Pechstein Site Master Plan Project
ceqa-2ae1c360a80db3e342.description: The Project would entail seven components identified in the Pechstein Site Master Plan, including four facilities within the Pechstein Reservoir property, one facility adjacent to the Pechstein Reservoir property, and two buried pipelines beneath paved public and private roadways. The proposed components at the Pechstein property include a new 10 million gallon circular concrete reservoir, referred to as the Pechstein II Reservoir; replacement of the existing Pechstein I Reservoir's roof; reconfiguring the downstream terminus connections of the Vista Flume to the existing and new reservoir tanks; and consolidating two existing pump stations into a single new pump station. The San Diego County Water Authority's existing VID-3 Flow Control Facility would be replaced at a new location south of the Pechstein property. A new 18-inch-diameter pipeline would be installed beneath the southern branch of Buena Creek Road to the HB Reservoir, southwest of the Pechstein property. A new 30-inch-diameter pipeline would be installed exiting the Pechstein property to the northwest and running beneath Buena Creek Rd and Monte Vista Dr, improving redundancy and reliability as a secondary feed for VID’s 837 Pressure Zone.

ceqa-ef8548146f8ae8a2ed.description: PRJ-1062368 The project proposes a Coastal Development Permit (CDP), Neighborhood Development Permit (NDP), a Site Development Permit (SDP), and Utility Easement Vacation for the demolition of an existing 4-story, 84,000 square-foot {sf) office building, trash and mechanical enclosures, and the construction of a new 4-story, 112,400 sf Commercial Office Building for Research and Development (R&D) uses and a new 6-story 189,795 sf parking garage, associated hardscape and landscape improvements, and other associated improvements (replacement of the central plant, new generator, and new trash enclosure} at 10509 Vista Sorrento Parkway. Description of Previous Project: The City of San Diego previously prepared a Program Environmental Impact Report (PEIR) SCH#) 2022090061 for the Mira Mesa Community Plan Update. The PEIR was certified by the Council of the City of San Diego December 14, 2022, per Resolution No. R-314479. The Mira Mesa Community Plan (MMCP) involved a comprehensive update that incorporates relevant policies from the City of San Diego General Plan and provides a long-range, comprehensive policy framework and vision for growth and development in the Mira Mesa community. The MMCP provides community-specific policies that further implement the General Plan with respect to the distribution and arrangement of land uses and the local street and transit network; implementation of urban design guidelines; recommendations preserving and enhancing natural open space and historical and cultural resources; and prioritization and provision of public facilities within the Mira Mesa community.

ceqa-dfb6c8473bfb26cde9.name: Environmental Sampling by BNSF Railway at National City Marine Terminal
ceqa-dfb6c8473bfb26cde9.projectTitle: Environmental Sampling by BNSF Railway at National City Marine Terminal
ceqa-dfb6c8473bfb26cde9.description: The proposed project would involve soil sampling by BNSF Railway (Applicant) in the city of National City, California. Work to specifically complete the proposed project would involve soil sampling at three locations, up to five (5) feet, using a hand auger on the National City Marine Terminal. Applicant would prepare a Hazardous Materials (HazMat) Work Plan for submittal to the District prior to any sampling activities. The proposed work is anticipated to occur in late 2026 and would take approximately one (1) day to complete, with re-sampling as needed. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the Applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-f795ac4df5156def22.name: Tidelands Land Use and Occupancy Permit to IQHQ-RADD I, LLC for Valet Zone Installation at RaDD Public Right of Way
ceqa-f795ac4df5156def22.projectTitle: Tidelands Land Use and Occupancy Permit to IQHQ-RADD I, LLC for Valet Zone Installation at RaDD Public Right of Way
ceqa-f795ac4df5156def22.description: The proposed project is a Tidelands Use and Occupancy Permit (TUOP) to IQHQ-RaDD I, LLC (Tenant) for their use of roadway area and sidewalk area along North Harbor and West Harbor Drive directly in front of the IQHQ Research and Development District located in the city of San Diego, California. The areas proposed for use under this TUOP are currently used as three (3) passenger loading zones with a length of 66 linear feet each, and are proposed to be used for the purpose of conducting valet parking services, as well as passenger and commercial loading and unloading, and for no other purpose whatsoever without the prior written consent of the Executive Director of District in each instance. Approximately 1,782 square feet of sidewalk will be used for valet operations, and approximately 1,782 square feet of roadway area will be used for vehicles as needed during operations, both along three sections of curb, totaling approximately 198 linear feet of curb space. These valet locations are proposed within existing passenger loading zones, and visitors may continue to use the loading zone for loading and unloading purposes, as originally planned in these areas. Tenant would place temporary, moveable podiums and A-frame signage during operations. Tenant would adhere to the following conditions: • Valet service shall not utilize or park vehicles in the metered parking stalls along Harbor Drive or prevent the members of the public from using any metered spaces; • Valet service shall not demand payment from individuals who park in the metered spaces; • Valet service shall not place signs, cones or temporary valet booth in the roadways directing the public away from metered parking spaces; • Valet service shall allow passenger loading and unloading in the valet locations without the need to utilize valet services. Furthermore, the valet service use of the sidewalk space shall not cause an inconvenience to passenger loading and unloading in the valet locations. • Valet service shall not section off or privatize the public sidewalk space in any way and shall not block the flow of pedestrian traffic on the sidewalk. The Tenant would be responsible for compliance with all laws and regulations associated with the activities on or in connection with the above-described premises, and in all uses thereof, including those regulating stormwater and hazardous materials. No new development, construction, or increase in the size of the property is proposed or authorized as part of the TUOP. It is anticipated that the TUOP would have a total term of approximately five (5) years. The TUOP may be terminated by the District or Tenant as a matter of right and without cause at any time upon providing thirty (30) days’ notice in writing to the other party of such termination.

ceqa-76be0d40d4ff063815.name: Administrative Office Data Re-Cabling Project (CIP27401)
ceqa-76be0d40d4ff063815.description: The Helix Water District Administration Office is a 30,000 square foot, four-story office building constructed in 1986. The District purchased and renovated the building in the mid-1990s. It serves as the primary public facing facility for the District and houses a large portion of District staff , as well as critical information technology infrastructure. The building’s existing data cabling infrastructure, which was part of the building renovation in the 1990s, has become functionally obsolete and has reached the end of its useful life. This Project will replace the existing Administration Office network data cabling with current technology. Existing Category 5 data cabling with be replaced with both fiber optic and Cat 6E cables, as well as related network components. This re-cabling will result in the network system’s ability to transmit significantly more data to keep up with the growing use of video and graphics applications. Project construction is anticipated to begin in November 2026 with anticipated completion June 2027. This project will benefit District customers by maintaining reliability of service and avoiding costly emergency repair expenses. The Administrative Office is critical to the District's operations.

ceqa-a2bae69a64bdaaf65b.name: Districtwide Firebreak & Weed Abatement
ceqa-a2bae69a64bdaaf65b.description: The project would involve clearing of a 30-foot firebreak around the majority of the perimeter of the Cuyamaca College campus and 30- and 15-foot fire breaks around the majority of the perimeter of the Grossmont College campus, as well as weed abatement on portions of both campuses. Work for the firebreaks would involve removal of weeds, brush, and dead, dry, and readily combustible vegetation, without disturbing the underlying soil or root structure. Work for weed abatement at both campuses would involve selectively removing dry grasses, weeds, invasive vegetation, and other combustible materials primarily through hand-cutting, trimming, and weed-whipping. Existing trees and sensitive native vegetation would be protected through installation of fencing along the approved limits of disturbance, flagging by a qualified biologist of native plants designated for avoidance, and biological monitoring. Work will be scheduled outside of the nesting bird season and Crotch’s bumble bee flight season to the extent feasible. If work must occur within the nesting bird season (February 1 to August 31) in areas that provide potential nesting habitat, a nesting bird survey would be required prior to the start of work, and the recommendations of the biologist would be followed to avoid impacts to nesting birds. If work must occur within the Crotch’s bumble bee flight season (April 1 to August 31) in portions of the proposed Cuyamaca College weed abatement areas with potential to provide Crotch’s bumble bee habitat, protocol surveys for the species would be required prior to the start of work and the recommendations of the biologist would be followed to avoid impacts to the species.
ceqa-a2bae69a64bdaaf65b.crossStreets: Grossmont College Drive and State Route 125; Fury Lane and Jamacha Road

ceqa-5c36508223c14bbd40.name: Ocean Breeze Ranch (TM-5615TER) License Agreement
ceqa-5c36508223c14bbd40.description: The proposed project involves a license for the use of County facilities and property. This license will allow the Ocean Breeze Ranch development to access County-owned areas to construct roadway improvements required for the extension of a public segment of Dulin Road west of Old Highway 395, terminating in a new public cul-de-sac. The work to be authorized by the license includes: (1) Grading of the roadway corridor and placement of fill within the roadway footprint, including all earthwork needed to establish design elevations and ensure structural stability of the roadway improvements; (2) construction of approximately 14,289 square feet of engineered fill slope extending from the cul-de-sac terminus to existing site topography, together with a 10-foot-wide 5,200 square-foot buffer area and 598 square feet of grading within the future right-of-way dedication area for a total affected area of approximately 20,087 square feet; (3) Grading, construction, and installation of a vehicular entrance with six bollards to provide ingress and egress to San Luis Rey Park, including permanent improvements necessary to establish safe and functional park access. This project was originally approved on December 13, 2019, by the County of San Diego Planning Commission. The project site is 1,403 acres and the original project included 396 residential lots, public and private parks, trails, landscaping, roads, equestrian facilities, open space, road and utility improvements, and grading. In April 2025, the County of San Diego Planning Commission approved a Revised Map Time Extension for the Previously Approved Project (Tentative Map 5615) (Modified Project). The Modified Project included a time extension and revisions to the Previously Approved Project’s grading design in order to avoid extensive import or export of soil in addition to other changes. Specifically, the Modified Project included changes to 86 lot lines (i.e., 57 residential lots, 25 open space lots, 2 public park lots, and 2 private park lots); lowered building pad elevations in PA1 and PA3 and raised building pad elevations in PA2; revised utility alignments; an additional lot line to split the 100-acre subarea off of the 308.9-acre eastern hills excess biological open space; realigning Street B and associated surface improvements and utilities; adding drainage basins; revising West Lilac Road to provide a dual left turn lane and eastbound bike lane; an additional borrow site in PA3; construction of an equestrian Major Use Permit (MUP) emergency fire access per PDS2016-MUP-16-012; and addition of off-site traffic mitigation. In addition, on December 11, 2025, a major grading permit was issued to allow the preparation of the project site for construction of the approved subdivision and associated improvements. The original Ocean Breeze Ranch project was processed in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15183, and the 15183 environmental checklist was previously circulated for public disclosure in 2019 for the approved project. A 15183 Checklist was prepared for the Modified Project in 2025, along with specific technical studies pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). CEQA Guidelines Section 15183 requires focus on those impacts that are new or more severe than those analyzed in the County's General Plan Program EIR (i.e., peculiar impact of the project or project site). Therefore, a focused Mitigated Negative Declaration was also prepared in 2025 for the project in order to address potential impacts to Crotch's bumble bee.
