ceqa-284fb5e95c1da5cce3.name: Shellfish Basket Study at Zuniga Shoals
ceqa-284fb5e95c1da5cce3.projectTitle: Shellfish Basket Study at Zuniga Shoals
ceqa-284fb5e95c1da5cce3.description: The San Diego Unified Port District (Applicant or Port) proposes to perform baseline testing of the health and quality of adult oysters, mussels, and seaweed at one location in Zuniga Shoals (Figure 1) using shellfish baskets and conducting concurrent water quality monitoring at this location (the shellfish and seaweed health testing and water quality testing are collectively referred to as the “Project”). The Project is anticipated to occur over the course of 80 days in the fall or winter of 2026-2027 and would include: (1) species harvesting and depuration; (2) the installation of a buoy system (see Figure 2), which would include 12 shellfish baskets containing shellfish and seaweed species; and (3) sampling of the shellfish and seaweed, and water quality monitoring. The purpose of the Project is to assess the potential for deployed shellfish to be used to promote denitrification and water quality filtration through shellfish and seaweed co-culture experiments at the proposed study location with denitrification capacity assessments. The results of the Project would provide data on the denitrification capacity of shellfish and seaweed. Findings could be used in conjunction with previous shellfish basket study and water quality monitoring findings to inform the potential for future shellfish and seaweed aquaculture siting, as well as the use of shellfish and/or seaweed for potential restoration activities and bioremediation projects. The Project would study two species of shellfish and two species of seaweed: adult Pacific oysters (Crassostrea gigas), adult Bay mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis/M. trossulus), green seaweed (Ulva lactuca), and kelp (Macrocystis pyrifera). As described below, all shellfish and seaweed used in the Project would be harvested from existing shellfish and seaweed populations in San Diego Bay (Bay) under Scientific Collecting Permit #S-251420001-25161-001 issued by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW). Shellfish and seaweed would be harvested by hand from existing structures within the Bay. Then, the harvested organisms would undergo depuration at the Coastal and Marine Institute Laboratory at San Diego State University to eliminate the sampling bias associated with the existing Bay water quality conditions. This depuration would occur seven days before deployment. After harvesting and depuration, the shellfish and seaweed species would be placed into 12 shellfish baskets for deployment. Following depuration, the buoy system would be installed at the Project location. No eelgrass resources are known to occur within the project footprint. Please see Figure 2 for the configuration of the proposed buoy system. This would include: • One 600-pound 2 foot by 2 foot by 2-foot concrete block and up to three additional concrete weights in five-gallon buckets that are up to 100 pounds each and would be placed on the seafloor • One 5/8” nylon line approximately 35 feet in length, which would connect the concrete block to a surface buoy • One 5/8” nylon line approximately 15 feet in length (tether line), which would be connected to an additional surface buoy and connected to the longer nylon line with a 3/8” shackle • 12 shellfish baskets, approximately 25 inches by 10 inches by 6 inches in size, which would be secured to the tether nylon line via secure clips on the baskets, and • At least two additional submerged standard rubber marine-grade buoy, to ensure the baskets remain at a depth compatible with sampling, if necessary. In total, the buoy system would have an approximate total radius of up to 30 feet and a bottom radius of three to four feet distributed between the concrete block and additional weights. A maximum of two people would be required to deploy, and later remove, the buoy system (Figure 2) at the proposed location (Figure 1). Following completion of the study, Port staff would remove all baskets from the water. Port divers would approach the site again, evaluate conditions at the surface and at bottom depth, bring the buoy onboard and retrieve the weights by chain/cable onto the vessel. Port staff will provide notification to Coastal staff when the baskets are deployed and removed. The 12 baskets would be filled with the shellfish and/or seaweed species as follows: • Two baskets would contain between 100-140 mussels • Two baskets would contain between 100-140 mussels and 3 pounds of kelp • Two baskets would contain between 100-140 oysters • Four baskets would contain between 100-140 oysters and 100-140 mussels • Two baskets would contain between 100-140 oysters and 3 pounds of Ulva. The buoy system would be deployed over a total estimated time of 80 days. It is anticipated that the shellfish baskets would be installed about a week after the buoy system is deployed, and that the shellfish baskets would be removed about a week prior to removal of the buoy system. Shellfish tissue, seaweed samples, and water samples would be collected frequently, anticipated to be on a weekly basis, during the deployment of the shellfish baskets. The deployment period of the shellfish baskets would allow adequate time for the shellfish to filter water and accumulate nutrients present in the surrounding waters. Taking multiple samples would be necessary because it would allow the Applicant to assess how water quality, shellfish tissues, and seaweed samples change over time with the presence of shellfish and seaweed during the deployment period, and additional sampling may be needed during the deployment period. The Applicant would send the collected samples to an off-Tidelands location (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Weck Laboratories) for analysis. On the final day of deployment, all equipment, including any remaining shellfish and seaweed, would be removed from the water. Removal of the buoy system from the proposed location would require approximately one day to complete. The Project location would be accessed by small boat for basket installation, sampling, and removal. To conduct this study, the following would apply to the Applicant to manage and reduce marine debris: Marine Debris Reduction and Management. Port staff and/or consultants shall carry out the operation consistent with the following marine debris reduction and management practices: A. Storm Damage and Debris. As soon as safely and reasonably possible following storm or severe wind or weather events, Port staff and/or consultants shall patrol each study location for escaped or damaged equipment. All equipment that cannot be repaired and placed back into service shall be properly recycled or disposed of at an appropriate onshore facility. In addition, Port staff and/or consultants shall retrieve or repair any escaped or damaged equipment that it encounters while conducting routine sampling and/or maintenance activities associated with the pilot project. If the escaped gear cannot be repaired and replaced, it shall be properly recycled or disposed of on land. B. Gear Marking and Replacement. Port staff and/or consultants shall mark all shellfish baskets and floats in an easily identifiable manner with identification information. Markings shall be securely attached and robust enough to remain attached and legible after an extended period in the marine environment (e.g. heat transfer, hot stamp, etching, etc.). Existing floats currently in use shall be marked or replaced with marked versions when replanted and all unmarked gear shall be replaced in this way. In the event that gear, or equipment becomes displaced or dislodged from the experiment, it shall be the Port’s responsibility to retrieve the material from the shoreline, open water, eelgrass beds, mudflat, or submerged bottom with minimal damage to the resources affected. Once located, such material shall be removed as soon as feasible and properly disposed of, recycled, or returned to use. C. Ongoing Operations. Port staff and/or consultants shall not leave or temporarily store tools, loose gear, or construction materials on its leased tidelands or surrounding areas. All study equipment installed on and in use at the study sites shall be kept neat and secure and maintained in functional condition. Port staff and/or consultants shall carry out regular bed inspections and maintenance activities to help ensure that broken, collapsed, fallen, or buried gear is fixed or removed in a timely manner. D. Bed Cleaning at Harvest. Port staff and/or consultants shall carry out a thorough inspection to locate and remove loose, abandoned or out of use equipment, tools, and accumulations of oysters from the surrounding substrate. Oyster shell shall not be intentionally placed or deposited within the lease outside of cultivation gear, and oysters or oyster shell accidentally spilled during the experiment shall be immediately collected and removed. E. Excessive Gear Loss or Maintenance Failures. If the Port is found to be responsible for consistently extensive loss of equipment into the marine environment or is consistently failing to maintain its equipment in an intact and serviceable condition, Port staff and/or consultants shall modify its equipment and/or operations to minimize equipment loss and mitigate impacts to affected habitat. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the Project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the Applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater, as well as acquiring necessary permits from relevant resource agencies, such as the California Coastal Commission, Army Corps of Engineers, and Regional Water Quality Control Board, including the necessary real estate or access agreements, or coastal development permitting for the proposed project site, which is not within the District’s permitting or coastal jurisdiction.

ceqa-8b0e5ca3504220b580.name: Ocean Breeze Ranch (TM-5615TER) License Agreement
ceqa-8b0e5ca3504220b580.description: The proposed project involves a license for the use of County facilities and property. This license will allow the Ocean Breeze Ranch development to access County-owned areas to construct roadway improvements required for the extension of a public segment of Dulin Road west of Old Highway 395, terminating in a new public cul-de-sac. The work to be authorized by the license includes: (1) Grading of the roadway corridor and placement of fill within the roadway footprint, including all earthwork needed to establish design elevations and ensure structural stability of the roadway improvements; (2) construction of approximately 14,289 square feet of engineered fill slope extending from the cul-de-sac terminus to existing site topography, together with a 10-foot-wide 5,200 square-foot buffer area and 598 square feet of grading within the future right-of-way dedication area for a total affected area of approximately 20,087 square feet; (3) Grading, construction, and installation of a vehicular entrance with six bollards to provide ingress and egress to San Luis Rey Park, including permanent improvements necessary to establish safe and functional park access. This project was originally approved on December 13, 2019, by the County of San Diego Planning Commission. The project site is 1,403 acres and the original project included 396 residential lots, public and private parks, trails, landscaping, roads, equestrian facilities, open space, road and utility improvements, and grading. In April 2025, the County of San Diego Planning Commission approved a Revised Map Time Extension for the Previously Approved Project (Tentative Map 5615) (Modified Project). The Modified Project included a time extension and revisions to the Previously Approved Project’s grading design in order to avoid extensive import or export of soil in addition to other changes. Specifically, the Modified Project included changes to 86 lot lines (i.e., 57 residential lots, 25 open space lots, 2 public park lots, and 2 private park lots); lowered building pad elevations in PA1 and PA3 and raised building pad elevations in PA2; revised utility alignments; an additional lot line to split the 100-acre subarea off of the 308.9-acre eastern hills excess biological open space; realigning Street B and associated surface improvements and utilities; adding drainage basins; revising West Lilac Road to provide a dual left turn lane and eastbound bike lane; an additional borrow site in PA3; construction of an equestrian Major Use Permit (MUP) emergency fire access per PDS2016-MUP-16-012; and addition of off-site traffic mitigation. In addition, on December 11, 2025, a major grading permit was issued to allow the preparation of the project site for construction of the approved subdivision and associated improvements. The original Ocean Breeze Ranch project was processed in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15183, and the 15183 environmental checklist was previously circulated for public disclosure in 2019 for the approved project. A 15183 Checklist was prepared for the Modified Project in 2025, along with specific technical studies pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). CEQA Guidelines Section 15183 requires focus on those impacts that are new or more severe than those analyzed in the County's General Plan Program EIR (i.e., peculiar impact of the project or project site). Therefore, a focused Mitigated Negative Declaration was also prepared in 2025 for the project in order to address potential impacts to Crotch's bumble bee.

ceqa-86819752d449486640.description: Drill 9 borings each to a depth of 40 feet. Most borings will be drilled within paved shoulders of Caltrans I-805 medians. See attached SIP files for additional information. Work at each boring location will take approximately 4-8 hours (single shift).

The areas for use under this Lease are proposed to be used only and exclusively for the purpose of the sale, service, rental, leasing, demonstration, and related use of marine equipment and vessels, including without limitation kayaks, paddleboards, personal watercraft, dinghies, boats, and similar vessels and equipment, and office space for maritime-related purposes, and mooring for boats, yachts, yacht brokerage, and charter vessels limited to the four (4) slips located on the water area only and all uses which are normally and customarily ancillary or incidental to any or all of the foregoing. Specifically, the Modified Project included changes to 86 lot lines (i.e., 57 residential lots, 25 open space lots, 2 public park lots, and 2 private park lots); lowered building pad elevations in PA1 and PA3 and raised building pad elevations in PA2; revised utility alignments; an additional lot line to split the 100-acre subarea off of the 308.9-acre eastern hills excess biological open space; realigning Street B and associated surface improvements and utilities; adding drainage basins; revising West Lilac Road to provide a dual left turn lane and eastbound bike lane; an additional borrow site in PA3; construction of an equestrian Major Use Permit (MUP) emergency fire access per PDS2016-MUP-16-012; and addition of off-site traffic mitigation. The original Ocean Breeze Ranch project was processed in accordance with CEQA Guidelines Section 15183, and the 15183 environmental checklist was previously circulated for public disclosure in 2019 for the approved project. A 15183 Checklist was prepared for the Modified Project in 2025, along with specific technical studies pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). CEQA Guidelines Section 15183 requires focus on those impacts that are new or more severe than those analyzed in the County's General Plan Program EIR (i.e., peculiar impact of the project or project site). Therefore, a focused Mitigated Negative Declaration was also prepared in 2025 for the project in order to address potential impacts to Crotch's bumble bee.

ceqa-e0cfa1e83e6a9ee24f.name: Rooftop BMU Replacement by Manchester Grand Hyatt
ceqa-e0cfa1e83e6a9ee24f.projectTitle: Rooftop BMU Replacement by Manchester Grand Hyatt
ceqa-e0cfa1e83e6a9ee24f.description: The proposed project is a like-for-like equipment replacement of one (1) building maintenance unit (BMU) located atop the Harbor Tower at Manchester Grand Hyatt (Applicant) in the city of San Diego, California. The BMU, a permanent piece of rooftop equipment used to safely access exterior components of the building for maintenance and cleaning, has reached the end of its typical service life, has been decertified, and is now in need of replacement. Work to specifically complete the proposed project would involve utilizing a helicopter for removal of the existing unit from the rooftop, placement of a new unit, and transfer of the decommissioned unit to an offsite location. The current BMU sits and moves on existing steel tracks which would remain in place. Utilizing hand tools, the BMU would be removed in eight (8) sections, and the new BMU equipment would be similarly installed in eight (8) sections onto the existing tracks. A temporary ground-based equipment staging area would be established on Galleon Way, between Manchester Grand Hyatt and Marriot Marquis for the new BMU unit and expired unit after removal. Upon arrival, the helicopter would proceed along the planned flight path and hover in place above the neighboring Marriott Marquis while ground crews on the rooftop would connect the “longline” cable and rigging configuration which allows the helicopter to load and carry materials to and from the staging area and Harbor Tower. The aircraft would lift the expired equipment vertically from its current mounting on top of the Hyatt, then place the unit down in the staging area. Once detached, the new equipment would be connected and lifted from the staging area and positioned into place by workers located atop the Hyatt. This sequence would be repeated for the planned eight (8) BMU installation sections. The helicopter would perform all removal and replacement activities and then vacate the area; it would never land in the project area, only hover over the designated area and flight path. Per flight regulations, the flight plan outlines a required closure radius for the project to ensure safety during operations. Temporary closures required for the proposed project would include Galleon Way, the pool decks, top two (2) floors, and rooftop of both the Hyatt and Marriott Marquis, the area surrounding Sally’s Restaurant, and portions of the southern facing Marriott Marquis outdoor space. Closure of the adjacent promenade and retail businesses would be avoided. Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to occur in December 2026, would take approximately one (1) day to complete, and would require approximately ten (10) workers in four (4) trucks to complete the work. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the Applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-d58d54cef31d70c940.name: DIVERTING DAM ANNUAL MAINTENANCE
ceqa-d58d54cef31d70c940.description: Background: Upon completion (in 1887) the Cuyamaca and Diverting dams became integral pieces of infrastructure for the San Diego Flume Company (Helix Water District isthe successor). Water was stored behind Cuyamaca dam during the rainy season and then transferred via Boulder Creek and the San Diego River to the Diverting dam. Once at the Diverting dam, water was released into the flume, and eventually stored in La Mesa for distribution to its customers. By 1937, the flume was abandoned, due to the construction of EI Capitan Dam and Reservoir. The District retains the right to store up to 10,000 acre-feet of water annually in EI Capitan Reservoir. The Diverting Dam continues to be used as a metering station to account for the District's storage rights in EI Capitan Reservoir, and will continue to be used in this manner for the foreseeable future. An average of 6,565 acre feet per year flows through this metering station and is ultimately transferred from EI Capitan Reservoir to either Lake Jennings, or Helix Water District's R. M. Levy Water Treatment Plant thusly serving as local water supply and helping to reduce the amount of imported wafer required in the County. Project: The District is proposing a maintenance project to remove trash, debris, silt and vegetation that facilitates the inspection and continued safe operation of the dam and metering station. Since 2003 the district has maintained a Streambed Alteration Agreement with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife. The current agreement is EPIMS-SDO-57397-R5, issued on January 7, 2026. All project work will be in compliance with the SAA; per SSA Section 2.1 (Work Period), no vegetation or sediment removal work will be performed between February 2 and September 15, to avoid potential impacts to nesting birds. The benefits associated with the proposed project include the ability to transfer local water supply in an efficient manner, reduce the dependence on imported water, and the continued integrity of the dam. Another benefit will be the reestablishment of a small pool of water behind the dam that in the past has been used by wildlife. This will benefit both the customers of Helix Water District as well as the continued safety of downstream properties. Project is slated to begin after September 15th in accordance with the SAA permit and be completed by February 1, 2027.

ceqa-db58d5e753ff884162.description: Caltrans proposes to perform ramp pavement rehabilitation to remove 0.2’ existing asphalt and replace it with 0.2’ rubberized asphalt in San Diego on eastbound SR 54 on the mainline from post mile T10.993 – T14.212. All work is within the existing ramp pavement and there will be no staging location.

ceqa-e7a2eae7a54d7b44c5.name: Encampment Deterrent at Camino Del Rio South at Eastbound Collector to Fairmount Avenue
ceqa-e7a2eae7a54d7b44c5.projectTitle: Encampment Deterrent at Camino Del Rio South at Eastbound Collector to Fairmount Avenue
ceqa-e7a2eae7a54d7b44c5.description: Caltrans proposes to install approximately 70-feet of chain link fence Type (CL-6) along existing bicycle jughandle at Camino del Rio South at the eastbound I-8 collector to Fairmount Avenue adjacent to I-8. This is an exclusionary measure to discourage the re-establishment of unsheltered individuals. Caltrans proposes to perform encampment deterrent measures to prevent persons experiencing homelessness (PEH)) being established. Project work includes installing 24-36-inch minus rock, brow ditch cleaning, culvert cleaning, vegetation excess growth removal, tree stump removal, and install fencing. All work is within existing Caltrans right-of-way.

ceqa-6d8e0682396a690d11.name: Install Concrete V-Ditch on SR-905 in San Diego County
ceqa-6d8e0682396a690d11.projectTitle: Install Concrete V-Ditch on SR-905 in San Diego County
ceqa-6d8e0682396a690d11.description: Caltrans proposes to remove approximately 1,100 linear feet (PM 5.4 to 5.6) of damaged concrete v-ditch and replace the concrete v-ditch, install 4,600 linear feet (PM 5.7 to 6.6) of concrete v-ditch, and replace three (3) damaged concrete aprons. Caltrans will not be touching the actual inlets/drainage systems, just the concrete ditch and aprons. The project is needed because erosion from fill material has clogged the existing multiple drain inlets, which have caused an overload on drainage system and slope washouts. The project is located in San Diego County on the eastbound SR-905 from I-805 to Caliente Avenue along thrie-beam guardrail. The estimated cut quantity is approximately 7,500 cubic feet and the depth of soil disturbance is less than 6 inches.

ceqa-fb5873aa9575a11a30.name: Repair Sinkhole and Failed Culvert on I-15 Near Old Highway 395
ceqa-fb5873aa9575a11a30.projectTitle: Repair Sinkhole and Failed Culvert on I-15 Near Old Highway 395
ceqa-fb5873aa9575a11a30.description: Caltrans proposes a District Director’s Order (DDO) to repair a damaged sinkhole caused by failed culvert to further prevent damage on a busy roadway near the Old Highway 395 Overcrossing (Bridge No. 57-0869). The scope of this emergency contract is to backfill any voids under the shoulder, remove and replace failed culvert section, and repair the damaged shoulder.

ceqa-043019407980850ca9.name: Culvert Repair along SR 78 near Julian
ceqa-043019407980850ca9.projectTitle: Culvert Repair along SR 78 near Julian
ceqa-043019407980850ca9.description: Caltrans proposes a District Director’s Order (DDO) to replace a failed culvert along SR 78 near the community of Julian in San Diego County at post mile 54.1. The scope of this emergency contract is to backfill any voids under the travel way, remove and replace failed culvert, and repair the roadway structural section. The project includes construction area signs, traffic control systems, hot mixed asphalt (HMA) paving, and striping.

ceqa-6ce35109c78ab169cf.name: PL26-0083/PL26-0084 – SIKH SOCIETY OF SAN DIEGO FACILITY EXPANSION
ceqa-6ce35109c78ab169cf.projectTitle: PL26-0083/PL26-0084 – SIKH SOCIETY OF SAN DIEGO FACILITY EXPANSION

ceqa-88ef4368ed52c6b4c7.projectTitle: 5011 Tierra del Oro Beach Access Right-of-Entry (ROE)
ceqa-88ef4368ed52c6b4c7.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-88ef4368ed52c6b4c7.description: The homeowner of 5011 Tierra del Oro in the City of Carlsbad requests approximately 25 days of access through Carlsbad State Beach to reconfigure an existing rock revetment at the base of the bluff below their property. State Parks will issue a Right of Entry permit to allow access to complete the project. A Notice of Intent to issue a Coastal Development Permit was sent to the applicant. Ministerial approval was provided for the project via the City of Carlsbad on August 17, 2023, by Principal Planner, Cliff Jones. Further project details regarding the beach access for the project may be obtained by submitting a request to the project Environmental Coordinator listed below. All project measures and conditions shall be followed as indicated within the Right of Entry permit.

ceqa-996a4f77e680c6c557.name: Pier View Way Bridges and Lifeguard Headquarters and Beachfront Facilities Phase II
ceqa-996a4f77e680c6c557.projectTitle: Pier View Way Bridges and Lifeguard Headquarters and Beachfront Facilities Phase II Project
ceqa-996a4f77e680c6c557.description: Improvements to the Pier Bridges, Lifeguard Headquarters, Junior Seau Beach Community Center, and Junior Seau Amphitheatre/Bandshell, as well as the pier plaza and adjacent public spaces. ceqa-c6e3afab723a703b13.name: The Olivenhain Municipal Water District has established Water Capacity Fees within Zones of Benefit effective November 16, 2026.
ceqa-c6e3afab723a703b13.projectTitle: The Olivenhain Municipal Water District has established Water Capacity Fees within Zones of Benefit effective November 16, 2026.
ceqa-c6e3afab723a703b13.description: The Project is to increase water capacity fees within Zones of Benefit based on the 2023 Water Capacity Fee Study for new customers and developments within the areas already served by the Olivenhain Municipal Water District. The purpose is the raising of essential funds to meet anticipated capital expenses in order to maintain existing water service levels within existing service areas. The fees will not be used to expand existing levels of water service.

ceqa-3556b108371544bde3.description: The project consists of disposition of 1.068 acres of APN 678-252-11 in San Diego County to the State of California, Department of Transportation for public use.

ceqa-e4d5ef8853b95a208d.name: Mulefat and Coastal Sage Scrub Habitat Restoration (26/27-SD-03)
ceqa-e4d5ef8853b95a208d.projectTitle: Mulefat and Coastal Sage Scrub Habitat Restoration (26/27-SD-03)
ceqa-e4d5ef8853b95a208d.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-e4d5ef8853b95a208d.description: Native plant communities at Border Field State Park support a broad array of wildlife including the state and federally endangered Least Bell's Vireo and federally threatened Coastal California Gnatcatcher. Flooding and excessive sedimentation have caused a proliferation of non-native invasive weed infestations at that decrease biodiversity and degrade the quality of habitat for nesting and foraging. This project will restore approximately 3.5 acres of mulefat scrub and coastal sage scrub habitat at Border Field State Park. Further project details and measures to be implemented to avoid and/or minimize environmental impact may be obtained by submitting a request to the project Environmental Coordinator listed below.

ceqa-e9fee877192dd3a0df.name: Stencil Parking Stalls, Green Curb and Parking Signs by San Diego Unified Port District at Port Park in Barrio Logan
ceqa-e9fee877192dd3a0df.projectTitle: Stencil Parking Stalls, Green Curb and Parking Signs by San Diego Unified Port District at Port Park in Barrio Logan
ceqa-e9fee877192dd3a0df.description: The proposed project would involve stenciling in nine (9) “T” stencils on existing pavement to define new parking stalls, painting the curb green, and adding new and replacement parking signs within and adjacent to the Port Park in Barrio Logan (formerly Cesar Chavez Park) by San Diego Unified Port District (District) in the city of San Diego, California. The west side of Chicano Park Boulevard (directly adjacent the Port Park in Barrio Logan) currently has signage for no parking between 10:30pm-6am and signage for the 3-hour parking limit. The proposed project would replace the existing signage and would keep the same parking hours and limits as those aforementioned. The replacement signage would be installed on the fence where the existing signage is located. On the east side of Chicano Park Boulevard (across the street from Port Park in Barrio Logan) there is currently unmarked street parking available for approximately nine (9) parking spaces. The proposed project would match the parking conditions on the west side of the street (painted green curb, signage on new posts and on the adjacent fence for no parking between 10:30pm-6am and for the 3-hour parking limit and “T” stencils on the pavement to define the parking stalls). This would gain approximately nine (9) parking spaces for the adjacent park and would allow the District to monitor and enforce parking regulations. The proposed project would encourage the use of these parking spaces for park users rather than for nearby businesses. Within the Port Park in Barrio Logan parking lot, the proposed project would replace the existing signage and would keep the same parking hours and limits as those currently onsite. The replacement signage would be installed on the fences, posts and poles where the existing signage is located. Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to occur in approximately Summer 2026 and would take approximately two (2) days to complete using small equipment, hand tools and a work truck with ongoing maintenance as-needed. During this time, there would be temporary impacts to parking spots in order to complete pavement marking and curb painting, as well as temporary impacts to the parking spots at individual sign install locations to establish safe work zones. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the District would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-0a16ac10bb23e29e07.name: Storage Tent No. 2 Modifications by BAE Systems at Tenth Avenue Marine Terminal
ceqa-0a16ac10bb23e29e07.projectTitle: Storage Tent No. 2 Modifications by BAE Systems at Tenth Avenue Marine Terminal
ceqa-0a16ac10bb23e29e07.description: The proposed project would involve the addition of a sprinkler system and slight reduction in size to an existing storage tent at Tenth Avenue Marine Terminal by BAE Systems San Diego Ship Repair, Inc. (Tenant) in the city of San Diego, California. A CEQA and Coastal Determinations and Notice of Approval (CatDet) (Project No. 2024-088) was issued in late-2024 for the Tenant to install a second storage tent (storage tent no. 2) on their leasehold to provide additional onsite storage, increase operational efficiency, and reduce the amount of truck trips needed to transport equipment to and from the Tenant’s auxiliary warehouse located offsite. The storage tent no. 2 was erected approximately one year ago within the Tenant’s leasehold. The proposed project would involve modifications to the existing storage tent no. 2 as follows: • Reduce the width of the tent from 80 feet to 70 feet and reduce the height from 34 feet to 28 feet, with the length remaining 170 feet. • Installation of a sprinkler system. Installation of the sprinkler system would require trenching to connect the newly proposed sprinkler system to an existing water source onsite. o The sprinkler system would utilize salt water from the on-site pressurized salt water system via an existing underground supply line. There would be new 6” piping tied into a nearby lateral with a gate valve located approximately 140 feet from the new riser. The new riser would include protection bollards. o Trenching required for the proposed pipe would include trenching of approximately 140 feet in length x approximately 4 feet deep x approximately 2 feet wide. Trenching required for each bollard would be approximately 2 feet wide x 2 feet long x approximately 3 and a half feet deep • In addition to the existing storage activities conducted in the tent structure, the Tenant would also use the area for various employee engagement activities including morning briefings, “stretch and flex” (worker limbering exercises), and other existing related activities. None of the planned physical or use modifications expand or modify current shipyard uses, employment, or other aspects of authorized activity or operations by BAE Systems at the site. Construction of the proposed project is anticipated to occur in approximately Summer 2026 and would take approximately six (6) months to complete, with ongoing maintenance as needed and future removal anticipated. Proposed equipment required for the project would include concrete saws, an excavator, compactor, high-reach booms, forklifts, hand tools and associated equipment. All staging for the proposed Project would occur within the Tenant's leasehold. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the Applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-812528c97965bd1c38.name: Drone Show Event on October 10, 2026 at Embarcadero Marina Park North
ceqa-812528c97965bd1c38.projectTitle: Drone Show Event on October 10, 2026 at Embarcadero Marina Park North
ceqa-812528c97965bd1c38.description: The proposed project is for an approximately 10-minute drone show on October 10, 2026 at Embarcadero Marina Park North (EMPN) in San Diego, CA. The drones would be deployed from and recovered at the southeastern edge of EMPN and displayed southwest of the launch site directly over the water (Attachment A). The proposed event would have a duration of one (1) day, including set-up at approximately noon and clean-up in the evening. A temporary safety perimeter would be established on the southeast curved edge of EMPN using cones and maintained by staff. The safety perimeter would include both the flight path from which the drones would launch and the area of water over which the show would be performed. The safety is positioned as close to the water as possible to provide the safest and most direct flight path from the staging area to the over-water show area, and to minimize temporary impacts to public access to the fullest extent feasible. Pedestrian access within the safety perimeter would be temporarily restricted for a total of approximately 15 minutes prior to and during the drone show. Adjacent park space would remain open at all times. Following the approximately 15-minute restriction period, the walkway would be reopened. No other closures of the walkways or road are anticipated to occur. The proposed event would be publicly viewable at no cost from various areas throughout the Embarcadero. Once the drone show concludes and the drones are secured, the temporary safety perimeter would be removed. Staging for the proposed event would consist of a flight operations tent station and approximately 300 drones. In the unlikely event a drone descends into the water, a dedicated safety boat would be on site to recover the drone. The drone show operation would have staff assigned as visual observers. Visual observers are responsible for scanning and monitoring for any and all airborne activity, such as aircraft, failed drones, and activity involving wildlife, and reporting any relevant observations to the District. Additionally, the Applicant is required to comply with FAA regulations and obtain any applicable approvals.

ceqa-128d8dc08fd75cf88e.name: Right of Entry Permit between the County and Bonita Historical Society Taste of Bonita
ceqa-128d8dc08fd75cf88e.projectTitle: Right of Entry Permit between the County and Bonita Historical Society Taste of Bonita
ceqa-128d8dc08fd75cf88e.description: The project consists of a Right of Entry Permit with the Bonita Historical Society for temporary use of a 17,700 square-foot portion of an existing parking lot in front of Bonita Museum and Cultural Center for hosting the Taste of Bonita community event. The parking lot would be used on Saturday, September 19, 2026, from 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. No improvements are proposed.

ceqa-482622f6580c4aa333.name: Bridge Deck Repairs on I-5
ceqa-482622f6580c4aa333.description: A bridge deck maintenance project at 15 bridges on interstate 5 in San Diego County. Project work includes application and placement of Methacrylate and Polyester Concrete overlay, replacing joint seals, cold planing existing bridge deck and placing Hot Mix Asphalt-A for 14 locations. After the completion of the above work, the bridge decks shall be re-striped. One bridge location on 17th street ramp overcrossing shall have beneath-the-deck repairs only, consisting of girders repair.

ceqa-a91f30678618212576.name: Remove and Replace Concrete Median Barriers, Install Signs on SR-76
ceqa-a91f30678618212576.projectTitle: Remove and Replace Concrete Median Barriers, Install Signs on SR-76
ceqa-a91f30678618212576.description: Caltrans proposes to prevent wrong way entrances onto SR 76. The area of concern is in San Diego County along SR 76 from PM R16.4 to R16.9. Caltrans will upgrade of 24 linear feet (LF) of center median barrier and removal of existing signs and installation of new signs is to increase visibility of prohibited movement and prevent further incidents. Caltrans proposes to remove 24 LF of existing 36” high center median barrier and replace with 48” high CB (Type 60PR) with a 10” footing. This barrier is natural color concrete. Caltrans will install Do Not Enter/Wrong Way Sign Packages at various locations and on barrier. Construction Area signs will be installed, and Temporary K-rail will be placed per standard specs and plans. Ground disturbance per standard plans (awaiting confirmation) 3’-6” and 5’ depth potential at 4”x4” and 6”x6”. Potential vegetation trimming to ensure visibility of newly installed signs, or no vegetation trimming at all. Potential vegetation removal or trimming on EB direction to provide appropriate visibility for installed sign. Road Work Ahead and End Road Work construction signs will be installed before and after work zone in center medians. See attached exhibit for approximate sign locations and package amounts. Posts in center median will be barrier mounted. Two new posts will be installed on each direction for a total of four posts. Assumed depth is 3’-6” and 5’ for the posts that are 4”x4” and 6”x6”.

ceqa-41f9531447ed5c24f4.name: First Amndmnt to the Ground Lease Disp. Agrmnt between the City of San Diego and 101 Ash Venture LP, a California Limited Partnership re the City owned property
ceqa-41f9531447ed5c24f4.projectTitle: First Amndmnt to the Ground Lease Disp. Agrmnt between the City of San Diego and 101 Ash Venture LP, a California Limited Partnership re the City owned property
ceqa-41f9531447ed5c24f4.description: City of San Diego City Council (City Council) approval of the First Amendment to the Ground Lease Disposition Agreement (First Amendment) between the City of San Diego (City) and 101 Ash Venture LP (Developer) for the redevelopment of the City-owned property located at 107 Ash Street, formerly designated as 101 Ash Street (Property), into a mixed-use affordable housing project (Project) and making related findings regarding the fulfillment of economic opportunity objectives consistent with Government Code section 52201. The First Amendment updates the previously approved transaction documents to align with the Project's updated development program and financing structure, specifically HUD financing requirements, and to facilitate all requirements necessary to close escrow and commence redevelopment of the Property. Key modifications include extending the Ground Lease term from 60 to 65 years and corresponding affordability requirements; revisions to the Ground Lease and City Promissory Note necessary to accommodate the Project's financing and closing requirements; and increasing the Project from 250 to 252 residential units consisting of 249 affordable units and three (3) unrestricted manager's units.

ceqa-cf24b55a0f38891e63.projectTitle: Pavement Rehab Northbound Offramp to Via Rancho Parkway on I-15
ceqa-cf24b55a0f38891e63.description: Caltrans proposes Off Ramp Pavement Rehabilitation in the City of Escondido on northbound I-15 Via Rancho Parkway Off-ramp at post mile 26.728. All work is within the existing ramp pavement and no staging location.

ceqa-192ac0b23f15de6faa.name: Install Rumble Bars on I-905 in San Diego County
ceqa-192ac0b23f15de6faa.projectTitle: Install Rumble Bars on I-905 in San Diego County
ceqa-192ac0b23f15de6faa.description: Caltrans proposes to place raised rumble bars in San Diego County in Otay Mesa on eastbound SR-905 from Airway Road undercrossing to the Otay Mesa Port of Entry. The raised rumble bars are used to attract the drivers' attention and to alert them of traffic slowdown or stoppage. Project work consists of placing raised rumble bars in nine (9) locations with the rumble bars placed across the lanes of the travel way. All work is within the state right of way and there is no staging location.

ceqa-704a236ad1c4ab4004.name: Starlight Solar Major Use Permit
ceqa-704a236ad1c4ab4004.description: The Starlight Solar Project consists of a Major Use Permit (MUP) and Fire Protection and Mitigation Agreement for the construction and operation of a 100 megawatt (MW) solar photovoltaic energy generation facility with 217.4 MW of battery energy storage on approximately 588 acres. Phase one of the project consists of development of approximately 20 MW of solar generation and 17.4 MW of battery energy storage on approximately 125 acres. Phase two consists of development of approximately 80 MW of solar generation and 200 MW of battery energy storage on approximately 456 acres. The project includes photovoltaic modules mounted on support structures, inverter and transformer platforms, battery storage facilities, an on-site collector substation, a transmission line to connect the project to the existing SDG&E Boulevard Substation, consisting primarily of underground facilities with a short overhead segment, internal access and fire roads, fencing, fuel modification zones, six water tanks for fire protection, and associated site infrastructure to support the solar energy generation and storage facility. PDS2022-MUP-22-010; PDS2022-ER-22-21-002
ceqa-704a236ad1c4ab4004.crossStreets: South of Interstate 8 and Old Highway 80, east of Tierra del Sol Road and Along Jewel Valley Ro

ceqa-4454697b564d02c16d.name: City of Poway Treated Water Facilities & Redundant Pipeline Project
ceqa-4454697b564d02c16d.projectTitle: City of Poway Treated Water Facilities & Redundant Pipeline Project
ceqa-4454697b564d02c16d.description: The Project proposes new water facilities to replace and abandon existing water facilities and provide treated water to the City. Specifically, the City of Poway would construct a transmission pipeline with associated vaults within Espola Road and Lake Poway Road, a new booster pump station, a forebay tank, piping between the pump station/forebay tank and existing clearwells, a sodium hypochlorite system, and a surge tank. In addition, the existing pump station approximately 700 feet east of the Espola Road intersection on the south side of Lake Poway Road would be demolished. As part of the Project, the San Diego County Water Authority would construct a new Flow Control Facility (FCF) at the Project’s connection to the Ramona Pipeline.

ceqa-74168f5017942dbdb7.name: 12th and Imperial Station Digital Wayfinding
ceqa-74168f5017942dbdb7.description: On August 2, 2023, MTS awarded its Agreement for Master Concessionaire Services (G2653.0-23) to BriceHouse Station, LLC ("Master Concessionaire") to provide professional concession and advertising services to the general public at all Trolley and Transit Stations. The Master Concessionaire contract authorizes Master Concessionaire to execute license agreements with third-party vendors. On March 26, 2026, MTS through Master Concessionaire, executed a Vendor License Agreement with Big Outdoor Opco, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Big Outdoor") to modernize three MTS transit stations, including the 12th and Imperial Station, by providing MTS customers and transit riders with wayfinding and informational messaging. On August 21, 2026, MTS, through Master Concessionaire, executed the First Amendment to the Vendor License Agreement with Big Outdoor to modify the dimensions of the digital information boards at 12th and Imperial Station to increase the size of the overall structure and displays ("Project"). The Project location is located on MTS property and will improve customer information and wayfinding for transit riders by dedicating display time for wayfinding and informational messaging such as train schedules and special transit-ridership promotions. Further, the displays at the Project location will include a static MTS transit map that will not change with the rotating digital screen copy. The transit map will provide an additional wayfinding resource to transit riders. The Project is statutorily and categorically exempt from environmental review under the California Environmental Quality Act, as further explained below. The Project location will have two one-sided digital displays oriented in a "V" shape with an overall structure size of approximately 14 feet, 2 inches wide by 28 feet tall, with each digital display measuring approximately 12 feet wide by 18 feet, 0.75 inches tall. The area occupied by the digital information boards will not exceed a total area of 5,000 square feet. The Project also includes an additional static MTS transit map display solely for MTS use as a supplemental project design feature to further enhance transit related messaging, wayfinding and leverage the larger digital information board. The Project may display digital messaging between the hours of 5:00am and 12:00am each day. The Project has significant benefits for transit riders and for the surrounding community. It will allow MTS to promote its transit services; provide wayfinding information for the surrounding entertainment area; share information about upcoming events in the local community; post Public Service Announcements, Amber Alerts and other public safety messages; provide a unique advertising location to attract other events that help the local economy; and generate additional revenue to support public transit operations in MTS's service area.

ceqa-7647c4cb1f0cd93696.name: Copley Park Division Digital Information Board Project
ceqa-7647c4cb1f0cd93696.projectTitle: Copley Park Division Digital Information Board Project
ceqa-7647c4cb1f0cd93696.description: On September 17, 2026, San Diego Metropolitan Transit System (“MTS”) Board of Directors authorized the Chief Executive Officer to execute a License Agreement with Clear Channel Outdoor, LLC (“CCO”) to design, construct, operate, and maintain a double-sided digital information board on MTS owned property at the Copley Park Division facility adjacent to State Route 52 (“Project”). The agreement provides for an initial term of 20 years, with two additional five-year renewal options that could extend the total term to 30 years. The digital display is anticipated to include approximately 672 square feet of advertising area on each display face, with an overall structure height of approximately 60 to 70 feet. The final location, size, and design of the structure will be subject to MTS review and approval during the design process. The total area occupied by the project will not exceed 5,000 square feet of MTS property. Under the agreement, CCO will be responsible for all costs associated with project development, including design, permitting, construction, operation, maintenance, utilities, insurance, technology upgrades, and eventual removal of the structure. CCO will also be required to periodically modernize the digital display technology to ensure the facility remains consistent with generally accepted industry standards. At the end of the agreement term, or upon earlier termination, CCO will be responsible for removing the structure and restoring the property. The agreement reserves dedicated display time for MTS communication needs. MTS will receive one dedicated eight-second advertising slot during each rotation cycle on one display face, together with additional display time on the second face on an as-available basis. This display time may be used for: • Transit promotional messages • Service alerts • Wayfinding messages • Ridership promotions • MTS partner and stakeholder messages • Special event information • Emergency notifications • Public safety agency information • Amber alerts • Other transit-related communications. Because of the project's proximity to State Route 52, the display will operate in accordance with applicable Caltrans requirements. Advertising content will be limited to static digital images, and full-motion advertising will not be permitted. The display will utilize LED technology equipped with automatic dimming controls that adjust brightness levels based on ambient lighting conditions. All advertising content displayed on the structure must comply with MTS Board Policy 21 governing revenue-generating advertising. The agreement is structured to provide MTS with both guaranteed and performance-based revenue while allowing the agency to leverage privately funded infrastructure to expand customer information, emergency communications, and transit-related messaging. The project will create a prominent regional communications platform while generating a new source of non-fare revenue to support the agency's long-term financial sustainability.

ceqa-e415d4dfcb4a6e5bf1.name: Repair of Two Existing Mooring Dolphins by Maritime Museum at North Embarcadero
ceqa-e415d4dfcb4a6e5bf1.projectTitle: Repair of Two Existing Mooring Dolphins by Maritime Museum at North Embarcadero
ceqa-e415d4dfcb4a6e5bf1.description: The proposed project is for the repair of two existing mooring dolphins located within the Maritime Museum of San Diego leasehold at 1492 N Harbor Drive, San Diego, CA 92101, adjacent to the North Embarcadero Promenade. The two mooring dolphins were originally built in the 1980s and consist of four 18-inch steel piles supporting a concrete deck. The decks have a mooring cleat located on the top and pad eye located on the face of the deck. Each dolphin has a 12-inch diameter fender stanchion on the north side to provide support for the ferry Berkeley during mooring. Guide piles anchored on the south faces of the dolphins support a floating dock that runs from the North Embarcadero to the west end of the Berkeley. An above-water and underwater inspection conducted by Simpson, Gumpertz & Heger, Inc. and L3 Engineering on January 22, 2026, found that the east and west mooring dolphins are in need of repair due to damage that has significantly reduced the load-carrying capacities of the dolphins. The inspection recommended repairs should be performed with reasonable urgency. Work would occur above, at and below the waterline but would not extend to the bay floor. The heaviest corrosion occupies a band approximately 4 ft high beginning about 4.5 ft below the deck soffit and the piles below the waterline exhibit only minor coating loss and shallow pitting. However, cleaning and jacket installation would occur along 20 ft of the piles. Specific work to complete the proposed project would include the following: Pile Repairs • Mobilize a dive spread, floating work platforms, crew, materials and containment to the Museum and complete all safety and access submittals. • Mechanically clean the top 20 linear feet of each of the eight piles to remove marine growth, corrosion by-product, loose scale and other bond inhibiting material over the full circumference, to the extent of the jacket. • Furnish and install steel reinforcing cages around each pile in accordance with FX-70 installation details, positioned to span the deteriorated band and develop into sound steel above and below it. • Install 24 inch inside diameter Denso SeaShield FX-70 FRP jackets on stand-offs, close the tongue and groove seam and seal the top and bottom of the annulus. Jackets would not extend to the bay floor. • Pump the annular space full of SeaShield underwater grout, verify complete fill and finish the top bevel seal. • Clean up and remove all debris and packaging generated by the repairs. Steel Bracing Replacement Above the Waterline • Remove the corroded fender stanchion bracing at Piles 1-B and 2-B on both dolphins and replace in kind. • Remove the failed and corroded floating dock guide connections and walers at Piles 1-A and 2-A on both dolphins and replace in kind. • All replacement steel to be hot dip galvanized (equivalent to the existing) with stainless steel fasteners. All work would be performed over water from the existing floating dock and a 20-foot x 20-foot floating work platform, which would be moored to the existing floating dock at the facility; no other vessels would be moored at the site. Temporary Construction Best Management Practices (BMPs) would be implemented to protect water quality throughout the duration of the repair activities as follows: • Equipment-specific secondary containment. The grout mixing and pumping station would be set within a portable spill containment berm on the deck of the floating work platform, with drip pans or containment trays beneath the mixer, pump and all powered equipment. Containment would be provided at the source - at each piece of equipment and material - so that no runoff reaches the deck edge or the water. • Closed placement system. All mixed grout would be pumped directly from the mixer into the sealed FX-70 jacket annulus through fitted pumping ports. The jackets would be closed forms with bottom seals in place before pumping begins; no grout is placed into open water. • Material handling. Bagged grout and epoxy components would be staged on spill containment pallets on the floating work platform and kept covered until use. • Equipment washout. Mixer and tool washout would be collected in a watertight washout container on the platform and disposed of upland. No washout or rinse water would be discharged to the bay. • Spill response. A spill kit would be maintained on the floating work platform, and no fueling would be performed over water. • Housekeeping. All debris and packaging generated by the work would be collected daily and removed from the site. The platform deck would be cleaned at the end of each shift. • Personal protective equipment. All team members would wear the proper personal protective equipment for the task in accordance with the job hazard analysis, including USCG-approved work vests for personnel working over water. The contractor would inspect the BMP-related equipment each morning before operations begin and would replace containment berms, trays and pallets as required to maintain effective containment. These BMPs would be temporary construction measures and would be removed at demobilization. The repair described above would be a structural repair that would restore load path across the deteriorated section of each pile rather than simply coating or protecting what remains. This repair would return the dolphins to service for a minimum of ten additional years. The Museum would remain open and the floating dock would remain in public use throughout the repair process. All work would be performed from the existing floating dock and from punts - small floating work platforms - positioned alongside the dolphins. No vessels would be moored or operated at the site and no berthing or vessel staging would be required. The contractor would occupy only a portion of the dock width at any one time and would maintain a clear, continuous pedestrian route past the work area for the duration of the proposed project. Public access along the floating dock would remain open. The work area would be delineated and controlled at all times and all equipment, hoses, umbilicals and materials would be kept clear of the pedestrian route. Construction would take approximately (10) days and would commence in October 2026. All work would be performed during daytime working hours, Monday through Friday. Daily start times would be coordinated with the Museum to suit dock operations, events and visitor traffic. Work would take place during the daytime only, Monday through Friday. Daily start times would be coordinated with the Museum to accommodate dock operations, events and visitor traffic. All in-water work would be performed by a surface-supplied commercial dive team under the direction of a California Registered Civil Engineer, who would be on site as required to verify conditions as exposed and to accept each pile before the jacket is closed. Field operations would be contingent upon safe weather, sea state, tide, current, underwater visibility and diving conditions. Due to its nature and limited scope, construction of the proposed project would generate a minor amount of vehicle trips and would require limited use of equipment. Therefore, impacts related to air quality, greenhouse gas emissions, and transportation and traffic are not anticipated to occur. Furthermore, the Applicant would be responsible for complying with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding construction demolition debris, hazards and hazardous materials, and stormwater.

ceqa-6c78892e0a98016581.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-6c78892e0a98016581.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to Salk Institute for Biological Studies (EPA ID# CAD078731668) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, 10 milliliters of perchloric acid and one (1) 25-gram container of 1-hydroxybenzotriazole hydrate must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at the Salk Institute for Biological Studies located at 10010 N. Torrey Pines Road, La Jolla, California 92037. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued for Veolia Environmental Services (Veolia) to chemically stabilize the hazardous waste prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site. Background: Shock and/or temperature sensitive materials can decompose or detonate with external energy when dry or concentrated. If the material is improperly handled, there is a potential for a reaction, which includes fire, deflagration, or detonation. Due to the presence of temperature/shock sensitive materials, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilization is recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Project Activities: The treatment of these hazardous wastes involves the addition of a solution to the containers in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemicals. Treatment will take place within a designated exclusion zone. Only technicians from Veolia will be allowed in the exclusion zone. Movement, preparation, and treatment of the containers will be in accordance with established standards. Within 10 business days of the expiration of this permit, Salk Institute for Biological Sciences will submit a final report, signed in accordance with Title 22, CCR Sec. 66270.11(d). The report shall include certification that the treatment area has been cleared of all residual hazardous waste generated from this emergency treatment and all generated waste has been properly managed. The Emergency Permit is effective beginning September 10, 2026, and shall expire on November 9, 2026.

ceqa-0d97425bda5b3f8d8e.name: Addendum to the Final Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Loveland Reservoir Fishing Relocation Project- Loveland Reservoir Trail Safety Improvements Project
ceqa-0d97425bda5b3f8d8e.description: The Final 1996 Mitigated Negative Declaration evaluated the relocation of public fishing access from U.S. Forest Service land to Sweetwater Authority (Authority) property on the eastern portion of Loveland Reservoir. To maintain public access, the Authority granted the Forest Service an easement encompassing a parking area, reservoir access trail, and a 50-foot wide shoreline strip above the high-water mark. The relocation project included construction of turn lanes from Japatul Road and a 0.78-acre graded parking area accommodating approximately 50 vehicles. Additional improvements included installation of trash receptacles, restrooms, informational trailhead signage, and erosion control measures along the access trail. A portion of the California Riding and Hiking Trail was also realigned to avoid conflicts with the new driveway, while planning for future amenities including expanded restroom facilities and a floating pedestrian bridge. Sweetwater Authority is now proposing safety-oriented improvements along the existing trail network to enhance public safety, improve trail stability, and maintain long-term recreational access. The existing trail contains narrow segments, steep drop-offs, eroded surfaces, and informal user-created paths that present safety concerns and contribute to disturbance of adjacent vegetation and habitat. In some locations, recreationists currently use branches, fallen tree trunks, or logs to cross a drainage channel or travel through vegetated areas, potentially exposing users to hazards such as unstable footing, falls, snakes, poison oak, ticks, and other trail-related risks. The proposed Project would include general trail safety and stabilization improvements, installation of a pedestrian bridge at the drainage crossing, and construction of a small observation deck adjacent to the existing trail alignment. The observation deck would provide a designated elevated vantage point for scenic viewing, wildlife observation, exercise, and passive recreation. Collectively, these improvements are intended to provide safer and more clearly defined recreational access within the existing trail vicinity while minimizing informal travel through surrounding areas.
ceqa-0d97425bda5b3f8d8e.crossStreets: Japatul Road, approx. 0.6 miles east of the intersection of Japatul Rd and Sequan Truck Trail

ceqa-29dc38066907656e81.name: EMERGENCY BLUFF STABILIZATION NORTH OF ENCINAS CREEK BRIDGE ON THE WEST SIDE OF CARLSBAD BOULEVARD
ceqa-29dc38066907656e81.projectTitle: EMERGENCY BLUFF STABILIZATION NORTH OF ENCINAS CREEK BRIDGE ON THE WEST SIDE OF CARLSBAD BOULEVARD
ceqa-29dc38066907656e81.description: The project involves the Declaration of Local Emergency and completion of emergency bluff stabilization work along the west side of southbound Carlsbad Boulevard, north of the Encinas Creek Bridge. City staff identified coastal bluff erosion on June 25, 2026, and subsequently observed minor changes in pavement cracking along the roadway shoulder. A Sept. 8, 2026, geotechnical technical memorandum identified active ongoing bluff retreat with the potential for additional, unpredictable instability with little to no warning, threatening the integrity of southbound Carlsbad Boulevard and creating a risk to public safety, coastal access, and roadway infrastructure. Emergency stabilization consists of extending the existing rock revetment approximately 192 feet north through placement of approximately 4- to 8-ton rock rip-rap along the affected bluff. The work may extend into an additional approximately 65-foot portion of the bluff if necessary to address field conditions and stabilize the affected area. The work is limited to that necessary to stabilize the bluff, maintain the continued operation of southbound Carlsbad Boulevard, and prevent or mitigate further erosion and roadway damage. The city has submitted an application to the California Coastal Commission for an Emergency Coastal Development Permit for the emergency work.

ceqa-ab5df2c711cd797365.name: Oceanside Sewer Improvements Program (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SDO-64984-R5)
ceqa-ab5df2c711cd797365.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMSSDO-64984-R5 pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602 to the City of Oceanside. The Project is limited to the construction, installation, replacement, and rehabilitation of underground wastewater conveyance infrastructure. The Project will install 1) approximately 15,000 feet of the 36-inch Oceanside Mesa Garrison (OMG) Force Main, 2) 10,000 feet of the 24-inch Mission Avenue Lift Station (MALS) Force Main, 3) 700 feet of new 22-inch HDPE Bypass Pipeline, 4) 1,500 feet of a new 24-inch gravity main pipeline, 5) 1,000 feet of 24-inch diameter gravity sewer with inverted siphon crossing beneath Garrison Creek, and 6) construction of the new El Corazon Lift Station (ECLS). Project activities include vegetation trimming and clearing, grubbing, grading, trenching, excavation of concrete-lined and earthen channel material, and pipeline improvements mentioned above. The majority of the pipelines will be installed using conventional cut-and-cover methods. Trenchless installation methods will be employed where the pipeline crosses beneath the San Luis Rey River, an existing concrete drainage channel north of the City’s Mission Basin Groundwater Purification Facility (MBGPF), the Caltrans right-of-way (ROW) at State Highway 76 and Mission Avenue, and the portion of the pipeline extending northwest from Garrison Street to the new ECLS.

The project is subject to the Limited Agricultural (A70) Use Regulations of the Zoning Ordinance, and to the Semi-Rural Residential (SR-10) General Plan Land Use Designation and Semi-Rural Regional Category area of the General Plan. Legal access to the site will be provided by a driveway connected to Mountain Meadow Road, an existing county-maintained public road approximately 1-mile east of Interstate Highway I-15.

ceqa-0117db26a840d7dc97.name: York Drive Senior Living
ceqa-0117db26a840d7dc97.description: The project consists of a Major Use Permit and a Certificate of Compliance for merging of lots for a 183-unit deed-restricted senior living development on an approximately 4.27-acre property. The Major Use Permit would authorize the construction of a four-story senior living development in a single main building. The proposed building is approximately 46-feet tall and each floor ranges in size from approximately 34,233 square feet to 34,762 square feet. The development will include amenities for the residents such as a library and a community kitchen primarily on the first floor. The majority of units will be distributed through the second, third, and fourth floors. The remaining portions of the project site include a parking lot, landscaping, signage, and stormwater and drainage facilities. The project will include widening of York Drive along the project frontage to accommodate a longer turn lane onto South Santa Fe. The project will result in the replacement of a bench with a shelter at a nearby North County Transit District bus stop along South Santa Fe Avenue as well as repainting of the existing crosswalk at the intersection of South Santa Fe Avenue and York Drive. The project will also include offsite sewer improvements including replacement and upsizing of sewer lines along and near portions of El Valle Opulento. The Zoning Use Regulation of the site is Rural Residential (RR). The General Plan Designation for the Site is Village Residential (VR-2) and the General Plan Regional Category for the site is Village. The project is located on an approximately 4.27-acre site near 1822-1864 York Drive within the North County Metropolitan Subregional Planning Area. The project has been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act and a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) was prepared for the project and circulated for public review. Project Name and Number(s): PDS2021-MUP-21-008; PDS2021-CC-21-0120; LOG NO. PDS2021-ER-21-08-008
ceqa-0117db26a840d7dc97.crossStreets: Southeast Corner of York Drive and South Santa Fe Ave Intersection

The project proposes to permit a previously constructed rear-yard retaining wall that is up to five feet in height, and a deck; to remove a portion of the existing retaining wall that is within an existing drainage easement; to add a custom pool, spa and stormwater improvements; and to revegetate the area below the existing deck. The project also includes a Multiple Species Conservation Program, Multi-Habitat Planning Area boundary line correction to remove areas from the City's planned conservation area that were previously developed. The 0.52-acre project site located at 5004 Hastings Roa dis zoned Residential Single Unit (RS-1-1 and RS-1-7) and Open Space- Residential (OR-1-1), and designated Open Space and Residential in the Mid-City: Kensington - Talmadge Community Plan area. Additionally, the project site is within the Airport Land Use Compatibility Overlay Zone (Montgomery Field), parking Standards Transit Priority Area, Transit Priority Area, Affordable Housing Parking Demand (High), Airport Land Use Compatibility Plan Airport Influence Area (Montgomery Field - Review Area 2), Federal Aviation Administration Part 77 Noticing Area (Montgomery Field), and the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. ceqa-d2f38e2b8dc77fffed.name: Ramona Boutique Hotel
ceqa-d2f38e2b8dc77fffed.description: The project is a Site Plan and Lot Merger application for the development of a two-story, 101-room boutique hotel on approximately 3.3 acres in the unincorporated community of Ramona. The project site consists of three parcels (APNs 282-141-32, 282-141-33, and 282-141-34), which would be consolidated into a single legal parcel through a Lot Merger. The site has a General Commercial land use designation and is within the RM-V4 District of the Ramona Village Center Form-Based Code. Existing structures and improvements would be demolished to accommodate the project. The proposed development would include approximately 60,327 square feet of gross building area and would include 101 guest rooms, a lobby and breakfast area, fitness room, guest laundry, meeting/event space, outdoor courtyard and deck, swimming pool, and associated guest-service areas. The project would provide 102 parking spaces, including electric-vehicle infrastructure and bicycle parking. The hotel would operate 24 hours per day, seven days per week, and is anticipated to employ approximately 18 employees. Vehicular access would be provided by two commercial driveways from Main Street/State Route 67; no access is proposed from Vermont Street. Main Street frontage improvements would include a ten-foot-wide decomposed granite trail and would be designed to preserve and avoid disturbance to the historic eucalyptus trees. On-site improvements would include internal circulation and fire access, landscaping, utilities, and stormwater facilities. Water and sewer service would be provided by the Ramona Municipal Water District, and electrical service would be provided by San Diego Gas & Electric.
ceqa-d2f38e2b8dc77fffed.crossStreets: Fronting Main Street/State Route 67 between Vermont Street and Letton Street

ceqa-3bd959ea73fb4344d8.description: A Conditional Use Permit (CUP) and Planned Development Permit (PDP) to modify an existing Wireless Communication Facility (WCF) located at 12227 Spring Canyon Road in the RS-1-8 (Residential-Single Unit) zone within the Scripps Miramar Ranch Community Plan area, and City Council District 5. ceqa-557f4cf6f51fa641ae.name: Socially Equitable Cannabis Program
ceqa-557f4cf6f51fa641ae.description: The Socially Equitable Cannabis Program (SECP) allows for new cannabis facilities in the unincorporated areas of the county, including cultivation, distribution, manufacturing, microbusiness, retail, on-site consumption lounges, temporary cannabis events, and testing laboratories. The action taken by the San Diego County Board of Supervisors (Board) on August 19, 2026 included certification of a Program Environmental Impact Report, adoption of a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program, and Findings/Statement of Overriding Considerations, adoption of amendments to the San Diego County Zoning Ordinance, first reading of the amendments to the County Code of Regulatory Ordinances, as well as first reading of the Social Equity Program, adoption of a Board policy related to minimum funding requirements for enforcement, and the first reading of the associated licensing and permitting fees. This action by the Board on September 2, 2026 included the second reading and formal adoption of amendments to the Regulatory Code, Social Equity Program, and licensing and permitting fees, fully implementing the SECP.

ceqa-c8117ff158af23c184.name: San Diego Mesa College Comprehensive Master Plan
ceqa-c8117ff158af23c184.projectTitle: San Diego Mesa College Comprehensive Master Plan
ceqa-c8117ff158af23c184.description: The project proposes improvements across the approximately 106-acre Mesa College campus. The projects would generally demolish existing aging facilities on the campus and replace them with more modern facilities that would accommodate existing programming. The CMP is conceptual in nature and project designs are expected to be refined during future planning and design phases. The Athletics Complex and the Performing Arts and Administration Center and Parking Structure projects are anticipated to be designed and constructed in the near term. Remaining campus-wide and long-term projects in the CMP include classroom and office spaces; on-campus housing; relocation of the high school, facility services, and child development center; a community clinic; and circulation and utility improvements. The near-term projects are analyzed at the project level in the PEIR, while campus-wide and long-term improvements and analyzed at the program level. Refer to the Draft PEIR for a complete project description.

ceqa-686019b6a6240ea040.name: Launching the County of San Diego’s Tijuana River Capture and Cleanup Initiative (Districts: All)
ceqa-686019b6a6240ea040.projectTitle: Launching the County of San Diego’s Tijuana River Capture and Cleanup Initiative (Districts: All)
ceqa-686019b6a6240ea040.description: The proposed activity consists of allocating funding and conducting administrative and organizational actions necessary to initiate Phase 1 of the Tijuana River Capture and Cleanup Initiative. These actions include allocating and transferring $1,800,000 to support project evaluation and development; utilizing and amending existing Department of Public Works as-needed consultant contracts to provide adequate capacity for engineering analyses, alternatives development, and pre-design work; and initiating coordination with partner agencies on preliminary planning, environmental review, permitting pathways, and other foundational components needed to identify and advance a future treatment and capture system on the U.S. side of the Tijuana River.
