ceqa-efb27cbb64a19316da.name: FIFRA Section 18 Specific Emergency Exemption: Use of Clethodim in Rice to Control Weedy Red Rice
ceqa-efb27cbb64a19316da.projectTitle: FIFRA Section 18 Specific Emergency Exemption: Use of Clethodim in Rice to Control Weedy Red Rice
ceqa-efb27cbb64a19316da.description: This specific exemption request is necessary to reduce losses by the California rice industry due to a continued infestation of weedy red rice in cultivated rice fields. Multiple factors are contributing to the emergency situation, including the absence of commercially viable control methods and the pest’s taxonomic similarity to the main crop, which hinders effective segregation and eradication of weedy red rice. Currently, there are no effective herbicides available that allow spot treatments to safely kill weedy rice. The accepted cultural practices available to growers such as fallowing and roguing are also cost prohibitive, making them unsuitable for growers to rely upon long term without incurring further economic hardship.

ceqa-d8442a8474c31c30bf.name: Nevada Cement Company LLC Stockton Terminal Modernization Project
ceqa-d8442a8474c31c30bf.projectTitle: Nevada Cement Company LLC Stockton Terminal Modernization Project
ceqa-d8442a8474c31c30bf.description: The proposed project entails modification of Nevada Cement Company LLC's existing lease and modernization of its bulk cementitious-material receiving and distribution terminal at 205 Port Road 1 in the Port of Stockton's East Complex. The leasehold would increase from approximately 4.92 acres to approximately 10.98 acres. Proposed improvements include rehabilitation of Berth 3/4; installation of a new enclosed ship unloader and conveyance system; replacement of Bunkers 6 and 7 with a new storage dome; upgrades to truck and rail loading systems; rail, civil, and utility improvements; and installation of infrastructure at Berth 2 to support future barge loading. The improvements would increase unloading efficiency and storage and loading capacity while remaining within the terminal's existing permitted throughput limits. Construction would occur in phases over approximately 2 to 5 years, with terminal operations continuing during construction.

ceqa-1be94463720506f8c4.name: 826826_45200001_PGE_UGS
ceqa-1be94463720506f8c4.description: PG&E plans to rework two wells to meet CalGEM Underground Gas Storage inspection and construction requirements as specified in 14 CCR § 1726. The proposed scope of work includes the following activities: retrieve existing tubing string and packer, retrieve production liner, perform casing integrity wireline surveys, replace existing wellhead, install new production liner and gravel pack, and install new tubing string and packer. The proposed project will require, at a minimum, the following equipment: workover rig (double), mud pumps, cuttings bin, blowout prevention equipment and accumulator, generator, fuel tanks, fluid tanks, and light towers. All equipment will be staged and operated within the existing facility footprint and existing roadways will be used for access. This includes all ancillary equipment which may be required such as pump trucks, vac trucks, and casing storage. No new surface construction activities are planned with the rework. No new permanent facilities will be constructed and no expansion to associated facilities or roadways will be required. The project is anticipated to last from May to November 2026. The well will be returned to service as a gas storage well with no change or expansion of existing use. Waste material will be properly disposed of as non-hazardous or hazardous waste at a facility licensed to accept the waste. Secondary containment will be utilized for liquid HazMat's and workover fluids. No erosion controls will be required as these sites are all graveled. Water will be applied as mitigation for dust suppression from vehicle traffic. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving 1 permit(s) for Pacific Gas and Electric Company (P0300) to rework the well(s) listed below, in the McDonald Island Gas Oil Field in San Joaquin County. API # Well Name 0407720241 Whiskey Slough 13-W

ceqa-1f6ca587f8bc94b287.name: DWR Ponds – Vegetation Maintenance
ceqa-1f6ca587f8bc94b287.description: DWR will contract with ruminant grazers for the purpose of vegetation control. Ruminant grazing contractors will erect temporary, lowvoltage electrified fencing with signage and will use ruminants to graze parcels. An estimated 221 acres will be grazed. Additionally, DWR may use an industrial mower, weed whackers, and hand tools to mow the vegetation that the ruminant grazers are not able to graze, due to unsafe consumption of certain plants.

ceqa-60db9b1adb5d0b4289.name: Conditional Use Permit No. PA-2500420
ceqa-60db9b1adb5d0b4289.description: A Conditional Use Permit to establish the use type Renewable Energy – Utility-Scale Solar Energy System. The project proposes a ground mount solar system on approximately 18.5-acres of an approximately 20-acre parcel that will be built over a period of 3-years. The project will generate up to 4 megawatts (MW) of alternating current (AC) energy and will interconnect to Pacific Gas and Electric Company’s (PG&E) pre-existing electrical distribution system adjacent to the site along the northwest boundary. The power generated from this facility will be sold to PG&E. The project site is classified as Prime Farmland. All solar equipment will be mounted on driven steel piers rather than slab foundations, avoiding soil compaction and facilitating full restoration of agricultural use at the end of the project’s operational life. Vegetation will be maintained under and between the solar rows using a drought-tolerant, pollinator-friendly seed mix to promote soil stability, reduce erosion, and maintain soil health throughout the system’s life.

ceqa-3bd343bd9069f99a2e.name: JOC 2026 Odell Avenue Emergency Approach Repairs
ceqa-3bd343bd9069f99a2e.projectTitle: JOC 2026 Odell Avenue Emergency Approach Repairs
ceqa-3bd343bd9069f99a2e.description: JOC 2026 ODELL AVENUE EMERGENCY APPROACH REPAIRS Project Description Project Location: Odell Avenue: San Joaquin County Bridge 29C-098 North approach. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: The structure of the roadway and bridge have been compromised due to undermining at the northern Abutment which has exposed the Abutment piles and the underside of the Abutment. As a result, the roadway subbase is washing under the Abutment creating voids underneath the roadway leaving the northern approach at risk of failure. Scope of Work: To remediate the roadway and bridge Abutment at San Joaquin County bridge 29C-098. Reconstruction duties include but are not limited to: 1. Digging out and reconstructing the north approach under both lanes. 2. Reconstructing roadway with a concrete slurry sub-base and placing Aggregate Base (AB) lifts before capping the road with 0.25 feet of Asphalt Concrete (AC). 3. Installing 18 inches minus Rock Slope Protection (RSP) and grout under the bridge at Abutment 4. All aspects of installation must meet the approval of San Joaquin County Bridge Engineering and must be performed in accordance with San Joaquin County Public Works Job Order Contracting (JOC) standards and procedures. Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily residential with single family homes. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with this well-maintained bridge. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-d67f37a3fd986a7dfa.name: River Road Resurfacing 2027
ceqa-d67f37a3fd986a7dfa.description: RIVER ROAD RESURFACING 2027 Project Description Project Location: River Road: 1,200 feet east of McHenry Avenue to Henry Road. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: The original roadway of River Road from McHenry Avenue to Santa Fe Road was constructed in 1928 with 2 inches of oil rock and 4 inches of gravel. In 1974, the road from Santa Fe Road to Henry Road was constructed with 2 inches of Asphalt Concrete (AC). In 1973, the road was reconstructed from McHenry Avenue to Harrold Avenue with 0.25 feet of AC over 0.35 feet of Aggregate Base (AB). In 1975, the road was reconstructed from Harrold Avenue to Santa Fe Road with 0.25 feet of AC over 0.45 feet of AB. The road from McHenry Avenue to Santa Fe Road was resurfaced with 0.25 feet of AC in 2003. The road from McHenry Avenue to 1,187 feet east of McHenry Avenue was resurfaced in 2017. The existing roadway has been maintained with periodic chip seals with the most recent chip seal in 2022. The existing pavement in the project location consists of some rutting and transverse, longitudinal, and edge cracking throughout the project limits. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Resurfacing existing roadway on River Road (32 feet wide from 1,200 feet east of McHenry Avenue to Santa Fe Road and 25 feet wide from Santa Fe Road to Henry Road) with 0.25 Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA) (Type A). 2. Repairing pavement structural failure areas with full depth 0.50 feet of HMA (Type A). 3. Replenishing 4 feet wide Shoulder Backing: 2 feet (8%) and 2 feet to conform. 4. Applying Penetration Treatment at all intersection radii plus 50 feet or to conform. 5. Constructing HMA (Type A) driveways. 6. Adjusting monument frames and covers. Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily agricultural. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with this well-maintained road. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-614c9252301afb7f26.name: East Lathrop Stormwater Master Plan
ceqa-614c9252301afb7f26.description: Although never formally adopted, the draft 2006 Storm Drainage Master Plan remains the City's most recent comprehensive storm drainage assessment. The City of Lathrop General Plan Update EIR (SCH #2021100139), certified September 19, 2022, analyzed citywide buildout, including drainage and other infrastructure needs. In 2024, the City began updating its stormwater master planning to address current needs and support sustainable redevelopment in Historic Lathrop. The City found that the resulting East Lathrop Stormwater Master Plan revisions do not increase impact severity, and that the certified EIR's conclusions and mitigation measures remain applicable.

ceqa-0d42d1bc89f27f9179.name: Conditional Use Permit No. PA-2400500
ceqa-0d42d1bc89f27f9179.description: Conditional Use Permit application to establish a religious assembly facility. The project is proposed to be completed in two phases over five years. Phase 1 includes the conversion of an existing 4,765 square foot agricultural building to a temple. Phase 2 includes the conversion of an existing 2,642 square foot agricultural building to a meditation hall. Access to the religious assembly facility shall be limited to Lammers Road only. The applicant proposes a maximum attendance of 70 people for daily operations and a maximum of 600 attendees per day at six (6) proposed annual accessory events, with attendance not to exceed 150 people at any one time. Daily operating hours are from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, and 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., Saturday and Sunday. An average of five (5) staff members are anticipated on-site for daily operations. The Property is zoned AG-40 (General Agriculture, 40-acre minimum) and the General Plan designation is A/G (General Agriculture).

ceqa-f101595d7a1e3d4696.name: Delta Water Supply Intake Pump Monitoring Station Installation UH27008
ceqa-f101595d7a1e3d4696.projectTitle: Delta Water Supply Intake Pump Monitoring Station Installation UH27008
ceqa-f101595d7a1e3d4696.description: The project entails installing new real-time water quality monitoring probes and equipment onto the City's existing Intake Pump Station (IPS) structural infrastructure. The project will provide continuous real-time monitoring probes for temperature, turbidity, conductivity, pH, algae, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll, and total organic carbon. This data is important to assess the water quality in the Delta. The project site is located west of the City of Stockton approximately 6,100 feet from the end of Eight Mile Road, on the south bank of Empire Tract in San Joaquin County, California

ceqa-fcadccab00ee9fabb4.name: New Elementary School Project on Tinnin Road
ceqa-fcadccab00ee9fabb4.description: The proposed New Elementary School Project on Tinnin Road (proposed project) involves the construction and operation of a new transitional kindergarten (TK) through 8th grade public elementary school campus on an approximately 18-acre parcel (APNs 224-030-16 and 224-022-45) at 20877 South Tinnin Road in unincorporated San Joaquin County, California (project site), within the City of Manteca’s SOI. The project site consists of two parcels of previously disturbed and fallow agricultural land and is designated PQP in the City of Manteca General Plan. The proposed project would accommodate approximately 1,200 students and approximately 80 staff members, including teachers, administrators, and support personnel. The proposed project would include multiple one-story buildings totaling approximately 103,924 square feet, consisting of an administration building (Building A), four classroom buildings (Buildings B through E), a multipurpose building (Building G), a custodial building (Building F), and two shade structures (Buildings S1 and S2). The administration building would be approximately 6,421 square feet. The classroom buildings would range from approximately 18,875 to 21,972 square feet each. The multipurpose building would be approximately 11,198 square feet, and the custodial building would be approximately 1,260 square feet. Each shade structure would be approximately 1,320 square feet.
ceqa-fcadccab00ee9fabb4.crossStreets: South Tinnin Road and East Woodward Avenue

ceqa-771c4b85409d7b6bc7.name: Nile Garden Elementary School Annex Project
ceqa-771c4b85409d7b6bc7.projectTitle: Nile Garden Elementary School Annex Project
ceqa-771c4b85409d7b6bc7.description: The proposed project involves the construction and operation of an annex campus to support the existing Nile Garden Elementary School located at 5700 E Nile Avenue in unincorporated San Joaquin County, California. The proposed project would consist of four primary buildings and one ancillary structure totaling approximately 56,392 square feet. Facilities would include approximately 22 classrooms, a multipurpose building designed to accommodate indoor assembly and cafeteria functions, a compact administrative building, and two learning commons. Supporting structures would include a shade structure of approximately 1,920 square feet. The proposed project would include a new internal student drop-off and pick-up area located along the northern edge of the annex buildings, along with internal drive aisles connecting to the existing campus circulation system and to Union Road. Construction of the proposed project would occur in a single phase beginning in February 2028 and would take approximately 1.5 years to complete, with construction anticipated to be completed by July 2029. Upon completion, the annex campus is expected to be fully operational and integrated with the existing school.
ceqa-771c4b85409d7b6bc7.crossStreets: E Nile Avenue and Union Road

ceqa-db8a32ec7d45992a6f.name: South Delta Data Collection Project
ceqa-db8a32ec7d45992a6f.description: Project consists of land, boat, and drone surveys at various locations, collecting detailed data to support the South Delta Gates Project. Activities will include bathymetric surveying on canal waterways using ADCP RC boat, spot surveys using total stations or RTK base stations and rovers, and drone data collection. These activities are expected to have minimal impact though there may be some vegetation removal using hand tools/handheld trimmers to allow survey data collection. There will be cross sections surveyed every 50’ along centerline of the waterways in the project area, any vegetation along these cross sections may be trimmed back to allow for data collection. There will also be utilities location activities that may require digging to daylight utilities. A drone will be flown within the footprint of the survey area, ~250' above ground surface, to collect aerial imagery.

Beneficiaries of the project are pedestrians, bicyclists, motorists, and the general public.

ceqa-bb147031b0dd5f7810.name: Agreement to Purchase Water released by the Oakdale Irrigation District and the South San Joaquin Irrigation District for diversion and use by the San Luis &
ceqa-bb147031b0dd5f7810.projectTitle: Agreement to Purchase Water released by the Oakdale Irrigation District and the South San Joaquin Irrigation District for diversion and use by the San Luis &
ceqa-bb147031b0dd5f7810.description: [PROJECT TITLE CONTINUED:] Delta Mendota Water Authority and the California Department of Water Resources (Project). Oakdale Irrigation District (OID) and South San Joaquin Irrigation District (SSJID), collectively referred to as “Districts”, will release up to 50,000 acre-feet of water at Goodwin Dam (Project) in addition to water releases required to be made by the United States Bureau of Reclamation (Reclamation) at New Melones Reservoir to benefit migratory fish on the Stanislaus and San Joaquin Rivers. The water proposed to be released will be purchased by the San Luis & Delta Mendota Water Authority (SLDMWA) and the Department of Water Resources (DWR). The water OID and SSJID release will be surplus to the irrigation demand of each district. The release will occur at Goodwin Dam during April and May of each year between 2026 and 2030 and will be coordinated to assist and supplement Reclamation’s releases in meeting their legal obligations of the 1995 Water Quality Control Plan for the April-May pulse flow objective at Vernalis. The volume of water each year is dependent on the hydrological year type, and is as follows: Above Normal, up to 50,000 acre-feet Below Normal, up to 50,000 acre-feet Dry, up to 50,000 acre-feet Critically Dry, up to 20,000 acre-feet The Project agreement may be renewed for an additional 5 years upon written notification by the parties. The delivery volume above would remain the same if renewed. The Project will be subordinate to the rights of: 1) the Cities of Lathrop, Manteca, Escalon and Tracy pursuant to each city’s Water Supply Development Agreement with SSJID; 2) the Chicken Ranch Rancheria Me-Wuk Indians of California under their Emergency Water Supply Agreement with the Districts, and; 3) the landowners outside the boundaries of OID who are enrolled in OID’s 10-Year Out-of-District Water Sale Program. If the end-of-month September storage level in New Melones Reservoir is projected to be below 700,000 acre-feet during any year of the Project term, the parties shall consult with Reclamation on an agreeable release amount for that year. The Districts, in consultation with Reclamation and the Stanislaus Watershed Team, shall be responsible for determining the schedule of the delivery. The released water will be diverted by the SLDMWA and State Water Project Contractors (SWP) at the Jones and Banks pumping stations at a 1:1 ratio.

ceqa-db1dcdd41fb9ce75a3.name: Transmission Line Clearance Mitigation Moderate and Low Risk Project Various
ceqa-db1dcdd41fb9ce75a3.projectTitle: Transmission Line Clearance Mitigation Moderate and Low Risk Project Various
ceqa-db1dcdd41fb9ce75a3.description: The SFPUC owns and operates the Hetch Hetchy Power System which includes three hydroelectric powerhouses. Hydroelectricity generated at these facilities is delivered using SFPUC-Hetch Hetchy-owned transmission lines within its 168-mile rights-of-way to a PG&E substation in the city of Newark where the power is passed through to San Francisco. The SFPUC’s transmission facilities consist of 11 transmission lines and are located within Tuolumne, Mariposa, Stanislaus, San Joaquin, and Alameda counties. To ensure sufficient clearance between the conductors and the ground, SFPUC would conduct one of the following at over 100 locations (locations may have multiple towers) along the transmission lines: • Limited Grading/Site Clearing: Limited grading beneath the conductors (power lines) to increase the clearance distance between the ground and power lines. • Increase Tension: Increasing tension on existing power lines to raise conductors to meet requirements on sections between dead-end towers. • Insulator Replacement (Floating Dead-ends): Replacing existing insulators on the arms of the tower from a vertical suspension to a horizontal orientation. • Insulated Crossarms: Replacing the tower arms with a high-strength insulator assembly that allows forthe power lines to be raised up just underneath the arms • Tower Raises: Increasingthe height ofthe tower and thus the transmission lines • Tower Replacement: Replace the existing tower with a taller tower • New Midspan Tower: Constructing a new mid-span tower in-line with the existing transmission alignment to raise up the existing power line(s) • Reconductor: Replacing the power lines with new High-Temperature Low-Sag power lines (reconductor) • Hybrid Solutions: Implementing a combination of one or more ofthe above solutions. The overall work area would be up to an approximate 50-foot perimeter outside the base of each tower. Staging areas would likely be accommodated within the existing SFPUC rights-of-way and would center around the various tower locations. The staging areas would be used for storage of materials, construction vehicles, equipment, worker facilities, and dumpsters to temporarily store discarded materials. The project construction is anticipated to start in early 2027. Construction ofthe entire project would require a total of approximately 36 months. The work duration at each individual tower location will vary depending on the type of mitigation strategy pursued and could range from a few days for grading to six weeks for tower replacement or installation of a mid-span structure.

ceqa-475f0ee509033aafd5.name: Michigan Avenue Sidewalk Gap Improvements
ceqa-475f0ee509033aafd5.description: MICHIGAN AVENUE SIDEWALK GAP IMPROVEMENTS Project Description Project Locations: Michigan Avenue: Kirk Avenue to 1,000 feet east of Kirk Avenue. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: Michigan Avenue was originally constructed in 1948 and is a 22-foot-wide roadway, constructed with 2-inch bituminous surfacing over gravel. It was resurfaced in 1992 with a 0.17-foot overlay with fabric as a 44-foot-wide roadway. The curb, gutter, and sidewalk along the left-side (Kirk Avenue to Ryde Avenue), and the portion on the right-side (1,000 feet east of Kirk Avenue to Ryde Avenue), were constructed prior to the 1992 overlay with the widening, however no records are available. In 2011, the roadway was resurfaced by cold planing 0.20 feet of existing pavement and replacing it with 0.20 feet of asphalt concrete, and repairing the existing curb, gutter, and sidewalk by removing and replacing them. Michigan Avenue was last slurry sealed in 2023. Michigan Avenue currently has no safe pedestrian walkway along the right side of the roadway from Kirk Avenue to 1,000 east of Kirk Avenue to serve the public or nearby schools. There is no connection to existing sidewalk facilities. There are also no existing drainage facilities along the right side of the roadway creating poor drainage conditions. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Installing approximately 1,000 feet of concrete curb and gutter and 5.0-foot concrete sidewalk along the right side of the roadway from Kirk Avenue to 1,000 feet east of Kirk Avenue. 2. Widening the existing pavement from 0 to 3 feet to match the existing pavement depth on the right side of Michigan Avenue within the project limits. 3. Installing one (1) ADA ramp at crosswalk at Kirk Avenue and Michigan Avenue. 4. Paving all driveways with concrete or Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA) from the back of the sidewalk with a slope not exceeding 10%. 5. Modifying storm drainage facilities, including storm drain laterals and inlets, and matching the existing gutter’s flow line with the newly installed gutter flow line. 6. Installing two (2) storm drain inlets. 7. Adjusting existing Sanitary Sewer Lateral as required. 8. Removing 4 trees at 2874 Michigan Ave (3 walnut, 1 small). 9. Removing 1 tree at 2825 Bristol Ave (1 oak). Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily residential with single family homes. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with these pedestrian and drainage improvements. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-284bfc1a263aafe47f.description: Tentative subdivision map for Tract 3936 a Medium High Density Residential site in Mountain House Master-Planned Community Neighborhood K, also known as Lot 15 - Tract 3934. This subdivision map proposes 104 fee simple residential lots that will be owned and maintained by the City of Mountain House. The residential lots will be developed as 104 single family detached homes. Each unit will have a 2-car garage and private yards. All proposed roads will be public and dedicated to the City. There will be no Common area lots or HOA proposed. The Project consists of subdividing an approximately 9.89-acre vacant parcel (APN 258-04-016) within Neighborhood K into 104 single-family detached residential lots consistent with the Mountain House General Plan, Master Plan, and Specific Plan II. Each lot will include a two-car garage and private yard area, and all home designs will comply with the Mountain House Single Family Residential Design Manual. The Project achieves a net density of approximately 10.5 dwelling units per acre, which is within the allowable R-MH density range. The project proposes lot designs that will not accommodate the required secondary unit dwellings as required by the Mountain House Master Plan. Therefore, the applicant has chosen to expand the number of secondary unit dwellings in Tract 3927 and 3928 in Neighborhood K. As such, the Revisions to Approved Actions (RAA-26-001) would modify Condition of Approval #10 (Planning), increasing the minimum Second Unit Dwellings required for Neighborhood K from 52 to 59. Primary access is provided via Spinardi Way, Tachi Way, Graycliff Avenue, and Nirankar Way, forming a complete circulation block within Neighborhood K. Utilities, including water, wastewater, and stormwater, will be installed as part of the subdivision improvements and dedicated to the City for long-term maintenance and operation.

ceqa-3640e1a5ae4c845734.description: The project site is located southwest of the intersection of West Yosemite Avenue and South Airport Way in the western portion of the City of Manteca. The project site currently includes a mix of industrial and commercial uses, as well as singlefamily residences. The City of Manteca General Plan designates the project site as Industrial (1), Commercial Mixed Use (CMU), and Medium Density Residential (MDR). The site is zoned Light Industrial (M1), Planned Development (PD), CMU, and Limited Multiple-Family Dwelling (R2). The Yosemite Mixed Use Conversion (Batched GPAs Site 5) Project would include a General Plan Amendment (GPA) to change the General Plan land use designation of the project site from I, CMU, and MDR to CMU, as well as a rezone from M1, PD, CMU, and R2 to CMU. The proposed GPA and rezone would result in a net increase of CMU land uses, and a net decrease of I, PQP, and MDR land uses within the City’s General Plan planning area. Under the proposed land use/zoning designations, the maximum development potential of the site is 251,341.2 square feet (sf) of commercial uses and 519 residential units. Development of the project site is not currently proposed.

ceqa-b92335adb6b624f85f.name: Transmission Line Clearance Mitigation Moderate and Low Risk Project
ceqa-b92335adb6b624f85f.projectTitle: Transmission Line Clearance Mitigation Moderate and Low Risk Project
ceqa-b92335adb6b624f85f.agency: City and County of San Francisco
ceqa-b92335adb6b624f85f.agencyName: San Francisco, City and County of
ceqa-b92335adb6b624f85f.description: The SFPUC owns and operates the Hetch Hetchy Power System which includes three hydroelectric powerhouses. Hydroelectricity generated at these facilities is delivered using SFPUC-Hetch Hetchy-owned transmission lines within its 168-mile rights-of-way to a PG&E substation in the city of Newark where the power is passed through to San Francisco. The SFPUC’s transmission facilities consist of 11 transmission lines and are located within Tuolumne, Mariposa, Stanislaus, San Joaquin, and Alameda counties. To ensure sufficient clearance between the conductors and the ground, SFPUC would conduct one of the following at over 100 locations (locations may have multiple towers) along the transmission lines: ?? Limited Grading/Site Clearing: Limited grading beneath the conductors (power lines) to increase the clearance distance between the ground and power lines. ?? Increase Tension: Increasing tension on existing power lines to raise conductors to meet requirements on sections between dead-end towers. ?? Insulator Replacement (Floating Dead-ends): Replacing existing insulators on the arms of the tower from a vertical suspension to a horizontal orientation. ?? Insulated Crossarms: Replacing the tower arms with a high-strength insulator assembly that allows for the power lines to be raised up just underneath the arms ?? Tower Raises: Increasing the height of the tower and thus the transmission lines ?? Tower Replacement: Replace the existing tower with a taller tower ?? New Midspan Tower: Constructing a new mid-span tower in-line with the existing transmission alignment to raise up the existing power line(s) ?? Reconductor: Replacing the power lines with new High-Temperature Low-Sag power lines (reconductor) ?? Hybrid Solutions: Implementing a combination of one or more of the above solutions. The overall work area would be up to an approximate 50-foot perimeter outside the base of each tower. Staging areas would likely be accommodated within the existing SFPUC rights-of-way and would center around the various tower locations. The staging areas would be used for storage of materials, construction vehicles, equipment, worker facilities, and dumpsters to temporarily store discarded materials. The project construction is anticipated to start in early 2027. Construction of the entire project would require a total of approximately 36 months. The work duration at each individual tower location will vary depending on the type of mitigation strategy pursued and could range from a few days for grading to six weeks for tower replacement or installation of a mid-span structure

ceqa-3a489c605475ed0839.description: A Conditional Use Permit for 14.5-acre ground-mounted photovoltaic energy facility. The project will generate up to 3 megawatts of solar energy utilizing photovoltaic solar modules, inverters, and appurtenant electrical equipment and distribute the useable energy to the electric grid. The modules will be mounted on a steel racking system employing single-axis tracker technology that efficiently tracks the sun’s movement throughout the day and maximizes the efficiency of solar collection. The rows of modules will be anchored in the ground using driven piers, and the overall height of the array is not expected to exceed 15 feet above the existing ground surface at maximum tilt. The Project will interconnect to the existing Pacific, Gas, and Electric electrical distribution system adjacent to the site along East Comstock Road.

Facilities would include approximately 22 classrooms, a multipurpose building designed to accommodate indoor assembly and cafeteria functions, a compact administrative building, and two learning commons. ceqa-926053fd30dafe53f4.name: California Stream Gage Improvement Program – San Joaquin County Stream Gage Upgrade Project
ceqa-926053fd30dafe53f4.projectTitle: California Stream Gage Improvement Program – San Joaquin County Stream Gage Upgrade Project
ceqa-926053fd30dafe53f4.description: CALIFORNIA STREAM GAGE IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM – SAN JOAQUIN COUNTY STREAM GAGE UPGRADE PROJECT Project Description Project Location: Various locations along levees throughout the County. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: During storm and flood events, San Joaquin County relies on stream gages to provide accurate, real-time information on water levels and stream flows throughout the County. This data is critical for flood forecasting, emergency response, public safety, water resource management, and the protection of freshwater ecosystems. The California Stream Gage Improvement Program (CalSIP) will provide upgrades to our existing gaging stations. These improvements increase the reliability and availability of hydrologic data needed to support flood preparedness and informed water management decisions. Scope of Work: The San Joaquin County Stream Gage Upgrade Project will enhance seven existing stream gage locations, including: 1. Bear Creek at Alpine Rd 2. Five Mile Creek near its confluence with Fourteen Mile Slough 3. Duck Creek between Union Pacific Railroad and Airport Way 4. French Camp Slough at Airport Way 5. Corral Hollow Creek at Corral Hollow Road 6. Temple Creek at South Wagner Road 7. Lone Tree Creek at Escalon Bellota Road Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily rural with single family homes. There may be large trees adjacent to the project areas. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The primary beneficiaries of this project are the residents, businesses, agricultural community, and visitors throughout San Joaquin County. By improving the reliability and availability of real-time stream gage data, the County will be better equipped to monitor changing water conditions, forecast potential flooding, and make informed emergency response decisions during storm events. Enhanced hydrologic data will support timely public notifications, improve coordination with local, state, and federal agencies, and assist in protecting lives, property, critical infrastructure, and agricultural resources. Additionally, the improved stream gage network will provide long-term benefits for water resource management, infrastructure planning, and environmental stewardship.

ceqa-b183f5f516a5c20845.name: Conditional Use Permit No. PA-2500075
ceqa-b183f5f516a5c20845.description: Conditional Use Permit application to construct and operate a manure anaerobic digestion facility by configuring two above-ground cow manure “digesters”. Located on a 2.9-acre portion of an existing 78.8-acre dairy site, the project includes installation of two containment structures measuring 40 feet wide by 180 feet deep (7,200 square feet) and approximately 12.5 feet in height with a concrete base with a rubber bladder. A third external bladder will be used as an emergency methane gas containment in lieu of a combustion flare. Manure wastewater from the existing lagoons and manure will be pumped approximately 100 yards into the digester bladders. The biogas from the bladders will be converted into biomethane gas (RNG) and compressed then loaded onto gas trucks for final distribution. Once fully operation it is estimated that the project will generate 12 truck trips a month. (Use Type: Renewable Energy – Biomass)

ceqa-2912a40704903e8ad0.name: EVSE Project at CAL TRANS District 10 - Stockton Maintenance Facility
ceqa-2912a40704903e8ad0.projectTitle: EVSE Project at CAL TRANS District 10 - Stockton Maintenance Facility
ceqa-2912a40704903e8ad0.description: The project consists of installing the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) infrastructure for fleet use. This initiative is designed to create a fully operational system that will eventually support one dual port, pedestal-mounted Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS). Note that the installation of the EVCS itself is outside this current scope and may be handled by others at a later date. As part of this project, two parking stalls will be specially stenciled and restriped. Clear signage will be installed to indicate that these stalls are reserved for electric vehicle use, ensuring easy identification and proper use The project involves the installation of buried conduits, fixed bollards, wheel stops, and new electrical equipment, including all necessary wiring, to deliver a complete and functional system. Electrical power for the EVSE will be drawn from an existing source already available at the site. All aspects of the work, including waste disposal, will be conducted in strict compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances. The work will involve pavement saw cutting, trenching, backfilling, and restoring the affected lot surface to its original condition once the installation is complete.

ceqa-d3fc43e608028f467b.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes a maintenance project in San Joaquin County near Lathrop on Route 5 at Post Mile (PM) R15.59 and 17.04. ceqa-7a2b96dc4d8a09064d.projectTitle: Mossdale Tract Area Urban Flood Risk Reduction Project
ceqa-7a2b96dc4d8a09064d.agency: San Joaquin County Area Flood Control Agency
ceqa-7a2b96dc4d8a09064d.agencyName: San Joaquin County Area Flood Control Agency
ceqa-7a2b96dc4d8a09064d.description: The proposed project area covers 22,400 acres, including Reclamation District 17 ([RD 17], 16,110 acres) and portions of the cities of Stockton, Lathrop, Manteca, and unincorporated San Joaquin County. The RD 17 levee system is comprised of state-federal project levees (also referred to as State Plan of Flood Control [SPFC]) along the San Joaquin River and French Camp Slough. The proposed project would include the construction and operation and maintenance of flood risk reduction and multi-benefit components in and adjacent to the proposed project area. Project components include fix-in place improvements with habitat enhancement and revegetation, dryland levee extension, ecosystem restoration, and recreational features along the levee system.

ceqa-861fe9e16941b8737e.name: Permit No. 8064-1 – Watkins Low Water Crossing Replacement Project
ceqa-861fe9e16941b8737e.description: To replace the existing Watkins low-water crossing as part of the Calaveras Fish Passage Improvements for Flashboard Dam and Low Water Crossing Project. The project includes replacement of the existing concrete crossing and riprap with ten precast Type 2 reinforced concrete box culvert sections arranged in two rows of five culverts, each approximately 10 feet wide, 21 feet long, and 8 feet high, and construction of associated concrete wingwalls. The project also includes grading approximately 650 linear feet of streambed. Grading will create a 10-foot-wide low-flow channel with 2:1 side slopes and includes approximately 2,204 cubic yards of excavation and 1,815 cubic yards of fill within an approximately 43,000-square-foot project footprint. Disturbed areas will be finished with native material and engineered streambed material.

ceqa-487b4de60a7726ecec.description: Approval and implementation of a Plan for Enforcement Case No. 2026-15769 to remedy installation of an unauthorized 8-inch diameter PVC pipe through the right bank of the Mormon Slough project levee. The corrective work consists of excavating the levee 8 to 12 feet deep, fully removing the pipe, then restoring the levee to pre-project conditions using the native, moisture-conditioned soil for compacted backfill in 4 to 6-inch lifts. ceqa-8a642d616c1e19a4dc.name: Mokelumne Acres Sinkhole Repair IMMRP
ceqa-8a642d616c1e19a4dc.description: MOKELUMNE ACRES SINKHOLE REPAIR IMMRP Project Description Project Location: Valley Oak Place: 908 Valley Oak Place Woodbridge, CA 95258. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: A section of the existing 36-inch storm drainpipe from the intersection of Valley Oak Place and Meadowlark Drive to approximately 100 feet east is damaged. Storm water runoff is leaking into the subgrade area under the pipe section and causing erosion which is leading to failure of the structural section and sinking of the asphalt section of the pipe. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Excavating trench to expose existing storm drain line. 2. Removing and replacing all damaged and broken portions of the existing 36-inch Reinforced Concrete Pipe (RCP). 3. Compacting pipe bedding areas. 4. Pouring concrete collars at pipe joints. 5. Backfilling and compacting subgrade above pipe. 6. Placing Class 2 Aggregate Base (AB) to match existing structural section; Compacting to 95%. 7. Placing Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA) to match existing structural section. 8. Asphalt restoration to be in accordance with San Joaquin County Standards and drawings. Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily residential with single family homes. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with these improved storm drainpipes. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-ac328c0a71a6032ddb.name: Linne Road and Chrisman Road Thermo Replacement
ceqa-ac328c0a71a6032ddb.projectTitle: Linne Road and Chrisman Road Thermo Replacement
ceqa-ac328c0a71a6032ddb.description: LINNE ROAD AND CHRISMAN ROAD THERMO REPLACEMENT Project Description Project Location: Linne Road and Chrisman Road: Includes intersection and approaches. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: The intersection of Linne Road and Chrisman Road receives a high volume of truck traffic and has an elementary school on the southeast corner. The thermoplastic traffic striping and pavement markings show a great amount of wear and need to be replaced. The County is using the opportunity to test the durability of two different products, one being traditional thermoplastic and the other being preformed thermoplastic tape. The cost versus durability will then be evaluated over the next several years, to determine which is the best option for future use in similar conditions. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Grinding and replacing existing thermoplastic striping and pavement markings. Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily agricultural. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with these new traffic striping and pavement markings. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-0c93686ad4f80f53ce.name: Rutledge Way and Sheridan Way Resurfacing
ceqa-0c93686ad4f80f53ce.projectTitle: Rutledge Way and Sheridan Way Resurfacing
ceqa-0c93686ad4f80f53ce.description: RUTLEDGE WAY AND SHERIDAN WAY RESURFACING Project Description Project Location: Rutledge Way: Vicksburg Place to Gettysburg Place, Sheridan Way: Vicksburg Place to Gettysburg Place. See attached Vicinity Map. Project Justification: The existing residential streets Rutledge Way and Sheridan Way were part of the Lincoln Village, Unit 5 and Unit 7 subdivision constructed in 1950. Existing construction plans indicate that Rutledge Way's 28-foot roadway was originally constructed with an oil surface over 5-inch gravel with 5-foot curb, gutter, and sidewalk. Sheridan Way's 28-foot roadway was constructed with 2-inch Asphalt Concrete (AC) over 6-inch gravel with 6-foot curb, gutter, and sidewalk. Coring sample did not reach base/subbase, but there is at least 3 inches of AC on Sheridan Way, and at least 5 inches of AC on Rutledge Way. As part of an overall pavement maintenance strategy, these roads are programmed for slurry seal on a 7-year cycle, with the last slurry seal taking place in 2016. The existing roadway surface on Sheridan Way exhibits moderate alligator cracking and some oxidation. The existing roadway surface on Rutledge Way exhibits high alligator cracking and some low edge cracking. There are several areas where the existing gutter pan has been paved over/slurry sealed on both Rutledge Way and Sheridan Way. There are areas throughout project limit where flowline is slightly higher in the gutter pan, thus restricting efficient flow. There are some areas of failed existing curb, gutter, and sidewalk that have heavy cracking. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Cold planing existing roadway (28 feet wide) to a depth of 0.17 feet and placing 0.17 feet Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA) (Type A) 2. Repairing pavement structural failure areas with 0.25' HMA (Type A). 3. Scraping existing AC out of gutter pan on both roadways. 4. Removing all part-circle culverts, driveway pipes, and steel plates in gutter. 5. Grinding high areas of existing flowline and gutter to help with water flow. 6. Removing existing curb, gutter, and sidewalk at failed locations and replace in kind. 7. Removing and replacing existing curb ramps to provide pedestrians requiring accessibility access in accordance with the ADA requirements. Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage is primarily residential with single family homes. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety and fewer hazards with these well-maintained roads. Overall, there will be reduced maintenance concerns and more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-0dc24b33c5b9e3d03a.projectTitle: San Joaquin County Park Automated Gate System Project
ceqa-0dc24b33c5b9e3d03a.description: SAN JOAQUIN COUNTY PARK AUTOMATED GATE SYSTEM PROJECT Project Description Project Locations: Micke Grove: 11793 Micke Grove Rd, Lodi, Shumway Oak Grove: 4520 W Eight Mile Rd, Stockton, Regional Sports Complex: 7171 CA-99, Stockton. Installing automatic gates where manual gates exist for Micke Grove and Shumway Oak Grove. 3. Installing a small concrete island for the Regional Sports Complex to install the automatic gate system. ceqa-c4dcf4b2bb561daa94.name: Shopping Center Parking Ordinance and Specific Plan Amendments
ceqa-c4dcf4b2bb561daa94.projectTitle: Shopping Center Parking Ordinance and Specific Plan Amendments
ceqa-c4dcf4b2bb561daa94.description: The 2011 Sustainability Action Plan and 2025-2027 Strategic Priorities direct staff to reduce parking requirements and make the City more business friendly. ceqa-feeec38cf562c4d84d.name: Sprouts Farmers Market Wall Signs

ceqa-5c164a0118fbe0ed06.name: Interstate 580/Corral Hollow Road Interchange Bridge Improvement Project
ceqa-5c164a0118fbe0ed06.projectTitle: Interstate 580/Corral Hollow Road Interchange Bridge Improvement Project
ceqa-5c164a0118fbe0ed06.description: Caltrans, in cooperation with the City, proposes to enhance local and regional traffic circulation and reduce existing and future congestion at the Interstate 580/Corral Hollow Road interchange resulting from buildout of the Tracy Hills Specific Plan. The current Interstate 580/Corral Hollow Road Interchange is a Tight Diamond configuration with single-lane on- and off-ramps. A two-way stop sign controls the intersections of Corral Hollow Road and the ramp entrances/exits. The project proposes reconfiguring the existing Tight Diamond with a Diverging Diamond interchange. The proposed project includes the following improvements: • Widen and upgrade the Corral Hollow Road Overpass structure (Bridge Number 29-0080) to match the existing four lanes along Corral Hollow Road on either side of the interchange and construct a new concrete barrier between the vehicle lanes and a new center-running multi-purpose bike/pedestrian path. • Reconfigure the eastbound and westbound Interstate 580 ramp intersections with Corral Hollow Road to a Diverging Diamond configuration and install a new two-phase signal. • Install new traffic signals at the eastbound and westbound ramp intersections at Corral Hollow Road. • Stripe crosswalks on the north leg of the westbound Interstate 580 ramp intersection and the south leg of the eastbound Interstate 580 ramp intersection. The eastbound on-ramp crosses Corral Hollow Creek. Two design options are being considered to address the crossing: • Design Option A would involve widening the existing bridge over the Corral Hollow Creek (Bridge Number 29-0081L) to accommodate the eastbound on-ramp, including an additional lane and paved shoulder. •Design Option B would involve complete replacement of the existing Corral Hollow Creek Bridge. The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes to conduct multimodal improvements for the Interstate 580/Corral Hollow Interchange between post mile 7.6 and post mile 8.6 in San Joaquin County

ceqa-dc21e9ac3f19798f00.name: End-of-life replacement of TMS Field Devices
ceqa-dc21e9ac3f19798f00.projectTitle: End-of-life replacement of TMS Field Devices
ceqa-dc21e9ac3f19798f00.description: The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) proposes the End-of-Life Replacement of Traffic Management System (TMS) Devices Project (Project) to replace 108 TMS elements at various locations in Alameda and San Joaquin Counties on State Route (SR) 13, 24, 61, 84, 92, 123, 185, 238, 260, and Interstate 80, 205, 580, 680, 880, and 980. Specifically, the electronic components of 6 CCTV, 3 CMS, 10 EMS, 7 Freeway Ramp Metering Systems, 16 HAR, 35 Traffic Signals, and 57 Traffic Monitoring Stations, will be replaced at various locations. No excavation or new ground disturbance is anticipated, although some minor vegetation removal may be needed. No new right-of-way (ROW) acquisition is anticipated, but temporary construction easements (TCEs) may be necessary for construction.

ceqa-496a26b9c14c3bcde8.name: Administrative Use Permit No. PA-2500375
ceqa-496a26b9c14c3bcde8.description: Administrative Use Permit application for three components. The first component is an Entertainment Permit to allow live entertainment at the existing Koe's Bar facility. The second component is to permit food trucks for food service during normal operating hours and events. The third component is permitting an as-built 340 square-foot patio cover that is within 25% of the existing legal square footage of the facility. The project site has direct access from North State Route 99 East Frontage Road. The project site is served by a well for water, a septic system for wastewater disposal, and natural storm water drainage. The project site is not under a Williamson Act contract. The Property is zoned C-C (Community Commercial) and the General Plan designation is CIC (Community Commercial).

ceqa-28f6e499fabba5901d.name: General Plan Text Amendment No. PA-2600209
ceqa-28f6e499fabba5901d.projectTitle: General Plan Text Amendment No. PA-2600209
ceqa-28f6e499fabba5901d.description: General Plan Text Amendment application: The County of San Joaquin is preparing an amendment to the adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element (6th cycle), a State-mandated policy document that is a component of the San Joaquin County General Plan. The overall purpose of the Housing Element Update is to identify current and projected housing needs; show locations where housing can be built; and set goals, policies, and programs to meet the community’s housing needs. The foundation of the Housing Element is the Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA). Proposed revisions address the incorporation of the City of Mountain House and the related reallocation of a portion of the County’s RHNA to the city, reducing the County's RHNA from 8,808 to 5,113 housing units.

ceqa-395c61e63ef8cc9ad2.name: Adoption of Revisions to Water and Wastewater Schedules of Rates and Charges, Capacity Charges, and Other Fees Not Subject to Proposition 218 for (FY) 2027
ceqa-395c61e63ef8cc9ad2.projectTitle: Adoption of Revisions to Water and Wastewater Schedules of Rates and Charges, Capacity Charges, and Other Fees Not Subject to Proposition 218 for (FY) 2027
ceqa-395c61e63ef8cc9ad2.description: On June 9, 2026, the Board of Directors of East Bay Municipal Utility District (Board) adopted revisions to water and wastewater rates and charges, capacity charges, and other fees for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027. The various rates, charges, and fees approved by the Board included FY 2027 water system capacity charges, wastewater capacity charges, recreation use fees, real property use application fees, and Public Records Act fees, water and wastewater rates, charges, and fees are applicable to the EBMUD service area as shown in Exhibit 1. Real property use application fees are applicable to requests for use of EBMUD properties located in the EBMUD service area (shown in Exhibit 1) and in EBMUD watershed areas in Amador, Calaveras, and San Joaquin Counties (shown in Exhibits 2 and 3). The changes to the recreation use fees apply to EBMUD recreation facilities in the EBMUD service area (shown in Exhibit 1) and in Amador, Calaveras, and San Joaquin Counties (shown in Exhibits 2 and 3). Further information about these rates, charges, and fees is available at https://www.ebmud.com/rates.

ceqa-4fd93a52495a289c97.name: General Plan Amendment/ Zone Reclassification & Administrative Use Permit No. PA-2500411, -412
ceqa-4fd93a52495a289c97.projectTitle: General Plan Amendment/ Zone Reclassification & Administrative Use Permit No. PA-2500411, -412
ceqa-4fd93a52495a289c97.description: This project includes: • General Plan Map Amendment/Zone Reclassification No. PA-2500411 to change the General Plan map designation and zoning designation of a 1.01-acre parcel from General Agriculture (A/G, AG-40) to Warehouse Industrial (I/W, I-W). • Administrative Use Permit PA-2500412 to establish a traffic control business on the 1.01-acre parcel. The project includes converting an existing 5,498-square-foot farm services building to an office for administrative functions and construction of a 4,000-square-foot building for equipment storage and minor repairs. ceqa-9f56f237cb7ea604b3.description: SAN JOAQUIN COUNTY COMMUNITY CENTER PARKING LOT REPAVING PROJECT Project Description Project Locations: Larch Clover Community Center: 11157 West Larch Road, Tracy, Garden Acres Community Center: 607 Bird Avenue, Stockton, Taft Community Center: 389 West Downing Avenue, Stockton, Gianone Community Center: 2885 East Harding Way, Stockton. See attached Vicinity Maps. Project Justification: Current parking lot conditions at the four community centers (Larch Clover, Garden Acres, Taft, Gianone) include erosion which cause a public safety concern. This project was developed as a way to repair the parking lots and improve the conditions of these important community assets. Scope of Work: The project will consist of: 1. Removing and replacing the parking lots at four community centers (Larch Clover, Garden Acres, Taft, Gianone). Environmental Setting: In these portions of the San Joaquin County, land usage varies but is primarily residential with single family homes. There are many large trees adjacent to the project area. Nesting and migratory birds, protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, may nest within these trees. Furthermore, the Swainson’s Hawk, a raptor species of concern within the State of California and listed as threatened may nest adjacent to or within the project area. A pre-construction survey for nesting Swainson’s Hawks and other migratory birds is recommended if construction is scheduled to occur from February 15th to September 1st. Beneficiaries: The public will see increased safety with new parking lots at the community centers which will support a healthy community through reliable recreational spaces. Overall, community assets will be more efficient and there will be more reliability within the project area.

ceqa-7dae34ae7ba8e1d4a4.name: Adoption of the 2024 Municipal Service Review and Sphere of Influence for the Woodbridge Irrigation District
ceqa-7dae34ae7ba8e1d4a4.projectTitle: Adoption of the 2024 Municipal Service Review and Sphere of Influence for the Woodbridge Irrigation District
ceqa-7dae34ae7ba8e1d4a4.description: The project consists of the preparation and adoption of the 2024 Municipal Service Review (MSR) for the Woodbridge Irrigation District, together with the associated Sphere of Influence (SOI) determination. The MSR is an informational planning and feasibility study prepared pursuant to the Cortese-Knox-Hertzberg Local Government Reorganization Act of 2000 (Government Code§§ 56000 et seq.), including Government Code§§ 56425 and 56430. The MSR provides a comprehensive overview and analysis of the services WID currently provides, and presents written determinations in the seven categories mandated by Government Code § 56430: (1) growth and population projections; (2) the location and characteristics of disadvantaged unincorporated communities; (3) the present and planned capacity of public facilities and adequacy of public services; (4) the financial ability of the agency to provide services; (5) the status of and opportunities for shared facilities; (6) accountability for community service needs, including governmental structure and operational efficiencies; and (7) any other matters related to effective or efficient service delivery. The MSR and SOI cover WID's current service area boundary and define WID's Sphere of Influence boundary. WID is not proposing any annexation or detachment of territory to its service area, any change of organization or reorganization, or any new or expanded physical facilities as part of this project. The MSR collects and presents baseline technical and administrative information intended to inform future planning and decision-making by WID and the San Joaquin Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCo). The purpose of the project is to satisfy the requirements of the Cortese-Knox-Hertzberg Act and to support informed, orderly planning for the provision of irrigation and related water services. The beneficiaries of the project are WID, LAFCo, and the public, who benefit from the comprehensive, publicly available information the MSR provides. Any future boundary change,annexation, out-of-boundary service extension, or construction of facilities that may be considered in reliance on the MSR would be a separate, discretionary action subject to its own independent environmental review under CEQA at the time it is proposed.

ceqa-c4c8077ef9e875d1cc.name: Stockton San Joaquin River Pipeline Remediation Project
ceqa-c4c8077ef9e875d1cc.projectTitle: Stockton San Joaquin River Pipeline Remediation Project
ceqa-c4c8077ef9e875d1cc.description: The City of Stockton proposes improvements to an existing 36-inch Regional Wastewater Control Facility pipeline, which is used on occasion to divert wastewater flows. While state and federal regulations require a minimum cover depth of five feet, river scour over time has caused a reduction in the required cover depth in portions of the pipeline crossing. Therefore, the purpose of the project is to bring the pipeline into compliance with state and federal regulations. The proposed project would involve both in-water and terrestrial work, including grading on the landside of the levee, dredging/excavation of the channel bed above and around the pipeline, and the addition of gravel and rip rap fill above and around the pipeline. Water quality protection measures and in-water work windows would be implemented during project construction to ensure adequate protection of the San Joaquin River and its aquatic resources.

As the MPO for the San Joaquin County region, SJCOG is required to prepare an SCS or Alternative Planning Strategy that demonstrates how GHG reduction targets will be met through integrated land use, housing, and transportation planning. ceqa-3c2d6259026c8b2d1a.name: Old and Middle River Pump Stations Water Quality Monitoring Instrumentation Improvements Project
ceqa-3c2d6259026c8b2d1a.projectTitle: Old and Middle River Pump Stations Water Quality Monitoring Instrumentation Improvements Project
ceqa-3c2d6259026c8b2d1a.description: This Project consists of the installation of upgraded water quality monitoring equipment at CCWD’s Old River and Middle River intakes in the Sacramento-San Joquin Delta. Currently, water samples at these intakes are pumped out of wet wells that pass through two-inch diameter piping, which is at high risk of being blocked by the spread of invasive golden mussels (Limnoperna fortunei). The purpose of this project is to install new water quality monitoring equipment that will provide more reliable monitoring data and will decrease the risk of being blocked by golden mussels. A total of two multiparameter sondes will be installed, one at Old River and one at Middle River. Each sonde will be incased in a six-inch diameter HDPE pipe stilling well and mounted to the existing concrete cantilever platforms located in front of the fish screen at each intake, where they will extend into the water to collect water quality data. These larger diameter stilling wells will significantly decrease the risk of clogging due to golden mussels and will be easier to access and maintain. See Figure 1 for a Project vicinity map and Figures 2 and 3 for Project location maps. Data from these sondes will be transmitted back to the electrical building at each site through new and existing conduits. The Project is expected to take three months, with construction occurring between June and August of 2026. Equipment laydown and vehicle staging will occur in previously disturbed areas, such as paved roads and parking areas, within the boundaries of the pump stations on CCWD property. The following types of equipment are expected to be present at the project site: crew trucks, a boat or barge, and power tools. Project activities will occur in previously developed and disturbed areas on CCWD property. No vegetation removal or tree removal will occur. No ground disturbance will occur, and there will be no impact to the banks or beds of the rivers at either intake. Equipment installation will occur from land via the concrete cantilever platforms and from a boat or barge in the water immediately below the platform. The Project is not anticipated to adversely affect natural resources or areas of known cultural or historic resources.

ceqa-55f767df5ec4b5f31a.description: The purpose of the Mokelumne River Confluence Multi-Benefit Project is to rehabilitate the levee section from Station 822+00 – 1038+00 to the Delta Specific PL 84-99 Standard and create waterside habitat. Landside work includes raising the levee crown to achieve sufficient freeboard above the 100-year flood elevation and stabilizing the landside slope through the construction of a toe berm. Additionally, a setback levee will be constructed from Station 857+00 – 864+00. Waterside work includes excavation of the existing levee at the setback levee, to construct a habitat bench above Mean Lower Low Water. The habitat bench and setback levee waterside slope will be planted with native riparian species, creating approximately 1 acre of Delta Levee Waterside Habitat. Plantings will be monitored and maintained to ensure success criteria are met.

The project is also exempt from CEQA under Class 30, Minor Actions to Prevent, Minimize, Stabilize, Mitigate, or Eliminate the Release or Threat of Release of Hazardous Waste or Hazardous Substances, categorical exemption (California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section 15330), because the proposed activity consists of excavation and disposal of contaminated soils in regulated units offsite. Finally, the project is exempt from CEQA under Class 33, Small Habitat Restoration Projects, categorical exemption (California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Section 15333), because the proposed activity does not exceed five acres in size to assure the maintenance, restoration, enhancement, or protection of habitat for fish, plants, or wildlife. ceqa-beb809a8688cca3177.name: Potentia-Viridi Battery Energy Storage System
ceqa-beb809a8688cca3177.description: The primary components of the BESS facility include an operations and maintenance (O&M) building, a project substation, the gen-tie line, and interconnection facilities within the PG&E owned and operated Tesla Substation. The energy storage facility would utilize modular and containerized components to operate a 400- megawatt (MW) BESS with an energy storage capacity up to 3,200 MW-hours. The project would draw electricity from the power grid to charge and store electrical energy and discharge back to the power grid when the stored energy is needed. The BESS enclosures would be prefabricated off-site and arrive at the site ready to be installed and commissioned. Each modular BESS enclosure would include battery packs on racks, a battery management system, fire protection, and ancillary power electronics within a specialized steel-framed, non-occupiable container. The BESS enclosures would approximate 10-feet high, and may have a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system for optimal performance and safety. Power for the HVAC system, lighting, and other electrical systems would be provided through separate auxiliary power connection to the on-site project substation with connection lines installed above and/or below ground.

ceqa-10ed8f82d10375b9c8.name: Mokelumne River Integrated Conjunctive Use Program
ceqa-10ed8f82d10375b9c8.projectTitle: Mokelumne River Integrated Conjunctive Use Program
ceqa-10ed8f82d10375b9c8.description: MICUP is a proposed coordinated effort to put unappropriated Mokelumne River water to beneficial use in the Subbasin through approval of Water Right Application 29835 (A029835). The County, as lead agency, proposes to implement MICUP together with the following Partner Agencies: North San Joaquin Water Conservation District (NSJWCD), Stockton East Water District (SEWD), and City of Stockton. MICUP would entail diverting unappropriated Mokelumne River water either to serve existing beneficial uses, such as agricultural irrigation and municipal and industrial water supply demands, or to recharge surface water to underground storage for later extraction from existing production wells to meet existing demands. Under A029835, as amended, MICUP would divert up to 110,000 acre-feet per year (AFY) between December 1 and June 30, using a combination of existing and proposed infrastructure. In addition, up to 48,000 AFY of water stored in Camanche and/or Pardee Reservoir by East Bay Municipal Utilities District (EBMUD) under existing operations could be allocated to MICUP if EBMUD determines it has stored water in excess of EBMUD's needs and legal and/or operational obligations, including contract obligations to Woodbridge Irrigation District and NSJWCD. The Water available under MICUP would serve existing Partner Agency demands currently met with groundwater pumping. The proposed MICUP diversions would be junior to all existing water rights on the Mokelumne River.

ceqa-8d80dbb8938dc52f6d.name: Tracy Northeast Business Park Project
ceqa-8d80dbb8938dc52f6d.description: Development on the Dermody Property would consist of approximately 1,811,259 square feet of warehouse/distribution and/or manufacturing space located in three buildings, as well as an approximately 12.4-acre stormwater detention basin with pump station that would be City owned and managed. It is anticipated that Suvik would process a site-specific Development Review Permit at some point in the future, subsequent to certification of this EIR; thus, the specific layout and other site planning and building details for the Suvik Property are not currently known. However, for purposes of a conservative analysis, a conceptual building orientation plan for the Suvik Property has been prepared to provide site-specific information, based on reasonable assumptions, regarding a conceptual building orientation to facilitate project-level review and analysis hereunder. For the purposes of analysis in the DEIR, buildout of the Suvik Property is estimated to consist of a maximum total of approximately 1,015,166 square feet of warehouse/distribution and/or manufacturing uses (as well as ancillary office use), which conservatively reflects the maximum allowable density per acre identified in the NEI Specific Plan (which would govern development of the proposed project). The proposed project also includes demolition of existing agricultural structures, removal of existing trees and crops, installation of related on- and off-site road and utility improvements to serve the proposed project, and grading of a total of approximately 450,000 cubic yards, which would be balanced on-site. Of the approximately 450,000 cubic yards of material graded, approximately 300,000 cubic yards would occur on the Dermody Property, with the remaining approximately 150,000 cubic yards occurring on the Suvik Property. The project site is zoned General Agriculture, with a minimum parcel size of 40 acres (AG-40) on the County’s Zoning Map. The City of Tracy General Plan designates the project site as Industrial. As discussed more fully in the DEIR, the proposed project would be consistent with the planned industrial uses under the City’s land use vision for the project site and vicinity. In connection therewith, the co-applicants for the proposed project are seeking approval of a boundary reorganization from the San Joaquin Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCo) to annex the project site into the City of Tracy and detach the project site from the Tracy Rural Fire District, as well as City approval of the proposed pre-zoning of the project site to a designation of NEI Specific Plan and an amendment to the boundaries of the Northeast Industrial (NEI) Specific Plan to incorporate the project site into its boundary (as well as any other conforming amendments necessary to ensure consistency). As an employment-generating use, the proposed project is expected to employ approximately 2,103 people on-site at full buildout. Potentially Significant Environmental Effects: Analysis of the Project determined that there would be potentially significant impacts related to Aesthetics, Agricultural Resources, Air Quality, Biological Resources, Cultural Resources, Energy, Geology and Soils, Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Hazards and Hazardous Materials, Hydrology and Water Quality, Land Use and Planning, Noise, Public Services, Transportation, Tribal Cultural Resources, Utilities and Service Systems, and Wildfire. However, feasible mitigation measures identified in the DEIR would reduce the majority of these potential impacts to a less than significant level. Impacts that would remain significant even after implementation of all feasible mitigation measures include the following: • Project-Level and Cumulative Conversion of Prime Farmland (AG-1, AG-CUM-1); • Project-Level and Cumulative Air Quality Impacts (AIR-1, AIR-CUM-1, AIR-2, AIR-CUM-2, AIR-3, AIR-CUM-3); and • Project-Level and Cumulative Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) (TRANS-1 TRANS-CUM-1) • Project-Level Roadway Safety Hazard Impacts (TRANS-2) As stated in the DEIR, the project site is not listed as a hazardous materials site enumerated under Government Code Section 65962.5.

ceqa-22479c411baffd023d.description: Administrative Use Permit application for a new Verizon Wireless telecommunication facility proposed by Vertical Bridge. The project consists of the construction of a new 100-foot monopole within a 50-foot by 50-foot lease area enclosed by an 8-foot-high chain-link fence with barbed wire and brown privacy slats, and a 12-foot-wide access gate equipped with a Knox Box. The facility will include a 600A switchboard, a PG&E transformer on a concrete pad with protective bollards, and a 25-foot by 20-foot Verizon Wireless equipment lease area containing two outdoor equipment cabinets, a 30KW standby generator with a 164-gallon diesel tank and containment basin, and a GPS antenna. The monopole will support multiple Verizon Wireless antennas, including panel, AIR, and microwave antennas, along with associated radios, hybrid cables, and service lights. ceqa-00ae2f17b06cf54b5f.name: Minor Alteration No WA2026048--Pipe Replacement Deferred Maintenance Project
ceqa-00ae2f17b06cf54b5f.projectTitle: Minor Alteration No WA2026048--Pipe Replacement Deferred Maintenance Project
ceqa-00ae2f17b06cf54b5f.description: The project proposes to replace an existing 24-inch metal corrugated pipe (DSID 19635)with a 24-inch reinforced concrete pipe, and remove an existing 12-inch concrete pipe culvert (DSID 19960) andits appurtenant structures. DSID 19635 is a system feature as shown in the “Lower San Joaquin River Flood Control Project Operation and Maintenance Manual for Levees, Irrigation and Drainage Structures, Channels, and Miscellaneous Facilities, Part 1, 1967”. At DSID 19635, the existing inlet and outlet structures and 111.5 feet of existing pipe will be removed and disposed. The replacement pipe will be reinforced concrete, and voids under and around the pipe will be backfilled with controlled low-strength material (CLSM). New inlet and outlet headwalls will be installed at the ends of the pipe and will fall within the footprint of the original design. The replacement pipe will comply with California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Waters, Division 1 (Title 23) which requires a flap gate on the waterside end with provisions for positive closure, either a slide gate or a sluice gate. The slide gate or sluice gate will be housed in a gatewell (riser) at the waterside edge of the levee crown. The levee slopes will be restored to existing grade, and a minimum of four inches of aggregate base will be installed on the levee crown road. At DSID 19960, 35 feet of the existing pipe, drain inlet, outlet structure, and flap gate will be removed. Overexcavation may be performed to remove any sandy or loose native material. An existing fence will be removed to facilitate construction and will be replaced afterwards.
