ceqa-1277786cf0bf8f42cb.name: Goleta Sanitary District Energy Storage Project
ceqa-1277786cf0bf8f42cb.projectTitle: Goleta Sanitary District Energy Storage Project
ceqa-1277786cf0bf8f42cb.description: Goleta Sanitary District (GSD) owns and operates the Goleta Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) located at One William Moffett Place, near the Santa Barbara Municipal Airport, in an unincorporated coastal area of Santa Barbara County, California. In order to achieve its long-term goal of energy neutrality and enhanced energy resilience, GSD proposes to install and operate a solar microgrid and battery energy storage system (BESS) at the Goleta Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) in Goleta, Santa Barbara County, California. The proposed microgrid system includes 807 kW of solar arrays (comprising approximately 45,680-square-feet), a 1,632 kWh/408 kW 4-hour Eos Z3 battery cube on a newly constructed 900-square-foot concrete pad, and approximately 600 feet of electrical ductbank routing. The solar installation, comprised of 1,552 photovoltaic modules, would be installed in three separate areas throughout the WRRF. The proposed system is expected to generate 1,414,000 kWh annually for the WRRF, meeting approximately 36% of its electrical needs.
ceqa-1277786cf0bf8f42cb.crossStreets: William Moffett Place; James Fowler Road, Sandspit Road

ceqa-36369b86c2c660d04f.name: Laguna County Sanitation District Wastewater Reclamation Plant Pond Lining Project
ceqa-36369b86c2c660d04f.projectTitle: Laguna County Sanitation District Wastewater Reclamation Plant Pond Lining Project
ceqa-36369b86c2c660d04f.description: The Laguna County Sanitation District owns and operates a wastewater reclamation plant serving the Orcutt community and the southern unincorporated Santa Maria area. The plant includes a series of ponds and tanks used to equalize variable incoming flows and support secondary and tertiary treatment processes. The project consists of taking Pond A and the Storage Basin out of service, regrading the pond bottoms, removing accumulated debris and vegetation, and installing concrete lining on the pond floors and interior side slopes. These improvements are required to comply with current Regional Water Quality Control Board regulatory criteria. No expansion of pond capacity or change in treatment function is proposed. Construction activities will occur entirely within previously disturbed areas of the existing wastewater reclamation plant.

ceqa-5d93e87612865e3529.name: 836544_36800001_SoCalGas_UGS
ceqa-5d93e87612865e3529.description: Southern California Gas Company has proposed to rework UGS well Miller 8, API #04-083-03411. The well is located in the La Goleta Gas Storage field in Santa Barbara County. The rework would punch and inject resin into the annulus to mitigate pressure buildup and inspect the integrity of the well. The work would include pulling the 3-1/2” completion tubing and associated BHA accessories, cleaning out the liner to bottom (if possible), running diagnostic logs to evaluate source(s) of annular pressure buildup in the 8-5/8” x 6-5/8” annulus, running a Punch-and-Inject tool, and injecting resin into the annulus. After resin injection, an assessment of the injection well would involve running inspection logs to evaluate the 6-5/8” production casing and pressure testing the production casing to meet the minimum pressure requirement (2140 psi). New 3- 1/2” tubing (to include a SSSV, a production packer and profile nipples) would be installed in the well. The well would be returned to service, and a noise/temp survey would be run to verify no communication from the storage zone to the production casing x tubing annulus (6-5/8” x 3-1/2”). Temporary equipment such as pumps and return bins would be needed. No permanent facilities would be constructed. No expansion of associated facilities would be required. Waste materials would be properly disposed of as nonhazardous or hazardous waste, as appropriate, at a facility licensed to accept the waste. The proposed work is expected to last between 45 and 60 days, with variance depending on the amount of fill and/or sand that the operator would need to cleanout in the wellbore, and the amount of resin injection intervals to complete as determined by log interpretations and vendor recommendations.

ceqa-62d8747830df23861a.name: Alisal Ranch Event Barn/Meeting Space
ceqa-62d8747830df23861a.description: The applicant is requesting approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) and Development Permit (DP) for the construction and operation of a new event and meeting facility complex at the existing Alisal Ranch Property located at 1054 Alisal Road with a project site totaling 1.66 acres in size. The application also includes a request for a parking modification to allow a reduction in the number of required parking spaces. The proposed project consists of approximately 14,710 square feet (sf) of new buildings and other improvements and including two event and meeting facilities, associated site improvements, and a parking modification request. The proposed project includes: • Construction of a small event facility in a barn motif, approximately 2,870 sf • Construction of a larger event facility in barn motif, approximately 7,380 sf • Construction of a meeting facility in a barn motif, approximately 2,850 sf • Construction of an entry pavilion to include restrooms, a bar, and storage, 1,410 sf • Associated trash enclosures • Associated site improvements including new landscaping, courtyard, and other frontage improvements • A parking modification request to allow a reduction in required parking to reduce the required additional parking spaces from 40 spaces to an additional 6 spaces, for a total 208 parking spaces • Associated landscaping improvements for the proposed development • Additional parking improvements, driveway, and other associated site improvements to support the event facility.

ceqa-03ed1d0703623c1877.name: Water Well Replacement Project
ceqa-03ed1d0703623c1877.description: VVCSD proposes to replace three aging groundwater wells (Wells 1 B, 3A, and 3B) with three new, replacement potable water wells on an approximately 0.76-acre site (Well Site E) within the Burton Mesa Ecological Reserve, to maintain the District's existing water supply capacity as the existing wells reach the end of their functional lifespan. The new wells would have a maximum expected yield of approximately 800 to 1,350 gallons per minute, similar to the existing wells, and would be equipped with electrical service, metering, monitoring, and security infrastructure. The wells would connect to the District's existing water distribution system through new lateral connections and replacement pipelines extending to existing Well Site 1. Construction would be phased as the existing wells are taken out of service and is anticipated to occur from July 2027 through December 2029. The Project does not propose an increase in groundwater pumping.

ceqa-37a28f654368d35e9f.name: The World is Yours, LLC, Nojoqui Farms Cultivation Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-59197-R5)
ceqa-37a28f654368d35e9f.projectTitle: Lake or Streambed Alteration Agreement for 1800 W. Highway 246-Santa Barbara Westcoast Farms, LLC Cannabis Cultivation Project
ceqa-37a28f654368d35e9f.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement EPIMS Notification No. EPIMS-SBA-59197-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to The World is Yours, LLC as represented by Shannon Conn. The Project includes cannabis cultivation on 53-acres of the property, including grow/canopy, processing, storing, packing, parking and water use and storage. Project operations include vegetation trimming within Nojoqui Creek for access to the well for reporting and occasional maintenance, as-needed repair of irrigation pipes, and water use from the existing well located within Nojoqui Creek.

ceqa-c7a12fe33b6c516791.name: Surfliner Inn
ceqa-c7a12fe33b6c516791.description: The Surfliner Inn Project (Project) is a proposed development that requires a Development Plan, a Coastal Development Permit, and a Conditional Use Permit for a commercial hotel and public improvements. The hotel would be developed and operated on an approximately 1.15-acre site located at 499 Linden Avenue. The Project would include a separate public parking lot on an approximately 1.27-acre property at 399 Linden Avenue. The new two-story hotel would consist of 36 guest rooms, a manager’s unit, café, visitor center, and a roof-top bar/lounge/event space and swimming pool area. The Project would include 28,235 square feet of landscaped areas and a total of 141 vehicular parking spaces. The parking areas would operate under a conjunctive parking arrangement, which would accommodate parking for hotel guests, hotel employees, and the general public.

ceqa-cf5f8c3e0362ed3970.name: Wallover LLC Lot Line Adjustment
ceqa-cf5f8c3e0362ed3970.description: The project is for a Lot Line Adjustment (LLA) to adjust lines between two parcels consisting of 602.42 acres (Existing Parcel 1: APNs 079-100-019, 079-090-006, and 079-090-007) and 34.34 acres (Existing Parcel 2: APN 079-060-024). The resulting parcels will consist of 524.1 acres (Proposed Parcel 1) and 112.66 acres (Proposed Parcel 2). The LLA is summarized as follows: Existing (acres) Proposed (acres) Parcel 1 602.42 524.10 Parcel 2 34.34 112.66 Total 636.76 636.76 The properties are located in the AG-11-100 Zone District. Both parcels are currently in agricultural production as avocado and lemon orchards, and no development is proposed as a part of this LLA. All existing structural development-consisting of two single-family dwellings, staff quarters, five barns, a staff office, two detached garages, a 10-million-gallon reservoir, a water treatment plant, and six wells-is located on Proposed Parcel 1. Proposed Parcel 2 will be served by water wells and septic systems once development is proposed. Access to Proposed Parcel 1 will continue to be provided off Vereda Leyenda Road, and access to Proposed Parcel 2 will continue to be provided off Farren Road. The application involves two legal parcels shown as Assessor's Parcel Numbers 079-060-024, 079-100-019, 079-090-006, and 079-090-007, located in the Goleta Community Plan area, Third Supervisorial District.

ceqa-8cf66bedf695bbc896.name: Abandoned Waterline Removal Project
ceqa-8cf66bedf695bbc896.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-8cf66bedf695bbc896.description: Remove and dispose of a series of surface-mounted abandoned stainless steel and cast-iron waterline pipes along the Gaviota Creek/Highway 101 corridor in Gaviota State Park. Located approximately 30-ft. above Gaviota Creek the waterlines are anchored to the hillside and weave in and around native trees, extending for approximately 1500 feet to the Southbound Highway 101 rest stop at Gaviota Pass in Gaviota State Park. Because of Gaviota Creek’s potential habitat for California red legged frog (CRLF) and steelhead, and the project site’s very constrained access, the pipelines will be secured to a crane boom by personnel stationed on a telescoping or articulated manlift. Once detached from their anchors, pipe sections will be cut and carefully removed by crane and subsequently loaded onto a flatbed trailer for removal and proper disposal. Entry into Gaviota Creek will be limited only to incidental retrieval of any existing debris and debris that may enter the stream as a result of the removal effort. The Project is not expected to require removal of any native trees, but tree trimming is likely, and some removal remains a possibility since many trees have grown in and around the pipeline over the decades since their installation. As there are no suitable locations within this area of the park for equipment and personnel to access the pipeline, equipment will be initially staged in the closed Caltrans rest stop, after which it will be moved into position along the shoulder of the highway. Therefore, Project implementation will necessitate the temporary closure of the Number 2 southbound lane, which necessitates a Caltrans Encroachment Permit as well as a Traffic Control Plan.

ceqa-e189870b1ac25e4f2b.name: Sediment Removal Along State Route 246 at Postmile 19.36 Project
ceqa-e189870b1ac25e4f2b.projectTitle: Sediment Removal Along State Route 246 at Postmile 19.36 Project
ceqa-e189870b1ac25e4f2b.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara
ceqa-e189870b1ac25e4f2b.description: The culvert conveys water from the unnamed ephemeral tributary to Santa Rosa Creek and has a history of plugging with sediment during storms. Accumulated sediment was excavated out of the culvert inlet, outlet, and interior for several years between 2001 – 2019, and has since clogged, leaving less than 1 foot of freeboard space remaining inside the culvert. Caltrans is proposing to trim two branches of one coast live oak (Quercus agrifolia) tree located within the understory beneath the canopy of the tree and overhanging the culvert outlet to provide sufficient clearance for machinery to access the culvert outlet and interior. A loader and/or excavator will be used to remove accumulated sediment from the streambed within 120 feet upstream of the culvert inlet and 30 feet downstream of the culvert outlet, while a tunnel mucker and/or skid steer will be used to remove accumulated sediment within 133 feet of the culvert interior. No vegetation removal along the banks of the unnamed tributary to Santa Rosa Creek is proposed to occur.

ceqa-ef7706856f5a04ef4c.name: One805 Live Event
ceqa-ef7706856f5a04ef4c.description: The Project is a request for a Coastal Development Permit with Hearing (CDH) to allow a two-day temporary event (charitable function) on Friday, September 25, 2026, and Saturday, September 26, 2026. The event days will be limited to a maximum of 2,000 persons on-site (guests, employees, and volunteers combined) per day. The event will begin at 3:00 pm and end at 10:00 pm on each of the two event days. Setup time will be from Monday, September 21, 2026, until the event begins. Clean-up/break-down of the event will be from Sunday, September 27, 2026, until Tuesday, September 29, 2026. All amplified sound will end by 10:00 pm on the days of the event. All generators and outdoor lighting will be shut off by 11:00 pm . A shuttle plan will be implemented that requires guests to shuttle to the event from approved parking locations off-site. Guests are not allowed to park on-site. The event organizer will provide potable water and portable restrooms for the temporary event. No grading or tree removal is proposed. Temporary fencing will be installed around environmentally sensitive habitat areas and bluff tops. Access is provided off Padaro Lane. The property is a 10.26-acre parcel zoned 3E-1 and shown as Assessor's Parcel Number 005-260-018, located at 2825 Padaro Lane in the 5ummerland Community Plan area, First Supervisorial District.

ceqa-41d0b308380d3a7dfb.name: De La Vina Street Bridge Replacement Project (Project) (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-30063-R5)
ceqa-41d0b308380d3a7dfb.projectTitle: De La Vina Street Bridge Replacement Project (Project) (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-30063-R5)
ceqa-41d0b308380d3a7dfb.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-41d0b308380d3a7dfb.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-41d0b308380d3a7dfb.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has amended Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-30063-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to the City of Santa Barbara as represented by Brian D’Amour. The Project is limited to the replacement of the De La Vina Street Bridge over Mission Creek. Project activities include demolition of existing bridge and buildings; utility relocation; creek diversion and dewatering; construction of diversion dams; installation of the new bridge, associated abutments, concrete wingwalls, rock slope protection, and downstream soldier pile walls; use of temporary work areas within the creek; and creek bank revegetation of native riparian species. The Project has been amended to include changes to the Permittee, Project description to include a temporary platform, alterations of the creek work window for Stage 1 in 2026, and an increase in the Project impact acreage.

ceqa-72842fca4f3acb1b6b.name: Moko It LLC -Swirla Vista
ceqa-72842fca4f3acb1b6b.description: The project is a request for a Coastal Development Permit to allow for a commercial change of use and interior tenant improvements to convert an existing Wells Fargo bank space of 756 square feet into a frozen yogurt retail shop. No expansion of the building footprint, no exterior structural modifications, and no changes to parking are proposed. No grading or tree removal is proposed. The parcel is served by the Goleta Water District, the Goleta West Sanitary District, and the Santa Barbara County Fire Protection District. Access is provided directly from Pardall Road . The property is a 0.21-acre parcel zoned General Commercial (C-2) and shown as Assessor's Parcel Number 075-121-007, located at 6530 Pardall Road in the Isla Vista Area, 2nd Supervisorial District.

ceqa-9620dc7bad5155695c.name: Emmawood B1 LLC (Project)
ceqa-9620dc7bad5155695c.description: The Department of Cannabis Control, pursuant to authority granted under Business and Procession Code Division 10, Chapter 2, Section 26012, approved Medium Outdoor commercial cannabis Licenses. The Project involves 8.22 acres (346,396 square feet) of mixed-light and nursery cannabis cultivation. The site is located at APN 001-080-041. Mature and immature plant cultivation will occur within four existing, permitted greenhouse structures totaling 346,396 square feet. Processing (e.g., drying, bucking, temporary storage) and employee break areas will occur in the existing, permitted 12,041 square foot packing house. Transport only distribution is proposed to remove the cultivation cannabis from the project site. The project also includes the following demolition and restoration scope of work on the northern side of the parcel to rectify an expired agricultural dwelling unit permit, to remove unpermitted storage and to enhance the property adjacent to Carpinteria Creek: i) removal of a previously permitted and non-conforming 1,600 square foot mobile home and its corresponding septic system, ii) removal of an incidental vegetable farm area of approximately 1,400 square feet, iii) removal of approximately 2,800 square feet of unpermitted storage/enclosure structures, and v) native plant enhances totaling approximately 45,889 square feet.

ceqa-1c861375e084d2b739.name: Landon Equestrian Arena and Case No. 24DVP-00035
ceqa-1c861375e084d2b739.description: Construction of a 45,000-gross-square-foot enclosed equestrian arena, including a 300-gsf water well pump house for fire suppression and a new 22,000-sf stormwater retention basin. The equestrian facility will be open daily from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. and available to private clients for horse training, breeding, and boarding. The facility operation will include 7 full-time employees and will be served by a new private on-site wastewater treatments system and the existing single-parcel domestic and agricultural water system .

ceqa-ee03ceced8d19ee36e.name: Isla Vista Owner, LLC, Alterations
ceqa-ee03ceced8d19ee36e.description: The project is a request for a Coastal Development Permit with Hearing (CDH) to allow the following: - Window changes. - Relocation of bicycle parking spaces. - Installation of a new trash enclosure. - Replacement of an existing six-foot tall fence. - Replacement of a second-floor access deck, walkway, and stairs. No grading or tree removal is proposed. The parcel is served by the Goleta Water District, Goleta West Sanitary District, and Santa Barbara County Fire Department. Access is provided off Del Playa Drive. The property is a 0.51-acre parcel zoned Medium Density Student Residential (SR-M-8) and shown as Assessor's Parcel Number 075-202-036, located at 6653 Del Playa Dr., in the Goleta Community Plan area, Second Supervisorial District.

ceqa-f31c12a66df3115bcd.name: North Nojoqui Grade Capital Preventative Maintenance and Drainage Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-45998-R5)
ceqa-f31c12a66df3115bcd.projectTitle: North Nojoqui Grade Capital Preventative Maintenance and Drainage Project
ceqa-f31c12a66df3115bcd.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara
ceqa-f31c12a66df3115bcd.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (EPIMS-SBA-45998-R5) pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, the project Applicant, the California Department of Transportation. The Project involves improving 3.75 miles of State Route 101 by replacing culverts and headwalls, shortening culverts, adding rock slope protection, and construction of a 450 linear foot vegetated rock slope protection embankment. The Agreement is being amended to account for an increase in vegetation impacts and increased sediment removal footprint at location 2.

ceqa-aaeb45851770307094.name: Adoption of an Interim Urgency Ordinance Temporarily Prohibiting the Establishment of New Firearms and Ammunition Retailers
ceqa-aaeb45851770307094.projectTitle: Adoption of an Interim Urgency Ordinance Temporarily Prohibiting the Establishment of New Firearms and Ammunition Retailers
ceqa-aaeb45851770307094.description: Adoption of an interim urgency ordinance entitled “An Urgency Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Goleta, California temporarily prohibiting the establishment of any new firearms and ammunition retailers within the City, finding the Ordinance exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act, and declaring the urgency thereof.”

ceqa-dc308dec23ac157898.name: Laguna County Sanitation District Treatment Plant Legacy Facilities Decommissioning Project (LFDECl)
ceqa-dc308dec23ac157898.projectTitle: Laguna County Sanitation District Treatment Plant Legacy Facilities Decommissioning Project (LFDECl)
ceqa-dc308dec23ac157898.description: The Laguna County Sanitation District owns and operates a wastewater reclamation plant serving the Orcutt and southern unincorporated Santa Maria areas. Several older treatment units-including the trickling filter, original headworks, and original grit chamber as well as several pond junction boxes-were constructed under earlier treatment configurations and have since been replaced by modern systems. Although inactive, these structures remain on site and require periodic monitoring to ensure structural integrity and worker safety. The Legacy Facilities Decommissioning Project will formally retire these inactive units by isolating and abandoning obsolete process piping, removing or filling unused structures, demolishing or stabilizing remaining appurtenances, and restoring the surrounding site to support ongoing plant operations. Work also includes reuse of trickling filter rock as structural backfill for future LCSD improvements (storage basin), reducing hauling and disposal requirements, and regrading pond A to prepare for future concrete lining as a separate project. All activities occur entirely within previously disturbed areas of the existing wastewater reclamation plant and do not expand treatment capacity or modify active treatment processes.

ceqa-40638b3f411e5a8678.name: Phase I Oil and Gas Prohibition Ordinance Amendments
ceqa-40638b3f411e5a8678.projectTitle: Phase I Oil and Gas Prohibition Ordinance Amendments
ceqa-40638b3f411e5a8678.description: Case No. 26ORD-00001 amends Article 35.5, Oil and Gas, Wind Energy and Cogeneration Facilities; of Section 35-1, the County Land Use and Development Code (LUDC), of Chapter 35, Zoning, of the Santa Barbara County Code, to prohibit the drilling of new and abandoned oil and gas wells in an effort to ensure enhancement and protection of the environment, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions consistent with the goals of the County's 2030 Climate Action Plan and as authorized by Assembly Bill 3233. Case No. 26ORD-00002 amends Division 9, Oil and Gas Facilities; of Article II, the Coastal Zoning Ordinance (CZO), of Chapter 35, Zoning, of the Santa Barbara County Code, to prohibit the drilling of new and abandoned oil and gas wells in an effort to ensure enhancement and protection the environment, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions consistent with the goals of the County's 2030 Climate Action Plan and as authorized by Assembly Bill 3233. Case No. 26GPA-00007 amends the Coastal Land Use Plan (CLUP) and updates outdated references to Public Resources Code § 30260, 30262, and 30263 to align with recently amended legislation (Senate Bills 704 (2023) and 237 (2025)) that revised the statute and modify existing language to clarify that new onshore exploratory oil and gas wells are prohibited .

ceqa-31241686eb15c25fa0.name: Amendment to the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement with the Department of Water Resources, State of California and Authorizing the Execution Thereof
ceqa-31241686eb15c25fa0.projectTitle: Amendment to the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement with the Department of Water Resources, State of California and Authorizing the Execution Thereof
ceqa-31241686eb15c25fa0.description: On October 1, 1996, the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement Between the Department of Water Resources, State of California, and Central Coast Water Authority Relating to the Operation and Maintenance of the Coastal Branch, Phase II (JPA) was executed. The JPA provides the authority to CCWA to operate and maintain the Coastal Branch facilities on behalf of DWR. This amendment extends CCWA's operation and maintenance activities to December 31, 2026.

ceqa-3a235bf02b5cc64071.name: La Purisima Mission State Historic Park - Cistern Drainage Trenching
ceqa-3a235bf02b5cc64071.projectTitle: La Purisima Mission State Historic Park - Cistern Drainage Trenching
ceqa-3a235bf02b5cc64071.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-3a235bf02b5cc64071.description: Project will repair and restore the existing drainage system associated with the Large Cistern at La Purisima Mission State Historic Park to improve drainage and alleviate an existing water leak. Work will: - Remove approximately 120 square feet of blackberry and poison oak vegetation to access the drainage line; - Expose and trench along approximately 70 linear feet of the existing lower drainage pipe to locate its termination point and identify obstructions; and - Clear pipe blockage and replace broken pipe. All best management practices will be observed to minimize impacts of park resources.

ceqa-6be7db1ef87a7010e7.name: First Amendment to Development Agreement (DA 2026-0001) with WH River Terrace 257, LLC (Williams Homes) for the River Terrace Project (EIR 04-01; SCH No. 200406
ceqa-6be7db1ef87a7010e7.description: An Addendum to a previously certified Environmental Impact Report (EIR 04-01; SCH No. 2004061107) and subsequent Addenda thereto was prepared for this item pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines. An Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for the original River Terrace project was approved on August 16, 2005, and certified as part of the original project approvals. In 2021, the City approved an Addendum to the original River Terrace Residential Project EIR and found that the Addendum was sufficient to document the changes or additions to the project (DR 20-09 and LOM 625). The Addendum in 2026 concluded that “no new or more severe environmental impacts beyond those disclosed in the 2005 Final EIR would occur as a result of the changes to the project proposed by DR 20-09/LOM 625. Based on a review of these materials and the proposed revisions to the Development Agreement included in the First Amendment, City staff have determined that the Addendum to the original River Terrace Residential Project EIR is sufficient to document that no revisions are required to the River Terrace EIR and Addenda thereto previously approved by the City. This action is pursuant to Section 15164 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
ceqa-6be7db1ef87a7010e7.crossStreets: North of the Intersection of East Laurel Avenue and North Twelfth Street

ceqa-358e194d2564b16dcb.name: Utility-Scale Solar Amendments Project
ceqa-358e194d2564b16dcb.description: The project proposes to remove the 600-acre utility-scale solar overlay restriction in Cuyama Valley and allow such utility-scale solar projects with Conditional Use Permits (CUPs) on various zoned lands throughout the unincorporated county. It also introduces a new "community-scale" solar category for smaller facilities and provides a permitting framework and standards for solar projects, including small-scale solar development. The project aims to streamline solar permitting processes and update multiple county plans and regulations to meet state requirements including the County of Santa Barbara Comprehensive Plan; Coastal Land Use Plan; County Land Use and Development Code (LUDC); Montecito LUDC; Article II Coastal Zoning Ordinance; and Uniform Rules for Agricultural Preserves and Farmland Security Zones (Uniform Rules).

ceqa-4aa26bd96290babb02.name: South Creek Streambed Profile Restoration Project (Request No. 1652-2026-100- 001-R5)
ceqa-4aa26bd96290babb02.projectTitle: South Creek Streambed Profile Restoration Project (Request No. 1652-2026-100- 001-R5)
ceqa-4aa26bd96290babb02.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, South Coast Region 5
ceqa-4aa26bd96290babb02.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 5 - South Coast, San Diego
ceqa-4aa26bd96290babb02.description: Pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1652, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife has approved the South Creek Streambed Profile Restoration Project submitted by the White Buffalo Land Trust. The primary purpose of the project is to restore degraded stream channels and floodplain function through habitat improvement, sediment control, bank stabilization, and large woody material enhancement. The project will mediate the limiting factors of riparian dysfunction and spawning requirements. The species likely to benefit from this Project include southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss).

ceqa-f9753057290b6fde27.name: The Groves Defensible Space
ceqa-f9753057290b6fde27.description: The project consists of 4 shaded fuel reduction treatments and treatment of emergency access road totaling 9.6acres located in the County owned open space intermixed with The Groves Housing Development in the foothills of the unincorporated community of Orcutt. The project will utilize hand crews to reduce flammable fuel volume by removing dead material, reducing ladder fuels, and selectively thinning standing vegetation. The existing fuel is predominately mature oak woodland with scattered chaparral and stands of Conifers. Mature trees will be limbed and pruned of dead branches. The cut material will be chipped and spread uniformly on site. The shrub dominated areas will be treated with a residual mosaic approach, leaving scattered shrubs and islands of intact formation comprising approximately 30% of the original cover. No mature trees will be removed. No work will occur within 50 feet of a riparian corridor. The project will greatly increase the defensible space around the community and also protect the open space wildland from a fire starting from the surrounding residential developments. The project will also involve maintenance of established emergency access road to the south of the Groves housing development. No heavy equipment is authorized under this document. A query of the National Diversity Database will be performed for each treatment to check for the presence of endangered plants and/or animals. DFW will be consulted for input as necessary. Chips will not be deposited within the standard width of a watercourse or lake protection zone.

ceqa-cdbfb436f5ff808e05.name: Caird Multi-Unit Housing Development
ceqa-cdbfb436f5ff808e05.description: The project is for a “use by right” approval of an 1,198-unit multi-family housing development pursuant to Government Code Section 65583.2(c). The project is also utilizing Senate Bill 330 and State Density Bonus Law. 300 units will be very low and low-income rental homes, and 898 units will be for-sale market-rate homes. The affordable rental homes will be constructed in conjunction with People’s Self-Help Housing. Additionally, the project applicant is partnering with a major local employer who will purchase approximately 160 of the market-rate homes to sell to their employees at below-market rates, subsidizing the differential. The homes will be designed in a variety of housing types and sizes, including single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums. The proposed unit breakdown is as follows: Residential Dwelling Unit Type Number of Units Market Rate – For Sale 898 Very Low Income (30-50% of AMI) Rental 60 Low Income (50-80% of AMI) Rental 240 Total Number of Units 1,198 Total Number of Affordable Units 300 (25% of total units) The project includes seven different for-sale, market-rate product types and affordable rental homes with a range of bedroom count and size. Below is a summary of the housing types: Type Bedroom/Baths Size (net sq. ft.) Garage Parking No. of Units Product 1: 3-Story Carriage Units 1-3/1.5-3 1,120-1,862 1-2 162 Product 2: 4-Story Flats 3/2 1,718-1,935 2 120 Product 3: 3-Story Flats & Townhomes 3/3-3.5 1,803-1,917 2 158 Product 4: 3-Story Flats & Townhomes 1-4/1-3.5 1,080-2,389 1-2 162 Product 5: 3-Story Townhomes 2-3/2.5 1,546-2,060 2 162 Product 6: 2-Story Detached Single-Family Dwelling 3-4/2.5-3.5 2,405-2,586 2 39 Product 7: 3-Story Townhome 3-4/3.5 2,047-2,530 2 95 Affordable: 4-Story Flats/Parking Structure 1-3/1-2 695-1,268 1-3 300 The project will be constructed in phases anticipated over an approximate 10-year period, based on market demand for home purchase. Project construction is expected to commence on the east side of the project site and make its way westward over time. The affordable housing buildings are also planned to be constructed in phases starting with the east building and then moving to the west building. The project phases are proposed as follows: Phase I: • Units – 148 affordable apartments and 159 multi-family market-rate units. • Infrastructure – Construct South Patterson improvements, Ekwill improvements along northern property line of Ekwill property, and temporary road from South Patterson along northern property line of 905 South Patterson and western property line of Giorgi property connecting to Ekwill Street. Phase II: • Units – 133 multi-family market-rate units and 39 single-family dwellings. Phase III: • Units – 152 affordable apartments and 60 multi-family market-rate units. • Infrastructure – Park construction to commence no later than issuance of final certificate of occupancy for Phase III, and completed within 24 months. Phase IV: • Units – 507 multi-family market-rate units • Infrastructure – Prior to construction of Phase IV, permanent access road from South Patterson to Ekwill/Ward Drive to be constructed. The project includes an approximately eight-acre public park with a sports field, playground, bike path, picnic area, and space for a community farmer’s marketplace. Public parking, including 60 public parking spaces, is proposed along the southern boundary of the park. A common area pool, recreation center, and community gathering amenity building is provided for use by all on-site residents. Approximately 41% of the site is dedicated to public, common, and private open space including tot lots, common area picnic and barbecue areas, and the public park. Each of the affordable housing buildings also contain a community amenity program including multipurpose and classroom spaces, common area kitchen, storage, and administrative space. Bicycle and walking paths are provided throughout the project development and will connect the community to the Class I Atascadero Multi-Purpose bikeway (Obern Trail) as well as the Class I bike path along the east side of Maria Ygnacio Creek. On-site stormwater detention is provided throughout the site in bioswales and bio retention basins. Parking for the market-rate homes will be provided in private garages connected to the homes and on-street parking depending on the product type. Parking for the affordable homes will be provided in parking garages within the center of each of the affordable buildings. On-street visitor parking will also be provided throughout the project site. A total of 2,790 parking spaces are provided for the 1,198 units, common amenity area, and public park. 1,048 bicycle parking spaces will be provided throughout the project site. Pursuant to APCD’s recommendation, the Project will evaluate incorporation of additional exposure reduction measures, including high-efficiency mechanical ventilation systems, enhanced filtration, stand-alone HEPA air filtration units, and resident education regarding filter maintenance. Feasible measures will be incorporated in the final construction design and plans. The Project will also pursue opportunities to provide enhanced filtration and/or resident information materials regarding the importance of maintaining HVAC and air filtration systems to support indoor air quality. The following waivers are requested pursuant to State Density Bonus Law: • Waiver to exceed DR Zone District 35-foot height limit. Project will have a maximum height of 66 feet from existing grade (55’-2” from finished slab). • Waiver to reduce DR Zone District building setbacks, in compliance with the “Setback Modifications Requested for Caird Multi-Family Homes” table included in the project materials. • Waiver to reduce DR Zone District parking setbacks. • Waiver to reduce DR Zone District private open space requirement for each dwelling unit. Private open space will be provided for each unit as specified on Sheet Site-6 of approved plans. • Waiver to reduce required 50-foot creek buffer to approximately 25 feet for flatwork and minor improvements; all habitable structures are setback a minimum of 50 feet from creek top-of-bank. • Waiver to reduce DR Zone District Common Open Space requirement to allow for less than 40% of the net site area to be common open space. The project provides approximately 36% public and common open space. The project includes frontage improvements along both sides of South Patterson Ave., including landscaped medians, bike lanes, parking, sidewalks, lighting, curbs, and gutters. Grading will include approximately 50,300 cubic yards of cut and 289,100 cubic yards of fill. Native trees that will be removed for the project consist of two coast redwoods, 13 pacific willows, two arroyo willows, and two coast live oaks. Three additional coast live oak trees will be significantly disturbed. The parcel will be served by the Goleta Water District, the Goleta Sanitary District, and the Santa Barbara County Fire Department. Access will be provided off of South Patterson Ave, Ekwill Street, and Gwyne Ave to Rhodes Ave. The project site is 87.4 acres, zoned DR-20/25 and DR-30/40, and shown as Assessor's Parcel Numbers 071-190-036, 065-090-031, 065-230-012, and 071-140-048, located at 905 S Patterson Ave., 600 S Patterson Ave., and 620 S Patterson Ave., in the Eastern Goleta Valley Community Plan area, Second Supervisorial District.

ceqa-6d94b08a36fb9059cb.name: APPROVAL OF KUBO GROUP (KUBO)’S EXCEPTIONAL METHD FOR ANALYZING THE DESIGN OF A HEATED GREENHOUSE IN SANTA MARIA, CALIFORNIA
ceqa-6d94b08a36fb9059cb.projectTitle: APPROVAL OF KUBO GROUP (KUBO)’S EXCEPTIONAL METHD FOR ANALYZING THE DESIGN OF A HEATED GREENHOUSE IN SANTA MARIA, CALIFORNIA
ceqa-6d94b08a36fb9059cb.description: The California Energy Commission (CEC) adopts and regularly updates regulations for new construction, additions, and alterations to residential and nonresidential buildings, which are contained in California Code of Regulations, Parts 1 and 6 (the California Energy Code). These regulations go through an extensive public process and are adopted at a CEC business meeting before going into effect. Part 1 of the Energy Code includes administrative regulations for implementation. In certain circumstances, interested parties or the CEC may identify Exceptional Methods that meet the minimum requirements of the Energy Code, but that require additional regulatory action to ensure compliance and consistency with the Energy Code. In these situations, section 10-109(e) of the 2025 Energy Code states that, “The Commission may approve an exceptional method that analyzes a design, material, or device that cannot be adequately modeled using the public domain computer programs. Applications for approval of exceptional methods shall include all information needed to verify the method's accuracy.” On June 24, 2026, KUBO submitted an application for CEC approval of KUBO’s Exceptional Method for the specified project design that demonstrates compliance with mandatory requirements for nonopaque envelopes in conditioned greenhouses as provided by the 2025 Energy Code. The application included documentation that analyzed the performance of a conditioned greenhouse project in Santa Maria, demonstrating that the design meets or exceeds the equivalent requirements of Section 120.6(h). The application was available for public comment through July 24, 2026. No comments were received. CEC staff reviewed the application submitted on June 24, 2026, including supporting analysis, and all written comments submitted. CEC staff’s analysis confirmed that: 1. KUBO’s conditioned greenhouse design for the specified project in Santa Maria, CA cannot be adequately modeled by any of the public domain computer programs used to demonstrate compliance with the 2025 Energy Code, 2. The proposed Exceptional Method adequately models the performance of KUBO’s design for the specified conditioned greenhouse in Santa Maria, California,, and 3. The proposed Exceptional Method for analyzing KUBO’s design, as applied to the Santa Maria project described in the application, accurately demonstrates a modest reduction of the energy budget compared to the mandatory requirements for nonopaque envelopes in conditioned greenhouses in the 2025 Energy Code. CEC staff and the Executive Director recommended that the CEC approve KUBO’s proposed Exceptional Method that analyzes the design of a conditioned greenhouse project in Santa Maria, California, consistent with Section 10-109(e). KUBO’s Exceptional Method was approved at the CEC’s August 17, 2026 Business Meeting.

ceqa-d3b3f63940403397cd.name: State Street Master Plan
ceqa-d3b3f63940403397cd.description: The State Street Master Plan is a long-term visioning document for the revitalization of downtown over the next 50 years. The State Street Master Plan covers the 400 through 1300 blocks of State Street (between Gutierrez and Sola Streets), approximately one mile in addition to the adjacent paseos, plazas, parking facilities, and cross streets that make up the broader downtown area.

ceqa-93fc667db403c4aef5.name: Goleta Water District - Corona Reservoir Rehabilitation & Filter Washtrough Replacements
ceqa-93fc667db403c4aef5.projectTitle: Goleta Water District - Corona Reservoir Rehabilitation & Filter Washtrough Replacements
ceqa-93fc667db403c4aef5.description: This project consists of replacing the deteriorated fiberglass filter troughs at CDMWTP with new stainless steel troughs and rehabilitating Corona Reservoir by removing the deteriorating interior liner, replacing join sealant, repairing concrete cracking and palling, replacing the entry ladder, and addressing a suspected minor floor leak. The filter troughs, in service since 1974, have deteriorated due to continuous exposure to water, sunlight and treatment chemicals. Replacement will improve filter reliability, particularly during outages, and ensure uninterrupted treatment. Rehabilitation of Corona Reservoir will preserve a critical storage facility and sustain reliable water service. Without this work, continued deterioration could impact water quality, create safety hazards, or force an emergency shutdown.

ceqa-a478488c5d96b28f54.name: 7360 Hollister Avenue Project
ceqa-a478488c5d96b28f54.description: The project would develop twelve (12) multi-family residential buildings with approximately 59 dwelling units on approximately 3.17 acres (2.92 net acres). The project would have a density of approximately 20.2 dwelling units per acre. This development would utilize the State Density Bonus Law and Senate Bill 330.

ceqa-811989200f61e88820.name: Santa Barbara Community College District Solar Power Array & Battery Energy Storage System Microgrid
ceqa-811989200f61e88820.projectTitle: Santa Barbara Community College District Solar Power Array & Battery Energy Storage System Microgrid
ceqa-811989200f61e88820.description: Notice of Exemption for the installation of solar photovoltaic carports, battery energy storage systems, transformers, inverters, and related electrical infrastructure within existing parking facilities on the East and West Campuses. The Board of Trustees of Santa Barbara City College has determined that the project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to the applicable categorical exemptions identified in the Notice of Exemption. The project includes the installation of 1.6 megawatts of carport-mounted solar arrays and associated battery energy storage systems across parking facilities on the East and West Campuses of Cliff Campus. The system will deliver 8-24+ hours of energy resilience, reduce carbon footprint, and lower long-term energy costs through renewable energy generation.

ceqa-215219a00890e200ac.name: Santa Barbara City College Educational Collections
ceqa-215219a00890e200ac.projectTitle: Santa Barbara City College Educational Collections
ceqa-215219a00890e200ac.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Marine Region 7
ceqa-215219a00890e200ac.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 7 - Marine, Monterey
ceqa-215219a00890e200ac.description: The Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a permit to Santa Barbara City College pursuant to Fish and Game Code Section 2081(a) for educational purposes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to take steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) during the course of sampling, subject to terms and conditions set forth in the permit. The purpose of this sampling is for the Santa Barbara City College’s permanent educational collections for classes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to potentially capture steelhead trout during surveys. The applicant will conduct year-round permanent collection sampling of nearshore marine species using bottom trawls through December 31, 2029.

ceqa-a0e8b5c3a3233f518c.name: South Creek Streambed Profile Restoration Project
ceqa-a0e8b5c3a3233f518c.projectTitle: South Creek Streambed Profile Restoration Project
ceqa-a0e8b5c3a3233f518c.agency: California Regional Water Quality Control Board, Central Coast Region 3
ceqa-a0e8b5c3a3233f518c.agencyName: Regional Water Quality Control Board, Region 3 - Central Coast, San Luis Obispo
ceqa-a0e8b5c3a3233f518c.description: The project will restore streambed profile and riparian function along South Creek, an intermittent, deeply incised tributary of La Hoya Creek within the Salsipuedes Creek watershed, which drains to the Santa Ynez River. The project applies low-tech, process-based restoration (LTPBR) to reverse channel incision and re-establish the connection between the stream and its historic floodplain. Restoration is achieved by installing simple, hand-built structures that mimic natural wood accumulations and beaver activity; post-assisted log structures (PALS) and beaver dam analogues (BDAs). These structures slow surface flows, capture and store sediment, raise the local water table, and initiate recovery of native riparian vegetation and aquatic habitat over time.

ceqa-410f2a61d8e598f2a1.name: Modular K-Rail System
ceqa-410f2a61d8e598f2a1.description: To prepare for the forecasted severe 2026/27 rainy season, the Airport proposes the temporary installation of a modular K-Rail system between Firestone Road and Firestone Ditch. Historically, inadequate floodwater conveyance in this area caused two airfield closures in 2025 and 2026. Therefore, this temporary barrier is critical to prevent future creek overtopping and protect the Airport, a major community transportation hub, from flooding.

ceqa-a217e917395dce347c.name: Effluent Storage Reservoir Expansion
ceqa-a217e917395dce347c.description: The Laguna County Sanitation District plans to expand the existing effluent storage reservoir located north of the Wastewater Reclamation Plant following removal of the soil stockpile created when the existing reservoir was constructed from 1991 to 1993. The proposed engineered expansion of the effluent storage reservoir would increase the reservoir capacity from 290 to 471 million gallons and increase the reservoir area from approximately 36 acres to 60 acres.
ceqa-a217e917395dce347c.developmentType: Waste Treatment:Sewer (Treated municipal wastewater storage reservoir expansion)(MGD 1.7)

ceqa-910d93c2dd9bbf4727.name: SBA Taxiways E, A3, and A5 Pavement Reconstruction Project
ceqa-910d93c2dd9bbf4727.projectTitle: SBA Taxiways E, A3, and A5 Pavement Reconstruction Project
ceqa-910d93c2dd9bbf4727.description: This Project consists of four different parts; Taxiway E “Echo”, Taxiway A3 “Alpha Three”, Taxiway A5 “Alpha Five”, and infield stormwater infiltration trenches. The three taxiways at the Santa Barbara Municipal Airport (Airport) require varying levels of large-scale pavement repairs to restore the asphalt concrete pavement to like new condition. Taxiway E will undergo a full-depth reconstruction for approximately 1,700 feet in length. During the reconstruction process, the Airport will reshape the geometry of Taxiway E, therefore expanding the amount of impervious pavement to enhance the safety and circulation of large commercial aircraft in the area south of the Airport terminal. Taxiway A3 will require a mill (grind) and fill (repave) rehabilitation, less intrusive than reconstruction, for a portion of the total taxiway, approximately 200 feet in length. Taxiway A5 has the most minimal pavement rehabilitation planned that only requires a protective seal coat applied to the taxiway surface for the whole length of the taxiway, approximately 300 feet. In response to the expansion of impervious pavement, the Airport will also add new infield stormwater infiltration trenches, primarily constructed of gravel, to encourage slow stormwater infiltration into the surrounding soils. Changes to the geometry of Taxiway E will also require relocation of taxiway edge lights along with its buried electrical conduit and modifications to the buried storm drain piping and infrastructure.

ceqa-dcc3e95517066d02fa.name: Phased Capital Improvements at Lower Mission Creek (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2024-003-05A1 (ITP))
ceqa-dcc3e95517066d02fa.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an amended ITP (No. 2081(b)-2024-003-05A1), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to the Santa Barbara County Public Works Department (Permittee). The Project involves a series of flood control improvements from Canon Perdido Street Bridge downstream to the Gutierrez Street Bridge. Project activities include re-grading the bed slope, vegetation removal, removal of old in-stream structures, bank armoring, diversion and dewatering activities, and installing riparian habitat zones above the vertical concrete wall outside of the channel and within the banks of the vertical concrete walls. The Project would increase the channel capacity to 3,400 cubic feet per second (cfs) and would provide approximately a 20-year level of flood protection. The Project will result in impacts to 2,600 linear feet of southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss) habitat. The project is expected to result in incidental take of southern California steelhead, which is/are designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). The amended ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation. On August 17, 2026, CDFW issued an amended ITP for the Project. Changes included in the amendment allow for Permittee to modify or secure in place water diversions or dewatering systems when precipitation is predicted, if done in accordance with a CDFW-approved diversion or dewatering plan and modify some language throughout the ITP for clarification purposes.

ceqa-800102c4c072f695f9.name: Water Well Replacement Project
ceqa-800102c4c072f695f9.description: VVCSD proposes to construct three (3) new replacement potable water wells, with a maximum expected yield of approximately 800 to 1,350 gallons per minute (gpm), to replace existing Wells 1B, 3A, and 3B, as they reach the end of their functional lifespan. Each new well would be equipped with electrical service, metering, monitoring, and security infrastructure, and would be connected to the District's existing water distribution system through new lateral connections and replacement pipelines extending to the District's existing Well Site 1. Temporary construction staging would occur in the vicinity of Exit 702/704 from SR-1. Construction is anticipated to take approximately 30 months, from July 2027 through December 2029.
ceqa-800102c4c072f695f9.developmentType: Water Facilities (Three replacement groundwater wells)(Type Groundwater well, MGD 5.832)

ceqa-2571084c1315ca6963.name: Housing Plan Program EIR
ceqa-2571084c1315ca6963.description: The Housing Plan implements 32 programs in the adopted 6th Cycle Housing Element, including ongoing programs, procedural changes, municipal code amendments, and other actions to meet state housing requirements and accommodate the City Regional Housing Needs Allocation of 8,001 new housing units. The proposed project includes adoption of an Adaptive Reuse Ordinance, preparation of a planning framework for the La Cumbre Plaza Planning Area, amendments to the Average Unit-Size Density (AUD) Incentive Program, adoption of Objective Design and Development Standards, updates to the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) ordinance, and process improvements to streamline permitting; Associated amendments to the Municipal Code, General Plan, and Local Coastal Program to maintain consistency with the Housing Element and State law. For environmental analysis purposes, this EIR assumes a conservative scenario in which up to 8,001 housing units could be permitted and constructed by 2035, along with associated nonresidential development anticipated under cumulative conditions. These updates do not authorize specific development projects but provide the regulatory and policy framework.

ceqa-bf66b2e26646f4e99e.name: CASF, Surfnet Communications Inc. Santa Barbara Fiber Project
ceqa-bf66b2e26646f4e99e.projectTitle: CASF, Surfnet Communications Inc. Santa Barbara Fiber Project
ceqa-bf66b2e26646f4e99e.description: In compliance with D.22-11-023, Staff determined that the Santa Barbara Fiber Project is eligible to receive up to $9,190,327 in CASF Infrastructure Account grant funding. Surfnet Communications, Inc. proposes to serve 336 unserved locations by constructing a FTTH network with up to 1,000 Megabits per second (Mbps) download and 1,000 Mbps upload in Santa Barbara County. The California Advanced Services Fund (CASF) program was initiated in 2008, after the program was first adopted by the Commission in Decision (D.) 07-12-054 and enacted into statute pursuant to Senate Bill (SB) 1193.

ceqa-662b6d98d0f9e53620.name: BDZ, Inc.
ceqa-662b6d98d0f9e53620.description: The Project will consist of The project is a request for up to 40 acres of outdoor cannabis cultivation under 12-foot high hoop structures. There will be no processing on-site. There will be up to 3harvests per year, with each lasting a maximum of 4 weeks. All cultivation will be set back at minimum 50 feet from the property lines. Existing structures on site include a 1,201 square foot farm employee dwelling and a 255 square foot concrete patio. Proposed structures to be used for cannabis activities include one 120 square foot guard shack, seven 320 square foot shipping containers to be used for cultivation equipment and fertilizer storage and twenty four 5,000 gallon fertigation tanks. An existing generator on-site will be disconnected from the well and will be used as an emergency back-up generator. Also proposed is a 30,000 square foot staging area to be used as a loading area.

ceqa-5dabd2b9d16c5f653a.name: Newlove 241 Rework (569898_PCEC_OG)
ceqa-5dabd2b9d16c5f653a.description: Pacific Coast Energy is applying for a permit to rework Newlove 241 and return the well to production. This well is located on the Newlove lease within the Orcutt Hill Oil Field boundaries in Santa Barbara County and is currently an active producer. This proposed rework will add 110 feet of new perforations across the Diatomite formation. Newlove 241 is currently drilled into the Diatomite formation to a depth of 962’ MD. There is no BFW/USDW in the immediate area of this location, however ephemeral water sands may exist to a depth of 100’ MD. This project will consist of minor site preparation and remediation work both prior to and post rig mobilization. Temporary equipment will be needed to complete the project which includes a backhoe, workover rig, pumps, water trucks, cement trucks. In addition, vehicles to transport personnel, materials and to mobilize and demobilize equipment and waste will be utilized. No permanent facilities will be constructed. No expansion of associated facilities will be required. Any waste materials generated will be properly disposed of as non-hazardous or hazardous waste at a facility licensed to accept the waste. All work will take place within the Newlove 241 location and the roads leading to and from that location. PCEC is asking the State of California for a rework permit to add additional perforations across the Diatomite formation in Newlove 241. Once this work is completed the well will be returned to production. The proposed project consists of the California Department of Conservation, Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) approving 1 permit for Pacific Coast Energy Company LP to rework the well listed below, in the Orcutt Oil Field: API number: 0408322670, well name: Newlove 241

ceqa-7d5fcd067f3d00ea3a.name: Pacific Pipeline Check Valve Project
ceqa-7d5fcd067f3d00ea3a.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-7d5fcd067f3d00ea3a.description: This project entails granting Pacific Pipeline Company (“PPC”) access to Gaviota State Beach solely for the purpose of accessing and excavating the existing check valve 325A CHK-11 GC (“Check Valve”) within pipeline Segment CA-325 at Gaviota State Park for regular maintenance and inspection, as well as installation of a ten-foot diameter corrugated metal pipe and lid around the existing Check Valve. The purpose of the pipe and lid is to allow operators to periodically access the Check Valve by opening a lid, thereby eliminating the need to repeatedly excavate the site. Access and installation of the pipe and lid require excavating an approximately 1,152 cubic foot area around the existing Check Valve. A construction crew will access the project site using Gaviota State Park Road 28 to reach the Check Valve location, where the temporary workspace will be approximately 75 feet long by 50 feet wide. Public access will not be affected during the planned project activities. During proposed work, PPC staff and/or its subcontractors shall adhere to all applicable municipal laws, state laws, federal laws, and standard construction best management practices to minimize the potential for environmental impacts and maximize safety of staff and park users.

ceqa-a5f34bdb8bbf612f72.name: Rancho La Laguna Development Plan and Vesting Tract Map
ceqa-a5f34bdb8bbf612f72.projectTitle: Rancho La Laguna Development Plan and Vesting Tract Map
ceqa-a5f34bdb8bbf612f72.description: The Project consists of a housing development project pursuant to the “Builder’s Remedy” provisions set forth in the Housing Accountability Act (Government Code Section 65589.5). Specifically, the Project includes a subdivision of two legal lots that constitute the Project site to create thirteen lots whose sizes range between 150 and 600 acres. The map will also establish a Residential Development Envelope (RDE) on each lot within which a single-family dwelling and Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) will be located. Additionally, ten (10) deed-restricted agricultural employee dwellings will be located within the RDE on Lot 7. Access to each of the proposed RDEs will be provided via improved and extended existing ranch roads. Each of the proposed RDEs would be served by a private on-site septic system utilizing the leach lines. All septic system components would be located within RDEs. Water service would be provided by either a public water system (preferred) or five State Small Water Systems Proposed under Case Nos. 24CUP-00026, 25CUP-00001, -00002, -00003, and -00004. Necessary access and utility easements will primarily be co-located within proposed access roads and driveways.
ceqa-a5f34bdb8bbf612f72.crossStreets: Alisos Canyon Road and Foxen Canyon Road

ceqa-76fa996588a098e78b.name: Solomon Canyon Shoulder Widening and Rumble Strip Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-34794-R5)
ceqa-76fa996588a098e78b.projectTitle: Solomon Canyon Rumble Strip/Shoulder Widening Project
ceqa-76fa996588a098e78b.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara
ceqa-76fa996588a098e78b.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed and amended Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (EPIMS-SBA-34794-R5), pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, the project Applicant, California Department of Transportation, District 5. The California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) is improving 12.9 miles of State Route 1 by widening the shoulders, replacing the guardrail, raising the road profile, replacing utility poles, adding rumble strips, installing a California tiger salamander exclusionary berm between postmiles 41.1 and 41.2, and replacing a paved roadside swale at post mile 41.73 with a vegetated swale. Project activities include culvert lengthening to accommodate the wider road resulting in permanent impacts to 14 unnamed streams. Work covered under this Agreement includes work within the bed, bank, and channel at 14 stream locations within the project area. The Agreement is being amended to allow for diversion and dewatering activities within the project area.

ceqa-53d45314321f0938c3.name: Wastewater Treatment Plant Improvements Project
ceqa-53d45314321f0938c3.description: The current WWTP process does not meet effluent water quality limits which went into effect in August 2024. The purpose of the project is to implement water quality improvements to address this deficiency. The project includes the replacement of the existing biologic process system that utilizes aeration ponds with an activated sludge process using a membrane bioreactor system (MBR); storm drain replacement, and re-lining of the wet wells at the Bell Street Lift Station. The beneficiaries of the project include the community of Los Alamos, as it receives its wastewater services from the District.

ceqa-8cf1297c8123d7ea57.name: San Roque Debris Basin Outlet Repair
ceqa-8cf1297c8123d7ea57.projectTitle: San Roque Debris Basin Outlet Repair
ceqa-8cf1297c8123d7ea57.agency: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-8cf1297c8123d7ea57.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-8cf1297c8123d7ea57.description: The San Roque Debris Basin, constructed in 1964 following the Coyote Fire, is an aging flood control facility and a total barrier to steelhead migration. The culvert pipe running through the existing dam embankment is damaged and not functioning from previous years of intense storms. The proposed improvements will consist of removing the existing concreted earthen filled dam, portions of the grouted rock embankment and 36-inch culvert. The replacement is opening the dam to an ungrouted, natural streambed between two grouted rock side slopes, using the stream simulation design technique. The grade at the current inlet structure will be lowered by approximately 5 ft at the thalweg rising in the basin to existing grades for a constant slope similar to reference reach conditions upstream.

ceqa-18f233f71231e7964b.name: Wandermnet farms LLC - Special Events
ceqa-18f233f71231e7964b.description: The Project is a request for a Minor Conditional Use Permit (MCUP) to allow for 12 temporary events per year, with a maximum of two per month. Each event will be limited to 150 guests. The events will consist of receptions, parties, weddings, and similar gatherings, and be conducted entirely outdoors utilizing the existing barn covered patio area, lawn area immediately south of the barn, and the residence pool deck and lawn area immediately adjacent to the residence. The interior of the barn and residence will not be used for temporary events. All facilities for the events will be portable and temporary in nature, including but not limited to: event tents, portable restrooms, portable catering amenities, a rental dance floor, rental dining tables, rental seating, temporary lighting, and temporary sound equipment. All temporary lighting will be fully shielded and directed downward. No cooking facilities are proposed, and all food and beverages will be provided by an event/catering company and brought to the site for each event. No permanent improvements are proposed as part of the project. Special events may occur up to 12 days per year from 10:00 am – 8:00 pm. Amplified music is proposed at the residence pool deck and background music is proposed at the barn patio. Noise levels will not exceed 65 dBA at the property lines. All amplified noise and temporary lighting will end by 8:00 pm. Set up for events will take place two days before the event, and clean-up will be completed within 48 hours of event completion. All noise generating activities related to equipment set-up and clean-up would be limited to the hours of 8:00 am – 5:00 pm. All proposed special events will be managed by a contracted event company which provides comprehensive event planning, preparation, event management, and post-event cleaning including temporary event structure and waste removal. A temporary catering tent will be located adjacent to the residence garage, with an adjacent bar and cocktail tent located south of the existing barn. Food preparation will be conducted entirely within the catering tent with light appetizers provided within the cocktail tent area and meal service to tables provided at the patio area south of the residence. The residential patio area will also accommodate a temporary dance floor and dining seating area, temporarily placed over the existing swimming pool. A live music (DJ/band) area will be located immediately south of the dining seating and dance floor area with the music directed north towards the residence. Temporary lighting provided by the event company will be provided in the patio area as needed. Temporary lighting will be powered using existing electrical receptacles at the patio without the need for a portable generator. Access to the event site will be provided by an existing paved private driveway from Toro Canyon Park Road. The existing driveway is 16 feet in width, with two feet of clearance on each side. Parking for special events with up to 50 guests will be located entirely on the property. Parking for events with greater than 50 guests will be provided offsite with private transportation from local hotels or the St. Joseph Church parking lot located approximately seven miles from the property in the City of Carpinteria. The shuttle bus will be parked in the existing driveway adjacent to the residence during the event, and this location will serve as the pickup/drop-off location for guests. The shuttle service will include scheduled pickup and drop-off times, and will typically require fewer than four round trips for the largest events. A total of 41 parking spaces can be accommodated on site. These areas include a gravel parking area near the property entrance, a compacted earthen parking area along the existing paved driveway near the barn, a compacted gravel area at the northern portion of the property adjacent to the water tank (north of the vineyard), and an ADA accessible parking space located in the existing flat parking area immediately adjacent to the existing barn. The existing topography and landscaping will minimize views of all proposed parking areas. Directional and parking signs will be provided, including "No Parking" and "Fire Lane - No Stopping" signs as required by the Fire Department. Each event will include approximately 27 employees (catering, DJ, personnel, etc.). Caterers and staff will leave the property by 9:00 pm on the evening of an event. 15 temporary parking spaces for employees and one ADA parking space will be available onsite. These parking spaces will be clearly marked and unavailable for guest parking. The property is served by the Ridgeland Mutual Water Company (RMWC), an existing private well which is used for agricultural irrigation, and a private onsite septic system. No water or wastewater treatment services will be required for the Project due to the temporary nature of facilities. The portable bathrooms will be located adjacent to the barn and will be delivered to the site for each event and removed at the end of the event (typically the next business day). No grading, no tree removal, and no landscaping is proposed with this permit. The Carpinteria-Summerland Fire Protection District will continue to provide fire service, and the Santa Barbara County Sheriff will continue to provide police services. Access to the event site will be provided off Toro Canyon Park Road via an existing driveway. The property is a 56-acre parcel zoned AG-I-40 and MT-TORO-40, and shown as Assessor’s Parcel Number 155-170-035, located at 3580 Toro Canyon Park Road in the Toro Canyon Community Plan Area, First Supervisorial District.

ceqa-63390290fb06a376c3.description: The Proposed Project has been developed to accommodate existing and forecast passenger demands at the Airport, as identified in collaboration with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The Proposed Project consists of improvements to the John T. Rickard Airline Terminal (Terminal) that would include an additional 16,500 square feet (sf) (approximately 310 sf larger than presented in the FPEIR) to the footprint of the Terminal and the redevelopment of approximately 20,400 square yards (sy) of Terminal and overflow apron (approximately 11,200 sy smaller than presented in the FPEIR). The airside pavement would not be expanded beyond existing limits. Additionally, compared to what was presented in the FPEIR, the Proposed Project would result in one fewer passenger loading bridge and a new access roadway instead of the realignment of the Terminal loop road. The adjustment to surface parking would result in the demolition of Building 122, which was not specifically addressed in the FPEIR, but would have been necessary for the expansion of the short-term parking lot and the extension of the Terminal loop road that were analyzed in the FPEIR. A portion of Building 122 is used as a breakroom for Airport employees, and the rest is leasable space. Following demolition, the breakroom would be accommodated within the redeveloped Terminal area.

ceqa-d9a59a9742ff34d034.name: SANDYLAND SHORELINE PROTECTION PROJECT
ceqa-d9a59a9742ff34d034.description: The proposed Project would repair and restore the 1983 design of the existing 3,700-foot-long Sandyland Seawall (shoreline protection in the form of a rock revetment) located between Sand Point Road residences and the coastline. Specifically, the proposed Project would involve repairing the revetment by placing up to 15,000 tons of 3- to 5-ton armor rocks to achieve the 1983 design of the revetment with a 16.4-foot crest elevation (relative to NAVD88 vertical datum), a 2:1 (horizontal:vertical) seaward slope, and a crest width of 10 feet. The repair would involve minor re-working of the revetment, using new (imported) armor rocks to fill voids in the revetment, correct low points and reduced width in the revetment crest, and address areas where existing armor stone has been dislodged. Where possible, existing displaced armor rock would be salvaged and re-used. In addition, the proposed Project would provide dune vegetation enhancement along the landward splash wall. Existing non-native vegetation would be removed and native dune vegetation would be planted to create additional habitat area. Construction of the dune feature may require the import of a small amount of sand for dune vegetation establishment in locations where sand cover does not exist. Lastly, of the 23 existing private access stairways constructed along the revetment to serve residents of Sand Point Road, under the proposed Project, 12 private access stairways would be demolished, and the design rock revetment would be restored in their place. The remaining 11 existing access stairways would be rebuilt.

ceqa-796d56280d8858f8e7.agency: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-796d56280d8858f8e7.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-796d56280d8858f8e7.description: The project involves the excavating, loading, and hauling of up to approximately 1,750 cubic yards of arsenic contaminated soil located at what is commonly referred to as the "Tatum Property" (APN 065-040-026). Stockpiles will be covered with continuous heavy-duty plastic sheeting or treated with the soil binder "Soil-Sement" to reduce fugitive particulates and Reactive Organic Compound (ROC) emissions. The excavated soil will be removed from the site by covered dump trucks. The County of Santa Barbara is the Lead Agency under CEQA on the Tatum Multifamily Housing Development Project. Environmental Health Services (EHS) Site Mitigation Unit (SMU) has primary oversight authority with respect to soil investigation and cleanup located at the Tatum Property (site) and has approved the Corrective Action Plan which includes the excavation, handling, and disposal of arsenic contaminated soil. The District's permit action ensures that excavation activities authorized by EHS comply with all District rules and regulations and are performed in a manner that minimizes potential air contaminant emissions.

ceqa-8fc801345975fb03b2.name: Orcutt Solomon Basin Maintenance
ceqa-8fc801345975fb03b2.agency: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-8fc801345975fb03b2.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-8fc801345975fb03b2.description: The Orcutt-Solomon Basin is an existing flood control facility that captures, stores, and percolates urban runoff to replenish groundwater while reducing flood risk. In recent years, the basin has experienced maintenance challenges due to inlet blockages from woody debris and sediment buildup within the outlet pipe. To address these issues, the project proposes replacing the existing concrete outlet structure and repairing pipe connections with a more durable, low-maintenance drainage design. The proposed maintenance will include improved debris screening to better capture leaves, branches, and other materials before they reach the outlet. This will help the basin drain more efficiently, reduce maintenance needs, and improve overall system performance during storm events. The maintenance activities at Orcutt-Solomon Basin will be completed in late summer and fall 2026 as part of the Flood Control District’s Annual Routine Maintenance Program and the associated permits. Orcutt-Solomon Basin is identified and analyzed as an existing facility within the Annual Routine Maintenance Program.

ceqa-9100d835b72ad5f0af.description: The following Notice of Exemption (NOE) covers activities as described in the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) guidelines. Any Department or Division may qualify for this exemption, as long as the work proposed meets the description as it is included in these guidelines and is not subject to any of the exceptions found in Section 15300.2 of the CEQA guidelines. Exceptions include project locations where impacts to hazardous or critical environmental resources may be impacted; projects where there are potentially significant cumulative impacts; projects which may damage scenic resources; hazardous waste sites; sites with historical resources. While these identified descriptions do not directly relate to all activities of each Department or Division, any activity that falls under one or more of the included descriptions could qualify as exempt.

ceqa-162f38fe7b57c1b12d.name: San Jose Creek Multipurpose Path Project (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-41011-R5)
ceqa-162f38fe7b57c1b12d.projectTitle: San Jose Creek Multipurpos Path Project
ceqa-162f38fe7b57c1b12d.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has amended Streambed Alteration Agreement (EPIMS-SBA-41011-R5), pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, the project Applicant, City of Goleta. The project is the construction of a section of a multipurpose path along San Jose Creek in the City of Goleta that will eventually connect two existing multipurpose paths to create one continuous one. It will run generally from the terminus of an existing multipurpose path at Goleta Slough in the south to the terminus of an existing multipurpose path in the north just north of where San Jose Creek crosses underneath United States Route 101. For construction purposes, the path is split into two segments, northern and southern. Both the northern and southern segments of the project take place within the limits of the stream; however, most project activities are taking place along the top of the bank with no activities within the bed of the stream. The northern segment will consist of a paved multipurpose path approximately 2,400 feet in length ranging from 10 feet to 14 feet in width, including shoulder widths. The maximum excavation depth will be approximately 3.5 feet. The southern segment of the project will consist of a paved multipurpose path approximately 1 mile in length ranging from 8 to 12 feet wide including shoulder widths. It will also include a 2-foot-wide and 3-foot-tall concrete barrier with a bicycle/pedestrian rail for purposes of separating the path from SR 217. The southern segment will include the construction of a pedestrian crossing over San Jose Creek near the northern end and the construction of a pedestrian box culvert under SR 217 near the southern end. This Amendment is to increase the acreage of temporary impacts from 0.24 acre to 0.34 acre and to extend the due date for several mitigation deliverables (submittal of habitat mitigation plan, submittal of endowment, draft conservation easement).
