ceqa-8f61adacfea3441adb.name: SEMCO Groundwater Monitoring Wells
ceqa-8f61adacfea3441adb.description: The project includes the installation of two groundwater monitoring wells in accordance with the Water Board’s approval of the technical workplan for the purposes of gauging depths to water and semi-annual data collection and monitoring. The project includes the installation of two 4-inch diameter groundwater monitoring wells to an approximate depth of 245 feet below ground surface (bgs). The 9-inch boreholes will be advanced to a maximum depth of 270 feet bgs using sonic drilling. The well locations will be cleared using soft-digging techniques to at least 5 feet bgs. Soil cuttings, decontamination water, and purge water will be properly tested and transported offsite for disposal.

ceqa-240aa5c8f5befa17aa.name: SEMCO Soil Vapor Extraction System
ceqa-240aa5c8f5befa17aa.description: The Water Board approved workplan for response that will include the installation and operation of a soil vapor extraction (SVE) system, and the installation of piping for a future possible retrofit to a vapor intrusion mitigation system (VIMS). Eight SVE wells will be installed and operated within the target treatment zone spaced approximately 56 feet apart, and aboveground piping will connect each wellhead to the SVE control panel/system. The SVE System will address the constituent of concern, trichloroethene (TCE), in the shallow zone at the Site. The target treatment area is approximately 17,000 square feet located on Assessor Parcel Number 111-291-037 (2936 Industrial Parkway, Santa Maria, CA 93455).

ceqa-f9d413be3122c1385d.name: Housing Plan Program EIR
ceqa-f9d413be3122c1385d.description: The Housing Plan implements 32 programs in the adopted 6th Cycle Housing Element, including ongoing programs, procedural changes, municipal code amendments, and other actions to meet state housing requirements and accommodate the City Regional Housing Needs Allocation of 8,001 new housing units. The proposed project includes adoption of an Adaptive Reuse Ordinance, preparation of a planning framework for the La Cumbre Plaza Planning Area, amendments to the Average Unit-Size Density (AUD) Incentive Program, adoption of Objective Design and Development Standards, updates to the Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) ordinance, and process improvements to streamline permitting; Associated amendments to the Municipal Code, General Plan, and Local Coastal Program to maintain consistency with the Housing Element and State law. For environmental analysis purposes, this EIR assumes a conservative scenario in which up to 8,001 housing units could be permitted and constructed by 2035, along with associated nonresidential development anticipated under cumulative conditions. These updates do not authorize specific development projects but provide the regulatory and policy framework.

ceqa-3a142620f8259b4776.name: Baron Ranch Post Storm Emergency Access Road and Bridge Repairs
ceqa-3a142620f8259b4776.projectTitle: Baron Ranch Post Storm Emergency Access Road and Bridge Repairs
ceqa-3a142620f8259b4776.agency: Santa Barbara County Public Works Department Resource Recovery and Waste Management Div.
ceqa-3a142620f8259b4776.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Public Works Department Resource Recovery and Waste Management Div.
ceqa-3a142620f8259b4776.description: The proposed project consists of emergency repair and cleanup activities to restore access along existing paved and unpaved access roads and vehicle bridge at Baron Ranch following storm events that occurred between December 23, 2025, and January 3, 2026. These storm events resulted in the deposition of mud, silt, rocks, woody debris, severe erosion, and damage to existing access roads and an onsite vehicle bridge, restricting safe access throughout the ranch. The roads provide access for wildfire fire protection, powerline repair and maintenance, restoration and conservation areas, wells, and for public trail maintenance and emergency access. Emergency repair activities will include the use of standard heavy equipment and hand operated equipment to remove storm-related debris from paved roadways, relocate heavy debris off of existing road surfaces, and grade existing dirt roads to restore pre-storm conditions. All work will occur within the footprint of existing roads/bridge and previously disturbed areas. No road widening, realignment, or expansion is proposed. Some localized work may be required at the vehicle bridge location within the creek channel to remove woody debris that has collected against the upstream side of the bridge and is wedged beneath the bridge structure. Work will be conducted during daylight hours and biological survey and/or monitoring will be conducted prior to or during the emergency repair work. The project is necessary to maintain public and worker safety, restore emergency and operational access, and prevent further damage to existing facilities.

ceqa-2d9ffadc5681d54ae7.name: Surfliner Inn
ceqa-2d9ffadc5681d54ae7.description: The Surfliner Inn Project (Project) is a proposed development that would include a commercial hotel and public improvements. The hotel would be developed and operated on an approximately 1.15-acre site located at 499 Linden Avenue. The Project would include a separate public parking lot on an approximately 1.27-acre property at 399 Linden Avenue. The new two-story (up to a height of 37.1-feet) hotel would consist of 36 guest rooms, a manager’s unit, café, visitor center, and a roof-top bar/lounge/event space and swimming pool area. The Project would include 28,235 square feet of landscaped areas and a total of 139 vehicular parking spaces. The parking areas would operate under a conjunctive parking arrangement, which would accommodate parking for hotel guests, hotel employees, and the general public. The Project would also provide 18 bicycle spaces.

ceqa-bde0f0d25c8df2baa7.name: ADU and JADU Regulation Amendments to Implement Changes in State Law (Case No. 25-0005-ORD)
ceqa-bde0f0d25c8df2baa7.projectTitle: ADU and JADU Regulation Amendments to Implement Changes in State Law (Case No. 25-0005-ORD)
ceqa-bde0f0d25c8df2baa7.description: The project includes the replacement of the City’s existing Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) regulations (Section 17.41.030 of the Goleta Municipal Code) with a new set of citywide ADU and JADU standards that will fully comply with the changes in State laws (Assembly Bill (AB) 462 (2025), AB 1154 (2025), Senate Bill (SB) 9 (2025), and SB 543). Changes to the City’s ADU and JADU regulations relate to: ADU and JADU Sizes, Quantity of Building Permit Only ADUs, ADU Permitting Process, ADU Processing in the Coastal Zone, Fire Sprinklers, JADU Owner-Occupancy, Disaster-Affected Areas, and Impact Fees. Additional revisions include minor alignments with State ADU law and clarifying clauses and subsection titles, where appropriate.

ceqa-a8f3b3826efb125d78.description: The proposed Project would include removal of Platform Holly to five feet below the mudline, removal of associated pipelines and power cables, and removal of the two seep tents.

ceqa-24b45e022eabe932c9.name: Emergency Response Actions from Impacts of December 2025 and January 2026 Storms
ceqa-24b45e022eabe932c9.projectTitle: Emergency Response Actions from Impacts of December 2025 and January 2026 Storms
ceqa-24b45e022eabe932c9.agency: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-24b45e022eabe932c9.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-24b45e022eabe932c9.description: Severe storms and rain events in early December 2025 and January 2026 resulted in flooding, sedimentation, and debris impacts throughout Santa Barbara County. As a result of the damages and the need to repair and restore drainage facilities, the Santa Barbara County Flood Control District has engaged in emergency response and will continue to implement measures to mitigate the emergency and prevent or mitigate subsequent emergencies during the remaining winter rainy season. The response activities may include, but are not limited to: debris removal, sediment management, channel dredging, creek and channel restoration, beach sediment disposal operations, vegetation management, and other flood control facility repairs and maintenance. There is not an insignificant chance of additional storms this winter rainy season, and immediate action is required to remove debris from the flood control system in order to create additional capacity in the event of additional storms.

ceqa-3c88e09f10a5f4c86e.name: Lompoc Valley Fuel Reduction Grant -Roadside Clearance
ceqa-3c88e09f10a5f4c86e.projectTitle: Lompoc Valley Fuel Reduction Grant -Roadside Clearance
ceqa-3c88e09f10a5f4c86e.description: The project consists of maintenance of roadside fuel reduction treatment along public roads totaling 22.1 miles (187 acres). The fire the purpose of this project is to comply with CA Fire Code road clearance requirements, increase fire apparatus response, reduce the fire size of any roadside ignitions and increase public safety during a potential evacuation. The project is located within the unincorporated area north and south of the City of Lompoc within Santa Barbara County Fire (SBC) jurisdiction. The four roads to be treated are; Burton Mesa Road (from the intersection of Rucker Road and Burton Mesa Road west to the intersection of Constellation Road and Burton Mesa Road), Harris Grade Road (from the intersection of Purisima Road north to the agricultural fields just south of Los Alamos), Rucker Road (from the intersection of Purisima Road north to the intersection of Rucker Road and Harris Grade Road), and San Miguelito Road (from the intersection of San Miguelito Road and West Willow Avenue to 0.75 miles before its terminus at Vandenberg Space Force Base property). The reduction of flammable fuel along roads will occur within a horizontal distance of 10 to 15 feet from the paved edge of the road and a vertical height (overhead) of 14 feet from the paved edge of the road. In addition, hazard trees (dead pine trees) located within 100 feet of the road will be removed. Methods to reduce flammable fuel are as follows: 1) Within chaparral/oak woodland areas vegetation within 15 feet of the road will be selectively removed using hand cutting of vegetation on both sides of the road. Flammable chaparral will be removed, flashy fuels will be weed whacked, and live trees will be limbed up and ladder fuels removed. Overhanging branches for a horizontal distance of 14 feet will be removed. Single specimen trees that are compromised or diseased within 15 feet of road may be removed. Cut material will be chipped and spread uniformly on site or accumulated into burn piles on site for disposal on the properly determined time. 2) 3) Within Bishop Pine areas located at the top of summit of Harris Grade Road healthy single specimen trees will be limbed up and ladder fuels removed using hand cutting of vegetation on both sides of the road. Overhanging branches for a horizontal distance of 14 feet will be removed. Cut material will be chipped and spread uniformly on site or accumulated into burn piles on site for disposal on the properly determined time. Areas that have continuous solid stands of Bishop Pine within 15 feet of the paved road edge on both sides of the road will be masticated to reduce the continuous vegetation cover. Individual healthy Bishop Pines will be selected to remain in place to allow for healthy growth of single specimen trees. Masticated material will be left on site to stabilize slopes and to retain soil moisture for single specimen trees. Periodic single specimen dead pine trees exist along Burton Mesa Roads. Any dead trees within 100 feet of the road will be removed. Where possible and when safe to accomplish dead tree trunks will be left in place. Branches attached to trees and any branches that have accumulated on the ground will be chipped or piled for burning later. Chipped debris will be spread uniformly on site he existing fuel is predominately Central Maritime Chaparral and scattered Oak trees. There is approximately 1 mile of Bishop Pine vegetation located at the summit of Harris Grade Road. Individual dead pine trees are located within 100 feet of all four roads. From the uniformity of their location they appear to have been planted along all four roads and are not part of the native habitat! A query of the National Diversity Database was completed to identify the presence of endangered plants and/or animals. Department of Fish and Wildlife will be consulted forrinput as necessary. necessary. Chips will not be deposited within the standard width of within 50 feat a watercourse or lake protection zone. No work will occur within 50 feet of a riparian corridor
ceqa-3c88e09f10a5f4c86e.crossStreets: Harris Grade Rd, Burton Mesa Rd, Rucker Rd, San Miguelito Canyon Rd

ceqa-b04b73b4953667b7ea.name: Solids Handling Improvement Project (SHIP)
ceqa-b04b73b4953667b7ea.description: Goleta Sanitary District (GSD) owns and operates the Goleta Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) located at One William Moffett Place, near the Santa Barbara Municipal Airport (SBA), in an unincorporated coastal area of Santa Barbara County, California. GSD is a special services district that provides wastewater collection, treatment, and disposal services to residents and businesses within the Goleta Valley. The GSD WRRF has an annual average design flow capacity to treat 7.64 million gallons per day (MGD) of wastewater, but it is currently treating an annual average flow of approximately 4.9 MGD. The treatment process at WRRF begins with bar screens to remove large debris, as well as aerated grit tanks and two cyclone separators to remove grit and sand. The wastewater then flows into three primary clarifiers for solids removal prior to secondary treatment. The secondary treatment at WRRF includes biofilters, three aeration basins, and four secondary clarifiers. Currently, GSD's WRRF has the following solids and gas handling process for treatment of solids recovered from wastewater. Primary Sludge (PS) coming from primary clarifiers is pumped to the digestion process. Waste activated sludge (WAS) generated from secondary treatment is thickened to 6% solids using two screw thickeners; the resulting thickened WAS (TWAS) is pumped to the digestion process. Combined PS and TWAS solids are stabilized in three mesophilic anaerobic digesters (MADs ), operated in parallel. Digested biosolids are dewatered by two screw presses and then loaded onto trucks for transport off-site. A small portion of the dewatered biosolids is diverted into sludge drying beds for further stabilization to become a Class A product. Biogas produced in the digesters is burned in boilers to provide hot water for heating the digesters and to supply other heating needs at the WRRF. Biogas that is not required for heating is flared through the waste gas burner. A condition assessment conducted in 2016 indicated that some of the unit processes at WRRF are nearing the end of their service life and would need rehabilitation and replacement soon. A Biosolids and Energy Strategic Plan (BESP) was developed in August 2019 by Hazen and Sawyer (Hazen), which evaluated biosolids unit processes in detail and recommended upgrading existing facilities to mitigate regulatory uncertainties affecting biosolids disposition, to diversify beneficial use outlets, and to approach energy neutrality for the facility. The BESP summarized the capacity evaluation for the existing solids processes, including digesters considering the current and anticipated future flows and loads, and identified the need to build a new digester to maintain firm capacity. Firm capacity was defined as the ability to maintain full treatment capacity with the largest single process unit out of service. The BESP also included assessment of the High Strength Waste (HSW) co-digestion and the feasibility and benefits of reaching energy neutrality. BESP provided GSD with a suite of improvement options for the WRRF, each with its own independent utility and purpose. Goleta Sanitary District is proposing to implement a Solids Handling Improvement Project (SHIP) at its Water Resource Recovery Facility (Project), which includes the construction of a thermal dryer facility. The addition of the thermal dryer facility will decrease the amount of hauled sludge, as well as increase the quality of biosolids produced, thus increasing the potential for beneficial reuse of the product. The proposed Project includes the following components: (1) a thermal dryer, which will heat dewatered sludge to transform it into Class A biosolids; (2) a thermal heater system, which will use natural gas to provide heat to operate the thermal dryer, with the option to convert using biogas produced by the digesters in the future, when gas production increases; (3) loadout facilities, intended to load Class A biosolids into trucks for removal from the site; (4) associated civil, structural, electrical and instrumentation work; and (5) a fire pump for fire suppression system at the new buildings.

No grading is proposed and no landscaping is proposed (existing landscaping was installed as part of the overall development of the site). Hours of operation will be from9am-9pm, seven days a week. There will be approximately five to nine employees working during any given shift, including delivery drivers. The project includes at least 10 parking spaces for employees and customers, along with 50 additional parking spaces that are shared with the rest of the shopping plaza.

ceqa-95f896df6a4e735531.name: De La Vina Bridge Street Replacement Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-071-05 (ITP))
ceqa-95f896df6a4e735531.projectTitle: De La Vina Bridge Street Replacement Project (California Endangered Species Act Incidental Take Permit No. 2081-2025-071-05 (ITP))
ceqa-95f896df6a4e735531.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has issued an ITP (No. 2081-2025-071-05), pursuant to Section 2081(b) of the Fish and Game Code to City of Santa Barbara. The Project includes replacement of the De La Vina Street Bridge over Mission Creek. The Project activities include demolition of an existing bridge and buildings; utility relocation; temporary creek diversion and dewatering; temporary construction of diversion dams; installation of the new bridge, associated abutments, concrete wingwalls, rock slope protection, and downstream soldier pile walls; use of temporary work areas within the creek; temporary installation of approximately 625 cubic yards of fill in the channel to act as a platform for a Drill Rig; and other activities. The covered activities under this Incidental Take Permit only include portions of Stage I of the Project which will be constructed from the issuance of this permit. Stage 1 of the Project entails the construction of the downstream portion of the bridge, abutments and channel walls, placement of rock slope protection to reconstruct the creek banks, creek grading, and temporary creek diversion. The Project is expected to cause the permanent loss of 0.01 acres of habitat for southern California steelhead (Oncorhynchus mykiss) due to alteration of the creek bank and temporary loss of 0.15 acres of habitat for southern California steelhead. Indirect impacts resulting in 7,275 linear feet will occur between the Project site and the bridge over Mission Creek on California State Route 192. The Project is expected to result in incidental take of southern California steelhead, which is/are designated as an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). The ITP referenced above as issued by CDFW authorizes incidental take of species listed under CESA that may occur as a result of Project implementation.

ceqa-ae4316efafc6619d0f.name: 3139 Sea Cliff Soil Remediation
ceqa-ae4316efafc6619d0f.description: The 3.02-acre lot is developed with an 1,845-square-foot single-unit residence and 480-square-foot attached garage on the southwest corner of the lot. The project proposes soil remediation by removal of contaminated soil. The project would result in excavation and exportation of contaminated soil to an appropriate permitted landfill. Excavations would be backfilled with uncontaminated soil from the site and with fill, balanced on site. The project includes a construction staging area and stabilized construction entrance at the southeast corner of the project site. Vegetation clearing and grubbing to accommodate the soil remediation includes the removal of approximately seventeen (17) front setback and approximately thirty-eight (38) interior trees. Retained trees would be protected with tree protection measures and removed trees would be replaced per the arborist’s recommendations in the report dated February, 13 2025 with approximately fifty-five (55) new trees. Erosion and sediment control measures would be implemented during excavation and grading activities. All areas disturbed would be hydroseeded with a native erosion control mix following completion of grading activities. No changes to the existing residence are proposed. The project would implement the Remedial Action Plan (RAP) dated October 7, 2025 and approved by Santa Barbara County Environmental Health Services (EHS) on October 10, 2025. The remediation would be completed under permit by the Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District (APCD) and the conditions of the Permit to Operate (PTO) issued by APCD on December 13, 2024. The project requires land use approval by the Staff Hearing Officer and design review approval by the Single Family Design Board.

The proposed project will add HOV lanes (to northbound and southbound) to SR-101 between Carpinteria and Santa Barbara. The widening is proposed to occur in the existing median and beyond the existing outside shoulders. The improvements to Highway 101 would include noise-attenuating pavement surfacing and drainage improvements. The project has increased the permanent impacts and subsequently will compensate for this change with increased mitigation.

ceqa-14323252476a306d01.name: ADU and JADU Regulation Amendments Urgency Ordinance to Implement Changes in State Law (Case No. 25-0005-ORD)
ceqa-14323252476a306d01.projectTitle: ADU and JADU Regulation Amendments Urgency Ordinance to Implement Changes in State Law (Case No. 25-0005-ORD)
ceqa-14323252476a306d01.description: The project includes the replacement of the City’s existing Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) regulations (Section 17.41.030 of the Goleta Municipal Code) with a new set of citywide ADU and JADU standards that will fully comply with the changes in State laws (Assembly Bill (AB) 462 (2025), AB 1154 (2025), Senate Bill (SB) 9 (2025), and SB 543). Changes to the City’s ADU and JADU regulations relate to: ADU and JADU Sizes, Quantity of Building Permit Only ADUs, ADU Permitting Process, ADU Processing in the Coastal Zone, Fire Sprinklers, JADU Owner-Occupancy, Disaster-Affected Areas, and Impact Fees. Additional revisions include minor alignments with State ADU law and clarifying clauses and subsection titles, where appropriate.

ceqa-aca8c657cc5d3a3877.name: Greenbark 30 Battery Energy Storage System Project
ceqa-aca8c657cc5d3a3877.projectTitle: Greenbark 30 Battery Energy Storage System Project
ceqa-aca8c657cc5d3a3877.description: The proposed Greenbark 30 Battery Energy Storage System Project, proposed by Scale Microgrids, LLC (Applicant), would be a battery energy storage system (BESS) with an output power of 30-megawatts (MW) and a storage capacity of 120-megawatt hours (MWh). The development footprint would be within the central portion of the 2.1-acre Project site parcel, within an interior perimeter road. The BESS operational area would consist of the interior perimeter road, BESS equipment, and a perimeter fence. The Greenbark 30 Battery Energy Storage Project would be located within a 2.1-acre vacant undeveloped site located at the northern terminus of Viajero Drive in western Goleta, California in Santa Barbara County. The property is adjacent to the existing Ellwood Generating Station (EGS) and is accessed from the northern terminus of Viajero Drive, approximately one-quarter mile north of Hollister Avenue. Battery energy storage units would be charged from the electrical grid and would discharge as a California Independent System Operator (CAISO) market participant. An interconnection application was approved by Southern California Edison (SCE) and BESS interconnection studies are underway. It is anticipated that the BESS would interconnect to the existing SCE 66-kilovolt electrical transmission line along Las Armas Road.

ceqa-2e0dd6feb251313252.name: Bonita Elementary School Drinking Water Improvements Project
ceqa-2e0dd6feb251313252.projectTitle: Bonita School Drinking Water Improvements Project
ceqa-2e0dd6feb251313252.description: The State Water Board is funding the Project referred to internally as Bonita Elementary School Consolidation with City of Santa Maria. The components of the Project to be funded by the State Water Resources Control Board include the consolidation of Bonita Elementary School (School) with the City of Santa Maria (City) via approximately 8,100 linear feet of a two-inch diameter service line from the planned terminus of the City’s water system near the City’s wastewater treatment plant to the School. The existing on-site well and 10,000-gallon storage tank at the School will be repurposed for non-potable use to meet peak demand, fire flow requirements, and irrigation demand. A hydropneumatic tank with a maximum capacity of 1,000 gallons, an air compressor, above-grade piping, and isolation valves may be added to meet peak flow demands. Minor piping modifications will be made to disconnect the School’s existing onsite well system from its potable water system, after which the School will connect to the City’s municipal water supply. Other improvements include installation of blowoffs along the pipeline, replacement of interior lead service lines in an existing building, and other appurtenances on the School’s property.

ceqa-26d7cf2ac1c354301b.name: Mission Isla Vista Partners LP Housing Development
ceqa-26d7cf2ac1c354301b.projectTitle: Mission Isla Vista Partners LP Housing Development
ceqa-26d7cf2ac1c354301b.description: The project is a request for a Development Plan submitted pursuant to Senate Bill 330 to allow for the demolition of an existing 1,620 square foot (SF) single-family dwelling and 455 SF garage, and the construction of three new, 3-story multi-family buildings totaling 15,093 net SF and 18,436 gross SF. The project includes 13 three-bedroom units and 3 two-bedroom units (totaling 45 bedrooms), a management office, and will have a maximum height of 36’-7”. Two of the units will be very low income units pursuant to State Density Bonus Law and two will be moderate income units pursuant to Coastal Plan policy. The project includes 24 parking spaces, 48 bike lockers, and 52 bike racks to serve the development. Other site improvements include a new trash enclosure, an approximately 180 foot 8-foot tall masonry wall along the southern property line and a portion of the western property line, two 6-foot tall gates and fencing, cluster mailboxes and cluster parcel boxes, concrete flatwork and landscaping. Grading will include 415 cubic yards of cut and 75 cubic yards of fill. No trees are proposed for removal. Public transit information, resources, and vouchers will be provided to all project tenants (unless the tenants already have a transit voucher through their school ID). The Applicant will evaluate the option to provide a car-share vehicle (such as zip-car) on-site. The Applicant will also voluntarily market the housing complex as a public-transit accessible site. Existing onsite development, consisting of one residential structure, one garage and various shed and storage containers are proposed for demolition and removal. The project is requesting a 45% density bonus, resulting in an additional five units above the zoning density per acre, and three concessions. The concessions include an increase to the allowed bedroom density, a reduction in front, side and rear setbacks, and an increase to maximum height limit for the SR-M Zone District. The parcel and project will be served by the Goleta Water District, the Goleta Sanitary District, and the County Fire Department. Access will be provided via Sueno Road. The property is 0.58-acres net, 0.65-acres gross, zoned SR-M-18 and is shown as Assessor's Parcel Number 075-092-009, located at 6737 Sueno Road in the Goleta Community Plan area, Second Supervisorial District.

ceqa-a0f0e05342adb9beff.name: 2025 California Building and Fire Codes
ceqa-a0f0e05342adb9beff.description: On December 2, 2025, the City of Santa Barbara adopted amendments to the Santa Barbara Municipal Code by Ordinance and by Reference the most current State Building Standards. The amendments to the Municipal Code result in the following: • Changes the height requirement for walls requiring a building permit from 3.5’ to 5’ feet to align with zoning code change (excludes retaining and non-retain block walls) • Adopts California Wildland-Interface Code as a stand-alone code and relocates previously amended related construction requirements from the California Residential and Building, Code to new Wildland-Interface Code. • Establish City of Santa Barbara Wildland Fire Plan as adopted. • Adds clarifying language for square footage calculation for determining when fire sprinklers are required on remodels and a Higher Hazard Occupancy Classification Table. • Adds definitions for spark arrester, tracer, tracer charge, and Wildland-Urbane Interface Area. • Updates International Code language referring to “Prevention Department”; replaces with “Fire Prevention Bureau”. • California has adopted the 2025 edition of the California Wildland Urban Interface Code which incorporates and replaces Chapter 49 of the 2022 California Fire Code.

ceqa-de9d83e4a3cb6721d3.name: Stonebrook Basin Drainage Improvements
ceqa-de9d83e4a3cb6721d3.agency: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-de9d83e4a3cb6721d3.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Flood Control District
ceqa-de9d83e4a3cb6721d3.description: Stonebrook Basin is an existing stormwater detention facility near California Boulevard and Old Mill Lane in Orcutt, CA. The basin property also functions as an open space park serving the surrounding neighborhoods. The proposed activity by the Santa Barbara County Flood Control and Water Conservation District involves minor improvements to improve drainage and reduce damp surface conditions on the eastern part of the property. The project involves re-contouring the basin bottom to allow stormwater and urban seepage nuisance water to drain more suitably around the perimeter of the basin. The activity involves grading the bottom of the basin, installation of new concrete inlet/outlet structures and an underground pipe to connect to the existing drain system, and re-seeding to re-establish turf and stabilize the soil. Stonebrook basin is an existing flood control facility. The activity would not expand the boundaries or change the use of the facility. The activity is a minor alteration of existing facilities.

ceqa-606a5f96faa70615a0.name: San Antonio Well Above Ground Facilities
ceqa-606a5f96faa70615a0.projectTitle: San Antonio Well Above Ground Facilities
ceqa-606a5f96faa70615a0.description: The project consists of rehabilitating and upgrading the San Antonio Well facility to maintain production and treatment capacity. Improvements include replacing the backwash tank, upgrading the filtration system, upsizing chemical storage, replacing the lift station, and repairing electrical, structural, and drainage systems. San Antonio Well, one of the District’s highest-producing wells, currently produces up to 730 gallons per minute. These upgrades will improve operational reliability, sustain maximum treatment capacity, and ensure continued water supply during droughts or water quality fluctuations.

ceqa-d23bc85c8ab01ee1e3.name: Goleta Water District La Riata Booster Pump Station
ceqa-d23bc85c8ab01ee1e3.projectTitle: Goleta Water District La Riata Booster Pump Station
ceqa-d23bc85c8ab01ee1e3.description: The project consists of constructing the La Riata Booster Pump Station to eliminate flow restrictions to the San Marcos Reservoir and Pressure Zone. The booster station will be located near the existing La Riata Reservoir and include a pitless pump station with underground submersible pumps, along with associated 12-inch diameter pipelines. The project will improve operational flexibility, increase fire flows, and prevent dewatering of the pressure zone during main breaks or wildfire events when multiple hydrants are in use. By reducing reliance on the existing reservoir and undersized pipelines, the project will ensure reliable water delivery and enhance fire protection for customers in the San Marcos Pressure Zone.

ceqa-f2e81efdf5f86dcef1.name: Goleta Water District Upsize Hollister Main
ceqa-f2e81efdf5f86dcef1.projectTitle: Goleta Water District Upsize Hollister Main
ceqa-f2e81efdf5f86dcef1.description: The project consists of upsizing approximately 4,500 linear feet of the Hollister Avenue Main from San Antonio Road to San Marcos Road. This work will replace the existing 10-inch steel pipeline installed in 1955 with a 16-inch ductile iron pipeline to accommodate increased flows from the new Hope Well. The project also includes installing the necessary service connections and valves to maintain allowable flow velocities and pressures. Upsizing the pipeline is necessary to safely convey increased groundwater production and allow the District to access the full delivery capacity of San Marcos and Hope wells.
ceqa-f2e81efdf5f86dcef1.crossStreets: Hollister Ave. between San Antonio and San Marcos Rd

ceqa-11f4c6c388560a6292.name: Goleta Water District Filter Washtrough Replacements
ceqa-11f4c6c388560a6292.projectTitle: Goleta Water District Filter Washtrough Replacements
ceqa-11f4c6c388560a6292.description: This project consists of replacing the deteriorated fiberglass filter troughs at CDMWTP with new stainless steel troughs. The filter troughs, in service since 1974, disperse water evenly over the top of filter media in each of six filters and remove water during backwash. Continuous exposure to water, sunlight, and treatment chemicals has caused chipping during periodic cleaning, and the problem will continue and worsen until the troughs are replaced. Replacement with stainless steel troughs will prevent debris from entering the filters, improve overall filter reliability, and ensure uninterrupted treatment at the facility.

ceqa-73f34d56a686433a88.name: Goleta Water District Corona Reservoir Rehabilitation
ceqa-73f34d56a686433a88.projectTitle: Goleta Water District Corona Reservoir Rehabilitation
ceqa-73f34d56a686433a88.description: The project consists of rehabilitating Corona Reservoir by removing the deteriorating interior liner, replacing joint sealant, repairing concrete cracking and spalling, replacing the entry ladder, and addressing a suspected minor floor leak. This work is needed to preserve a critical storage facility in the GWD distribution system and sustain reliable water service to customers, particularly during outages or when major transmission pipelines are out of service. Without rehabilitation, continued interior degradation and leak progression could impact water quality, create safety hazards, or force an emergency shutdown.

ceqa-87cbc04d7bc4c30617.projectTitle: Santa Barbara Mountain Communities Defense Zone Project
ceqa-87cbc04d7bc4c30617.agency: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-87cbc04d7bc4c30617.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-87cbc04d7bc4c30617.description: The use of an air curtain incinerator at various locations in or near the Los Padres National Forest in Santa Barbara County in support the Santa Barbara Mountain Communities Defense Zone Project. As part of the Santa Barbara Mountain Communities Defense Zone Project, fuel breaks will be created in the areas around the communities of Painted Cave, San Marcos Trout Club, Haney Tract, and Rosario Park. Shrubs cut for fuel breaks around infrastructure are often left onsite, posing a significant wildfire risk. In partnership with the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense, the USFS will use an air curtain incinerator to address biomass disposal and reduce hazardous fuels by converting biomass created as part of this project into biochar.

ceqa-46848aa16c9e4a2bd5.name: Alamo Pintado Bridge Replacement
ceqa-46848aa16c9e4a2bd5.agencyName: Caltrans, District 5 - San Luis Obispo/Santa Barbara
ceqa-46848aa16c9e4a2bd5.description: This project, located in Santa Barbara County on State Route 246 from post miles 30.173 to 30.435, proposes to replace the Alamo Pintado Bridge (Bridge Number 51 0130), which is rated scour critical. The scope of work includes installing straight abutment walls under the bridge, placing rock slope protection to protect the abutments, road embankment, and nearby existing infrastructure, and upgrading four existing outdated Americans with Disabilities Act curb ramps at the Alamo Pintado Road intersection. The proposed bridge work includes building a 14-foot-wide Class 1 Bikeway (multiuse path) with a 2-foot-wide barrier separating the path and the travelway. A retaining wall is proposed on the northeast side of the bridge, connecting the new Class 1 Bikeway to the existing one and allowing continuous travel to the Alamo Pintado Road intersection.

ceqa-c40f42924951139f0a.name: Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program - Santa Maria Rapid Transit
ceqa-c40f42924951139f0a.projectTitle: Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program - Santa Maria Rapid Transit
ceqa-c40f42924951139f0a.description: Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program (TIRCP) is a statewide program that provides funding to transit agencies for capital improvements that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, expand and improve transit services and integrate the County-wide rail and transit networks. In July 2023 the Santa Barbara County Association of Governments (SBCAG), partnered with City of Santa Barbara, City of Lompoc Transit, Clean Air Express, Santa Barbara MTD, and Santa Maria Regional Transit, to submit a Transit and Intercity Rail Program (TIRCP) application to the California State Transportation Agency (CalSTA) for the Santa Barbara County Charging Forward Project. The California State Transportation Agency awarded SBCAG $51,130,000. The Santa Maria City Council adopted Resolution 2025-57 on May 6, 2025, accepting $17,544,169 TIRCP funds for use toward Santa Maria Rapid Transit improvements as described in the SBCAG Charging Forward Project application.

ceqa-c800c44409118527d8.name: Wildfire Resilience Program Capacity Enhancement (Cachuma Resource Conservation District project)
ceqa-c800c44409118527d8.projectTitle: Wildfire Resilience Program Capacity Enhancement (Cachuma Resource Conservation District project)
ceqa-c800c44409118527d8.description: Notice of exemption for Coastal Conservancy approval of grant funding. The CRCD project consists of funding staff costs for a new three-quarter time staff assistant at the Cachuma Resource Conservation District (CRCD) to carry out CRCD’s mission by developing and administering wildfire resilience programs and projects recommended in the Santa Barbara County Regional Priority Plan (RPP) and the Santa Barbara County Regional Wildfire Mitigation Program (RWMP). Project activities will include: developing projects; conducting wildfire education, and providing technical assistance on fire management for members of the public and landowners; partnering with other public agencies and non-profits to apply for and secure funds to develop or expand wildfire mitigation strategies included in the RWMP and RPP such as regional fire fuel hazard reduction strategies (chipping, native restoration, roadside vegetation management, grazing, and prescribed/cultural burning) to benefit participating communities; representing CRCD in public forums and collaborative planning activities; assist with RPP website upkeep and maintenance; participating in training and peer-to-peer learning; and developing a long-term program funding plan. CRCD is transitioning to in-house wildfire program staff after using contractors in the program’s early stages. Funding this wildfire staff position will enable long-term development, coordination, and administration of RPP and RWMP projects. The CRCD project will encompass wildfire planning and mitigation efforts throughout Santa Barbara County, utilizing High and Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones as a guide and prioritizing Communities at Risk. Initial focus will build upon identified priority wildfire resilience and forest health projects and prior efforts in the wildland-urban interface. As the program develops, the CRCD will seek to identify new partnership opportunities within the county’s extensive forests and rangelands. While the CRCD project will focus primarily on Santa Barbara County, fire knows no bounds. As demonstrated by the 2025 Madre and Gifford fires in the Cuyama Valley of Santa Barbara County, wildfire can quickly spread into adjacent jurisdictions. Wildfire prevention and mitigation efforts are occurring in adjacent counties and the CRCD project will leverage existing partnerships to support priorities through regional collaborations.

The subsurface power line would be connected from an existing power pole and would be trenched below the existing power pole and would be trenched through the Carpinteria Bluffs Trail. ceqa-a22ba7685004923d36.name: Cabrillo Business Park (CBP) Lot 19 Google R&D Facility Case No. 25-0001-PCR
ceqa-a22ba7685004923d36.description: The proposed project (“Project”) will develop the currently vacant 7.6-acre Lot 19 of the Cabrillo Business Park (CBP), located at 6701 Discovery Drive (formerly 355 Coromar Drive), with a new research and development (R&D) facility (Project). The R&D facility is comprised of three (3) new buildings and related site improvements. The main R&D building, Building A, is comprised of 98,847 SF (net) with two stories and third-story mezzanine elements, located in the central portion of the Project site. Building A is supported by Building B, a single-story mechanical/electrical building (not occupied), and Building C, a three level 231-space parking structure. A portion of the first floor of the parking structure (Building C) is devoted to employee amenity uses, including a fitness room, showers/restrooms, bicycle, miscellaneous storage areas, and utility areas (5,383 SF, net). The total net building floor area of the Project is 104,230 SF. The Project also includes screened yard areas that contain ground-mounted electrical/mechanical equipment, above ground tanks to store helium, nitrogen, and back up fuel supplies, and other outdoor storage needs. The Project site is developed with an existing stormwater detention basin at the southern (rear) portion of the site. The Project does not propose any modifications to the existing detention basin area. The Project will serve as the primary research and development location to build, test, refine, and improve prototype quantum computing machines that will one day be manufactured for use by end-users to facilitate new processes and solutions across different industries and platforms. The Project falls within the scope of the CBP Specific Plan, approved earlier as part of the CBP Final Environmental Impact Report (“EIR”) (SCH No. 2000041129) previously certified on April 30, 2007. The CBP Specific Plan sets out steps for development projects on individual lots which will be processed and approved through a Project Clearance application. Here, the Project will be developed on Lot 19 of the CBP Specific Plan. The City prepared a Consistency Analysis with the CBP Final EIR, which includes a checklist analyzing the consistency of the proposed Project to the CBP Specific Plan requirements. Based on the Consistency Analysis, and pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines sections 15162 and 15168(c)(4), no subsequent or supplemental EIR is required for the proposed Project because of the following: • No substantial changes are proposed in the Project which will require major revisions of the previously certified CBP EIR (SCH No. 2000041129) due to the involvement of new significant environmental effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effects; • There are no substantial changes in the circumstances under which the Project will be undertaken that will require major revisions to the previously certified CBP EIR due to the involvement of significant new environmental effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant effect; and, • No “new information of substantial importance” exists, as set forth in CEQA Guidelines Section 15162(a)(3).

ceqa-29937c1f75a05a8fbd.name: East Campus Student Housing Project
ceqa-29937c1f75a05a8fbd.projectTitle: UC Santa Barbara Long Range Development Plan
ceqa-29937c1f75a05a8fbd.description: The East Campus Student Housing project would demolish the existing Santa Rosa Residence Hall and develop approximately 328,000assignable square feet and 470,200 gross square feet of new residential construction and renovate the existing Ortega Dining Commons. The project would provide approximately 1,688 beds (1,276 new undergraduate student beds in apartment-style units, 412 replacement residence hall beds), and a renovated dining commons facility. As part of the project, Long Range Development Plan Amendment (LRDP) #8 is proposed to increase the applicable LRDP height limit from 65 feet to 85 feet to accommodate two of the project buildings in the north-center of the site. LRDP maps will also be updated to reflect current circulation and parking conditions.

ceqa-0f68b9cba4ca134919.description: The project is a qualified housing development project that utilizes the “Builders Remedy” protections of the California Housing Accountability Act and State Density Bonus Law and includes the following proposed components on the project site: * Demolition of the existing on-site residence, garage, and barn. * A subdivision of the existing 14.38-net acre parcel into 59 separate lots (via a Vesting Tentative Map). * Construction and occupancy of 56 single-family dwellings on Lot 1 through Lot 56, of which 11 residences would be income deed restricted for 55 years (4 residences at extremely low income level, 1 residence at lower income level, 3 residences at moderate income level, and 3 residences at above-moderate income levels. * Use of Lot 57 through Lot 59 for open space containing landscape and stormwater facilities. The application permit types are a Vesting Tentative Tract Map, Development Plan, and Design Review.

ceqa-3a6dff3816f16c6715.name: Santa Barbara Airport Firestone Ditch Vegetation Maintenance (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-55636-R5)
ceqa-3a6dff3816f16c6715.projectTitle: Santa Barbara Airport Firestone Ditch Vegetation Maintenance (Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-55636-R5)
ceqa-3a6dff3816f16c6715.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-SBA-55636-R5, pursuant to Section 1602 of the Fish and Game Code to City of Santa Barbara as represented by Jessica Metzger. The project is the maintenance of Firestone Ditch through vegetation trimming, mowing, and channel bottom vegetation trimming. Approximately 1,500 linear feet of riparian/wetland vegetation trimming will occur on the west side of the channel, and 1,250 linear feet of mowing and trimming of non-native vegetation will occur on the east side of the channel. This maintenance is to keep hydraulic function of the channel, clear overgrown vegetation on roads, and allow safe passage for pedestrians and cyclists. Native oaks and willows will be trimmed to a height of 10-12 feet and out of road shoulders and traffic lanes on both Firestone Road and Hollister Avenue. Non-native vegetation, which includes oleander, olives, and Mexican fan palms, will be trimmed to ground level with the root systems remaining intact to avoid erosion concerns. Roadside vegetation trimming will occur once per year, mowing grassy areas will occur four times per year, and trimming vegetation from the channel bottom will occur once every other year.

ceqa-ea6ebf8b396f12a62b.name: UCSB Marine Operations Class Collections
ceqa-ea6ebf8b396f12a62b.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Marine Region 7
ceqa-ea6ebf8b396f12a62b.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 7 - Marine, Monterey
ceqa-ea6ebf8b396f12a62b.description: The Department of Fish and Wildlife is issuing a permit to the University of California, Santa Barbara (UC Santa Barbara) pursuant to Fish and Game Code Section 2081(a) for educational purposes. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to take steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) during the course of sampling, subject to terms and conditions set forth in the permit. The purpose of this sampling is for the UC Santa Barbara’s marine operation class collections. The Section 2081(a) permit authorizes the applicant to potentially capture steelhead trout during surveys. The applicant will conduct year-round permanent collection sampling of nearshore, offshore, and estuarine marine species through the use of otter trawls, fish traps, beach seines, hook & line – surface, hook & line – baited dropper loop, and hook & line – longline bottom set through December 31, 2027.

ceqa-1aa3b8d9251c14643c.name: City of Goleta Administrative Citations, Encampments, and Vehicular Camping Ordinance
ceqa-1aa3b8d9251c14643c.projectTitle: City of Goleta Administrative Citations, Encampments, and Vehicular Camping Ordinance
ceqa-1aa3b8d9251c14643c.description: The proposed Ordinance amends the City’s regulations on encampments (Goleta Municipal Code Chapter 12.01), vehicle dwelling (Goleta Municipal Code 10.04), and administrative citations (Goleta Municipal Code Chapters 1.02 and 2.02) in the following ways: 1. Removes the requirement that staff is to ensure adequate shelter is available before enforcement to making reasonable efforts to offer services before enforcement of encampment and vehicle dwelling regulations; 2. Adds indicia of what dwelling in one’s vehicle entails; 3. Removes the authority to tow a person’s vehicle parked on City streets that has been used for dwelling for more than 72 hours; 4. Incorporates state law with regard to City’s cost recovery remedies and prevailing party recovery of costs and fees with respect to administrative citations; and 5. Makes other ancillary amendments to effectuate the above-mentioned goals.

ceqa-c3afa91a009f460fbf.name: Construction of a New Replacement Well for the SB Corp Well
ceqa-c3afa91a009f460fbf.projectTitle: Construction of a New Replacement Well for the SB Corp Well
ceqa-c3afa91a009f460fbf.description: The subject project involves drilling, construction, and testing of the new replacement well to replace the existing Santa Barbara Corporation (“SB Corp”) Well that was drilled nearly 45 years ago and has been inactive for approximately 33 years due to inadequate production. The new replacement well will be drilled to a drought tolerant depth of approximately 750’ below ground surface (bgs). The existing well site will be reconfigured with a new iron and manganese removal treatment facility that will treat the new replacement well water to State drinking water quality standards.

ceqa-b286fa094d91ed3d25.name: Los Patos Underpass Removal Project
ceqa-b286fa094d91ed3d25.description: Following the closure and removal of the Los Patos Way off-ramp (Exit 95) on southbound U.S. 101, which would occur under the U.S. 101 HOV Project, The proposed Project would involve demolition and removal of the Los Patos Rail Bridge, including its abutments, center pier, girders, and decking. The bridge would be replaced with solid fill material, and Los Patos Way south of the railroad tracks would be configured as a cul-de-sac. During bridge removal and construction, rail service would continue via a temporary bypass track (shoofly) built on UPRR right-of-way, crossing Los Patos Way and Cabrillo Boulevard. The shoofly would be supported by 8,000 cubic yards of fill and would include a bridge over Cabrillo Boulevard. Grading and earthwork for the proposed Project is anticipated to last three weeks and the reconstruction of the rail components would be completed in two days (over one weekend).
ceqa-b286fa094d91ed3d25.crossStreets: Los Patos Way and U.S. Highway 101

ceqa-19103bf66b4e3151ee.name: North Fork Ranch Tentative Parcel Map
ceqa-19103bf66b4e3151ee.projectTitle: North Fork Ranch Tentative Parcel Map
ceqa-19103bf66b4e3151ee.description: This project is a request for a Tentative Parcel Map (Case No. 18TRM-00000-00001) to subdivide an existing 7,758-acre gross property with two legal lots into three lots ranging in size from approximately 1,013 acres to 4,745 acres on property zoned AG-II-100. The subject property under Case No. 18TPM-00000-00001 is located within Santa Barbara County, though the applicant also owns contiguous parcel in San Luis Obispo County that is labeled as “Not a Part” on the Tentative Parcel Map; it’s a remainder under San Luis Obispo County’s jurisdiction and subject to their local rules and requirements after approval of the subject parcel map under Santa Barbara County Jurisdiction. Within Santa Barbara County Jurisdiction, Proposed Parcel 1 consists of approximately 2,000 acres gross, Proposed Parcel 2 consists of approximately 4,745 acres gross, and Proposed Parcel 3 consists of approximately 1,013 acres gross. The purpose of the proposed subdivision and subsequent action in San Luis Obispo County is two-fold: 1) Northeast of Highway 166, the purpose is to provide a boundary solution between Proposed Parcel 3 and the existing parcel within San Luis Obispo County; the land contained within Proposed Parcel 3 is almost entirely within an existing legal lot (APN 147-020-046), but this property is included within the proposed subdivision in order to align the shared property line between these two parcels with the County line, which is the centerline of the Cuyama River, and is therefore ambulatory. The current property line results in portions of each legal parcel overlapping the County line. No new parcels will be created northeast of Highway 166. 2) Southwest of Highway 166, the purpose is to divide the existing single legal parcel (APN 147-020-045, ~6,745 acres into two legal parcels (Proposed Parcel 1 of ~2,000 acres and Proposed Parcel 2 of ~4,745 acres). The proposed parcel lines roughly follow the boundary between prime soils suitable for vineyard production and non-prime soils better suited to grazing. There is one existing main residence on the property, located on Proposed Parcel 1; the other parcels are not residentially developed, and no residential development is proposed at this time. Domestic water is currently provided to Proposed Parcel 1 by a Single-Parcel Domestic Water System utilizing existing wells near the Cuyama River north of Highway 166 on Proposed Parcel 3. Sewage disposal for the existing residence is provided by an existing private septic system. The applicant proposed one building envelope each on Proposed Parcels 2 and 3 to identify sites for potential future residential development near existing utilities and outside of constrained areas, and one building envelope over existing residential development on Proposed Parcel 1. The three building envelopes are each approximately 2 acres in area. The building envelopes include all areas of each proposed parcel where residential or residential-related accessory structures and associated improvements either are already developed or could be developed in the future, if desired. Domestic water serving potential future residences within proposed building envelopes on Proposed Parcels 1 and 2 would be provided by a Multiple-Parcel Domestic Water System utilizing the same existing well on Proposed Parcel 3 that already serves residential development on Proposed Parcel 1. Sewage disposal for potential future residences would also be provided by private septic systems within proposed building envelopes. Access to the subject property is from Highway 166 via existing Caltrans-approved access points and existing agricultural roads, and access to all proposed parcels would be available from Highway 166 via those same existing Caltrans-approved access points. Proposed Parcels 1 and 3 front Highway 166 at existing Caltrans-approved access points, while Proposed Parcel 2 will be accessed via a reserved 24-foot-wide easement over Proposed Parcel 1. Proposed Parcels 1 and 2 also have access via Cottonwood Canyon Road (60-foot-wide public road) and Schoolhouse Canyon Road (30-foot-wide private road per easement recorded as 20005-0089167). The Tentative Parcel Map application involves Assessor’s Parcel Nos. 147-020-045 and 147-020-046 located in the unincorporated Cuyama area, First Supervisorial District.

The affordability levels of these units are as follows: • 30% AMI = 72 units • 50% AM = 22 units • 60% AMI = 22 units • 80% AMI = 118 units The number of bedrooms and approximate unit square footage are as follows: Market-Rate Unit Summary Unit Type Unit Sq. Ft. No. of Bedrooms No. of Units Total Sq. Ft. A 773 1 288 222,624 B 1,020 2 432 440,640 Affordable Unit Summary Unit Type Unit Sq. Ft. No. of Bedrooms No. of Units Total Sq. Ft. 1 BED 457 1 115 52,555 2 BED 708 2 61 43,188 3 BED 930 3 60 55,800 The residential buildings are three stories in height and will be designed in the Goleta farmhouse style. Site amenities on Parcel 1 include a clubhouse, fitness center, pool, spa, barbecue patio, lounge areas, turf area, and community garden. Site amenities on Parcel 2 include a community room, fitness center, covered patio, fenced dog run, tot lot, and pedestrian walking loop. There will also be instructor-led adult educational, health and wellness, and skill building classes (such as financial literacy, computer training, home-buyer education, GED, resume building, ESL, nutrition, exercise, health information/awareness, art, parenting, on-site food cultivation and preparation, and smoking cessation), and health and wellness services and programs (such as visiting nurse programs, intergenerational visiting programs, and senior companion programs), free of charge to residents on Parcel 2 on an ongoing nature for a term of fifteen years. A portion of Parcel 1 is being developed and then dedicated to the County as a public park. The public park will be developed with a pergola-covered patio with picnic table seating, a passive turf area, and a concrete pathway. The applicant is requesting the following concessions and waivers under the State Density Bonus Law: Concessions: • Increase in allowed height from a maximum of 35’-0” to a maximum of approximately 40’-0”. Waivers: • Waiver of 40% open space requirement in the DR Zone. The project proposes approximately 34% of the site as open space. • Waiver to allow a portion of the side setback at the southwest corner to be used for vehicle parking. • Waiver to allow a reduction in the front setback for the buildings along South San Marcos Road from 20 feet to 10 feet to accommodate a new right-turn pocket to San Marcos Road. The applicant is requesting a vehicular parking ratio, pursuant to State Density Bonus Law, of: (A) zero to one bedroom: one onsite parking space, (B) two to three bedrooms: one and one-half onsite parking spaces. 1,447 parking spaces are proposed (1,150 on Parcel 1 and 297 on Parcel 2). 360 bicycle parking spaces are proposed on Parcel 1, and 120 bicycle parking spaces are proposed on Parcel 2. Grading will consist of 60,596 cubic yards of cut and 62,190 cubic yards of fill on Parcel 1 and 9,126 cubic yards of cut and 8,589 cubic yards of fill on Parcel 2. The following native trees will be removed on Parcel 1: nine coast live oak trees, one California sycamore tree. The trees will be mitigated with 32 coast live oak trees, two California sycamore trees, six Catalina ironwood trees, six California buckeye trees, and six western redbud trees. The parcels will be served by the Goleta Water District, the Goleta Sanitary District, and the Santa Barbara County Fire Department. Access will be provided off South San Marcos Road and San Simeon Drive. The properties are a 27.37-acre parcel and a 5.7-acre parcel zoned DR-20/30 and DR-30/40 and shown as Assessor's Parcel Numbers 065-040-041 and 065-030-012, located at 4960 Hollister Avenue and 125 South San Marcos Road in the Eastern Goleta Valley Community Plan area, Second Supervisorial District.

ceqa-a921a829edffc266ce.name: Platforms Hogan and Houchin Plugging and Abandonment Project
ceqa-a921a829edffc266ce.projectTitle: Platforms Hogan and Houchin Plugging and Abandonment Project
ceqa-a921a829edffc266ce.agency: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-a921a829edffc266ce.agencyName: Santa Barbara County Air Pollution Control District
ceqa-a921a829edffc266ce.description: For the purposes of review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the District’s Regulation VIII, New Source Review, the project consists of the actions described in District permits no. PTO 15962 01, PTO 15978 01, ATC 16435, ATC 16459, and ATC 16460. These permits authorize operations and equipment in support of the plugging and abandonment (P&A) of oil and gas wells associated with Platform Hogan and Platform Houchin. Specifically, the subject permits will authorize: the installation and operation of a new, portable crane and associated Tier 4 Final engine; the replacement of the Platform Hogan South Unit Crane engine with a new Tier 4 Final diesel-fired engine; the use of up to six (6) prime power, diesel engines for the purposes of well abandonment to be located on the abandonment rig; the use of one (1) additional diesel engine for emergency electrical power use in instances of power outages and disruptions that may be transported between platforms; and increases to the annual flaring limits at the platforms to support blowdowns of wells and perform end-of-life abandonments. P&A work will start at Platform Hogan and move to Platform Houchin sequentially as P&A operations cannot be conducted simultaneously due to the specialty equipment associated with the P&A process. The estimated completion of the P&A program at Platform Hogan is expected to be prior to the end of 2027. P&A work at Platform Houchin is anticipated to take an additional 1-2 years to complete.

ceqa-974532c57f3503aaad.name: Southern California Edison Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Installation
ceqa-974532c57f3503aaad.projectTitle: Southern California Edison Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Installation
ceqa-974532c57f3503aaad.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-974532c57f3503aaad.description: Pursuant to California Public Utilities Commission Decision 19-11-017, as mandated by AB 1083 (Charge Ready Parks), and agreed upon by a master agreement between the California Department of Parks and Recreation and Southern California Edison (SCE), this project proposes site and electrical infrastructure improvements for the installation of electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) by SCE and/or its subcontractors in the existing day use parking lot along Sandyland Rd. The purpose of this project is to support the usage of electric vehicles by providing charging locations in State Parks and will contribute to the State’s goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Eleven existing standard parking stalls and one existing handicapped stall will be replaced with twelve stalls equipped with ten Level 2 and two Direct Current Fast Charging (DCFC) charging ports, including two ADA van stalls and one standard ADA parking stall, resulting in a net gain of two handicapped van stalls and a loss of one existing standard parking stall that is not expected to impact visitor services. Construction activities include minor excavation, trenching, and backfilling to install new equipment. During construction, a traffic and pedestrian safety control plan will ensure there are no impacts to visitor services. A right of entry permit will be issued to SCE and/or its subcontractors to complete the work. All applicable regulatory permits are required prior to the start of construction, and all work shall adhere to Departmental policies and standard best management practices to minimize impacts to sensitive resources. Measures to be implemented to avoid and minimize impact may be obtained by submitting a request to the project contact listed below.

ceqa-2931853b31683eb046.description: The proposed project would include subdivision of the project site into 114 lots that would be developed with 105 detached single-family residences. ceqa-a21dfd618ee6a76c67.name: 761 Fleming Avenue Subdivision
ceqa-a21dfd618ee6a76c67.description: The proposed project would include the prezoning of the currently unincorporated approximately 2.08 acre property at 761 Fleming Avenue to the R-1-8 zoning district and the annexation of the parcel into the City of San José to facilitate subdivision of the site into nine separate residential lots. One single-family home would be constructed on each subdivided lot except for lot 4, which already includes an existing residence to be retained, for a total of nine houses on the project site. The new lots would range from approximately 6,015 square feet to 22,571 square feet. No accessory dwelling units (ADUs) are currently proposed but would be allowed in the future at the discretion of each property owner subject to applicable regulations. The project would include the extension of Townsquare Drive as a public street that terminates in a cul-de-sac to provide access to the proposed lots 5 through 9. The existing, unnamed private street that connects to Fleming Avenue would extend as a continuation of Townsquare Drive to the proposed cul-de-sac and provide access to lots 1-4, with the private street connecting to Fleming Avenue, and continuing to provide access to Fleming Avenue for the several adjacent existing residences that currently rely on the existing driveway for street access.

ceqa-e2feb90366f1c53bb5.name: Physical Specimen Collection and Curation
ceqa-e2feb90366f1c53bb5.description: The Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (District) proposes to establish a Physical Specimen Collection and Curations component of the District’s Inventory and Monitoring Program (Program). The Specimen Collection and Curation component supports the overarching goal of the Program to systematically document natural resources on District lands and provide reliable scientific information that supports resource protection, management, planning, and adaptive management. Specimens would be collected by District staff or by individuals authorized through a Direct Permit (authorized collectors), and would be collected only for inventory, monitoring, research, or educational activities. Specimens would be collected consistent with the District’s Standard Operating Procedures for Physical Specimen Collection and Curation[JM2.1][MC2.2][JM2.3] in a manner that minimizes impacts to species and habitats; and curated as traceable, verifiable reference materials that support repeatable identification and long-term monitoring, resource inventory, and long-term data integrity. Authorized collectors would not collect when doing so would reasonably be expected to cause undue harm to a local population, individual organism, or the surrounding environment. Collection activities would also avoid unnecessary disturbance to soils, water, vegetation, wildlife, and habitat features, including sensitive substrates and microhabitats. All specimen collection conducted under the Program would comply with applicable Federal, State, and local requirements, including any permits or permissions required for collection, possession, transport, and curation. Specimen categories proposed for collection include: • Plants: Authorized collectors would collect voucher specimens of vascular and non-vascular plants, limited to one primary voucher per taxon, occurrence, and collection event. • Fungal: Authorized collectors would collect the full fruiting body or other diagnostic fungal material present at the time of collection, limited to the minimum number of fruiting bodies and amount of associated substrate necessary for identification and curation. • Invertebrate: Authorized collectors would collect voucher specimens of insects and other terrestrial or aquatic invertebrate taxa, limited to a small representative number sufficient for identification, verification, and approved reference needs. • Vertebrate and paleontological: Authorized collectors would generally rely on non-collection methods (e.g., observations, photographs, remote cameras, acoustic recordings) rather than physical specimen collection. Except where capture or collection of live vertebrates is explicitly permitted and authorized, physical specimens of modern vertebrates would be collected only for approved objectives and only from non-living, naturally shed, abandoned, or deceased material in a manner that avoids disturbance or harm to live animals.

ceqa-39f63e314c91bee3ac.description: The Project would recontour an earthen mound currently preventing flow from Coyote Creek Branch A from entering a Highway 101 culvert (canal station 310+00) using a small excavator, repair a 50-foot-long section of earthen levee where it failed in 2017 (canal station 293+60) with 100 to 150 CY of clean levee fill, and clear an estimated 300 CY of sediment from a 480-foot-long, 8-foot-wide, 5-foot-tall concrete box culvert that conveys the canal beneath Highway 101 (canal stations 288+05 to 283+25) using a remote-controlled tracked machine and, if needed, a hydrovac tank truck. Valley Water Standard BMPs have been incorporated into the Project and would prevent sedimentation and degradation of water quality in downgradient waterbodies. The Project is scheduled for October/November 2026 and would take approximately 2 weeks to complete.

ceqa-bb3ff40148b6c0c02a.name: I-280 Culvert Replacement (EA 04-0V250)
ceqa-bb3ff40148b6c0c02a.description: Caltrans proposes removing and replacing a culvert system on the Interstate (I-) 280 southbound separation to State Route (SR-) 87 in Santa Clara County from post mile (PM) R2.8 to R3.0. There is a substantial amount of water seeping through the pavement and depressed areas between the two drainage inlets (Dis) on the asphalt concrete (AC) pavement. Based on visual inspections of the site and review of the as-builts, the settlement and cracks is likely due to the failure of the underdrain pipes. The underdrains have limited capacity as they are partially filled with soil, corroded, and at some locations are fully blocked, causing water seepage through the roadway surface. The foundation soils are migrating into the underdrain system and as a result, cavities and settlement have been created. To prevent the underdrain system from migrating into the water seepage, the existing underdrain will be removed and replaced with a new system consisting of 10” Perforated PVC pile (PPP) (Refer to D102 in 2022 Standard Plans), and a Class 3 Permeable Material (PM) drainage layer under the shoulder with a length of 330’ to draw down the inflow of the groundwater. Trenching of the roadway will be required to access the underdrain. The foundation soils under the pavement will be strengthened using compaction grouting in combination with sodium silicate, which is a fast-acting chemical setting agent. Before the construction of the new underdrain, the compaction grouting will be used within the limits of the settled areas to an approximate depth of 20 feet. The roadway will then be repaved with hot mix asphalt (HMA). Traffic control will be required during construction.

ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.name: Applied Materials Building 100 EPIC Center Semiconductor Research and Development Laboratory, Air District Permit Application No. 700650
ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.projectTitle: Applied Materials Building 100 EPIC Center Semiconductor Research and Development Laboratory, Air District Permit Application No. 700650
ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.agency: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.agencyName: Bay Area Air Quality Management District
ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.description: The Bay Area Air District is considering issuing an Authority to Construction and Permit to Operate under Air District Permit Application NO. 700650 for two new permitted stationary sources at the Applied Materials Arques campus at 974 East Arques Avenue in Sunnyvale: Source S-264, a semiconductor research and development laboratory containing vacuum deposition and plasma etching tools and wet process tools, with integral point of use abatement devices, eight packed bed acid scrubbers, a two stage concentrator wheel, and an electric regenerative thermal oxidizer, discharging through nine exhaust stacks; and Source S-265, a surface preparation (wipe cleaning) operation. The sources would be housed in Building 100, the Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center, a 592,567 gross square foot research and development building that implements Phase 1 of the Arques Campus Specific Plan. The City of Sunnyvale, as Lead Agency, certified the Arques Campus Specific Plan Environmental Impact Report in June 1999 (SCH NO. 1998092072) and approved the building and associated improvements in April 2024. The Air District's discretionary action is limited to the stationary source permits and the conditions under which the permitted sources may operate. The issuance of an Authority to Construct is a discretionary approval subject to CEQA. Through its evaluation of the permit application, the Air District developed a project specific emissions inventory quantifying emissions of greenhouse gases and criteria air pollutants that were not evaluated in the 1999 Arques EIR. Pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15163(a), which provides that either the Lead Agency or a Responsible Agency may prepare a supplement to an EIR, the Air District has prepared a focused Draft Supplemental Environmental Impact Report addressing Air Quality and Greenhouse Gas Emissions. The document identifies significant and unavoidable impacts related to a cumulatively considerable net increase in ozone precursor emissions and to the generation of greenhouse gas emissions and the resulting conflict with plans adopted for the purpose of reducing those emissions.
ceqa-dd74a0a83ee62d860b.crossStreets: East Arques Avenue and Commercial Street

ceqa-82046e4bf526db50c9.name: Gilroy to Central Valley Wye Project Segment of the San Jose to Merced Project Section
ceqa-82046e4bf526db50c9.projectTitle: Gilroy to Central Valley Wye Project Segment of the San Jose to Merced Project Section
ceqa-82046e4bf526db50c9.description: The Authority approved an alignment from San Jose to the Central Valley Wye based on the 2022 Final EIR/EIS for the San Jose to Merced Project Section. The Authority is exploring optimized design solutions from south of Gilroy to northeast of Gilroy to reduce project costs in light of current revenue forecasts. The Previously Approved Alignment extends 46.1 miles east from Gilroy through the Pacheco Pass and includes 15.1 miles in tunnel. The Authority has developed three new alternatives. Alternative 5 would follow the same alignment as the Previously Approved alignment, but would have 10.7 miles in tunnel. Alternatives 6 and 7 would diverge from the Previously Approved alignment, would travel south of the San Luis Reservoir across the Diablo Range, and would have 4 miles in tunnel. Alternative 5, 6 and 7 would initially have single-track alignments across the Diablo Range, double-track alignments beyond the hills and would be planned for initial operation in 2040. Alternatives 5, 6 and 7 would have double-track alignment the entire distance by 2050. All alternatives would include a Maintenance of Way Facility (MOWF) south of Gilroy, traction power facilities, train control and communication facilities, and access road. No new stations are include in this segment.

ceqa-b7d73ab1fbf9dd2ac2.name: Civic Center Master Plan

ceqa-b706c1c6c37973877a.description: The project applicant, Dividend Homes, Inc., is proposing a residential development that would involve the demolition of the existing commercial buildings and the construction of 35 units in five, sevenplex townhome buildings. Each building would be three to four stories and a maximum of 44 feet, 9 inches tall at the highest point as measured from the finished floor. Each unit would have a second-floor balcony and roof deck, providing 327 to 515 square feet of private outdoor space per unit.
