ceqa-26f92f02fe74c3fa7f.name: Guadalupe River Bridge Replacement Project
ceqa-26f92f02fe74c3fa7f.description: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (JPB), which operates the San Francisco Bay Area’s Caltrain passenger rail service, proposes the Guadalupe River Bridge Replacement Project (the Project) in the City of San José, Santa Clara County, California. Caltrain operates trains on two tracks, MT-1 and MT-2, over the Guadalupe River on two independent and immediately adjacent bridges, each carrying a single track. The downstream (Northerly) bridge (MT-1) consists of a wooden trestle bridge constructed in 1935; the upstream bridge (MT-2) consists of a concrete bridge constructed in 1990 as part of the Caltrans Highway 87 Project. To address safety issues and protect the rail bridge assets, Caltrain proposes to widen the channel; replace the MT-1 bridge with a new, longer bridge; and extend the MT-2 bridge on the southern side to help address geomorphic stability issues at the bridge abutments. JPB is the lead agency for the Project and adopted a Final Mitigated Negative Declaration (IS/MND) in February 2021. In March 2025 JPB adopted an addendum to the MND (Addendum No. 1) to address an updated Hydromodification Management Plan; changes in project duration and sequencing; revised limits for clearing and grubbing, grading, and erosion control; and some activities related to construction that could occur at night. In April 2026, JPB adopted an addendum to the MND (Addendum No. 2) to evaluate additional proposed changes to the Project that would include amendments to applicable permits. In August 2026, JPB adopted an addendum to the MND (Addendum No. 3) that incorporates a habitat restoration project at Hicks Creek (Hicks Creek Mitigation) within the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (District) Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve to provide mitigation for Project impacts in addition to proposed onsite mitigation. The restoration project, which includes removing invasive plants, concrete structures, and other impediments, and replanting the area with native species, will provide off-site mitigation credit for the Project’s jurisdictional impacts. The third addendum to the Project evaluated the proposed changes to the Project to identify and address any new potential environmental impacts that were not evaluated by the 2021 MND and the first and second addendums prepared in March 2025 and April 2026 respectively. The District is a responsible agency for the proposed mitigation work at the Hicks Creek Site. The District and JPB are entering into a Mitigation Agreement to authorize implementation of the Hicks Creek Mitigation project and establish JPB’s responsibility for project funding, design, permitting, construction, maintenance, monitoring, and adaptive management. Construction of the Hicks Creek Mitigation project is anticipated during summer 2027.

ceqa-cfc97f5dccc4285613.name: Subsurface Utility Exploration for the Palo Alto Grade Separation Project
ceqa-cfc97f5dccc4285613.projectTitle: Subsurface Utility Exploration for the Palo Alto Grade Separation Project
ceqa-cfc97f5dccc4285613.description: [PROJECT TITLE CONTINUED]: (Churchill Avenue, Seale Avenue, Meadow Drive, and Charleston Road Crossings) The proposed project consists of temporary subsurface utility investigation activities to support ongoing design and engineering of the City of Palo Alto Grade Separation Project (Grade Separation Project). Work would occur at 13 locations within the existing developed transportation corridors associated with Churchill Avenue, Seale Avenue, Meadow Drive, and Charleston Road crossings. Activities would include utility designations services and air-vacuum potholing – activities to verify the location, depth, size and material of existing underground utilities. The utility investigations will be conducted in accordance with applicable encroachment permit, traffic-control, and notification requirements. Potholes would be restored following the completion of investigation activities. The purpose of this project is to collect information needed to support utility coordination, engineering design, and utility relocation activities associated with the proposed grade separation improvements. Beneficiaries include Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), the City of Palo Alto, utility owners, and the public.
ceqa-cfc97f5dccc4285613.crossStreets: Caltrain right of way at Churchill Avenue, Seale Avenue, Meadow Drive, and Charleston Road

ceqa-d6d65ed6dfc944f6d0.name: New Valley High School Project
ceqa-d6d65ed6dfc944f6d0.description: The New Valley High School Project would relocate New Valley High School from its current location at 1875 Lawrence Road to the Educational Options Campus located at 1840 Benton Street, Santa Clara, California. The purpose of the proposed Project is to provide a consolidated, modern campus for the New Valley High School students. The proposed Project includes construction of a two-story building with new classrooms, labs, and new weight room. Parking improvements would include adding approximately 73 new parking spaces for a total of 356 parking spaces. A new Student Union would be constructed that would include outdoor seating areas with picnic tables and a new sports court. Existing locker rooms will be reconfigured to create separate rooms for New Valley High School and Adult Education. Other locker room improvements include new showers, changing rooms, and restrooms that comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). The existing Nutrition Services Kitchen would be renovated to support the new students and staff. Construction would occur for approximately 18 months expected to begin in July 2027. Construction hours are expected to be 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on Saturday. Off-campus road closures are not anticipated

ceqa-a966d2fffbd6771a2a.name: Bracher Elementary School Campus Removal Action Work Plan
ceqa-a966d2fffbd6771a2a.projectTitle: Bracher Elementary School Master Plan Project
ceqa-a966d2fffbd6771a2a.description: The Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) approved the Removal Action Workplan (RAW) for the Bracher Elementary School Campus (Project Site). The Cleanup document, referred to as a RAW, summarized previous environmental investigations and concluded that the remediation of soil is required to protect human health and the environment. The RAW addressed the impacts of the chemical of concern identified as, organochlorine pesticides (4,4-DDE) and metals (arsenic, lead, cobalt, mercury) in shallow soil. Remediation activities include: • Conduct limited excavation of the top 1 foot of affected soil across all current and future landscaping within the redevelopment area, including removal of the eastern soil stockpile; remove approximately 20,000 in-place cubic yards, requiring approximately 1,600 truckloads; and transport and dispose of the excavated soil off site. • Backfill with clean imported fill verified in accordance with DTSC’s Information Advisory on Clean Imported Fill Material (October 2001); install hardscape caps (building slabs, concrete/asphalt sidewalks and parking areas, rubber play surfaces, artificial turf); and install softscape caps consisting of a geotextile marker and a minimum of 1 foot of certified clean fill in landscaped areas. • Air/dust controls and monitoring during soil handling: implementation of the Dust Control Plan and Community Air Monitoring Plan (CAMP) with specified action levels and work stoppage thresholds, and adherence to BAAQMD lead/dust requirements. • Site security and implementation measures (perimeter fencing, work-zone controls, utility clearance, Health and Safety Plan (HASP), biological/cultural resources compliance consistent with IS/MND mitigation). • Preparation of a Removal Action Completion Report (RACR) documenting excavation, disposal manifests, air monitoring results, and post-action risk evaluation of soils remaining in place under the cap. • Finalize and implement a Site-wide Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Plan for the cap and record a Land Use Covenant (deed restriction) to require non-interference with the remedy and manage any future intrusive work. The Santa Clara Unified School District approved the Bracher Elementary School Master Plan Initial Study / Mitigated Negative Declaration (IS/MND) (State Clearinghouse Number 2024120148) on January 23, 2025. DTSC determined the prior environmental analysis adequately addresses the RAW activities, including soil import and export, and these activities will occur within the previously evaluated project boundaries. DTSC prepared a Statement of Findings, and the RAW will comply with all applicable IS/MND mitigation measures.

ceqa-2abaadce131157de2a.name: Tree Removal in Kirk Diversion Dam Vegetation Management Area
ceqa-2abaadce131157de2a.projectTitle: Tree Removal in Kirk Diversion Dam Vegetation Management Area
ceqa-2abaadce131157de2a.description: Located in Los Gatos Creek County Park in the town of Los Gatos, the Kirk Diversion is an instream facility on Los Gatos Creek used for diversion, re-diversion, and conveyance of water to groundwater percolation ponds in the Los Gatos Groundwater Recharge System. Kirk Diversion Dam is comprised of an inflatable rubber dam installed on top of a concrete apron. The inflatable dam is 90 feet long and spans the concrete apron. Kirk Diversion Dam may be inflated or deflated at any time to divert or redivert local flows, and will automatically deflate for unanticipated high flows when the depth of water is 1.4 feet above the dam crest. A sluice gate at the east side of the dam is used to bypass up to 250 cubic feet per second (cfs) through a low flow channel. The Kirk Diversion Dam Vegetation Management Area extends 100 feet downstream of the Kirk inflatable dam and concrete apron. Valley Water proposes to remove approximately 30 live standing, live fallen, dead/dying standing, and dead fallen native, non-native, and invasive trees from the Kirk Diversion Dam Vegetation Management Area to re-establish the clear zone below the dam; prevent damage to the inflatable dam from fallen trees, provide access to the area below the dam for maintenance; prevent flow obstructions and alteration of flow patterns in the low-flow channel downstream of the dam; and allow for visual inspection and camera surveillance of the inflatable dam and it’s appurtenances from downstream areas. Equipment would enter the Los Gatos Creek channel below Kirk Diversion Dam from the right bank. A temporary access ramp over the low flow channel would provide equipment access to the left bank. Depending on groundwater conditions during construction, temporary sump pumps and hoses may be used to maintain a dry work area on either side of the low flow channel. Water pumped out of the work area would be released back to Los Gatos Creek approximately 20 feet downstream of the Kirk Dam Vegetation Management Area. Trees would be removed using traditional climbing techniques. Valley Water Standard Best Management Practices (BMPs) and Santa Clara Valley Habitat Plan Aquatic Avoidance and Minimization Measures (Aquatic AMMs) have been incorporated into the project. The BMPs and Aquatic AMMs would protect riparian and aquatic habitat and prevent sedimentation and degradation of water quality in Los Gatos Creek. The project is anticipated to take 3 weeks to complete.
ceqa-2abaadce131157de2a.crossStreets: Knowles Dr and Dell Ave (closest cross streets)

ceqa-01ecffdda160539984.name: Los Gatos Stream Gauge 5119 Modification Project
ceqa-01ecffdda160539984.projectTitle: Los Gatos Stream Gauge 5119 Modification Project
ceqa-01ecffdda160539984.description: Located in Los Gatos Creek County Park in the town of Los Gatos, Los Gatos Stream Gauge 5119 (Gauge 5119) is used to measure instream bypass flows at the Kirk Diversion Dam established by the Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreement (LSAA) for the Kirk Diversion Operation and Maintenance Project (Notification No. 1600-2018-0386) to support downstream aquatic habitat. Gauge 5119 is located below a pedestrian bridge and on top of a concrete drop structure on Los Gatos Creek. The existing concrete drop structure is 53 feet long, extends 100 feet across the entire width of Los Gatos Creek, and serves as the weir for Gauge 5119. Flow over the top of the drop structure occurs as shallow sheet flow, and the Gauge 5119 flow readings correlate to the depth of the water on top of the concrete drop structure. Due to the shallow depth of water on top of the concrete drop structure, minor variations in stage (i.e., water surface elevation) result in large changes in flow readings, adversely affecting the accuracy of the flow measurements. Valley Water proposes installing a 1-foot-tall, 3/8-inch-thick steel weir plate over the top of the existing concrete drop structure. A v-notch in the center of the weir plate would concentrate low flows and produce larger changes in water depth for small variations in flow. This modification would improve the resolution and accuracy of the low flow measurements at Gauge 5119. A weir box would be affixed to the upstream face of the drop structure at the center of the weir. The weir box would provide hydrographers with a suitable cross section to take accurate discharge measurements for calibrating the stream gauge while reducing field safety hazards and streamlining data collection. A bubbler-type, differential pressure stream gauge enclosed in 1.5-inch-diameter galvanized pipe conduit would extend from the new gauge to an enclosed gauge house with a data logger above the right top of bank immediately upstream of the drop structure. Solar panels mounted on top of the enclosure would power the system. Valley Water Standard Best Management Practices (BMPs) and Santa Clara Valley Habitat Plan Aquatic Avoidance and Minimization Measures (Aquatic AMMs) have been incorporated into the project. ceqa-7ea49f5b4cc8e699a3.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Stanford University, Stanford, California
ceqa-7ea49f5b4cc8e699a3.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Stanford University, Stanford, California
ceqa-7ea49f5b4cc8e699a3.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-7ea49f5b4cc8e699a3.description: Project Description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to the Stanford University, (EPA ID# CAD982049439) to treat hazardous wastes through a controlled reaction with chemical solution; transfer and storage of Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) hazardous waste to a trailer that meets the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) flammable specifications and transport the hazardous waste to a final disposition facility. Specifically, two (2) 1-Liter containers of Ethyl Ether, one (1) 5-ml container of Acetaldehyde, two (2) 1-Liter containers of 2-Ethoxyethane, one (1) 500-ml container of Hydroxyethyl Methacrylate, one (1) 100-gram container of 2,4 Dinitrophenol, two (2) 5-gram containers of 2,4 Dinitrophenol and one (1)80-ml container of Sodium Azide Solution (10 total items) must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored in Stanford University’s Room 307 of Building 300 located at 260 Panama Street, Stanford, California. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued for treatment of chemicals to chemically stabilize the hazardous wastes prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site by Clean Harbors Environmental Services (CHES). Background: The peroxide-forming and polymerizable materials, like Ethyl Ether, Acetaldehyde, 2-Ethoxyethane or Hydroxyethyl Methacrylate, may react with atmospheric oxygen to form highly shock-sensitive, explosive peroxides and polymers. Upon accumulation or expiration, these compounds can violently explode when exposed to heat, friction, or mechanical shock. The proper way to destruct a peroxide-containing chemical (in aqueous) requires a prior test for existing peroxide levels. If NO peroxide is detected, a small amount of inhibitors (like Hydroquinone) will be added to each 1 liter of peroxide forming liquid. If LOW (< 100 ppm peroxide) levels of peroxide are present, a small amount of Ferrous Ammonium Sulfate Solution will be added to each 1 liter of peroxide forming liquid. If HIGH levels of peroxide are present, H&S or Operations must be contacted to determine an alternative method of management. Shock-sensitive / temperature sensitive material, like 2,4 Dinitrophenol or Sodium Azide Solution, has potential for a reaction, which includes fire and/or deflagration, when material becomes dry or improperly handled. The proper way to destruct this kind of material is to dilute its concentration with adequate solvent (DI water) or to adjust its pH to a proper pH range to become less reactive. Ensure that all solids are saturated and all lumps are broken up with plastic stirrer. Be sure to wet cap and threads of the container. Maximum 1-gallon charge sizes, utilizing as many containers as needed. Due to the potential explosivity and the sensitivity to shock and friction, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilizations are recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility.

ceqa-fff88cefa0ac9f19a1.description: The Campbell Well Field (CWF) is a groundwater facility comprised of three production wells and associated utility infrastructure owned and operated by Valley Water, located at 47 Maravilla Court, Campbell, CA. The Project is to decommission Well B (State ID# 07S01W27P009) of the CWF. Well B is located within a pump house near a residential area (see Figure 1). The pump house is located within an approximately 1,800 square foot level and paved area on Valley Water owned land. Overhead access for well decommissioning activities is through a 4-foot by 4-foot skylight in the roof of the pump house. The well would be sealed with cement poured in one continuous event and will be installed to the level of the top of the well casing and smoothed to match the existing pump pedestal surface. Within the paved area is a storm drain that discharges directly into San Tomas Aquino Creek, which is located approximately 0.4 miles west of the western boundary of the site. All vehicles and equipment will access the site using the sole ingress/egress access point off Campbell Avenue.

ceqa-e69e786f04b3f7fe11.name: Caltrans District 4 Vegetation Management Program Corridor -Contract 3 Wildfire Adaptation Fuel Reduction Vegetation and Tree
ceqa-e69e786f04b3f7fe11.projectTitle: Caltrans District 4 Vegetation Management Program Corridor -Contract 3 Wildfire Adaptation Fuel Reduction Vegetation and Tree
ceqa-e69e786f04b3f7fe11.description: The vegetation management will reduce wildfire fuels by establishing shaded fuel breaks, reducing fuel loads, maintaining fire breaks, and help maintain access of the State Highway System (SHS) during emergency events. These actions help ensure the SHS provides consistent access for emergency first-responders and the public during wildfire events, help create a strategic control line for pre-suppression efforts, and increase the likelihood of successful wildfire containment by lowering fire intensity, severity and slowing the rate of spread. Ultimately, the project will help protect and serve nearby communities, critical infrastructure, and natural resources. Treatment objectives include reducing ladder fuels and dense understory vegetation to disrupt vertical fuel continuity. Herbicide treatments will be applied to cut stumps and targeted regrowth under the direction of licensed professionals to maintain long-term hazard reduction. Vegetation Management work will be conducted at 27 Locations along the SHS in eight Bay Area counties.

ceqa-4744a34cdde905a20e.description: The proposed project would involve a General Plan Amendment (GPA) and Rezone (RZ) to modify the existing land use and zoning designations of the project site. The proposed GPA would change the General Plan land use designation from Commercial to Mixed Use Flex and the proposed RZ would change the zoning from General Commercial to Mixed Use Flex (MU-F). ceqa-77fecbf14265f14889.name: Guadalupe River Bridge Replacement Project
ceqa-77fecbf14265f14889.description: Caltrain approved reconstruction and extension of two rail bridges over the Guadalupe River in San Jose to address safety issues. The Guadalupe River channel is also approved to be widened. This project is known as the Guadalupe River Bridge Replacement Project (GRBR). In February 2025 JPB adopted an addendum to the MND (Addendum No. 1) to address an updated HMMP; changes in project duration and sequencing; revised limits for clearing and grubbing, grading, and erosion control; and some activities related to construction that could occur at night. In April 2026, JPB adopted an addendum to the MND (Addendum No. 2) to evaluate additional proposed changes to the Project that would include amendments to the applicable permits. These changes included constructing a new long-term site access on Willow Street, pruning in the floodplain areas starting in April, performing minor, low-impact tasks post-sunset; initiation of clearing and grubbing, and placement of access mats, temporary gravel for pipe support, and gravity diversion pipes, in the floodplain (away from the river) beginning on June 1. This addendum incorporates the habitat restoration project at Hicks Creek within the Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District Sierra Azul Open Space Preserve, herein referred to as the Hicks Creek Mitigation Project. The restoration project, which includes removing invasive plants, concrete structures, and other impediments, and replanting the area with native species, will provide off-site mitigation credit for the GRBR Project’s jurisdictional impacts. This third addendum to the GRBR Project MND (Addendum No. 3) evaluates the proposed changes to the Project to identify and address any new potential environmental impacts that were not evaluated by the 2021 MND and the first and second addendums prepared in February 2025 and April 2026 respectively, determine the severity or magnitude of any new or more severe environmental impacts, and determine whether the new or more severe environmental impacts of the July 2026 Modified Project changes would require substantial revisions to the MND. Under CEQA, once a negative declaration has been adopted for a project, no subsequent environmental impact report or negative declaration shall be prepared unless JPB, as the CEQA lead agency, determines that, based on substantial evidence, one of the qualifying criteria is met. Based upon the information provided in Addendum No. 3, the effects of the Hicks Creek Mitigation Project would not meet the qualifying criteria. As such, an addendum is appropriate, and Addendum No. 3 was prepared to address the environmental impacts of the Hicks Creek Mitigation Project (CEQA Guidelines §15164).

ceqa-89d8cff11fda04c678.name: Tree of Heaven Removal at South County Maintenance Yard
ceqa-89d8cff11fda04c678.projectTitle: Tree of Heaven Removal at South County Maintenance Yard
ceqa-89d8cff11fda04c678.description: The invasive tree of heaven is a growing management issue at the South County Yard. Left unmanaged, tree of heaven will damage the hardscape and buildings, so treatment is necessary before tree of heaven spreads throughout the facility, damages infrastructure, and spreads beyond Valley Water-owned lands. Several large trees grow along the southern fenceline, one large tree is in the middle of the parking area, and several suckers and saplings are scattered throughout the facility, growing in cracks in concrete and near buildings. Two herbicide-based approaches are proposed to remove these trees. Trees under about 6” DBH (diameter at breast height) would be treated with basal bark triclopyr. This is a treatment in which herbicide is painted or sprayed onto the lower 12-15” of the bark including the root crown using an oil-based herbicide. Trees greater than 6” DBH would be treated with hack-and-squirt treatment with concentrated imazapyr. This treatment involves using a small hatchet to make shallow cuts into the cambium around the trunk while leaving intact strips of bark so that conductive tissues can continue to push herbicide down into the root system. Removal efforts would start in August or September. A crew of 3-4 applicators would finish the initial treatment in half a day. Tree of heaven requires multiple years of sustained management efforts. About 30 days after the initial treatment, an inspection would determine whether follow-up treatment is needed that season. Two treatments per season for the first three years is typical, though stubborn trees may require additional treatments. Dead biomass (peeling bark, fungi, no nearby suckers) may be removed after a year of showing no signs of life.

ceqa-56a957f6c4c7c938be.name: Rengstorff Avenue Grade Separation Project
ceqa-56a957f6c4c7c938be.description: The Rengstorff Avenue Grade Separation Project spans a t-shaped area formed by Rengstorff Avenue and the Caltrain corridor. Along the Caltrain corridor and the adjacent Central expressway, the Project extends from a point north of Escuela Avenue to a point approximately adjacent to Ortega Avenue, and along Rengstorff Avenue the Project extends approximately 650 feet to the north and approximately 600 feet to the south of the rail corridor. Rengstorff Avenue is a critical north-south route between U.S. Highway 101 and El Camino Real that also serves as a gateway to the technology companies located near the bay to the north of the railroad tracks. The purpose of and need for the Project is to: (1) improve public safety by eliminating the existing at-grade railroad crossing at Rengstorff Avenue; and (2) improve traffic circulation and emergency response time, and to reduce queuing caused by the frequent rail traffic. The Project will involve lowering Rengstorff Avenue and its intersection with Central Expressway (County Route G6), which runs parallel to and north of the Caltrain tracks. The low point of Rengstorff Avenue under the railroad tracks will be approximately 22 feet below existing ground level. The Project will reconstruct and slightly realign the two existing Caltrain tracks by approximately five feet to the south, but the two tracks will remain at their current elevation. A 120-foot-long rail bridge will be constructed to carry the tracks over the lowered Rengstorff Avenue. The existing Leland Avenue and Crisanto Avenue intersections with Rengstorff Avenue, on the south side of the Caltrain train tracks, will be closed due to the proposed lowering of Rengstorff Avenue. A connector roadway will be constructed to maintain access between Rengstorff Avenue and Leland Avenue immediately south of its current location. The Leland Avenue connector roadway will be located along west side of Rengstorff Avenue and connect with Rengstorff Avenue approximately 270 feet south of the existing intersection. A new parking lot will be provided along the Leland Avenue connector roadway to provide 1:1 replacement of existing parking at the La Plaza Market parking lot that is impacted by the project. Crisanto Avenue will be terminated with a cul-de-sac east of Rengstorff Avenue. A new pedestrian overcrossing will be constructed across the lowered Rengstorff Avenue at Crisanto Avenue to maintain east/west pedestrian/bicycle access between Crisanto Avenue and Leland Avenue that would otherwise cross the existing intersection. Stairs and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant ramps will connect the pedestrian overcrossing with Rengstorff Avenue. Rengstorff Avenue will include cycle tracks and a landscaped buffer between the roadway and flanking sidewalks. Designated bike lanes would be added to Central Expressway approaching the Rengstorff Avenue intersection. The Project will include several retaining walls and landscaped terraces to provide support for excavation along the lowered portion of roadways.
ceqa-56a957f6c4c7c938be.crossStreets: Caltrain corridor and Central Expressway; Rengstorff Avenue

ceqa-1ab02af618f9610608.name: Geotechnical Testing for the Monterey Road Wildlife Crossing Geotechnical Borings
ceqa-1ab02af618f9610608.projectTitle: Geotechnical Testing for the Monterey Road Wildlife Crossing Geotechnical Borings
ceqa-1ab02af618f9610608.description: The proposed location for the Monterey Road Wildlife Crossing is in an area with substantial changes in materials and topography. The proposed wildlife crossing is located at the base of Tulare Hill at the confluence of Fisher Creek and Coyote Creek. Rock is shallow below the hill and can be seen outcropping on the hillside and along cuts for Monterey Road and the Union Pacific Railroad. The valley bottoms are composed of alluvium and borings made in the valley indicate a deep alluvial profile overlying rock. The cuts and fills made for construction of Monterey Road and the Union Pacific Railroad further complicate the distribution of materials at the site. Geotechnical borings are necessary to understand these properties and extents of these materials to evaluate potential alternatives, identify potential hazards, and to provide design recommendations.

ceqa-b7634ad639d63254cd.description: The 5.55-acre project site is located at 3521-3591 Homestead Road in Santa Clara (Assessor’s Parcel Numbers [APNs] 290-23-053 and -049). The project site is bounded by Lochinvar Avenue to the north, commercial development to the east, Homestead Road to the south, and Lawrence Expressway to the west. The project site is currently developed with three one-story commercial buildings and surface parking lots. The western site parcel (APN 290-23-053) has a 3,366 square foot building and a 24,221 square foot building occupied by various commercial uses. The eastern site parcel (APN 290-23-049) has a 43,971 square foot building occupied by a supermarket. As proposed, the project would demolish all structures and site improvements on-site and construct 57 three-story townhomes and 90 four-story townhomes across 14 buildings with a density of 27.3 dwelling units per acre (du/ac). The project would designate 23 of the residences as below market rate (affordable) units. The buildings would range in height from 36 to 51 feet. Additionally, the proposed project would include a 5,000 square foot standalone single story commercial space on the south side of the project site. The layout of the project site is shown on Figure 3.2-1. The proposed project is currently designated Neighborhood Mixed Use in the General Plan and zoned MU-NC. The Neighborhood Mixed Use designation is intended for pedestrian-oriented development focuses on ground floor retail and residences above this. The designation requires a residential density between 20-36 units per acre and a minimum floor area ratio (FAR) of 0.1. The zoning designation is consistent with this land use description. No General Plan Amendment is proposed for the project. The proposed project is submitting a density bonus application pursuant to SB330 and the applicant is requesting waivers and design concessions for the height of buildings on-site, which exceed the maximum height limitation. Access to the site is currently provided by two driveways on Homestead Road, one driveway on Lawrence Expressway, and two driveways on Lochinvar Avenue. Access driveways would be reduced to two driveways under the proposed project. One driveway would be located on the north side of the site from Lochinvar Avenue, and the other driveway would be located on the south side of the site accessible from Homestead Road. Both, 26 foot wide, full-access driveways would be in the same position as two of the existing driveways. Each unit would have a garage with two parking spaces accessible by an interior driving aisle and 47 guest parking spaces would be available in surface parking throughout the project site. In total, approximately 341 parking spaces would be available on-site.

ceqa-877acb7cd151b5e866.name: San Pedro Ponds Pipeline Installation Project

ceqa-877acb7cd151b5e866.description: The San Pedro Ponds are used to percolate imported Central Valley Project water from San Luis Reservoir into the Llagas Groundwater Subbasin. The San Pedro Ponds are part of the Upper Llagas Recharge System, which includes in-stream recharge along Llagas Creek and the Madrone Channel. The project would underground the existing 2,200 linear feet of 12-inch-diameter HDPE pipe, connect the San Pedro Ponds to the Madrone Channel by installing approximately 450 linear feet of new 12-inch-diameter HDPE pipeline and connecting it to an existing storm drain manhole, and install new energy dissipation vaults and 8-foot-wide by 8-foot-long rock slope protection outfall structures at Ponds 3 and 7 to protect the pond slopes from erosion. The project is needed to maximize groundwater recharge at the San Pedro Ponds, provide a new storm drain connection between the San Pedro Ponds and Madrone Channel, and protect Ponds 3 and 7 from bank erosion at the outfall structures.

ceqa-939c239a6bcde1ec78.description: The proposed trails would be constructed on an existing 47-acre property and would connect to the existing trail systems of Santa Teresa County Park and Calero County Park. The project involves the construction of a new recreational multi-use trail connection between two Santa Clara County parks for use by hikers, bikers, and equestrians and additional parking lots. The proposed project would include a main trail with connected seasonal trails that would provide visitors with access to rest areas, a vista point, and picnic areas. Two steel truss bridges (up to 55 feet long) with concrete headwalls would be installed along the main multi-use trail where it would cross over Santa Teresa Creek and Arroyo Calero. Trail user access to the trail alignment would be available at the two primary trailhead entry points on the northern and southern end of the project site. A new parking area is proposed directly east of the existing Rancho San Vicente Parking area to the south of McKean Road. A new parking area is proposed along San Vicente Avenue adjacent to the northern trailhead to replace existing, unimproved roadside parking. A signalized crossing would be installed at the intersection of Fortini Road and McKean Road. A raised multi-use crossing would be installed across San Vicente Avenue to allow trail users to cross between Santa Teresa County Park and the proposed project. Existing barbed wire fencing along the project site perimeter would remain in place or would be replaced with wildlife-friendly fencing. Existing fencing within the interior of the project site would be removed.

ceqa-336fec4fcdfb78688e.projectTitle: Housing Incentive Program Expansion and 788 San Antonio Road Mixed-Use Project
ceqa-336fec4fcdfb78688e.description: The project would involve demolition of the existing structures and paving on the site and merging two parcels for the construction of an eight-story, 228-unit building consisting of five stories of rental apartments above one story of rental apartments and garage and two stories of garage and amenity spaces (total of eight stories). The Project is Proposed in Accordance with California Government Code Section 65589.5(d)(5) “Builders Remedy". The project would also include a south-facing courtyard and a roof deck area. The project would include a mix of studio units (19), one-bedroom units (121), two-bedroom units (63), and three-bedroom units (25). Thirteen percent of the base units, or 30 units, would be provided as below market rate units. Vehicular access would be provided from both San Antonio Road and Leghorn Street. In accordance with CEQA, the City of Palo Alto prepared a Consistency Evaluation demonstrating that the prior environmental analysis in the original EIR certified in 2020 adequately addresses the potential environmental effects of the project, and the project does not require subsequent environmental review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15162, and supports the City's finding that the project would not result in significant newissues nor exceed the level of impacts identified in the previously certified 2020 EIR requiring additional analysis under CEQA.
ceqa-336fec4fcdfb78688e.crossStreets: San Antonio Road and Leghorn Street

ceqa-40cb25e71f7e75cf53.name: Icon/Echo Mixed Use Project
ceqa-40cb25e71f7e75cf53.description: The project is a Site Development Permit to allow the construction of a mixed-use project consisting of two eight-story buildings with up to 665 multifamily residential units and approximately 1,320 square feet of commercial space on an approximately 2.11-gross-acre site. The project includes the demolition of all existing buildings on-site, totaling approximately 22,527 square feet, and the removal of 29 trees (9 ordinance-size, 20 non-ordinance-size). This project includes extended construction hours from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm Monday through Saturday.

ceqa-4d92ce7431c0bd227a.name: Pacheco Microwave Refresh Project
ceqa-4d92ce7431c0bd227a.description: Valley Water proposes to install communications equipment and associated supporting features that would involve minor alterations to the interior and exterior of existing structures and facilities used to provide public water supply services. Deteriorated mechanical equipment that was not damaged from an environmental hazard also would be rehabilitated to meet current standards of public health and safety.

ceqa-f9aa7d49a76bc66bb2.name: H25-040, T25-024, and ER25-226: 1425 Cherry Avenue Residential Project
ceqa-f9aa7d49a76bc66bb2.projectTitle: H25-040, T25-024, and ER25-226: 1425 Cherry Avenue Residential Project
ceqa-f9aa7d49a76bc66bb2.description: Site Development Permit to allow the construction of two single-family houses and a fourplex through the demolition of one existing triplex, an additional dwelling unit, and multiple accessory structures (three sheds and a carport) and the removal of six ordinance-size trees on an approximately 0.33-gross-acre site.

ceqa-4ef172b046ab74c866.name: Issuance of Authority to Construct for Eighty-Four Emergency Backup Natural Gas Engine Generators, Sources S-7 through S-90. (Air District Application 704043).
ceqa-4ef172b046ab74c866.description: The Bay Area Air Quality Management District (Air District) has issued an Authority to Construct to Microsoft for eighty-four (84) backup natural gas engine generators, each abated by a 3-way catalyst system, at the San Jose Data Center. The Data Center would consist of two single-story buildings. The northern building is approximately 244,676 square feet in size, and the southern building is approximately 152,283 square feet, for a total of approximately 396,914 square feet. The maximum total data center electricity demand at full load would not exceed 99 MW. A total of 224 natural gas generators are proposed to provide backup power for the two data center buildings' servers. Two diesel-fired generators are also proposed to provide emergency power for life safety systems of the buildings. In addition, two diesel fire pumps will be used for fire suppression and are located next to a water storage tank at the northwestern area of the Data Center site. The Air District has already issued Authority to Constructs for 140 natural gas backup generators, two diesel-fired backup generators, and two diesel fire pumps at the San Jose Data Center. This Authority to Construct authorizes Microsoft to install the remaining eighty-four natural gas backup engine generators. The facility is permitted to operate these backup engines for emergency purposes. In addition to emergency use, the generators will be operated up to 50 hours per year per engine for reliability-testing operation, and up to 459 hours per year per engine as part of the Pacific Gas & Electric Company's Base Interrupted Program. They will not be used for routine data center operations.

ceqa-a605cc08167cc09495.name: 14789 Oka Road Project
ceqa-a605cc08167cc09495.description: The proposed project would include the removal of the existing orchards, subdivision of the site into 18 residential lots, and development of 138 townhome units within 18 residential buildings. The townhomes would include 54 two-bedroom units with a tandem garage and 84 three-bedroom units with a two-car garage and a porch. An approximately 0.41-acre open space area with two stormwater bioretention basins, walkways, and a seating area would be located in the northeastern portion of the site. Primary site access would be provided by two new driveways off Oka Road. The proposed project shall also include the construction of a new sidewalk, planting strip, on-street parking, and a bike lane along the Oka Road frontage, consistent with the Jewish Community Center frontage to the south. The proposed project would require approval of a Condominium Vesting Tentative Map, and an Architecture and Site Plan Review. The applicant team has submitted a formal Senate Bill (SB) 330 application for the project site and the project is subject to Builder’s Remedy. Therefore, the proposed project does not require Town approval of a General Plan Amendment or Rezone. The approximately 6.71-acre project site, identified by APNs 424-08-035 and -074, is currently developed with orchards planted throughout. Los Gatos Creek and its associated levee and riparian corridor are located west of the project site and State Route (SR) 17 is located to the east beyond existing agricultural land. Surrounding land uses include a mobile home community to the north; agricultural land and a single-family residence to the east; the Los Gatos Swim and Racquet Club to the northeast, across Oka Road; the Addison-Penzak Jewish Community Center of Silicon Valley and associated preschool, as well as apartments, to the south; and Los Gatos Creek Trail and multi-family residences to the west beyond Los Gatos Creek. The project site’s land use designations are Public and Low Density Residential (LDR) pursuant to the Town of Los Gatos 2020 General Plan and is zoned Residential, 8,000 square foot (sf) minimum lot area (R-1:8) and R-1:8: Housing Element Overlay (HEOZ).

ceqa-a5414eeee7f1843883.name: Lantz Drive Special Permit
ceqa-a5414eeee7f1843883.description: The subject property (APN: 712-28-040) is located in Coyote Valley, south of San Jose and north of Morgan Hill, on Lantz Drive between Scheller Avenue and Palm Avenue. The property is located in an area of residential uses, with single family residences on its north, south, and western sides, and agricultural lands located to its east. The subject property is approximately 2.37 acres, as are the neighboring residential properties. The property has a General Plan designation of Agriculture Large Scale, with a zoning of Agriculture with a 40-acre minimum lot size, in the coyote valley climate resilience combining district (A-40ac-cv). The project is located within the coyote valley climate resilience area, a resource of statewide significance, and is subject to the coyote valley climate resilience combining district (“-cv”) provisions in the County Zoning Ordinance which limits lot coverage development (building footprints) to 7,500 square feet for non-agricultural uses, and overall development areas (building footprints plus additional site improvements such as driveways and utilities) to 1 acre for non-agricultural uses and 2 acres for agricultural uses. The remainder of a property in the -cv district is to be used for on-site agriculture, meaning at least three out of every five-year period, either: (a) no less than six acres under cultivation, (b) no less than sixty percent of the parcel under cultivation, or (c) no less than twenty-four acres dedicated to raising livestock. The use on the property is residential with one primary dwelling unit. Single-family residences are a “byright” use in the agricultural zoning district, and no land use entitlements are required. The subject property obtained building site approval through a recorded subdivision tract map. The project proposes to legalize existing unpermitted 499 square foot pool house with three plumbing fixtures which is subject to Special Permit (§ 4.20.020(I)(2)). The total development area is approximately 0.85 acres and occupied by buildings, accessory structures, and associated improvements as delineated on the proposed site plan. Refer to Figure 2 for a Site Plan. The footprint of all buildings and structures over 30 inches in height is 4,047 square foot and is in conformance with the “-cv” provisions cited above. No grading or tree removal is proposed for the project.
ceqa-a5414eeee7f1843883.crossStreets: Lantz Drive between Scheller Avenue and Palm Avenue

ceqa-930fef66d87e303b18.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Lumileds, San Jose, California
ceqa-930fef66d87e303b18.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Lumileds, San Jose, California
ceqa-930fef66d87e303b18.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-930fef66d87e303b18.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to the Lumileds, (EPA ID# CAR000058081) to treat hazardous wastes through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, one (1) 1-liter container of 1,4 Dioxane, one (1) 1-liter container of Tert-Amyl Methyl Ether, one (1) 0.5 -liter container of Tert-Butyl Methyl Ether, one (1) 0.1-liter container of 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, and one (1) 0.1-liter container of 1,2 Dimethoxyethane must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at Lumileds located at 370 W. Trimble Road, San Jose, CA 95131. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued to chemically stabilize the hazardous wastes prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site by Clean Harbors Environmental Services (Clean Harbors). Background: The containers have peroxide formation present on either the inside, outside, or the bottom of the chemicals’ containers, as well as the thread container caps. The presence of peroxide formation may be unstable at relatively low concentrations, resulting in fire and/or explosion if improperly handled. Due to the presence of peroxide formation, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilization is recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Project Activities: The treatment of these hazardous wastes involves the addition of solutions to the containers in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemicals. Treatment will take place within a designated exclusion zone. Only technicians from Clean Harbors will be allowed in the exclusion zone. Movement, preparation, and treatment of the containers will be in accordance with established standards. Within 10 business days of the expiration of this permit, Lumileds will submit a final report, signed in accordance with Title 22, CCR Sec. 66270.11(d). The report shall include certification that the treatment area has been cleared of all residual hazardous waste generated from this emergency treatment and all generated waste has been properly managed. The Emergency Permit is effective beginning August 24, 2026 and shall expire on October 24, 2026.

ceqa-24000e0fc14c486eaf.name: I-680 Cold Plane AC Pavement and Place RHMA-G (EA 04-4X930)
ceqa-24000e0fc14c486eaf.projectTitle: I-680 Cold Plane AC Pavement and Place RHMA-G (EA 04-4X930)
ceqa-24000e0fc14c486eaf.description: Caltrans proposes cold plane of asphalt concrete (AC) pavement and placement of rubberized hot mix asphalt (RHMA) Type G on Interstate (I-) 680 in Santa Clara County from post mile (PM) M0.0 to M1.6. The project is located on I-680 from the 280-680/101 Separation to 0.1 mile south of the Alum Rock Avenue overcrossing. Construction equipment may include, but not be limited to, AC trucks, grinders, loaders, pavers, rollers, and portable compactors. Any removed pavement delineation and striping will be replaced. All work is limited to the paved roadway prism within Caltrans right of way (ROW).

ceqa-20ec567c3ffd0dfd1b.name: Curtner Avenue Sanitary Sewer Extension
ceqa-20ec567c3ffd0dfd1b.description: 434 linear foot extension of 8-inch diameter sewer and modification of the sewer lateral serving 1240 Curtner Avenue to connect to the extended sewer.

ceqa-684cdf95d27d2affb2.name: North Bound Capitol Expressway at 3974 Seven Trees Blvd. Soundwall Repairs
ceqa-684cdf95d27d2affb2.projectTitle: North Bound Capitol Expressway at 3974 Seven Trees Blvd. Soundwall Repairs
ceqa-684cdf95d27d2affb2.description: The work shall consist of replacing several sound-walls and sound-wall columns.

ceqa-9f3399263725115ade.name: De Anza College 2021-2026 Facilities Master Plan and Measure G Master Projects List
ceqa-9f3399263725115ade.projectTitle: De Anza College 2021-2026 Facilities Master Plan and Measure G Master Projects List
ceqa-9f3399263725115ade.description: The 2021-2026 Facilities Master Plan and Master Projects List serve as a guide for ongoing development and renovation of the 112-acre De Anza College campus. It includes construction of a new Creative Arts Building, either construction of a new Services for Students Building or renovations to existing spaces, various demolitions, renovations and replacements of multiple facilities, enhanced technology upgrades, updated utility infrastructure, and improved multi-modal circulation in and around campus. The maximum proposed demolition is 86,000 square feet and the maximum proposed new construction is 50,000 square feet.

ceqa-9f3399263725115ade.developmentType: Educational (Construction (50,000 sq ft) and Demolition (86,000 sq ft))

ceqa-89b1cadac6ce6ad31b.name: Wrong-Way Driver Prevention Measures Project (EA 04-4X750)
ceqa-89b1cadac6ce6ad31b.description: Caltrans proposes installing wrong-way driver prevention measures at 30 locations in San Francisco and Santa Clara Counties. The project is located at various locations on I-80 and I-280 in San Francisco County and on SR-17, SR-87, US-101, and I-880 in Santa Clara County. Work includes measures such as red enhanced reflective pavement markers, Type V arrow upgrades, chevron markings, wrong-way signs, one-way signs, limit lines, and high visibility crosswalk ladders. All work shall be limited to the paved roadway prism within Caltrans right of way.

ceqa-4b9bc0fc94c8a17a76.name: 1250 Oakmead Parkway
ceqa-4b9bc0fc94c8a17a76.description: The proposed project is being pursued under the “Builder’s Remedy” provisions of the Housing Accountability Act Government Code Section 65589.5(d)(5), which allows for housing development projects that do not comply with a site’s General Plan land use designation or zoning requirements when a jurisdiction’s Housing Element is noncompliant with state law at the time the project’s Senate Bill (SB) 330 preliminary application is filed. As such, no General Plan amendment or rezoning is required for the project. The project also qualifies for protections under SB 330, which was adopted to increase residential unit development, protect existing housing inventory, and expedite permit processing timelines. The project would demolish the existing office building, associated surface parking, and on-site landscaping, and construct a residential development consisting of 318 residential units including (20 percent) 64 deed-restricted affordable units. The project would construct a total of 17 townhouse buildings providing a total of 103 townhouse units on the western portion of the site. All 17 townhouse buildings would be three stories tall with a maximum height of 42 feet. The project would also construct a five-story, multi-family residential building on the eastern portion of the site that would include an attached, five-story parking structure for residents. The multi-family residential building would contain a total of 215 units situated around a central courtyard. The multi-family residential building and parking structure would have a maximum building height of 60 feet and a total area of approximately 389,039 square feet. The project would also include site access, utility and right of way, and landscaping improvements. The proposed buildings would achieve LEED Silver certification by incorporating green building measures.
ceqa-4b9bc0fc94c8a17a76.action: Land Division (Subdivision, etc.), Site Plan, Use Permit

ceqa-c0027af89f933e78ef.name: Baylands Trail Replenishment Project
ceqa-c0027af89f933e78ef.description: The proposed Palo Alto Baylands Trail Replenishment Project entails the replenishment and repair of the surface of the trail leading from the parking lot east of Embarcadero Road west to the Lucy Evans Baylands Interpretive Nature Center. The project is located within the Baylands Nature Preserve, a 1,940-acre open space tract of marshland that is owned by the City of Palo Alto (City). The project site includes: a portion of the San Francisquito Creek Trail, a gravel parking lot that would serve as a staging area, and a portion of Embarcadero Road. The raised trail connecting Embarcadero Road to Baylands Interpretive Nature Center is prone to flooding due to seasonal inundation and weather impacts. The project would add four 4-inch layers of aggregate totaling at least 12-inches to the existing 12.5-foot-wide trail. The additional layers will result in about a 9-foot path width along the top of the trail. The additional aggregate will extend from the far side of the access path to the Nature Center to the western edge of the road pavement of Embarcadero Road, roughly 250 feet.

ceqa-3792ad91178d431dc7.name: 3240 Scott Boulevard Residential
ceqa-3792ad91178d431dc7.description: The project would demolish the existing office building to construct an eight-story, 225-unit, multi-family residential development. The eight-story residential building would reach a maximum height of 95 feet and would have a Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of 2.61. Of the 225 units, 34 units (or approximately 15 percent) would be provided at various levels of affordability. In addition to the residential units, the project would include an eight-story parking tower, pedestrian trail, two ground level courtyards, rooftop deck, clubhouse, pool, and gym. The project also includes site access, utility, and right-of-way improvements. Since residential uses are not permitted under the current General Plan and zoning designation for the site, the project would require a General Plan Amendment from Low Intensity Office/R&D to Very High Density Residential, and a rezone from Light Industrial (LI) to Very High Density Residential (R-5).
ceqa-3792ad91178d431dc7.action: General Plan Amendment, Rezone, Site Plan

ceqa-65a5d63b23170dc911.name: Tularcitos Creek Downstream North Hillview Drive Levee Repair
ceqa-65a5d63b23170dc911.projectTitle: Tularcitos Creek Downstream North Hillview Drive Levee Repair
ceqa-65a5d63b23170dc911.description: The Tularcitos Creek Downstream North Hillview Drive Levee Repair Project is intended to address damage to the west bank levee caused by rodent burrowing and associated erosion and to protect property and public safety by reducing the risk of continued erosion. The project would repair approximately 2,932 LF of the existing levee, and the total area of temporary disturbance would be approximately 2.7 acres. The west bank levee would be reconstructed using SMP-2 Method 1A, which involves installation of a buried rock structure (rock buttress) to protect against erosion scour, stabilize the channel embankment, and provide a stable foundation for the repair, which is currently compromised by saturated soils.
ceqa-65a5d63b23170dc911.crossStreets: North Hillview Drive and Paseo Refugio

ceqa-f4cd90c972a73d95a2.name: Sinkhole Repair- 1V670/0427000013
ceqa-f4cd90c972a73d95a2.description: Repair a sinkhole in Santa Clara County. On July 18, 2026, the Field Maintenance Team discovered a sinkhole in the number 2 lane of State Route 82 at Post Mile 17.9 in Santa Clara County.

ceqa-662a9a7c2fe993ed3c.name: Athletic Fields Turf Replacement
ceqa-662a9a7c2fe993ed3c.description: Foothill-De Anza Community College District will replace the artificial turf systems on four athletic fields at Foothill College and two athletic fields at De Anza College. The project includes removal and replacement of the existing artificial turf and infill; inspection and localized repair the existing shock pad, aggregate base, and drainage system, where necessary, to restore the existing field to its intended function; and installation of new synthetic turf, infill, and field markings. The project would occur entirely within the existing athletic field footprints and would not expand the existing use or capacity of the facilities.
ceqa-662a9a7c2fe993ed3c.crossStreets: Perimeter Road and El Monte Road; Campus Drive and S Sterling Road

ceqa-7a3258026d78fccd89.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Cepheid, Sunnyvale, California

ceqa-7a3258026d78fccd89.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to Cepheid, (EPA ID# CAR000235697) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, one (1) 500-milliliter (mL) container and one (1) 100 mL container of Tetrahydrofuran; two (2) 1-liter containers of Diethylene Glycol Butyl Ether; one (1) 1-liter container of Dipropylene Glycol Butyl Ether; one (1) 1-liter container of Propylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether Acetate; and one (1) 25-mL container of Acrylonitrile must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Background: The containers have peroxide formation present on either the inside, outside, or the bottom of the chemicals’ containers, as well as the thread container caps. The presence of peroxide formation may be unstable at relatively low concentrations, resulting in fire and/or explosion if improperly handled. Due to the presence of peroxide formation, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilization is recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Project Activities: The treatment of this hazardous waste involves the addition of a solution in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemical. ceqa-55cd1a92dc63fb985b.name: Single-family residence, Barn, Stables, ADU and JADU
ceqa-55cd1a92dc63fb985b.projectTitle: Single-family residence, Barn, Stables, ADU and JADU
ceqa-55cd1a92dc63fb985b.description: Construction of a new 11,875 sq. ft. single-family residence, an 8,600 square foot barn, 5,882 stables, 1,200 square foot ADU and a 499 square foot JADU with 200 square foot attached garage. Proposed grading includes 3,229 cubic yards of cut, 2,984 cubic yards of fill, maximum cut and fill height of 6 feet. Building Site Approval, Grading Approval and Design Review (Tier II) for a new 11,875 sq. ft. single-family residence, an 8,600 square foot barn, 5,882 stables, 1,200 square foot ADU and a 499 square foot JADU with 200 square foot attached garage. Proposed grading includes 3,229 cubic yards of cut, 2,984 cubic yards of fill, maximum cut and fill height of 6 feet for a new driveway, bio-retention pond and associated site grading. The subject property is zoned to allow single-family residences by right. The project is a covered project under the Santa Clara Valley Habitat Plan (HCP).
ceqa-55cd1a92dc63fb985b.crossStreets: Shillingsburg Avenue and San Vincente Avenue

ceqa-0fccc97e76704a3ce2.name: West Santa Clara Landscape Resiliency Project, California Vegetation Treatment Program (CalVTP)
ceqa-0fccc97e76704a3ce2.description: Located along the western boundary of Santa Clara County, the West Santa Clara Landscape Resiliency Project (WSCLRP) covers approximately 143,375 acres, from the wildland-urban interface (WUI) of the Santa Clara Valley and southern Bay Area west into the Santa Cruz Mountains. The proposed treatment types are ecological restoration, WUI fuel reduction treatments, and fuel breaks, and the proposed treatment activities are prescribed burning, manual treatments, mechanical treatments, targeted herbicide application, and prescribed herbivory. Treatment types and activities are consistent with those evaluated in the CalVTP Program EIR. Treatments would be phased and maintained over time based on availability of funding, resources, community outreach opportunities, and partner collaboration. This project serves to facilitate future landscape-scale wildfire resilience treatments across a variety of settings and land ownership types (e.g., landscape-scale treatments on public land in primarily wildland conditions, small-scale treatments conducted adjacent to urban homes that combine vegetation management efforts with defensible space treatments). This work aims to mitigate wildfire risk, increasing community and ecological wildfire resiliency and enhancing biological diversity. A Project-Specific Analysis and Addendum (PSA/Addendum) has been prepared for the project as a later activity covered by the California Vegetation Treatment Project (CalVTP) Program Environmental Impact Report (EIR). The proposed treatment types and the treatment activities are consistent with those evaluated in the CalVTP Program EIR. The attached material includes a Notice of Determination that the proposed project is within the scope of the CalVTP PEIR.

ceqa-c49d278625a45ab06f.name: 1030-1038 McKendrie Street Residential Project
ceqa-c49d278625a45ab06f.description: The proposed Project would include merging two parcels at 1030 and 1038 McKendrie Street, demolishing the existing surface parking lot and development, and constructing two new multi-family buildings containing 12 townhome-style units. Each townhome unit would be three stories with an attached garage on the ground floor. The Project would include a single 26-foot-wide driveway that provides ingress/egress to the site from McKendrie Street. An internal circulation road, which would be a private road, would provide access to each of the townhome garages. Six visitor parking spaces would be provided on the internal circulation road. The Project would also include a General Plan Amendment to change the land use designation to Mixed Use Neighborhood.

ceqa-663bb6dfce35e209bd.name: Lakeside Reserve Pond 6 Desedimentation and Restoration Project
ceqa-663bb6dfce35e209bd.projectTitle: Lakeside Reserve Pond 6 Desedimentation and Restoration Project
ceqa-663bb6dfce35e209bd.description: The Santa Clara Valley Habitat Agency will implement restoration and repair of an existing cattle stock pond (Pond 6). Pond 6 historically provided water for cattle grazing and aquatic breeding habitat for native amphibians. Over time, structural failure and sedimentation have reduced pond depth, hydroperiod, and habitat quality. The project restores ecological functions of the pond through excavation and berm repair. Project activities include: • Removal of approximately 100 cubic yards of accumulated sediment • Stabilization and repair of pond berm and spillway • Limited recontouring within existing pond basins to create a mix of deep pool and shallow margin habitat
ceqa-663bb6dfce35e209bd.crossStreets: Uvas Rd and Oak Glen Ave

ceqa-2133bf85f00baa4818.name: Ax Sherwood Avenue Residential Project
ceqa-2133bf85f00baa4818.description: The project would demolish the existing commercial building and single-family residences on-site and redevelop the site with seven buildings containing a total of 33 townhouse units. The proposed townhouses would each be three stories with a private garage. The townhouse buildings would have a maximum height of 36.5 feet. The project would utilize the State Density Bonus Law to request one concession related to the affordable unit bedroom mix and waivers from development standards for commercial floor area, setbacks, building step-backs and articulation, open space, ground-floor design, window recesses, entrance orientation and design, loading requirements, and pedestrian-scaled entrance features.

ceqa-7123c51507b6509e31.name: 349 1st Street Residential Project
ceqa-7123c51507b6509e31.description: The project would demolish the existing two-story commercial building and redevelop the site with a six-story, 19-unit residential condominium building with a maximum height of 84 feet, 11.5 inches. Four units (21 percent) would be provided as below market rate units for low-income households. The project would include a parking garage with at-grade parking and basement-level automated parking system, bicycle parking, rooftop terrace, utility improvements, and frontage improvements at the intersection of First and Whitney Streets. The project is proposed pursuant to the provisions of Government Code Section 65589(d)(5) known as the “Builder’s Remedy.”

ceqa-8d24dcd286deb8069a.name: West Valley College PE/Wellness Building
ceqa-8d24dcd286deb8069a.description: The District proposes to construct a new 99,000 square foot Wellness Facility including a new gym and other fitness and health facilities, and 44 parking spaces. The new building would be located on an existing track and field site. The project is intended to serve to address the facility needs identified in the Facilities Master Plan and provide the desired community and student recreational and wellness amenities.

ceqa-c58e95a0d6e4f33374.name: University Station Residential Project
ceqa-c58e95a0d6e4f33374.description: The project proposes to demolish the four existing office buildings (which total 216,000 square feet of office space) and two parking garages, and construct a new five-story building with up to 297 multi-family residential units and up to 111 three-story townhouse units distributed amongst 26 buildings. The multi-family residential building’s roof would include screened mechanical units, and the maximum height of the building would be approximately 64 feet above grade. The maximum height of the townhouse units would be approximately 38 feet. Thirteen of the townhouse units would be located on what is currently a 0.94-acre parcel in the City of San José (as discussed in further detail below) and the remaining townhouse units and the multi-family building would be on the parcel in the City of Santa Clara. The average density of the project would be 37 dwelling units per acre. The project would also construct a new approximately 8.5-foot-wide sidewalk along the project frontage adjacent to the proposed multi-family residential development on El Camino Real and along the project frontage on Campbell Avenue. As proposed, the project would annex the 0.94-acre San José parcel to the City of Santa Clara. If the detachment and annexation of the parcel are approved, the Santa Clara General Plan would be amended to designate the annexed parcel to Santa Clara Station Mixed Use (Santa Clara Station Regional Commercial and Santa Clara Station High Density Residential) and the annexed parcel would be rezoned to the Mixed Use-Regional Commercial (MU-RC) zoning district.

ceqa-a9aab2c6ee4d22ce0d.projectTitle: 2540 Greenstone Ct. & Capitol Expressway Soundwall Repairs
ceqa-a9aab2c6ee4d22ce0d.description: The work shall consist of replacement of one damaged soundwall panel and two new concrete columns.

ceqa-3f2a14691e3fce647b.name: Calero Valve Yard Geotechnical Borings and Utility Potholing
ceqa-3f2a14691e3fce647b.projectTitle: Calero Valve Yard Geotechnical Borings and Utility Potholing
ceqa-3f2a14691e3fce647b.description: The proposed project involves two components: 1) collecting geotechnical information to support the design for the construction of a sheet pile wall for flood protection around the Calero Valve Yard, and 2) potholing to locate existing underground utilities. Both the geotechnical and potholing activities are needed to inform the final design of the future Calero Dam Seismic Retrofit Project (CDSRP). The geotechnical activities would include drilling three borings utilizing a truck mounted drill rig via hollow stem augering methods and excavating an approximately 100-foot trench along the boring alignment. Borings would be drilled up to 25-feet deep and would be backfilled with cement bentonite grout mixture per Valley Water Well Ordinance Program standards. Potholing activities would involve excavating approximately four potholes utilizing a hydrovac truck along a portion of the Almaden Valley Pipeline near Calero Reservoir. The potholes are needed to establish the configuration of the pipeline’s concrete encasement to inform relocation of an existing valve vault box to occur as part of CDSRP. All excavated areas would be backfilled with native, excavated material and compacted. In total, approximately 1500 square feet of ruderal vegetation would be disturbed for the geotechnical and potholing activities. Overall, activities would take approximately six days to complete.

ceqa-6765aa92f93371ea18.description: The project is a Planned Development Permit to allow the construction of a new 6-story mixed-use building with 65 residential units and approximately 14,070 square feet of commercial and community amenity use, including office, workshop, and gallery space, one level of below-grade parking, and a Taiko performance building on an existing approximately 0.74-gross acre vacant site. ceqa-e4e179704e4a0bb95c.name: Sky Harbour Hangar Expansion Project
ceqa-e4e179704e4a0bb95c.projectTitle: PP18-103 Amendment to the Mineta San Jose International Airport Master Plan
ceqa-e4e179704e4a0bb95c.description: The project includes a Special Use Permit to expand the existing general aviation facilities on a 7.0-acre site within the San José Mineta International Airport. The expanded facilities would consist of a hangar addition comprising a new 28,000-square-foot aircraft hangar, 235-square-foot office space, and concrete ramp paving for aircraft parking. The existing hangar would be retained and undergo a hangar door relocation from the South to the East elevation. The hangar addition would be constructed directly to the south and would have a height of approximately 39 feet above ground level.

ceqa-6750b54a8b27834d78.name: 1320 N Diana Avenue Housing Project
ceqa-6750b54a8b27834d78.description: The project development area is approximately 13.75 acres and would include development of 86 housing units consisting of 68 single-family detached homes and 18 duet homes. Seven percent of the housing units are proposed to be designated as affordable to extremely low-income households, but the applicant has not provided information as to which unit types and units will be so designated. Two existing residences would remain, while one existing residence and associated structures, including greenhouses, sheds, and ancillary buildings, would be demolished. With the exception of a single residence at 1320 North Diana Avenue, which is proposed to be demolished, all structures on-site are less than 45 years of age. The project is being processed by the County pursuant to Senate Bill (SB) 330. The project would require site grading and installation of water, wastewater, storm drain, electrical, gas, and telecommunications infrastructure. Residential architecture would include Spanish, Traditional, Farmhouse, and Craftsman styles. Access would be provided from North Diana Avenue and connecting local streets within the surrounding neighborhood. Water service is proposed to be provided by a new public water system consisting of on-site groundwater production wells, water storage of approximately 43,500 gallons, and distribution infrastructure. Wastewater would be collected, treated, and disposed of onsite through a new wastewater treatment system. The water system and wastewater treatment system are proposed to be maintained privately for the development. Stormwater infrastructure would include drainage pipes, inlets, water quality treatment facilities, detention features, and related appurtenances. Landscaping would be incorporated along internal roadways, within residential areas, and adjacent to stormwater management facilities. Site preparation would include grading and removal of 31 trees. The project would be constructed in multiple phases over approximately two years.

Improvements include but is not limited to slope repairs, raising of levee height, repairing cracks and breaches, widening of access roads, relining/replacement of crossover pipes, and erosion control.

ceqa-7130946a2fbea259b8.name: Fountain Oaks Ranch
ceqa-7130946a2fbea259b8.description: Construct 175 single-family residential units and 44 duet (attached) residential units, totaling 219 residential units; along with utility infrastructure including water supply, wastewater treatment facilities with leach fields, and storm drainage systems. and circulation and parking on approximately 54.9 acres. Common area improvements would include a detention basin, neighborhood park, and landscaped open space parcels. All of the 44 duet units would be deed-restricted affordable housing for low-income households. The existing structures at 2215 Tennant Avenue would remain. The project would also dedicate right-of-way to the County along Tennant Avenue and Hill Road. The project would be constructed in a single phase over approximately 3 years. ceqa-3323305ead4894aa0b.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Dionex Corporation, Sunnyvale, California
ceqa-3323305ead4894aa0b.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, Dionex Corporation, Sunnyvale, California
ceqa-3323305ead4894aa0b.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-3323305ead4894aa0b.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to Dionex Corporation, (EPA ID# CAD05539487) to treat hazardous waste through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, one (1) 500-milliliter (mL) container of Butyl Vinyl Ether; one (1) 250-mL container of Ethyl Vinyl Ether; four (4) 500-mL containers and one (1) 100-mL container of Acrylic Acid; one (1) 100-mL container of Borane Tetrahydrofuran; one (1) 500-gram container of 2’,2’-Azobis(2,2-imidazolin-2-yl) propane dichloride; one (1) 500-gram container of 2’,2’-Azobis(2,2-imidazolin-2-yl) propane hydrochloride; one (1) 500-gram container of 2’,2’-Azobis(2,4-dimethyl-4-methoxyvaleronitrile); two (2) 500-gram containers of 2’,2’-Azobis(2-methylpropionile; four (4) 100-gram containers of 4’,4’-Azobis(4-cyanovoleric acid); and one (1) 500-gram container of Benzoyl Peroxide must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at Dionex Corporation located at 1228 Titan Way, Sunnyvale, California 94085. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued for to chemically stabilize the hazardous waste by Clean Harbors Environmental Services prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site. Background: The containers have peroxide formation present on either the inside, outside, or the bottom of the chemicals’ containers, as well as the thread container caps. The presence of peroxide formation may be unstable at relatively low concentrations, resulting in fire and/or explosion if improperly handled. Also temperature/shock-sensitive materials can decompose or detonate with external energy when dry or concentrated. If the material is improperly handled, there is a potential for a reaction, which includes fire, deflagration, or detonation. Due to the presence of peroxide formation and temperature/shock sensitive chemicals, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilization is recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Project Activities: The treatment of this hazardous waste involves the addition a solution in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemical. Treatment will take place within a designated exclusion zone. Only technicians from Clean Harbors Environmental Services will be allowed in the exclusion zone. Movement, preparation, and treatment of the containers will be in accordance with established standards. Within 10 business days of the expiration of this permit, Dionex Corporation will submit a final report, signed in accordance with Title 22, CCR Sec. 66270.11(d). The report shall include certification that the treatment area has been cleared of all residual hazardous waste generated from this emergency treatment and all generated waste has been properly managed. The Emergency Permit is effective beginning August 3, 2026 and shall expire on October 2, 2026.

ceqa-b9015268abee826cfd.name: 3155 El Camino Real Residential Project
ceqa-b9015268abee826cfd.description: Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program. Rezone from Thoroughfare Commercial (CT) to Planned Development (PD) to allow development of a 60 unit residential project and a Tentative Tract Map to create 60 for sale residential condominiums and a common lot to serve the development. Project involves demolition of three one story commercial pad buildings totaling 27,780 sq. ft. and surface parking lot. To support the project, the City of Santa Clara requires that the project applicant (Toll Brothers) remove a deteriorated roadway bridge on Valley Water fee title property that was installed in 1968 and does not meet current City codes. The project applicant would saw-cut the top of the roadway bridge and remove the center supporting column to remove the structure. The lower section, which forms a box culvert, would be left in place. Removal of the bridge was fully analyzed as part of the City’s IS/MND. Valley Water would issue an encroachment permit to the project applicant to remove the bridge from its fee title property.

ceqa-089402c7884b78e6d7.name: City of Morgan Hill - Glen Ayre Hillside Water Reservoir Project
ceqa-089402c7884b78e6d7.projectTitle: City of Morgan Hill - Glen Ayre Hillside Water Reservoir Project
ceqa-089402c7884b78e6d7.description: The project will upgrade the existing tank (35-feet in diameter) with a capacity of 100,000 gallons.
