ceqa-0d4c211299555fb100.name: Kennedy Meadows Roadside Fuels Reduction Project
ceqa-0d4c211299555fb100.projectTitle: Kennedy Meadows Roadside Fuels Reduction Project
ceqa-0d4c211299555fb100.description: The Project will reduce hazardous roadside vegetation along approximately 3 miles of Sherman Pass Road to improve life safety, roadside safety, ingress and egress for evacuation, and reduce the intensity and spread of wildland fire into the wildland-urban interface. Tulare County Fire Department Type II IA crews will physically remove and/or chip vegetation along the roadway right-of-way and adjacent properties. All work will be within the County Right-of-way and will extend no further than 80 feet from centerline of roadway, creating a 160-foot wide (including the road) reduction of fuel, where access is authorized. Sherman Pass Road is County maintained, is located within the State Responsibility Area, and portions of the project corridor extend through the Sequoia National Forest. The roadway is in a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone and serves as the primary ingress and egress route for approximately 200 habitable residential structures. The Project also includes public outreach intended to improve community wildfire safety and readiness.

ceqa-e1493ee9e14f520d25.name: Tulare County Behavioral Health Residential Campus Project
ceqa-e1493ee9e14f520d25.projectTitle: Tulare County Behavioral Health Residential Campus Project
ceqa-e1493ee9e14f520d25.description: The 2.72-acre site is the former Casa Grande Assisted Living Facility and contains two existing buildings, onsite parking, and an unimproved area. The County acquired the property in 2023 and proposes to renovate and repurpose the existing campus as the Tulare County Behavioral Health Residential Campus to provide inpatient/residential behavioral health and supportive services. In addition to renovation and reuse of the existing facilities, Building 2 would be expanded by approximately 4,480 square feet on the south end of the building. The preliminary plans identify Building 2 as approximately 24,360 square feet following the addition. The current action includes program funding, renovation/conversion, the Building 2 addition, and operation of the existing campus.

ceqa-34ba856dfe89ef2fe6.name: Upper Posey Roadside Fuels Reduction Project
ceqa-34ba856dfe89ef2fe6.projectTitle: Upper Posey Roadside Fuels Reduction Project
ceqa-34ba856dfe89ef2fe6.description: The Project will reduce hazardous roadside vegetation along approximately 3.9 miles of Mountain Road 3 (Old Stage Road) and Guhl Avenue. Tulare County Fire Department Type IIA crews will thin, prune/limb, chip, and remove hazardous fuels along existing roadway corridors. Hazard trees may be removed; within fuelreduction areas, trees less than 12 inches DBH may be removed, remaining trees may be limbed to approximately 6 feet, and approximately 70 percent of standing brush may be removed, with a target stem spacing of approximately 16 feet. All work will be within the County Right-of-way and will extend no further than 80 feet from centerline of roadway, creating a 160-foot wide (including the road) reduction of fuel. The Project will improve emergency access and evacuation, reduce wildfire intensity and spread, and help protect approximately 317 homes and 982 residents in a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone.

ceqa-05689519be90fea180.name: Woodville Elementary Pedestrian Improvements Project
ceqa-05689519be90fea180.description: The project consists of constructing ADA compliant curb ramps, sidewalks, curb and gutters and driveways adjacent to Woodville Elementary School in the community of Woodville.

ceqa-c02bcf84d08a084ef0.name: Bardsley Avenue Sidewalk Improvements
ceqa-c02bcf84d08a084ef0.description: The project addresses a safety concern regarding the discontinuous sidewalk section on the north side of Bardsley at Morrison St., on the east and west sides. The project will install an ADA-complaint sidewalk.

ceqa-4f57447d805015afac.name: Wiersma RV and Mini Storage (GPA 26-001 & PZC 25-011)
ceqa-4f57447d805015afac.projectTitle: Wiersma RV and Mini Storage (GPA 26-001 & PZC 25-011)
ceqa-4f57447d805015afac.description: The applicant proposes Zone Change No. PZC 25-011 to change the existing zoning for APNs: 073-140-045 & 047 from the Exclusive Agriculture – 40 Acre Minimum (AE-40) Zone to the Service Commercial with a Mixed Use Overlay Zone (C-3-MU). The Tulare County Resource Management Agency (RMA) proposes General Plan Amendment No. GPA 26-001 to amend Part II: Figure 2-1 of the Corridors Framework Plan of the Tulare County General Plan 2030 Update to change the segment of State Route 198 (SR-198) between Road 64 and the Kings/Tulare County Border (Road 44) from a Major Roadway to a Regional Growth Corridor. GPA 26-001 also proposes to change the land use designation from Valley Agriculture to Mixed Use. The property currently contains an existing 3.8 acre walnut dehydrator facility, an approximately 7.71 acre walnut orchard, and 5.69 acres of fallow land on the 17.20 acre property. Existing structures on the property include a 30 foot by 40 foot tool storage shop addition; a 40 foot by 120 foot open cover with 20 foot by 40 foot enclosed for storage; a 30 foot by 66 foot shade cover to existing shade for ag equipment; a polyethylene gas line to supply natural gas to (3) nut dryers, piping, electrical and anchoring equipment; a 35 foot wide commercial asphalt concrete drive approach to Tulare County Improvement Standards, Plate A-17 and A-17C, starting 17 feet west of the center line of Road 52 and 519 feet north of the center line of SR-198; a 30 foot by 60 foot shade addition to existing shade cover for Walnut Dehydrator Facility; and a 1,200 square foot metal storage building. The purpose of the application would be to facilitate the establishment of a 3.6 acre RV Storage Facility with 160 spaces, a 440 Square Foot Office/2,087 Square Foot Residence with a 1,002 Square Foot Garage, and a 9.6 acre Future Mini-Storage Facility because there is no longer water to farm the 17.20 acre property. The existing walnut dehydrator would continue to operate. The new facilities would be added to the existing walnut dehydrator facility, which would continue to operate. However, the 7.71 acre walnut orchard that is on the property will be removed due to the lack of water to continue farming the property. The property doesn’t have access to surface water. The proposed facility will operate every day from 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. It will be fully fenced and gated to ensure security. Additionally, an office and residence will be located on-site to provide oversight and maintenance, though there will be no full-time employees. A designated retention basin will be utilized for rainwater runoff, complying with local environmental requirements. Access to the site would be from Road 52. The applicants believe that the proposed facility will serve the growing storage needs of the community while aligning with Tulare County’s zoning and development standards. The applicants have stated that they are prepared to comply with all necessary permits and regulations to ensure a seamless approval process.
ceqa-4f57447d805015afac.developmentType: Commercial (RV & Mini Storage with onsite manager residence & rental office)(Sq. Ft. 122530, Acres 17.2, Employees 2)

ceqa-1236e4b6f8f1685640.name: Extension of Uncodified Urgency Interim Ordinance No. 3669 - Temporary Moratorium on New Data Center Development
ceqa-1236e4b6f8f1685640.projectTitle: Extension of Uncodified Urgency Interim Ordinance No. 3669 - Temporary Moratorium on New Data Center Development
ceqa-1236e4b6f8f1685640.description: The County of Tulare is extending Uncodified Urgency Interim Ordinance No. 3669, which establishes a temporary moratorium on new data center development in the unincorporated areas of Tulare County. The extension will continue the moratorium for an additional ten (10) months and fifteen (15) days, through August 6, 2027. During the moratorium, the County will continue to evaluate data center development and develop comprehensive land use regulations addressing potential impacts and appropriate development standards, including zoning requirements, infrastructure needs, environmental considerations, public safety, water and energy considerations, noise, and land use compatibility. The purpose of the moratorium extension is to allow sufficient time for the County to complete this evaluation and develop appropriate permanent zoning and development regulations governing new data center development. The residents and communities of unincorporated Tulare County, as well as the County generally, will benefit from the additional time to evaluate and establish appropriate land use regulations for future data center development.

ceqa-c2de5d7e0585a1a57a.name: Deer Creek Stream Gauge Vegetation Removal
ceqa-c2de5d7e0585a1a57a.projectTitle: Deer Creek Stream Gauge Vegetation Removal
ceqa-c2de5d7e0585a1a57a.description: Hand tools and a weed eater will be used to remove vegetation within the dry channel, from the levee road to the current waterline, and 10 feet upstream and downstream of the station. If the parcel of record to be divided is greater in size than is required in the zone district in which it is located, a maximum of one (1) homesite parcel shall be permitted The proposed project would authorize one additional residence for the property owners and/or their family and would not authorize expansion of agricultural operations, or any other use unless separately reviewed and approved by the County.

ceqa-4137c8f16c94a6527c.description: The applicant proposes the establishment and operation of a contractor storage yard to support an off-site landscaping business. Development of the site includes construction of a 3,600-square-foot metal shop building, installation of an on-site wastewater treatment/septic system, and graveled access road. The contractor storage yard would accommodate parking and storage of up to twelve pickup trucks, twelve cargo or flatbed trailers, lawn maintenance equipment and mowers, employee parking, and associated site access and circulation improvements necessary for daily operations. An Initial Study (IS) was prepared by the Environmental Planning Division of the Resource Management Agency (RMA) for PSP 26-013, identifying potentially significant environmental effects associated with the project. A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) were subsequently prepared, concluding that although the project may have the potential to significantly affect the environment, the incorporation of mitigation measures would reduce all impacts to levels where no significant effect would occur, and no substantial evidence exists indicating that the revised project would result in significant impacts. The MND (SCH #2026080007) describes these mitigation measures and explains how they reduce potential effects to lessthan- significant levels, as supported by the environmental checklist prepared pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Based on the analysis in the Initial Study and accompanying technical documentation, all potential impacts—including Biological Resources; Cultural, Tribal, and Paleontological Resources; Geology and Soils; and Noise—were determined to be less than significant or less than significant with mitigation incorporated.

ceqa-f73993fbb79eb15d89.projectTitle: Tipton Community Services District Well No. 6 Equipping and Distribution System Connection Project
ceqa-f73993fbb79eb15d89.description: The proposed Project consists of equipping a previously drilled well with a pump and associated appurtenances and connecting the well to the Tipton Community Services District's existing water distribution system. Work will include installation of a 75-horsepower well pump equipped with a variable-frequency drive (VFD) and related appurtenances, construction of approximately 30 feet of piping to connect the well to the existing distribution system, and minor trenching and backfilling as necessary. Construction is expected to take approximately 20 working days. Once completed, the previously drilled well will be available to supply water through the District's existing municipal water system. The Project would improve the reliability and redundancy of the District’s existing water system and would not expand the District’s service area or provide water for a specific development project. No new well drilling is proposed. The Project would occur at the site of an existing, previously drilled municipal well and would involve a limited area of temporary ground disturbance. Disturbed surfaces would be restored following installation. The Project would not affect a designated sensitive environmental resource, scenic highway, hazardous-waste site identified pursuant to Government Code section 65962.5, or historical resource. There are no unusual circumstances associated with the project that would create a reasonable possibility of a significant environmental effect, and the project would not contribute to a significant cumulative impact from successive projects of the same type in the same place. Therefore, none of the exceptions in CEQA Guidelines section 15300.2 applies.

ceqa-f0005106ce8ceebac6.name: Seaborn Reservoir Project
ceqa-f0005106ce8ceebac6.description: Alternative A – Seaborn Reservoir Alternative A would consist of developing an internal storage reservoir in an abandoned aggregate mining operation where surface water can be re-regulated (filled and emptied) for use by the Project Owners. The Project would be located on the Seaborn Property approximately one mile southeast of the City of Woodlake. The centroid of the Project is 36°23’39.62” N, 119°4’1.87” W. The approximately 235-acres water storage facility equipped with a bidirectional pipeline, an inlet/outlet structure at McKays Point, an outlet structure into the St. Johns River, and a pump station (see Figure 1). Water diverted from the Kaweah River at McKays Point will flow by gravity through a new pipeline to the Seaborn Reservoir across the adjacent property, which is also owned by the Property Owners. Conveyance features would be installed in the southeast corner of the reservoir area to deliver water to and from the St. Johns River and Kaweah River for use by the Project Owners. The area surrounding the internal reservoir would be restored as a habitat area, including native plants and riparian habitat. Restoration of the habitat area would be completed in collaboration with an entity that specializes in habitat restoration. During construction, non-native plants would be removed, and native plant species would be preserved to the greatest extent feasible. Alternative B-- Kaweah Return Location Alternative B would include all of the same features as Alternative A except the water outlet would be due south to the Kaweah River rather than returning water at the McKays Point Structure. This alternative would also be 290 acres and would include a water storage facility equipped with a pipeline, an inlet at McKays Point, and an outlet that would flow into the Kaweah River (see Figure 1). Water diverted from the Kaweah River at McKays Point would flow via gravity through a new pipeline toward the Seaborn Reservoir. Conveyance features would be installed in the southeast corner of the reservoir to deliver water to and from the Kaweah River for use by the Project Owners. The pipeline south to the Kaweah River for pumped return water is anticipated to require less vertical elevation across the pipeline than in Alternative A, which could potentially lessen long-term pumping costs. All other features associated with Alternative B would be the same as in Alternative A. Alternative C – Land Fallowing Alternative C would not require construction or alter the existing land in the Project area and would instead improve water supply through land fallowing. Land fallowing is a practice that involves leaving farmland unplanted for a year or more to conserve water supplies, particularly groundwater. Some benefits associated with land fallowing include soil restoration, and water conservation. To achieve the target water volume, nearly 2,200 acres (assuming a demand of 3 acre-feet per acre) would need to be fallowed. While Alternative C would reduce water demand, it would not result in the distribution of captured water supply to the Project Owners’ service area. This Alternative would also not provide any flood reduction benefits.

ceqa-18f49119e255a12882.name: CASHP Overflow Parking Lot Expansion
ceqa-18f49119e255a12882.agency: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ceqa-18f49119e255a12882.description: The proposed project is to expand the overflow parking lot at Colonel Allensworth SHP. The existing overflow parking lot is compressed decomposed granite over road base. The proposed area would expand the area by 41,584 square feet on already disturbed soil. No new ground disturbance will take place. The parking expansion is needed to meet the needs of the park’s special events.

ceqa-32f120bd76d773e51a.name: Tulare County Zoning Ordinance Update PZC 25-005 (Agricultural Zones) and PZC 25-008 (Residential Zones)
ceqa-32f120bd76d773e51a.projectTitle: Tulare County Zoning Ordinance Update PZC 25-005 (Agricultural Zones) and PZC 25-008 (Residential Zones)
ceqa-32f120bd76d773e51a.description: The Project is proposing to update Ordinance No. 352, the Tulare County Zoning Ordinance, specifically the Agricultural and Residential Zones, by removing redundant language, updating outdated language that may be conflicting with other sections, and updating uses to be consistent with the Tulare County General Plan and other applicable laws and policies. Text Amendment No. PZC 25-005 is proposing to update the Agricultural Zoning sections, and Text Amendment No. PZC 25-008, is proposing to update the Residential Zoning sections of the Tulare County Zoning Ordinance.

ceqa-c182fddf5f7f172010.name: HSIP Cycle 12 Guardrail Safety Improvements Project HSIPL-5946(233)
ceqa-c182fddf5f7f172010.projectTitle: HSIP Cycle 12 Guardrail Safety Improvements Project HSIPL-5946(233)
ceqa-c182fddf5f7f172010.description: The purpose of the Project is to improve the safety on rural segments of County roads for the traveling public by implementing roadway safety countermeasures consistent with the goals of the Highway Safety Improvement Program. The Project consists of repairing, replacing, and upgrading existing damaged, outdated, or destroyed guardrail facilities to meet current safety standards at four locations. The Project also includes minor shoulder corrective work necessary to support the guardrail improvements and improve roadside safety. Work would occur within existing County road rights-of-way and would not add automobile travel lanes, expand roadway capacity, or change the existing roadway use. Construction is anticipated to begin in summer 2027. The beneficiaries of the Project include users of the County roads.

ceqa-d3399164a33160eafe.name: CDFA Nursery Inspection Program FY 26/27
ceqa-d3399164a33160eafe.description: The County is considering entering into an Agreement with the State of California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA) to provide funding for the County of Tulare Agricultural Commissioner’s Office to offset costs of providing and continuing the Nursery Inspection Program that is responsible in preventing the introduction and spread of agricultural pests through nursery stock and protect County agriculture and the consumer against economic losses resulting from the sale of inferior, defective, or pest-infested nursery stock. This agreement may require the County to mitigate or remediate infestation or infested nursery stock.

ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.name: Tule River Indian Tribe of the Tule River Reservation Shan King-Hwy 190-Hartsell Economic Development Fee-to-Trust Project
ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.projectTitle: Tule River Indian Tribe of the Tule River Reservation Shan King-Hwy 190-Hartsell Economic Development Fee-to-Trust Project
ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.agency: United States Department of the Interior, Indian Affairs
ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.agencyName: Bureau of Indian Affairs, United States
ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.description: The project consists of placing the Subject Property into federal trust status for the benefit of the Tribe and the subsequent development by the Tribe of a small commercial development area with existing uses-including citrus grove operations, grazing land, and open space-continuing on the remainder of the property.
ceqa-7d13034050b41da2ce.developmentType: Commercial (Sq. Ft. 50000, Acres 4.3, Employees 10), Waste Treatment (wastewater)(MGD .00824), Water Facilities (Well)(Type Well, MGD .0103), Other (parking and landscaping)

ceqa-cb9f1fee4c41bbc92e.name: Grants Check Structure Project
ceqa-cb9f1fee4c41bbc92e.description: The District proposes to reconstruct a failed water flow regulating structure within the St. Johns River. A new concrete pad will be installed for the placement of the pneumatically actuated gates, which will span the entire width of the existing St. Johns River channel on the new concrete pad. The gate system relies on an airbladder to inflate and raise or deflate and lower the gate system and is composed of a gate panel, anchoring system, air bladder, hinge flap, clamp casting, seals, and retraining straps. The Project will be designed to meet the flow capacity of 8,000 cubic feet per second. The pneumatic gate is designed to be low maintenance, allowing large debris, tree logs or stumps to pass with flowing water without any blockage. The gates will allow the flow to be regulated during normal operations by inflating the air bladder. The concrete pad will be designed to allow heavy equipment like excavators and trucks to access the gates in the event of an emergency. The gates and air bladder will only be accessible during dry seasons or when there is no flow in the river channel. Construction is anticipated to take 180 days and will occur when the St. Johns River is largely dry.
ceqa-cb9f1fee4c41bbc92e.crossStreets: South of Ave 328 west of N. Demaree Street

ceqa-fd75e8895d047c7ed2.name: Zone Variance No., PZV 25-029 and Tentative Parcel Map No., PPM 25-019 – Strable
ceqa-fd75e8895d047c7ed2.projectTitle: Zone Variance No., PZV 25-029 and Tentative Parcel Map No., PPM 25-019 – Strable
ceqa-fd75e8895d047c7ed2.description: Zone Variance No. PZV 25-029 and Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 25- 019 to divide an existing approximate 7.41-acre parcel into four (4) parcels, (Proposed Parcel 1 = 2.06 acres, Proposed Parcel 2 = 1.77 acres, Proposed Parcel 3 = 1.79 acres, and Proposed Parcel 4 = 1.79 acres) located in the AE-20 (Exclusive Agricultural – 20 acre minimum) Zone. Zone Variance No. PZV 25-029 is to address the creation of a parcel less than the minimum acreage. The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-f24ff635528d86a88c.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-047 – Chase
ceqa-f24ff635528d86a88c.projectTitle: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-047 – Chase
ceqa-f24ff635528d86a88c.description: The Applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit (PSP26-047) to allow an second residence, exceeding 1,200 square feet (sqft), on an existing 7.52-acre parcel located at 31650 Road 160 Visalia, Ca 93292 (APN: 108-090-060). The property is located in the AE-20 (Exclusive Agricultural – 20 Acre Minimum) Zone, within the Rural Valley Lands Plan, and has a General Plan land use designation of Valley Agriculture. The project site contains two SFD’s (a 1716sqft mobilehome and a 4,839 sqft SFD w/ 534 sqft patio, 145 sqft porch, 747 sqft breezeway, 874 sqft garage & 461 sqft carport), two septic systems (A2201748) and there are no permit records for the other septic system), a domestic well (A2302308), a 40’x80’ ag storage structure for personal use (A2203487), and a 18kw ground mount solar system (A2600094), onsite. The proposed project would authorize one additional residence for the property owners and/or their family and would not authorize expansion of any agricultural operations, or any other use unless separately reviewed and approved by the County.

ceqa-15d4d3eb122443b687.name: Minor Modification No. MIM 26-022 to PSP 17-081, Helia Van Beek
ceqa-15d4d3eb122443b687.projectTitle: Minor Modification No. MIM 26-022 to PSP 17-081, Helia Van Beek
ceqa-15d4d3eb122443b687.description: Turning Leaf Organics (Applicant) is requesting to allow source separated vegetative food material, as defined by CalRecycle , and agricultural by-product material as additional allowable feedstocks at the existing Turning Leaf Organics Tulare Compost Facility located at 25948 Road 92, Tulare, California (APN 149-010-009 ), in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agriculture 40 Acre Minimum) Zone, within the Rural Valley Lands Plan, with the Land Use Designation of Valley Agriculture. The existing permit authorizes a solid waste recycling facility for commercial composting of dairy manure and green material. The proposed modification would allow the facility to accept compatible plant derived vegetative food material, including fruit and vegetable residuals, produce culls, trimmings, and similar pre-consumer organic materials, , as well as agricultural by-product material consisting of vegetative material with small amounts of naturally occurring nuts and oils and no added oils or other additives. No expansion of the approved facility footprint, operational area, or operational capacity is proposed.

ceqa-0a8430c0b57ace2ca0.name: Special Use Permit, PSP 26-005
ceqa-0a8430c0b57ace2ca0.description: Special Use Permit to authorize a temporary campground consisting of up to twenty-five (25) camping sites for guests of the existing California Hot Springs Resort, for a period not to exceed two (2) years unless extended by the Planning Commission, and to authorize six (6) additional hard-sided yurt guest units (Units 13 through 18) associated with the existing resort operation, on approximately 3.0 acres of Proposed Parcel 2 (176.36 acres), in the PD-O (Planned Development – Recreation Overlay) and AF (Foothill Agricultural) Zones, outside Urban Boundaries, within the Mountain Framework Plan, and designated Resource Conservation. The temporary campground would provide lodging accommodations during the phased development of additional resort guest units, while the hard-sided yurts would provide permanent resort lodging accommodations.

ceqa-3183d84d5e8195b8e7.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-014 – Gutierrez
ceqa-3183d84d5e8195b8e7.projectTitle: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-014 – Gutierrez
ceqa-3183d84d5e8195b8e7.description: The Applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit to allow the third, existing (since 2025) residence onsite (including an exception for mobilehome being over 10 years old), not to exceed 1,440 square feet, on an existing 1.14-acre parcel located at 12867 Road 176 Porterville, CA 93257, (APN 300-130-042). The property is located in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural – 40 Acre Minimum) Zone, within the Rural Valley Lands Plan, and has a General Plan land use designation of Valley Agriculture. The project site currently contains two (2) existing dwellings, one (1) mobilehome that is not permitted (GC2500183; this special use permit is to correct the code violation for this as-built on the property), two (2) septic tanks and leach line systems, two (2) driveway approaches’, one (1) well, and one (1) metal shop. The proposed project would authorize one (1) additional residence for the property owners and/or their family and would not authorize expansion of agricultural operations, or any other use unless separately reviewed and approved by the County. The beneficiaries of the project would be family of the Applicant.

ceqa-2200b46ee748576cf4.name: Domestic Well for the Sertich Cabin (CEQ 26-021)
ceqa-2200b46ee748576cf4.projectTitle: Domestic Well for the Sertich Cabin (CEQ 26-021)
ceqa-2200b46ee748576cf4.description: The proposed Project site is located in the mountain community of Hartland, is not within an Urban Development Boundary, and the property is zoned A-1 (Agricultural Zone). The property owner is requesting an administrative variance for construction of a new (replacement) well to supply the property with water for the domestic uses consistent with the existing zoning. The location of the new well is unable to comply with the minimum setback requirements from the leach lines. The contractor will install a 100-foot annular seal. to eliminate the risk of contamination on the new well site. The beneficiary of the Project is the property owner.

ceqa-539bd11471924110c7.name: PSP 26-032 – Manuel Lira
ceqa-539bd11471924110c7.description: The project involves a request for a special use permit in order to establish a third residence of about 2,200 square feet single-family dwelling unit. The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-91d220b851907039c0.name: PSP 26-022 – GMA Engineering
ceqa-91d220b851907039c0.description: The project involves allowing the construction of a 4,967 square foot structure that will be utilized as a warehouse, which will contain a single use restroom. In the future an office with an area of less than 1,000 square feet may be added within the structure in the M-1 (Light Manufacturing) Zone. The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-f35388550919653de3.name: RPCA Solar 17, LLC Project (PSP 25-092)
ceqa-f35388550919653de3.description: The proposed solar energy generation facility is located in unincorporated Tulare County just north of Porterville on approximately 13.6 acres of three parcels totaling 17.6 acres (APN 243-090-037, 243-090-092, and 243-090-093; Figure 1). The Project area is situated at elevations ranging between approximately 420 to 430 feet above mean sea level (AMSL). Avenue 182 (Ave 182) and State Route 65 (SR 65) bisects the [JW1.1]middle lower third of the Project area, with two parcels situated north of the road and one parcel situated to the south (Figure 2). The two northern parcels are bounded to the west by the Friant-Kern Canal, to the northeast by State Route 65, and to the south by Ave 182Road 232. The southern parcel is bounded to the north Ave 182and east by Road 232, and by rural residential parcels to the south and west. Land surrounding the Project area consists of agricultural land and scattered rural residential properties. The Project area is situated in Section 9 of Township 21 South and Range 27 East within the Porterville, California 7.5-minute U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) quadrangle. The corresponding latitude and longitude at the approximate center of the Project area is 36°07’16.35” north latitude and -119°03’20.95” west longitude. The proposed small-scale utility solar generation project is located in the Exclusive Agricultural “AE” zoning district. RPCA Solar 17, LLC (sponsor/applicant) has entered into a long-term lease agreement with the property owner, the Antoine Bechara Revocable Trust, to facilitate the development and long-term operation of the Project. When complete, the Project will generate up to 3 megawatts (MW) of alternating current (AC) clean, reliable solar energy. The Project will interconnect to Southern California Edison’s (SCE) pre-existing electrical distribution system adjacent to the site. The power generated from this facility is expected to be sold to the Clean Power Alliance through a long-term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). The Project will utilize solar modules to convert the sun’s energy into usable (AC) power. Single-axis tracking technology will be utilized to allow the modules to efficiently track the sun throughout the day and maximize the efficiency of solar collection. The rows of modules will be anchored in the ground using driven piles, and the approximate height of the array is 8 feet, and the maximum height of the array will not exceed 15 feet above ground at maximum tilt. The Project will be fenced in with a six-foot chain-link fence with a foot of straight wire on top for a total fence height of approximately seven feet. A minimal opening of no more than 1one foot may be provided at the base of the fence at appropriate intervals as a wildlife-permeable design. The Project sites and panel arrays would be accessed via an all-weather gravel road that surrounds both sections of the Project area and is approximately 20 feet wide and over 5,000 feet in length. Electric power connections will be provided via existing overhead power lines adjacent to Ave 182/Road 232 in the middle of the Project site. Approximately 50 feet from Ave 182/Road 232, these overhead power lines will transition to power pole connections and then underground utility runs adjacent to the access road. Utility connections will be underground from this point to the power station and transformer located in the middle of the project area. The Project will require minimal regularly planned maintenance and will be operated remotely. The Project sponsor will enter into an operations and maintenance contractor[JW2.1] to provide proper operation and maintenance of the facility; and general maintenance of the Project grounds. Native groundcover restoration and maintenance after installation will provide increased site drainage and groundwater percolation and limit sheet flows out of the project area. No firearms or pets will be allowed on the site during construction of the Project or during ongoing operations and maintenance activities. All heavy equipment and vehicles used during Project construction will be washed prior to mobilization to the site to prevent the spread of noxious weeds. Construction equipment will be cleaned of mud or other debris that may contain invasive plants and/or seeds and inspected to reduce the potential for spreading noxious weeds. All mitigation measures will be incorporated into the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program developed for the Project, and the Applicant will implement all monitoring and reporting obligations as detailed in this IS/MND.

ceqa-f2054e21c1b91005bc.name: Pavement Rehabilitation EA 06-1K250
ceqa-f2054e21c1b91005bc.description: Project is located on State Route 99 in Tulare, 0.2 miles south of Ave. 120 overcrossing to 0.1 mile north of Elk Bayou. Work involves removing and replacing RHMA-O (0.10’) and RHMA-G (0.20’) with dig-out repairs at various failed locations from post mile 19.5 to post mile 25.2, along with fog seal and 2-foot shoulder backing where needed. Chevron markings to be applied on gore areas of the ramps from post mile 15.1 to 19.5. All work stays within the Caltrans right of way.
ceqa-f2054e21c1b91005bc.crossStreets: On State Route 99 from Ave. 120 overcrossing to Elk Bayou

ceqa-1b24522135661ad76e.name: Former Lamoure’s Cleaners and Former Country Club Cleaners Visalia Dry Cleaner Investigation Project Removal Action Work Plan – Soil and Soil Vapor
ceqa-1b24522135661ad76e.projectTitle: Former Lamoure’s Cleaners and Former Country Club Cleaners Visalia Dry Cleaner Investigation Project Removal Action Work Plan – Soil and Soil Vapor
ceqa-1b24522135661ad76e.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-1b24522135661ad76e.description: The project includes installing and operating a soil vapor extraction (SVE) system at the former Lamoure’s and Former Country Club Cleaners properties to address soil and soil vapor impacts by volatile organic compounds (VOCs), primarily tetrachloroethene (PCE), presumed to have resulted from spills and other handling processes from several former dry-cleaning facilities. The project is anticipated to take approximately seven years at the former Lamoure’s site and three months over a one-year period at the former Country Club site. Remediation activities include: • Construct and install full-scale and temporary soil vapor extraction (SVE) systems, including SVE wells, nested soil vapor probes, and below-ground polyvinyl chloride (PVC) conveyance piping at the former Lamoure’s Cleaners and Country Club Cleaners properties. • Air/dust controls and monitoring during construction: implementation of temporary stormwater management best management practices (BMPs), and dust control measures. • Site security and implementation measures (Traffic Control Plan (TCP), and a Site-specific Health and Safety Plan (HASP)). In addition, Mitigation Measure NOI-1 (Operational Noise Reduction) is implemented to address potential noise impacts and ensure compliance with City of Visalia Ordinance 8.36.040. • Preparation of a Construction Completion Report documenting completion of removal action activities. • Finalize and implement an Operation, Maintenance, and Monitoring (OM&M) manual for each SVE system.
ceqa-1b24522135661ad76e.crossStreets: 2901 South Mooney Boulevard and 2000 West Whitendale Avenue

ceqa-a9fb3d0fbf34cd4923.name: 2026 Road Repair and Accountability Act (RRAA) Project 1
ceqa-a9fb3d0fbf34cd4923.projectTitle: 2026 Road Repair and Accountability Act (RRAA) Project 1
ceqa-a9fb3d0fbf34cd4923.description: The Project consists of repairing asphalt materials on multiple segments of existing County roads. The work includes a combination of isolated pavement repairs followed by the installation of new asphalt surfacing. All projects will include corrective work (adding a thin course of granular material for leveling to minimize drop-off heights for overlays) to be performed on the shoulders of the roadways. Furthermore, all newly surfaced roadways will receive new traffic stripes and pavement markings. Efficient and responsive improvements and maintenance of the County road network will enhance the safety and security of the public by improving the access of pedestrians and the transportation infrastructure for the general population throughout the region. Construction is anticipated to begin during the third quarter through the fourth quarter of 2026. The beneficiaries of the Project include users of the County roads.

ceqa-2a083dcb5bd3ff5ad9.name: One-Way STOP Control on Avenue 404 at Road 64, southwest of Dinuba
ceqa-2a083dcb5bd3ff5ad9.projectTitle: One-Way STOP Control on Avenue 404 at Road 64, southwest of Dinuba
ceqa-2a083dcb5bd3ff5ad9.description: This project will enhance vehicular circulation and traffic safety at the intersection of Avenue 404 and Road 64, and will consist of installing a One-Way Stop sign on Avenue 404 at Road 64, located southwest of the incorporated City of Dinuba, CA. This "T" intersection is currently uncontrolled, with no posted Stop sign. In response to concerns regarding traffic safety, the Tulare County Resource Management Agency (RMA) conducted an investigation. To improve the vehicular circulation and safety at this intersection, the Traffic Operations Division determined that this intersection meets the requirements of Section 2B.04 Right of Way at Intersections of the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CA MUTCD), and is consistent with the California Vehicle Code (CVC), Section 22450(c), which states in part that “a local authority may adopt rules and regulations by ordinance or resolution providing for the placement of a stop sign at any location on a highway under its jurisdiction where the stop sign would enhance traffic safety”.

ceqa-cb07a8ef37095724b0.name: 2026 Slurry Seal Program
ceqa-cb07a8ef37095724b0.description: The 2026 Slurry Seal Program Project consists of slurry sealing approximately 9 miles of existing County roads within unincorporated communities in Tulare County, including road segments in or near South Visalia Area, Ivanhoe, North/South Porterville Area, Springville, Pixley, and Strathmore. The work would occur on existing paved roadways, including road segments within subdivisions with curb and gutter. The purpose of the Project is to preserve and protect the underlying pavement structure, extend pavement service life, and provide a renewed driving surface for users of these facilities. The Project would not add automobile travel lanes or expand roadway capacity. Construction is anticipated to begin in the third quarter of 2026 and be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026.

ceqa-164a7e7983378813df.name: Avenue 56 Permanent Restoration Improvements Project
ceqa-164a7e7983378813df.description: Avenue 56 serves as a major collector road from the community of Alpaugh to State Routes 43 and 99. In early 2023, Avenue 56 was submerged by floodwater that damaged the roadway. An emergency restoration project was undertaken to elevate the roadway by five feet. The proposed project is needed to implement permanent improvements to address safety concerns.

ceqa-6c99598ff0e3ea8070.name: MHDSF Winter HQ Fuel Reduction
ceqa-6c99598ff0e3ea8070.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-6c99598ff0e3ea8070.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-6c99598ff0e3ea8070.description: The proposed project will involve fuel reduction activities on 30 acres of state and 50 acres of adjoining private property. The project location ranges in elevation from 3,680-4,400 feet. The vegetation type of the project area is an oak woodland forest community. The overstory consists of ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa), incense-cedar (Calocedrus decurrens), California black oak (Quercus kelloggii), and interior live oak (Quercus wislizeni). The understory consists of white leaf manzanita (Arctostaphylos viscida), buckbrush (Ceanothus cuneatus), deerbrush (Ceanothus integerrimus), California buckeye (Aesculus californica), and western poison-oak (Toxicodendron diversilobum). Project work will reduce hazardous fuel loads by removal of underbrush, and dead, dying and diseased vegetation. Project activities will be completed by hand crews and include thinning of brush and shrubs; thinning and limbing of small trees; removal of dead material; piling and burning of cut biomass material. No heavy equipment will be used during this project.

ceqa-8afe18f4266eecf9ed.name: Villa Margherita—TSM No. 5608, CUP No. 2026-05, and Exception No. 2026-05
ceqa-8afe18f4266eecf9ed.projectTitle: Villa Margherita—TSM No. 5608, CUP No. 2026-05, and Exception No. 2026-05
ceqa-8afe18f4266eecf9ed.description: Villa Margherita Tentative Subdivision Map No. 5608: A request to subdivide the property into 82 lots for single-family residential uses, landscaping outlots, lighting, and parks, to be located within the R-1 zone. Conditional Use Permit No. 2026-05: A request to allow a planned unit development with reduced lot area and setbacks. Exception No. 2026-05: A request for exceptions to the Objective Design Standards regarding façade design elements.
ceqa-8afe18f4266eecf9ed.crossStreets: East Tulare Avenue and South Burke and South Edison Streets

ceqa-104577a8e8f20f867a.name: Minor Modification No. MIM 26-017
ceqa-104577a8e8f20f867a.description: The Applicant, Fernjo Dairy #3 (Joseph Fernandes, Owner), is requesting to allow for the construction of a process pit, extending the sand lane to flush the existing dairy facility and the addition of wastewater transfer lines from Fernjo Dairy #3 (Tulare County Dairy Facility ID No. 99) to Fernjo Dairy #1 (Tulare County Dairy Facility ID No. 95). The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-d0d98ea8f74966e1e2.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-041– Mariscos La Langosta
ceqa-d0d98ea8f74966e1e2.projectTitle: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-041– Mariscos La Langosta
ceqa-d0d98ea8f74966e1e2.description: The Applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit to allow an alcohol license to sell beer and wine at the existing restaurant on site, on a 0.94 acre parcel, located at 40311 Sierra Drive, Three Rivers, Ca 93271 (APN 068-130-040). The property is located in the in the C-2-SC (General Commercial – Scenic Corridor Combining) Zone, within the Three Rivers Community Plan area, and has a General Plan land use designation of Commercial Recreation. The project site currently contains a commercial building described as a 2852sf restaurant. The proposed project would authorize an alcohol license to sell beer and wine onsite, for the restaurant consumers, property owners and/or their family and would not authorize expansion of any other use unless separately reviewed and approved by the County.

ceqa-5b08b9b200a9f251c7.name: Statewide Monitoring Network Modernization Project: Chagoopa Plateau Station Upgrades
ceqa-5b08b9b200a9f251c7.description: DWR proposes to upgrade outdated data collection equipment and replace a 17-foot wilderness pole at the Chagoopa Plateau hydrometeorological station with a galvanized hinged fold tilt pole anchored to a buried ballast tray base (8.5' x 8.5' x 16"). The hinged fold tilt pole and ballast tray base would be transported by helicopter. Soil probes would also be installed within 30 feet of the station by excavating a 3' x 3' x 3' temporary soil pit and shallow conduit trench from the station to the probes. The proposed tilt pole would also address potential safety concerns with ongoing maintenance activities at the station.

ceqa-7ff69233176aa38e28.name: Cardoza Contractor Storage Yard (PSP 26-013)
ceqa-7ff69233176aa38e28.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-013 would allow the establishment and operation of a contractor's storage yard on Assessor's Parcel Number (APN) 195111021 to support an off-site landscaping business. The Project involves construction of a 3,600squarefoot metal shop building and installation of an on-site wastewater treatment/septic system. The proposed use would include parking and storage of up to twelve pickup trucks, twelve cargo/flatbed trailers, lawn service equipment and mowers, employee parking, and related site access and circulation improvements. Site improvements include driveway and access upgrades, utilities, lighting, fencing, screening, landscaping, storm water management and drainage facilities, and other features shown on the approved site plan. A 20footwide all weather gravel road would provide access to the shop building. An open parking area would be located south of the shop building, sloped gently to direct storm water to an existing animal enclosure/pen located within the project parcel.
ceqa-7ff69233176aa38e28.crossStreets: North side of Avenue 228 quarter mile west of Road 140
ceqa-7ff69233176aa38e28.developmentType: Commercial (Landscaping Contractor Yard)(Sq. Ft. 3600, Acres 4.8, Employees 27)

ceqa-5e53209afee31c8689.name: Conditional Use Permit No. 2026-06
ceqa-5e53209afee31c8689.description: Conditional Use Permit No. 2026-06: a request to establish an approximately 363,000 square foot personal mini storage facility on approximately 20 acres in the I (Industrial) and I-L (Light Industrial) zone districts.

ceqa-dd43ab9c934236d4e8.name: Tulare County Stream Channel Routine Maintenance Agreement Project
ceqa-dd43ab9c934236d4e8.projectTitle: Tulare County Stream Channel Routine Maintenance Agreement Project
ceqa-dd43ab9c934236d4e8.description: Tulare County proposes to enter into a long-term 12-year Streambed Alteration Agreement with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) for ongoing implementation of routine maintenance activities within jurisdictional improved and unimproved stream channels and drainage facilities, and associated CDFW jurisdictional areas throughout the County. The County anticipates completing approximately 30 maintenance projects per year over the 12-year life of the agreement. Routine maintenance activities may include removal, replacement, or repair of drainage facilities; channel alignment maintenance; debris or obstruction removal; silt, sand, gravel, or sediment removal under dry conditions; vegetation control in channels or on banks; goat/sheep grazing for vegetation and thatch management; minor erosion control work; repair of previous erosion control work; and geotechnical sampling or subsurface cultural resource sensitivity testing. Exact methods, locations, and the extent of individual maintenance activities would be submitted to CDFW for review and approval through the Verification Request Form process.
ceqa-dd43ab9c934236d4e8.developmentType: Other (Routine stream channel and drainage facility maintenance)

ceqa-8fd9f8f90a6baa01f9.name: Special Use Permit PSP 26-043- Second Residence larger than 1,200 sq. ft
ceqa-8fd9f8f90a6baa01f9.projectTitle: Special Use Permit PSP 26-043- Second Residence larger than 1,200 sq. ft
ceqa-8fd9f8f90a6baa01f9.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-043 is requested to allow a second dwelling unit larger than 1,200 sq. ft. on a 5.11-acre parcel located parcel located at 24503 Avenue 90, Terra Bella. ceqa-360eb3e17cd9b696aa.description: The 2.99-acre Project consists of correcting the hydrologic alterations to Windy Springs Meadow caused by historical ranching infrastructure, channelization, and meadow berm construction. The Project will restore the natural hydrologic and ecological functions of Windy Springs Meadow, its associated springs, and the intermittent tributary that flows through the meadow. Work includes removing artificial containment structures from two springheads, reestablishing the natural spring outflow channel through localized bank grading and cobble placement, and lowering or removing two man made berms to restore surface sheet flow and expand wetland hydrology. Salvaged meadow sod and native vegetation will be reused to stabilize disturbed soils and fill shallow anthropogenic depressions.

ceqa-d7ac1ca672614f343d.name: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, EMD Millipore Sigma Company, Visalia, California
ceqa-d7ac1ca672614f343d.projectTitle: Emergency Permit for Management of Hazardous Waste, EMD Millipore Sigma Company, Visalia, California
ceqa-d7ac1ca672614f343d.agency: California Department of Toxic Substances Control
ceqa-d7ac1ca672614f343d.description: The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), pursuant to authority granted under California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 22, Division 4.5, Chapter 20, Sec. 66270.61, has issued an Emergency Permit to the EMD Millipore Sigma Company, (EPA ID# CAR000301093) to treat hazardous wastes through a controlled reaction with chemical solutions. Specifically, thirty eight (38) 1-liter containers, two (2) 100-milliliter containers, four (4) 4-liter containers, and three (3) 500-milliliter containers of Diethyl Ether; six (6) 100-milliliter containers of Cyclophenyl Methyl Ether; one (1) 500-milliliter container of Diisopropyl Ether; thirty four (34) 1-liter containers, one (1) 500-milliliter container, and twelve (12) 100-milliliter containers of Tetrahydrofuran; two (2) 1-liter containers and one (1) 4-liter container of 1,4 Dioxane; thirteen (13) 100-gram containers, one (1) 200-gram container, one (1) 1-liter container, and six (6) 500-milliliter containers of Acrylic Acid; one (1) 2-liter container of Styrene and two (2) 500-milliliter containers of Styrene; four (4) 2-liter containers of Methyl Methacrylate; and one (1) 500-gram container of Benzoyl Peroxide must be stabilized prior to transport to an authorized hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facility. These chemicals are currently being stored at EMD Millipore Sigma Company located at 8511 West Riggin Avenue, Visalia, California. DTSC has determined as a safety precaution to prevent an accident or severe injury, an Emergency Permit should be issued to chemically stabilize the hazardous wastes by Clean Harbors Environmental Services (Clean Harbors) prior to storage and eventual transportation off-site. Background: One hundred thirty-two (132) containers have peroxide formation present on either the inside, outside, or the bottom of the chemicals’ containers, as well as the thread container caps. The presence of peroxide formation may be unstable at relatively low concentrations, resulting in fire and/or explosion if improperly handled. One (1) container has shock and/or temperature sensitive materials that can decompose or detonate with external energy when dry or concentrated. If the material is improperly handled, there is a potential for a reaction, which includes fire, deflagration, or detonation. Due to the presence of peroxide formation/shock-sensitive materials, DTSC considers these chemicals to be an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment. Chemical stabilization is recommended prior to transport to a permitted treatment, storage, and disposal facility. Project Activities: The treatment of these hazardous wastes involves the addition of solutions to the containers in a controlled manner to reduce the reactive or ignitable characteristics of the chemicals. Treatment will take place within a designated exclusion zone. Only technicians from Clean Harbors will be allowed in the exclusion zone. Movement, preparation, and treatment of the containers will be in accordance with established standards. Within 10 business days of the expiration of this permit, EMD Millipore Sigma Company will submit a final report, signed in accordance with Title 22, CCR Sec. 66270.11(d). The report shall include certification that the treatment area has been cleared of all residual hazardous waste generated from this emergency treatment and all generated waste has been properly managed. The Emergency Permit is effective beginning July 23, 2026 and shall expire on October 20, 2026.

ceqa-997a554cb3585ddfa7.description: The Uhl Pocket project involves 103 acres of hazardous fuel reduction work along the Uhl Pocket Fire Control Road as well as the recurring road maintenance of the Uhl Pocket Fire Control Road located within Tulare County, CA. The Uhl Pocket Fire Control Road serves as a point of ingress and egress for fire suppression and emergency response activities. Road maintenance activities will consist of grading, filling of existing ruts, repair of existing water drainage facilities, the cleanout of existing drainage facilities, and the removal of obstructions within the road such as fallen rocks and trees. Road maintenance activities will occur within the prism of the existing road. Fuel reduction activities will occur within a 100 ft buffer, from the roads downslope edge, on the north side of the road and to the prevailing ridge line on the south side of the road, approximately 75-200 ft from the roads upslope edge. Fuel reduction activities will include mastication, limbing, brush cutting, piling, and the subsequent burning of the piles. CAL FIRE staff and contractors will reduce fuel loads through the above mentioned treatment activities to create a shaded fuel break and maintain adequate access for fire suppression resources on the fire control road.

The 2026 update to the 2022 RTP/SCS is focused on continued implementation of the 2022 RTP/SCS, with updates to ensure consistency with federal, State, and local planning requirements. As have past RTPs, the proposed 2026 RTP/SCS shows how the region can invest limited transportation funds to maintain, operate and improve an integrated, multi-modal transportation system with the purpose of facilitating the efficient movement of people and goods. The updated plan identifies specific strategies, policies, and actions, including a list of programmed and planned transportation projects feasibly within the region’s anticipated transportation funding levels, to meet the current and future needs of the region. The planning horizon of the proposed 2026 RTP/SCS is 2049.

ceqa-f16b8a07f11825f94c.name: Terra Bella Quarry, PMR 25-003
ceqa-f16b8a07f11825f94c.description: Holliday Rock Co., Inc. has applied to the County of Tulare for a Surface Mining Permit and Reclamation Plan to develop the proposed Terra Bella Quarry over a 50-year period through approximately 2076. The 318-acre project would disturb about 237 acres, including 223 acres dedicated to excavation, and is expected to produce up to 250,000 tons of crushed stone annually from an estimated 50 million tons of reserves for use in regional construction and infrastructure projects. Operations would include drilling, blasting, hauling, crushing, screening, and washing materials on-site using heavy equipment and recycled well water, with approximately 37 to 38 daily one-way truck trips and up to 15 employees working 10-hour days, five days per week. The project also includes supporting facilities such as a processing plant, stockpiles, maintenance areas, access roads, and parking areas.
ceqa-f16b8a07f11825f94c.crossStreets: 1 mile east of Avenue 80 and Road 268

ceqa-55036e423959bb12d6.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-009 – Flores
ceqa-55036e423959bb12d6.projectTitle: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-009 – Flores
ceqa-55036e423959bb12d6.description: The Applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit to allow construction of one second residence, not to exceed 1,200 square feet, on an existing 4.91-acre parcel located at 39007 Road 140, Cutler, APN 035-160-036. The property is located in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural – 40 Acre Minimum) Zone, within the Rural Valley Lands Plan, and has a General Plan land use designation of Valley Agriculture. The project site currently participates in the Employee Housing Program and contains six existing dwellings. The proposed project would authorize one additional residence for the property owners and/or their family and would not authorize expansion of the existing Employee Housing Program, agricultural operations, or any other use unless separately reviewed and approved by the County.

ceqa-6f703e9ba4489a8f70.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-027 – CRAVENS
ceqa-6f703e9ba4489a8f70.projectTitle: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-027 – CRAVENS
ceqa-6f703e9ba4489a8f70.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-027 to allow a Second Residence, on a 1.92 acre parcel, in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agriculture – 40 Acre Minimum) Zone, within the Rural Valley Lands Plan, with the Land Use Designation of Valley Agriculture.

ceqa-edadb42c25c581ac45.name: Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reading (ALPR) Camera Installation Project
ceqa-edadb42c25c581ac45.projectTitle: Flock Safety Automated License Plate Reading (ALPR) Camera Installation Project
ceqa-edadb42c25c581ac45.description: The project consists of the installation of a Flock Safety automated license plate reading (ALPR) camera on behalf of the Visalia Police Department. The installation includes a new breakaway support pole with concrete foundation, solar panel, and camera unit installed within public right-of-way. The purpose of the installation is to assist law enforcement in identifying vehicles associated with criminal activity. The beneficiaries of the project include law enforcement and the public at large, as the installation supports public safety objectives within the City of Visalia.

ceqa-9748a377fe6f9bfce3.name: Windy Springs Meadow Restoration Project (Request No. 1652-2026-094-001-R4)
ceqa-9748a377fe6f9bfce3.projectTitle: Windy Springs Meadow Restoration Project (Request No. 1652-2026-094-001-R4)
ceqa-9748a377fe6f9bfce3.agency: California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Central Region 4
ceqa-9748a377fe6f9bfce3.agencyName: Fish and Wildlife, Region 4 - Central, Fresno
ceqa-9748a377fe6f9bfce3.description: Pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1652, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife has approved the Windy Springs Meadow Restoration Project as submitted by Jon Christensen. The three-acre Project will address meadow degradation that is largely attributed to anthropogenic modifications. Project activities include but are not limited to the removal of artificial containment systems around two springheads, removal and/or lowering of earthen berms, and the installation of low-tech process-based treatments. The Project is intended to restore hydrologic function and habitat quality within the 46-acre Windy Springs Meadow.

ceqa-9b36c39859f00fc23b.name: Revised WDRs for Setton Pistachio and Porterville Citrus Terra Bella Processing Facilities
ceqa-9b36c39859f00fc23b.projectTitle: Revised WDRs for Setton Pistachio and Porterville Citrus Terra Bella Processing Facilities
ceqa-9b36c39859f00fc23b.agency: California Regional Water Quality Control Board, Central Valley Fresno Region 5
ceqa-9b36c39859f00fc23b.agencyName: Regional Water Quality Control Board, Region 5 - Fresno
ceqa-9b36c39859f00fc23b.description: The revised Waste Discharge Requirements (WDRs) will regulate the discharge of pistachio- and citrus-processing wastewater generated by the Setton Pistachio and Porterville Citrus facilities in Terra Bella (collectively, the Terra Bella Processing Facilities). The updated WDRs authorize a maximum daily and total annual discharge of pistachio process wastewater of 3.0 mgd and 80 million gallons, respectively, and allow a maximum daily discharge of citrus process wastewater of up to 0.08 mgd.

ceqa-35bd37920464ed8d18.name: Visalia Community Garden Rehabilitation
ceqa-35bd37920464ed8d18.description: Put an unused unmaintained community garden plot back into service as a site for youth instruction and projects, community building, production of fruits and vegetables for use by gardening participants or wider distribution, and expansion of space available to the adjacent community center.

ceqa-f28c97c3e7ad77349b.description: This project is a Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 26-012 requested by Janet Colson Kaiser, 19999 Road 96, Tulare, CA 93274 (agent: Lane Engineers, Incorporated, 979 N. ceqa-1eb7fa96f78010ffb6.description: This project is a Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 26-010 requested by Bonifacio Gonzalez, 1036 North Dove Road, Earlimart, CA 93219 (agent: Lane Engineers, Incorporated, 979 N. ceqa-7f769c5ad5c46da3bb.description: The Zone Variance PZV 26-009 is to allow a division of non-conforming parcel in AE-20 (Exclusive Agricultural Minimum 20-acre) Zone and a Waiver of final map requested Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 26-008 is to create two (2) new parcels from the original 4.75- acres, Parcel 1= 1.82-acre and Parcel 2= 2.93-acre. The beneficiary is the property owner and his family.

ceqa-fc65478f457d497e5a.name: Zone Variance No. PZV 26-013
ceqa-fc65478f457d497e5a.description: The Applicant, Deer Creek Pistachio, LLC, is requesting a proposed on-site monument sign of approximately 70 square feet to serve the Setton Farms (Deer Creek Facility). The sign is proposed to be located within both the required front yard zoning setback (25-foot minimum) and the building line setback (50-foot minimum from the centerline of the right-of-way). The property is zoned AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural – 40-acre minimum). The beneficiary of the project would be for the Applicant (Setton Farms Facility).
