ceqa-828c76ac07250c590a.name: Special Use Permit PSP 26-012- SIERRA MINI MART
ceqa-828c76ac07250c590a.projectTitle: Special Use Permit PSP 26-012- SIERRA MINI MART
ceqa-828c76ac07250c590a.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-012 is requested to allow 15,000 gallons Above Ground Steel Fuel tank for an existing convenience grocery Store and Shell Gas station. The proposed Above-Ground Steel Fuel tank is to add a new diesel service to the existing convenience store and Shell gas station. The subject site is located within the Terra Bella Urban Development Boundaries in C-2-MU (General Commercial with Mixed Use overlay) zone. The beneficiary is the property owner.

ceqa-049dd964d2d6b7399f.name: Lemon Cove Water System Improvement Project
ceqa-049dd964d2d6b7399f.projectTitle: Lemon Cove Water System Improvement Project
ceqa-049dd964d2d6b7399f.description: The State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) is a Responsible Agency for the Project. The State Water Board’s Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (SRF) Program is financing the Project referred to internally as New Well and Storage Tank Installation Project. The Project will involve improving an existing drinking water system owned and operated by the Applicant. The proposed Project will include the following: 1) two production wells, 2) site piping, valves, and flow monitoring equipment, 3) fencing, 4) access roadway improvements, 5) electrical control panels, 6) transmission pipeline, 7) water storage tank that is approximately 24 feet tall and approximately 26 feet in diameter, 8) bladder tank, 9) tank access road, and 10) booster pump station with variable frequency drives. PROJECT NUMBER: 5400616-001C

ceqa-055e7affb094cecfe7.name: Freight Elevator Renovation, Porterville Development Center
ceqa-055e7affb094cecfe7.projectTitle: Freight Elevator Renovation, Porterville Development Center
ceqa-055e7affb094cecfe7.description: The proposed project will renovate the warehouse freight elevator at the Porterville Development Center. The project will remove and replace piston, cab controls, cab door, motors, and call buttons, at the freight elevator.

ceqa-2c2cefd58c5fe8419a.name: Tulare-Dayton Improvements - Tulare CA
ceqa-2c2cefd58c5fe8419a.description: This project is a street improvement project located north of Tulare Avenue (SR 137) and east of Dayton Street. The project is both a pavement management project that will improve deteriorated streets within the project area, and a utility project that will repair/replace aging water, sewer and storm drainage facilities. Additionally, certain ADA-compliant concrete features will be constructed. This vital project will significantly improve public infrastructure within the project boundaries, enhancing public safety and improving the City’s ability to reliably provide public services to residents.
ceqa-2c2cefd58c5fe8419a.crossStreets: Academy Avenue between Dayton Street and Laspina Street

ceqa-133f186509550f8c4d.name: Windy Springs Meadow Restoration
ceqa-133f186509550f8c4d.description: The Project is designed to restore the ecological form and function of Windy Springs meadow and the associated springs and intermittent tributary to increase resilience to climate change and wildfire. Implementing the Project will provide social benefits including engaging tribal members and providing educational and cultural opportunities for tribal members, college students and others. Restoration actions will be implemented on 3.1 acres of the meadow. WCB Project Tracker ID: 2025154.

ceqa-811f0e6afcb23a5cc5.name: Tule River Tribe Complete Streets and Two Pedestrian Bridges Project
ceqa-811f0e6afcb23a5cc5.projectTitle: Tule River Tribe Complete Streets and Two Pedestrian Bridges
ceqa-811f0e6afcb23a5cc5.description: The Project predominantly includes the construction of two new pedestrian bridge crossings. Generally, the Project would provide safer routes for Tule River Tribe pedestrians to cross the South Fork of the Tule River (Tule River) to access an education center and gymnasium and provide safe river crossings via pedestrian bridges. The Project is exclusively located along the South Fork of the Tule River exclusively within the Tule River Reservation, which is located approximately 20 miles southeast of the City of Porterville. Project components include: 1. Replacement of the existing pedestrian swinging bridge. 2. A new pedestrian bridge to connect Cow Mountain Road and the corridor to the Justice Center. 3. Class 1 trail. 4. Approximately 3,765 SF of concrete sidewalk. 5. Seven (7) accessible curb ramps. 6. Two (2) streetlights for the N. Reservation Road corridor. 7. Eight (8) new solar-powered Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) (4 locations. 8. 2 RRFBs assumed per location). 9. Two (2) raised pedestrian crossings. 10. Reconfiguration of back-in-angled parking stalls. 11. Landscaping and irrigation for the length of the project. 12. Signing and pavement delineation for the corridor, including pedestrian bridge.
ceqa-811f0e6afcb23a5cc5.crossStreets: No. Reservation Road between Cow Mountain Road and Mission Dollar Bridge

ceqa-422ed572cac505fc5b.name: 2025 Road Repair and Accountability Act (RRAA) Project 2
ceqa-422ed572cac505fc5b.projectTitle: 2025 Road Repair and Accountability Act (RRAA) Project 2
ceqa-422ed572cac505fc5b.description: The Project consists of repairing asphalt materials on multiple segments of existing County roads. The work includes a combination of isolated pavement repairs followed by the installation of new asphalt surfacing. All projects will include corrective work (adding a thin course of granular material for leveling to minimize drop-off heights for overlays) to be performed on the shoulders of the roadways. No additional roadway capacity is added. Furthermore, all newly surfaced roadways will receive new traffic stripes and pavement markings. Efficient and responsive improvements and maintenance of the County road network will enhance the safety and security of the public by improving the access of pedestrians and the transportation infrastructure for the general population throughout the region. Construction is anticipated to begin during the first quarter through the second quarter of 2026. The Project will benefit users of the roadways.

ceqa-e3ef9c986ccabc62d4.name: Road 130 Palm Elementary Sidewalk Improvements Project
ceqa-e3ef9c986ccabc62d4.projectTitle: Road 130 Palm Elementary Sidewalk Improvements Project
ceqa-e3ef9c986ccabc62d4.description: The purpose of this project is to grind and replace the existing two-lane undivided, 40-foot-wide pavement section of Road 130 between Avenue 416 and Tactacan Avenue. All newly resurfaced roadways will receive new traffic stripes, pavement markings, and pedestrian crossings. Additional improvements include construction of curb and gutter, sidewalks, accessible curb ramps, drive approaches, and related striping/signing. Improvements to the path of travel will result in improved visibility for motorists approaching pedestrian crossings, accommodate people in disabilities, and increase safety for pedestrians using the facilities. The project will not result in an increase to the roadway’s vehicular capacity. Efficient and responsive improvements of the County road networks will enhance the safety and security of the public by improving the access of pedestrians throughout the region. Construction is anticipated to begin in summer of 2027 and is expected to be completed by fall of 2027. Beneficiaries of the project include vehicles and students/pedestrians utilizing this roadway corridor.

ceqa-e3b1317b1f96edb241.name: Earlimart Sheriff Substation Paving Project
ceqa-e3b1317b1f96edb241.description: The Earlimart Sheriff Substation Paving Project will consist of repaving existing parking areas, adding drought tolerant landscaping, and on-site storm water retention basins. The existing parking area is deteriorated and in need of repaving. The repaving will include the removal of the existing deteriorated oiled sand/asphalt material. New aggregate base will be added to improve the long-term durability of the parking areas. Once the existing paving demolition/removal is complete the new asphalt concrete paving will be installed. Grading will be moderately adjusted to allow for the onsite storm water retention. The site has existing ADA parking and path of travel that has previously been updated and will not be disturbed. Beneficiaries of this Project are users of this parking lot, including law enforcement personnel and the public.

ceqa-f27221ffd0dbb9654a.name: Comfort Inn & Suites Repair OWTS Project (CEQ 26-018)
ceqa-f27221ffd0dbb9654a.projectTitle: Comfort Inn & Suites Repair OWTS Project (CEQ 26-018)
ceqa-f27221ffd0dbb9654a.description: The proposed Project is an existing Comfort Inn & Suites Sequoia Kings Canyon hotel, with 103 existing rooms, parking areas, pool/spa, onsite public water system, and an existing onsite wastewater treatment system. The proposed Project is limited to repair and modification of the existing onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS) to address Water Board compliance issues, improve wastewater treatment and distribution, and support ongoing permit processing. The Project includes installation of a new 15,000-gallon primary septic tank, reuse of the existing 15,000-gallon tank as a pre-anoxic tank, new Orenco AX-MAX media bed filtration treatment units, UV disinfection, digital flow metering, controls, piping/electrical work, and repair, replacement, and limited modification of existing drip/leach dispersal components necessary to serve the existing hotel use and maintain compliance with applicable wastewater requirements of existing drip/leach dispersal components. The proposed Project does not propose new hotel rooms, new hotel buildings, new lots, expanded lodging operations, increased guest capacity, new retail/restaurant use, or a change in land use. The purpose is to maintain the existing hotel use while correcting wastewater system deficiencies and obtaining required environmental/permitting clearance. Short-term and construction-period controls include maintaining hotel plumbing in leak-free condition, operational controls to stay within permitted flow limits, temporary pump-and-haul/pump truck support as needed, and phased construction to maintain controlled hotel operations and site access. Construction is expected to follow a 6-8 week phased schedule after permits and long-­lead equipment are available.

ceqa-8e7d07f823ba4a7e5e.name: Murry-Park-Pond-Path-Improvements
ceqa-8e7d07f823ba4a7e5e.description: The project will consist of the installation of a 5' wide concrete path, solar lighting (50 ft apart) 6' benches (6) and 6' ADA picnic tables (5) around the perimeter of the existing Murry Park Pond. The 16.8-acre park is heavily used by the public with the pond being the key feature of the park. Installation of the proposed improvements would provide increased accessibility to this park feature and additional seating, as well as lighting for increased safety.

ceqa-b9703bb8063d8963fe.name: Castle Fire Ecological Restoration Project
ceqa-b9703bb8063d8963fe.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-b9703bb8063d8963fe.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-b9703bb8063d8963fe.description: The California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL FIRE) will implement mechanical fuels treatments, dead tree removal, manual piling, and assist in prescribed burn unit preparation across 39,335 acres of the Sequoia National Forest. Treatments will take place within the perimeter of the Castle Fire footprint and will support the ecological restoration of the severely damaged forest lands. Project treatments will support not only ecological restoration but will help reduce fuel loading in and around the wildland urban interface.

ceqa-a7487c3f83f06fb50f.name: Case Mountain Post-Fire Restoration and Management
ceqa-a7487c3f83f06fb50f.projectTitle: Case Mountain Fire Fuel Reduction Project
ceqa-a7487c3f83f06fb50f.description: The TCRCD proposes to implement various vegetation and fuels treatment activities on approximately 1,100 acres of land over a 10-year period in the Case Mountain area to maintain a forest structure that would decrease the risk for catastrophic wildfire, reduce road hazards associated with dead trees, and promote the survival and growth of giant sequoia stands. The objective of the proposed project is to protect large legacy sequoia trees from high-intensity wildfire, restore a more diverse and resilient forest structure, return the role of fire to the ecosystem, and protect the public from road and wildland fire hazards within the Case Mountain area.

ceqa-7fb88932dbf3a498a4.name: MLRP Basin Project (Lake or Streambed Alteration Agreement No. EPIMS-TUL-61710-R4)
ceqa-7fb88932dbf3a498a4.description: The California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) has executed Lake or Streambed Alteration Agreement (EPIMS-TUL-61710-R4), pursuant to Fish and Game Code section 1602, to the project Applicant, East Kaweah Groundwater Sustainability Agency. The Project includes activities related to the construction and operation of a new pre-cast reinforced flared concrete turnout structure within Cottonwood Creek to support future groundwater recharge, by diverting water to a proposed adjacent groundwater recharge basin.

ceqa-03bd715d85f7a2d124.name: Use Permit No. PSP 26-024 (AA)
ceqa-03bd715d85f7a2d124.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-024 (AA) to allow the establishment of a second residential unit (1,600 sq. ft. single-family dwelling) on a 56,628 sq. ft. parcel in the R-A-65 (Rural Residential – 65,000 sq. ft. minimum) Zone. The beneficiary of the Project is the land owner.

ceqa-75c68fb7523d8152bf.name: Oakmore Ranch Project
ceqa-75c68fb7523d8152bf.description: The proposed project consists of approximately 235 acres located in unincorporated Tulare County, located immediately east of Oakmore Street, south of State Route 137 (Tulare Avenue) and north of Avenue 228. The project area is immediately adjacent to the existing City of Tulare city limit boundary to the west and is within the City of Tulare’s adopted Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Plan Area. The site is bordered by: • Chandler Grove Master Plan to the south • Mission Oak High School to the southwest • College of the Sequoias (COS) Tulare Campus to the south • Agricultural and rural residential uses to the north and east See Figure 1 (Regional Location and Vicinity Map) and Figure 2 (Annexation Boundary Map). The proposed project consists of the annexation, pre zoning, and amendment of the General Plan land use designation for the approximately 235 acre Oakmore Ranch planning area. The project would bring the planning area into the City of Tulare’s jurisdiction and establish land use and circulation frameworks consistent with the City’s long range planning documents, including the North COS TOD Plan Area. No specific development project is proposed for approval as part of this action. The EIR will evaluate the annexation and associated land use designations at a programmatic level, with the understanding that future development within the planning area will require separate, project level CEQA review once detailed site plans, phasing, and infrastructure designs are available.
ceqa-75c68fb7523d8152bf.crossStreets: Southwest corner of Tulare Avenue (SR-137) and Oakmore Street
ceqa-75c68fb7523d8152bf.developmentType: Other (Annexation, GPA and Prezone, no specific development at this tim)

ceqa-a1572d9f63b2357abb.name: Teviston Community Services District 1,2,3-Trichloropropane Mitigation
ceqa-a1572d9f63b2357abb.description: The Project includes water treatment improvements to Well 3, including the construction of a treatment facility that would consist of a 37.500 galloon backwash supply tank and pump and backwash holding basin. a pair of Granular Activated Carbon vessels. a sand separator and cartridge filter equipment, a chemical storage enclosure, and an onsite concrete truck pad. Additionally, a 2,000-foot pipeline would be installed approximately four feet below ground surface that would connect the treatment site for Well 3 to the District's newly constructed Well 4 to aid in the compliance of water quality regulation

ceqa-18616f7fccc49601ec.name: Yokohl Creek Gauging Station Stilling Well
ceqa-18616f7fccc49601ec.projectTitle: Yokohl Creek Gauging Station Stilling Well
ceqa-18616f7fccc49601ec.description: Replacement to Yokohl Creek Gauging Station to restore this facility back to its pre-disaster design, function and capacity within the existing footprint. The Gauging Station is for uncontrolled channel flow monitoring downstream of Terminus Dam at Lake Kaweah.

ceqa-4ad1bb21782369a481.name: Permit No. 20042 – East Kaweah GSA Multi-Benefit Land Repurposing Program Basin: Flying Dragon Ranch Project
ceqa-4ad1bb21782369a481.description: Approval of Permit No. 20042, under California Code of Regulations, Title 23, Article 3, Section 6, for work within an adopted plan of flood control: To construct a turnout facility with a 36-inch reinforced concrete pipe intake for a multi cell groundwater recharge basin facility, located on an approximately 60-acre site north of the community of Ivanhoe adjacent to Cottonwood Creek. The proposed turnout facility will allow the East Kaweah Groundwater Sustainability Agency to divert surface water from Cottonwood Creek into the proposed basin area for groundwater recharge.

ceqa-cff4191787665909fe.name: SK Vanderstelt Recharge Basin Project
ceqa-cff4191787665909fe.description: The Proposed Project consists of the construction of new recharge basins, a new concrete diversion weir and turnout structure in the St. Johns River to facilitate groundwater recharge in areas adjacent to the main channel. The Proposed Project also includes a discharge structure downstream that will enable the District to return unused surface water to the main channel for downstream purposes. Construction will include the clearing and site preparation, including excavation for the diversion weir, turnout and discharge structures, earthwork, backfill, compaction and surface restoration efforts to complete the recharge basins and new structures.

ceqa-a6634b90f4d68bd0f1.name: Entertainment Plaza Clean California Improvements Project
ceqa-a6634b90f4d68bd0f1.projectTitle: Entertainment Plaza Clean California Improvements Project
ceqa-a6634b90f4d68bd0f1.description: The project includes comprehensive improvements to the existing Entertainment Plaza, including but not limited to new shade structures, an amphitheater, playground enhancements, picnic areas, landscape and irrigation improvements, monument signage, and other miscellaneous park upgrades within the City of Dinuba, Tulare County, as shown on the plans.
ceqa-a6634b90f4d68bd0f1.crossStreets: L St. & M St. and Kern St. & Ventura St.

ceqa-6cce628387aa149811.name: 2025 Corridor Improvements Project
ceqa-6cce628387aa149811.description: The project consists of various roadway and site improvements throughout the City of Dinuba, including the grind and overlay of Kamm Avenue and El Monte Way, and the full reconstruction of College Avenue. The work also includes upgrades to ADA curb ramps, construction of new median islands with landscaping, and replacement of existing water and sewer mains.
ceqa-6cce628387aa149811.crossStreets: This project is located throughout various streets in Dinuba

ceqa-9fd218be84f5d70e5d.name: City of Tulare Recreation Parks and Library Department Ground Operations
ceqa-9fd218be84f5d70e5d.projectTitle: City of Tulare Recreation Parks and Library Department Ground Operations
ceqa-9fd218be84f5d70e5d.description: Project activities comprise continued routine maintenance of an existing OHV park, including road, track, and other facility maintenance (e.g ., grading, weed abatement, dust control, manage/erosion control, trash removal, restroom cleaning), fencing, signage installation, and soil monitoring. No expansion of existing maintenance activities or facility operations is proposed.
ceqa-9fd218be84f5d70e5d.crossStreets: north side of Avenue 216 (Paige Ave) west of West Street

ceqa-19044a34cb1416fc05.name: Addendum to the Pixley Rechage Basin, “Deer Creek Basin Expansion" Project
ceqa-19044a34cb1416fc05.description: The Project would include a 38—acre expansion of the Pixley Recharge Basin from 160 to 198 acres. The Project would utilize excess surface water from the Friant Division of the Central Valley Project for groundwater recharge. Any surface water to be diverted to the recharge basin during operations would include imported surface water, either through purchase, contract, or transfer. The Pixley Irrigation District Recharge Basin is currently named the Deer Creek Basin, and this Project is identified as the Deer Creek Basin Expansion Project. The proposed groundwater recharge basin expansion would be composed of cells totaling 38 acres which would be adjacent to the existing 160—acre basin. Water would be diverted from the existing canal which runs adjacent to the property and parallel to Highway 99. Vehicular access to the Project would be available on Avenue 72 where a network of unpaved private roads on the property provides full access to the recharge basin. During construction, workers would utilize existing facility parking areas and/or temporary construction staging areas for parking vehicles and equipment. During operation of the Project, maintenance vehicles would be required to come approximately three times a week for required maintenance. However, the Project would not require any permanent, onsite employees during operation. No additional utilities or electrical service would be required as a part of the Project

ceqa-01df6b5560b82291a8.name: Yokohl Creek Recharge Project
ceqa-01df6b5560b82291a8.description: The Project consists of the construction a new concrete check structure in Yokohl Creek to increase the recharge capacity of the reach. The Proposed Project also includes a discharge structure along Yokohl Creek near Road 220 that will enable the District to deliver surplus surface water to the creek for recharge purposes.

ceqa-ab9549a67c029117dd.name: Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 26-007, Mancebo

ceqa-5295c79b8227db51f3.description: This project will enhance vehicular circulation and traffic safety at the intersection of Avenue 276 and Road 180. The project will consist of installing a One-Way Stop sign on Avenue 276 at Road 180, located west of the incorporated City of Exeter, CA. This "T" intersection is currently uncontrolled, with no posted Stop sign. In response to concerns regarding traffic safety, the Tulare County Resource Management Agency (RMA) conducted an investigation. To improve the vehicular circulation and safety at this intersection, the Traffic Operations Division determined that this intersection meets the requirements of Section 2B.04 Right of Way at Intersections of the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CA MUTCD), and is consistent with the California Vehicle Code (CVC), Section 22450(c), which states in part that “a local authority may adopt rules and regulations by ordinance or resolution providing for the placement of a stop sign at any location on a highway under its jurisdiction where the stop sign would enhance traffic safety”. Users of this intersection will benefit from this project.

ceqa-db9501a49220eebf18.name: Clements Ranch Tentative Tract Map No. 5606
ceqa-db9501a49220eebf18.projectTitle: Clements Ranch Tentative Tract Map No. 5606
ceqa-db9501a49220eebf18.description: The Project site consists of approximately 370 multi-family high-density units, 153 single-family medium-density units in a gated community with a Homeowners Association (HOA), and 139 single-family low-density units in a non-gated community, for a total of approximately 662 units. The Project site area will have three phases of buildout: • TD 1 – Phase 1: Development of lots 1-78, outlots A-E, G-I, and L, Sunnyside Avenue and Streets A, B, E, and C • TD 1 – Phase 2: Development of lots 140-158, 197-231, 252-265, 286-292, and outlots O and P • TD 2 – Phase 1: Development of lots 79-189, outlots F, J-K, and Streets A, C, E-H • TD 2 – Phase 2: Development of lots 159-196, 232-251, 266-285, and outlots Q, R, and T There is no proposed development of the multi-family units at this time; however, this area is considered Phase 3. On- and off-site improvements include circulation roads, interior local streets, curbs, gutters, sound barriers, sidewalks, streetlights, neighborhood connections to walking trail, open spaces, landscaping, a water well to be maintained by the City of Visalia, and stormwater basins. All streets are to be offered for dedication for public street purposes. All residential units will be equipped with 450-watt solar panels, utilize all electric appliances, and will be EV-ready (pre-wired during construction to allow for installation of an EV residential charger in the future). The multi-family portion of the Project will realign and underground the Tulare Irrigation Canal. Outlots will be utilized and dedicated as follows: • Outlots A, B, E, F, and J-L: Dedicated to the City of Visalia for open space, pedestrian, and public landscaping • Outlots D and H: Dedicated to the City of Visalia for trail purposes • Outlot C: For a water well that will be maintained by the City of Visalia • Outlot G: Stormwater basin to be dedicated to the City of Visalia • Outlot I: Dedicated to Tulare County Irrigation District • Outlots M-R and T: Maintained by private HOA • Outlot S: To be deeded to Southern California Edison (SCE) Water will be provided by the California Water Service Company, and sewer will be provided by the City. Discretionary Actions: The following discretionary actions are required for the Project: • Annexation into the City of Visalia (Annexation No. 2025-02) • Annexation approval by Tulare County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCo) • General Plan Amendment (GPA No. 2025-04) to modify existing General Plan designations to optimize the residential development on the parcel and amend Figure 4-1 of the Circulation Element • Prezone to R-1-5 (Single-Family Residential), R-M-2 (Medium-Density Multi-Family Residential), R-M-3 (Multi-Family Residential) and QP (Quasi-Public) • Tentative Tract Map No. 5606 • Conditional Use Permit (CUP) for a Planned Unit Development (PUD) (CUP No. 2025-24) The Project site would be prezoned as R-1-5, R-M-2, R-M-3, and QP. The General Plan Amendment would modify the existing General Plan designations to optimize the residential development on the parcel and amend the Visalia Circulation Element to remove the “K” Avenue new one-mile-long, two-lane collector from Lovers Lane to Road 248, as referenced in Figure 4-1 Roadway Classifications and Table 4-5 Planned Circulation Improvements of the City’s General Plan. There is an SCE substation approximately 0.50 miles east of the Project site that would not allow for the extension of “K” Avenue. A new Sunnyside Avenue, one-mile-long, two-lane collector from the Lovers Lane/Sunnyside Avenue intersection to Road 248, is to be added to Figure 4-1 and Table 4-5. The CUP/PUD will allow certain deviations of the Visalia Municipal Code standards to develop single-family homes within the Medium-Density land use/R-M-2 designation, allow for reduced setbacks, street sizes, and parcel sizes for the medium density parcels.

ceqa-df5ca9eb6609b38411.name: Circle J
ceqa-df5ca9eb6609b38411.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-df5ca9eb6609b38411.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-df5ca9eb6609b38411.description: The Circle J project will reduce excessive fuel loading and eradicate noxious weeds near the City of Springville that pose a threat to life, property, and the environment. This area was selected due to its proximity to private dwellings, critical infrastructure, and its heavy recreational use. The Circle J Ranch is an outdoor education venue for students in Tulare County and holds important recreational value to the residence of Springville. The Circle J project will include the removal of dead and down woody material through the process of pile burning. CAL FIRE crews will fall, buck, and pile dead oak material for pile burning activities. Crews will use chainsaws to limb oaks five feet from the ground surface to prevent future oak mortality in the event of wildfire. CAL FIRE Equipment operators will use a rubber-tracked skid steer with a brush grapple to assist crews in the piling of dead woody material. Broadcast burning activities will be conducted to remove noxious weeds such as Xanthium strumarium and non-native thistles. The removal of these noxious weeds will improve the overall health of native grasses and increase the grazing potential on the property. Handlines and or wet lines will be constructed to support broadcast burning activities. All treatment activities will reduce fuel loads near the community of Springville, providing for life safety in the event of a wildfire in the project vicinity and decrease the spread of noxious weeds on the rangelands surrounding Springville, CA.

Generally, the Project would provide safer routes for Tule River Tribe pedestrians to cross the South Fork of the Tule River (Tule River) to access an education center and gymnasium and provide safe river crossings via pedestrian bridges. The Project is exclusively located along the South Fork of the Tule River exclusively within the Tule River Reservation, which is located approximately 20 miles southeast of the City of Porterville. Project components include: 1. Replacement of the existing pedestrian swinging bridge. 2. A new pedestrian bridge to connect Cow Mountain Road and the corridor to the Justice Center. 3. Class 1 trail. 4. Approximately 3,765 SF of concrete sidewalk. 5. Seven (7) accessible curb ramps. 6. Two (2) streetlights for the N. Reservation Road corridor. 7. Eight (8) new solar-powered Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) (4 locations. 8. 2 RRFBs assumed per location). 9. Two (2) raised pedestrian crossings. 10. Reconfiguration of back-in-angled parking stalls. 11. Landscaping and irrigation for the length of the project. 12. Signing and pavement delineation for the corridor, including pedestrian bridge.

ceqa-2da00576c80b940a9b.projectTitle: Goshen Avenue multi-use trail reconstruction from the Goshen Community to Mooney Boulevard
ceqa-2da00576c80b940a9b.description: Goshen Ave. – Camp Dr. to Mooney Blvd.: This project will remove and replace the existing Class 1 multi-use paved trail along Goshen. Additionally, the project will update the existing landscape & irrigation; install new fencing; install new path lighting; install storm drain improvements; construct pedestrian ramps to be compliant with the current American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and Public Right of Way Guidelines (PROWAG); intersection traffic signal improvements; and make improvements to the railroad as required by the rail agency. Rail improvements include replacing the existing track panels and signals. American St. - Ave. 308 to Goshen Ave.; Ave. 308 – Camp Dr. to American St.; Camp Dr. – Ave. 310 to Ave. 308; Goshen Ave. – Effie Dr. to Camp Dr.; Effie Dr. – Ave. 308 to Goshen Ave.; Ave 308 – Rd. 67 to Effie Dr.: This project will install, within existing rights-of-way, a Class II or Class IV or protected bike lanes, sidewalk with curb and gutter, traffic calming features such as bulb-outs, traffic circles, islands, and protected intersections; driveways; storm drain improvements; lighting improvements; and pedestrian curb ramps to be compliant with the current American with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements and the Public Right of way Guidelines (PROWAG); the project will include demolition, grading, concrete, pavement, fencing, striping, and electrical work.

ceqa-ee59603f0e3c018ff8.name: Annexation of Setton Farms Property to Terra Bella Sewer Maintenance District
ceqa-ee59603f0e3c018ff8.projectTitle: Annexation of Setton Farms Property to Terra Bella Sewer Maintenance District
ceqa-ee59603f0e3c018ff8.description: The County of Tulare proposes to annex Setton Pistachios of Terra Bella, Inc., (Setton Farms) into the Terra Bella Sewer Maintenance District (TBSMD), which is a dependent special district of Tulare County. The property receives municipal sewer service through an Extraterritorial Services Agreement. Annexing Setton Farms' property will allow streamlined governance by the TBSMD.

ceqa-38ae23540346aed9d0.name: East Kaweah Groundwater Heuer Monitoring Well
ceqa-38ae23540346aed9d0.projectTitle: East Kaweah Groundwater Heuer Monitoring Well
ceqa-38ae23540346aed9d0.description: The East Kaweah Groundwater Sustainability Agency (EKGSA) proposes to install one monitoring well approximately 0.2 miles south of Avenue 200 in unincorporated Tulare County, to assist in the monitoring network established by the EKGSA through the groundwater sustainability planning effort required by the Sustainable Groundwater Management Act. The well would be specifically used to monitor groundwater levels and water quality in the area, and would not require the use of any power.

ceqa-ee92e5ce2eb6a1c7da.name: East Kaweah Groundwater 5th Avenue Monitoring Well
ceqa-ee92e5ce2eb6a1c7da.projectTitle: East Kaweah Groundwater 5th Avenue Monitoring Well
ceqa-ee92e5ce2eb6a1c7da.description: The East Kaweah Groundwater Sustainability Agency (EKGSA) proposes to install one monitoring well just northwest of 5th Avenue in unincorporated Tulare County, to assist in the monitoring network established by the EKGSA through the groundwater sustainability planning effort required by the Sustainable Groundwater Management Act. The well would be speci?cally used to monitor groundwater levels and water quality in the area, and would not require the use of any power.

ceqa-3d25db96b7522666ca.name: Grandview Gardens and East Plano Consolidation Project
ceqa-3d25db96b7522666ca.projectTitle: Grandview Gardens and East Plano Water Consolidation Project
ceqa-3d25db96b7522666ca.agency: State Water Resources Control Board, Divison of Financial Assistance
ceqa-3d25db96b7522666ca.description: The State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) is funding the Project referred to internally as Grandview Gardens and East Plano Consolidation with Porterville. The Project includes the consolidation of the East Plano and the Grandview Gardens water systems into the City of Porterville's community water system. • The East Plano water system consolidation involves the installation of approximately 600 feet of eight-inch polyvinyl chloride (PVC) water main and 980 feet of four-inch PVC water main, along with 14 one-inch water services, meters, boxes, and related structures like fire hydrants and fittings. The current water main will be abandoned in place, the existing well station will be demolished, and all present water meters and boxes will be removed. • The Grandview Garden water system consolidation involves the installation of approximately 3,320 feet of eight-inch PVC and 25 feet of six-inch PVC, along with 83 new one-inch water services including meters and boxes. The project also includes abandoning the existing main, demolishing the well station, and removing all current meters and boxes

ceqa-4d8177d24799c821d6.name: Mooney Blvd Improvements
ceqa-4d8177d24799c821d6.description: Widen southbound SR-63 to the west of Mooney with pave-out, new cub/gutter, and sidewalk from Cartmill Ave. to Ribolla Ave. Extend existing median improvements south from Cartmill Avenue to Ribolla Avenue. Install signage, striping, and markings as required in support of the widening efforts. Relocation of traffic signal poles and related equipment (appurtenances) at the southwest comer of Mooney Boulevard and Cartmill Avenue. The Project would provide a public benefit, particularly to southbound vehicular traffic along the Mooney Blvd. condor. between the Cities of Tulare and Visalia.

ceqa-1fbd66286169276ce7.name: Setback Variance No. PSV 26-001
ceqa-1fbd66286169276ce7.description: The project is requesting to allow the construction of a trash enclosure and shade structures within the building and yard setback areas on a parcel in the C-2-MU (General Commercial with a Mixed-Use Overlay) Zone. The trash enclosure is within the property line, and the enclosure's doors, would not exceed the property line. While the proposed enclosure would meet the side yard requirements for the C-2 Zone, the building line setback would be unfilled unless allowed with a setback variance. The proposed shade structures are located within both the front yard setback of ten (10) feet and building setback. The setback variance proposes the shade structures to be constructed within the setback area of the property as the enforcement of the setback requirements would limit the project and reduce the buildable area by approximately 6,000 square feet.

ceqa-3391bb725020ae68fb.name: Agricultural Diminishment No. PAD 26-001 - Ritchie
ceqa-3391bb725020ae68fb.description: The Tulare County Board of Supervisors has received a request (PAD 26-001) for the diminishment of Agricultural Preserve No. 293, consisting of three (3) parcels totaling 279.73-acres owned by Jeffrey B Ritchie Family Limited Partnership. A Notice of Nonrenewal (WAN 21-013) was filed and was approved by the Tulare County Board of Supervisors on August 2, 2022, by Resolution No. 2022-0677. Tentative Cancellation (WAC 22-002) was approved by the Tulare County Board of Supervisors on November 29, 2022, by Resolution No. 2022-1005. The beneficiaries of the project will be the citizens of Tulare County and City of Visalia.

ceqa-f0f050e8a935db8bed.name: Special Use Permit PSP 26-003- CARRANZA
ceqa-f0f050e8a935db8bed.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 26-003 requested to allow a contractor’s storage yard use to repair recreational vehicles on the southern 0.5- acre portion of 1.5-acre property. The subject site is zoned AE-10 (Exclusive Agriculture – 10 Acre Minimum) Zone and lies within the Rural Valley Land Plan area and is designated for Valley Agricultural land use. The beneficiary is the property owner.

ceqa-071c1d48765f767ed2.name: Performing Arts Theater, AcCEL Center, and Library Project
ceqa-071c1d48765f767ed2.projectTitle: Performing Arts Theater, AcCEL Center, and Library Project
ceqa-071c1d48765f767ed2.description: The proposed project includes development of a performing arts theater, the AcCEL Center, and a library on the project site. The single-story. 31 ,000-square-foot performing arts theater would be located in the southeast portion of the site and would include a 60-foot-high fly space above the stage, 500 seats, and up to 15 staff, and would host approximately 60 academic and after-school events annually. The proposed project would also include construction of the single-story, 24,442-square-foot AcCEL Center, which would accommodate approximately 80 students and 20 staff and Include a shade structure, play area, basketball courts, and landscaping, as well as a two-building, approximately 12,000-square-foot library that would accommodate up to 100 occupants and 5 staff. The proJect would include a 500- space parking lot serving the performing arts theater and a 67-space parking lot serving the AcCEL Center and library, landscaping, sidewalks, installation of two photovoltaic systems, outdoor lighting, and perimeter fencing and gates. The project construction would occur in two phases: Phase 1 (AcCEL Center and library) from approximately May 2026 to June 2027 and Phase 2 (performing arts theater) from approximately January 2028 to January 2030.
ceqa-071c1d48765f767ed2.crossStreets: Avenue 264/Liberty Road and N Mooney Boulevard

ceqa-afa4f31b3678487be9.name: Minor Modification No. MIM 26-005
ceqa-afa4f31b3678487be9.description: The Applicant, William and John Jongsma Dairy, is requesting approval to allow for the addition of four (4) corrals to ensure proper health and welfare for the herd located on the existing dairy site. The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-db934159cf54b31bde.name: Minor Modification No. MIM 26-007
ceqa-db934159cf54b31bde.description: The Applicant, Moonlight Dairy (John Moons, Owner), is requesting to allow for a new concrete silage slab, one (1) commodity barn, two (2) freestall barns, two (2) shade structures, two (2) loafing barns, nine (9) corral shade structures, additional calf hutches, additional open lot corrals and the relocation of the manure storage area to improve site layout and manure management efficiency located on an existing dairy site. The beneficiary of the project is the Applicant.

ceqa-e803f33d3dd38ee3a2.name: Allensworth Community Plan Update (General Plan Amendment No. GPA 25-006 and Specific Plan No. SPA 25-001)
ceqa-e803f33d3dd38ee3a2.description: A Negative Declaration (ND) was prepared and a Notice of Determination (NOD) filed for the Allensworth Community Plan Update (General Plan Amendment No. GPA 25-006 and Specific Plan No. SPA 25-001. The Tulare County Board of Supervisors passed Resolution 2022-0342 on April 19, 2022, approving the General Plan Initiation No. GPI 22-001 to authorize the Allensworth Community Plan Update to provide a roadmap for building on the existing cultural, ecological, and social assets of Allensworth to develop a beautiful and climate-resilient rural community that provides a safe place to live, learn, work, play, and prosper and attracts community-minded residents, including families, veterans, and retirees. The boundary subject to the Allensworth Community Plan Update (General Plan Amendment No. GPA 25-006 and Specific Plan Project No. SPA 25-001) generally includes the approximately 5.9 sq. mile area south of Avenue 56, west of State Route 43 and the railroad, north of Avenue 24, and east of the planned California High Speed Rail line. The area within the boundary would be subject to the proposed Community Districts to designate particular character areas within Allensworth. The proposed plan’s goals and objectives are consistent with the Tulare County General Plan 2030 Update’s (2012) Planning Framework Element, Land Use Element, Environmental Resources Management, Open Space Element, Water Resources Element, Transportation and Circulation Element, Healthy and Safety Element, and the Environmental Justice Element. Development Boundary by adding approximately 2,794 acres to the proposed community Urban Development Boundary to encompass a total of approximately 3,845 acres. The GPA would also change the existing "Valley Agriculture" land use designation of the acreage currently within the RVLP to the “Mixed Use” land use designation. This modification would refine the Tulare County General Plan and increase the probability of receiving grant funding for the community. The Specific Plan, Project No. SPA 25-001, proposed “Community Districts,” which will direct future development in Allensworth. The proposed Community Districts are as follows: Town Center and Future Town Center Area, State Park and State Park Expansion Area, High Value Farm & Garden Area, Allensworth Community Savannah, and Historic Properties District. Each proposed district is defined in the Community Plan and lists consistent General Plan land use designations that will be used to guide future development.

ceqa-f6339e6889dafb4f99.name: 7Points Group Inc
ceqa-f6339e6889dafb4f99.description: The Project will consist of the addition of a cannabis nursery already within a facility already operating a medium indoor cannabis grow and distribution. The premises is located on a parcel that is fully developed with an existing 116,320SF industrial warehouse on a 7.72 acre lot. The zoning designation is industrial. No expansion beyond the current used footprint is pursued, as the nursery activities will occur in rooms previously designated as immature canopy areas for the medium indoor license. The water will be supplied by the City of Woodlake with an onsite groundwater well for backup. SoCal Edison supplies sufficient electricity.

ceqa-737c5635eaa32661d5.name: Visalia Water Reclamation Facility Digester No. 9 Project
ceqa-737c5635eaa32661d5.projectTitle: Visalia Water Reclamation Facility Digester No. 9 Project
ceqa-737c5635eaa32661d5.description: The project would include improvements to the City’s existing Water Reclamation Facility (WRF), including construction of a new fixed cover anaerobic digester (Digester No. 9) to provide necessary redundancy to the digestion system if the existing Digester No. 8 needs to come offline for routine maintenance. The structure would be 116 feet in diameter (approximately 10,568 square feet [sf]) with a tank volume of approximately 297,700 cubic feet (cf). The tank would include 73,980 cf of sludge storage volume and 184,950 cf of sludge digestion volume. The design of the associated structures to support Digester No. 9 would match the design of Digester No. 8 and would include pumps, valves, heat exchangers, and a 384-sf electrical building.

ceqa-768642684d81c347fe.name: Permit No. 20024 – To Authorize Cross Creek Bridge Repair
ceqa-768642684d81c347fe.projectTitle: Emergency Road and Bridge Repairs Related to March 2023 Storm Event Damages
ceqa-768642684d81c347fe.description: To authorize the 87-foot, three span concrete Diagonal 60 bridge over Cross Creek and the reinforced foundations with rocks for erosion protection of the embankment, bents and abutments, and sealing any eroded areas that may have developed around or beneath the bridge abutments.

ceqa-d16379aaafa8ecbe19.name: Worth Peak
ceqa-d16379aaafa8ecbe19.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ceqa-d16379aaafa8ecbe19.agencyName: Forestry and Fire Protection, Department of
ceqa-d16379aaafa8ecbe19.description: The Worth Peak Project will remove noxious weeds and excessive fuel loading near the City of Porterville that poses a threat to life, property, and the environment. This area was selected due to the proximity to private property, proximity to critical infrastructure and public recreation sites, fire history, and the ability to collaborate efforts across interested parties (Tulare County Fire, Porterville City Fire, CAL FIRE, and the Lower Tule River Irrigation District). The project abuts Tulare Counties Bartlett Park to the South and the U.S. Army Corp of Engineers Success Lake Dam to the East. This Project will include the removal of noxious weeds and vegetation through broadcast burn activities. Existing roads and fence lines will be used as boundaries for burn activities. Handlines and/or wetlines will be constructed where existing control lines prove to be inadequate as control lines for burning activities. Broadcast burn activities will reduce fuel loads near the adjacent homes and farmlands providing life safety for residence of the community and first responders in the event of fire activity in the project vicinity.

ceqa-f0d071048e0ec0e86a.name: Goshen Community Plan Update
ceqa-f0d071048e0ec0e86a.description: The project is proposing updates to the Goshen Community Plan. In July 2025, Tulare County filed an application for a General Plan Amendment to update the Goshen Community Plan to modify the existing Goshen UDB to include additional acreage directly west and south of the unincorporated community of Goshen and to change the Land Use Designation for the expansion area from “Valley Agriculture” to “Mixed Use”. Various studies and reports will discuss possible infrastructure improvements to serve the expanded UDB.
ceqa-f0d071048e0ec0e86a.crossStreets: North of Hwy 198, South of Avenue 320, East and West of SR 99
ceqa-f0d071048e0ec0e86a.action: Community Plan, General Plan Amendment, Rezone

ceqa-1abfeb7b9fc6ba3bf2.name: Tulare County Zoning Ordinance Update PZC 25-005 (Agricultural Zones) and PZC 25-008 (Residential Zones)
ceqa-1abfeb7b9fc6ba3bf2.projectTitle: Tulare County Zoning Ordinance Update PZC 25-005 (Agricultural Zones) and PZC 25-008 (Residential Zones)
ceqa-1abfeb7b9fc6ba3bf2.description: The Project is proposing to update Ordinance No. 352, the Tulare County Zoning Ordinance, specifically the Agricultural and Residential Zones, by removing redundant language, updating outdated language that may be conflicting with other sections, and updating uses to be consistent with the Tulare County General Plan and other applicable laws and policies. Text Amendment No. PZC 25-005 is proposing to update the Agricultural Zoning sections, and Text Amendment No. PZC 25-008, is proposing to update the Residential Zoning sections of the Tulare County Zoning Ordinance. This is a countywide project, the coordinates provided represent the approximate geographic center of Tulare County.

ceqa-8196b94df6ebf53c0f.name: Agricultural Well for the River Oaks Company Property (CEQ 26-011)
ceqa-8196b94df6ebf53c0f.projectTitle: Agricultural Well for the River Oaks Company Property (CEQ 26-011)
ceqa-8196b94df6ebf53c0f.description: The proposed Project site is located northeast of the City of Visalia and is not within any Urban Development Boundary and is zoned AE-20 (Exclusive Agricultural – 20 Acre Minimum). The property owner is requesting an administrative variance for construction of a new well to supply the property with water for agriculture uses consistent with the existing zoning. The contractor is unable to comply with the well-ordinance minimum annual seal requirement of 50’. With the applicant’s approval, the contractor is requesting a variance to the 50' Annular Seal requirement; only doing 25' Annular Seal to obtain higher pumping production from the well. The applicant will benefit from the Project as it is intended to meet their water needs for agriculture purposes.

ceqa-f7d99982c904b9d384.name: Title: Accepting Lot 62 of Tract No. 404 at the South End of Kramer Drive as a Public Right-of-Way
ceqa-f7d99982c904b9d384.projectTitle: Title: Accepting Lot 62 of Tract No. 404 at the South End of Kramer Drive as a Public Right-of-Way
ceqa-f7d99982c904b9d384.description: The proposed action is the acceptance of Lot 62 of Tract No. 404 as County public road right-of-way. The need for this action was identified following the conditional approval of Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 24-046, which authorized division of a 76.77-acre parcel into four parcels and a remainder. The map relied in part on an apparent access point at the south end of Kramer Drive, originally dedicated by Tract No. 404, to serve Parcel 4 and the remainder. Lot 62 is a one-foot reserve strip at the south end of Kramer Drive, conveyed to the County by grant deed recorded January 16, 1964, in Volume 2471, Page 365 of Official Records. Under the County ordinance in effect at the time, the strip was established to control access to adjoining properties for 21 years. That restriction period has expired. Acceptance of Lot 62 will formally establish access from Kramer Drive to the PPM 24-046 parcels. No improvements or construction are proposed or required. The project benefits the County and the subdivider by clarifying right-of-way limits and confirming legal access from a public road.

ceqa-41538b9ba03f8d89ff.name: Well No. 5A Auxiliary Power and Pumps Project
ceqa-41538b9ba03f8d89ff.projectTitle: Well No. 5A Auxiliary Power and Pumps Project
ceqa-41538b9ba03f8d89ff.description: The Proposed Project consists of a new standby diesel 500kw generator and three (3) booster pumps at the District’s Well No. 5A site to improve domestic water supply delivery. Proposed Project features (generator, automatic transfer switch, building, pumps and electrical connections) will be constructed above ground at the well site. Construction activities include earthwork, site grading, concrete work and electrical work.
ceqa-41538b9ba03f8d89ff.developmentType: Water Facilities (Installation of three (3) water booster pumps)(Type Pump Station, MGD 2), Other (Standby Diesel Generator - 500 kW; Automatic Transfer Switch)

ceqa-32c9ae1d812c1a1197.name: Del Oro Water Co. River Island Territory #1 East & West Fairway Uranium Treatment Systems-Water Supply Permit Amendment
ceqa-32c9ae1d812c1a1197.projectTitle: Del Oro Water Co. River Island Territory #1 East & West Fairway Uranium Treatment Systems-Water Supply Permit Amendment
ceqa-32c9ae1d812c1a1197.description: The Applicant proposes installing and operating two ion exchange water treatment systems within the boundaries of their existing water system facilities. The systems will filter uranium out of the drinking water to protect public health. Resin regeneration will be performed using sodium chloride brine stored in on-site brine tanks. Spent regenerant and rinse water will be captured in dedicated on-site waste storage tanks and hauled off-site for proper disposal as required. Wells 2, 4, and 5 will be reactivated.

ceqa-5ee2b078b9917fa993.name: Porterville Developmental Center - Re-pave Parking Lots and Roads
ceqa-5ee2b078b9917fa993.projectTitle: Porterville Developmental Center - Re-pave Parking Lots and Roads
ceqa-5ee2b078b9917fa993.description: The proposed project consists of repaving or resurfacing an existing road, pedestrian pathways and parking lots at the Porterville Developmental Center. Parking areas at Buildings 1,2/3, 6 and 35/26 will be repaved/resurfaced. South Circle Drive, within the Secure Treatment Area, will be resealed/resurfaced. New concrete will receive pigmentation to tone down the brightness of the new work to make it more compatible with the existing and historic paving. Additionally, two areas currently covered with decomposed granite will be paved with asphalt to create formal parking areas.

ceqa-3ec99b90a67e7221ea.name: HSIP Cycle 12 Pedestrian Crossing Improvements Project HSIPSL-5946(234)
ceqa-3ec99b90a67e7221ea.projectTitle: HSIP Cycle 12 Pedestrian Crossing Improvements Project HSIPSL-5946(234)
ceqa-3ec99b90a67e7221ea.description: The Project consists of improving pedestrian crossings at various locations. The work includes installation of Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) with advanced synchronized flashing beacons, as well as upgraded pavement markings. Pedestrian crossing improvements will significantly enhance public safety, improve pedestrian security and enhance pedestrian circulation in these disadvantaged communities. Construction is anticipated to begin during the late Spring of 2027.

ceqa-b5e401603647d88c7c.name: Westmore Senior Apartments
ceqa-b5e401603647d88c7c.description: Westmore Senior Apartments is a proposed 40-unit affordable senior housing new construction development on a 2.12-acre urban infill parcel (APN 199-140-034 ). This project provides housing for low- and very low-income seniors as primary beneficiaries while promoting efficient land use and housing production goals.

ceqa-349662f67d4a437363.name: Huff Energy Solutions Solar Project (Special Use Permit No(s). PSP 25-060 & PSP 25-062)
ceqa-349662f67d4a437363.projectTitle: Huff Energy Solutions Solar Project (PSP 25-060 & PSP 25-062)
ceqa-349662f67d4a437363.description: A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) was prepared and a Notice of Determination (NOD) filed for the Huff Energy Solutions Solar Project for two (2) approximately 3-Megawatt ground-mounted solar photovoltaic facilities on the same site resulting in approximately 6 Megawatts produced and covering a total of 13.22-acres of the parcel. The project site for PSP 25-060 is a 5.72-acre portion of the northwest corner of the forty (40) acre parcel, and PSP 25-062’s project site covers a 7.5-acre portion of the east side of the same forty (40) acre parcel.

ceqa-34b1bf69a77fc5e16b.description: This project is a Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 25-058 requested by Fernando Martin, Maria Ines Ramirez Martin, Daniel Martin, Ronnie Martin and Eduardo Martin, P. ceqa-4dce5823e6d1e3cfb1.description: This project is a Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 25-057 requested by Faria Family I Limited Partnership, 13691 Road 136, Tipton, CA 93272 (agent: Neil Zerlang – Land Surveyor, P. O. Box 281, Exeter, CA 93221) to allow the division of 132.57 gross acres into two parcels: Proposed Parcel 1= 2.62 gross acres and Proposed Parcel 2= 129.95 gross acres in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural - 40 acre minimum) Zone.

ceqa-5c2c94d427f8aa17d5.name: 190/65 Gap Rehab II
ceqa-5c2c94d427f8aa17d5.description: The project will occur in Tulare County, near Porterville, on State Route (SR) 190 between 0.2 mile east of Road 232 to 0.3 mile east of SR 190 and SR 65 separation. The project would remove 0.25 foot of the existing asphalt concrete (AC) pavement and replace it with 0.25 foot Hot Mix Asphalt. The project would also place traffic stripes, markings, and pavement markers. All work will be within state right-of-way.

ceqa-7512669d7b29727c62.name: Minor Modification – MIM 26-001 to PSP 03-029 (PC)
ceqa-7512669d7b29727c62.description: Special Use Permit No. PSP 03-029 (PC) was approved by the Tulare County Planning Commission on October 22, 2003, as resolution no. 8021 and recorded on November 6, 2003, as Document No. 2003- 0110801, which established an Agricultural Service Establishment on a 2.2-acre site within the AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural – 40 Acre Minimum) Zone. The requested minor modification MIM 26-001 is to increase the number of allowed trucks from 5 to 15. The beneficiaries of the Project would be the applicant.

ceqa-c942dd99a80368abb1.name: Hope Elementary School Water System Improvements Project
ceqa-c942dd99a80368abb1.projectTitle: Hope Elementary School Water System Improvements Project
ceqa-c942dd99a80368abb1.description: The State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) is a Responsible Agency for the Project. The State Water Board is funding the Project referred to internally as Hope School Water System Consolidation with Porterville Project. The components of the Project, to be funded by the State Water Board, include the consolidation of Hope Elementary School with the City of Porterville’s existing water system. The Project will construct 12-inch water mains, including approximately 6,550 linear feet along South Indiana Street and 5,300 linear feet along West Teapot Dome Avenue, of which approximately 1,345 linear feet will be installed via jack and bore drilling under State Route 65. Additional components include installing 23 one-inch water services for future residential connections; a four-inch service connection, water meter, and backflow preventer at the school; removing the existing storage tank and appurtenances; and destroying and abandoning the existing Wells 1 and 2. Fire hydrants will be installed approximately every 500 feet along the new mains.

ceqa-5281702c055240eacb.name: Ecological Restoration Project – Kenedy Meadows (CEQ 25-005)
ceqa-5281702c055240eacb.description: The proposed Project is designed to restore the ecological form and function of Windy Springs meadow and the associated springs and intermittent tributary to increase resilience to climate change and wildfire. Objectives of the proposed Project include removing infrastructure from the springs, meadow, and spring outflow channel that alter hydrology; controlling invasive plants; expanding cover of culturally significant, wildfire resistant, and climate resilient plants; enhancing habitat for aquatic, wetland, and riparian-dependent species; and decreasing sediment mobilized from road drainages. Implementing the proposed Project will provide ecological and social benefits including: restoring hydrologic and geomorphic function, increasing groundwater storage, slowing floodwaters, expanding the wetland buffer to wildfire spread, sequestering carbon through development of meadow soils and vegetation, identifying existing and future wildlife habitat and developing strategies to restore habitat resiliency, engaging tribal members, and providing educational opportunities for college students and others.

ceqa-69e8e1db12927671d5.name: Tentative Parcel Map (Waived) PPM 25-055
ceqa-69e8e1db12927671d5.description: Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 25-055 is to create two (2) new parcels from the original 280 acres, Parcel 1=3.00 -acre and Parcel 2= 277.00-acre located in the AE-40 (Exclusive Agricultural minimum 40- acre) zone. The purpose is to divide a homesite parcel from agricultural land in-consistence with the Tulare County zoning ordinance, and no additional projects proposed. The beneficiary is the property owner.

ceqa-d9cf325779cec058ec.name: Special Use Permit No. PSP 25-095
ceqa-d9cf325779cec058ec.description: The Applicant, Luis Orozco, is requesting to allow for a third residence on a 3.03-acre property located in the AE-20 (Exclusive Agricultural – 20-acre minimum) Zone. The beneficiary of the project would be for the Applicant.

ceqa-a8a36c9d9471a5e360.name: Tentative Parcel Map No. PPM 25-052

ceqa-99c046e4e42e6c28bd.name: Enterprise Street Annexation and Subdivision Project
ceqa-99c046e4e42e6c28bd.projectTitle: Enterprise Street Annexation and Subdivision Project
ceqa-99c046e4e42e6c28bd.description: The proposed project would consist of the annexation of nine parcels, totaling 128.1 acres, from the County of Tulare jurisdiction to the City of Tulare. The proposed project would include the development of three of the nine parcels proposed for annexation, totaling 116.53 acres. No development is proposed within the remaining six parcels proposed for annexation, totaling 11.57 acres. Any future development occurring within these six parcels would require a separate project-specific analysis. The proposed project would construct a total of 566 single-family homes across three residential developments, identified as Wallace Estates, Pioneer Estates, and Pistachio Village. Figure 1 identifies the location of the nine parcels proposed for annexation and the location of the three parcels proposed for development. Wallace Estates would develop 286 single-family homes, a 3.06-acre neighborhood park, and supporting landscaping, lighting, parking, vehicular and pedestrian circulation, and utility infrastructure. Figure 2a shows the site plan for Wallace Estates. Pioneer Estates would develop 131 single-family homes, a 1.40-acre neighborhood park, and supporting landscaping, lighting, parking, vehicular and pedestrian circulation, and utility infrastructure. Figure 2b shows the site plan for Pioneer Estates. Pistachio Village would develop 149 single-family homes, a 3.20-acre neighborhood park, and supporting landscaping, lighting, parking, vehicular and pedestrian circulation, and utility infrastructure. Figure 2c shows the site plan for Pistachio Village. It is anticipated that each residential development would be developed individually over the next 5 years. In addition, the proposed project would construct curbing along the project frontages on North Enterprise Street and West Prosperity Avenue. The proposed project would construct a 12-foot-wide Class I bike path along the North Enterprise Street project frontage. The proposed project would also construct a 5-foot-wide concrete sidewalk along the project frontages on West Prosperity Avenue and West Pleasant Avenue.

Well No. 3 is expected to yield about 300 gallons per minute, and installation of a 10,000-gallon pressure tank, 15 horse-power booster pump, 166 linear feet (LF) of new water distribution line and 500-LF of new irrigation main to all valve boxes from Well No. 3. ceqa-09f60b837f778baafb.name: London West Pond
ceqa-09f60b837f778baafb.description: The District proposes to develop an approximately 80-acre recharge facility known as the London West Pond located northwest of the community of London in Tulare County. The Project site lies immediately west of the existing London Pond recharge facility. The new 80-acre basin would consist of multiple cells and would connect to the existing Kennedy Schoolhouse Ditch pipeline, which would be replaced with an open ditch through the site. The proposed Project also includes construction of a diversion structure, turnouts, and a spillway, on the east side of the property to allow for spill to the existing London Pond recharge facility. Two existing wells on the Project site would be available for use as recovery or monitoring wells.

ceqa-ccddde0d296c9d29e3.name: Paregien Basin
ceqa-ccddde0d296c9d29e3.description: The District plans to develop an approximately 50-acre recharge facility known as the Paregien Basin located directly south of Highway 198, northeast of the City of Farmersville. The new groundwater recharge basin would include a new turnout connection from Deep Creek. The Project would also include approximately 350 feet of pipeline connecting the new turnout to the proposed basin. The pipeline connection from the proposed recharge basin to Deep Creek will be located on the south side of the existing West Pond, which is not a part of the Project. The area to the north and east of the existing pond will be avoided as it has been identi?ed as a potentially sensitive habitat area. No Project activities will occur in this area. The proposed turnout would be developed with a capacity for approximately 20 cubic feet per second (CFS). The proposed turnout facility would consist of cast-in-place concrete structure, control gate(s), trash rack, and related appurtenances from the west bank of Deep Creek to divert to the proposed basin. The turnout structure would connect to an inlet pipeline approximately 350 linear feet (LF) from Deep Creek into the proposed Paregien Basin. The turnout structure would have a maximum excavation depth of 15 feet below ground surface for establishing proper compaction under the structure and pipeline. All excavation material would be balanced on site. Construction would include equipment mobilization, excavation of earthwork for the recharge basin and construction of basin perimeter berms. The Project site would contain temporary staging areas for construction equipment and material storage during the construction effort. Basin construction would include performance testing (i.e. compaction testing) and demobilization. Excavation material would be used on site for berm construction along the perimeter of the basin. New berm construction would not exceed six feet in height, measured from the exterior toe to the top of new berm. The maximum depth of ground disturbance for the basin would be as much as nine (9) feet. Through the improvements of this proposed multi-cell recharge basin, it is anticipated to recharge approximately 1,260 acre-feet (AF) on an average annual basis. However, the site is capable of recharging more in wet years when surplus water is available for longer durations. The 1,260 AF estimate is derived based on an estimated recharge rate of 0.5 AF per acre across the approximately 50 acres of wetted area for an estimated duration of 50 days, which is an approximate average of historical water availability on the Kaweah system. Typical surplus surface water availability is generally between March and June. However, in very wet years, water could be diverted for recharge whenever excess supply is available, which could occur from January to September or October.

ceqa-94fa69896ef2098a08.name: Tulare County Weed Management Agency
ceqa-94fa69896ef2098a08.description: The purpose of the Tulare County Weed Management Agency is to treat and control Ailanthus altissima, Tree of Heaven, Arundo donax, Giant Reed, Centaurea solstitialis, Yellow Star Thistle Spartium junceum, Spanish Broom, Tamarix spp., Tamarisk or other A, B,Q and Cal-IPC noxious weed listed. The listed above exists in large population, relatively easy to eradicate and growth habits make certain control methods more feasible. The control of invasive weeds is vital to the presentation and future ecological heath of the riparian areas of the Kaweah River drainage along the main river from the Sequoia National Park and protects our agricultural resources and agricultural production throughout Tulare County.

ceqa-33fda349b9f889688f.name: One-Way STOP Control on Road 36 at Avenue 408, West of Dinuba
ceqa-33fda349b9f889688f.projectTitle: One-Way STOP Control on Road 36 at Avenue 408, West of Dinuba
ceqa-33fda349b9f889688f.description: This project will enhance vehicular circulation and traffic safety at the intersection of Road 36 and Avenue 408. The project will consist of installing a One-Way Stop sign on Road 36 at Avenue 408, located west of the incorporated City of Dinuba, CA. This "T" intersection is currently uncontrolled, with no posted Stop sign. In response to concerns regarding traffic safety, the Tulare County Resource Management Agency (RMA) conducted an investigation. To improve the vehicular circulation and safety at this intersection, the Traffic Operations Division determined that this intersection meets the requirements of Section 2B.04 Right of Way at Intersections of the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CA MUTCD), and is consistent with the California Vehicle Code (CVC), Section 22450(c), which states in part that “a local authority may adopt rules and regulations by ordinance or resolution providing for the placement of a stop sign at any location on a highway under its jurisdiction where the stop sign would enhance traffic safety”.

ceqa-7ec25c652e10fe4d22.name: Allensworth Community Update (GPA 25-006 & SPA 25-001)
ceqa-7ec25c652e10fe4d22.description: The Tulare County Board of Supervisors passed Resolution 2022-0342 on April 19, 2022, approving the General Plan Initiation No. GPI 22-001 to authorize the Allensworth Community Plan Update to provide a roadmap for building on the existing cultural, ecological, and social assets of Allensworth to develop a beautiful and climate-resilient rural community that provides a safe place to live, learn, work, play, and prosper and attracts community-minded residents, including families, veterans, and retirees. The boundary subject to the Allensworth Community Plan Update (General Plan Amendment No. GPA 25-006 and Specific Plan Project No. SPA 25-001) generally includes the approximately 5.9 sq. mile area south of Avenue 56,west of State Route 43 and the railroad, north of Avenue 24, and east of the planned California High Speed Rail line. The area within the boundary would be subject to the proposed Community Districts to designate particularcharacter areas within Allensworth. The proposed plan’s goals and objectives are consistent with the Tulare County General Plan 2030 Update’s (2012) Planning Framework Element, Land Use Element, Environmental Resources Management, Open Space Element, Water Resources Element, Transportation and Circulation Element, Healthy and Safety Element, and the Environmental Justice Element. The UDB Modification proposed through General Plan Amendment No. GPA 25-006 would modify the existing Allensworth Hamlet Development Boundary by adding approximately 2,794 acres to the proposed community Urban Development Boundary to encompass a total of approximately 3,845 acres. The GPA would also change the existing "Valley Agriculture" land use designation of the acreage currently within the RVLP to the “Mixed Use” land use designation. This modification would refine the Tulare County General Plan and increase the probability of receiving grant funding for the community. The Specific Plan, Project No. SPA 25-001, proposed “Community Districts,” which will direct future development in Allensworth. The proposed Community Districts are as follows: Town Center and Future Town Center Area, State Park and State Park Expansion Area, High Value Farm & Garden Area, Allensworth Community Savannah, and Historic Properties District. Each proposed district is defined in the Community Plan and lists consistent General Plan land use designations that will be used to guide future development.

ceqa-59974e37411f5c473b.name: Orosi Library Remodel
ceqa-59974e37411f5c473b.description: The County of Tulare Orosi Branch Library received a Building Forward grant fund for life, safety, and more upgrade projects. This project will modernize the Orosi Branch Library with key enhancements, including ADA-compliant accessibility upgrades, restroom remodeling, electrical, HVAC, and plumbing system improvements, new landscaping, new flooring, exterior renovations, a redesigned circulation desk, and the addition of a new parking lot and driveway. This building is currently designated under California Register of Historical Resources under California Public Resources Code (PRC) Section 5024.1. As such, the project will modernize the library that preserves its historical integrity. The beneficiaries of the project are library users and entire community.
